dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-park.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below is listed by the subject and level they have taught to examination, because that is the variable that changes outcomes. None is listed by how far they live from Al Sufouh, because for a student on a screen that number has no meaning.

intro.heading: A map search sorts by the wrong column
paragraphs: A near me search is a sensible instinct in the wrong market. It works well for a dentist or a car service, where the thing being bought is local by nature. It works poorly for a Diploma subject specialist, because the pool of people who have taught, say, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at higher level through to examination is small, distributed across the emirate by where they happen to live, and completely unrelated to the distance from Dubai Knowledge Park. Sorting that list by proximity does not improve it. It shortens it.

Knowledge Park compounds the effect for a specific local reason. It is not a residential neighbourhood with a school in the middle of it. It is a free zone in Al Sufouh built around universities, training institutes and corporate learning providers, sitting between Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City with the tram along its edge. Households connected to it live in Al Sufouh, The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, the Marina and JBR, and the children attend schools scattered across Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and the coastal corridor. A search centred on the free zone is centred on offices.

What families are really trying to establish with a near me search is something reasonable: that the tutor is real, reachable and available at a workable hour. Those are the right concerns and none of them requires geography. They are answered by asking what level the tutor has taught, for how long, whether students were taken through to examination, which time zone they will be teaching from, and what they will and will not do with coursework. Five questions, all verifiable, none of them on a map.

This page is built around those questions. It sets out where subject supply genuinely thins in the IB at higher level, what a short match time looks like and what a long one means, what a district like this does to the weekly rhythm, and what we publish about our own limits. It also states the position on delivery plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because that is a service we run only in India, and every lesson for a Knowledge Park family is one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

One more thing worth saying at the start. There are situations where somebody in the room is the better arrangement, and a young child who needs company to stay on task is the clearest of them. We do not sell that format here, and we would rather say so on this page than have the conversation in week three of a block that was never going to suit. The same applies in reverse: where a request is narrow enough that only a handful of people in the country have taught it, we will tell you the wait rather than fill the slot with somebody plausible.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-park.programmesIntro: An IB request from this corridor can mean one of three programmes plus the transitions between them, and the word tutor carries a different job in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three higher level and three standard level subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and internal assessments. This is where specialism is least substitutable: a higher level subject is a different course from its standard level version, not a longer one, and a tutor who has taught only the standard level course will run out of ground.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this corridor attend schools in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, and the deadlines that shape their term are the school's internal coursework dates rather than the external session. Ask for those in writing and plan around them; it is the single most useful piece of information a family can hold.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked from zero to eight, combining into a grade from one to seven. The work is criterion-specific: a weak criterion points at a named skill such as investigating patterns or processing and evaluating, and working on the whole subject is the slowest way to move the number.
programmes.countryNote: Requests from here often arrive with a report that a parent cannot read, because there are no percentages on it. Laying the four criterion levels side by side for each subject and finding the outlier takes five minutes and converts a vague worry into one specific piece of work.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations. Enquiries are mostly about securing foundations a later programme will assume: reading fluency, number sense, writing structure and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud. Short and frequent beats long and occasional at this age by a wide margin.
programmes.countryNote: This is the age group where presence in the room has the most genuine value, and where we are least likely to be the right provider. We say so when asked rather than selling a format that suits us. Where online does work at primary level it is because sessions are short, routine and tightly structured.

programmes.name: Into or out of the IB
programmes.description: Students moving from a British, American, Indian or national system into the MYP or Diploma, or leaving the IB for A Levels. Work begins with an audit against the specification rather than with teaching, because transfers arrive unevenly rather than uniformly behind and the audit finds three or four real gaps instead of a syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: The free zones in this cluster have a relocation rhythm, so mid-year arrivals are normal here. A general revision programme is the wrong purchase for a transfer and it is what they are most often sold; one audit session is cheaper and more accurate.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-park.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects we are asked for from this corridor. Read the notes as a guide to what each one actually demands, and the supply table further down for how quickly each is typically matched.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested and the least substitutable at higher level, where proof, calculus fluency and the exploration carry the grade. A standard level specialist cannot cover it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with written justification carrying more marks than students expect. Chosen by many as the lighter route and not always correctly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Command terms and uncertainty decide the grade with content. Higher level sets in Dubai schools are often small, which is why outside support is sought more here than in other sciences.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Notation is marked as right or wrong: state symbols, charges and mechanism arrow origins. Precision work moves this grade faster than extra content does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology and long answers with enough distinct points. The investigation and its internal deadline often matter more to a term than the content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams, definitions and the internal assessment commentaries. Strong writers lose marks by writing well rather than by writing to the criteria.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Applying a tool to a real context rather than describing the tool. Structure carries the written assignment more than content does.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the guided textual analysis. Fluency is not analysis, and the distinction is where most of the recoverable marks sit.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A common choice in this corridor given the local employment base. The solution and its documentation are assessed together, which surprises confident programmers.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Structural support: narrowing a question, building a claim and counterclaim, using one real example well. Both are coached, and neither is ever written by a tutor.

sections.heading: What proximity actually buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Proximity buys three things and they are worth naming properly rather than dismissing. It buys presence, which for a younger child or a student who will not stay on task alone is genuinely valuable. It buys a lower coordination burden: no screen to set up, no headphones to find, no camera to angle. And it buys a feeling of accountability, because a person at the table is visibly working for the hour you paid for.

What it costs is selection. Requiring a tutor to be within a short drive of Al Sufouh at a particular hour removes most of the list before quality is considered at all. For a general request that is tolerable, because many people can help a Year 7 student with written structure. For a higher level Diploma subject it is severe, because the number of people who have taught that specific course to examination is modest to begin with and the geographic filter cuts it again.

That trade-off scales with how specific the requirement is, which is the single most useful idea on this page. A vague requirement can be met by many people, so optimise for convenience. A narrow requirement can be met by few, so optimise for the narrow thing and treat everything else as secondary. Most families know which situation they are in and then choose as if they were in the other one, usually because the near me search made convenience the visible variable and specialism the invisible one.

There is a second cost that nobody prices, which is reliability. An arrangement where somebody travels is exposed to the evening roads around three free zones, and a tutor who arrives fifteen minutes late has consumed a quarter of a sixty-minute lesson paid for in full. Over an eight-week block in this corridor that is a material loss, and it is larger than any plausible difference in teaching quality between two competent tutors.

sections.heading: Where IB supply genuinely thins, subject by subject
paragraphs: No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to phone numbers in other countries without saying so. We take the opposite approach because it is more useful: here is where matching is quick, where it is slow, and where we will tell you we cannot help.

Standard level maths, the standard level sciences, English A, Economics and Business Management are matched quickly, as is MYP support across most subject groups. These are the subjects most students take and the ones most teachers have taught. If your request sits here, the conversation about availability is short and the choice is about fit rather than about scarcity.

Higher level requests behave differently, and the reason is arithmetic rather than reluctance. A higher level course is a different syllabus from its standard level counterpart, so the qualifying pool is only those who have taught the higher level version through to examination. Add a specific gap - a particular HL extension, a mechanism-heavy stretch of chemistry, proof in Analysis and Approaches - and the pool narrows again. Add a fixed weekday slot and it narrows once more. None of those filters is unreasonable; together they produce a short list, and a provider claiming otherwise is not counting.

The table states the picture honestly. The right-hand column is the one that matters: what we disclose before a booking rather than after one. Where we cannot cover a request properly we say so instead of placing a generalist, because a generalist on a specialist paper six weeks from a session produces sessions that confirm what the family already knew.

sections.heading: Five questions that tell you more than a postcode
paragraphs: If a map cannot sort tutors usefully, something has to. These five questions can be asked of any provider in any format, the answers are verifiable, and the willingness to answer is as informative as the answers themselves. We would encourage a family to ask them of us and of everyone else they are considering, in the same words.

The first is which level of the subject the tutor has taught, and for how long. The second is whether they have taken students through to examination in it, because teaching a course and finishing a course are different experiences. The third is where they are based and which time zone they will teach from, which affects scheduling and which several providers in this market conceal. The fourth is whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which applies to individuals tutoring in the UAE. The fifth is exactly what they will and will not do with an internal assessment or an Extended Essay.

That last question is the most discriminating of the five. A provider who answers it precisely has thought about academic honesty. A provider who answers it vaguely, or who implies that a draft could be improved for the student, has told you something important at no cost to you. One provider examined for this project advertises completed internal assessments at a published price, which is an academic-malpractice trigger under the International Baccalaureate's own rules and a consequence that falls on the student.

The table sets out each question with why it matters, what a good answer sounds like and what should worry you. It is deliberately usable against us as well as against anyone else, because a checklist that only flatters its author is marketing rather than advice.

sections.heading: Why this particular district has unusual tutor geography
paragraphs: Knowledge Park is worth understanding on its own terms because it explains why a near me search behaves strangely here. The free zone was established around education and human-resource activity: branch campuses, training institutes and corporate learning providers, with the tram running past and the Metro a short distance inland. It is adjacent to Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, and together the three form a continuous belt of offices and institutional buildings rather than of family housing.

The practical consequence is that a search centred on the free zone is centred on workplaces. The households are in The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, Al Sufouh proper, and down the coast in the Marina and JBR. The schools are mostly in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. A parent at a desk in Knowledge Park at two in the afternoon who searches for a tutor near me is asking a question about where they are standing rather than about where the lesson will happen, and the two are frequently several kilometres apart.

There is an irony worth naming. The district contains a high density of people with teaching qualifications, because that is what the free zone is for. Almost none of them is a secondary-school subject specialist available at 17:30 on a Tuesday, and several would be constrained by their own employment arrangements. Proximity to a university campus is not proximity to a Diploma physics teacher, and the search results will not distinguish between the two.

What does genuinely differ by neighbourhood here is timing rather than supply. Students returning to Al Sufouh, Barsha Heights, The Greens or The Views can realistically start a session at 17:00 on most weekdays. Students returning to the Marina or JBR cannot, and a slot booked earlier will be rescheduled within a month. That is the local fact worth building a plan around, and it applies whichever provider a family chooses.

sections.heading: Building a week that actually survives: the local rhythm
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement is only worth the sessions that happen, and in this corridor the sessions that happen are the ones placed where the week has room. That is a scheduling exercise rather than an educational one, and it is worth five minutes of thought before any booking. The variables are the school's finish time, the return journey, activities, a parent's working hours, and in many households a second child with a different timetable.

The pattern we see most often is that weekday evenings from 17:30 are the reliable territory, with earlier slots workable only for students returning to the nearer neighbourhoods. Weekend mornings are excellent for longer or coursework-focused sessions, because nothing is competing and the student is not already tired. Mid-afternoon on a weekday almost never works during term, and families who try it tend to be rebooking within a fortnight.

Two household rules make a block finish rather than fragment. The first is one subject per evening: a second session on the same night is attended rather than used, and the student retains very little of it. The second is the same subject on the same night each week, so nothing has to be negotiated. Those two decisions are entirely within a family's control and they do more for consistency than any choice of tutor.

The table maps the week as it tends to work here. Treat it as a starting point for a conversation rather than a prescription, and adjust it for the actual school and the actual journey. Where a parent works in the free zone and is unavailable at session time, written notes after each lesson and a recording carry the information that a doorstep conversation otherwise would.

sections.heading: Diploma, MYP and PYP: what support looks like at each level
paragraphs: The three IB programmes need three different kinds of help and the same word covers all of them, which is why enquiries are often mismatched to what gets delivered. In the Diploma the work is subject-specific and technical: content gaps, command-term precision, uncertainty and notation, and process coaching on coursework. Specialism matters most here and substitution works least.

In the Middle Years Programme the work is criterion-specific rather than subject-specific. A student with a low criterion C in two subjects may have one problem with two symptoms, because the communicating and producing-text criteria reward structure that transfers. The useful first step is to read the report properly: four criterion levels per subject, side by side, looking for the outlier, then asking the teacher which task produced it. That conversation is free and it is more valuable than the first three tutoring sessions.

In the Primary Years Programme the work is foundational and the honest recommendation is often not us. Reading fluency, number sense, writing structure and explaining reasoning aloud are best built in short frequent sessions, and at this age presence in the room has real value. Where online does work at primary level it is because the sessions are short, highly routine and tightly structured, and because a parent is nearby rather than on a call.

Transitions deserve their own treatment. A student arriving mid-course from another system should get an audit before any teaching: specification topic by topic, what was covered and to what depth, compared with the new school's teaching order. Transfers arrive unevenly, not uniformly behind, and the audit typically finds three or four genuine gaps rather than a syllabus. It is one session, and it prevents months of paying to cover material the student already holds.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the limits we put in writing
paragraphs: Delivery format is a preference. What a tutor does with assessed work is not, and it is the thing a parent should be most careful about in this market. One provider examined for this project sells completed internal assessments at a published price. That is an academic-malpractice trigger under the International Baccalaureate's own rules, and the consequence sits with the student rather than with the seller.

Our limit is the same in every subject and on every page. A tutor teaches, explains, sets work, marks it, and gives feedback on the student's own writing. For an internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an MYP Personal Project, that means coaching the process: narrowing a question until it is answerable, planning, teaching how sources are evaluated and cited, and reading a draft the student wrote to reply with the questions an examiner or supervisor would ask next.

What a tutor must never do is write, draft, complete or rewrite any part of the work, supply data, or provide another student's work as a model to adapt. We will not do it and would rather lose the enquiry. The reason we publish the limit instead of just holding it is that a parent cannot easily compare providers on teaching quality and can compare them instantly on this, which makes it the most useful thing we can put in writing.

The school is the authority on permitted support for any specific task. Supervisors set internal rules, record the help given, and sometimes require a declaration. Ask them early, because the answer occasionally changes what kind of help is useful. We are also explicit about what we are not: a tutor-matching platform with no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and with no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE.

whyPoints.description: For a young child, or a student who needs an adult beside them to stay on task, presence has real value. We do not sell that in the UAE and we say so on the page rather than discovering it with you in week three of a block that was never going to work.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IB tutor near me in Dubai Knowledge Park return so little?
faqs.answer: Because the free zone is a belt of offices and institutions rather than a residential neighbourhood with a school in it. Knowledge Park sits in Al Sufouh between Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, built around universities, training institutes and corporate learning providers. The households connected to it are in The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, the Marina and JBR, and the schools are in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. A search centred on the free zone is centred on workplaces, which is why the results feel thin and unhelpful.

faqs.question: Does it matter where an IB tutor lives if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Only for the time zone. What matters is which level of the subject the tutor has taught, for how long, and whether they have taken students through to examination in it. Distance has no mechanism by which it could affect any of those. We do state where a tutor is based before you book, because it affects whether a 17:30 Gulf Standard Time slot is comfortable for them and because several providers in this market conceal it while routing UAE parents to numbers in other countries.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send someone to our home near the free zones?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Knowledge Park families are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a Diploma student needing a specific subject at a specific level that is the stronger option rather than a compromise, because the match is made on teaching history instead of on who can reach Al Sufouh in the evening peak. For a very young child, presence in the room has real value and we are not the right provider.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IB tutor be matched for a student in this corridor?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the request. Standard level maths and sciences, English A, Economics and most MYP subject groups are matched quickly. Higher level requests with a specific named gap draw on a genuinely short list, because three filters apply at once: the level, the topic and your preferred slot. Less commonly taught Diploma subjects may not be available at all, and we say so rather than placing a generalist. Where a wait is involved, you get the expected length in writing before any booking is made.

faqs.question: What are the five questions worth asking any IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Which level of this subject have you taught, and for how long? Have you taken students through to examination in it? Where are you based, and in which time zone will you teach? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? And exactly what will you do, and refuse to do, with an internal assessment or Extended Essay? All five are verifiable and the fifth is the most discriminating: a provider who answers it vaguely, or hints that a draft could be improved, has told you something important at no cost to you.

faqs.question: When is a capable tutor close by a better buy than a subject specialist further away?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the requirement is broad. A Year 7 student who needs help with written structure, or a Year 9 student rebuilding number confidence, can be well served by many capable people, and convenience is a reasonable thing to optimise for. The calculation reverses as the requirement narrows. A Diploma student six weeks from a higher level paper with a specific gap can be helped by few people, and adding a travel-radius filter to a short list produces a shorter one. The rule is simple: the narrower the need, the less geography should matter.

faqs.question: Why is higher level supply thinner than standard level?
faqs.answer: Because a higher level course is a different syllabus rather than a harder version of the same one, so the qualifying pool is only teachers who have taught the higher level material through to examination. Fewer students take it, so fewer teachers have taught it. Add a specific gap, such as a particular HL extension or proof work in Analysis and Approaches, and the pool narrows again. In Dubai schools higher level sets are often small, which is also why a student can be the only person in their class stuck on a particular problem.

faqs.question: What time should we book a session for a student returning to the Marina?
faqs.answer: 17:30 or later. The afternoon return from Al Barsha or the coastal schools to the Marina and JBR is the slowest in this corridor, and a slot booked before 17:30 will be rescheduled within a month. For students returning to Al Sufouh, Barsha Heights, The Greens or The Views, 17:00 is realistic on most weekdays. Weekend mornings are the best and most underused slot of all, particularly for coursework coaching or a whole paper under time, because nothing competes and the student is not already tired.

faqs.question: How do we read an MYP report before deciding what to buy?
faqs.answer: Lay out the four criterion levels for each subject side by side and look for the outlier. Levels of six, six, three and six point at one specific skill rather than at the subject. Then compare the same criterion type across subjects: a low communicating or producing-text criterion in three subjects at once is usually one problem with three symptoms. Finally, ask the teacher which task produced the lowest level and what a higher level would have required on that task. That conversation is free and worth more than the first three sessions of anything.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment or the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes. A tutor can help narrow a research question until it is answerable, plan the work, teach how sources are evaluated and cited, and respond to the drafts your child wrote with the questions an examiner or supervisor would ask next. A tutor must not write, draft, complete or rewrite any part of it, supply data, or provide another student's work as a model. Your child's supervisor sets the rules for permitted support in their case, so ask early, since the answer sometimes changes what kind of help is useful.

faqs.question: If the first tutor is not a good fit for our child, what then?
faqs.answer: We change tutor at no cost, and we would rather do it in week two than defend a match into week six. Fit is not only about subject knowledge: pace, manner and the ability to be blunt with a particular teenager all matter, and they are hard to predict from a profile. The free trial lesson exists partly for this reason. We do not tie a change of tutor to any outcome-based refund arrangement, because a refund guarantee tied to a grade is the kind of promise that should be read very carefully whoever offers it.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor who has taught at our child's specific school?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and it is a common instinct. What matters is the programme, the subject and the level, which are set by the International Baccalaureate rather than by the school. Where the school does matter is in sequencing and deadlines: the department's teaching order and its internal coursework dates shape what a tutor should be working on this month. Those are obtained by asking the school for the scheme of work and the internal deadlines, and any good tutor can use them without having worked in the building.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial, and what are the conditions?
faqs.answer: The first session is free, it runs for a full lesson, and it is spent working on your child's own material rather than on a conversation about our services. There is no card requirement to book it and no obligation afterwards. You receive a short written note naming the problem, its likely cause and the order in which to address it, and that note is yours whether or not you continue. If the honest conclusion is that four sessions would do what a term was being bought for, the note will say that.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any IB or KHDA approval?
faqs.answer: No, and no page here will suggest otherwise. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and we operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we hold none because we have no premises. Where this page names a regulator, it is to explain what that body does and to point you at its own pages.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-park.closingBody: A near me search sorts tutors by the one variable that has no effect on your child's grade. Tell us the programme, the subject, the level and what is going wrong, and we will tell you how long a match takes, where the tutor is based, and whether we can help at all. Lessons run one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What a near me search for an IB tutor actually turns up on this coast
paragraphs: Type IB tutor near me in LA Mer and the results are mostly agencies with a Dubai landing page, a lead form, and no statement of who teaches what. Several route the enquiry to a phone number outside the UAE. None of the six competitor pages examined in October 2026 names a single Diploma subject specialism against a named tutor, and one of the better-ranking pages names no Dubai neighbourhood at all. So the honest starting point is that the search does not answer the question you are asking. It answers a different question, which is who has bought the phrase.

The question you are asking is about supply. The Diploma is six subjects plus Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service, and the subjects split further into Higher and Standard Level with different papers and different internal assessments. That means a LA Mer parent is not looking for an IB tutor. They are looking for, say, a Physics HL tutor who has supervised the Group 4 scientific investigation, or a Maths Analysis and Approaches SL tutor who can tell a student why their exploration will not score above the middle band on Criterion B. Those are small populations.

Now put a geographic filter on top. LA Mer sits on reclaimed beachfront off Jumeirah 1, reached from the Jumeirah Road, with evening parking that fills. A tutor who must physically be in your living room at 6pm has to live and drive within roughly twenty minutes of that, at the hour the Jumeirah Road is at its slowest. Multiply a small population of genuine subject specialists by a twenty-minute radius at rush hour and the number you are left with, for most Diploma subjects, is zero or one. That is the real answer to near me, and no agency wants to give it.

So the alternative is to drop the radius rather than drop the specialism. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. What that buys a LA Mer family is a shortlist defined by the syllabus instead of by the drive. The Chemistry HL specialist who has read a hundred Group 4 investigations does not have to live in Jumeirah to teach your child.

The rest of this page is the detail that makes that claim checkable: which Diploma subjects have genuinely thin local supply and which do not, what an IB tutor has to know that a general subject tutor does not, the internal assessment criteria by letter, the Higher and Standard Level weightings that change how many hours a subject needs, the schools on this coast that run the Diploma, what happens during Ramadan, and the point at which a tutor must stop and the student must write.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-la-mer.programmesIntro: LA Mer families meet the IB at three different points, and the tutoring question is different at each. These are the stages, with what the programme actually demands of a student in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against named criteria and moderated externally. The load is not the difficulty; the simultaneity is. A student handles four internal deadlines, an Extended Essay and a TOK essay in the same twelve months.
programmes.countryNote: No IB points threshold for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency has been read on an official source, so none is published here. A LA Mer family should put that question to the school's IB coordinator and to the Ministry directly. Any tutoring site quoting you a specific IB equivalency score without a moe.gov.ae citation is guessing on your behalf.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, ending for many students in the personal project. MYP marks are reported on a one-to-eight scale per criterion rather than as percentages, which is the first thing parents transferring from a British school find disorienting. Nothing about MYP grading predicts a Diploma grade directly.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, MYP students at Jumeira Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School Jumeirah also carry KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies requirements alongside the programme, which is time on the timetable that a British-curriculum family new to the system does not expect.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with no external examinations. Tutoring at this stage is rarely about a grade and usually about a specific gap, most often in number fluency or in writing at length. Short, frequent sessions work; exam-style drilling does not, because there is no exam to drill for.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving on the Jumeirah coast mid-year from another system often land in PYP with a mismatch in arithmetic method rather than ability. Closing that in Year 5 is cheap and quick; discovering it in MYP 3 is neither.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Offered at far fewer UAE schools than the Diploma, so a LA Mer student on this route is almost certainly looking outside the immediate neighbourhood for subject support, which makes the radius argument on this page even sharper.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP enrolment in Dubai is small, local specialist supply is thin in the literal sense: there may be no nearby tutor who has worked the reflective project at all. This is one of the clearest cases where online access to a wider pool is not a convenience but the only route.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: Supply is not uniform. Below are the Diploma subjects LA Mer families ask for, what each one actually assesses, and where a general subject tutor stops being enough.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic and proof-heavy, with calculus carrying the HL paper weight. The exploration is marked against named criteria, and most mid-band explorations fail on mathematical communication rather than on mathematics. A tutor who has not read a marked exploration cannot diagnose that, which is why AA is the subject where generalist help disappoints fastest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with technology assumed throughout. Students who choose AI expecting an easier route often meet statistical inference and find it unfamiliar rather than easy. Course choice between AA and AI is a university-prerequisite decision as much as an ability one, and worth settling before Year 12 begins.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields dominate the mark allocation, and the scientific investigation is where HL candidates lose ground they cannot recover in papers. Uncertainty treatment is the single most common weakness in Dubai school cohorts, and it is teachable in a handful of sessions if someone names it early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the HL difficulty. Students arrive from IGCSE comfortable with moles and unprepared for the quantitative reasoning the Diploma expects. The investigation rewards a tightly controlled research question, and a broad one is the most common reason a capable student scores in the middle.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume plus command terms. A student who writes everything true about a process scores below one who answers the verb. Statistical handling in the investigation surprises Biology candidates more than it surprises Physics candidates, because less of the course prepares them for it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the marks, and the internal assessment commentaries must each link to a specific article and a specific part of the syllabus. Students lose marks by choosing an article that is interesting rather than one that is analysable, which is a decision a tutor can improve in one session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary forms, with an individual oral and a written assessment. The oral is the component students most underestimate, because it is assessed on a line of argument held across ten minutes rather than on fluency. Rehearsal with feedback is the intervention that works.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven with a substantial internally assessed project. Strong students often produce description where evaluation is required and discover it only when a mark comes back. Teaching the command structure of an evaluative paragraph is worth more here than any amount of content revision.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Offered at several levels, and the route a student takes changes the assessment entirely. In Dubai this interacts with KHDA's mandatory Arabic requirement, which runs alongside the licensed curriculum regardless of what the school teaches internationally. Short frequent sessions outperform long weekly ones in every level of this subject.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, both assessed on the quality of the knowledge argument rather than on subject content. Students who treat TOK as an opinion piece score poorly. A tutor coaches the argument structure and reads drafts; the writing itself has to be the student's own work, without exception.

sections.heading: The radius problem, said out loud
paragraphs: A visiting tutor serving a 6pm appointment in LA Mer leaves their own area around 5:10pm and gets home around 8:10pm. That is three hours of an evening for one teaching hour, which caps the number of families any one tutor can serve and forces them to work a tight geographic patch. The practical effect is that your shortlist is not drawn from everyone who teaches Diploma Chemistry in Dubai. It is drawn from everyone who teaches Diploma Chemistry, is free on a Tuesday, and lives close enough to Jumeirah 1 to make the trip pay.

For a handful of subjects that is still a reasonable pool. Maths at Standard Level, English A, Business Management and Economics are taught widely enough across Dubai that a nearby competent tutor genuinely exists. For others the pool thins sharply: Physics HL, Chemistry HL with investigation experience, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, Arabic A, and any of the less common Group 6 or Group 3 options. For Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, the number of people within twenty minutes who have actually supervised either is very small.

sections.heading: What an IB tutor has to know that a subject tutor does not
paragraphs: A competent A Level chemist is not automatically a competent Diploma chemistry tutor, and the difference is not content. It is three things. First, the internal assessment, which is marked against named criteria and moderated, and which a tutor must be able to read like a marker rather than like a teacher. Second, the command terms, which the IB uses with a precision that changes what a correct answer looks like. Third, the core, because a Diploma student's time is being eaten by the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge whether or not your subject tutor acknowledges it.

The command terms are the fastest diagnostic a parent can apply. Ask a prospective tutor to explain the difference between outline, describe, explain and evaluate as the IB uses them, and what each is worth in practice on a Paper 2 question. A tutor who answers crisply has marked work. A tutor who treats them as synonyms for write about it will teach your child a great deal of chemistry and leave their marks where they are, which is the most frustrating outcome a family can pay for.

The second diagnostic is the internal assessment criteria. Every Diploma internal assessment is assessed against criteria labelled by letter, each with its own mark band and its own descriptors, and the mark is not a global impression. A student can know the subject thoroughly and still score in the middle because one criterion was never addressed. The table below sets out the shape of this; mark allocations and criterion sets are revised by cohort, so confirm the current version against your child's subject guide and their school's IB coordinator rather than against any tutoring page.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and what it does to the hours
paragraphs: Parents often ask how many sessions a Diploma subject needs, and the answer is set mostly by level rather than by subject. Higher Level adds content, adds a paper in most subjects, and raises the analytical demand on the internal assessment. A Standard Level subject that is going adequately usually needs one weekly hour and a block before the papers. A Higher Level subject that is going badly can absorb ninety minutes a week for two years and still want more in the final term.

The second thing level determines is the ceiling on usefulness. There is a point past which more tutoring in a Higher Level subject stops helping, because the binding constraint has become the student's available hours rather than their understanding. A Diploma candidate carrying three Higher Levels, an Extended Essay and a TOK essay has a finite week. A family buying four sessions a week across three subjects is often buying the thing that makes the other two worse.

Use the table to decide where hours go, not to decide whether to buy them. The right question is which single component, in which single subject, is currently losing the most marks for the least effort to fix. That is usually one of three things: an internal assessment criterion never addressed, a command term misread consistently, or a topic taught while the student was absent. All three are cheap to fix and none of them needs a two-year commitment.

sections.heading: The core: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and where a tutor stops
paragraphs: The Extended Essay and the TOK essay are the two components where the near me search becomes actively dangerous, because the same search returns sites that will write them. One page competing in this cluster sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A family under deadline pressure in February of Year 13 is exactly the family that gets tempted, and the consequence of a malpractice finding lands on the student's Diploma, not on the vendor.

What legitimate support looks like is concrete and genuinely valuable. On the Extended Essay, a tutor helps narrow a research question until it can be answered within the word limit, evaluates whether the chosen sources will sustain an argument, reads a draft the student has written and says where the reasoning breaks, and maps the school's interim deadlines backwards so the essay is not written in one weekend. On Theory of Knowledge, a tutor coaches the structure of a knowledge argument and the use of real examples, and reads drafts critically.

What is not permitted is writing, rewriting, editing to a standard, or supplying text that ends up in the submission. IB Gram tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work; they do not produce coursework. We also do not reproduce or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, because those belong to the IB and reproducing them is both a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. We reference and link the official source instead. Word limits and component requirements are revised by cohort, so confirm the current ones with your child's coordinator.

Not legitimate: writing, rewriting, editing to completion, or supplying text

sections.heading: Who regulates the school, and why a LA Mer parent should care
paragraphs: A Diploma student's tutoring plan is governed by their school's calendar and internal deadlines, and the school is governed by an emirate regulator. In Dubai that is KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. For a LA Mer family that is the only regulator that applies, but families move within the UAE often enough that the full map is worth having, and ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched.

The regulator does more than inspect. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely quality assurance sits at emirate level. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule underneath every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

One thing a regulator does not do is endorse tutors. There is no such thing as a KHDA-approved private tutor, and any tutoring service implying that status is misrepresenting it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises, involving initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and operates no office or centre in the UAE.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar, and when Diploma work actually happens
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written without the UAE calendar in it will fall apart twice a year. Ramadan shortens the school day across the Emirates, shifts family routines towards the evening, and lands in the academic year at a point that moves, because it follows the lunar calendar. For a Year 13 Diploma student that can coincide with the final run into examinations or with the last internal assessment deadlines, and the difference between a plan that accounts for it and one that does not is substantial.

What works in practice is moving sessions rather than cancelling them. Post-Iftar slots are productive for many families, and a student who would be unfocused at 5pm during Ramadan is often sharp at 9pm. Online delivery makes that trivially schedulable, which is a genuine practical advantage over a visiting tutor whose own evening is already committed. Shorter, more frequent sessions also work better than long ones during the month.

The second calendar feature is the gap between school terms and examination series. The school year in Dubai does not end when the Diploma examinations end, and the summer break is long. For a student moving into Year 13, a short block of sessions in the summer on the one subject that went badly is the highest-value tutoring available all year, because it is the only time the student is not simultaneously handling four other deadlines. Families who use the summer this way rarely need the panic block in spring.
bullets: Ramadan dates move each year; a tutoring plan should assume disruption rather than a fixed date
Post-Iftar sessions are straightforward online and difficult with a visiting tutor
Shorter and more frequent beats long and weekly during the month
A summer block between Year 12 and Year 13 is the cheapest grade movement on offer

sections.heading: How to test whether a tutor really knows the Diploma
paragraphs: Four questions, asked before you pay anything, will separate a Diploma specialist from a competent subject teacher. First: which level and which paper is my child weakest on, and how would you know? A specialist asks to see a marked paper rather than answering. Second: name the internal assessment criteria for this subject and tell me which one my child is likely losing marks on. A specialist names letters and descriptors. A generalist describes the project.

Third: what will you not do on the internal assessment? The right answer is immediate and specific, covering writing, rewriting and editing to completion, and it should come without hesitation. A tutor who is vague here is a tutor who has been vague with other families. Fourth: what is my child's school's interim deadline for this component, and how does your plan sit against it? A specialist wants the school's dates, because the school's dates are the real constraint, not the IB's.

Then take the free trial lesson, which is one lesson per family and happens before any payment is taken. Watch for whether your child does most of the talking and writing, and whether the session ends with something specific that was not true at the start. A session that felt good and covered a lot of ground is usually a session where the tutor did the thinking. The point of the trial is to watch teaching, not to be persuaded. If the tutor spends the trial describing their experience rather than teaching a topic, that is the answer to whether they know the Diploma, and the answer is no.
bullets: Ask the tutor to name the internal assessment criteria by letter
Ask what they will not do on assessed work, and expect a fast, specific answer
Give them the school's interim deadlines, not just the IB's session
In the trial, watch who is talking and writing

sections.heading: What online one-to-one actually looks like for a Diploma student
paragraphs: The scepticism parents bring to this is reasonable, and it is usually about writing. A Diploma session involves derivations, diagrams, mechanisms and annotated graphs, and a conversation over video with nothing shared is useless for all of them. What makes it work is a shared whiteboard both people write on, screen sharing for the student's own draft or marked paper, and a session recording the student can go back to, which is something no home visit provides.

The practical gains for a LA Mer family are scheduling and continuity. A session can start at 4:30pm straight after the Al Wasl or Al Safa school run instead of waiting for a tutor to cross Dubai at 6pm. A missed session can be rescheduled inside the same week rather than fitted into someone's driving route. Two subject specialists can take back-to-back slots on one evening. And when a family travels, which families on this coast do, the schedule travels with them.

The thing it does not do is supervise. A visiting tutor is a physical presence that makes a teenager sit down, and for a student whose problem is genuinely that they do not start work, online one-to-one is not the fix and we will say so. That is an organisation problem, and the honest intervention is a structure the family enforces, not an hour bought weekly. Tutoring works on understanding and technique. It does not work as a substitute for a schedule.
bullets: Shared whiteboard, screen sharing and an optional session recording
Sessions can begin at 4:30pm rather than 6pm
Two specialists back to back on one evening is straightforward

For Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Theory of Knowledge, it may be a week or longer, and we will tell you that instead of filling the slot with whoever is free.

process.description: Six sessions shows whether a named weakness is closing. The next school assessment shows whether it closed in the place that counts. Two review points in a term is enough; families who never review are the ones still paying for a weak match in the final year.

faqs.question: Is there really an IB tutor near me in LA Mer who knows my child's exact subject?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics at Standard Level, English A, Economics or Business Management, probably yes. For Physics HL, Chemistry HL with investigation experience, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Arabic A or Theory of Knowledge, the pool within a drivable radius of Jumeirah 1 at 6pm is very small and sometimes empty. That is the honest answer, and it is why IB Gram teaches LA Mer students over live video instead. Dropping the radius keeps the specialism; keeping the radius means dropping it.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor's travel time to Jumeirah 1 change who is available?
faqs.answer: Because it caps their working evening. A 6pm appointment on the LA Mer side of the Jumeirah Road means leaving home around 5:10pm and returning around 8:10pm, so one teaching hour consumes three. A tutor can realistically serve two nearby families a night, which forces them to work a tight patch of Dubai. Your shortlist therefore becomes whoever teaches the subject, is free that day, and lives close enough for the trip to pay. That is a much smaller list than the list of people who teach the subject well.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective Diploma tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Four things. Ask them to name the internal assessment criteria for the subject by letter and say which one your child is probably losing marks on. Ask them to distinguish outline, describe, explain and evaluate as the IB uses them. Ask what they will not do on assessed work, and expect an immediate, specific answer. And give them your school's interim deadline dates and ask how their plan fits. A specialist answers all four crisply; a competent subject teacher without IB marking experience will not.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Chemistry HL and Maths AA for the same student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually a mistake to want it. The internal assessments are marked on different criteria, the papers reward different techniques, and the person who is genuinely strong at both is rare enough that insisting on one tutor shrinks your shortlist far more than it saves you in scheduling. Online, two specialists can take back-to-back slots on the same evening with no travel gap between them, which is the arrangement most LA Mer Diploma families end up with once they stop looking for one person.

faqs.question: Does my child's school year group match what you call Year 12 and Year 13?
faqs.answer: Diploma Programme students are in the final two school years, generally ages sixteen to nineteen, which Dubai British-system schools label Years 12 and 13 and some IB schools label DP1 and DP2. The labels matter less than the position in the two-year course: whether the first internal assessments have been set, whether the Extended Essay question is fixed, and how far the school is through the syllabus. Tell us those three things and the year-group label becomes irrelevant to planning.

faqs.question: How does online tutoring handle derivations, diagrams and mechanisms?
faqs.answer: Through a shared whiteboard that both tutor and student write on, so a mechanism is drawn and annotated in front of the student rather than described. The student's own marked paper or draft is shared on screen and worked through directly. Sessions can be recorded, which a home visit never offers and which students use most before papers. This is the part parents are most sceptical about and it is also the part the free trial lesson settles fastest, usually inside the first twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Which IB schools near LA Mer would my child most likely attend?
faqs.answer: Jumeira Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School Jumeirah are the IB continuum schools closest to this stretch of the coast, with Raffles World Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai drawing from further out. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places in total. These schools are named as neighbourhood context; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's Extended Essay if we are short of time?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. A tutor may help narrow the research question, evaluate whether the sources will sustain an argument, read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning fails, and map the school's interim deadlines backwards. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit to completion, or supply text that ends up in the submission. A malpractice finding falls on the student's Diploma. One site competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments; that is the thing to walk away from.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to be my child's own teacher from school?
faqs.answer: Avoid it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. The ADEK detail is press-reported, so check the current policy document before relying on exact wording. The practical rule anywhere in the UAE is not to arrange paid tutoring from your child's own class teacher.

faqs.question: How do sessions work around Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. School days shorten, routines shift later, and the month falls at a different point in the academic year each year because it follows the lunar calendar. Post-Iftar sessions work well for many families, and shorter, more frequent sessions beat long weekly ones during the month. Online scheduling makes a 9pm slot easy to arrange, which is awkward for a visiting tutor whose evening is already routed. For a Year 13 student the plan should assume disruption rather than a fixed date.

faqs.question: Which IB session do students in the UAE sit?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB schools sit the May session, with November available as an alternative route at a small number of schools worldwide. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Any site quoting you an exact IB session date should be able to cite ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator. Confirm dates there, and plan your tutoring against your school's internal deadlines, which are earlier and more binding.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education recognise an IB Diploma for UAE university entry?
faqs.answer: The equivalency process exists for international certificates, but no IB points threshold has been read on an official Ministry source, so this page publishes none. For the British track the sourced requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the IB, ask your school's coordinator and the Ministry. Equivalency is not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP now. When does Diploma tutoring become worth buying?
faqs.answer: The useful moment is the summer between the last MYP year and the start of the Diploma, on the one or two subjects where the student intends to take Higher Level. MYP criterion grades do not predict Diploma grades, so the handover is where gaps hide. A short block then is worth more than a year of weekly sessions in DP1, because the student is not yet carrying four internal assessments, an Extended Essay and a TOK essay in the same twelve months.

faqs.question: What if we try a tutor and the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: Say so early and change. The review point we suggest is six sessions, which is enough to see whether a named weakness is closing and not enough to have spent a term. Signs of a weak match are specific: the tutor talks more than the student, sessions cover ground without ending in anything concrete, or the internal assessment criteria never come up. Changing tutor at session six costs very little. Discovering the mismatch in the final term costs the year.

faqs.question: Is a nearby Higher Level specialist quoted differently from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Pricing is set at the consultation after the free trial rather than published as a list, because it depends on subject, level and frequency. For market context, published Dubai rates put specialist IB and A Level tuition at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Unitors starting its IB tuition at AED 200, from sources read in October 2026. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. What is fixed is that the free trial lesson comes before any payment, one per family.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-la-mer.closingBody: If your child needs Standard Level maths or English A support, a capable tutor near LA Mer probably exists and you should look for one. If they need Physics HL, Chemistry HL with investigation experience, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Theory of Knowledge, the twenty-minute radius is the thing standing between you and a specialist. Send the subject, the level, the component and one marked paper, together with your school's interim deadlines. We will tell you whether someone is free, when, and what the wait is if they are not.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-living-legends.tutorsIntro: The teachers below work with Diploma and Middle Years Programme students in Living Legends and the neighbouring communities. Availability is shown by hour as well as by subject, because in a commuting household the hour is what fails first.

intro.heading: No school inside the gates, so the journey sets the clock
paragraphs: Living Legends is a single master community of villas and apartment towers arranged around a golf course, gated, sitting off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam. It is a pleasant place to live and it contains no secondary school. Every Diploma student here therefore travels, most often north and west toward Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate or the Al Khail Road corridor, and in some cases south-west toward the Al Qudra belt. That journey, not the school bell, is what determines when tutoring can happen.

Work the chain through honestly. School days across Dubai's private sector finish broadly between half past two and half past three. A bus route that collects across several communities can take forty minutes or more even over a short distance, because the route rather than the distance sets the time. A student dropped last is often home closer to half past four. Then they need to eat and stop being a passenger, which is another thirty or forty minutes. The arithmetic puts the first genuinely productive weekday slot for a Diploma student here at around six.

What makes that harder is that the rest of the evening is rarely empty. Dubai Sports City sits immediately adjacent, and a large share of Living Legends households have children in academy programmes there, training between five and seven on several weekdays. Where that applies, the weekday evening is not the opportunity at all and the weekend morning is. Pretending otherwise produces a tutoring plan that survives a fortnight and then starts being rescheduled.

There is a further element that outsiders miss. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. KHDA calculates instructional time for those subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. A Diploma student therefore carries a fuller taught week, and more homework, than someone counting six subjects would assume.

IB Gram's response is to remove travel from the arrangement rather than negotiate with it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a session can begin minutes after the student is home, move to a Saturday morning without rearranging anybody's car, and place two siblings back to back with different specialists. Nobody is sent to a Living Legends address; home visits are a service we operate only in India. What follows is the timing detail, the subject-supply reality, the calendar read backwards, and what the market charges. The order matters: a family that fixes the hour first and chooses the specialist second ends up with a plan still running in March, while one that books the nearest available name in the tidiest-looking slot is usually renegotiating by half term.

sections.heading: The journey audit: where the hours actually go
paragraphs: Before choosing a tutor, audit the journey, because it is the constraint everything else bends around. The exercise takes ten minutes and it is the most useful preparation a parent in this community can do. Write down the school finish time, the time the student is actually through the door on a normal Tuesday, and the time they are fed and able to concentrate. Then write down what already occupies the evening.

For most Diploma students from Living Legends the numbers land in a narrow range. Finish between half past two and half past three. Journey of twenty to thirty minutes in free-flowing traffic, longer on a bus that serves several communities, and longer again in the afternoon peak. Home between four and half past four, occasionally later from the further schools. Thirty to forty minutes to eat and decompress. First productive moment at around half past five, and realistically six for a subject that needs thinking rather than reviewing.

That is why a 5pm slot, which looks tidy on paper, is the commonest scheduling mistake here. It gets booked, it works twice, and then it becomes the session that is always being moved. By November the family concludes that tutoring is not working, when in fact the teaching was never the problem. A 6pm slot booked honestly in September is still running in March.

The table below sets out the pattern by school area, because the destination rather than the community determines the journey. These are the ranges this community produces rather than statements about any particular school's timetable, so treat them as the starting point for an audit of your own week.

sections.heading: Building the week around what is actually left
paragraphs: Once the journey is audited, the next step is deciding what each remaining window is for. This is the part families skip, and skipping it is why plans with the right tutor still fail. A Diploma week in this community has perhaps three usable study windows after travel, training, mandatory subjects and homework, and each window suits different work.

The short weekday window, forty-five to sixty minutes, is for consolidating the topic the school taught this fortnight. It suits worked examples, a handful of questions and a check on understanding. It does not suit anything requiring a sustained chain of reasoning, because the student is twenty minutes past a journey and the clock is visible.

The weekend morning window, ninety minutes or more, is for everything else: multi-step problems, uncertainty and data work, full timed papers, internal assessment analysis, Extended Essay structure, Theory of Knowledge discussion. These are the tasks that disproportionately decide grades and that are disproportionately squeezed out of a commuting week. Deliberately assigning them to the weekend is the single biggest improvement most families here can make without spending more.

The third window is the one nobody plans: the school holiday. Winter and spring breaks are the only periods in a Diploma year with genuinely free daytime hours, and they land at useful points relative to internal deadlines. A short intensive block in a break often achieves more than six weeks of squeezed term-time slots. Families who travel can keep sessions running from wherever they are, which is a straightforward consequence of lessons being delivered over video.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the UAE academic calendar
paragraphs: The UAE calendar does things to a tutoring plan that no competing page in this market addresses, and anticipating them is worth more than any revision technique. Ramadan shortens school days across the Emirates, shifts energy to the evening, and makes afternoon concentration genuinely harder for fasting students. A plan written in September that assumes a 5pm slot will hold every week of the year has not accounted for it.

The adjustments are simple once expected. Sessions move later, often after Iftar, when students are fed and alert. Length shortens while frequency holds, because sustained concentration rather than motivation is what is in short supply. Heavy new content is better front-loaded before the month begins, with the Ramadan weeks used for consolidation, command-term work and discussion that tolerates a shorter attention span. Non-fasting students in the same household are affected too, because the school day has shortened for everyone.

Holidays run the other way and are underused. The winter and spring breaks are the only stretches with free daytime hours, and they fall at useful points relative to school internal deadlines. A concentrated block then, particularly on an internal assessment or an Extended Essay section, converts better than the same number of hours spread across squeezed term-time evenings. Summer is different again: useful for transition work ahead of a new level, less useful for technique that needs a live syllabus.

On the examination calendar itself, the rule for a UAE page is firm. IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. For Cambridge qualifications the UAE series are June and November, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around it uses a date that does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification; confirm those with the school's coordinator.
