sections.heading: Who actually teaches the IB within reach, and why the pool is thin
paragraphs: Having fixed the hour, the second question is who can fill it, and here the honest answer is uncomfortable for a proximity search. Living Legends is a single gated community. The number of households inside it with a Diploma student in a particular subject at a particular level, in a given year, is very small, and no independent specialist can build a diary from that.

So specialists do not locate by community. They locate by road access and travel, pricing the journey, or they widen their subject range until the diary fills with whoever is nearby regardless of course. Both are rational responses to a dispersed market and neither produces what a family here actually wants. The visiting specialist charges the top of the in-home band and the local generalist teaches an adjacent course competently.

There is a deeper scarcity that gets misread as a local problem. Higher Level cohorts at individual Dubai schools are often small, so the number of teachers in the whole emirate who have taken a particular Higher Level course through to a final session recently is smaller than the number who teach the subject. That means scarcity is city-wide, and a radius filter narrows an already thin pool on the one variable that has no bearing on teaching quality.

Remove distance and the question becomes answerable: who has taught this course at this level, and can they take six o'clock on a Tuesday? A household inside the Living Legends gate gets the same answer as one in Arabian Ranches. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and stating that plainly is better than implying a coverage area we could not serve honestly. Specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates, which a parent should know at the outset.

sections.heading: Fitting the IB core into a commuting week
paragraphs: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the internal assessments are the components most likely to be squeezed out, because none of them has a weekly lesson defending its place in the timetable. They carry real weight and real deadlines, set by the school months before the board's own windows, and a student who manages subject homework competently can still reach a submission date with nothing drafted.

These components need a different shape of support. Not a short weekly slot but occasional longer sessions, spaced weeks apart, each with a clear deliverable: the research question tested for viability, the method agreed, a first section drafted and reviewed, the argument checked against the criteria. Four well-placed sessions across a term do more than twelve fortnightly check-ins, and they belong in the weekend window rather than a weekday one.

The boundary on this work matters as much as the timing, and it should be stated rather than assumed. A tutor may teach content, explain what each criterion asks for in the criterion's own language, test whether a research question will survive contact with real data or real sources, read a draft the student has written and say where it is losing marks, model an analysis on different material, and teach referencing properly. A tutor must never produce the work: not the exploration, not the Extended Essay, not the Theory of Knowledge essay, not a Personal Project.

One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, whose diploma can be withheld. Nor will we supply board material: IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source and works from what the school has legitimately issued.

sections.heading: What proximity costs when you price it properly
paragraphs: Price the convenience separately from the teaching and the in-home premium becomes legible. Market rates in Dubai put in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The difference between those bands is the journey.

In this community the premium buys more than a journey: it buys a gate wait as well. A tutor booked for six who clears security at ten past has delivered fifty minutes of a sixty-minute lesson. Across a school year at two sessions a week, consistent losses of that size add up to a serious quantity of paid teaching not received, and most families never total it because it arrives in small pieces.

Expressed monthly the comparison is sharper. In-home blocks of four two-hour sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Eight contacts against four, at roughly half the price, with the difference being logistics. Above both bands sit the specialists: IB and A Level specialist provision at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting examination-year specialist support at AED 200 to 450 plus. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED, and budget online runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52.

None of these is an IB Gram price, and each names the provider or source that published it, which matters in a market where three of the six most visible pages publish no figure at all and two quote in US dollars. Our own answer to the price question is a free trial lesson and a conversation, because the only figure that predicts anything is whether this specialist moves this student.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and claims to refuse
paragraphs: A parent asking who is nearby should also ask who is permitted, because the UAE has a clear rule and most tutoring pages step around it. Private tuition is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing and takes two working days, there is no sound reason for a tutor not to hold one. Individuals offering private tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so a page quoting an amount is guessing.

There is a second rule that bears on the convenient-local-tutor instinct. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify against the current ADEK text, but the direction is clear: the teacher who happens to teach your child's class is the wrong person to pay privately.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai is KHDA, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education and inspecting on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

sections.heading: When the hour you want is already taken
paragraphs: In a commuting community the constraint is almost never the subject; it is the hour. Half past five to seven on a weekday is what nearly every family in Dubai asks for, and it is the window in which the largest number of students across the city are simultaneously free. Saying so is more useful than implying unlimited availability, because a parent who understands the shape of the problem can solve it in one conversation.

Three adjustments usually work. Shifting a session fifteen or twenty minutes later opens options a 5.30pm request does not, because demand concentrates in a narrow band rather than spreading across the evening. Moving one of two weekly sessions to a weekend morning frees the weekday slot that matters most, and for core components the weekend is the better home anyway. And taking a less contested day, typically Sunday or Monday, often resolves it immediately.

Where the subject itself is narrow the answer may be a wait rather than a workaround. Theory of Knowledge supervision at short notice, a rarely offered Group 2 language, Computer Science Higher Level with a specific paradigm, or Career-related Programme reflective project support can all take longer to match. In those cases we give a date rather than putting a near-fit in front of a final-year Diploma student, which is the decision most likely to waste a family's term.

No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is precisely why families discover one in week three. Ours is stated instead, alongside the delivery disclosure: lessons are taught by specialists who may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, nothing is delivered to a UAE address, and home visits exist only in our India service.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor based inside Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not a Diploma specialist, and the arithmetic explains why. A single gated community holds a limited number of households, only some have Diploma students, and only some of those need a particular subject at a particular level in a given year. That cannot sustain a specialist locally. Visiting specialists therefore price the journey into the fee, and local generalists widen their subject range. IB Gram does not send anybody to a UAE address at all; lessons run one-to-one over live video and the match is made on course and level.

faqs.question: What time does a Diploma student from here actually get home?
faqs.answer: Later than the bell suggests, because there is no secondary school inside the community. School finishes between half past two and half past three, the journey to Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills or the Al Khail corridor runs twenty to thirty minutes in free traffic and longer on a multi-community bus route, and most students are home between four and half past four. Add thirty to forty minutes to eat and settle, and the first genuinely productive weekday slot sits at around six.

faqs.question: Why does a 5pm session never seem to last the term?
faqs.answer: Because it was booked against the school finish time rather than the arrival time. A 5pm slot for a commuting Diploma student means starting twenty minutes after they walked in, while they are still catching up with themselves, and it is the first thing to be moved when anything else happens. Families usually conclude by November that tutoring is not working, when the teaching was never the problem. A 6pm slot booked honestly in September is still running in March, which is worth more than an earlier one on paper.

faqs.question: How do we fit tutoring around training in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Not in the obvious slot. Academy training next door routinely occupies five until seven on several weekdays, which removes the window every other family also wants. Two alternatives work: a short session immediately after school and before training, when the student is already in a working frame of mind, and a weekend morning block, which is where most academy households settle. Both are straightforward online and expensive as a visit, since a tutor arriving at half past seven charges for the hour and the journey.

faqs.question: Which schools do Living Legends students generally attend?
faqs.answer: Younger children mostly travel to nearby provision in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam, where families name GEMS Metropole School, Victory Heights Primary School, Bradenton Preparatory Academy, South View School and GEMS FirstPoint School at The Villa. Secondary and Diploma students travel further, to schools along the Al Khail Road corridor and in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah area, including GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail, Safa Community School, Kent College Dubai and Fairgreen International School. Schools are named as travel context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: What should go in a weekend session rather than a weekday one?
faqs.answer: Anything that needs a sustained chain of reasoning. Full timed papers, multi-step mathematics and physics problems, uncertainty and data analysis, internal assessment drafting, Extended Essay structure and Theory of Knowledge discussion all belong in a ninety-minute weekend window. Weekday slots suit consolidating the topic the school taught that fortnight: worked examples, a handful of questions, a check on understanding. Assigning the windows deliberately usually improves outcomes more than adding a third session.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the schedule for a household here?
faqs.answer: School days shorten across the Emirates and energy moves to the evening. Sessions typically shift later, often after Iftar, and shorten while keeping their frequency, because sustained concentration rather than motivation is what is scarce. Heavy new content is better front-loaded before the month begins, with the Ramadan weeks used for consolidation, command-term work and discussion. Non-fasting students in the same household are affected too, since the shortened school day changes the whole week's rhythm, not just one child's.

faqs.question: Can one evening cover two children with a ninety-minute arrival gap?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that gap is exactly why consecutive online slots work so well here. A primary-age child from this community is often home by three and available at half past three; their Diploma sibling arrives at half past four and is usable from six. Two slots with two specialists fit naturally in sequence and the second carries no travel cost because nothing is travelling. With a visiting tutor the same arrangement means two journeys and two premiums, or one compromised session.

faqs.question: Do school holidays help a Diploma student in this community?
faqs.answer: More than most families use. The winter and spring breaks are the only periods in a Diploma year with genuinely free daytime hours, and they fall at useful points relative to school internal deadlines. A short intensive block then, particularly on an internal assessment or an Extended Essay section, converts better than the same hours spread across squeezed term-time evenings. Households that travel over the breaks can keep sessions running from wherever they are, which follows from lessons being delivered over video.

faqs.question: How do mandatory UAE subjects affect the available study time?
faqs.answer: They reduce it, and a plan built from the six Diploma subjects will overestimate what is free. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes, which means a fuller taught week and proportionate homework.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium really buy in a gated community?
faqs.answer: A journey and a gate wait. Market figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and monthly, four two-hour visits are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 while roughly AED 799 buys eight online sessions. On top of the price gap, a tutor who clears security ten minutes late has delivered fifty minutes of a paid hour. For a young child presence does real work; for a Diploma student it does not.

faqs.question: Which exam session applies to a student at a UAE school?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date a family plans around is a real harm; confirm with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications a sibling may be taking, the UAE series are June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, its November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Should I ask a Living Legends tutor about their MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the answer should be immediate. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE states no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published. Ask also whether your child attends the tutor's own school, since a code of conduct bars that.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free at the hour our journey allows?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a date rather than offering a near-fit. The contested window across the whole city is half past five to seven on a weekday, so three adjustments usually resolve it: shifting fifteen or twenty minutes later, moving one of two weekly sessions to a weekend morning, or taking a less contested day such as Sunday or Monday. Where the subject itself is narrow, such as short-notice Theory of Knowledge supervision or a rarely offered Group 2 language, a wait is the honest answer rather than a substitute.

intro.heading: A Diploma week is already full before tutoring arrives
paragraphs: The honest answer to this search is that proximity is not the problem. A Diploma student in Meydan is carrying six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS, and in DP2 three internal assessments arrive in roughly the same term as the other two core components. The question is not where a tutor is. It is which hours exist, and what they are being taken from.

Meydan makes that question sharper than most districts. There are almost no schools inside the development, so every child travels out — commonly to Hartland International School or North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland, to Repton School Dubai or GEMS Modern Academy across in Nad Al Sheba, or further to Swiss International Scientific School Dubai at Al Jaddaf and the Al Barsha schools. Arrival home ranges from before 15:30 to after 16:45 depending on which. On top of that sit CAS commitments, which in many schools are deliberately placed after school.

So a weekly tutoring slot in this district is competing with a real timetable rather than with idleness. The families who get value from support here are the ones who decide in advance what the session is displacing, and the ones who waste money are the ones who add an hour on top of a week that has no hour in it. The second group reschedule four times and stop by half term.

Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen licensed curricula, with the IB accounting for around 7% of enrolment. The emirate's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. IB cohorts in individual schools therefore remain modest, which has a direct consequence for this search: the number of Higher Level specialists in any one subject living within a short drive of Meydan is small, and that is arithmetic rather than a sales argument.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India. For a DP2 student the practical consequence is that a session can be placed in the one gap the week actually has, moved by a message when a CAS commitment or an internal deadline moves, and kept running while the family is abroad, which in this corridor happens for weeks at a time.

One thing worth doing before any first conversation, and it takes about half an hour. Write the week down: school finish, journey home, CAS commitments, fixtures, and the dates of the next two component deadlines. Then look at what is left. Families in this district who do that arrive with a precise question — which hour, which subject, which deadline — and get a precise answer. Families who do not arrive asking for a weekly hour, get one, and spend a term discovering that the hour was never available in the first place.

Lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, never a UAE home visit

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-meydan.programmesIntro: The Diploma is one programme with four very different years inside it, counting the year before it starts. These are the stages a Meydan family passes through, described by what each one does to the week.

programmes.name: The year before the Diploma
programmes.description: The cheapest and most useful year to buy support in, and the one families skip. The subject and level choices for the Diploma are made here, and the two habits DP1 assumes — timed written examination and extended independent writing to a word limit — are built here or not at all. A student arriving in DP1 without either is learning them while also learning six new courses.
programmes.countryNote: In the Meydan corridor students reach the Diploma from both MYP and IGCSE, often into the same DP1 class, and they arrive with opposite gaps. MYP students have never paced a two-hour paper; IGCSE students have never written 4,000 words or kept a process journal. Knowing which profile your child has is the most useful preparation available.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: Six courses begin in parallel, CAS starts, Theory of Knowledge appears on the timetable and the Extended Essay is introduced. The week is full but nothing is urgent until the final term, when internal assessment and Extended Essay topics are chosen. This is the year in which genuinely missing content can be rebuilt unhurriedly, and it is the year with the most usable afternoons.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students also carry KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons alongside the six subjects, which compresses the school week more than a European DP timetable would. Those minutes are inside the school day, so a tutoring plan competes with them rather than borrowing from them.

programmes.name: Diploma year two
programmes.description: The hardest year in the British or international school system to schedule anything into. Three internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay cluster in the same months while new Higher Level content is still arriving, mock exams take a term, and university applications run alongside. Tutoring here is almost always scheduled blocks rather than standing weekly hours.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB session or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB. Confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator, particularly before booking travel, since several circulating dates have never been verified.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, with a core including personal and professional skills, a reflective project, service learning and language development. A smaller week than the full Diploma and sometimes the right answer for a student strong in two subjects and sinking under six. Provision across Dubai is thin.
programmes.countryNote: Because availability is limited locally, a family weighing CP against the Diploma should settle the Ministry of Education equivalency question before committing. Equivalency is set by the Ministry and must be checked on moe.gov.ae for the specific qualification combination; no tutoring provider decides it and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: Six subjects compete for the same afternoons, and they do not all need the same kind of slot. Below are the Diploma subjects Meydan students bring, each with a note on the session shape it actually wants.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs an alert student rather than a long one, which puts it early in the afternoon and early in the week. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator while school homework almost never is, so non-calculator practice has to be deliberate. At Higher Level, Paper 3 continuation practice is a separate short job worth four sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-assumed throughout, so the losses sit in the interpretation sentence at the end of a question and in modelling assumptions left unstated. More forgiving of a later slot than Analysis and Approaches, because reading and writing survive tiredness better than long manipulation does.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where a tired session is least productive, because an abandoned rearrangement loses the back half of a question. Place early. The data-analysis section of Paper 1 is predictable in structure and under-practised, which makes it the best short block available in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Responds to repetition rather than length: the losses are precision habits, so two 45-minute sessions beat one 90-minute block. Suits a week in which two short gaps exist and no long one does, which describes most DP2 weeks in this corridor.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense and command-term sensitive, which makes it the subject that survives a later or tireder slot best, because recall and answer structure hold up when calculation does not. Useful to place on the day a CAS commitment ends late.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Needs an uninterrupted stretch for anything involving timed writing, so it is the subject most often worth a weekend block in this district. The Individual Oral is assessed on four criteria over 40 marks and is the most schedulable, most improvable component in the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are assessed rather than decorative, and diagram discipline — labelled axes, shifted curves, new equilibrium marked — is a short block that pays across every paper. The internal assessment is three commentaries with word limits, which makes it a defined piece of work to schedule around.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-driven, so sessions need enough length to read a stimulus and write a judgement from it. Students who list the parts of a framework without using it are the recurring pattern, and that is a technique fix rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles plus the exhibition. Short support at the title-choice stage is disproportionately valuable, because a title chosen badly costs the whole essay. A standing weekly TOK arrangement is rarely a good use of a full week.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words marked on five criteria over 34 marks, with the planning reflections contributing directly. Needs three or four scheduled feedback sessions on the student's own drafts rather than an ongoing slot. Nothing may be drafted, rewritten or supplied at any stage.

subjects.name: Internal assessments across the sciences and maths
subjects.description: Four criteria and 24 marks in the sciences with a 3,000-word limit; five criteria and 20 marks for the mathematical exploration. The single highest-value session in the Diploma is the one before data collection or drafting begins, checking the question can be answered by the method chosen.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. Where it is also an examined Diploma subject, support works within the school's own approved material rather than bringing in an alternative syllabus.

schoolClusters.note: The schools most Meydan Diploma students attend, close enough that an afternoon remains usable. Programme provision varies between them and changes over time, so ask each school directly which IB programmes it currently runs.

sections.heading: What 'near me' means when every child in the district commutes
paragraphs: Typing an IB tutor near me in Meydan into a search engine produces results sorted by distance, which for this district is close to meaningless. Meydan has almost no schools inside it. The children who live here are not local to their own education: they travel to Sobha Hartland, to Nad Al Sheba, to Al Jaddaf or further, and they come back through the same traffic everybody else does.

That matters twice over. First, the afternoon a tutor is competing for is already shortened by a commute, and shortened differently for every family depending on which school they chose. Second, a tutor who has to drive here is driving against every school run in the surrounding communities, and the twenty minutes District One's internal roads absorb before reaching Al Khail belongs in somebody's price.

The deeper problem with distance as a filter is supply. IB accounts for around 7% of Dubai's private-school enrolment, which means Diploma cohorts in individual schools are modest and Higher Level cohorts in any one subject are smaller still. The number of people living within a short drive of Meydan who teach Higher Level Chemistry every weekday afternoon is small by arithmetic, not by accident. Widening the search to the whole timezone is what makes a specialist available at all.

So the useful reframing of this search is: which hour does my child actually have free, and who is the best person in that hour? The rest of this page answers the first half, because the second half is easy once the first is settled. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: The Diploma week, and where the hours come from
paragraphs: A Diploma student does not have spare time that tutoring can occupy; they have time that tutoring has to take from something. Setting out what is already there is the only honest way to plan, and it is a conversation most providers skip because the answer sometimes is that no hour exists this term.

The fixed commitments are six taught subjects with homework attached, Theory of Knowledge on the timetable, CAS, and in Dubai the KHDA mandatory subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, required in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The variable commitments are internal assessment work, the Extended Essay, mock exams, university applications in DP2, and whatever CAS project the student has committed to.

The table below sets those out against what each displaces. The point of reading it is to decide, deliberately, what a tutoring hour is replacing: homework in another subject, CAS time, sleep, or nothing because the hour genuinely does not exist and the right answer this term is a scheduled block around one deadline instead of a weekly session.

That last option is the one most worth taking seriously in DP2. Three or four sessions placed around an internal assessment draft take roughly four hours total across a month. A weekly session across the same month takes four hours too, but spread as a standing commitment that collides with everything. The same spend, placed differently, is the difference between support that works and support that gets rescheduled until it stops.

sections.heading: Which subject belongs in which slot
paragraphs: Given a narrow window, the subject that goes into it should be chosen by the window rather than by which report was worst. This is the single most practical piece of scheduling advice available to a Meydan Diploma family, and it costs nothing to apply.

The rule is simple: calculation survives tiredness badly and recall survives it well. A student home at 16:00 can do an hour of Analysis and Approaches or Higher Level Physics productively. The same student at 17:45, after a CAS commitment, will abandon a rearrangement halfway and lose the back half of every question they attempt. Put that student on biology recall, geography case studies or an English reading task instead, and the hour produces something.

Length matters separately from timing. Chemistry precision habits, non-calculator maths fluency and command-term drilling all respond to repetition, so two short sessions beat one long one. Timed English writing, a full past-paper section and a coursework draft read properly need an uninterrupted stretch, which in this district usually means a weekend. Matching the shape to the task rather than standardising on sixty minutes is most of what makes a plan hold.

The table below sets out the pattern for the subjects Meydan students most often bring. It is a default rather than a rule — a particular student may concentrate better late than early — but as a starting point it prevents the commonest scheduling error in this corridor, which is putting the hardest subject in the worst slot because that is the slot that was free.

sections.heading: CAS, and the two afternoons nobody counts
paragraphs: Creativity, activity and service is a Diploma requirement rather than an extracurricular bonus, and in most schools it is placed after the school day because there is nowhere else for it to go. For a Meydan family that means the obvious tutoring slots are frequently already occupied, and the family does not realise it until the third rescheduled session.

The practical move is to get the CAS schedule in writing at the start of each term, alongside the fixture and club calendar, and to plan the tutoring slot around it rather than negotiating weekly. CAS commitments also tend to be the hardest thing to move, because they involve other people — a team, a service partner, a group project — in a way that homework does not.

There is a second effect worth naming. CAS projects cluster their intensity: a student may have months of light commitment and then a fortnight where a service project or a performance consumes every afternoon. That fortnight is almost always the wrong one to have booked a scheduled internal assessment feedback block into, and a quick look at the CAS calendar in September prevents the collision.

The upside of the online format here is specific rather than general. When a CAS commitment moves at short notice — and it does — a video session can shift by a day with a message. A visiting tutor's whole route has to change, and in a district reached through District One's internal roads that is not a small ask. Over a DP2 year the difference shows up as sessions kept rather than sessions cancelled.

sections.heading: Five components, one term, and when the sessions fit
paragraphs: DP2 is where Diploma students in this corridor come unstuck, and it is almost never about ability. Three internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay land in roughly the same months, while new Higher Level content is still being taught and university applications run alongside. The failure looks like a physics investigation written in four days because the maths exploration and a history investigation took the other three weeks.

Sequencing is therefore a tutoring job as much as a teaching one. The science investigations should go first because they depend on laboratory access and on data that might turn out unusable, which cannot be rescued over a weekend. The mathematical exploration can be written at a desk and is more movable. The Extended Essay needs early scoping and then intermittent drafting. The Theory of Knowledge essay needs its title chosen well and then a focused fortnight.

The practical exercise is to put all five deadlines on one page in September of DP2 and work backwards from the earliest, then decide which component will be done to a competent rather than an excellent standard — because with six subjects something will be, and choosing deliberately beats discovering it in April. That conversation takes thirty minutes and is worth more than any individual session.

The honesty boundary applies across all five and is worth stating here rather than burying. A tutor may discuss scope and feasibility, explain what each criterion asks for, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of submitted text to completion, supply a research question, or produce data. The declaration on every component is the student's, and one page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs, component by component
paragraphs: Because DP2 support is mostly blocks rather than standing hours, the useful way to price it is per component rather than per month. A feedback block on one internal assessment is three or four sessions. A Theory of Knowledge title conversation plus a draft review is two. A final-run paper block is two or three sessions a week for six to eight weeks. Those are finite numbers and they can be budgeted.

The market's hourly bands, read in October 2026 and belonging to whoever published them: budget online or undergraduate tutoring AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; a qualified subject tutor online AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; an IB specialist AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table giving 200 to 450 plus; in-home one-to-one AED 180 to 500 including travel; and a premium end reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. For a DP2 family the honest expectation is a lumpy spend: modest in DP1, concentrated in the component-heavy term and again in the final weeks.

One band distinction matters more in the Diploma than elsewhere. Coursework feedback is specialist work — judging whether a research question can be answered by a method, or whether an exploration carries enough mathematics for Higher Level, is mark-scheme experience rather than subject knowledge. Standard Level topic revision is not, and paying specialist rates for it is a waste. Ask which you are buying before agreeing a rate.

sections.heading: A DP2 student, two formats, one week
paragraphs: The comparison between a visiting tutor and live video is usually argued in the abstract. For a DP2 student in Meydan it can be argued concretely, because the week is known and the constraints are measurable rather than philosophical.

A visiting tutor gives presence, which matters less at seventeen than at thirteen but is not nothing: a parent can see the session happening and a student cannot drift. What it costs here is start time and flexibility. The tutor travels into a district with no schools of its own, against every surrounding school run, through internal roads that absorb twenty minutes before reaching Al Khail. A 16:00 slot becomes 16:40. And the slot cannot move when a CAS commitment shifts or the school adds a revision class.

Live video gives the opposite. The session starts when it says it starts. A short-notice move costs a message. The tutor is drawn from the whole timezone, which for a single Higher Level subject is the difference between a specialist and a generalist given the size of local DP cohorts. Coursework feedback works better on a shared screen, because the student's draft, the criteria wording and the comments sit together rather than being emailed back and forth.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The table below is reasoning behind an existing decision rather than a pitch, and the final column is the part specific to a Diploma student: what happens in the weeks when five components are live and the cadence has to rise.

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and a spring that disappears
paragraphs: The spring of DP2 is the part of the Diploma that most often gets away from a family in this corridor, because three separate pressures arrive together: component deadlines, the mock series, and a calendar that moves. Planning for it in September is the only version that works.

Ramadan shortens school hours and reorganises the day around Iftar and later sleep. Sessions generally move earlier into the gap the shorter school day creates, or later to post-Iftar timing, and the productive length drops — a focused 45 minutes beats a tired 90. For a DP2 student sitting papers in the spring the cadence usually holds and only the clock changes, because a four-week gap at that point is expensive.

Travel is the second pressure and the one this district feels hardest. Long Eid and half-term absences are normal here, and families frequently spend weeks outside the country. In-person tutoring simply stops during them. Because delivery is over live video the session follows the student, and time zones are handled by moving the slot rather than cancelling the arrangement. Across a DP2 spring that continuity is often the difference between a component submitted on time and one submitted badly.

The third pressure is the mock series and the fortnight after it, which is the most informative data a Diploma family receives in two years and has a short shelf life. Get the scripts back rather than just the grades, sort every lost mark into content, command term, slip or timing, and work only the dominant category for a fixed fortnight. In this corridor that category is usually timing, which is good news because it is the recoverable one.

sections.heading: The coursework boundary, in writing
paragraphs: Any family shopping for Diploma support in Dubai will meet an offer to help with coursework in a way that crosses a line, because one page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Knowing the boundary in advance is worth more than being warned about it afterwards, and the student is the one who carries the consequence.

What a tutor may do: teach the content, explain each criterion and its mark allocation, discuss whether a research question is feasible and whether a method can answer it, point out that a scope is too wide, read a draft the student has written and return written feedback on structure, method and argument, and model how a different piece of work handles a similar problem. All of that is teaching and all of it is expected.

What a tutor may not do: write any part of submitted text, rewrite a passage into better prose, supply a research question wholesale, produce or clean data, or edit a draft to completion. The declaration the student signs says the work is their own. Feedback incorporated into a student's own writing is normal and permitted; text written by somebody else is not, however it is described.

The same boundary covers materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright, some unreleased, so we reference and link ibo.org rather than hosting or distributing them. Your school holds licensed access. Separately, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and claims none.

Allowed: scope and feasibility discussion before writing or data collection

sections.heading: When no Higher Level specialist is free
paragraphs: Availability is the thing tutoring pages in this market conceal, and the researched set is consistent: a form, a promise of a fast match, and silence about the case where the specific subject at the specific level has nobody free. Several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying so. Disclosing a limit is cheaper than being caught by one.

The honest shape of coverage for a Meydan Diploma enquiry: core subjects at both levels — Maths Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, the three sciences, English A, Economics, Business Management — are reliably covered, and a trial is usually arrangeable within a few days. Narrower requests take longer. A single tutor covering two Higher Level subjects is a narrow pool. A specialist with investigation-marking experience in a particular subject is narrower still, and some requests cannot be met in a given term.

When that happens you get a date or a straight no rather than a generalist with the right label. A tutor who is strong at Standard Level and stretched at Higher Level is discovered in session three, and in DP2 a lost month is a component written badly. The free trial lesson exists so the judgement about subject depth belongs to you before anything is paid: a parent watching somebody mark a Paper 3 section or read an investigation draft can tell within twenty minutes whether they have done it before.

One further piece of transparency, since this page has made a scheduling argument throughout. If the hour genuinely does not exist in your child's week this term, the right advice is a scheduled block around one deadline rather than a weekly slot that will be rescheduled until it stops — and sometimes it is to wait until next term. A provider who proposes a standing arrangement for a week with no gap in it is proposing something that suits them.

process.title: Send the week, not just the subject
process.description: Name the school your child travels to, the year, the subject and level, roughly what time they are home, and the CAS and activity commitments. Then say which of the five DP2 components is next. Those facts decide whether this term wants a weekly session, a scheduled block, or nothing yet.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One live session with no payment and no card, spent on a past-paper section or a draft rather than on teaching a topic. You get a written note naming the dominant pattern in the lost marks, how many sessions it suggests, and which slot shape the subject actually wants given the arrival time.

process.title: Decide what the hour is displacing
process.description: A Diploma week has no spare time, so a tutoring session takes an hour from homework, CAS or sleep. Deciding which, in advance, is what makes the arrangement survive. Where the honest answer is that no hour exists, a block around one deadline is better than a weekly slot that will be moved until it dies.

process.title: Sequence the five components in September
process.description: Put all five DP2 deadlines on one page and work backwards from the earliest. Science investigations go first because they depend on laboratory access and data that may not work. Then decide which component will be done to a competent rather than an excellent standard, because with six subjects something will be.

process.title: Match the subject to the slot
process.description: Calculation subjects early in the afternoon and early in the week; recall subjects later; anything needing an uninterrupted stretch at the weekend. The commonest scheduling error in this corridor is putting the hardest subject in the worst slot because that was the slot that happened to be free.

process.title: Rebuild on the mock scripts, then run paper blocks
process.description: After mocks, sort every lost mark into content, command term, slip or timing and work only the dominant category for a fixed fortnight. Then move to two or three sessions a week of timed sections for a fixed number of weeks before the May session, and stop when it ends.

whyPoints.title: Built around the week that exists
whyPoints.description: Six subjects, CAS, Theory of Knowledge, five DP2 components and a commute out of a district with no schools of its own. We ask what is already there before proposing a slot, including the case where the answer is that no weekly hour exists this term.

whyPoints.title: Blocks rather than standing hours in DP2
whyPoints.description: Three or four sessions around one internal assessment take the same total time as a month of weekly sessions and achieve far more, because the target is a deliverable with a deadline rather than a general improvement with none.

whyPoints.title: Specialists drawn from the timezone, not the district
whyPoints.description: IB is around 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, so Higher Level cohorts in individual schools are small and so is the local pool of people who teach one subject at one level all week. Online delivery is what makes that match possible at all.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line stated to the student
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives feedback on work the student wrote. Nothing is drafted, rewritten or supplied for submission, and the boundary is said out loud in the first session because the declaration belongs to the student.

whyPoints.title: Continuity through Ramadan and travel
whyPoints.description: Sessions move earlier or post-Iftar during Ramadan and shorten to 45 minutes. Long absences are normal in this corridor, and because delivery is over live video the arrangement follows the student instead of pausing for three weeks of a DP2 spring.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with their sources, and no invented dates
whyPoints.description: Every band here is attributed and dated to October 2026. No specific IB session or results date appears, because ibo.org blocks automated checking — confirm each with your school's coordinator before booking anything around it.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Meydan, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For this district the distinction matters less than it looks: Meydan has almost no schools inside it, so children commute out and a visiting tutor would travel in against every surrounding school run. Because IB is around 7% of Dubai private enrolment, the local pool of single-subject Higher Level specialists is genuinely thin.

faqs.question: Where does a tutoring hour come from in a Diploma week?
faqs.answer: It has to come from something, which is the conversation most providers skip. Six taught subjects with homework, Theory of Knowledge, CAS, and in Dubai the KHDA mandatory subjects are already there. In DP2 add three internal assessments, the Extended Essay, the TOK essay, mocks and university applications. A tutoring hour displaces homework in another subject, CAS time or sleep. Decide which in advance, or accept that the right answer this term is a block around one deadline instead.

faqs.question: Why do three internal assessments all land in the same term?
faqs.answer: Because each subject sets its own internal deadline against the same external submission window, and schools rarely coordinate across departments. The result is three investigations, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay clustered in a few months while new Higher Level content is still arriving. The fix is sequencing rather than more hours: put all five on one page in September of DP2 and start with the science investigation, because it depends on laboratory access and on data that may not work.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subject should go in a late afternoon slot?
faqs.answer: A recall subject rather than a calculation one. Biology content, geography case studies, an English reading task or Theory of Knowledge structure all survive tiredness reasonably well. Analysis and Approaches maths and Higher Level Physics do not: a rearrangement abandoned halfway loses the back half of every question attempted, so an hour at 17:45 after a CAS commitment produces very little. Put those early in the afternoon and early in the week, and match the subject to the slot rather than the reverse.

faqs.question: How does CAS affect when sessions can happen?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, because CAS is a Diploma requirement rather than an optional extra and schools usually place it after the school day. That takes the obvious tutoring slots. CAS commitments are also harder to move than homework, since they involve a team, a service partner or a group project. Get the CAS schedule in writing at the start of each term, and avoid booking a feedback block into a fortnight when a service project or performance will consume every afternoon.

faqs.question: Is a weekly session or a scheduled block better in DP2?
faqs.answer: A block, in most cases. Three or four sessions placed around one internal assessment draft take about the same total hours as a month of weekly sessions and achieve considerably more, because the target is a deliverable with a deadline. A weekly slot in DP2 has to survive mocks, five component deadlines, CAS and university applications, and in a commuter district it rarely does. Blocks also end, which is why they are better value as well as more realistic.

faqs.question: What is the single most valuable session to buy in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The one before a science investigation's data collection begins, spent checking that the research question can actually be answered by the chosen method. A design fault is visible to an experienced marker in five minutes and invisible to the student for six weeks, and no amount of careful data collection repairs it. After that, the next-best purchase is a short block on command terms and timing, which transfers across every subject the student sits.

faqs.question: How much does Diploma support cost if we buy it in blocks?
faqs.answer: Price per component rather than per month. An internal assessment feedback block is three or four sessions; a Theory of Knowledge title conversation plus a draft review is two; an Extended Essay needs three or four across the year. At the IB specialist band of AED 200 to 450 or more an hour — TutorChase publishing AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table giving 200 to 450 plus, read October 2026 — those are finite and budgetable numbers rather than an open-ended monthly commitment.

faqs.question: Do we need a specialist, or will a qualified subject tutor do?
faqs.answer: It depends what you are buying. Standard Level topic revision sits comfortably with a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and paying specialist rates for it is a waste. Coursework feedback is different work: judging whether a research question is answerable by a method, or whether an exploration carries enough mathematics for Higher Level, is mark-scheme experience rather than subject knowledge. Ask which you are buying before agreeing a rate, and the answer should be straightforward.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is feasible and appropriately scoped, explain what each of the five criteria asks for and how the 34 marks are allocated, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not supply the research question, write or rewrite any part of the text, or edit it to completion. The planning reflections contribute directly to the mark and must also be the student's own. The declaration is theirs.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions when we travel for several weeks?
faqs.answer: They follow the student, with the slot moved to suit the new time zone rather than the arrangement pausing. Long Eid, half-term and summer absences are normal in this corridor, and in-person tutoring simply stops during them. Across a DP2 spring that continuity is often the difference between a component submitted on time and one submitted badly, which is why the format matters more in the second Diploma year than the first.

faqs.question: Can we trust the IB exam dates we find online?
faqs.answer: Take them from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page gets, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Dates circulate on secondary sites and get republished without verification. A family booking flights around one of those is acting on an unchecked number, and one email settles it.

faqs.question: My child came from MYP and is doing badly in DP1 tests. Why?
faqs.answer: Most likely examination technique rather than ability. Five years of criteria-based MYP tasks, however demanding, do not teach a student to pace a two-hour paper, to decide quickly between optional questions, or to abandon a question and return to it. That shows up as a capable student with mediocre test results. The fix is timed paper practice, which is quick and transfers across subjects. Students arriving from IGCSE have the opposite gap: extended independent writing and documented process.

faqs.question: Do the KHDA mandatory subjects affect a Diploma timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families new to Dubai are often surprised. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes sit inside a week already holding six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, so a tutoring plan competes with them rather than borrowing from them.

faqs.question: What if the Higher Level specialist we need is not available?
faqs.answer: You are told so with a date, rather than matched to a generalist with the right label. Core subjects at both levels are reliably covered and a trial is usually arrangeable within a few days. Narrower requests — one tutor across two Higher Level subjects, or a specialist with investigation-marking experience in a particular area — take longer and occasionally cannot be met in a term. In DP2 a lost month is a component written badly, which is why a straight no is the better answer.

faqs.question: Should we book anything at all if the week has no free hour?
faqs.answer: Not a weekly slot. A session booked into a week with no gap in it gets rescheduled until it stops, and the family pays for the lessons that did happen while concluding tutoring does not work. The better options are a scheduled block of three or four sessions around one specific deadline, a weekend arrangement if the school run is long, or waiting until next term. A provider proposing a standing arrangement for a full week is proposing what suits them.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-meydan.closingHeading: Send the week and the next deadline
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-meydan.closingBody: The useful version of searching for an IB tutor near me in Meydan is not a map. Send the school your child travels to, the subject and level, roughly what time they are home, the CAS commitments, and which of the five DP2 components is next. From those we can say whether this term wants a weekly session, a scheduled block around one deadline, or nothing yet — and if the specialist you need is not free, you get a date rather than a substitute. The first lesson is a free diagnostic with no payment and no card.

intro.heading: Why the nearest IB tutor is rarely the right one
paragraphs: A parent in Mirdif types "IB tutor near me" because proximity feels like a proxy for everything else: reliability, convenience, a person you can look in the eye. It is a reasonable instinct and it worked for a generation. The problem is what proximity costs once the subject gets narrow. The IB Diploma is not one subject taught at one level. It is six subjects, each at Higher or Standard Level, each with its own Internal Assessment, plus Theory of Knowledge and a 4,000-word Extended Essay. A student in Ghoroob taking Maths Analysis and Approaches HL, Chemistry HL and History SL needs three different specialists, not one generalist who lives eight minutes away.

Run the arithmetic on the radius. Draw a twenty-minute circle around Mirdif at four in the afternoon and you capture Al Mizhar, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej, Nad Al Hamar and part of Al Rashidiya. That is a large slice of eastern Dubai and still a small pool of adults who have taught IB Chemistry HL through a full two-year cycle, supervised an Internal Assessment against the five published criteria, and seen what a Paper 3 data-analysis question does to a student who has only practised Paper 1. Widen the circle to Dubai Festival City and Silicon Oasis and the pool grows; widen it past the city limit and the constraint disappears entirely.

That is the whole argument for online delivery, and it is an argument about supply rather than about technology. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because doing so would reintroduce the radius it just removed. Home visits are a service offered only in India. For a Mirdif family the lesson happens over live video, one-to-one, with a shared screen for working through a past-paper question and a document the student and tutor edit together between sessions.

The comparison runs the other way as well, which is the point of this page. Take the same question from Al Mizhar, from Uptown Mirdif, from a villa off Algeria Street, from an apartment in Dubai Festival City. The map changes. The school changes, sometimes from an IB continuum school to a British-curriculum school that runs IGCSE then the Diploma. The commute changes by fifteen minutes in either direction. None of that changes which specialist a Chemistry HL student needs, and none of it changes the answer to the search. The nearest community over gets the same recommendation, for the same reason.

What does change by community is logistics, and that is worth being specific about. A student at a school in Dubai Festival City who lives in Mirdif gets home later than a student walking back from a school inside Mirdif itself. A family in Al Khawaneej is further from the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road junctions that clog at five. These differences decide whether a session starts at 16:30 or 18:00, and they are real planning facts. They are not reasons to accept a tutor who has never taught the subject.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: Mirdif sits inside a cluster where the full IB continuum and the British route both have a strong presence, so a family here is often choosing between programmes rather than inside one. These are the programmes IB Gram supports for students in the eastern suburbs.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, scored 1-7 each, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the school against published criteria and moderated by the IB. UAE schools enter candidates for the May session. The Diploma is where tutoring demand concentrates, because the HL papers and the IA deadlines land in the same twelve months.
programmes.countryNote: Mirdif families reach Diploma schools in several directions: IB continuum schools inside the community, IB schools in Dubai Festival City, and British-curriculum schools in Academic City and Silicon Oasis that run the Diploma alongside A Level. A child's Diploma school and home community are often not the same place, which is the single most useful fact to tell a tutor in the first conversation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There are no public exams in most MYP years, so the signal a parent gets is a criterion profile rather than a percentage. A student can be strong on criterion A knowledge and weak on criterion C communicating, and the report will not say that in plain words.
programmes.countryNote: Eastern-suburbs parents frequently have one child in MYP and one in IGCSE at a different school, and compare two reports that are not comparable. An MYP 5 and an IGCSE grade 5 mean unrelated things. Tutoring at MYP level in Mirdif is usually about reading the criterion profile correctly before Diploma subject choices are locked in during Year 11.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examination, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Assessment is formative and descriptive, which is useful pedagogy and difficult reading for a parent who wants to know whether their child is behind in number fluency or reading age. Support at this stage is diagnostic: finding the specific gap rather than drilling a syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Mirdif has a dense primary market, with several schools drawing from the same residential streets, so cohorts shift between schools more than they do in newer communities. A child moving from a PYP school to a British-curriculum primary inside the same postcode will meet phonics and written-method expectations set out differently, and that gap is usually six to ten weeks of targeted work.

programmes.name: IGCSE and the route into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE qualifications taken at 16, graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Many eastern-suburbs students take IGCSE at a British-curriculum school and then enter the IB Diploma, which means switching from a modular, heavily past-papered assessment culture to one built on extended written work and internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-Diploma step is the most common tutoring request from the Mirdif cluster after Diploma subject help. The gap is rarely content. It is the length of answer expected, the command terms, and the fact that nobody marks an IB IA for recall. Five accredited IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or above also sit inside the Ministry of Education equivalency route, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects most often requested by families in Mirdif and the communities immediately around it. Each line says what the subject actually assesses, because that is what decides which tutor fits.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-calculus route. HL adds a Paper 3 of two extended problem-solving questions worth 20% of the grade, which is unlike anything in IGCSE. Marks go missing in the move from a correct method to a justified argument, and in the Internal Assessment where students pick a topic too large to explore in twelve to twenty pages.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work. The graphic display calculator is assumed throughout, and students lose marks for reporting an answer without the model or the degree of accuracy. HL carries its own Paper 3. Choosing AI over AA for an engineering or economics ambition needs checking against the named university's own entry page.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields and nuclear physics, with HL adding depth rather than new breadth in most topics. Paper 1 is multiple choice with no mark for method, so a careless unit conversion costs the whole item. The experimental Internal Assessment is marked on the quality of the investigation design, not on whether the result matched theory.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across physical, inorganic and organic chemistry. Organic mechanisms and the energetics calculations are the two places HL students stall. Paper 2 and Paper 3 reward precise command-term reading: explain, deduce and justify want different things, and a correct chemical fact written against the wrong command term scores nothing.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology and physiology, with HL extending into plant biology and animal physiology. Data-based questions carry heavy weight, and students who have memorised content lose marks reading an unfamiliar graph. The IA needs a measurable independent variable, which is where most weak Biology explorations fail before the writing starts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed partly through commentaries on real news articles. HL adds quantitative questions and a policy paper. Diagram accuracy carries marks on its own: an unlabelled axis or a shifted curve without an explanation of the mechanism is a predictable, avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance and marketing, with tools such as the Ansoff matrix and break-even analysis applied to case material. Students who write what a model is rather than what it shows about this firm score in the bottom bands. HL adds a research project on a real organisation of the student's choice.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary texts alongside literary works, assessed through a Paper 1 guided analysis, a Paper 2 comparative essay and an Individual Oral on a global issue. HL adds a 1,200-1,500 word essay on one studied work. The common failure is description of content where the mark scheme asks for analysis of authorial choice.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Prescribed subjects with source work in Paper 1, world history topics in Paper 2, and a regional option in HL Paper 3 of three essays in two and a half hours. The source questions have a fixed structure that rewards practice; the HL paper rewards planning speed. The Historical Investigation IA runs to 2,200 words and is marked on method as much as content.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points on the 45-point scale. TOK is assessed by an exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title; the Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a supervisor. Both are the student's own work. A tutor may teach the method, question the argument and give feedback, and may not write any part of it.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics and Sciences
subjects.description: Assessed against criteria A to D, with criterion C and D work on communication and reflection carrying as much weight as knowledge. Students who have never been taught what criterion B investigating patterns asks for will under-score while knowing the content. This is the most common diagnostic request from the Mirdif cluster below Diploma level.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Support here follows the school's own stream.

sections.heading: What "IB tutor near me" returns when you search it from Mirdif
paragraphs: Searched from a Mirdif address, the phrase returns a mixture of three things: tuition centres with premises somewhere in eastern Dubai, agency pages that list every community in the emirate including this one, and marketplace listings of individuals who have set their own radius. None of those results tells you the fact that matters, which is whether anyone in them has taught the specific subject at the specific level your child is sitting.

The honest answer to the search is that an IB tutor near me in Mirdif is, for most subjects, the wrong target. Proximity is a constraint, and a constraint always costs something. On a broad subject at a young age the cost is near zero, because many capable people can teach Year 7 maths. On IB Chemistry HL with an Internal Assessment due in eleven weeks, the cost is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available adult.

IB Gram removes the constraint by delivering every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Mirdif school run. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. What a Mirdif family gets instead is the whole pool rather than the twenty-minute slice of it, and a tutor matched to the subject and level rather than to the postcode.

The rest of this page tests that claim by comparison. It sets Mirdif against the communities next to it, prices the radius, prices the alternatives, and sets out what a tutor may and may not do with assessed work. If the comparison came out differently for Al Mizhar or Al Warqa than for Mirdif, it would say so. It does not.

sections.heading: Mirdif against the community next door, line by line
paragraphs: The eastern suburbs are not interchangeable. They differ in density, in school mix and in how long the car journey takes at the hour a tutoring session would start. The table below sets out those differences for the nine communities in this cluster, using the practical facts a tutoring plan actually turns on.

Read down the final column and the pattern is clear. What varies between Mirdif and Al Khawaneej is the hour a session can start and the school a student attends. What does not vary is the recommendation. A Chemistry HL student in Al Khawaneej needs the same kind of specialist as a Chemistry HL student in Mirdif, and neither of them is well served by a radius search.

That symmetry is why this page does not pretend Mirdif is unique. It is a well-established eastern suburb with a dense school market, good road access along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Ras Al Khor Road, and a mixed curriculum profile. Four of its neighbours could be described the same way. The differences are real and small; the subject-match problem is real and large.

One caveat on drive times: the figures below are typical weekday afternoon ranges, not promises. School-run traffic in this part of Dubai varies with the academic calendar, roadworks and the time the nearest school releases. Treat them as planning estimates and confirm against your own week. Because every UAE lesson here runs over live video, those drive times matter only for working out when a student is home and settled, not for whether a tutor can reach the door, and that is the one respect in which the comparison below is easier than it looks.

sections.heading: Pricing the radius: what a twenty-minute circle actually costs
paragraphs: A search radius is a filter, and every filter removes candidates. The question worth asking is what each ring of the circle removes. The table below describes what happens to the available pool as the radius widens from one community to no limit at all, in terms a parent can test by asking any agency the same questions.

The pattern is not linear. Going from Mirdif alone to the whole eastern cluster adds a lot, because it adds several school catchments and therefore several ex-teacher populations. Going from the cluster to the whole of Dubai adds less than you would expect, because the scarce thing is not people who tutor but people who have taught one named IB subject at one named level through a full cycle, with Internal Assessment supervision experience. Removing the geographic limit entirely is the step that changes the answer for narrow HL subjects.

There is a second cost to the radius that does not show up in a pool count: scheduling. A tutor travelling between homes in eastern Dubai can take perhaps three or four students in an afternoon, and the slots they can offer are shaped by the route rather than by your child's school release time. A tutor teaching over video can start at 16:30 for a Mirdif student and 17:30 for one in Al Khawaneej without either of them being a compromise.

The third cost is replacement. If a tutor matched on proximity stops being available, the replacement has to satisfy the same radius, which is why in-home arrangements in a single community so often end with a change of subject specialism rather than a change of tutor. An online match has a wider bench behind it.
