sections.heading: What a month of IB tuition costs around Mirdif, in AED
paragraphs: Start from the monthly number, because that is the figure a household budget is actually built on. Published market estimates for a weekly one-hour session in Dubai put a budget arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month, a mid-tier qualified subject tutor at AED 600-1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more, according to Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. Monthly packages advertised in this market include online plans from around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits.

Convert those to hourly and the bands become easier to compare against a quote. Budget online and university-student tutoring is quoted from AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel runs AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting 180-350. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are quoted at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 500-650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

Two things a Mirdif parent can verify independently. The in-home band starts higher than the online band at every tier, and the difference is not teaching quality, it is a car. And several providers in this market publish no price at all, which is worth noticing: one of the strongest pages currently ranking for Dubai IB tutoring asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it.

These are market figures, dated and attributed, not an IB Gram price list. Our own rate depends on subject, level and session length, and the trial lesson is free, so the sensible order is trial first and numbers second. Set the market bands beside Dubai school fees for context: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year.

sections.heading: Online against an in-home visit for an eastern-suburbs family
paragraphs: This is the comparison most Mirdif parents are actually running, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. An in-home visit has genuine advantages: a younger child concentrates better with an adult physically present, a parent can see what happened, and there is no device to manage. For primary-age support those advantages are real and a family who wants them should weigh them properly.

Against that, an in-home arrangement in the eastern suburbs prices travel into every hour, limits the tutor pool to whoever will drive to Al Khawaneej at five in the afternoon, and makes a mid-term replacement hard. It also tends to produce round-trip bookings of two hours, because nobody drives twenty-five minutes for a single hour, which is why the advertised in-home monthly packages are built on four two-hour visits rather than eight one-hour sessions.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, so this is not a choice we are selling either way. Home visits are an India-only service for us. What we can do is set the two models side by side on the dimensions that differ, and let a Mirdif family decide whether the trade is worth making for their child's age and subject.

For Diploma-level work the trade is usually one-sided. A Maths AA HL student working through a Paper 3 question benefits far more from a specialist who has marked that paper's style than from any seating arrangement. For a Year 4 reading intervention the calculation is different, and an honest page should say so.

sections.heading: The Diploma assessment pieces that make proximity irrelevant
paragraphs: It is worth being concrete about why subject match beats distance, rather than asserting it. Take the three assessment components that most often decide a Diploma point total and look at what help each one needs.

The Internal Assessment comes first. Every Diploma subject has one, it is marked by the school against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and it is written over months rather than in an exam hall. Useful support here is criterion literacy: knowing that a Biology exploration needs a measurable independent variable, that a Maths exploration is marked partly on personal engagement and mathematical communication, that a History investigation allocates specific marks to evaluation of sources. None of that knowledge is distributed by neighbourhood.

Second, the HL extension papers. Maths HL Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions; Physics and Chemistry Paper 3 carry data-analysis and option material; History HL Paper 3 is three essays in two and a half hours. These papers have their own technique, and the people who can teach it are those who have seen a lot of student attempts at them. In a twenty-minute radius around any single Dubai community there may be nobody who has.

Third, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, worth up to three points between them. A student loses those points to process failures far more often than to weak thinking: a prescribed title answered as a topic, a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words, a reflection written the night before. Process coaching is a teachable skill and a specialist one. The student writes the work; the tutor teaches the method and asks the hard questions about the argument.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what the inspection band means
paragraphs: A Mirdif family deals with KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. It inspects private schools annually and publishes a rating on six bands from Outstanding down to Very Weak. If your extended family lives elsewhere in the country, they deal with a different body, and the differences are substantive rather than cosmetic.

The regulator map for UAE private schools is complete and short. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate regulator does more than inspect.

What an inspection band does and does not tell a parent is worth stating plainly. It is a judgement about a school across many measures, published for a given year. It is not a prediction about one child in one HL subject. A student can be two grades below their potential in Chemistry at a school rated Outstanding, and that is the situation tutoring addresses. Read the band as context and the subject report as the signal.

On our own status, the position is simple and we will not blur it. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. We do not hold one and we do not claim one.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: This matters more in the IB than in most systems, because so much of the grade is coursework the student produces away from an exam hall. The IB treats the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay as the student's own work, and a breach is handled as malpractice. The consequence falls on the student, not on whoever helped. Any parent in Mirdif comparing providers should treat this as a screening question.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. Teach the subject content the assessment rests on. Explain the published criteria and what each one is asking for. Discuss whether a proposed topic is viable at this length. Question a research question that cannot be answered with the data available. Read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is under-served and why. Teach referencing. Help plan backwards from the school's deadline. Ask the uncomfortable question about an argument that does not hold.

What a tutor may not do is write, redraft to completion, or supply text that ends up in the submission. There are operations in this market that sell completed Internal Assessments outright, at prices around AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and a page that offers it is telling you what it is. We will not produce assessed work for a student at any price, and we will say so in the first conversation.

The practical version for a Mirdif family: ask the provider directly whether they will write an IA. A provider who hedges has answered. A provider who says no, and then explains what they will do instead, has given you something you can rely on when a deadline gets close and the temptation gets real.

sections.heading: Starting from Mirdif: the honest sequence
paragraphs: The first step is not booking. It is writing down what you already know, because that is what makes a match accurate rather than approximate. The school, the programme year, the six Diploma subjects with HL and SL marked, the most recent subject report or predicted grades, the IA deadlines the school has published, and the earliest time your child is realistically home and able to think. Six lines of information remove most of the guesswork.

Then the trial. A free trial lesson exists so that a specific tutor and a specific student can test whether they work together on a specific topic, which is not something a profile page can tell you. Pick a real topic that is currently causing trouble rather than a general introduction, and ask for the tutor's read on it afterwards. If the read is vague, the match is wrong and should be changed without ceremony.

On availability, the honest position rather than the comfortable one. Mainstream Diploma subjects at SL and HL are usually matched quickly. Niche Higher Level options, some second languages and certain IA supervision requests take longer, and in those cases the right answer is a wait of a few days for the correct specialist rather than an immediate match with someone approximately qualified. If nobody suitable is free, we will say that instead of filling the slot.

Finally, timing. Support started in the term before an assessment does more than the same number of hours bought in the fortnight before it. That is not a scarcity line, it is how coursework and exam technique actually improve. If you are reading this in the week before a mock, start anyway, and use the sessions on technique and on the specific papers rather than on rebuilding a topic from the beginning.

faqs.question: How far does a tutor have to live from Mirdif for it to matter?
faqs.answer: For an online lesson, not at all. Distance matters only when somebody has to travel, and nobody does: lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. What matters instead is time zone compatibility, so that a 16:30 or 18:00 slot works at both ends, and subject match. A tutor two streets away who has never taught Chemistry HL is a worse choice than a specialist who is not in Dubai at all. The question worth asking a provider is not where the tutor sits but how many full two-year cycles of your child's exact subject and level they have taught.

faqs.question: Is there any IB subject I cannot get help with from Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Mainstream Diploma subjects at both levels are matched routinely: the two Maths routes, the three sciences, English A, Economics, Business Management, History, Geography and Psychology. Harder to cover quickly are some second languages at Higher Level, a few smaller Group 6 arts options, and certain niche HL options within the sciences. For those the honest answer is a wait of several days for the right specialist rather than an immediate match with someone approximately qualified. If nobody suitable is available, we will tell you that rather than fill the slot and hope.

faqs.question: Does my child in Uptown Mirdif need a different tutor from one in Al Warqa?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the main finding of this page. The two students differ in what time they get home and often in which school they attend. They do not differ in what Maths AA HL requires, what the Internal Assessment criteria ask for, or how Paper 3 is marked. The tutoring recommendation comes out identical: match on subject and level, schedule around the real return time. The only practical consequence of the address is the session slot, which is why we ask for the earliest realistic start rather than assuming one.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson realistically start on a Mirdif school night?
faqs.answer: For a student at a school inside Mirdif, 16:30 is usually workable. For one travelling back from Dubai Festival City, 16:45 to 17:00 is more honest. For a student returning from Academic City or Silicon Oasis, 17:15 or later. These are planning estimates from typical weekday afternoon traffic in the eastern suburbs, not promises, and they shift with roadworks and the school's release time. Pick the slot from what your week actually looks like rather than from the earliest time that sounds efficient, because a session a tired child arrives late to is worth less than one half an hour later.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home rate higher in the eastern suburbs than the online rate?
faqs.answer: Because a car is priced into the hour. Published market figures for Dubai put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200-450 and above for a specialist, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table and the providers' own pages. In-home bookings also tend to be two hours rather than one, since few tutors drive twenty-five minutes to Al Khawaneej for sixty minutes, which is why advertised in-home monthly packages are built on four two-hour visits at AED 1,599-1,799.

faqs.question: My child is at an IB school in Dubai Festival City but we live in Mirdif. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes the session time and nothing else. Tell the tutor both facts at the start: the school sets the assessment calendar, the internal deadlines and the teaching sequence, while home sets when your child can concentrate. A student doing two car journeys a day arrives home later and more tired, so a 17:00 start on two weekdays often works better than an earlier slot on three. The school's published IA deadlines matter more than the distance between the two places, and those are the dates a session plan should be built backwards from.

faqs.question: How many IB subjects should a Mirdif family start tutoring at once?
faqs.answer: One or two. A Diploma student is already carrying six subjects, the core and whatever else their week holds, and three weekly tutoring sessions on top of that tends to produce attendance rather than progress. Start with the subject where the gap is largest or the stakes are highest, usually a Higher Level subject with an Internal Assessment due. Add a second only once the first has a rhythm. If three subjects genuinely look weak, that is often a study-method or workload problem rather than three content problems, and the trial lesson is a good place to test which it is.

faqs.question: What should a Mirdif parent send before a first lesson?
faqs.answer: Six things, and they take a few minutes to gather. The school name and programme year. The six Diploma subjects with Higher and Standard Level marked. The most recent subject report or set of predicted grades. The school's published Internal Assessment and coursework deadlines. Any past paper or piece of marked work that shows where marks were lost. And the earliest time your child is home and able to think. That last one is the item parents most often leave out and the one that decides whether a weekly slot survives the term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Internal Assessment for them?
faqs.answer: No. An Internal Assessment is marked by the school against the published criteria and moderated by the IB, and the work must be the student's own. A tutor can teach the subject content, explain what each criterion is asking for, test whether a topic is viable at the required length, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is under-served, and teach referencing. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it to completion, or supply text for it. Breaches are treated as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, which is why the line is absolute rather than negotiable.

faqs.question: Does a Mirdif school's KHDA inspection band tell me whether tutoring is needed?
faqs.answer: Not directly. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a rating across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. That is a judgement about a whole school for a given year, across many measures. It says little about one student in one Higher Level subject. Children are two grades below their potential at highly rated schools, and children thrive at schools rated in the middle of the scale. Read the band as context about the institution and read the subject report, the marked papers and the predicted grades as the signal about your child.

faqs.question: Do we need to check a MoHRE permit before hiring a tutor in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question to ask any individual tutor in the UAE. Private tutoring is regulated by permit: the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

faqs.question: Will the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons clash with IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: They occupy timetable space, which is worth planning around rather than fighting. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. If one of these subjects is itself the weak point, support follows the school's own stream rather than a parallel syllabus.

faqs.question: Is a Mirdif tuition centre group class cheaper than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: Usually yes per head, and that is the honest trade-off. A group class spreads the cost across several students and spreads the attention the same way, which works when the whole group needs the same broad revision at the same pace. It works poorly when one student's problem is a specific gap, a particular Internal Assessment, or Higher Level paper technique, because the class cannot stop for one person. Centres with premises in Dubai also operate under a different regulatory regime from individual tutors, including the KHDA permit route for training institutes. Compare on what your child's actual problem is, not on the hourly figure alone.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the HL subject we need?
faqs.answer: We say so. The alternative is matching a student to someone approximately qualified and letting the family find out in week three, which costs more than a wait does. In practice the options are a short wait of a few days for the right person, a start on a related subject where the need is also real, or a recommendation to look elsewhere if the gap is one we cannot cover at all. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is exactly why a parent should ask for one before paying for anything.

IB Gram delivers that match one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Send the school, the six subjects with their levels, the latest report and your earliest realistic slot, and take a free trial lesson on a topic that is genuinely going wrong.

intro.heading: The question is not who is near you. It is when the session starts
paragraphs: Parents in this district who search for a tutor nearby are usually solving a timetable problem rather than a shortage problem. There are Diploma teachers in Dubai. What there is not, on a Tuesday in October, is a free hour between the end of the school day and the point at which a sixteen-year-old stops being able to think. Everything useful about tutoring happens inside that window, and the window here is narrower than most families expect.

Work it through. School days at the schools serving this district end between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm. A student at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba can be home within twenty minutes. A student at a school in Al Barsha, Al Quoz or Al Safa is in the afternoon traffic, and the last stretch into a gated villa community adds to it, so arrival between 3:45pm and 4:15pm is realistic rather than pessimistic. Then subtract CAS commitments, school sport, music and the hour a Diploma student needs simply to stop.

What remains is roughly 4pm to 8pm, and not all of it is equal. A session at four meets a tired student who has just travelled. A session at five meets one who has eaten and settled. A session at seven meets one with homework still to do and the prospect of working past ten, which is how a well-intentioned tutoring arrangement starts costing a student sleep and then costs them the grade it was meant to protect.

This is where a near-me search quietly makes things worse. The tutors who answer it are the ones willing to drive here, and a tutor driving here is in exactly the same traffic as your child. A tutor who leaves Al Barsha at four arrives between a quarter to five and a quarter past, which pushes the session later and compresses the evening further. The journey is not a detail in the arrangement; it is the thing that decides which hour your child is taught in.

IB Gram removes the journey. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the session starts when the student is home and settled rather than when a tutor has cleared the gate. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below set out the timing school by school, what each hour of the evening is good for, how the Diploma week actually loads, and what to do in mock season and Ramadan.

Nothing on this page promises a grade. It sets out the one variable a household controls completely, which is the hour the session happens in, and shows what that hour is worth. Families who fix the time first and choose the tutor second get more from four sessions a month than families who do it the other way round get from eight, and it costs nothing to arrange in that order.

The practical consequence for scheduling is that a Diploma session has to replace homework time rather than being added to it, which means the tutor should be setting less work than the student would otherwise have done, not more. A session that pushes a student past ten at night is a net loss.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from this district attend schools across the central corridor, so the end of the school day and the length of the journey home vary household by household rather than community by community. That is why we ask for the school name and the finishing time before proposing a slot.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with the Personal Project in the final year, and a lighter but less predictable workload: an MYP task can arrive with a fortnight's notice and absorb three evenings. For scheduling, that argues for a session early in the week so the work set has somewhere to go, and for a fixed slot rather than one that moves around school deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students here are often younger siblings of Diploma students, which creates a scheduling collision in the same household: two children needing the same four-hour window. Sequencing them on different evenings works better than stacking them, and we will say so when the request arrives.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The age where timing matters most and tutoring matters least. A primary child is at their best immediately after a short rest and is finished by half past five, which gives a genuinely narrow window. Short sessions of thirty or forty minutes work better than an hour, and a defined block beats an open-ended arrangement at any time of day.
programmes.countryNote: Villa districts with young families attract a lot of local supply aimed at primary ages, often scheduled late because that is when a tutor finishes elsewhere. A seven-year-old taught at half past six is being taught at the wrong time, and no amount of tutor quality compensates for that.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mohammed-bin-r.subjectsIntro: Some subjects survive a late slot better than others, which is a practical scheduling fact rather than a judgement about difficulty. These are the courses we cover for this district, noted for when in the evening they work best.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs the student alert, because the work is timed practice and non-calculator drill rather than discussion. Best placed early in the window, and a poor choice for a seven o'clock slot after a full school day.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Slightly more forgiving late because the modelling and interpretation work is discursive, but calculator practice still needs concentration. Early to middle of the window is the sensible placement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy sections need an alert student; investigation feedback and criteria discussion survive a later slot well. Worth splitting the two kinds of work across different weeks rather than different hours.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving work needs the early window. Definitions, uncertainty discussion and practical write-up feedback are manageable later, which makes Physics unusually schedulable if the tutor plans for it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most forgiving science for a later slot, because much of the work is terminology precision and command-term practice, which is discussion-led rather than computation-led.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram work and evaluation practice both work reasonably late, which is useful in a household competing for the early window with a maths session for a sibling.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis discussion and Individual Oral preparation are well suited to a later slot. Timed writing is not, and should be placed early or set as practice between sessions instead.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study analysis survives a late slot better than most, which makes it a sensible subject to place second when two children share one evening window.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Discussion-led and genuinely fine late in the evening, which is fortunate because tutors who cover it are scarce and their available hours are often the ones nobody else wants.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Question-narrowing and draft feedback are conversations rather than exercises, so they fit anywhere in the window. The reading and writing happen in the student's own time regardless.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mohammed-bin-r.regionsTitle: Mohammed Bin Rashid City, and where its students actually go to school
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mohammed-bin-r.regionsIntro: Scheduling from this district depends on which school a child attends rather than which community they live in. These notes describe the journey each direction implies.

regions.name: District One
regions.note: Large plots and gated access, so the final stretch home adds time even once the main road is clear. A student at a nearby school is still home by about 3:15pm; one from the west is not.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Two schools inside the community, so some students walk home and are ready by three o'clock. The earliest genuine session start available anywhere in this district.

regions.name: Meydan
regions.note: Shares schools with this district and sits on the same road network. A session at four is realistic for students at local schools and not for those travelling from Al Barsha.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Established schools a short drive south, which is the easiest direction from here at the end of the school day. Students at these schools are typically home within twenty minutes.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Several schools and the corridor's tuition centres, reachable in fifteen minutes off-peak and considerably more at three o'clock when every school in the area releases at once.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Barsha
regions.note: The western school cluster, and the longest routine journey for students from this district. Arrival home between 3:45pm and 4:15pm is normal rather than unlucky.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: IB continuum provision near the creek crossings, a moderate run from here. Students at these schools generally manage a four o'clock start without difficulty.

schoolClusters.city: Inside and immediately around the district
schoolClusters.note: The schools whose students can realistically start a session at four o'clock, because the journey home is short or non-existent. For a household choosing between schools, this is a scheduling consideration most prospectuses never mention.

schoolClusters.city: The western and northern cluster
schoolClusters.note: The schools whose students from this district are in the afternoon traffic, which pushes the earliest workable session towards half past four. Worth knowing before fixing a weekly slot that will be missed every other week.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mohammed-bin-r.modesIntro: Three formats, all one-to-one and online, described here by when they fit rather than only by what they cover. For a household with a narrow evening window, placement in the week matters as much as content.

modes.title: Fixed weekly slot
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same hour every week, chosen from the student's actual availability rather than the tutor's convenience. A fixed slot survives a Diploma year better than a flexible one, because a flexible arrangement is renegotiated every week and eventually stops being renegotiated at all. Early in the week is usually better, so practice set has somewhere to go.
bullets: Same hour weekly, set from the end of the school day
Early in the week where possible, so practice has room

modes.title: Twin-session evening for two children
modes.description: Where two children in the household both need support, two consecutive sessions in one evening, with the subject that tolerates a later slot placed second. This keeps the rest of the week clear and avoids both children losing their best hour. It only works if the subjects are chosen with the clock in mind, which is the point of the subject notes on this page.

modes.title: Weekend intensive block
modes.description: For a pre-examination period or a student whose weekday evenings are genuinely full, two longer sessions at the weekend instead of weekday slots. A Saturday morning session reaches a rested student, which for timed paper practice is worth more than two tired weekday hours. It also sidesteps the traffic question entirely.

sections.heading: When a session can actually start, school by school
paragraphs: The useful version of this page is a timing table, because the answer differs by school rather than by community. A student at a school inside the district and a student at a school in Al Barsha live on the same street and have evenings that begin forty minutes apart. Any scheduling advice that ignores that is advice about somebody else's child.

The table works from a simple chain: when the school day ends, how long the journey home takes at that hour, how long a student needs before they can work, and therefore when a session realistically begins. The third element is the one families skip. A sixteen-year-old who has been in school since half past seven needs twenty minutes and something to eat before they are any use, and a session that starts the moment they walk in buys an hour of a student who is physically present and mentally elsewhere.

The right-hand column gives the in-home comparison, which is the part a near-me search never shows. A tutor travelling from the city's teaching concentrations is in the same traffic, plus the gated access at this end, so the in-home start is consistently later than the online one. For a student at a nearby school the difference is around forty-five minutes. For a student travelling from the west, the in-home session is pushed towards five o'clock, which is the hour the evening cannot really spare.

Use the table to set the slot before you choose the tutor, not after. Decide which hour your child can genuinely work in, then ask who is available then. Doing it the other way round is how a household ends up with an excellent tutor in an hour that does not work, and then concludes after two terms that tutoring does not help.

table.caption: FROM THE END OF THE SCHOOL DAY TO THE START OF A SESSION
rows: Further west or on the Marina side
Any school, with a CAS or sport commitment

sections.heading: What each hour of the evening is good for
paragraphs: Not all of the four o'clock to eight o'clock window is interchangeable, and treating it as though it is explains a lot of disappointing tutoring. A student's capacity changes across the evening in a predictable way, and matching the kind of work to the hour produces more from the same number of sessions without costing anything.

The first hour after a student has eaten and settled is the best one, and it should be used for whatever requires sustained concentration: timed paper practice, non-calculator maths, problem solving, anything where the clock is part of the exercise. This is also the hour most households give away, because it is the hour a tutor driving across Dubai cannot reach.

The middle of the window suits teaching: new content, worked examples, criteria explained, a marked script gone through question by question. The student is awake, the pressure is off, and absorbing an explanation is easier than producing work under time. The last hour of the window suits discussion: Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay question, essay planning, anything where talking is the work. It does not suit timed practice, and a tutor who sets a timed paper at half past seven is wasting the paper.

The practical application is to choose the slot and the subject together. A household with one early slot and two children should put maths in it and put the discursive subject later. A student with CAS on Tuesdays should have their timed-practice subject on Monday. None of this is complicated and almost nobody does it, because the slot is usually set by the tutor's diary rather than by the student's capacity.

sections.heading: How a Diploma week actually loads, and where tutoring fits
paragraphs: A Diploma student's week is fuller than the timetable suggests, and a tutoring plan that ignores the load either fails or displaces something that mattered. Six subjects generate homework on most evenings. CAS has to actually happen rather than being recorded. Internal assessment deadlines cluster, and the Extended Essay sits somewhere in the background becoming more urgent.

The consequence for scheduling is that a tutoring session should replace work rather than add to it. If a tutor sets ninety minutes of practice on top of a full evening of school homework, the student does one or the other, and usually they do the school work because that is what gets collected. A good tutor asks what the school has set this week and sizes the practice to fit inside the evening the student has, which sometimes means setting very little.

That also argues against two tutoring sessions a week in one subject, which is a common purchase in districts where it is affordable. A student already carrying six subjects does not have two spare hours of attention for one of them, and the second session tends to become supervised homework rather than teaching. One well-placed session with proportionate practice does more, and it leaves the week intact.

The table below sets out a plausible week for a DP2 student in this district, with the tutoring slot placed rather than added. It is an illustration rather than a prescription, and the point is the method: map the fixed commitments first, find the hour that is genuinely free and genuinely usable, and put the session there.

sections.heading: Mock season, Ramadan and the weeks the plan has to bend
paragraphs: A weekly slot that works in October will not work in every week of the year, and a tutoring arrangement that cannot bend gets abandoned instead. Three periods reliably break a fixed schedule in this district, and all three are predictable far enough ahead to plan for rather than react to.

Mock season is the first. During mocks, a student's evenings are consumed by the next morning's paper, and the most valuable session of the entire year is the one immediately after the results, spent marking the script question by question with the student. The weeks during mocks are often best paused; the week after should be booked in advance, because everyone else wants it too.

Ramadan is the second, and online delivery handles it in a way an in-home arrangement cannot. Sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, which works precisely because there is no journey to renegotiate at either end, and a student who has fasted is better served by a later session than an afternoon one. Agree the shift in advance rather than week by week, so the slot is held rather than lost.

Travel is the third. Households in this district travel, often for extended periods, and an online session follows the student rather than the address. The one thing to settle in advance is the time zone the session is pinned to, so a student in Europe or India is not sitting a Higher Level lesson at six in the morning. A session that follows the family is the difference between a two-week gap and no gap at all.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session, in weeks rather than months
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and the scheduling version of counting backwards is more useful than the spending version for a household whose problem is the clock. The question is not only when to start but how many usable hours remain between now and the session, which is a smaller number than the calendar suggests once school holidays, mocks and internal deadlines are removed.

Two cautions. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, including internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines, which are the ones that actually constrain an evening. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including this one, and treat an internal deadline as firm from the moment it is announced.

The table counts backwards in terms of what the evenings are doing rather than what the IB is doing. Read it to see where the free weeks actually are, because that is where a block of sessions can be placed without displacing school work. Most households discover they have fewer genuinely usable weeks than they assumed and that the usable ones are earlier than they expected.

The practical conclusion is to book the scarce weeks early. The week after the DP2 mock is the single most valuable tutoring week of the year in this district, and it is the one every family wants. A household that books it in October gets it; one that asks for it in February is choosing from what is left, which is a quality cost rather than a price one.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and why the timetable is fuller than it looks
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a household here the departmental commentary inside a report is more useful than the band, and it is also a free second opinion on whether a weak grade reflects the student or the teaching.

The scheduling point is the mandatory UAE subjects, which run alongside the Diploma rather than instead of it and which families new to Dubai consistently underestimate. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Instructional time for those subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. The practical effect for a Diploma student is fewer free periods in the school day than the programme on paper implies, which means more work comes home and the evening window is doing more than a parent assumes when they plan two tutoring sessions a week.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. KHDA separately requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question for a school rather than for a tutoring service.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why a late session makes it worse
paragraphs: There is a connection between scheduling and integrity that nobody in this market mentions. A student working at half past ten on an internal assessment due the next morning is the student most likely to accept help they should not accept, and at least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. The pressure that makes that offer attractive is built out of evenings that were overcommitted weeks earlier.

The boundary itself is fixed regardless of the hour. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the language the examiner uses, question a research question until it is answerable with the resources available, warn that a method will generate too little data, teach the underlying content, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. That is substantial help and it is the help worth paying for.

What a tutor may not do is choose the question, supply the method or the data, write any part of the text, or edit a draft into its final form, nor hand over a worked example close enough to the student's own task that copying becomes the obvious step. We state this to the student in the first session rather than in small print, because the pressure arrives later and a boundary explained under deadline is a boundary explained too late.

The scheduling remedy is to protect the deadline weeks rather than to fill them. Internal assessment weeks should have no tutoring in them at all, with the question-narrowing session placed well before and the draft-feedback session placed early enough to be acted on. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the official source.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what we ask before proposing a slot
paragraphs: Three pieces of information decide the slot, and we ask for them before proposing anyone. Which school your child attends and what time the day ends. What fixed commitments exist in the week, including CAS, sport and music. And which evening, in your judgement, your child could actually work in. The third is a parent's answer rather than ours, and it is usually right.

Then the subject, the level, the latest grade and the teacher's last comment quoted rather than summarised, with a photograph of a marked paper if you have one. That tells us who to propose. The slot and the tutor are separate decisions and should be made in that order, because an excellent tutor in an unusable hour produces nothing and leaves a household believing the problem was the teaching.

We run a free trial lesson, and we run it at the time you would actually use rather than at a convenient showcase hour. That matters: a trial at eleven on a Saturday tells you nothing about whether your child can work with this person at half past four on a Wednesday. Afterwards, ask for a written account of what is costing marks, and ask the tutor whether the slot felt right for the work.

And the honest part. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time hours this district wants are the first to fill, and the week after mock results is the most contested week in the year. When the hour you want is not available we say so and offer an alternative hour, a different evening, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time. We will not take a booking for a slot we cannot hold, and the trial lesson is free so asking costs nothing.

process.title: Tell us the school and the finishing time
process.description: The end of the school day plus the journey home decides the earliest workable slot, and it varies by forty minutes or more between schools serving this district. Without it any proposed time is a guess dressed up as a recommendation.

process.title: List the fixed commitments
process.description: CAS, school sport, music and anything else that cannot move. We schedule around them rather than asking a student to drop them, because a tutoring slot that competes with a commitment loses, and then the arrangement quietly lapses.

process.title: Choose the hour before the tutor
process.description: Decide which hour your child can genuinely work in, then ask who is available then. Doing it the other way round produces an excellent tutor in an unusable slot, which is how households conclude that tutoring does not work for their child.

process.title: Match the subject to the hour
process.description: Timed practice and non-calculator maths need the early window; discussion work, essay planning and Theory of Knowledge survive a later one. Where two children share an evening, the discursive subject goes second.

process.title: Free trial at the slot you would use
process.description: We run the trial lesson in the hour you intend to book, not a convenient showcase time. A Saturday trial says nothing about a Wednesday at half past four, which is the hour your child will actually have to work in.

process.title: Book the scarce weeks in advance
process.description: The week after DP2 mock results is the most valuable and most contested tutoring week of the year. A household that books it in October gets it; one that asks in February chooses from what is left.

whyPoints.title: Timing worked out, not assumed
whyPoints.description: We publish the chain from the end of the school day through the journey home to the earliest workable start, school cluster by school cluster. No other page in this market treats the clock as the binding constraint, which for a Diploma household it usually is.

whyPoints.title: No journey at either end
whyPoints.description: An online session starts when the student is home and settled rather than when a tutor has cleared afternoon traffic and gated access. For a student at a western school that is three quarters of an hour of the best part of the evening.

whyPoints.title: The subject matched to the hour
whyPoints.description: Timed practice in the early window, teaching in the middle, discussion late. It costs nothing to get right and it produces more from the same number of sessions, which is why we ask about the week before proposing a slot.

whyPoints.title: Practice sized to the evening
whyPoints.description: A session should replace homework time rather than be added to it. A tutor who sets ninety minutes on top of a full evening has guaranteed that the student does one or the other, and it will not be ours.

whyPoints.title: Deadline weeks protected
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment weeks get no tutoring at all, with question-narrowing placed well before and draft feedback early enough to act on. Filling those weeks is how deadline pressure turns into an integrity problem.

whyPoints.title: A trial at the real hour

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start from this district?
faqs.answer: Online, between 3:45pm and 4:45pm depending on the school. A student at a school inside the district can be home by just after three and settled by a quarter to four. One travelling from Al Safa or Al Barsha is often not home until a quarter past four, which makes half past the earliest honest start. With an in-home tutor add roughly forty-five minutes at every point in that range, because the tutor is in the same afternoon traffic plus the gated access at this end.

faqs.question: Why does a nearby tutor still arrive late?
faqs.answer: Because nearby is measured in distance and the problem is time. A tutor driving from the city's teaching concentrations leaves at four and meets the same school-run traffic your child did, then adds the final stretch into a gated villa community where the last two kilometres can take as long as the previous twelve. The result is an arrival between a quarter to five and a quarter past, which pushes the session into the hour the evening cannot spare and compresses everything after it.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to the house in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We say so plainly because near me is the phrase parents search. For a household here the practical gain from online delivery is the forty-five minutes at the start of the evening, which is the part of the evening a student can actually concentrate in, plus a session that can move inside the same week without anyone wasting a journey.

faqs.question: Is four o'clock too early, straight after the school run?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the fix is twenty minutes rather than an hour. A student who has been in school since half past seven needs to arrive, eat something and stop before they are any use, so a session starting the moment they walk in buys an hour of someone physically present and mentally elsewhere. Build the gap in deliberately. For most students the best hour of the evening is the one that begins twenty to thirty minutes after they get home, and it is the hour most households give away.

faqs.question: Which subjects work in a late slot and which do not?
faqs.answer: Discussion-led work survives a late session well: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay question-narrowing, essay planning, English analysis, Business Management case study work. Anything where the clock is part of the exercise does not, which means timed paper practice, non-calculator mathematics and problem-solving physics belong in the early window. If a tutor sets a timed paper at half past seven they are wasting the paper, and that is a scheduling error rather than a teaching one.

faqs.question: We have two children who both need tutoring. How do we fit both in?
faqs.answer: Two consecutive sessions on one evening, with the more discursive subject placed second, keeps the rest of the week clear and avoids both children losing their best hour. Separate tutors, not a shared session, because year groups and weaknesses differ and a shared hour leaves each child idle for half of it. The alternative is different evenings, which works well when one child's subject genuinely needs the early window and the other's does not.

faqs.question: Should we add a second weekly session in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A Diploma student already carries six subjects, three core components and homework on most evenings, so there are rarely two spare hours of genuine attention for one subject. The second session tends to become supervised homework at the same rate as teaching. One well-placed session with practice sized to fit the evening does more. The exception is a bounded pre-examination block of six to ten weeks, where the intensity is justified because the window is short.

faqs.question: What happens to the schedule during mock exams?
faqs.answer: Pause during, book the week after. While mocks are running a student's evenings belong to the next morning's paper, and a tutoring session competes with revision that is more urgent. The week immediately after results is the single most valuable tutoring week of the year, because there is a marked script to work from, and it is also the most contested week in this district. Book it in advance rather than asking for it when the results arrive.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the tutoring timetable?
faqs.answer: Sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, which works precisely because online delivery means no journey to renegotiate at either end. A student who has been fasting is better served later in the evening than in the afternoon, and the shift is worth agreeing in advance so the slot is held rather than released to another family. School timings also change during Ramadan, so the chain from the end of the school day to the start of a session needs recalculating rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue while we are travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for households here that travel for extended periods it is one of the clearer advantages of online delivery. The lesson follows the student rather than the address, so a fortnight away need not cost a fortnight of a subject. The single thing to settle in advance is which time zone the session is pinned to, so a student in Europe or India is not sitting a Higher Level lesson at six in the morning, and tell us early enough that the slot can be held.

faqs.question: Are weekend sessions better than weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: For timed paper practice, often yes. A Saturday morning reaches a rested student, and ninety minutes of properly timed work then is worth more than two tired weekday hours. It also sidesteps the traffic question entirely. The drawback is that a weekend slot is easier to cancel than a weekday routine, so it works best as a bounded block before an examination session rather than as a permanent arrangement, with weekday evenings kept for school work.

faqs.question: Why is the school timetable fuller than the Diploma suggests?
faqs.answer: Because the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The effect is fewer free periods, so more work comes home and the evening is already doing more than a parent assumes.

faqs.question: Should we book tutoring during internal assessment deadline weeks?
faqs.answer: No, and protecting those weeks is the more useful intervention. Internal assessment deadlines cluster across subjects and sit near the Extended Essay deadline, so those evenings are already full. The question-narrowing session belongs well before the work starts, and draft feedback belongs early enough to be acted on. Adding sessions during the crunch produces a tired student and, at worst, the deadline pressure in which students accept help they should not accept.

faqs.question: When should we start if the examination session is two terms away?
faqs.answer: Now, lightly, and build in. Two terms is a workable amount of time, and the sequence that works is a diagnosed weakness addressed weekly through the first term, then a bounded intensive block of six to ten weeks before the session. School holidays are the most underused usable weeks in the year and are worth a short catch-up block. What fails is nothing for two terms followed by a large open-ended commitment made in the month with least room for it.

faqs.question: What if the hour we need is already taken?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than booking a slot we cannot hold. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time hours this district wants fill first, and the week after mock results is the most contested of the year. intro.heading: Three things proximity genuinely helps with, and five it does not
paragraphs: A proximity search is not irrational. There are real things that being nearby helps with, and they are worth naming before the argument against distance is made. A tutor who lives in Motor City can sit in the room with a nine-year-old who cannot yet manage a screen. They can be there within an hour in an emergency. And they know the local schools socially, which occasionally produces useful context about a particular teacher or a particular cohort.

What proximity does not help with is longer. It does not tell you whether the tutor has taught Economics at Higher Level, or marked a historical investigation, or seen a Paper 3 mark scheme. It does not tell you whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit that UAE law requires. It does not tell you which provider model you are buying from, which determines who employs the tutor, who replaces them if the match fails, and who you complain to. It does not tell you whether your child is simply short of a grade or at risk of a condition that stops the Diploma being awarded at all. And it does not tell you what the hourly figure actually includes.

Those five are all checkable, and this page is organised around checking them. It sets out the six Diploma subject groups so a request can be made precisely. It explains the Diploma award conditions, because a student with a grade 1 in one subject has a different problem from a student eight points short. It compares provider models on features a parent can verify. It quotes the permit position from MoHRE's own published rules. And it gives the Dubai rate bands with the provider and the month attached to each.

Motor City's own position in this market is worth stating. GEMS Metropole School sits inside the community and runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so there is no Diploma cohort here at all. Diploma students commute out across the Dubailand corridor, which means the local pool of people who have taught the Diploma is not thin — it is close to nonexistent. A proximity search in this postcode is sorting a list that barely contains the thing being searched for, which is why the rest of this page spends its time on filters that do have something to sort.

Teaching for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. We say so at the top because the alternative is letting a family book and then discover it, which is the most common complaint in this market.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each of six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1-7. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service complete the core, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE combination. UAE candidates sit the May session; no IB session or results dates appear on this page because ibo.org blocks automated verification and your Diploma coordinator holds the real calendar.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.description: A student may take individual Diploma courses and receive certificates for them without pursuing the full Diploma. The subjects are identical and graded the same way; what is absent is the core requirement and the award conditions. For some students this is a deliberate and sensible choice rather than a fallback, particularly where a university route asks for named subjects rather than a Diploma total.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools handle course candidacy differently and some will not offer it, so the policy question belongs with your Diploma coordinator early in DP1. For a family in Motor City weighing it, the practical point is that the tutoring need is identical — the same papers, the same internal assessments — but the core pressure disappears.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, scored from 0 to 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade, with the Personal Project in the final year. Assessment is internal and continuous, so there is no external session and no award conditions of the Diploma kind. The subject-group structure here is broader than the Diploma's and students take all eight.

The step from eight MYP subject groups to six Diploma subjects is itself a decision, and it is made at the same point the Higher Level choices are made.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-motor-city.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects requested from the Motor City area, organised by the group each sits in. Naming the group is what makes a tutoring request precise, because the assessment shape is similar within a group and very different across groups.

subjects.name: Group 1: English A Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided analysis of unseen non-literary text; Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works; the Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract. Higher Level adds a 1,200-1,500 word essay. Extract choice decides the Individual Oral before a word is spoken.

subjects.name: Group 2: Spanish or French B
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a written task in a specified text type, so register and format carry marks independently of grammatical accuracy. Paper 2 covers listening and reading. The individual oral uses a visual stimulus at Standard Level and a literary extract at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Group 3: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams score separately from the prose around them: axes labelled, curves shifted, new equilibrium marked. Three commentaries of 800 words each, built on real published articles, are internally assessed. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper where arithmetic slips cost more than theory gaps.

subjects.name: Group 3: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is source-based and rewards provenance analysis rather than summary; Paper 2 is comparative essay work. Higher Level adds three essays in 150 minutes on a regional option. The historical investigation is internally assessed with a school deadline in DP1 or early DP2.

subjects.name: Group 3: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be named, dated and evaluated rather than described. The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experiment with full statistical treatment, and students routinely propose a study they cannot ethically or practically replicate in a school setting.

subjects.name: Group 4: Biology
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36% covers multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 at 44% is extended response, and the scientific investigation is 20%. Content volume is the difficulty, and answer length matched to the mark allocation is the cheapest habit to fix.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route with Paper 1 sat without a calculator; Applications and Interpretation is calculator-permitted and statistics-led. The Exploration is 20% at both levels on both courses. Several degree routes specify Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Group 6: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Three assessed components: the comparative study, the process portfolio and the exhibition. All three are internally generated work with school deadlines spread across two years, and the process portfolio is where students who make strong final pieces most often lose marks.

subjects.name: Group 6 alternative: a second Group 3 or 4 subject
subjects.description: Students may replace the Group 6 arts subject with a second subject from Groups 1 to 4. This is the most common choice among students heading to science or economics degrees, and it changes the internal assessment load substantially because arts components are replaced by a second investigation.

subjects.name: The core: TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS
subjects.description: The TOK essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title and the exhibition is three objects with a 950-word commentary. The Extended Essay has a 4,000-word limit. CAS is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded, which makes it an award condition rather than an optional extra.

sections.heading: The six subject groups, and why naming the group makes a better request
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes six subjects, one from each of six groups, with an option to replace the Group 6 arts subject with a second subject from Groups 1 to 4. Three are at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. The structure matters for a tutoring request because the assessment shape is broadly consistent within a group and very different between groups, so 'my child needs help with their essay subject' is a much weaker request than 'my child needs help with a Group 3 internal assessment'.

Within Group 3, individuals and societies, the pattern is source handling, argument construction and an internally assessed investigation. Within Group 4, the sciences, it is a 36% paper of multiple choice and data analysis, a 44% extended-response paper, and a 20% investigation. Group 5 mathematics has its Exploration at 20% and, at Higher Level, a third paper. Group 6 arts is almost entirely internally generated work with school deadlines spread across two years.

The practical consequence is that the right tutor is often identified by component rather than by subject. A student losing marks on source provenance in History and a student losing marks on source provenance in a Group 3 option are being assessed on the same skill, and a tutor who has taught either can usually help with the other. Conversely, a tutor strong on Group 4 investigations may be no use at all on a Group 6 process portfolio even though both are internally assessed.

This is also where the Group 6 substitution decision belongs. Replacing the arts subject with a second science or a second Group 3 subject is the common choice for students heading to science, medicine or economics degrees, and it changes the internal assessment load materially: an arts process portfolio and exhibition are replaced by a second investigation with its own method approval and submission dates. Families weigh that decision on content and almost never on workload, which is where it actually bites.

sections.heading: Points are not the only thing that can go wrong
paragraphs: Most families think about the Diploma as a running total out of 45 with 24 as the pass mark. That is half the picture. The full Diploma is awarded only when a set of published conditions is satisfied alongside the total, and a student can reach 26 points and still not be awarded the Diploma. Understanding which condition is at risk changes the tutoring decision completely, because the required improvement may be in a subject the family was not worried about.

The conditions cover the shape of the grade profile as well as its sum. A grade 1 in any subject is a failing condition on its own. There are limits on how many grade 2s and how many grade 3s a profile may contain. There are separate points floors for the Higher Level subjects taken together and the Standard Level subjects taken together, so a student who is strong at Standard Level and weak at Higher Level can hit 24 in total and still fall short. An E grade in either Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a failing condition. And Creativity, Activity, Service has to be completed — it is not graded, but it is required.

What that means practically is that the most urgent subject is not always the lowest one. A student at 25 points with a grade 2 in a Standard Level subject may need that single grade moved to 3 far more than they need two points anywhere else. A student with a strong total and an E in TOK has a core problem, not a subject problem, and no amount of chemistry tutoring addresses it. Triage has to start from the whole profile.

The conditions are published by the IB and are stable, but they are also exactly the kind of thing worth confirming with your Diploma coordinator for your child's session rather than taking from a tutoring page. Ask for the award requirements in writing and read them against the latest predicted grades. That single exercise, done in DP2 term four, reorders most families' spending priorities.

sections.heading: Which provider model are you actually buying from?
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market compares itself favourably with an unnamed alternative. A more useful exercise is to identify which of six models you are dealing with, because the model determines who employs the tutor, who replaces them if the match fails, whether you ever speak to the person teaching before paying, and who is accountable when something goes wrong.

A specialist agency recruits and allocates tutors, usually at the higher end of the rate range, and typically holds the relationship rather than letting you choose. An international marketplace lists independent tutors and takes a commission; you choose, but the platform's responsibility ends at introduction. A freelance or independent tutor is a direct relationship with no intermediary, which is simple and cheap and leaves you with no replacement if it fails. A tuition centre sells group classes from premises, which in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit. School-run support is free and delivered by the student's own teachers, subject to the ethics rules on teachers tutoring their own pupils. An online platform like IB Gram matches a tutor and delivers over video.

The questions that separate them are all answerable in one exchange. Who employs the tutor. Can I meet them before paying. What happens if the match is wrong. Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and does it include VAT. Is there a replacement policy in writing. Does the tutor hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. Does the provider have UAE premises, and if so, does it hold the permit those require. Any provider unwilling to answer those in writing has told you something.

On our own side of that table, plainly: IB Gram matches one tutor to one student and delivers over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There is a free diagnostic lesson before any payment, so you see the tutor teach first. There are no UAE premises, no examination-centre status and no regulator approval of any kind. Home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free for a narrow course, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty and we say so before booking.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in this market answers, and it has a precise published answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

The eligible categories are published and broader than most parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow that a parent can act on. First, because the permit is free and takes two working days, there is no legitimate reason for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one, and asking to see it is a reasonable request rather than an awkward one. Second, no fine amount should be quoted to you by anyone. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and figures circulating as specific sums could not be verified, so a provider quoting one is repeating something unsourced.

A separate point applies to anyone operating with premises. A tutoring operation with staff and premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a different authorisation from the individual permit and 'KHDA approved tutors' is not a thing it creates. There is also an ethics dimension in Abu Dhabi, where ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also barring serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording.

sections.heading: What a parent can actually verify about a rate
paragraphs: Three of six researched competitors in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So the first verifiable thing about a rate is whether it exists in AED and whether the provider will put it in writing before a lesson. That alone eliminates a surprising proportion of the market.

The second is the basis. Is the figure per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson. Does it include VAT or not — and note that this page makes no claim about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees in general, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation; the only honest statement a provider can make is whether its own quoted figure is inclusive. Does a home visit carry a travel supplement, and is there a minimum booking length. Is there a cancellation window. Is the first lesson charged.

The third is the market context, which is published and checkable. Read in October 2026: Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or above, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 including travel; TutorChase quotes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650. Monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240-600, AED 600-1,200 and AED 1,000-2,000 or above across the tiers, with packages in this market around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page because level, component and urgency move it, and a number invented for a landing page would misquote most cases. What is verifiable on our side is the sequence: a free diagnostic lesson first, then a written diagnosis with a session estimate, then a quote, then a decision. Nothing is charged before you have read the diagnosis.

sections.heading: What distance costs a Motor City family in practice
paragraphs: Having argued that proximity is the weakest filter, it is worth being concrete about the cost of using it here. Motor City has no Diploma school inside it. The nearest substantial Diploma cohort is at JESS Arabian Ranches, and the rest of the corridor's Diploma provision sits at Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School, Greenfield International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai. A tutor resident in Motor City who has taught the Diploma is therefore a coincidence rather than a category.

The timing arithmetic compounds it. Diploma students from this postcode commute out and are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30, which makes about 18:00 the earliest realistic session start. A visiting tutor spends forty to sixty minutes each way in term traffic and needs a two-hour minimum booking to justify it, with a latest workable start of roughly 18:30. The window in which both the student and a visiting specialist are available is therefore about thirty minutes wide, on weekdays, for a pool that barely exists.

Online, that window opens to 18:00 through 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, sessions can be 45 or 60 minutes, and two sessions a week on different evenings is routine. The tutor is selected for having taught the named course at the named level, which for a Group 2 language at Higher Level or a Group 6 arts component is the difference between a match and none.

Home visits remain the right choice for some students, and the honest cases are worth repeating: a younger child who cannot self-manage a screen, or a student whose written method needs correcting as it is produced. IB Gram does not offer them anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison here is informational. What we will not do is claim a local presence we do not have: there is no UAE office, no centre and no branch.
