sections.heading: Starting, with the honesty boundaries stated
paragraphs: The first message should name the course and the level, say which component is weak, and include the full predicted grade profile if the concern is the Diploma award rather than a single subject. Send a marked piece of work. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day naming the error patterns, or naming which award condition is at risk and what would have to move. Nothing is charged before you read it.

Availability is good across Groups 1 to 5 at both levels for UAE evening slots, with a match normally inside one to three working days. Group 2 languages beyond Spanish and French, Group 6 arts components and the Career-related Programme reflective project are thinner, and some cannot be filled from UAE-resident tutors at all. Where that is the case the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking rather than after it.

On academic honesty, which this page has a particular duty to state because at least one provider ranking for UAE IB searches sells completed Internal Assessments. Submitting purchased work is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, up to loss of the Diploma. A tutor may interrogate a research question, check a method's feasibility, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, teach citation and referencing, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure by rewriting, or edit prose into a standard the student cannot produce, and may not supply completed coursework of any kind.

And the claims we do not make, for completeness. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. It holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, is not an examination centre and cannot enter a candidate. It does not describe tutors as current IB examiners, because that status cannot be evidenced here and would not be used to imply access to marking or paper content if it could. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked at source, never reproduced or distributed.

process.title: Check the whole grade profile, not one subject
process.description: If the worry is whether the Diploma will be awarded, send all six predicted grades plus TOK and the Extended Essay. A single grade 2 moved to a 3 can matter more than two points elsewhere, and that is invisible if you only look at the lowest subject.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge, spent on the student's own work, before any payment. This is also how you verify the tutor: you watch them teach your child before committing, which is the opposite of the common market pattern where allocation follows payment.

process.title: Ask the verification questions
process.description: Who employs the tutor, where they are based, whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, whether the rate is per hour or per lesson and what it includes, and what happens if the match is wrong. Ask us and ask anyone else you are considering, and compare the written answers.

process.title: Weekly slot reviewed on school marks
process.description: Same tutor, same time, 45 or 60 minutes, scheduled from 18:00 to allow for the commute out of Motor City, with slots to 21:00 and post-Iftar timing in Ramadan. Progress is judged on the school's next marked assessment, read against the original written diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: Sorted by what you can check, not by distance
whyPoints.description: Provider model, tutor location, permit status, rate basis and replacement policy are all verifiable in one written exchange. Distance is verifiable too, and it is the only one of the five that has no effect on a Diploma grade.

whyPoints.title: Award conditions triaged before subjects
whyPoints.description: A student can reach 24 points and still not be awarded the Diploma. Where the concern is the award rather than a grade, we start from the whole profile, because the subject that needs moving is frequently not the lowest one.

whyPoints.title: The permit position quoted from source
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is free, lasts two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service in two working days. Because it is free and fast, asking to see it is reasonable.

whyPoints.title: No fine figures and no tax claims
whyPoints.description: The ministry did not specify fine amounts, so we quote none, and we make no general claim about the VAT treatment of tuition fees because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation. We will only state whether our own quoted figure is inclusive.

whyPoints.title: You see the tutor before you pay
whyPoints.description: A free diagnostic lesson comes before any charge and before any commitment, which makes the match checkable rather than promised. If the fit is wrong after it, you have paid nothing and we change the match.

whyPoints.title: Honest about a nonexistent local pool
whyPoints.description: No Diploma school sits inside Motor City or Sports City, so a resident tutor who has taught the Diploma is a coincidence rather than a category. We say that rather than implying a local specialist network that does not exist.

faqs.question: Why does a search for an IB tutor near Motor City return so little?
faqs.answer: Because there is no Diploma school inside Motor City or the adjacent Sports City development. GEMS Metropole School runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, and Victory Heights Primary School and Bradenton Preparatory Academy are primary-weighted, so every Diploma student from this postcode commutes out across the Dubailand corridor. A resident tutor who has taught the Diploma is therefore a coincidence rather than a category, and a proximity search is sorting a list that barely contains what you are looking for.

faqs.question: What does being nearby genuinely help with?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they are worth acknowledging. A tutor in the community can sit beside a younger child who cannot yet manage a screen session independently. They can be physically present quickly if something is urgent. And they often know the local schools socially, which occasionally produces useful context about a particular cohort or teacher. What proximity cannot tell you is whether they have taught your child's course at your child's level, whether they hold a MoHRE permit, or what happens if the match fails.

faqs.question: Is 24 points on its own enough for the full Diploma to be awarded?
faqs.answer: Yes, which surprises most families. The full Diploma requires a set of published conditions alongside the total: no grade 1 in any subject, limits on how many grade 2s and grade 3s the profile may contain, separate minimum points totals across the Higher Level and Standard Level subjects, neither Theory of Knowledge nor the Extended Essay graded E, and Creativity, Activity, Service completed. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the award requirements in writing and read them against the latest predicted grades, ideally in DP2 rather than later.

faqs.question: Which subject should we fund if the Diploma itself is at risk?
faqs.answer: Often not the lowest one. If a condition on the grade profile is what threatens the award, moving a single grade 2 to a 3 can decide it while two extra points elsewhere would not. If a Higher Level points floor is the problem, strong Standard Level grades do not substitute for it. If Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is heading for an E, that is a core problem and no amount of subject tutoring addresses it. That is why triage starts from the full profile rather than from one report.

faqs.question: How do I tell what kind of tutoring provider I am dealing with?
faqs.answer: Ask who employs the tutor, whether you can meet them before paying, what happens if the match is wrong, and whether the provider has UAE premises. A specialist agency allocates and holds the relationship. A marketplace introduces independent tutors and stops there. A freelance tutor is a direct arrangement with no replacement if it fails. A tuition centre with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit. An online platform matches and delivers over video. The model determines accountability more than the price does.

faqs.question: Which tutors in the UAE are eligible for a private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: A wider group than most parents expect. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. Because the permit is free and MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time, there is no legitimate reason for a UAE-based tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: Is it rude to ask a tutor to show their MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: No, and the economics make it reasonable. The permit costs nothing and MoHRE's own service page for 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website or e-services system. A tutor working legitimately in the UAE has no obstacle to holding one. Treat reluctance as information. Separately, do not accept a fine figure from anyone: the ministry did not specify fine amounts, so any specific sum circulating is unsourced.

faqs.question: What should I ask about a quoted hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Whether it is in AED and in writing; whether it is per hour or per lesson and how long a lesson is; whether it includes VAT; whether a home visit carries a travel supplement and a minimum booking; whether the first lesson is charged; and what the replacement policy is if the match fails. Three of six researched competitors in this market publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars, so a written AED figure with its basis stated already narrows the field considerably.

faqs.question: Should we replace the Group 6 arts subject with a second science?
faqs.answer: Many students heading to science, medicine or economics degrees do, and it is permitted. The point families usually miss is the workload change rather than the content change: an arts process portfolio and exhibition are replaced by a second scientific investigation, with its own method approval date and its own submission deadline, often overlapping the first one. A student taking two Group 4 subjects plus the Extended Essay and the TOK essay in the same period has a crowded DP2 that the timetable does not show.

faqs.question: What time can a Motor City Diploma session start?
faqs.answer: About 18:00 for most families, because Diploma students here commute out of the community and are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30. Online sessions run to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, so a second weekly session can sit at 20:00 after a fixture without displacing it, and either can be 45 minutes rather than a full hour. A visiting tutor needing a two-hour minimum and finishing by around 18:30 leaves a workable window of roughly half an hour, which is why the format matters here more than in most postcodes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge if it is heading for an E?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be treated as urgent rather than as a side issue, because an E in either Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma. The TOK essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title and the exhibition is three objects with a 950-word commentary, so the volume of work is small and the leverage high. A tutor can unpack the title, test the knowledge claims a student proposes and give criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own draft, but cannot write any part of it.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for my child's course?
faqs.answer: We tell you, before you book. Groups 1 to 5 at both levels have good UAE evening cover and normally match within one to three working days. Group 2 languages beyond Spanish and French, Group 6 arts components and the Career-related Programme reflective project are thinner, and some cannot be filled from UAE-resident tutors at all. In those cases the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor's location is stated before any booking rather than discovered afterwards.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office or centre in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. There is no UAE office, no centre, no branch and no examination-centre status, and we cannot enter a candidate for any examination. We hold no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and no KHDA Educational Services Permit — which is the authorisation a Dubai training institute with premises actually requires. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers and one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page, so this is worth checking of anyone.

faqs.question: Everyone else lists a May exam window. Why will you not?
faqs.answer: Because none could be verified at source. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an examination date is something a family reorganises travel and a revision plan around. UAE candidates sit the May session; for the window, the results date and the candidate release time, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly. The deadlines that constrain a student first are internal anyway, and the school sets all of those.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-motor-city.closingHeading: Check five things, and distance is not one of them
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-motor-city.closingBody: Before paying anyone for IB help in Motor City, get five answers in writing. Which provider model it is and who employs the tutor. Where that tutor is based. Whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and takes two working days, so there is no reason not to. What the AED rate covers, per hour or per lesson, inclusive or not. And what happens if the match is wrong. Then make the request precise: the course, the level, the component, and the whole grade profile if the Diploma award itself is at risk. Take the free diagnostic lesson before committing to anything.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mudon.tutorsIntro: The profiles below name subjects and levels rather than areas, because that is the match that matters. A request for Chemistry HL organic mechanisms goes to someone who has taught Chemistry HL, whether they sit in Dubai or elsewhere, and the lesson arrives in Mudon over video either way.

intro.heading: Distance is the wrong search term for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is decided by a small number of specific things. In Physics, by whether a student states the assumption behind a calculation in an extended response. In Chemistry, by whether curly arrows start from the right place. In Maths Analysis and Approaches, by whether Paper 1 arithmetic survives three lines without a calculator. In Economics, by whether a diagram is applied to the named market rather than described. None of those depend on where the tutor sits.

Mudon makes the point sharply. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand with no secondary school inside its boundary, so students travel outward: to Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, GEMS International School Al Khail, Nord Anglia in Al Barsha South, or Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City. A tutor within twenty minutes of Al Salam or Naseem is drawn from whoever happens to live in Motor City or Dubai Sports City, which is a pool of generalists covering several subjects at two levels.

That is adequate for Standard Level support where the task is pace-keeping. It is not adequate for Higher Level sciences and mathematics, where the marks sit in the detail of how an answer is constructed. A tutor who has taught Chemistry HL across several cohorts knows which three topics eat the most marks in Paper 2 and what the mark scheme accepts for a mechanism; a generalist knows the content. The gap between those two states is the grade.

So this page is organised by syllabus rather than by geography. It sets out the assessment structure of the subjects Dubailand families request most, the weightings per paper at each level, the command terms that cause the most avoidable losses, what the Internal Assessment criteria actually reward letter by letter, and how a past-paper session is run so that it produces a diagnosis rather than a score.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so a session can sit at 4.15pm for a student home early or after 8pm for a household where both parents commute. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. Nothing on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon door, and the comparison tables further down make the case for the online route on its own terms.

One more reason the postcode is the wrong filter: a Diploma cohort in this belt is small and spread across several schools, so the subject a family needs help with is rarely the subject the nearest available tutor teaches best. Families discover this after a term of polite, unproductive sessions. Starting from the syllabus avoids it, and the sections below are ordered the way a subject teacher would order them rather than the way a directory listing would.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mudon.programmesIntro: Mudon students meet the IB at different points, and the subject work looks different in each. These are the three programmes families in this belt actually ask about.

programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria labelled A to D and marked out of eight, converted to a 1 to 7 grade through published boundaries. The Personal Project runs in the final year. Because there is no external paper until the optional eAssessments, the criteria are the whole of the assessment language.

That is a conversation about wording, and it works well on a shared screen with the student's own marked task in front of both parties.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The core components: a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge exhibition and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title, plus a 4,000-word Extended Essay in a chosen subject. Together they carry points on top of the subject grades and they are the components students most often leave until they are expensive to fix.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay subject choice is where Mudon students most often go wrong, picking a topic they find interesting rather than one with accessible sources and a research question that can be answered in 4,000 words. That decision is worth one session well before any writing starts.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-mudon.subjectsIntro: What follows is subject detail rather than a list: what each component tests, where the marks are usually lost, and what a session therefore practises.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is non-calculator, so an early algebraic slip propagates and follow-through marks only partly rescue it. Paper 2 rewards using the graphing calculator to confirm reasoning rather than to search. HL adds Maclaurin series, three-dimensional vectors and harder differential equations, and Paper 3 is an extended investigation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and interpretation. The habitual loss is producing correct mathematics and omitting the sentence that interprets it in context, which is where the mark scheme puts the credit. HL adds matrices, graph theory and complex numbers, with Paper 3 as a modelling investigation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice, Paper 2 short and extended response, Paper 3 covering experimental work and the option. Extended responses lose marks when assumptions go unstated. The HL extension in fields and electromagnetic induction is where grade boundaries separate students who know the content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and organic. Organic mechanisms are the most requested topic in this belt, and the fix is curly-arrow discipline practised under time rather than re-reading notes. Paper 3 rewards data handling and uncertainty treatment.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions reward careful reading of axes, units and scale before any biology is applied. Students lose marks giving descriptive answers where the command term asked them to explain or to evaluate, and in HL on the biochemical detail Standard Level never reaches.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries form the Internal Assessment, and diagram accuracy carries real marks: an unlabelled axis, a curve shifted without explanation, or a diagram that is described rather than applied to the named market all cost more than a thin evaluation paragraph.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue with two extracts, and at HL the HL Essay. Paper 2 answers that treat the texts in sequence rather than in conversation lose on the comparison criterion.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study and stimulus papers where tools earn marks only when applied to the named organisation. At HL the research project adds a primary-research element that needs a workable question, which is the part students underestimate.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects against an internal assessment prompt, and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. Essays that answer the title in general terms, without areas of knowledge structuring the argument, are capped however fluent the writing.

sections.heading: What a Diploma paper actually asks for
paragraphs: Students who are stuck at a 4 or 5 usually know more content than their grade suggests. What they have not learned is the form of answer each paper rewards. A Physics Paper 2 extended response is not a longer short answer; it is a structured argument in which the physics has to be named, the assumption stated and the arithmetic shown. A Chemistry Paper 2 mechanism question wants arrows from lone pairs or bonds, not a description of what happens.

Weightings matter because they tell you where the available marks are. In most Diploma sciences the Internal Assessment accounts for around a fifth of the grade and the external papers the rest, with Paper 2 carrying the largest single share. In Mathematics the two or three papers split the external marks and the exploration carries the internal portion. A student who treats every component as equally important spends hours in the wrong place.

The practical move is to look up the current subject guide weightings with the school's subject teacher, write them on the front of the folder, and plan the term against them. Exact percentages change between subject guide cycles, so the figures should come from the school or the IB's own published guide rather than from a tutoring page, including this one.
What a session can do is convert those weightings into a working order: the component with the most available marks and the largest current loss goes first.

sections.heading: Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the choice that causes the most retrospective regret in this belt, and it is made in Year 11 before anyone has seen a Diploma paper. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route with calculus at its centre. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with technology assumed throughout. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and both are respectable; they simply lead different places.

The admissions question is the one worth checking first. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses at competitive universities expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a student who takes Applications may find a shortlist shortens after offers are published. Business, design, psychology and several social-science routes are comfortable with Applications. Requirements vary by university and change, so the check belongs with the school's careers office and the university's own published entry profile rather than with a tutor.

The difficulty question is separate and more often misunderstood. Applications at Higher Level is not an easy option; its Paper 3 modelling investigation and its statistical content defeat plenty of students who assumed otherwise. The honest framing is fit: a student who enjoys proof and manipulation will do better in Analysis, and one who prefers interpreting real data will do better in Applications.

Where a student is already placed and struggling, the tutoring question is not the route but the paper. Analysis students usually need non-calculator fluency. Applications students usually need the interpretation sentence.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks a Diploma student throws away
paragraphs: The IB publishes command terms per subject and defines each one precisely. Students read them as synonyms. Describe, explain, evaluate, justify, outline, deduce, suggest and compare demand different answers, and a perfectly good piece of subject knowledge written against the wrong command term earns a fraction of the marks available.

The pattern is visible in any marked script. A question asking a student to explain why a rate of reaction increases receives a description of what happens. A question asking for evaluation receives two advantages and no judgement. A question asking the student to deduce receives a stated conclusion with no reasoning line. None of those are knowledge failures, which is why more content revision does not fix them.

The drill is mechanical and it works. Take ten past-paper questions from the student's own subject, cover the stems, and have the student state only what each command term obliges them to produce before writing anything. Within a few weeks the reading becomes automatic. It is the highest-return fortnight available to a student at a 4 or 5 in almost any subject group.
The table lists the terms that cause the most avoidable loss and what each one actually requires.

Two cautions. The definitions differ slightly between subject guides, so the list a student works from should be the one in their own subject's guide rather than a general version. And command terms interact with marks available: a two-mark explain question wants one causal link, not a paragraph, and writing four costs time that the extended response at the end of the paper needed.

rows: An account of features or a process, no reasons required

Every sentence must contain a causal link

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, read letter by letter
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject marks its internal component against lettered criteria with published descriptors, and the marks are not distributed the way students assume. In the sciences the investigation is assessed on the design and the analysis and the conclusion and the evaluation, which means a technically modest experiment, well designed and honestly evaluated, outscores an ambitious one written up loosely.

The mathematical exploration is the clearest example. Students pour effort into the mathematics and lose marks on presentation, personal engagement and reflection, which are separately credited. A reflection that says the topic was interesting earns little; one that identifies a limitation in the model and considers what would change if an assumption were relaxed earns properly. The mathematics does not have to be exotic to score well; it has to be correct, communicated and owned.

In Economics the three commentaries are assessed on diagrams, terminology, application, analysis and evaluation against a published article. Students regularly lose marks because the article is too old, too long or does not contain the economics they want to apply. Choosing the article is part of the assessment and deserves a session of its own.

What a tutor does here is explain each descriptor, ask the questions the descriptor implies, and mark the student's own draft against it. The draft stays the student's work, which is both the rule and, in practice, the only way the student learns what the criteria mean.

A last point on timing. Criteria reward process, and process has to exist before it can be written up. A student who runs the experiment, then reads the criteria, has already lost the design marks. Reading the descriptors before the practical, and keeping a dated log while it happens, is worth more than any amount of polishing afterwards, and it is the one piece of advice that costs nothing to follow.
bullets: Science investigations: design and evaluation carry marks a strong result alone does not
Mathematical exploration: presentation, personal engagement and reflection are separately credited
Economics commentaries: article choice is part of the assessment
Theory of Knowledge essay: areas of knowledge must structure the argument
Extended Essay: the research question decides the ceiling before any writing starts

sections.heading: How a past-paper session is actually run
paragraphs: A session that opens with a past paper and closes with a mark is a wasted hour. The paper is the instrument, not the purpose. The sequence that produces something useful is narrower: a timed section under conditions, immediate reconciliation against the mark scheme line by line, and then a named pattern the student can state back in one sentence.

The reconciliation step is the one most students have never done. Reading a mark scheme properly is a skill: understanding that a mark is awarded for a specific statement, that alternatives in brackets are acceptable, that consequential marks can rescue a wrong early value, and that a correct answer without the required working does not always score. Students who learn to mark their own work stop guessing what examiners want.

Then the pattern. The point of the exercise is a sentence like: I lose marks in extended response because I calculate and never state the assumption. Once a student can say that, the next fortnight has an obvious plan, and the plan is testable at the next timed section. Without that sentence, every session restarts from zero.

Across a block, the scripts accumulate into evidence. That is what the session notes record, and what a review conversation every few weeks is actually about: which pattern closed, which is still open, and which component the remaining marks sit in.

One practical note on logistics. The paper should be the real thing from the student's own subject and board, printed or on screen with a clock running, not a worksheet of selected questions. Selected questions remove the choice of where to spend time, and choosing where to spend time is half of what a Diploma paper tests.
bullets: Timed section first, under conditions, with the clock visible
Mark-scheme reconciliation line by line, done by the student
The error pattern stated in one sentence by the student
The next fortnight planned against that sentence and retested

sections.heading: Where Mudon students study the Diploma, and what that changes
paragraphs: Subject menus differ between Diploma schools, and a tutoring plan should start from the school's actual offer. Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches is the nearest Diploma provision to Mudon and the one most families in this belt name. Further along Al Khail Road, GEMS International School Al Khail and Nord Anglia International School Dubai run IB routes, and Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City runs the continuum from Primary Years upward.

What that means practically is that two Mudon students described as doing the IB may be sitting different subject combinations with different internal deadlines and different option topics in Physics or Biology. A tutor who asks which school before asking which topic is not being nosy; the school decides the scheme of work, the mock timing and in some subjects the option studied.

It also decides the laboratory. Internal Assessments in the sciences depend on the equipment a school has and the practical scheme it runs, and online tutoring prepares the design, the data treatment and the evaluation around whatever the school can actually provide. Pretending otherwise would be dishonest about what a video lesson can do.
Schools are named here as market context. IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them and claims no endorsement from any of them.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. Because Diploma students in Dubailand are drawn from several schools into a handful of sixth forms, a Mudon student's classmates are often new to them, and the informal revision network that carries a cohort through Year 13 takes time to form. A weekly session with a subject specialist partly compensates for that, which is a reason some families start in the first term rather than waiting for a disappointing report.

sections.heading: Honesty rules for subject coursework
paragraphs: Subject tutoring and coursework tutoring are the same job with a different boundary. On a past paper, a tutor can show a model answer, because the paper is practice. On an Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, the work is assessed and must be the student's own, authenticated by the teacher. A malpractice finding does not reduce a mark; it can remove the Diploma.

So the permitted actions are specific. Teaching the subject content behind the investigation. Explaining what a criterion rewards and asking the questions it implies. Interrogating a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. Critiquing a method, including saying that it will not produce usable data. Marking a draft the student wrote against the descriptors and saying where it falls short. All of that is teaching.

The prohibited actions are equally specific: drafting any part of the text, rewriting a paragraph, editing to completion, supplying a worked exploration to adapt, or providing data the student did not collect. One provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is the service to refuse, and it is worth telling a teenager explicitly why, because the offer will reach them even if it does not reach you.

Board material carries its own rule. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables stay with their publishers; sessions reference and link to the official pages rather than circulating copies.
bullets: Model answers belong to practice papers, never to assessed coursework
Permitted: content teaching, criterion explanation, method critique, marking the student's own draft
Prohibited: drafting, rewriting, editing to completion, supplying data or a worked exploration
Official board material is linked, not redistributed

sections.heading: What subject tuition costs in Dubai, with the sources named
paragraphs: Look at this from the specialist end rather than the budget end, because that is where a Higher Level subject request lands. Named IB and IGCSE specialists in this market publish AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision runs AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are the rates attached to the kind of subject depth this page argues for.

Below that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts one weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. For context on household budgets, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27.
These are market rates with their sources named rather than IB Gram prices. What this page does offer is a free trial lesson and a consultation before any payment is taken.

process.title: Say the subject, the level and the school
process.description: Chemistry HL at Jumeirah English Speaking School and Chemistry HL at Fairgreen are not the same request, because the scheme of work, the option studied and the internal deadlines differ. Naming the school in the first message saves a session of discovery and sets the calendar the tutor works to.

process.title: Attach one marked script
process.description: A marked Paper 2, a returned exploration draft or a mock script tells us whether the losses are content, construction, timing or command-term reading. That diagnosis is the whole value of the first hour, and it is much better made from evidence than from a description.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the subject tutor
process.description: The trial runs over live video at no cost and before any payment, with the student rather than the parent doing most of the talking. If the match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is proposed. Nothing is owed for the trial itself whichever way it goes.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives the school run
process.description: Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. A 4.15pm start suits a student home early from Arabian Ranches; after 8pm suits households where both parents commute. Because no travel is involved, a slot can move within the evening or shift after Iftar during Ramadan at no cost.

process.title: Review against the components every few weeks
process.description: Session notes name the topic, the error pattern and the next target. Every four to six weeks the plan is checked against the school's deadlines and the component the remaining marks sit in, so the hour follows the available marks rather than running through a syllabus in order.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not on distance
whyPoints.description: A search for a tutor near Mudon returns generalists based around Motor City and Dubai Sports City. A search by subject returns people who have taught Physics HL or Chemistry HL repeatedly. At Higher Level that difference is the one the grade responds to.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes are read, not described
whyPoints.description: Students mark their own work against the published scheme in session, which is how they stop guessing what an examiner wants. Learning to read a mark scheme is a transferable skill that keeps paying after the tutoring stops.

whyPoints.title: Command terms are drilled explicitly
whyPoints.description: Describe, explain, evaluate, deduce and justify demand different answers, and a fortnight of mechanical practice converts that from knowledge into reflex. It is the highest-return short intervention available to a student sitting at a 4 or 5.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support stays inside IB rules
whyPoints.description: Criterion explanation, method critique and feedback on the student's own draft are teaching. Drafting, rewriting and supplying text are not, and no tutor here will do them. The boundary is stated because the alternative risks the student's Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries a source
whyPoints.description: AED bands are attributed to the providers and the cost table that published them. Regulatory facts carry their government sources. Nothing on this page is a statistic about our own students, because no such figure could be verified by a reader.

whyPoints.title: Thin coverage is disclosed
whyPoints.description: Some combinations, including Further Mathematics at Higher Level and the less-taught languages, have limited availability. Where that is the case you are told, with a timescale or an alternative, rather than being matched with a generalist and left to discover it.

faqs.question: Does it matter that an IB tutor is not physically near Mudon?
faqs.answer: For the work that moves a Diploma grade, no. Extended-response construction, mechanism drawing, mark-scheme reading, exploration criteria and command-term discipline all happen on a shared screen, and the student keeps the annotated script. What proximity would buy is a physical presence, and from Mudon it would also narrow the choice to tutors living around Motor City and Dubai Sports City, who tend to cover several subjects at two levels. At Higher Level in the sciences and mathematics, choosing by subject rather than by distance is the trade that actually helps.

faqs.question: Which Diploma component should we attack first?
faqs.answer: The one where the largest share of available marks meets the largest current loss. In most sciences that is Paper 2, which carries the biggest single external share and is where extended-response technique lives. In Mathematics it depends on the paper pattern and on whether the exploration is still open. The Internal Assessment is worth attacking early because it is the only component with a deadline you can still influence. Look up the current weightings with the school's subject teacher, write them down, and plan against them rather than against a syllabus order.

faqs.question: My daughter understands Chemistry but scores 4s. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly answer construction rather than content. The pattern in marked Higher Level scripts is consistent: the calculation is right and the assumption behind it is never stated; the mechanism is broadly correct and the arrows start in the wrong place; an evaluate question receives two advantages and no judgement. None of that is fixed by more revision. It is fixed by marking her own work against the published scheme until she can state her own error pattern in one sentence, then drilling that pattern on timed questions for a fortnight and retesting.

faqs.question: Should my son take Maths Analysis or Applications at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Start from where he wants to apply, not from which looks easier. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many competitive economics courses expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level; business, design and several social sciences accept Applications. Requirements vary by university and change, so check the university's own published entry profile with the school's careers office. On difficulty, Applications at Higher Level is not a soft option; its modelling investigation and statistical content defeat students who assumed it was. Fit matters: proof and manipulation suit Analysis, interpreting real data suits Applications.

faqs.question: How long is the Maths exploration meant to be, and what scores well?
faqs.answer: The exploration is a short piece of personal mathematical writing rather than a long report, and schools publish the current page guidance from the subject guide. What scores well is rarely exotic mathematics. It is a focused question, correct and clearly communicated mathematics, genuine personal engagement, and reflection that identifies a limitation in the model and considers what relaxing an assumption would change. Students lose marks on presentation, engagement and reflection while pouring effort into the mathematics itself. Those three criteria are separately credited, which is where a session is best spent.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my son's Physics Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, as teaching and feedback on his own writing. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the method will produce usable data, point out that an uncertainty has been ignored, say that a graph choice hides the relationship, and mark his draft against the published descriptors. What a tutor must not do is draft or rewrite any part of it, edit it to completion, or supply data he did not collect. The work is authenticated by his teacher, and a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma rather than just the marks.

faqs.question: Why do command terms cost a Mudon student so many marks?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction words the IB defines precisely for each subject: describe, explain, evaluate, justify, deduce, outline, suggest, compare and contrast. Students read them as synonyms and answer the wrong question with good knowledge. A question asking for explanation receives a description; one asking for evaluation receives two lists and no judgement. The repair is mechanical: take ten past-paper questions, cover the stems, and have the student state only what each term obliges before writing. Within a fortnight the reading becomes automatic, which is unusually fast for anything in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Is the Extended Essay worth paying for tutoring on?
faqs.answer: One or two sessions at the right moment are worth more than ten later. The decision that sets the ceiling is the research question, and it is made before any writing: a question that can actually be answered in 4,000 words, in a subject where accessible sources exist, with a method the student can carry out. Most weak Extended Essays are not badly written; they are answering an unanswerable question. A tutor can interrogate the question, critique the method and mark drafts against criteria. The essay itself must be entirely the student's work.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Higher Level science need?
faqs.answer: One a week through the term is the usual starting point, moving to two in the eight to twelve weeks before a session if the marked scripts justify it. More than two a week rarely helps during term, because the limiting factor is the student's own practice time between sessions rather than input. The exception is a holiday block, where three or four sessions in a week can close a content gap that term time cannot absorb. The marked work decides this, which is why we ask for a script before proposing a frequency.

faqs.question: Do your tutors know which option topic my child's school teaches?
faqs.answer: Not until you tell us, and it matters. Schools choose option topics and schemes of work, so two Diploma students in Dubai nominally studying the same subject can be sitting different content with different internal deadlines. Naming the school in the first message, alongside the subject and level, means the tutor sets past-paper questions from the right option and works to the right deadlines. It also tells us what laboratory equipment is available, which shapes what can realistically be proposed for a science investigation.

faqs.question: What does a specialist Diploma tutor cost per hour in this market?
faqs.answer: Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. These are market figures with their sources named rather than IB Gram prices, and a free trial lesson comes before any payment either way.

faqs.question: Can online lessons prepare a science investigation without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: They prepare everything around the practical, which is where most of the marks are. The experiment belongs to the school and its equipment; the design, the variable control, the uncertainty treatment, the graph choice, the analysis and the evaluation belong to the write-up, and those are what the criteria reward. A session can rehearse the design before the student goes into the laboratory and interrogate the data afterwards. Any page claiming video lessons replace school practical work would be overselling, which is why this one does not.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 9 and the criterion marks make no sense to us. Can that be explained?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful single sessions a Middle Years family can buy. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, marked out of eight, and converted to a 1 to 7 grade through published boundaries. A criterion mark is not a percentage and not a measure of effort; it describes what a piece of work demonstrated against a descriptor. Reading the descriptors next to the student's own marked task usually makes the gap obvious, and it is normally about what the work shows rather than about knowledge.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a timescale or an alternative, rather than matched with a generalist. Common combinations such as Biology SL, Maths Applications SL and English A are usually covered within a few days. Narrower ones, including Further Mathematics at Higher Level, some of the less-taught languages and certain option topics, can take a week or more, and occasionally the honest answer is that we cannot cover it well. Saying so costs a booking and avoids a wasted term, which is the trade we would rather make.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Muhaisnah Diploma and Middle Years enquiries are asked one thing before they take a booking: describe the assessment model for this course from memory. The ones who can are the ones on this page.

intro.heading: Distance is the wrong filter, and here is the better one
paragraphs: There is a reason "near me" is the phrase people type. It feels like a proxy for everything else: somebody local is accountable, reachable, probably recommended by a neighbour. In a city laid out like Dubai, with IB provision clustered in particular districts and almost none of it in Muhaisnah itself, that proxy breaks. The tutors nearest to Muhaisnah 1 through 4 are overwhelmingly CBSE and British-curriculum generalists, because that is what the surrounding schools teach. A Diploma student needs something narrower.

So this page proposes a different filter, built from things you can actually check. Can the tutor tell you how the 45 points are constructed, without looking? Can they name the criteria for your child's internal assessment and what each is worth? Do they know the difference between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and which one your child's university target expects? Those questions take four minutes and they separate specialists from subject graduates far more reliably than a postcode does.

The second half of the filter is about the school, not the tutor. Dubai publishes more usable information about its private schools than almost any other education market in the world, and almost nobody reads it. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale and publishes subject-level findings. If you are deciding whether your child's difficulty is a teaching problem, a programme-fit problem or a workload problem, the inspection report for their school is a free and better starting point than any tutoring enquiry.

Then there is the honest answer to the literal question. Is there an IB tutor near Muhaisnah? For common subjects, yes, somebody will travel, and the market rate for in-home visits in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. For a Higher Level specialist in a less-taught subject, probably not. IB Gram does not solve this by sending anyone to your door; home visiting is a service we run only in India. In the UAE we teach one-to-one over live video, which is how a Muhaisnah family reaches a specialist who would never have driven here.

What follows is the material that makes the better filter usable. The inspection bands and what each actually implies. The Higher and Standard Level decision, which drives more of a Diploma outcome than any individual grade. How the points are built, including the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix that families consistently underestimate. The mark allocations for each internal assessment, by criterion letter. What distance really costs a Muhaisnah evening. And how the first and second years of the Diploma require two different kinds of help.

None of it assumes you will contact us. A parent who reads the inspection report for their child's school, works out where the recoverable points sit, and then asks the subject teacher one precise question has already done most of the useful work, often for nothing. Tutoring is worth buying when a specific capability is missing and the school cannot give it one-to-one attention. It is not worth buying as insurance, and a provider who tells you otherwise about a regulatory process or a university offer is selling urgency rather than teaching.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.programmesIntro: Before anything else, be certain which part of the IB continuum your child is in, because the assessment logic changes completely between them and so does the tutoring.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, examined externally at the end of two years, plus an internally assessed component in each subject worth roughly a fifth of the grade. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay feed a separate matrix worth up to three points. Subject grades run 1-7; the total runs to 45 with conditions attached to a pass.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma enquiries from Muhaisnah almost always arrive with a specific arithmetic problem: a predicted total two or three points below a university offer, and a clear idea of which two subjects are responsible. That is the most tractable kind of request, because the work can be aimed precisely rather than spread.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. No external examination unless the school opts into eAssessment. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed against three criteria, each out of 8. Judgements rest on most recent and most consistent achievement rather than an average.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years enquiries from this catchment are usually about interpretation rather than content. A parent sees a 5 out of 8 on criterion C and cannot tell whether that is a problem. Teaching the student to write deliberately against a descriptor lifts marks without adding any new material, and it is the single highest-return intervention at this stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based units rather than separate subjects, with the Exhibition in the final year. Reporting is descriptive and continuous, which is appropriate for the age and makes specific skill gaps hard to spot. Numeracy and written structure are where undiagnosed weaknesses tend to sit until criterion marking begins in the Middle Years Programme.
programmes.countryNote: From Muhaisnah and the surrounding apartment communities, PYP requests concentrate on reading fluency and number confidence. Short frequent sessions work better than long ones at this age, and twenty-five minutes twice a week after a long bus journey beats ninety minutes once.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Muhaisnah enquiries name most often, described by where the marks actually move rather than by syllabus summary.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Grades move on presentation discipline and on the exploration. Students who can do the mathematics still lose marks for unstated methods and unlabelled sketches, and HL proof questions reward structured argument over cleverness.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with heavy technology use. The recurring loss is a correct calculator output with no interpretation attached, and HL adds matrices and graph theory that students meet nowhere else in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions, graph meaning and uncertainty handling decide outcomes. A student can rearrange any equation and still fail to say what a gradient represents, which is the question the paper actually asks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the load. The reliable failure is recall without explanation, because the longer questions ask for a trend to be accounted for rather than stated.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision above all. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer, and data-based questions on unfamiliar studies reward method literacy rather than memorised content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Fully labelled diagrams, then evaluation that weighs and concludes. The portfolio of commentaries is where most avoidable marks go, usually because the article was chosen before the concept was understood.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application to the specific stimulus rather than generically, plus quantitative questions students assume are optional. The HL research project rewards a narrow question on a real organisation over an ambitious one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the individual oral built on a global issue, and the HL essay marked out of 20 across four criteria. Writing about how a text works, rather than what it says, is the shift that moves bands.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Named studies deployed with method and limitation, and essays built to a command term. The experimental study's design decides most of its marks before any data exists.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, networks and abstract data structures on paper, plus a solution built for a real client. Documentation carries the criterion marks, so a working program with a thin write-up scores poorly.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation on provenance rather than content, plus the historical investigation with its own criteria. HL adds a depth study examined in a third paper, which is where the reading load becomes real.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition, each assessed separately and each with its own word or page limits. Students lose marks on documentation and curatorial rationale rather than on making, which surprises most families.

sections.heading: What a KHDA inspection report tells you that a tutor cannot
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by the UAE government as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes the result on a six-band scale. Most parents know their school's overall band and stop there, which wastes the document. The value is in the subject-level and phase-level detail underneath, because that is where a report says something actionable about your child's actual situation.

Read it with a specific question. If your child is struggling in Diploma Physics and the report identifies science attainment in the post-16 phase as a relative weakness, you are looking at a different problem from a student struggling in a subject the report identifies as a strength. The first is partly a provision issue and tutoring is a genuine supplement. The second is more likely to be about that individual student's technique, which is cheaper and faster to fix.

The bands themselves are worth understanding in plain language, because the labels are easy to over-read. The table below gives each band and what it practically implies for a family weighing up extra support. It is not a ranking of schools; it is a translation of a regulator's vocabulary into the decision you are actually making.

One more use. Dubai's private school sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK provision at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, were announced for the 2026-27 intake, creating 16,846 new places. If you are weighing a move, that supply picture matters as much as any inspection band.

sections.heading: Higher or Standard Level: the decision that drives everything else
paragraphs: Of all the choices a Diploma student makes, the Higher Level selection does the most damage when it is wrong, and it is the one families get least help with. Three subjects at Higher Level means three courses with more content, an extra paper in several subjects, and a higher expectation in the internal assessment. Choose three that align with the university route and the workload is justified. Choose one because a friend did, and it sits on the timetable for two years taking time from the subjects that matter.

The table sets out what actually differs between the levels across the things that change a grade. Read the final column carefully: the honest reason to take a subject at Higher Level is that a destination requires it or the student is genuinely strong in it, not that Higher Level looks better on a transcript. Universities read the subject requirement, not the count.

The commonest fixable error we see from eastern Dubai students is a Higher Level choice made without checking the university requirement in the destination country. For mathematics in particular, the route choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation has real consequences: engineering and many science programmes expect the former, often at Higher Level, while business, social science and some economics routes accept the latter. Changing route in the second year is usually not possible.

If your child is already committed and the level is wrong, the useful tutoring question is narrow: can this subject be stabilised at a grade that protects the total, while the points are recovered elsewhere? Often the answer is yes and it is cheaper than trying to force the Higher Level grade up. That calculation is what the points-targeted work on this page is for, and it starts from the predicted grades rather than from ambition.

sections.heading: How 45 points are actually built, and where the cheap points are
paragraphs: Families routinely plan a Diploma as six separate subjects and then discover the total does not work that way. Six subjects graded 1-7 give a maximum of 42. The remaining three points come from a matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade and the Extended Essay grade. A pass requires a minimum of 24 points with a set of additional conditions on individual grades and on the core components, so a student can reach 24 and still not be awarded the Diploma.

That structure has a practical consequence nobody tells parents in Muhaisnah: the matrix points are frequently the cheapest on the board. A student who treats the Extended Essay as an administrative hurdle and the Theory of Knowledge essay as unmarkable opinion is leaving points on the table that would cost many more hours to recover in a Higher Level science. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria and Critical thinking alone carries 12 of them, which is a specific, teachable thing.

The second place points hide is a Standard Level subject sitting at a 5 that could be a 6. The arithmetic is unsentimental: a point is a point, and a point recovered in a subject the student finds manageable costs a fraction of a point forced out of the Higher Level course they find hardest. Families resist this because the weak subject feels like the problem. The total does not care which subject the point came from.

This is why the first conversation we have with a Diploma family from this catchment is arithmetic rather than subject choice. Give us the predicted grades, the offer and the matrix position, and the answer to "which subject should we tutor" is usually visible in ten minutes, and is quite often not the subject the parent came in asking about.

sections.heading: Every internal assessment, by criterion letter and marks
paragraphs: This is the table the research behind these pages found nowhere in the market: internal assessment criteria named by letter with their mark allocations. It matters because students write to a word count and a deadline when they should be writing to a mark scheme. A student who knows that the Extended Essay's Critical thinking criterion carries 12 marks writes a different essay from one who does not, and the difference is not effort, it is aim.

Use it as a checklist with your child rather than as reading. Pick the component they are working on, find the criterion with the largest allocation, and ask them to show you where in their draft that criterion is served. If they cannot point at it, that is the session's work, and it is work a tutor can do properly in an hour without touching a sentence of their writing.

Two notes on accuracy. Criteria and allocations are revised when a subject guide is reissued, so confirm against the current guide for your child's subject and cohort, which the school's IB coordinator can supply. And weightings differ between Standard and Higher Level in several subjects even when the criteria names are identical, so check the level as well as the subject.

The boundary on all of this is firm and we state it on every page. A tutor may explain what a criterion asks for, question a research design, and tell a student which descriptor their draft does not yet meet. A tutor may not write, restructure or finish any part of the work that will be submitted. The sessions that help most end with the student holding three specific problems and the document unchanged.

sections.heading: What proximity actually buys a Muhaisnah household
paragraphs: Having argued that distance is the wrong filter, it is only fair to say precisely what it does buy, because for some families it is worth paying for. A tutor physically present supervises. For a child under about eleven, or for an older student with genuine attention difficulties, an adult in the room is a service and a screen is not a substitute. If that describes your household, in-home tutoring is the right purchase and the market band is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

For a Diploma student, the calculation runs the other way, and the reason is arithmetic rather than preference. A tutor arriving at a Muhaisnah address at 6pm has crossed Al Ittihad Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at the worst hour, and arrival slippage of ten or fifteen minutes is normal. Across thirty weeks that is several complete lessons. An online session starts on time, and the written work can be marked in the shared document before the next slot rather than collected at the following visit.

The other thing distance buys is a smaller shortlist, which is the part families do not see until they are in it. The tutors who can reach Muhaisnah conveniently are the ones who already work this side of the city, and they are disproportionately generalists covering several curricula. For Visual Arts, Psychology, Computer Science or a first-language literature option at Higher Level, the local pool is close to empty, and we would rather say so than offer you whoever is free.

For completeness: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, in any emirate. It is an India-only service for us. Everything described on this page happens over live video, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, with a free trial lesson before anything is charged.

sections.heading: DP1 and DP2 need different help, and families buy the wrong one
paragraphs: The first and second years of the Diploma are different jobs and most tutoring is sold as though they were the same. In the first year the risk is foundational: a student who does not consolidate the early units carries a gap into a two-year linear course with no mechanism for catching up. In the second year the risk is operational: too many deadlines colliding, internal assessments competing with mock examinations, and a student who knows the content losing marks to pace and presentation.

First-year work should therefore be content-led and unhurried, one subject, weekly, with the internal assessment's research question raised early rather than late. The single most useful thing a tutor does in the first year is force the exploration or investigation question to be interrogated before data exists, because an unworkable question discovered in the second year costs weeks that are not available.

Second-year work should be triage. Which components are still movable, which are already submitted, where does the arithmetic say points are recoverable, and what can realistically be done in the weeks remaining before study leave. A second-year family asking for weekly content coverage across three subjects usually needs something sharper and smaller, and saying so costs us revenue and saves them a term.

There is a third case worth naming: the student arriving into the Diploma from a Middle Years Programme or an IGCSE year, which in this catchment is common. The gap is not content, it is independence and assessment literacy. A student used to criterion marks or to IGCSE's structured question types meets a Diploma paper expecting sustained argument and extended reasoning, and the adjustment takes a term. Tutoring that recognises this spends the first sessions on how the assessment works, not on the next unit.

sections.heading: Which Diploma subjects this catchment is actually short of
paragraphs: Patterns in enquiries from eastern Dubai are consistent enough to be worth publishing, because they tell you where to expect difficulty finding help regardless of who you ask. Mathematics at both routes and both levels is well covered. Chemistry and Biology are well covered. Physics at Higher Level is noticeably thinner than at Standard Level, which matters because Higher Level Physics is also one of the most commonly required subjects for engineering routes.

Economics and Business Management at Higher Level are moderately covered, with the constraint being the internal assessment rather than the papers; plenty of tutors can teach the theory and fewer can tell a student why their chosen news article cannot support the key concept they have selected. English A at Higher Level is similar: teaching the texts is easy to find, teaching the HL essay against its four criteria is less so.

The genuinely thin areas are Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts, Film, Theatre and first-language literature in languages other than English. For these, expect a match to take one to two weeks and expect the specialist to be outside the UAE, teaching over the same platform at a Gulf Standard Time slot. We publish that rather than concealing it, because the alternative is a family discovering in week three that their Psychology tutor is a Biology teacher.

None of this changes with proximity. A search for a Visual Arts Diploma specialist within reach of Muhaisnah returns almost nothing, and that is not a failure of the search. It is a supply fact about a programme that serves roughly 7% of Dubai's private-school pupils and concentrates in particular districts. The only lever available is widening the geography, which is exactly what a live video lesson does.

sections.heading: Four minutes that separate a specialist from a subject graduate
paragraphs: Use this on any tutor, local or online, including ours. Four questions, none of which requires you to know the subject. First: how is my child's final grade in this subject made up, component by component, with the percentages? A specialist answers immediately and in numbers. Second: what is the internally assessed component called in this subject, and what are its criteria worth? The name changes by subject, and a tutor who says "the coursework" has answered a different question.

Third: what will you not do with my child's internal assessment? You want this answered firmly and without prompting, because the providers who will write it exist in this market and one of them publishes a price for completed work. Fourth: name one thing my child should be able to do after six sessions that they cannot do now. A specialist narrows this rather than widening it, and the narrowness is the signal.

If a tutor's answers are vague on the first two, they teach the subject rather than the qualification, which is adequate for the Middle Years Programme and inadequate for a second-year Diploma student eight weeks from study leave. If they hedge on the third, stop. If the fourth answer is "improve their grade", they are planning to improvise, and improvisation at AED 200 an hour is an expensive way to pass an evening.

Our free trial lesson exists to be used this way. We would rather a family interrogate the match in the first thirty minutes and reject it than discover the mismatch in March. A tutor who resents those four questions is telling you something useful at no cost.
