faqs.question: Is there an IB specialist living near Muhaisnah at all?
faqs.answer: For well-covered subjects, yes, somebody will travel to this part of Dubai, and the published market band for in-home visits is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. For a Higher Level specialist in Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts or a first-language literature option, realistically no. The schools around Muhaisnah teach mostly Indian and British curricula, so the local private-tutoring market reflects that rather than the Diploma. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses in any case; we match on the course and level and teach one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: How are the 45 Diploma points actually put together?
faqs.answer: Six subjects each graded 1 to 7 give a maximum of 42. The final three come from a matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade with the Extended Essay grade. A Diploma requires a minimum of 24 points plus a set of further conditions on individual grades and the core components, so reaching 24 does not by itself guarantee the award. The practical consequence is that the matrix points are often the cheapest available, and a student treating the Extended Essay as paperwork is leaving points that would cost far more hours to recover in a Higher Level science.

faqs.question: What does my school's KHDA band actually tell me about my child?
faqs.answer: Less than the detail underneath it. KHDA inspects annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes subject-level and phase-level findings, and those are the useful part. If your child is struggling in a subject the report identifies as a relative weakness in their phase, that is partly a provision question and extra support genuinely supplements. If they are struggling in a subject the report calls a strength, the issue is more likely their own technique, which is cheaper and quicker to address. Read the report with that specific question in mind.

faqs.question: My child picked three Higher Levels and is drowning. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask a narrower question than "how do we fix all three". Work out which Higher Level grade is genuinely recoverable, which needs only to be stabilised so it does not damage the total, and whether a Standard Level subject sitting at a 5 could reach a 6 more cheaply. A point is a point regardless of where it comes from, and the total does not care. Families resist this because the hardest subject feels like the problem, but the arithmetic usually says the available point is somewhere else, and it is a far shorter piece of work.

faqs.question: Which Diploma internal assessment criterion carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: It varies by component and it is worth knowing for your child's. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 and criterion C, Critical thinking, carries 12 of those on its own. The Mathematics exploration is out of 20 with Use of mathematics worth 6. The science investigation is out of 24 across four criteria of 6 each. The Theory of Knowledge essay is judged out of 10 as a single global impression. Confirm against the current subject guide for your child's cohort, because allocations change when a guide is reissued.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child takes Maths AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and the consequence is at university rather than at school. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra and calculus route, commonly required for engineering and many science programmes, often at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, accepted for business, social sciences and several economics programmes. Check the specific requirement of the destination before committing, because changing route in the second year is usually not possible. If the route is already wrong for the target, the conversation is about alternative entry paths rather than about tutoring.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a tutor for a less common IB subject?
faqs.answer: One to two weeks for Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts, Film, Theatre and most first-language literature options other than English, and the specialist will usually be outside the UAE teaching over the same platform at a Gulf Standard Time slot. Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology are typically two to five days. Physics at Higher Level sits in between. We publish the wait rather than filling the slot, because the alternative is a family finding out in week three that their Psychology tutor teaches Biology.

faqs.question: Is a first-year Diploma student too early for tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and the first year is where the money goes furthest. A linear two-year course has no built-in mechanism for catching up, so a gap left in the first term is carried to the final paper. The highest-value first-year work is forcing the internal assessment question to be interrogated before any data exists, because an unworkable exploration or investigation discovered in the second year costs weeks that are not available. Second-year support is triage by comparison, useful but working with much less room to manoeuvre.

faqs.question: My child moved into the Diploma from MYP and the grades fell. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is extremely common in this catchment and it is usually not a content problem. A student used to criterion-marked tasks meets a Diploma paper that wants sustained argument and extended reasoning, and the adjustment takes roughly a term. The same happens coming in from IGCSE, where question structures are more scaffolded. Useful tutoring spends the first few sessions on how the assessment works, with the subject content as the vehicle rather than the target, and parents who understand that stop reading the first report as a verdict.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my child's Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the correct version of that help is narrow. A tutor can read the draft against the five published criteria, say which descriptor is not yet met, question whether the research question is answerable in the word limit, and test the quality of the sources. A tutor cannot write, restructure or finish any part of it. The school allocates a supervisor who owns the formal process, and the most useful session before a supervisor meeting is often rehearsing the questions the student will be asked about their own progress.

faqs.question: Why would an online tutor be better than one who comes to our building?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, both measurable. First, who you can choose: restricting the list to tutors who can reach Muhaisnah at six in the evening removes most people who teach a particular Diploma course for a living and keeps the generalists. Second, delivered teaching minutes: a tutor crossing Al Ittihad Road at the afternoon peak arrives late more weeks than not, and across thirty weeks that is several complete lessons. The genuine exception is a younger child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, where in-home work is the right purchase.

faqs.question: What should we be doing about Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Treating it as assessed work rather than as a discussion class. The essay is judged out of 10 against a single global assessment instrument, and together with the Extended Essay grade it feeds a matrix worth up to three Diploma points. Students who read it as unmarkable opinion write unmarkable essays. The teachable part is using a prescribed title as a genuine question, building an argument on specific knowledge claims with real examples, and handling the counter-position properly rather than mentioning it in a final sentence.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Agree one specific capability in advance and check it at session six using the student's own marked work, not impressions. For a Diploma student that is usually a technique: propagating uncertainties without prompting, labelling a diagram fully under time pressure, or writing an evaluation paragraph that weighs and concludes. If it has not moved, the diagnosis or the match is wrong and should change. Waiting for the next school report is too slow, because the report lands after the term you were trying to rescue.

faqs.question: Are there cases where you tell a family not to book?
faqs.answer: Regularly. A second-year student eight weeks from the session with four subjects below target needs triage and a conversation with their IB coordinator, not four tutors. A student whose marked papers show the content is secure and the timing collapses needs a short technique block, not a year-long weekly slot. A student who is not sleeping needs neither. We would rather say that at the consultation and lose the booking than sell a package that was never going to work from a Muhaisnah address or anywhere else.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.closingBody: If you remember one thing from this page, make it the four questions. Ask any tutor how the grade is built, what the internal assessment criteria are worth, what they will refuse to do with it, and what your child will be able to do after six sessions. The answers take four minutes and they are a far better filter than a map. Send us the course and level as the school writes them, the predicted grades, the last marked paper and the two evening slots that survive your school run, and we will name a specialist and offer a free trial lesson. Nothing is charged before it, and we will tell you if the honest answer is that tutoring is not your best lever.

intro.heading: What the phrase near me is really asking, and a better answer
paragraphs: Typing near me into a search box is a proxy. What a parent in Nad Al Hamar actually wants is somebody reliable, available at a usable hour, who knows the Diploma course their child is sitting. Proximity is a reasonable stand-in for the first two of those and useless for the third. A district on the eastern side of Dubai, bounded by the Ras Al Khor sanctuary and the Dubai-Al Ain Road, has a certain number of resident subject specialists, and in a Higher Level science or a minority language that number can be zero.

The search also hides a second assumption, which is that lessons happen in person. For UAE families, IB Gram's teaching is online: one-to-one, live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the country; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature. It is the reason a Nad Al Hamar family can be matched to a tutor who has taken four students through a Physics internal assessment rather than to whoever lives two streets away.

Once geography stops being the organising variable, the useful one becomes the calendar. The Diploma is a two-year qualification sitting inside a UAE school year that runs from late August to June, with a winter break, a spring break, Ramadan somewhere in the first half of the calendar year, and a May examination session. Each of those does something specific to what a student can absorb and what a tutor should be doing. Most families discover this by accident in their second year.

This page therefore sets out the year rather than the sales pitch: what each term is for, how Ramadan reshapes a month, the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside the Diploma in every Dubai private school and consume timetable time that families forget to count, the regulator map across the seven emirates, and the four provider models you are choosing between when you hire anyone at all. There is a rate table with sources, because three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price.

Nad Al Hamar children travel out to schools in Dubai Festival City, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Academic City, and come home between about 3.50pm and 4.35pm. That one fact drives the practical half of everything below, because a plan that cannot survive the school run is not a plan. The second practical fact is that an online slot can be held at 6.30pm reliably, which an in-home visit crossing the same roads cannot. The rest of this page is the year in detail, the Ramadan pattern, the mandatory subject rules, the regulator map and a model-level rate comparison.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-hamar.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run in Dubai schools and the near-me question arrives from families in all three, with quite different needs.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity and service requirement. Most subjects carry an internally assessed component marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The grade is accumulated across two years, which is why the calendar rather than the hourly rate is the thing that decides outcomes.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in a Dubai private school also carries the emirate's mandatory subjects, because KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed curriculum. That is timetable time a family planning six Diploma subjects plus tutoring tends not to count, and it is a real constraint on the week.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, with a Personal Project in the final year. Grades are reported on a one-to-eight scale per criterion rather than as percentages, which is the thing parents most often ask a tutor to translate. The useful work here is the generalisation and justification the criteria reward, which school reports rarely explain.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Hamar families with a child in MYP 4 or 5 have one decision worth attention: standard or extended mathematics. Extended is the honest route into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student who takes standard and then chooses AA HL has a gap that shows in the first term of DP1.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations and mathematics and literacy embedded in units of inquiry. Support at this stage is about fluency and written method rather than technique, and short frequent sessions work better than long ones because attention rather than content is the constraint.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools also deliver the mandatory UAE subjects from the primary years, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ between the two groups.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-hamar.subjectsIntro: The near-me search is subject-blind, which is its main weakness. These are the Diploma subjects Nad Al Hamar families ask about, with the specific thing that usually needs fixing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Non-calculator technique at Paper 1 and, at Higher Level, an extended investigation paper. The problem is almost always hand fluency rather than understanding, because a student fluent with a graphic display calculator can carry a hidden algebra gap for years.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology throughout. At Higher Level the statistical content is substantially harder than the course's reputation, and the students who struggle are often the ones who chose it to avoid calculus.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment, graph linearisation and the mathematical handling of fields. The internal assessment loses marks on data processing rather than on experimental design, which is a specific and quickly teachable gap.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry is where Higher Level separates, and calculation accuracy under time pressure explains most of the rest. Significant figures and units cost single marks repeatedly across a whole paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume plus command-term precision. Students who revise by rereading accumulate knowledge they cannot deploy, and the fix is answering past questions under timed conditions rather than covering the syllabus again.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Taken as a Diploma language and, separately, required as a mandatory subject in Dubai private schools. KHDA requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold the authority's approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential point at school level.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure carry the essay papers, with quantitative questions added at Higher Level. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries, and article selection is the step that quietly determines the mark.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the comparative essay and the individual oral. The oral is the component most often left unrehearsed and the one that rehearses best on video, because the format is already a conversation through a screen.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The essay is capped at 4,000 words; TOK carries an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Both are coached rather than taught, and the limit on what a tutor may do is tighter here than anywhere else in the programme.

sections.heading: The UAE school year as a Diploma student lives it
paragraphs: A Dubai private school year runs from late August to June, with a winter break around the turn of the year, a spring break, and a short mid-term break in each half. Layered on that are the school's internal Diploma deadlines, a mock window, Ramadan in the first half of the calendar year, and the May session itself. The shape repeats, which is why naming the months rather than the dates is both safer and more useful.

August and September are the cheapest months in which to fix something and the ones nobody buys. A DP1 student is meeting the step up from IGCSE or MYP, and a DP2 student has coursework already due. Both are at a point where an hour spent on study method, note systems and the handling of command terms pays for the whole year. The first term is also when subject and level choices either settle or start to fail, and a change of level is easier in October than in February.

October to the winter break is content, with the first internal assessment deadlines appearing for DP2 students. After the break comes the mock window at most Dubai schools, and then a stretch in which predicted grades are issued and coursework is finalised. The spring is revision. By the final six to eight weeks the honest work is timed papers, mark-scheme logic and error correction, because content learned at that point rarely reaches a paper.

Two things about the year are worth stating because this market gets them wrong. First, UAE schools sit the May Diploma session, and specific IB session and results dates are not published on this page because they are revised and we have not verified them with the IB; your coordinator and ibo.org are the sources. Second, for the IGCSE year below, Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series and Pearson Edexcel runs May and June and November. The February and March series is India only.

sections.heading: Ramadan, and how a Diploma plan should be built around it
paragraphs: Ramadan reshapes a month of the UAE academic year, and a tutoring plan that ignores it loses that month. School days shorten, which brings the Nad Al Hamar door time forward by an hour or more and changes what the afternoon can hold. Household rhythms change in the evening. Students fasting are not at full capacity in the late afternoon. None of this is an obstacle if it is planned; all of it is an obstacle if it is improvised in the second week.

Two patterns work. The first is the early-afternoon session, taken advantage of because the school day has finished earlier than usual, with the session kept short at forty-five minutes. The second is the post-Iftar slot, later in the evening, which suits older students and families who prefer the evening undisturbed before the meal. Both are straightforward over video. Neither works well with a tutor driving across the eastern suburbs at Iftar, which is a genuine practical argument rather than a rhetorical one.

The planning consequence sits before the month rather than inside it. A DP2 student whose revision schedule assumes a normal Ramadan will fall behind, and the four weeks after it are already close to the session. The correct move is to front-load: bring forward the content-heavy work into the preceding weeks, and treat the Ramadan weeks as maintenance, with lighter sessions aimed at retention rather than new material.

The second planning consequence is about internal deadlines. If a school's coursework date falls during or immediately after Ramadan, the drafting work has to be done before. Students routinely plan to use the month for writing and then do not, and a tutor who looks at the school's internal calendar in advance can flag that in September rather than discover it in the last fortnight.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects nobody counts in the timetable
paragraphs: A Diploma student in a Dubai private school is not only doing the Diploma. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. That is timetabled time, and families planning six Diploma subjects plus tutoring consistently fail to count it.

The rules have real texture. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the authority's approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential question a parent can ask at a school meeting.

One constraint affects how tutoring in these subjects can honestly be described. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support in Arabic as an additional language is therefore about fluency, exposure and the school's own material rather than about a parallel scheme, and any provider offering its own curriculum for these subjects is describing something the rules do not permit.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it is worth knowing
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai hear KHDA and assume it is the national position. It is not. The UAE has five bodies covering private schools and the map is worth holding, particularly for a family who may move emirate. In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools.

In Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge does the same. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum and fee approval sits with the regulator rather than only inspection.

Why a parent should care: the regulator sets the inspection regime that produces the rating on your child's school, and it is the body to approach with a complaint that the school has not resolved. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

Worth saying plainly, because this market gets it wrong: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge International or Pearson, and claims none of those things. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we hold no premises in the UAE and therefore no such permit. Any provider describing its tutors as regulator-approved should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Agency, marketplace, freelance or centre: what you are choosing between
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself favourably to an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing. The honest comparison is at the level of model, because each model has a structural strength and a structural weakness that no amount of service quality changes. There are four, plus the school's own support, and the right answer depends on what is wrong rather than on which is best.

An agency selects and manages tutors, charges more, and carries the replacement risk. A marketplace lists many tutors cheaply and leaves the selection to you, which suits a confident parent and punishes an uncertain one. A freelance tutor hired directly is the cheapest per hour for the same quality and the least resilient: one illness and a term's rhythm stops. A tuition centre group class is the cheapest per head and moves at the scheme's pace rather than your child's.

The school's own support is the option families forget and should try first, because it is usually free and always aligned with the actual assessment. Subject clinics, coursework surgeries and the coordinator's own guidance cost nothing and the staff know the internal deadlines. A parent who has not asked what the school offers before paying for tutoring may be buying something already available.

IB Gram sits in the agency column: we select, match and replace, we publish what we will not do, and we do not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE. sections.heading: The Nad Al Hamar evening, measured rather than assumed
paragraphs: Everything above is academic until it meets the school run. Nad Al Hamar is twelve to fifteen minutes from Dubai Festival City off-peak and twenty to twenty-five at pickup. Mirdif is eighteen to twenty off-peak and thirty to thirty-five at 3pm. Al Qusais and Academic City are longer. Door times land between 3.50pm and 4.35pm on an ordinary day, after 5pm on an activity day, and earlier during Ramadan.

A Diploma student then needs some of the evening for their own work, which is not optional and not compressible. The slot that holds across a full term is 6pm to 7.30pm, often ninety minutes rather than sixty once coursework is live, because reading a draft and discussing it properly does not fit into an hour. For revision blocks the pattern changes to shorter and more frequent, with a weekend morning for the one session that needs a full timed paper plus review.

The reason this is a real argument rather than a stylistic preference is that an in-home tutor travelling to Nad Al Hamar at 5.40pm is on the same roads your child came home on, and will build a buffer into their schedule to absorb that. The buffer is paid for either in the rate or in the start time. An online session at 6.30pm starts at 6.30pm, every week, including the weeks when the roads are worst.

For households with two or three children, the pattern that works is consecutive slots on one evening rather than different tutors on different days. One-to-one means one student in the session, so two children cannot share an hour, but they can share an evening, and giving up one weeknight is easier than giving up three.

sections.heading: What a first session should prove, and what it should not promise
paragraphs: A trial lesson is a test of the match, not a sales meeting, and a parent should judge it on evidence rather than on rapport alone. Three things should come out of forty-five minutes. The tutor should be able to name, specifically, what your child does not yet do: not weak on calculus, but does not recognise when the chain rule applies. They should be able to say which component or paper the marks are being lost on. And they should say what they would leave alone, because a tutor who proposes to fix everything has not diagnosed anything.

What a first session should not produce is a predicted outcome. Nobody can promise a grade, a points total or an improvement of a stated size, and a provider who does is making a claim they cannot stand behind. Treat a guaranteed result with real scepticism; it is the clearest signal available that the person talking is selling rather than teaching. The same applies to any statistic offered without a number of students, a date and a method behind it.

The practical mechanics of our trial: forty-five minutes, one-to-one over live video, no card details collected, no obligation afterwards, and a short written note to the parent naming what the tutor found. If what your child needs is a different pace, a different personality or a tutor who asks questions rather than demonstrates methods, say so and we propose someone else. Those mismatches are visible in one session and expensive to leave in place.

Finally, the question some parents still want to ask after all of the above: will someone come to the house. No. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we provide in India only. If an adult in the room is the requirement, hire an independent local tutor, ask to see their MoHRE private tuition work permit, and use the published rate bands on this page to judge whether the quote is fair.

faqs.question: Why does a search for a tutor near Nad Al Hamar return so few IB specialists?
faqs.answer: Because the search sorts by distance from a residential district on the eastern edge of Dubai, and resident Diploma specialists are thinly spread. In a Higher Level science or a minority language the number living within a twenty-minute radius can be zero on any given evening. Once lessons move to live video the constraint disappears and the pool becomes everyone who has taught that course at that level. That is the main practical argument for the online model, and it is specific rather than rhetorical.

faqs.question: Which month should we start Diploma tutoring if we want value for money?
faqs.answer: September, and almost nobody does. The first term is when study method, note systems and command-term handling can be fixed cheaply and compound for two years. The spring of DP1 is the next best, because internal assessment topics are chosen then and a thin topic sets a ceiling nothing later can raise. The expensive month is April of DP2, where the content window has closed and the only remaining gains are pacing, technique and accuracy.

faqs.question: How should a DP2 revision plan handle the Ramadan weeks?
faqs.answer: Front-load. Bring content-heavy work into the weeks before the month, and treat the Ramadan weeks as maintenance: shorter sessions, retention rather than new material. School days shorten, so the door time comes forward by an hour or more and an early-afternoon slot becomes available; the alternative is a post-Iftar session. Fix which pattern you want in advance rather than improvising in week two, and check whether any coursework deadline lands during or just after the month.

faqs.question: What are the mandatory UAE subjects my child takes alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: In Dubai private schools, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. That is timetabled time families rarely count when planning six Diploma subjects plus tutoring.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates our school, and does it regulate tutors too?
faqs.answer: In Dubai it is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, Sharjah is SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah is the Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the Ministry of Education. Individual tutors are a separate matter: they need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is free and valid for two years. A business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA training-institute permit.

faqs.question: Is an agency worth paying for rather than hiring a tutor directly?
faqs.answer: It depends what you need. Hiring directly is cheaper for the same quality and has no cover: one illness and the term's rhythm stops. An agency charges more and carries selection, matching and replacement. A marketplace is cheap and leaves selection to you. A centre group class is cheapest per head and moves at the scheme's pace. Before any of them, ask what your child's school already offers free, because subject clinics and coursework surgeries are aligned with the actual assessment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in another country teach a Dubai Diploma student properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided two conditions hold. The tutor works on Gulf Standard Time, so a 6.30pm Nad Al Hamar slot is an ordinary slot rather than an awkward one, and they know the course your child is actually sitting rather than a national variant of it. What they cannot do is tell you your school's internal deadlines, which is why we ask for the school's own calendar at the start. A tutor who has never seen your school's assessment schedule is working half blind.

faqs.question: What should a first Diploma session actually tell us?
faqs.answer: Three specific things. What your child does not yet do, named precisely rather than generally: not weak at calculus, but does not recognise when the chain rule applies. Which paper or component the marks are being lost on. And what the tutor would leave alone, because a plan to fix everything is a plan built on no diagnosis. What it should not produce is a predicted grade or a promised improvement, and a provider offering one is selling rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Do you have an office in Dubai we could visit?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE and does not claim one. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run in India only. We mention this because two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers while displaying a local address, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. A stated address you cannot visit is worth questioning.

faqs.question: Which schools would a Nad Al Hamar Diploma student usually attend?
faqs.answer: Mostly the Dubai Festival City cluster, including Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai, and the Mirdif and Al Mizhar belt, including Uptown International School. Other eastern-suburb schools take students to IGCSE before an A Level or Diploma split. Dubai had 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate a modest share of enrolment next to the UK and Indian curricula. Schools are named here as local context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of tutoring is reasonable for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: One session a week in the subject that most threatens the points total is the sensible default, rising to two in DP2 or before a mock window. Beyond two the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time rather than taught hours, and additional sessions displace the independent work that actually consolidates learning. A student carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay has less spare capacity than an hourly plan suggests. Start at one and review at four weeks.

faqs.question: Our family travels for most of the summer. Can sessions continue?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer between DP1 and DP2 is one of the best windows to use. Agree the time-zone shift before the trip rather than during it, run at a lighter frequency, and aim the work at internal assessment drafting, which benefits from calm weeks more than from term-time urgency. Sessions resume at the usual Gulf Standard Time slot on return. This continuity is the single most common reason families in the eastern suburbs moved to video delivery in the first place.

faqs.question: Is there any way to check how good our school actually is?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the regulator rather than through a tutoring site. Dubai private schools are inspected by KHDA and the published rating sits on a six-band scale from the highest to the weakest. Abu Dhabi schools are inspected by ADEK, Sharjah by SPEA. Read the published report rather than the headline band, because the subject-level and phase-level detail is where a parent learns whether the weakness is in the years their own child is in. We do not publish ratings we have not read on the regulator's own site.

faqs.question: What do you refuse to do, so we know before booking?
faqs.answer: Four things. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; teaching is online and home visits are India-only. We do not produce, rewrite or edit assessed work, in any subject, at any price. We do not host or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because they belong to the IB and the boards. And we do not claim approval, accreditation or partnership from any regulator, board or school, because we hold none.

Each one works to a named syllabus and a named paper, not a general subject label, so a Nad Al Sheba student sitting Chemistry HL gets a Chemistry HL teacher rather than a generalist science tutor.

intro.heading: What a Nad Al Sheba parent is really asking when they type this
paragraphs: Nad Al Sheba sits between Dubai–Al Ain Road and the Meydan corridor, which puts a cluster of large private schools within a short drive and a very different set of schools within a long one. Families here send children to Repton School Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy inside the district itself, to Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai across in Sobha Hartland, and to Swiss International Scientific School Dubai over at Al Jaddaf. Several of those schools run the IB Diploma; several run it alongside a British secondary track. So a search for an IB tutor near me in Nad Al Sheba is rarely a search for geography. It is a search for somebody who knows the exact course the child is enrolled on.

That distinction matters because the IB is not one syllabus. A student in DP1 at one Nad Al Sheba school may be taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level with a 20-mark exploration due in term two, while a neighbour two streets away is taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level with a completely different Paper 2 and a graphic-display-calculator requirement throughout. A tutor who covers maths but has never marked an AA HL Paper 3 is the wrong tutor for the first student and a perfectly good one for the second. Distance tells you nothing about which you are getting.

The second thing hidden inside the query is time. Nad Al Sheba school days end between 14:30 and 15:30 depending on the school and the year group, and the drive back from the Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf schools in afternoon traffic eats most of an hour. A tutor who has to cross Dubai to reach you either arrives at 17:30 or charges for the journey. Online delivery removes that arithmetic entirely: a 16:00 session is a 16:00 session, and the half-hour saved either side is the difference between a child who can concentrate and one who cannot.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation, and the rest of this page argues it on the evidence: the market rate for a home visit in Dubai carries a travel premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour over the same teaching delivered online, and what that premium buys is proximity rather than subject depth.

Everything below is built around syllabus content, because that is the part no competing page in this search publishes. You will find the assessment weightings by paper, the command terms that turn a correct answer into a zero, the internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations, the published word limits for every DP component, what the KHDA inspection band on your school's report actually means, and the academic-honesty line a tutor may not cross. Where a figure is a market rate rather than ours, it is attributed to whoever published it and dated.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-sheba.programmesIntro: Nad Al Sheba students arrive at the IB by three different routes: a full continuum from PYP, a jump from a British Year 11 into DP1, or a move from MYP into the Diploma inside the same school. Each route leaves a different gap, and the three programmes below are described in terms of the gap rather than the brochure.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP assesses through transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than terminal papers, which is why a strong PYP report can sit alongside a shaky grasp of written number work. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic: find whether the child can explain a method aloud, whether place value and fraction equivalence are secure, and whether reading comprehension holds up on an unfamiliar text. The exhibition in the final PYP year is the first piece of extended independent work most children produce, and it rewards planning more than knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP sits alongside KHDA's mandatory subjects: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. A Nad Al Sheba family new to the emirate often meets Arabic as a timetabled subject for the first time here, and that is frequently the first tutoring request.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks on a 1-8 scale against four criteria per subject, and the criteria are published. A student scoring 5s is usually losing marks in one criterion consistently rather than everywhere, and the fix is to read that criterion's wording with them. The MYP eAssessment and the Personal Project in the final year are where the programme becomes concrete, and the Personal Project is assessed on the process journal as much as the product.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Sheba sits near schools running MYP into DP inside one building, so the transition is internal and the school controls the pacing. That makes the MYP-to-DP gap narrower on paper and wider in practice: students who were never examined under timed conditions meet their first two-hour paper in DP1. Mock-paper practice under a clock is the single most useful thing to add in the final MYP year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The arithmetic matters: 42 points come from the six subjects at 7 each, and up to 3 more from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. A student with three HL subjects is carrying three internal assessments, an Extended Essay and a TOK essay in the same twelve months, and the failure mode is almost never ability. It is sequencing.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. Dubai DP students also carry the KHDA mandatory subjects alongside the Diploma, which compresses the timetable further than a DP cohort in Europe would recognise. Published IB session and results dates are not restated here: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills, reflective project, service learning and language development. It is offered in a small number of UAE schools and is sometimes the right answer for a student who is strong in two subjects and sinking under six. Tutoring here concentrates on the DP courses carried forward and on the reflective project, which is assessed on process evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP provision in Dubai is thin, families comparing it against a full Diploma usually need a conversation about MoE equivalency before they commit. Equivalency rules are set by the Ministry of Education and must be checked on moe.gov.ae for the specific qualification combination; nobody at a tutoring platform can decide that for you, and no page should imply otherwise.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-sheba.subjectsIntro: Below are the DP subjects Nad Al Sheba students most often ask for, described by what the assessment actually tests and where the marks go missing. The descriptions name papers and weightings because that is the level at which tutoring decisions get made.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: HL adds Paper 3, a two-question extended investigation worth 20% of the grade, and it is the paper that separates a 6 from a 7. Students lose marks by writing conclusions the working does not support and by abandoning a part-marked question halfway. The exploration carries another 20% and is marked on criteria A to E over 20 marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A calculator is assumed throughout, which misleads students into skipping the algebra that justifies an answer. Statistics and modelling dominate, and marks disappear in the interpretation sentence at the end of a question rather than in the computation. HL adds Paper 3 with extended data-driven problems.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The new syllabus is organised around five themes, and HL extension content is examined alongside core material rather than in a separate paper. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and data analysis. Marks go in unit errors, in failing to state an assumption, and in describing a graph instead of using its gradient.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity are the two organising themes, and the HL additions sit inside both. The scientific investigation is worth 20% and is marked on four criteria over 24 marks with a 3,000-word limit. Energetics and equilibrium questions are where sign conventions quietly cost two marks at a time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do more damage in Biology than in any other science: an answer that explains when the paper said outline earns the outline marks only. The syllabus is unification-and-diversity themed, and data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments reward reading the axes carefully more than recall.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis on unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 a comparative essay, and the Individual Oral is assessed on four criteria over 40 marks. The HL essay adds a 1,200-1,500 word formal essay. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing the writer's choices.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, not decorative: an unlabelled axis or a missing new equilibrium point costs marks that the surrounding prose cannot recover. Paper 3 at HL is quantitative and policy-focused. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, each with its own word limit.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools — Ansoff, BCG, force field analysis — are examined for application to the stimulus, not for definition. HL adds the business research project. Standard-level students lose marks by listing a tool's parts instead of using it to reach a judgement the question asked for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions are specified by the IB and are marked as written, which catches students who code fluently in Python and translate loosely. HL adds abstract data structures and resource management. The solution development internal assessment is assessed on documented process, not on how impressive the program looks.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic under KHDA requirements, and the DP language B route is where that obligation meets an examined grade. Productive writing is assessed on message, language and conceptual understanding of audience and purpose, so register errors cost more than vocabulary gaps.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK essay is 1,600 words on one of six prescribed titles, and the exhibition presents three objects against a knowledge question. Students write about the topic rather than about knowledge, which is the single most common reason a thoughtful essay lands in band C rather than band A.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words in a chosen DP subject, marked on five criteria over 34 marks, with the reflections on planning and progress contributing directly. A tutor may discuss method, scope and argument structure and give written feedback; a tutor may not draft, rewrite or supply text for it.

sections.heading: What this search returns in Nad Al Sheba, and what it should return
paragraphs: Typing an IB tutor near me in Nad Al Sheba into Google produces three kinds of result: agency pages with no prices, marketplace listings sorted by distance, and blog posts about the area written by somebody who has never been in it. None of them answer the question a parent is actually holding, which is whether the person they are about to pay knows the paper their child is sitting in five months.

Distance is a poor proxy for that. A tutor eight minutes away in Meydan may teach general science to Year 9 and have never seen a DP Chemistry investigation marked against the four criteria. A specialist who teaches Chemistry HL every weekday afternoon is the better answer even though the lesson arrives over video. The research behind this page measured sixty competitor pages in this market: three of six publish no price at all, five of six carry no data table, and the best page in the cluster runs about 2,294 words. The information a parent needs to decide simply is not on those pages.

So the honest version of the answer is this. Nad Al Sheba is well served for schools and poorly served for subject-specific tutors, because the pool of people within a twenty-minute drive who teach one IB subject at one level is small by arithmetic. Online one-to-one widens that pool to the whole timezone without widening the price. The sections that follow give you the syllabus detail to test any tutor you speak to, including ours — the command terms, the criteria letters, the weightings and the limits. A tutor who cannot discuss those fluently is not a specialist, whatever the map says.

sections.heading: Command terms: where a correct answer still scores nothing
paragraphs: The IB publishes a command-term glossary for every subject, and examiners mark to it. A student who writes a complete and accurate explanation in response to a question that said state has written something true and unmarked. This is the most recoverable source of lost marks in the whole Diploma, because it costs nothing to learn and shows up on every paper.

The pattern in Nad Al Sheba cohorts is consistent with the pattern everywhere: students who moved into the DP from a British Year 11 over-write, because IGCSE rewarded detail; students who came up through MYP under-write, because MYP criteria rewarded reflection over precision. Both groups need the same drill, from opposite directions. Twenty minutes of a weekly session on command terms for four weeks changes a paper score more reliably than four more hours of content revision.

The table below covers the terms that appear most often across the science, maths and humanities papers. Learn the mark bracket alongside the term: a two-mark question wants two scoring points and nothing else, and the time spent on a third point is time stolen from a later question. Past-paper work is where this becomes automatic, which is why a revision block is spent on marking rather than on sitting.

One more thing is worth drilling alongside the term itself: the number of scoring points the mark bracket implies. A three-mark explain question wants three linked statements, and a student who writes five is being generous with time they will need on the last page. Nad Al Sheba students sitting three Higher Level subjects run out of minutes on at least one paper most mock seasons, and almost always on the paper where they wrote most.

sections.heading: Internal assessment by criteria letter, mark allocation and word limit
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where a Nad Al Sheba DP student's grade is decided quietly, months before the papers. In maths and the sciences it carries 20% of the subject grade. In some humanities and language courses it carries more. It is marked against published criteria with published mark allocations, and the student can read those criteria. Most do not, which is the whole opportunity.

The published limits are equally concrete and equally ignored. A 3,000-word scientific investigation that runs to 4,200 words has not impressed anybody; the excess is unread. A TOK essay is 1,600 words against one of six prescribed titles, and an essay that writes about the topic instead of about knowledge lands in a lower band however elegant it is. An Extended Essay is 4,000 words marked over five criteria and 34 marks, with the reflections on planning contributing directly to the total.

The table below is the reference sheet. Check it against your child's current subject guide before relying on it, because the IB revises components on a rolling cycle and the school's coordinator holds the current version. What the table is for is the conversation a parent needs to have at the start of DP1: which of these is due when, in what order, and which two of them collide in the same month.

One further habit helps more than any content revision in DP1. Ask your child to read the criterion wording aloud and then say, in their own words, what a top-band response does differently from a middle-band one. If they cannot, the criteria have not been read, and no amount of redrafting will fix a piece of work that was aimed at the wrong target. This takes ten minutes and it is the cheapest mark recovery available in the Diploma.

sections.heading: What a parent in Nad Al Sheba can verify about tutoring prices
paragraphs: Start with what you can check yourself, because that is the only pricing claim worth anything. Open the five or six tutoring sites that rank for this search and look for a number. Three of the six measured for this page publish none. Two quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. One publishes an hourly rate that contradicts the price in its own structured data. That is the state of pricing transparency in this market, and it is why the figures below are attributed rather than asserted.

The bands come from competitor pages that published them and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They describe the market, not IB Gram's price list. The spread is wide for a reason: the bottom of it buys a confident undergraduate, the middle buys a trained teacher, and the top buys reputation that may or may not change the lesson. Monthly packages seen across the same set run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Two practical notes for a Nad Al Sheba budget. First, the in-home band sits AED 50 to 150 an hour above the equivalent online band, and that gap is travel, not teaching. Second, exam-year intensity costs more than exam-year rates: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and the variable driving that is how many sessions a week, not the hourly figure. sections.heading: The academic-honesty line, written down
paragraphs: This section exists because one page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers IB malpractice procedures, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. Any parent shopping for IB support in Dubai will meet an offer like it, so the boundary is worth having in plain words before you do.

What a tutor may do: teach the content, explain the criteria, discuss a research question's scope and feasibility, suggest a method, point at a weakness in an argument, read a draft the student wrote and return written feedback on it, and model how a different piece of work handles a similar problem. All of that is teaching, and all of it is what the IB expects a supervisor and a tutor to do.

What a tutor may not do: write any part of the submitted text, rewrite a passage into better prose, supply a research question wholesale, produce the data, or edit a draft to completion. The student's declaration on every submitted component says the work is their own. If a tutor's feedback has been incorporated, that is normal and fine — feedback is allowed and expected. Text written by somebody else is not, however it is described. We also do not host, reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are the board's copyright and are linked rather than copied.

Say the boundary out loud with your child rather than leaving it implied. Students rarely set out to breach academic honesty; they drift into it when a deadline is close and somebody offers to help, and the help arrives as text. A student who has been told once, clearly, what feedback looks like and what substitution looks like will recognise the offer when it comes.

sections.heading: Your KHDA report, and what the band on it means
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band. Nad Al Sheba parents use those bands to choose schools and then rarely look at what the band is measuring, which is a missed source of information about where tutoring would help.

The useful move is to read the subject-level commentary rather than the headline band. An inspection report that praises attainment but flags progress in a specific phase is telling you something actionable about that phase's teaching. A report strong on the British secondary section and quieter on the DP cohort is telling you where the school's depth sits. That is a better guide to whether your child needs outside subject support than the overall word on the cover.

Context for the cost conversation: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The emirate's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three IB — creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or accreditation of any kind, and no tutoring platform should imply that it does: a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are about to hire actually permitted to teach here?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in the Nad Al Sheba market asks, and it has a clean answer. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Two consequences follow. First, anyone who tells you the permit is expensive, optional or unavailable to them is either misinformed or not applying. u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts, so no figure should be quoted to you. Second, the permit carries a code of conduct. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's conduct rules similarly bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

For a Dubai family that means one thing in practice: do not arrange paid tutoring with your child's own classroom teacher, however convenient it looks. Ask instead where the tutor is based, what permit or employment basis they hold, and whether lessons are delivered online or in person. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system. It is the authoritative place to check, and it takes a minute.

sections.heading: Past papers, used properly, in the weeks that matter
paragraphs: A Nad Al Sheba student in DP2 generally has access to more past papers than hours, and uses them in the least productive order: front to back, untimed, marking their own work generously. The marking is where the learning is. A paper sat without being marked against the official scheme has taught the student how it feels to sit a paper, which they already knew.

The sequence that works is narrow and dull. Sit one section under the real clock. Mark it against the official scheme, cell by cell, deciding for each lost mark whether it was content, command term, arithmetic or time. Tally the four categories across three papers. Whichever category dominates is the only thing worth working on for the next fortnight, and the other three get ignored on purpose. Students resist this because it means leaving known weaknesses alone; it works because mark recovery is concentrated, not spread.

Where the papers come from matters legally. Schools hold licensed access, and the boards publish specimen and past material through their own platforms. We reference and link official sources — ibo.org, cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com — and work from the copies your school or the board provides. We do not host, reproduce or hand out board papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, because they are copyright material and some of it is unreleased.

The other half of the discipline is question selection, which nobody teaches. On papers with a choice, a student who reads all options and picks in ninety seconds consistently outscores one who starts the first question that looks familiar. That is a drillable skill and it takes about four sessions. It is also the part of exam technique that transfers across every subject your child is sitting, which makes it unusually good value for a single hour.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Families moving into Nad Al Sheba from outside the UAE are regularly surprised by this, and it is the most under-written topic in the entire Dubai tutoring market. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its published requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisation rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

There is a timetable consequence a DP parent should know. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes come out of a week that already holds six Diploma subjects, TOK and CAS. For the mandatory subjects themselves, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so tutoring support for them works within the school's own material rather than around it.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what an IB student needs, and what nobody can tell you yet
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that converts a school-leaving qualification into something a UAE authority recognises, and it decides university applications inside the country. Four of the ten query clusters researched for this project contained no competitor mention of it at all, and one competitor publishes the wrong subject count for the British track. Getting it right is free authority.

For the British track the rules are published and specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is no figure on this page, and that is deliberate. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, so publishing one would be invention. Check the current IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of the equivalency or attestation process, and tutoring is not a requirement for it — anybody suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory procedure.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what we say instead of pretending
paragraphs: Availability is the thing every tutoring page in this market conceals. The pattern in the researched set is a form, a promise of a match within 24 hours, and silence about what happens when the specific subject at the specific level has nobody free. Several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying so. Both are trust failures, and disclosing the limit is cheaper than being caught by it.

Here is the honest shape of coverage for a Nad Al Sheba enquiry. Core DP subjects — Maths AA and AI, the three sciences, English A, Economics, Business Management — are reliably covered at both levels, and a trial session is usually arrangeable within a few days. Less-taken subjects, and specific combinations like a Physics HL tutor who can also take Maths AA HL Paper 3, take longer. Some requests cannot be met at all in a given term, and the right answer then is a date or a no, not a placeholder tutor.

What we do not do is substitute a generalist for a specialist and leave the family to discover it in session three. If the subject-level match is not available, we say so, give an expected timeframe, and you decide. The free trial lesson exists for the same reason: it is the cheapest way for a parent in Nad Al Sheba to test whether the person on the screen actually knows the paper, before any money moves.

process.title: Tell us the course, not the subject
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the year, the exact course code or title, the level, and the next assessment date. 'Maths HL at a Nad Al Sheba school, AA, exploration due in February' gets a specialist. 'Needs help with maths' gets a conversation first. The school's current unit matters more than the syllabus front page.

process.title: A diagnostic trial lesson, free
process.description: One live session with the tutor we think fits. It is spent finding where the marks are going rather than teaching a topic, usually by working a past-paper section and marking it together. You get a written note afterwards saying what the pattern is and how many sessions it suggests. No payment is involved in this lesson.

process.title: Agree the slot and the plan
process.description: Pick a weekly time on Gulf Standard Time that survives the Nad Al Sheba school run and whatever activity sits after it. The plan is written against the school's assessment calendar: which weeks are coursework weeks, which are mock weeks, and which topics are deliberately being left alone until later.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written notes
process.description: Each session ends with a note naming what was covered, what was set, and which criterion or command term the next session targets. Parents in this corridor often ask for the note rather than a progress percentage, because a percentage invented by a tutoring platform means nothing and a criterion letter means something.

process.title: Reassess at the half-term mark
process.description: Six to eight sessions in, the question is whether the mark pattern has moved. If it has not, the diagnosis was wrong or the tutor is not the right fit, and both are our problem to fix. Changing tutor mid-term is normal and costs nothing; carrying on because the slot is booked is how money gets wasted.

process.description: In the term before papers, the weekly subject session usually becomes two or three shorter sessions built entirely around timed sections and official mark schemes. The content work stops. This is also when the written list of topics to leave alone becomes useful, because by then there is no time to cover everything.
