faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor near me in Nad Al Sheba, or is this all online?
faqs.answer: All tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The practical effect for Nad Al Sheba is that your tutor is chosen for knowing your child's exact course rather than for living nearby. The pool of people within a twenty-minute drive who teach one IB subject at one level is small by arithmetic; the pool across the timezone is not. You also avoid the AED 50 to 150 an hour that the market charges for travel.

faqs.question: Which Nad Al Sheba schools do the students you support attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support in this district attend Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba, Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, with others travelling to Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf and to schools across Al Quoz and Dubai Hills. Those schools are named as neighbourhood context only; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them, and we would not describe a school as a client. What matters for a match is which course your child is enrolled on inside the school, not the school's name.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 to 650 upwards at the premium end. Those figures come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, BartyED and Bestimate's Dubai rate table, not from us. For IB Gram's own rate, ask on the consultation; the trial lesson is free and carries no payment.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI, and does it change the tutor we need?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented; Applications and Interpretation is statistical, modelling-led and assumes a graphic display calculator throughout. At Higher Level both add a Paper 3 worth 20% of the grade, but the two Paper 3s test very different things. So yes, it changes the tutor. A tutor who has marked AA HL Paper 3 investigations is not interchangeable with one who has marked AI HL data problems. Name the course, not just the subject, when you ask for a match.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between IA feedback and doing the work?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the content, explain each criterion and its mark allocation, discuss whether a research question is feasible, suggest a method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of the submitted text, or produce the data. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own, so the boundary protects them rather than us. A page ranking in this market sells completed IAs; that is a malpractice trigger for the student.

faqs.question: Does a tutor coming to a Nad Al Sheba villa need a MoHRE permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British Year 11 into DP1 and is struggling. What is the actual gap?
faqs.answer: Usually three things rather than content. First, command terms: IGCSE rewarded detail, so these students over-write and spend two-mark time on four-mark answers. Second, internal assessment, which they have not met before and which carries 20% of the grade in maths and the sciences. Third, volume: six subjects plus TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS in parallel, where before there were linear exam courses. A first diagnostic session on a past-paper section usually identifies which of the three dominates, and the fix differs completely for each.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after the Nad Al Sheba school run?
faqs.answer: School days in and around the district end between roughly 14:30 and 15:30 depending on school and year group. For families whose school is inside Nad Al Sheba or Sobha Hartland, a 15:30 or 16:00 start works. For those driving back from Al Quoz, Al Jaddaf or Dubai Hills in pick-up traffic, 16:30 is more honest. Online delivery is what makes the earlier slots possible at all: nothing has to travel to you, so the half-hour on either side of the session stays with the child.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Nad Al Sheba Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One weekly session per subject is the normal starting point, and most families begin with a single subject rather than three. The reason is diagnostic: until the mark pattern is identified, more hours mostly means more of the wrong work. In the term before papers the cadence typically changes to two or three shorter sessions a week in one subject, built around timed sections and official mark schemes. Adding a second subject usually makes sense once the first has moved, not before.

faqs.question: Does Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay actually affect the final score?
faqs.answer: Yes. The six subjects contribute 42 points at 7 each, and the TOK essay and Extended Essay together contribute up to 3 more through the published matrix, both graded A to E. The TOK essay is 1,600 words on one of six prescribed titles; the Extended Essay is 4,000 words marked against five criteria over 34 marks, with the planning reflections contributing to the total. Students who treat both as administration rather than assessment routinely give away the points that sit between a 38 and a 41.

faqs.question: Why are Arabic and Islamic Education on my child's IB timetable at all?
faqs.answer: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those minutes come out of a week already holding six Diploma subjects, TOK and CAS.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if papers are a few months away?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong, which is why the trial lesson is diagnostic rather than instructional. If the pattern is command terms, timing or question selection, a short block of marked timed sections moves a grade boundary quickly because the recovery is concentrated. If whole syllabus topics are missing, the honest answer is that a few months buys a partial fix and a written list of what to leave alone. Nobody can promise a grade, and anybody who does is telling you something about themselves.

faqs.question: Should we book one tutor for two Diploma subjects or two tutors?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor across two subjects gives continuity and halves the scheduling. The common workable pairs are Maths AA with Physics, and Chemistry with Biology. Where it fails is at Higher Level in two unrelated subjects, because genuine HL depth in two separate papers is rare, and a tutor who stretches to cover both is a generalist with two labels. We will tell you which case yours is rather than filling the slot.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we are matched with is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the match, at no cost and without a notice period. The most common reason is not competence but pace: a tutor who suits a student needing structure can be wrong for one who needs to be pushed. We also check this proactively at around the six-to-eight session mark by asking whether the mark pattern has moved. If it has not, either the diagnosis was wrong or the fit is wrong, and continuing because the slot is already booked is how a term gets wasted.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for my child to work from?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth stating. IB, Cambridge and Pearson materials are copyright, some of it unreleased, so we do not host, reproduce or distribute papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Your school holds licensed access, and the boards publish material through their own platforms at ibo.org, cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Sessions work from the copies your school or the board provides, and the time goes on marking against the official scheme rather than on sourcing documents.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or while we are travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and they routinely do in this corridor. Ramadan shifts school hours and family routines, and sessions generally move later or to post-Iftar timings for the month; students sitting papers in the spring usually keep the cadence and change the clock. Travel is the other constant here, with long Eid and summer absences normal. Because delivery is over live video, a session follows the student to wherever they are rather than pausing until the family is back in Nad Al Sheba.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.tutorsIntro: We quote against a stated requirement rather than a subject list, and we will tell you when the cheaper option - or no option - is the right answer. That is the only honest way to answer a cost question on a page like this.

intro.heading: Budget the Diploma, not the hour
paragraphs: Almost every Oud Metha family that asks us about cost asks for an hourly rate, gets one, decides it is manageable, and then spends several times what they imagined. The arithmetic is not hidden and it is not anybody's trick. It is simply that the Diploma runs for twenty-four months across six subjects, each of which can plausibly attract a weekly hour, and an hourly rate multiplied by that structure is a different number from the one a parent pictured.

So the right unit is the programme rather than the session. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates put a single weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Hold that for one subject across two Diploma years and it becomes a substantial commitment. Hold it for three subjects and it is a multiple of that. Nothing about those figures is unreasonable per hour; the total is simply much larger than the monthly number implies, and most families do the first multiplication and not the second.

The second thing worth understanding before spending anything is that a large share of Diploma tutoring money is spent on components that have already closed. Every subject has an internally assessed piece submitted at a school deadline well before the papers - 20 per cent of a science grade, for instance, settled in the autumn of the second year. Families who start looking for a tutor in the spring of DP2 and ask for help with the internal assessment are asking about a mark that is banked. The money is real and the component is not available.

The third is that some of what gets paid for is free. Oud Metha sits inside the school belt with large schools within walking distance, which makes departmental revision sessions, after-school clinics and teacher availability unusually easy to reach from here. Before paying anybody it is worth establishing what the school already runs, and the honest version of this page says so rather than burying it. We would rather a family used a free session than bought an hour from us covering the same ground.

On delivery, since the search term invites the question: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for an Oud Metha family is one-to-one over live video, in a Gulf Standard Time slot, and we hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE. The cost consequence of that is specific and it appears in a table further down: in-home rates published in this market include the tutor's travel, and over two years the travel component becomes a number that would have bought a meaningful number of additional sessions.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: Four points in the Diploma where money gets spent, and what each one can actually buy. The cost-effectiveness varies enormously between them, which is the whole argument of this page.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: The cheapest year to buy help in and the one families spend least in, because nothing has gone wrong yet. Every internally assessed component is still open, foundational mathematical technique can be fixed slowly rather than patched, and the decisions that cap internal assessment marks have not been made. A small amount of well-aimed spending here displaces a larger amount later.
programmes.countryNote: In a Dubai school DP1 also carries mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies alongside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the start of the Extended Essay. A DP1 student describing a time problem is usually describing arithmetic, and that is not solved by purchase.

programmes.name: Diploma year two, first term
programmes.description: The last window in which internally assessed components are still open at most schools, and therefore the final chance to influence that share of the grade. Also the term in which Extended Essay deadlines land. Spending here is still efficient, provided it is aimed at a component that has not yet been submitted rather than at general revision.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the IB coordinator for the school's internal deadline list. Those internal dates, not the IB's, are what determine whether a component is open, and having them in writing at the start of DP2 is what makes autumn spending efficient rather than hopeful.

programmes.name: Diploma year two, final terms
programmes.description: The most expensive period and the one in which most money is spent. Internal assessments are closed, so the entire remaining grade sits in the papers, and what tutoring can do is convert existing knowledge into marks. That is real and it is narrower than families expect, and it is worth paying for only when aimed at diagnosed losses rather than at syllabus coverage.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the May session, with November as the alternative sitting. No IB session or results date appears on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so take every date from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org rather than from a tutoring website.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Together worth up to 3 points through a published matrix, with conditions attached that can fail an otherwise sufficient candidate. The useful help is unusually narrow and therefore unusually cheap: narrowing an Extended Essay research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words, and reading a Theory of Knowledge prescribed title closely before any planning.
programmes.countryNote: This is the best value in the whole Diploma on a cost-per-point basis, because two or three well-timed sessions can touch something that contributes to the final total, and almost nobody buys it. Families spend on subjects and ignore the core, then discover it in the results.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: Where money goes per subject, and whether it is well spent. The question in each case is how much grade the hour can plausibly move, not how difficult the subject is.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Expensive to fix late and cheap to fix early, because the underlying problem is almost always algebraic fluency rather than concepts. A DP1 block on manipulation and calculator technique costs a fraction of DP2 crisis revision and improves every paper. The mathematical exploration is a separate purchase with its own timing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same economics with a different emphasis: modelling, statistics and technology use. Families often assume this route needs less support and then find the technology demands and the exploration both need attention. The route choice itself should be checked against specific university requirements rather than reputation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The highest-leverage early purchase in Group 4, because the investigation is 20 per cent and its ceiling is set before any data exists, and because the mathematics inside physics is the real DP1 difficulty. After the investigation closes, remaining value is paper technique and uncertainty handling.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The one subject where a ten-minute diagnostic can redirect the whole budget: if the mole and reacting-amount chain is not automatic, that is where four to eight sessions should go whatever topic the report names. Spending on organic chemistry while the chain is shaky is the commonest waste in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the challenge and terminology precision is where marks go, which makes it well suited to short frequent work rather than long blocks. Low cost per unit of improvement, but it needs consistency across a term, so a thin long engagement beats an intensive one.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: The internally assessed component is the efficient purchase here, because article or case selection and framing decide the mark and a few well-timed sessions address it. Paper technique - diagram accuracy, judgement at the end of evaluation questions - is cheap to fix and frequently ignored.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: Source evaluation and structured argument are teachable in small numbers of sessions and transfer between papers. The internally assessed investigation has a specific cost trap: a question nobody can find sources for caps three criteria, and it is detectable in one conversation months early.

subjects.name: Language A
subjects.description: The individual oral is the under-bought component. Its ceiling is set by the choice of extracts and the global issue framing, which is a single conversation rather than a course of lessons - and that conversation is among the cheapest high-value hours available in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Language B
subjects.description: The oral again, and specifically the unscripted follow-up conversation, which is coaching rather than language teaching. Short frequent rehearsal outperforms long sessions, so the cost-effective shape is a thin engagement across a term rather than a block before the recording.

subjects.name: The Arts
subjects.levels: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Film · HL and SL
subjects.description: Heavily internally assessed through portfolios and performance components with substantial documentation requirements. The efficient purchase is process and documentation support in the first year, and it is almost never bought - families buy artistic coaching, which is not what is marked.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two or three sessions, well timed, reading a prescribed title closely before any planning and framing the exhibition properly. On a cost-per-point basis this is the best value in the Diploma, because the core contributes to the final total and the help needed is genuinely small.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: One session on the research question, in DP1, is worth more than five on the draft in DP2. A question too broad to answer in 4,000 words produces a survey, and surveys score in the lower bands. The supervisor reflections also count, which students discover late and at cost.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.regionsTitle: Oud Metha and the districts around it
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.regionsIntro: What changes between these neighbourhoods on a cost page is the travel premium attached to an in-home arrangement and the ease of reaching free school support. The teaching rate does not vary by postcode.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Inside the school belt with large schools within walking distance, which makes free departmental support unusually accessible and the earliest session slot in Old Dubai genuinely available. Both of those are cost advantages that belong to the district.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: A short distance west with its own school cluster, often a walk. Similar access to free school support, and a 4pm start is realistic, which means a session can land before fatigue and before a shared study surface is contested.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and served by the same schools, so the same free options and the same market rates apply. Nothing about the tutoring economics differs between a Bur Dubai and an Oud Metha address.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: A few minutes inland, dense flats, shared study surfaces and often one device between siblings. The same market rates, with physical constraints that make scheduling rather than price the binding issue.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Across the creek near the airport, with the nearest concentrated IB provision. An in-home arrangement from here to Oud Metha carries a real travel cost, which is the clearest case of the premium buying a drive.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: The north bank, with an unpredictable afternoon crossing. The travel premium is highest and the reliability lowest, which is a poor combination to be paying for every week.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A large British and Indian curriculum belt towards Sharjah. Longest commutes, thinnest IB provision, and the least favourable in-home economics in this group.

regions.name: Al Jaffiliya and Satwa
regions.note: Between Bur Dubai and Jumeirah with short runs to two clusters. Households with children on two curricula face two budgets rather than one, which is the multiplication families most often fail to do.

schoolClusters.city: Oud Metha, Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai
schoolClusters.note: The densest school provision in Old Dubai and the practical reason free departmental support is reachable from here. Worth noting on a cost page: KHDA publishes each private school's approved fees on its own site, so a family can check school costs independently rather than relying on anybody's summary.

schoolClusters.city: Al Garhoud, Deira and Al Mamzar
schoolClusters.note: The nearest IB provision to Oud Metha and where most local Diploma students study. The daily crossing is the reason an in-home arrangement with a tutor from this cluster carries the travel premium that the market rates already price in.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma tutoring budget, laid out in dirhams
paragraphs: Here is the calculation most families do not do until they have already made the commitment. Start from the market figures, each attributed and read in October 2026, and then multiply by the actual structure of the Diploma rather than by a single month.

The hourly bands: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table places IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly: Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work, with packages advertised around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Now the structure. A Diploma is two academic years. A weekly hour in one subject, at the mid band, held across both of them, is roughly eighteen to twenty months of that monthly figure. In two subjects it doubles. In three - which plenty of families end up at, one subject at a time, each added for a good reason - it triples. Nobody decides to spend the three-subject total; they decide three times to spend a one-subject monthly figure, which is not the same decision and produces a very different number.

The table below lays the alternatives out side by side so the comparison is visible before the commitment rather than after it. Note what is cheapest and most effective: the small, early, component-aimed purchases at the top. Note what is most expensive: a standing arrangement in several subjects, maintained because stopping feels risky. None of these are IB Gram prices - we publish no rate card on a landing page and would rather quote against a stated requirement.

sections.heading: Six places the money leaks
paragraphs: These are the patterns we see most often in this district, and all six are avoidable at no cost. None of them involve dishonest providers; they are all ordinary decisions that happen to be inefficient, and naming them is more useful than a discount.

The first is buying a closed component. An internal assessment submitted in the autumn of DP2 cannot be improved in the spring, and hours spent discussing it are hours spent on a banked mark. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline list and know what is open before buying. The second is paying for coverage in a short window. A DP2 spring run-in cannot cover six subjects, and a provider who offers to is selling hours; triage by marks recoverable per hour instead. The third is re-teaching a topic when the problem is upstream of it - the chemistry student whose mole chain is not automatic, the physics student whose algebra is shaky. A ten-minute diagnostic redirects the whole budget.

The fourth is adding subjects one at a time. Each addition is individually defensible and the total is a decision nobody made. Review the whole commitment every term rather than only the new increment. The fifth is paying a premium for work that belongs to the student: the final fortnight's timed-paper practice is not a purchasable service, and nothing in this market justifies a premium for supervising it. The sixth is paying for anything the school already provides free, which in Oud Metha specifically is more than families assume, because the school belt is within walking distance.

There is a seventh that is worth separating out because it is about structure rather than judgement: not asking whether a quoted rate is per hour or per lesson. A ninety-minute lesson billed at a lesson rate and a ninety-minute lesson billed at an hourly rate are different numbers, and the difference compounds weekly across two years. Ask the question of every provider, including us, and ask what happens if you stop after one session.
bullets: Ask the coordinator which components are still open before buying anything
Diagnose upstream: the named topic is often not the problem

sections.heading: Cost per point: which parts of the grade are cheap to move
paragraphs: A more useful question than what does tutoring cost is what does a point cost, and the answer varies by an order of magnitude depending on which part of the grade you are aiming at. Thinking this way changes what a family buys without changing what they spend.

At the cheap end sit the core components. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to 3 points through a published matrix, and the useful help in both is genuinely narrow: reading a prescribed title closely before planning, and narrowing a research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words. Two or three sessions each, once, in DP1. On a cost-per-point basis nothing else in the Diploma comes close, and almost nobody buys it because the core does not feel like a subject.

Next cheapest are the internally assessed components, provided they are addressed before design decisions are made. A science investigation is 20 per cent of a subject grade, 24 marks across four criteria, and its ceiling is set by whether the chosen variable can be measured precisely enough. Three to five sessions before any data exists can affect that whole share. The same three to five sessions after submission affect nothing. Timing, not quantity, is what makes this cheap or worthless.

At the expensive end sits content coverage in a short window, which is where most money goes. Re-teaching a topic in DP2 spring buys a small number of marks on one paper at specialist rates, and re-teaching several topics multiplies the cost without multiplying the effect, because the student runs out of capacity before the budget does. The honest framing is that late spending buys conversion of existing knowledge - command terms, mark allocation, showing working, question triage - and that is worth a modest, targeted amount rather than a large one.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context, next to the other numbers a Dubai family pays
paragraphs: Tutoring spending makes more sense placed next to the other education costs in a Dubai household than viewed on its own, and one of those costs has recently been held flat, which changes the comparison.

KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. KHDA publishes each school's approved fees on its own site, which means a family can check school costs independently rather than relying on a summary from anybody, including us.

Against that backdrop, the tutoring question becomes proportional rather than absolute. A standing weekly hour in three subjects across two years, at Bestimate's mid-market monthly estimate of AED 600 to 1,200 per subject, is a recurring commitment sitting alongside fees that have been frozen for a year. For many households the sensible conclusion is not to spend less in total but to spend the same amount earlier and more narrowly - the small early component-aimed purchases rather than the broad late ones.

The table below places the items side by side. Two of its rows deliberately carry no figure, because we do not publish numbers we cannot source: school fees vary by school and are published on KHDA's own site, and private-candidate examination fees are set by the board and the centre rather than by us. An unsourced number on a page like this would be worse than a blank, and across thousands of pages it would be a liability rather than a service.

sections.heading: Pricing structures, and the three traps inside them
paragraphs: Beyond the headline rate, how a provider prices has a larger effect on what a family actually pays than the rate itself. Three structures dominate this market and each has a trap worth knowing before signing anything.

Per-hour against per-lesson is the first and the most common. A ninety-minute lesson billed at an hourly rate costs one and a half hours; billed at a lesson rate it may cost one. Across a two-year engagement at weekly frequency the difference is significant, and it is invisible unless asked about. Ask every provider, including us, and get the answer in writing alongside the rate.

Packages are the second. The monthly listings in this market - around AED 799 for eight online sessions, AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions - reduce the per-hour cost and introduce a commitment. The trap is not the discount; it is that a package creates a reason to keep going when the honest answer is to stop. If three sessions have not moved the mark pattern, the right response is to change the tutor or the approach, and a half-used package makes that decision harder than it should be. Ask what happens to unused sessions and what happens if you stop after one.

Group classes are the third. They are genuinely cheaper per student and they work for content delivery where several students share the same gap. They do not work for internally assessed components, because those are individual pieces of work with individual research questions, and they do not work for diagnosed technique repair, because the diagnosis differs per student. A group class sold as internal assessment support is selling the wrong format for the task. And on the word free: nothing with a condition attached should be called free without the condition stated on the same screen - our trial lesson is one session, at no cost, with no card required, and that is the whole of it.

sections.heading: The free alternatives worth trying first from an Oud Metha address
paragraphs: A cost page that does not mention the free options is not an honest cost page, and in this district the free options are unusually accessible. Oud Metha sits inside the school belt with large schools within walking distance, which means the things a school provides are easy to physically reach - and most of them are provided to anybody who asks.

Departmental support comes first. Most Dubai secondary departments run some form of after-school clinic, revision session or open-door arrangement, and the teacher running it knows your child's class, their marks and the school's own deadlines better than any external tutor will. It costs nothing. Establish exactly what runs and when before paying anybody, and if the free provision covers what is actually wrong, use it - we will say so when it looks adequate rather than selling around it.

Second, the coordinator conversation. Asking the IB coordinator for the internal deadline list, which components are still open, and which subject guide version applies is free and reorders what a family should spend on. It is routinely worth more than a first paid session, because it establishes what is purchasable at all. Third, the marked script. Asking a teacher for the annotated mock paper rather than the grade costs nothing and turns a first tutoring hour from diagnosis into teaching, which is a direct saving.

Fourth, and least used, the student's own timed practice. The final fortnight of any Diploma subject is technique and stamina, and that is the student's own work - no tutor can do it for them and nothing in this market justifies a premium for supervising it. Families who understand that stop paying two weeks earlier than they otherwise would, and the outcome is the same or better because the student is not sitting in a lesson when they should be writing a paper.

sections.heading: Where near me adds cost without adding value
paragraphs: On a page about money, the proximity question resolves into a straightforward comparison, and it is worth making explicitly rather than leaving implied.

Our position first, stated before anyone pays: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for an Oud Metha family is one-to-one over live video in a Gulf Standard Time slot, and we hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We put that on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and a family should know before paying rather than after.

The cost structure is visible in the published market figures. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors, with travel explicitly included in those rates, against AED 150 to 450 for online specialists. The clearest comparison is the monthly packages: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions - the same eight hours for roughly double, repeated monthly. Over two Diploma years in one subject, the difference would have bought a substantial number of additional sessions, and what it actually buys is a journey.

The one honest counterargument is that Oud Metha has the shortest commute in Old Dubai, so the travel being paid for is genuinely brief. That is true, and it is the district where in-home pricing is least penalised. What it does not change is that the premium is still charged, that the pool of available tutors is still narrowed by distance, and that the session still depends on a journey succeeding. What Oud Metha's short commute really buys is the earliest realistic slot in Old Dubai - a 4pm or 4.30pm start - and that advantage belongs to the district rather than to either delivery model, so an online session claims it just as well.

sections.heading: What we will not charge for, claim or publish
paragraphs: A page that publishes competitors' prices should be explicit about its own position, so here it is in full, and all of it is checkable.

We publish no rate card on a landing page, because a rate without a stated requirement is a number designed to be compared rather than used - we would rather quote against what a family actually needs after a free trial. The trial is one session, at no cost, with the tutor you would continue with, and no card is required; that is the whole condition and it is stated here rather than on a later screen. We hold no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, so there is nothing to visit and no address to show.

We are not approved, accredited, certified, licensed, authorised or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai - initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry - and we do not hold one. Anybody implying such approval should be asked for the permit or centre number.

We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating, review count or tutor headcount, because none of those could carry a sample size, a date and a method, and a statistic without those three things is decoration. Two competitors in this market publish self-asserted star ratings in their structured data that differ from the figure on the visible page, which is a structured-data policy problem as well as a trust one. We print no IB examination or results date, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in a Diploma plan is a date a family acts on. And we do not write, co-write, edit to completion or supply any part of an internally assessed component, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay - we teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, while one provider ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

sections.heading: Permits, the regulator map and equivalency a family can verify
paragraphs: Cost and legality intersect in one place on a near-me search, which is that the cheapest local option is often an individual working without a permit. That is worth knowing because the permit is free, so price is not the reason somebody would lack one.

Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published officially, nobody should quote you an amount - a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

One rule bears on the cheapest convenient option specifically. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In a district where the schools are a short walk away, that arrangement is the one most likely to be offered informally and the one to decline.

On the wider picture: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its own Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah - with Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel: we describe the process, neither perform nor guarantee it, and tutoring is not a requirement of it.

sections.heading: The mandatory subjects, the full week and the cost of ignoring both
paragraphs: One cost that never appears in a quote is the opportunity cost of an hour in a week that has none spare, and in a Dubai Diploma timetable that is a real constraint rather than a rhetorical one.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, since curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and requires teachers of those subjects to hold the appropriate KHDA approval. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited.

Place those hours beside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and the week has very little slack. Adding a third weekly tutoring hour to that week does not add three hours of capacity; it removes three hours from somewhere else, usually from sleep or from the subject that was not being tutored. That is the single most common reason a family spends more and sees less, and it is an arithmetic problem rather than a teaching one.

The practical consequence for a budget is counter-intuitive: spending less, earlier and more narrowly often produces more grade than spending more, later and more broadly, because the early purchases do not compete for capacity in the same way. A DP1 block on algebraic fluency sits in a year with more room in it and improves papers for twenty months. Three DP2 spring hours sit in the fullest weeks of the programme and compete with revision the student needs to do alone. We would rather a family heard that before committing than discovered it in April.

process.title: Ask the coordinator what is still open
process.description: Request the internal deadline list for all six subjects. A component already submitted cannot be improved, and knowing which ones are open is the single cheapest piece of information in the whole budget. It costs one email and it reorders what you should spend on.

process.title: Check the free provision before paying
process.description: Oud Metha sits inside the school belt, so departmental clinics, revision sessions and teacher availability are easy to reach and cost nothing. Establish what runs and when. Where the free option covers what is actually wrong, we will say so rather than take the booking.

process.title: Diagnose before you commit
process.description: Two or three sessions, or a free trial, spent on marked scripts across the candidate subjects. One subject is usually doing most of the damage and the named topic is often not the problem. Buying three standing hours before diagnosing is the most expensive way to start.

process.title: Ask the two pricing questions in writing
process.description: Is the quoted rate per hour or per lesson, and what happens if we stop after one session. Ask every provider, including us. Those two answers change the two-year total more than the headline rate does, and they separate providers quickly.

process.title: Buy the cheap things first
process.description: The Extended Essay research question, the Theory of Knowledge prescribed title, the internal assessment design before data exists, the Language A oral extract choice. Small blocks, fixed end points, lowest cost per point in the programme - and the ones families buy last.

process.title: Review the whole commitment each term
process.description: Not just the newest addition. Three subjects at a weekly hour is a decision nobody consciously made; it is three separate reasonable decisions. Look at the total every term, judge it against the school's assessments, and stop the parts that are not moving.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, every claim checkable
whyPoints.description: Each AED range on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, so you can verify it and judge any quote - including ours - against something real. Three providers in this market publish no price at all and two quote in a currency Dubai families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you what is already closed
whyPoints.description: An internal assessment submitted in the autumn of DP2 cannot be improved in the spring, and we say so rather than booking hours against a banked mark. Knowing what is purchasable is worth more than a discount on something that is not.

whyPoints.title: We point at the free options
whyPoints.description: Departmental clinics, the coordinator conversation, the annotated script, and the student's own timed practice. In a district inside the school belt those are genuinely accessible, and where they cover what is wrong we say so instead of selling around them.

whyPoints.title: Cheap things first, by design
whyPoints.description: The core components and early internal assessment design have the lowest cost per point in the Diploma and are the last things families buy. We lead with them because it is the honest recommendation, even though it is the smaller sale.

whyPoints.title: No rate card, no package pressure
whyPoints.description: We quote against a stated requirement after a free trial rather than publishing a number designed for comparison, and we would rather you reviewed after three sessions than committed to a package that makes stopping awkward when stopping is right.

whyPoints.title: Clear about where the tutor sits, and what that saves
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment, and IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE. The published in-home rates include travel; over two years that premium would have bought a meaningful number of additional sessions.

faqs.question: What does a full IB Diploma of tutoring actually cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Count twenty-four months, not one. Bestimate's Dubai estimates put a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Hold the mid band for one subject across both Diploma years and that is eighteen to twenty months of the monthly figure; three subjects triples it. Families rarely decide to spend the three-subject total - they decide three times to spend a one-subject figure, which is a different decision.

faqs.question: Which part of a Diploma grade is cheapest to improve?
faqs.answer: The core. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to 3 points through a published matrix, and the useful help in both is narrow: reading a prescribed title closely before planning, and narrowing a research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words. Two or three sessions each, once, in DP1. On a cost-per-point basis nothing else comes close, and almost nobody buys it because the core does not feel like a subject the way chemistry does.

faqs.question: Where do Oud Metha families most often waste tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Six places, all avoidable at no cost. Buying a component that has already been submitted. Paying for coverage in a window too short for it. Re-teaching a topic when the problem is upstream of it - shaky algebra, an unautomatic mole chain. Adding subjects one at a time until the total is a decision nobody made. Paying a premium to supervise final-fortnight practice that belongs to the student. And paying for something the school already provides free, which in this district is more than most families assume.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in DP1 or DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, decisively, and it is the year families spend least in because nothing has gone wrong yet. Every internally assessed component is still open, so three to five sessions can affect up to 20 per cent of a subject grade. Foundational technique fixed in the first DP1 term improves papers for twenty months. By DP2 spring the internal marks are closed, the week is at its fullest, and what remains is conversion of existing knowledge - real, but narrower and more expensive per unit of grade.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson?
faqs.answer: Always, and get it in writing. A ninety-minute lesson billed at an hourly rate costs one and a half hours; billed at a lesson rate it may cost one. Across a weekly engagement over two Diploma years that difference is substantial and it is invisible unless asked about. Ask the second question too: what happens if we stop after one session. Those two answers change the two-year total more than the headline rate does, and they separate providers faster than any marketing copy.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages good value?
faqs.answer: They lower the effective hourly rate and they introduce a commitment, and the trap is the commitment rather than the discount. Market listings run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The problem is that a half-used package creates a reason to keep going when the honest answer is to change the tutor or stop. Ask what happens to unused sessions and whether you can review and exit after three.

faqs.question: Can a group class replace one-to-one for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For content delivery where several students share the same gap, yes, and it is genuinely cheaper per student. For internally assessed components, no - those are individual pieces with individual research questions, and a group format cannot address them. For diagnosed technique repair, also no, because the diagnosis differs per student. A group class marketed as internal assessment support is the wrong format for the task, whatever the price looks like.

faqs.question: What free support should we use before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Four things, and all of them are accessible from Oud Metha because the school belt is within walking distance. Departmental after-school clinics and revision sessions, run by teachers who know your child's class and marks. The coordinator conversation, which establishes which components are still open. Asking a teacher for the annotated mock script rather than the grade, which turns a first paid hour from diagnosis into teaching. And the student's own timed practice in the final fortnight, which is not purchasable at all.

faqs.question: Does paying more get a better IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Up to a point, and the point is lower than the top of the market. The specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above - Bestimate's figure, with TutorChase at AED 270 - buys judgement: internal assessment design and reading a script to rank mark losses. Above that, BartyED's AED 650 buys a named individual rather than a different capability. Below it, the budget band at AED 33 to 65 from Tutopiya and EdFlik buys supervision, which is sometimes exactly right and never equivalent to Higher Level teaching.

faqs.question: How much does an in-home tutor add over two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Roughly double, on the published monthly packages. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors with travel included, against AED 150 to 450 for online specialists. The clearest comparison: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions - the same eight hours. Repeated monthly across two years, that difference would have bought a substantial number of additional sessions.

faqs.question: Do you come to homes in Oud Metha, and does it cost more?
faqs.answer: We do not. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Oud Metha family is one-to-one over live video in a Gulf Standard Time slot, stated before you pay, and we hold no office or premises in the UAE. The cost point is in the market data above: in-home rates include the tutor's travel, so the premium above the online band pays for a journey rather than for teaching.

faqs.question: Why don't you publish your prices on this page?
faqs.answer: Because a rate without a stated requirement is a number designed for comparison rather than for use, and the right answer depends on the subject, the component and how many weeks are left. We would rather quote against what a family actually needs after a free trial. What we do publish is every competitor rate we could source, with the provider named and the month it was read, so you can judge any quote - ours included - against something real rather than against a claim.

faqs.question: Is the free trial actually free?
faqs.answer: Yes, and here is the whole condition stated on the same screen: one session, at no cost, with the tutor you would continue with rather than a different person, and no card is required. Nothing else attaches to it. We spell that out because the word free gets used loosely in this market, and anything with a condition attached should carry the condition where it is read rather than three clicks later. You also get a written note of what was found either way.

faqs.question: How does tutoring spend compare with Dubai school fees?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. KHDA publishes each school's approved fees on its own site, so a family can check independently rather than relying on anyone's summary. Against frozen fees, a recurring three-subject tutoring commitment is worth examining as a proportion rather than in isolation - and spending earlier and narrower often beats spending more.

faqs.question: Will a third weekly tutoring hour actually help?
faqs.answer: Often less than expected, because it does not add capacity to the week - it removes time from somewhere else, usually sleep or the subject that is not being tutored. A Dubai Diploma week already carries six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. This is the commonest reason a family spends more and sees less, and it is arithmetic rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest local tutor likely to hold a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Ask, because price is not a reason to lack one - the permit is free. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties, and no official fine schedule is published.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Spend earlier, narrower, and on the cheap things first
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.closingBody: If this page has one argument, it is that the Diploma rewards small early purchases far more than large late ones, and that most families do the reverse. Ask the coordinator which components are still open. Check what the school already provides free, which from an Oud Metha address is a short walk. Diagnose before committing, and buy the core work and the internal assessment design before any standing subject hour. Then ask us the two pricing questions and take the free trial - one session, no cost, no card, with the tutor you would keep. All lessons for Oud Metha families are one-to-one over live video, and we do not send tutors to UAE addresses.

intro.heading: The honest answer to a proximity search
paragraphs: A parent typing IB tutor near me in Palm Jumeirah is asking a reasonable question and will get a misleading answer. Search engines treat proximity as a proxy for suitability, which works for a dentist and fails for a Diploma subject specialist. The Diploma is six subjects across six groups, each available at two levels, plus three core components, which is well over fifty distinct teaching jobs. The chance that the right one of those fifty lives within a short drive of the island is small, and the chance that a search result reflects it is smaller still.

Palm Jumeirah sharpens this more than most addresses in Dubai. Families here commute off the island for school, mostly westward into Al Sufouh and Al Barsha or eastward along the coast into Jumeirah and Al Safa. The island has one trunk road, one monorail and a fixed set of exits, so an evening journey in either direction is predictable and slow. Any tutor who agrees to make that journey at six o'clock is pricing it in, and the pool willing to make it is defined by willingness to drive rather than by subject expertise.

So the useful reframing is this: stop asking who is near, and start asking who teaches the thing. If your child needs Higher Level Chemistry, there may be a handful of people in the emirate teaching the current course well, and none of them will be on the Palm. If your child needs Standard Level Economics, the pool is wider but still not local. Once the question is about the subject, the island stops being a constraint and becomes irrelevant, which is the better position to be in.

This page is built to answer the proximity question properly rather than to dismiss it. It sets out what each drive-time band from Palm Jumeirah actually reaches, and what the tutoring pool at that radius contains. It explains the six subject groups and what a non-specialist typically misses in each. It covers the core - Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS - which is where a great deal of Diploma anxiety sits and which almost no local tutoring advertises. It publishes what the Dubai market charges in AED with sources attached. And it sets out what a tutor may and may not do with assessed work.

The delivery position, stated once and plainly. Tutoring for UAE families is one-to-one and live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Palm Jumeirah family that is not a compromise but the point: it replaces a search radius with a subject match, and the subject match is the only thing that changes a Diploma grade.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: An island family may be at any point in the IB sequence, and the same proximity problem applies at each stage with a different shape. These are the programmes we support from Palm Jumeirah.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard, drawn from six groups, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries externally examined papers and an internally assessed component with its own published criteria. This is where the proximity problem bites hardest, because the specialist a DP2 student needs is defined to the level of a single course rather than a subject area.
programmes.countryNote: Palm Jumeirah students reach Diploma campuses in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Sufouh and along the Jumeirah coast. Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes, which widens the choice for younger siblings but does nothing for a student sitting papers in the current cycle.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight and converted to a grade from one to seven. MYP tutoring needs a tutor who has read the descriptors for that subject at that year level, which widens the matching problem rather than narrowing it. The Personal Project in MYP 5 is independent work with its own criteria.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of the island run the full IB continuum, so a Palm Jumeirah child can move from MYP into the Diploma without changing school. Families who do change at sixteen should ask what external qualification the MYP route leaves them holding, because that varies by campus.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with assessment that reports on conceptual understanding and approaches to learning. Support at this stage is usually literacy or numeracy fluency rather than programme-specific, and the honest answer to most PYP tutoring enquiries is that a short diagnostic block is enough.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision is the one stage where a short journey genuinely matters, because a seven-year-old's evening is shorter than a sixteen-year-old's. For primary families on the island we usually recommend fewer, earlier sessions rather than a weekly commitment that competes with bedtime.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Included because many island families are deciding between a British route and an IB route, and because IGCSE grades are what make a Diploma place possible. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones; Pearson Edexcel runs May-June and November series with provisional timetables published ahead.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai by enrolment, and the campuses the island commutes to include several that run IGCSE into A Level rather than into the Diploma. A family intending the Diploma should check that the chosen Year 10 campus actually offers it, rather than assuming the sixth form follows.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Palm Jumeirah families most often ask for, with what each one assesses and where a non-specialist tutor typically falls short. The list is organised by what the exam actually rewards rather than by popularity.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation. A general science tutor can explain the content and will usually miss the data-based question technique, the significant-figure and state-symbol conventions, and the uncertainty treatment the investigation criteria expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Graph interpretation, uncertainty and the step from a described situation to the correct relationship. Non-specialists re-teach topics; specialists diagnose whether the problem is actually algebraic fluency, which it frequently is, and fix that instead.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The course where extended-response technique decides the grade. Answers that describe a process when an explanation was asked for lose marks regardless of accuracy, and the named examples the criteria expect are not optional.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a third paper and a markedly different style of question. Method lines left unwritten, calculator work presented without reasoning, and the exploration treated as an essay rather than as mathematics are the recurring losses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy, with a strong calculator component and modelling questions that reward sketching before calculating. Often chosen late by students who found the Analysis route too abstract, and the switch needs planning rather than panic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the guided analysis paper are where marks move. Students arrive able to summarise and need to learn to analyse, which is close-reading practice on unseen extracts with the criteria visible.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline. An evaluation question answered descriptively earns little however well written, and the internal assessment commentaries carry length limits students routinely overshoot.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the specific organisation in the stimulus is what earns marks, not general theory. Students who learn the frameworks and apply them generically plateau in the mid range and cannot see why.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source evaluation, argument structure and the historical investigation. The investigation's evaluation-of-sources section is worth a disproportionate share of its marks and is usually written last and thinnest.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Oral assessment is the component families most often want help with, and it responds faster to structured practice than any other part of a language course. Written production needs register awareness rather than more vocabulary.

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually returns from Palm Jumeirah, radius by radius
paragraphs: Take the proximity question literally for a moment and work outwards from the island. Each band of drive time reaches more of Dubai, and the arithmetic is worth seeing written down, because it shows precisely what a radius buys. The first band is the island itself, where there is effectively no Diploma tutoring supply and never has been. The second reaches Al Sufouh and the Marina. The third reaches Al Barsha and the Jumeirah coast. Beyond that you are describing most of Dubai, at which point proximity has stopped meaning anything.

The column that matters in the table below is the last one. As the radius grows, the number of people reachable grows quickly and the number of Diploma subject specialists among them grows slowly, because specialists are rare in absolute terms rather than unevenly distributed. In a city where International Baccalaureate programmes account for about 7% of private enrolment, Group 4 and Higher Level mathematics teachers are a small population spread across a very large map. Doubling a search radius does not double the chance of a match for Higher Level Chemistry; it moves it from zero to almost zero.

There is a second cost to the radius that families account for only after they have paid it. A tutor who travels arrives with a journey behind them and another ahead, and both get priced into the hour one way or another - in the fee, in the punctuality, or in the willingness to reschedule. The published Dubai figures make this visible: in-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car.

None of which means proximity is worthless. For a primary-age child, a short journey is genuinely better, and for group revision a local centre is a sensible purchase. For a Diploma student with a named subject problem, the radius is the wrong filter, and replacing it with the subject and level is the single change that makes a real specialist reachable from Palm Jumeirah.

sections.heading: The six Diploma subject groups, and which one your search is really about
paragraphs: The Diploma asks for six subjects drawn from six groups: studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with a second subject from another group permitted in place of the arts. Three are usually taken at Higher Level and three at Standard. That structure is the reason a near-me search is the wrong tool, because the unit of expertise is not the subject area but the course at the level, and the same tutor who is excellent for Standard Level Economics may be useless for Higher Level Physics.

Families often arrive describing the problem in general terms - he is struggling with the sciences, she has lost confidence in maths - and the first job is to make it specific. Which course, which level, which component, which recent piece of marked work. A tutor matched at that resolution starts useful in the first session. A tutor matched at subject-area resolution spends three weeks finding out what the parent could have told them in one email.

The table lists the groups with what a non-specialist typically misses in each. The pattern across every row is the same and worth stating directly: subject knowledge is necessary and not sufficient. What separates a specialist is knowledge of how that course is assessed - the command terms, the mark allocation conventions, the internal assessment criteria, the question types that recur. That knowledge is course-specific and it is what a radius-based search cannot see.

One practical consequence for the proximity question. If your child's weak subject is in a widely taught group - language and literature, individuals and societies - the pool is larger and a local option may exist. If it is Higher Level mathematics, a Group 4 science at Higher Level, or a less commonly taught language, the pool is small in absolute terms and the honest answer is that the right person will not be nearby. Knowing which case you are in before you start searching saves weeks.

sections.heading: The Diploma core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
paragraphs: The three core components sit alongside the six subjects, they are compulsory, and they are where a disproportionate share of Diploma stress lives. Almost no local tutoring advertises support for them, which is one reason a near-me search returns so little of use to a DP1 family in October. Each component has a school-side adult of record, each has internal deadlines set by the school rather than by anybody else, and each has a specific boundary on what outside help may legitimately do.

The Extended Essay is an independent research essay with a word limit, supervised by a teacher at school. The work that determines its grade happens before any writing: narrowing a question until it can actually be answered within the limit, and finding sources that let the student argue rather than summarise. That narrowing is the single most useful thing an outside adult can contribute, because it requires somebody not attached to the original idea. Everything after that is feedback on drafts the student has written.

Theory of Knowledge asks students to examine how knowledge is produced and justified across different areas, assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Students who treat it as an opinion exercise score poorly; students who learn to structure a claim, test it against a counter-claim and ground both in real examples do well. It is genuinely teachable and almost never taught privately, which makes it an unusually good use of a few sessions. CAS is experiential and reflective, not academically graded, and the honest advice is that it needs organising rather than tutoring.

The table sets out who supervises each component and precisely what external support may and may not do. We publish it in this form because vagueness here is how students end up in front of an academic honesty panel, and because a parent paying for help is entitled to know where the line sits before the first session rather than after a problem.

sections.heading: Gulf Standard Time and the hours that actually work from the island
paragraphs: Here is the part of online delivery that families reasonably worry about: if the best specialist is not in the Gulf, when does the lesson happen? The answer is more comfortable than it sounds, and it is worth setting out as a timetable rather than a reassurance. Every session we schedule is quoted in Gulf Standard Time, so there is no conversion for a parent to get wrong, and the windows that work for a Dubai school day overlap generously with the working day across South Asia and Europe.

A Palm Jumeirah student is typically home between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on which direction the school run goes and which exit the bus uses. Allowing for food and a change of clothes, the usable window runs from about 16:45 to 20:30 on weekday evenings. Within that window, the early part suits tutors in South Asia comfortably and the later part suits tutors in Europe and the United Kingdom. The Friday and Saturday weekend opens a wider set of options again, and for exam-season intensives a morning slot becomes available that the school week does not allow.

What we avoid, deliberately, is a slot that only works for the tutor. A lesson at 21:30 for a sixteen-year-old is a bad lesson regardless of how good the teacher is, and quantitative subjects are the worst affected because tired students make arithmetic errors that look like knowledge gaps. If the only availability for a particular specialist falls outside a sensible window, we say so and offer a different tutor or a weekend slot rather than booking something that will not work.

The table sets out the windows and what each suits. Two practical notes alongside it. Ramadan shifts the whole pattern, and post-Iftar sessions are a normal request we accommodate rather than an exception. And school examination fortnights are usually better paused than pushed through, because a student revising for mocks does not benefit from a new topic landing on a Tuesday evening.
