sections.heading: One tutor for two years, or a specialist for each subject?
paragraphs: Families ask this early and the answer depends on how many subjects are actually in trouble. If one is, the question does not arise. If three are, a parent is weighing continuity against expertise, and the two pull in different directions. One tutor across three subjects knows the student, the workload and the calendar, and costs less in coordination. Three specialists each know their course properly. Our general view is that continuity is worth a great deal at Standard Level and very little at Higher Level, where the course-specific assessment knowledge dominates.

There is a middle arrangement that works well and is rarely suggested. One subject specialist for the Higher Level course that is genuinely difficult, plus a single tutor handling the Standard Level subjects where the problem is organisation and technique rather than content. That typically means two people rather than three or four, keeps the weekly commitment manageable, and puts the expensive expertise where it changes a grade. For a Palm Jumeirah family juggling a long school run, fewer moving parts is itself a benefit.

Keeping the same tutor across both Diploma years is desirable and we try for it, but we do not promise it, because tutors' availability changes and promising it would mean either breaking the promise or keeping a poor match in place. What we do commit to is telling you early if a change is coming, and handing over properly - the error log, the topic history and the marked work go with the student rather than living in one tutor's head.

A final point on the trap in this decision. Some families, faced with three weak subjects, buy three hours a week in January of DP2 and discover in March that nothing has moved, because the limiting factor was never teaching time. It was that a student with six subjects, the core and a long commute had no capacity to absorb three hours of new input. The better answer in that situation is to pick the two subjects where marks move most per hour and leave the third alone, honestly and explicitly.

sections.heading: What a Diploma specialist is published at in Dubai, from the bottom of the market upwards
paragraphs: Work up the ladder rather than down it, because that shows what each rung adds. The bottom rung is budget online tutoring: Dubai rates are published from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. What that rung reliably buys is a present adult and company for homework. What it does not reliably buy is anybody who has taught the current version of your child's course, which for a DP2 student is the whole of the value.

The next rung is a qualified subject tutor working online, published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The addition at this level is genuine subject knowledge. The thing still frequently missing is assessment knowledge - command terms, mark allocation conventions, internal assessment criteria - which is course-specific rather than subject-specific. For many Standard Level problems this rung is the right purchase and the rung above is unnecessary.

The specialist rung is published at AED 200 to 450 and above: TutorChase quotes AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table reaches AED 450 and beyond. This is where assessment literacy lives, and it is the right rung for a Higher Level course or an internal assessment that has gone wrong. Above it sits a premium tier at AED 500 to 650 and more, with BartyED publishing AED 650; before paying it, ask exactly what the premium buys and ask for evidence of any examiner claim in writing, because examiner status is widely asserted and rarely evidenced.

In-home visits sit outside the ladder because they price a different product: AED 180 to 500 per hour from Bestimate and independent tutors, travel included, and monthly packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Every figure here was read from the provider's own page in October 2026 and none of them is an IB Gram price. Set against Dubai school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, a short diagnosed block at the right rung is a small and controllable decision.

sections.heading: What the school already provides, and when outside help is the right call
paragraphs: Before buying anything, find out what the campus already does. Most IB schools the island commutes to run subject clinics, a homework club, and scheduled consultation time with subject teachers, and most have a DP coordinator whose job includes exactly the conversation a worried parent wants to have. These are included in the fee. Families regularly pay for a tutor to explain something a subject teacher would have explained in a twenty-minute meeting, and the only reason is that nobody asked.

The signals that genuinely point to outside help are specific. A gap that has widened across two reporting cycles rather than one poor test. A student who has stopped asking questions in class, which is usually embarrassment rather than disengagement. An internal assessment that has not started six weeks before a school deadline. A Higher Level course where the student is coping with the content and failing the questions, which is an assessment problem the school may not have time to address individually. And a transition - new curriculum, new country, new level - where something specific is missing.

There are also situations where a tutor is the wrong purchase and we will say so. If a student is sleeping five hours a night, no teaching will land. If six subjects are all weak simultaneously, the problem is almost certainly workload or wellbeing rather than teaching, and the conversation belongs with the school. If a family is buying tutoring to manage their own anxiety about a capable student, more hours will not help the student and may harm them. We would rather lose the booking than take money for something that cannot work.

Where outside help is right, the sequence that works is small and early rather than large and late. One subject, diagnosed properly, one session a week, reviewed against marked work at six weeks. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the approach or stop. That sounds obvious written down and it is the opposite of what most families in Dubai actually do, which is to buy a large package in the panic month and never review it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the one boundary that is not negotiable
paragraphs: The IB's academic honesty rules make work produced by somebody else malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. That is the whole reason this section exists on a page about finding a tutor. While researching this cluster we found a provider selling completed internal assessments outright at a published price. A family who buys that is buying a risk their child carries into a university application, not a shortcut, and the correct response to such an offer is to leave.

The legitimate space is large and specific, and a parent should expect it to be described rather than implied. A tutor may explain each assessment criterion and what the next band up requires. A tutor may say plainly that a research question is too broad or that an exploration topic will not produce enough mathematics. A tutor may teach referencing, uncertainty treatment, source evaluation, essay structure and argument. A tutor may read what the student has written and tell them what is weak and why.

What falls outside is equally specific. Writing any part of an Extended Essay, an internal assessment, an exploration or a Theory of Knowledge essay. Redrafting a student's sentences into an adult register. Supplying an outline for the student to fill in. Generating data. Any of these turns the document into something the student cannot account for, and the school's academic honesty process is designed to notice exactly that.

The practical test, again, because it is the only one a parent needs: could the student explain and defend every line of the submitted work in a conversation with their supervisor? If yes, the help was teaching. If no, the help has created an exposure. We state this on every page rather than burying it, because a vague promise of coursework support is how this goes wrong, and because the student is the one who pays for it.

sections.heading: Starting from Palm Jumeirah, with the limits named
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Tell us the campus, the exact course and level, the exam session, and what the last marked piece of work looked like. We look for a specialist in that course with availability inside a sensible Gulf Standard Time window for an island school day. The first session is free and it is a diagnosis, built around a timed past paper rather than an introduction, and afterwards you get a written note naming the specific gaps with an hour count attached.

Now the limits, because this page has argued that honesty about availability is the thing the market lacks. Higher Level mathematics and Higher Level Group 4 sciences are the scarcest categories we recruit for. In a given week the best-matched specialist may have no slot in the island's usable evening window. When that happens we tell you and offer the real options: a different evening, a weekend morning, a different specialist, or a wait with a date attached. We will not fill the hour with a general tutor and let a family discover the mismatch in March.

We also tell you when the timeline is against you. A student starting Higher Level Chemistry support six weeks before final papers can improve technique and triage the three highest-value gaps, and cannot cover the course. Saying so costs us a booking and is the only responsible answer. Where the timeline is workable, the plan is specific: which topics, in which order, how many hours, reviewed against marked work rather than against a feeling.

And the things we will not do at all. We will not promise a grade, a point total or an improvement, and a provider who does is describing their sales process rather than your child. We will not write or redraft assessed work. We will not claim approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, from KHDA, from the Ministry of Education or from any school, because we hold none and the claim is both false and risky. What we will do is match on the subject rather than the postcode, mark the work honestly, and tell you early if it is not working.

process.title: Name the course and the level, not the subject
process.description: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a different teaching job from Standard Level Applications and Interpretation, and the match has to be made at that resolution. Send the course, the level, the session, and a photograph of the last marked piece of work. That email saves three weeks.

process.title: We match on the course, not the postcode
process.description: We look for somebody who teaches that exact course at that level with availability in a sensible Gulf Standard Time window for an island school day. Proximity is not a criterion, because the specialist who can help is statistically unlikely to live within a short drive of Palm Jumeirah.

process.title: A free trial built on a timed paper
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis. The student works a timed section while the tutor watches where the method actually breaks, then they mark it together against published criteria. It is the fastest way to separate a content gap from a technique gap, and it takes an hour.

process.title: A written plan with an hour count
process.description: You receive a short note naming the gaps in priority order with a plausible number of hours against each. Where the honest answer is six hours rather than sixty, it says six. Where the timeline is too short to cover a course, it says that instead of selling a package.

process.title: Weekly sessions, marked work, a six-week review
process.description: Lessons run to a schedule you set in Gulf Standard Time. Written work is marked between sessions and errors are logged by syllabus topic. At six weeks we review against the school's own marks, and if nothing has moved we change the plan or tell you to stop.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course and level, not by drive time
whyPoints.description: A radius selects for willingness to travel. A subject match selects for the ability to teach the thing your child is actually sitting. For a Higher Level course the second is the only one that moves a grade, and it is what makes a specialist reachable from the island at all.

whyPoints.title: Every session quoted in Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: There is no time-zone conversion for a parent to get wrong, and we do not book a slot that only works for the tutor. A 21:30 lesson for a sixteen-year-old is a bad lesson, and quantitative subjects suffer most, so we offer a weekend morning or a different tutor instead.

whyPoints.title: Core support that almost nobody sells
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry a disproportionate share of Diploma stress and barely appear in local tutoring. Scoping a research question and learning to structure a claim against a counter-claim are teachable in a few sessions, and the writing stays the student's own.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page was read from the provider's own page in October 2026 and is attributed. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this cluster publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a UAE family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Higher Level mathematics and Higher Level sciences are the scarcest matches we make, and some weeks the right person has no usable evening slot. We say so and give real options with dates attached. No competitor page we researched discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no grade promises
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or any school, and claims none. We name regulators to explain what they do and link the official route. We do not promise points, grades or improvements, in any phrasing.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near Palm Jumeirah who teaches my child's exact subject?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and the honest version of that answer is more useful than a hopeful one. The Diploma is six subjects across six groups at two levels plus three core components, which is over fifty distinct teaching jobs, and specialists are rare in absolute terms rather than unevenly spread. Island families commute off the Palm for school, and the tutoring supply in the first drive band is general rather than specialist. Replace the radius with the course and the level and the right person becomes findable, which is the whole argument of this page.

faqs.question: How many Diploma specialists realistically sit within a 30-minute drive of the Palm?
faqs.answer: Few, and almost never in the specific course you need. Dubai has 227 private schools running 17 curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for about 7% of private enrolment, so Higher Level science and mathematics teachers are a small population across a very large map. A 30-minute band from the island reaches Al Sufouh, the Marina, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, which contains plenty of general tuition supply and very little course-specific expertise. Doubling the radius does not double your chances; it moves them from zero to near zero.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Palm Jumeirah families drive to?
faqs.answer: Mostly westward into Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, where the widest set of IB campuses sits, and eastward along the coast into Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah and Al Safa. Journey times run roughly fifteen minutes to the first band and twenty to thirty-five to the second, considerably longer at the end of a school day. Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes. Confirm each campus's current programme offer and inspection outcome on KHDA's own site rather than from any list, including this one.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to live in Dubai to teach a Dubai Diploma student?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it is what makes a Higher Level specialist unfindable. What matters is whether the tutor teaches the current version of the course, knows how it is assessed, and can work in a session window that suits a Dubai school day. Every session we schedule is quoted in Gulf Standard Time so there is no conversion to get wrong. What does matter locally is understanding the school calendar, the mock timetable and the way a Dubai week runs, and that is learned rather than inherited by residence.

faqs.question: What are the six IB subject groups and which one needs help most often?
faqs.answer: Studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with a second subject from another group permitted instead of the arts. Mathematics and the sciences generate the most requests from island families, especially at Higher Level, because the assessment knowledge is course-specific and hardest to substitute. Individuals and societies subjects come next, usually over command-term discipline and internal assessment length limits rather than content. The arts generate the fewest requests and the marks there sit mostly in assessed documentation.

faqs.question: Who supervises the Extended Essay, the school or the tutor?
faqs.answer: The school. A teacher at the campus is appointed as supervisor, the school sets the internal deadlines, and the school's academic honesty policy governs. An outside tutor works around that, never instead of it. What a tutor usefully adds is the part that happens before writing: narrowing the research question until it can genuinely be answered within the word limit, and finding sources that let the student argue rather than summarise. After that, the contribution is feedback on drafts the student has written themselves.

faqs.question: What can an outside tutor do about Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and it is one of the best-value few sessions available. Theory of Knowledge asks students to examine how knowledge is produced and justified, assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Students who treat it as opinion score poorly; students who learn to state a claim, test it against a counter-claim and ground both in concrete examples do well. That structure is teachable. What a tutor may not do is supply the argument, provide an outline to fill in, or draft the essay.

faqs.question: How does CAS fit around tutoring sessions?
faqs.answer: CAS is experiential and reflective rather than academically graded, so it needs organising rather than tutoring, and we say so rather than selling hours against it. Where it genuinely collides with academic work is in DP1, when students take on commitments without mapping them against internal assessment deadlines and then lose three weekends in the same month. A single planning conversation that puts CAS commitments, subject deadlines and the Extended Essay on one calendar prevents most of that, and it is not something a family should pay a subject specialist for.

faqs.question: What session times work if the tutor is not in the Gulf?
faqs.answer: A Palm Jumeirah student is usually home between 15:45 and 16:45, so the usable weekday window runs from about 16:45 to 20:30 Gulf Standard Time. The early part suits tutors in South Asia comfortably and the later part suits Europe and the United Kingdom, so the overlap is generous. Friday and Saturday mornings open almost any time zone and suit longer internal assessment work. We avoid anything after about 20:30 for a school night, because quantitative subjects go badly with a tired student. During Ramadan, post-Iftar sessions are a normal arrangement.

faqs.question: Can we keep the same tutor through both Diploma years?
faqs.answer: We try for it and we do not promise it, because tutors' availability changes and a promise would mean either breaking it or keeping a poor match in place. What we do commit to is telling you early if a change is coming and handing over properly: the topic error log, the history of marked work and the plan move with the student rather than living in one tutor's head. Continuity is worth a great deal at Standard Level and rather less at Higher Level, where course-specific assessment knowledge matters more.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Palm Jumeirah family start lessons?
faqs.answer: For a commonly taught Standard Level course, usually within a few days, because the pool is wide enough that an evening slot exists. For Higher Level mathematics or a Higher Level science, it can take longer, and we will give you a date rather than a vague reassurance. The limiting factor is almost never our willingness; it is the overlap between a scarce specialist's availability and a usable Gulf-evening window for an island school day. If the wait is more than a fortnight we say so up front.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma specialist charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond. Below that, a qualified subject tutor online is published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Above it, premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits price a different product at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. All figures were read from providers' own pages in October 2026 and none of them is an IB Gram price.

faqs.question: Would a tutor come to the Crescent for an evening lesson?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Palm Jumeirah families are one-to-one and live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Independent tutors in the market do travel, and the published rates show what it costs: AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The Crescent is a long detour from the mainland and the quotes reflect it.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor may legally charge for private lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What may a tutor never do with my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Write any part of it, redraft the student's sentences into an adult register, supply a structure to fill in, or generate the data. Those are malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. What a tutor may do is substantial: explain each criterion and what the next band requires, say plainly when a research question or exploration topic will not work, teach uncertainty treatment, referencing and evaluation, and give written feedback on drafts the student has produced. The test is whether your child could explain and defend every line themselves.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-palm-jumeirah.closingHeading: Replace the radius with the subject
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-palm-jumeirah.closingBody: A near-me search from Palm Jumeirah is measuring drive time, and drive time does not predict whether somebody can teach Higher Level Chemistry or scope an Extended Essay question. Send us the course, the level, the exam session and the last marked piece of work, and we will match on those instead. The first session is a free trial built around a timed paper, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time after the commute home, and you will leave it with a written list of gaps and an hour count. If the honest answer is that the timeline is too short, we will tell you that as well.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-pearl-jumeira.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level, along with Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay process support. Pearl Jumeira bookings run one-to-one over live video, in slots set to Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What a proximity search returns, and why the IB breaks it
paragraphs: A near me search sorts by distance because distance is the only variable it can see. For a subject with a deep local market that is a reasonable approximation of availability. For the IB Diploma in Dubai it is a poor one, and the reason is arithmetic rather than opinion. In 2024-25 Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian. The teaching workforce follows the enrolment. A list sorted by proximity will therefore be dominated by people whose experience is British curriculum, however the listings describe themselves.

That matters because the Diploma is not a harder version of A Level or IGCSE. Six subjects run concurrently at two levels, each with an internal assessment carrying a fixed percentage of the grade. Three subjects are taken at Higher Level, which is not Standard Level with extra chapters but a different depth with different papers. Alongside them sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service, each with its own published criteria. Somebody who has taught the subject matter without having taught inside that structure will be a competent teacher of the content and an unreliable guide to the assessment, and the assessment is where the grade is lost.

Pearl Jumeira sharpens the problem again. The community sits on reclaimed land off the Jumeirah 1 shoreline, reached by a single causeway, so a visiting tutor must be free at a fixed hour, prepared for the late-afternoon approach, and in possession of the right subject at the right level. Each condition cuts the set, and they cut it multiplicatively. For a widely taught Higher Level subject the result may be one or two names. For a thinly taught one it is routinely none.

What families do next is predictable and understandable. The syllabus condition gets relaxed, because the distance condition is the one that is visible. A good general tutor arrives at a specialist rate, and the mismatch shows up months later in an internal assessment draft that has been written without reference to the criteria it will be marked against.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason this page argues for that is availability rather than technology: for a curriculum carrying 7 per cent of local enrolment, the difference between the whole pool and the causeway-reachable fraction of it is the difference between a Higher Level specialist and somebody doing their best.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level depth actually sits, subject by subject
paragraphs: A near me list does not distinguish between a tutor who has taught a subject and one who has taught it inside the Diploma at Higher Level. This section does, honestly, including where the answer is unflattering. The table below sets out the picture a Pearl Jumeira family should expect by subject group.

Read the right-hand column rather than the left. What a family needs to know is not whether a subject is hard but whether somebody who has prepared students for that specific assessment is realistically available. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Chemistry at Higher Level are the two tightest points in Dubai, the first because Paper 3 and the proof-style reasoning do not transfer from other maths teaching, the second because medicine and dentistry pathways concentrate demand there.

The core components are tighter still, and almost nobody says so. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay require somebody who has supervised them and read the published criteria closely, and the number of people in any city who have done that is small relative to the number of Diploma students who need help. A tutoring listing that offers Theory of Knowledge alongside twenty other subjects is making a claim worth testing with a single question: which assessment criteria does the Theory of Knowledge essay carry, and what does each reward?

Where supply is good, this page says so. Biology at Higher Level, English A, History and Economics are reasonably covered in Dubai, and a family requesting those has a genuine choice. That distinction between well-covered and thin subjects is the practical content of an availability conversation, and it is the conversation no competitor page in this cluster has.

sections.heading: Four questions that reveal Diploma experience rather than subject knowledge
paragraphs: You do not need to know the Diploma to test for it. Each of these questions has an answer that somebody who has worked inside the programme gives without pausing, and that somebody who has taught the subject elsewhere approaches generally.

First: what percentage of this subject's grade is the internal assessment, and what are the criteria called? Every Diploma subject has one, the percentage is fixed and published, and the criteria have names. A tutor who has prepared students for it will answer in a sentence. A tutor who has not will talk about coursework in general terms.

Second: what changes between Standard and Higher Level in this subject? The right answer is specific, naming additional content, additional papers where they exist, and the extra teaching hours. The wrong answer is that Higher Level covers the same material in more depth, which is true of nothing in particular and tells you the person has not taught both.

Third: where do students lose marks on the extended response questions? A Diploma teacher answers with command terms and mark allocations, because a four-mark explain question requires four distinct points and students reliably write three good ones at length. Somebody outside the programme answers with a general observation about exam technique.

Fourth: what may a tutor do with an internal assessment draft, and what may they not? The correct answer is firm and immediate: teach the criteria, teach the content, give feedback on what the student has written, and write none of it. Hesitation here is the most useful signal in the entire conversation, because it is a question about integrity rather than about expertise.
bullets: Internal assessment percentage and criterion names should come instantly

sections.heading: Reading a Dubai school inspection report, and what it does not tell you
paragraphs: Families searching for a tutor near them are often also assessing the school, and in Dubai that means reading a KHDA inspection outcome. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and its inspections place schools on a six-band scale. Understanding what the bands mean is useful; understanding what they do not measure is more useful.

The scale runs from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. A band is a judgement about a whole school across many measures, and it is published on the regulator's own site, which makes it a far better source than any tutoring website's claim about which schools are best. What it is not is a statement about a particular subject at Higher Level in a particular year, which is the thing a Diploma family actually wants to know.

That gap explains a pattern worth naming. A school in a high band can have a thin year in a specific Higher Level subject because one teacher left in August. A school in a middling band can have an exceptional Higher Level chemistry department. Neither shows up in the band. The question that gets closer to the truth is asked at the school rather than read in a report: how many students took this subject at Higher Level last year, and who is teaching it this year?

The regulator map is worth knowing in full, because it differs by emirate and almost no competitor page in this market names it. Dubai is KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate. Sharjah is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits with the emirate.

sections.heading: Scheduling, Gulf Standard Time and families who travel
paragraphs: A near me search is partly a search about convenience, and convenience in a Diploma year is mostly about whether a session survives the calendar. Pearl Jumeira households often travel between terms and sometimes during them, and the Diploma does not pause for it.

All sessions here are set in Gulf Standard Time, which is the reference the school's own deadlines use, so a weekly slot has a fixed relationship to the student's week rather than to a tutor's convenience. For a family spending part of a holiday elsewhere, the slot can hold rather than lapse, which is the difference between resuming in September where the student left off and spending the first fortnight re-establishing ground. A visiting arrangement cannot do that at any price.

Within term time the constraint is the afternoon. Schools in this cluster finish between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the causeway approach and the drive home take the next thirty to forty-five minutes, and activity programmes run to roughly 6pm. The practical Diploma windows are an early slot around 4:45pm where activities allow, and a reliable one from 6:45pm. Nothing useful happens after about 8:30pm on a school night, particularly in quantitative subjects.

One more scheduling feature of the Diploma deserves planning rather than reaction. The second year contains a term in which internal assessment deadlines, mocks and the densest content coincide. Everybody knows this term is coming and almost nobody books for it in advance. A family that reserves an extra weekly hour for that term in September pays the same as one that scrambles for it in January and gets a materially better arrangement, because in January the people with the right experience are already committed.

sections.heading: Coverage, match time and the honest version of availability
paragraphs: No platform covers every Diploma subject at every level in every slot, and the ones implying otherwise are the ones to question. Among the competitor pages reviewed for this market, none discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE families to contact numbers outside the country without saying so. Stating the limits is therefore unusual enough to be worth doing plainly.

The position is as follows. Well-covered subjects are matched quickly, and that includes most Standard Level teaching and Higher Level biology, English A, History and Economics. Tighter subjects, particularly Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Chemistry at Higher Level, are matched but may involve a wait for a specific slot. Narrow requests, including several Language B options and supervision-level support for Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay, may not be available at all, and in those cases the answer given is no rather than an assurance.

Nothing is taken on account against a match that has not been confirmed. That sounds like a small commitment and it is the one most often broken in this market, because a deposit against a hoped-for match converts a parent's urgency into revenue. Where a suitable tutor cannot be found, the useful thing a platform can do is say so quickly enough for the family to look elsewhere.

The table sets out what to expect. Reading it alongside the supply table earlier in this page gives a Pearl Jumeira family something a proximity search cannot: a realistic picture of what is available, where the gaps are, and how long a match is likely to take for the particular subject and level their child is sitting.

sections.heading: The boundary on assessed work, stated before anyone asks
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment with a fixed percentage of the grade, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sit alongside them. All of it must be the student's own work. On a page about finding a tutor, this belongs near the decision rather than in small print, because it is one of the few questions whose answer separates providers decisively.

What legitimate support looks like is substantial and worth paying for. Explaining what each criterion rewards and how the marks are allocated. Teaching the subject content the student has chosen to work with. Asking the questions that reduce an unanswerable research question to an answerable one. Showing how an argument or a calculation should be structured. Reading a draft the student has written and saying what is absent from it. For most students that is the highest-value work available in the programme, because the criteria are published and the failure modes are predictable.

What is not available here, at any price, is production. No part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay will be written, drafted, redrafted or supplied, and no research question will be handed over for adoption. At least one operator ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk that falls on the student rather than on the seller, and the consequence attaches to a transcript rather than to an invoice.

A related limit concerns materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB and to the examination boards, and are referenced and linked rather than redistributed. A tutor who offers a folder of copied material has answered a question about their standards that nobody had to ask.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what the proximity premium is buying
paragraphs: Market figures belong on this page because they are part of the availability argument rather than separate from it. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB rates from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Premium examiner-branded providers reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those figures belong to the named providers and were read in October 2026.

The point for a Pearl Jumeira family is what the upper bands are actually paying for. On an island served by one causeway, a substantial part of an in-home rate covers a drive across Al Wasl Road and a queue onto the island, and nothing in that drive improves a Higher Level chemistry session. Meanwhile the thing that does improve it, experience of the specific assessment, is not reliably priced at all, because the general and specialist pools quote similar numbers.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared papers, working annotated and kept, and recordings available. Nothing in the rate pays for travel, and the match is made on subject and level.

Some families will still prefer a person in the room, and that is a real preference rather than an error. The recommendation on this page is only that the choice be made with the supply picture visible. Run the four questions in the earlier section on whoever is reachable. If the answers are specific and confident, the local option is a good one. If they are general, the premium is paying for the causeway.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared papers, annotated working kept after the session and recordings available. The reason this page argues for that arrangement is supply rather than preference: for a curriculum at 7 per cent of local enrolment, the reachable pool and the real pool are very different sizes.

faqs.question: Can a weekly slot survive a family travelling during the Diploma?
faqs.answer: With an online arrangement, yes, and that is a practical rather than a cosmetic advantage. Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time, which is the reference the school's own deadlines use, so a slot holds rather than lapses when a household is away for part of a holiday. The alternative is resuming in September and spending the first fortnight re-establishing ground already covered. A visiting arrangement cannot continue through travel at any price.

faqs.question: When should a Pearl Jumeira family book the second Diploma year's extra hour?
faqs.answer: In September of the first year, not in January of the second. Every Diploma contains a term where internal assessment deadlines, mocks and the densest content coincide, and everybody knows it is coming. A family reserving an additional weekly hour for that term in advance pays the same as one scrambling when it arrives, and gets a materially better match, because by then the tutors with the right Higher Level experience are already committed to other students.

faqs.question: What times of day actually work for a Diploma session on the island?
faqs.answer: Two windows. An early slot around 4:45pm where the activity programme allows it, which is the strongest option because nobody is tired yet and which has to be claimed in September. And a reliable slot from 6:45pm, after food, which survives the whole year. School in this cluster ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the causeway approach plus the drive home takes thirty to forty-five minutes. After about 8:30pm quantitative subjects stop holding on a school night.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do with an internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Explain what each criterion rewards and how the marks are allocated, teach the subject content involved, ask the questions that narrow an unanswerable research question into an answerable one, show how an argument or calculation should be structured, and give feedback on what the student has already written. What a tutor may not do is write, draft, redraft or supply any part of it, or hand over a research question. Submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk carried by the student alone.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level chemistry tutor for this area?
faqs.answer: Usually quickly, with the caveat that a specific weekday slot may involve a wait, because Higher Level chemistry is among the tightest supply points in Dubai. Demand concentrates there through medicine and dentistry pathways. Where a particular slot cannot be filled, the answer given is a stated match time rather than a reassurance, and nothing is taken on account against a match that has not been confirmed. Where no suitable tutor exists, that is said rather than filled with a generalist.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost in Dubai, and is the island premium worth it?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's 2026 table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270. Premium examiner-branded providers reach AED 650, with BartyED at that figure. On a single-causeway island a large part of the in-home premium covers the approach, which improves nothing about the teaching.

faqs.question: Is there an advantage in a tutor who has taught at my child's school?
faqs.answer: There can be, and there is a constraint worth knowing. Familiarity with a school's internal deadlines and teaching order is genuinely useful. However, in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So ask whether the person teaches at your child's school, and expect an immediate answer.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-pearl-jumeira.closingHeading: Specify the level, test for the programme, then weigh the distance
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-pearl-jumeira.closingBody: A near me search cannot see the thing that matters for the Diploma, so the useful move is to supply it yourself. Name the subject and the level together. Run the four questions on anyone reachable, including us, and listen for how quickly the internal assessment percentage and criterion names arrive. Then decide whether a premium for somebody who can cross the causeway on a weekday afternoon buys anything a Higher Level specialist elsewhere does not. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with coverage limits stated before any booking and a free trial lesson first.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-remraam.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma subjects to students across the Dubailand corridor. Each profile names subject and level, and the first conversation is about where the student sits in the two-year cycle, because that decides what the hour should be spent on.

intro.heading: The same request means different things in Year 12 and Year 13
paragraphs: Two families send almost identical messages. One has a Year 12 whose first report came back a band below expectations. The other has a Year 13 eleven weeks from final papers. The words are the same and the right answer is not remotely similar, because in the first case almost every lever is still available and in the second only two or three are.

In Year 12 the levers are large. Subject and level combinations can sometimes still change. Internal assessment topics are being chosen, and those components carry a meaningful share of each subject grade with deadlines months out. The Extended Essay question is still open. Non-calculator fluency, notation discipline and answer construction can all be rebuilt without pressure. Money spent here buys ceiling.

In Year 13 the levers are narrow. The internal components are mostly submitted, the subject combination is fixed, and content genuinely absent will not become secure enough to deploy. What remains is technique, timing, command-term discipline and marked-script repair, and those still move marks, often substantially. Money spent here buys execution.

Remraam shapes the practical side rather than the academic one. It is a low-rise apartment community in Dubailand, built as Al Thamam and Al Ramth with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11, so Diploma students here have generally moved outward to Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City, and their evenings are longer than their younger siblings' were.

The reason this page leads with the calendar rather than with subjects is that families in this corridor consistently buy help at the least efficient moment. The pattern is predictable: nothing in Year 12 because the grades look survivable, then a heavy commitment in the spring of Year 13 when only technique is still movable. Reversing that order usually costs less in total and produces a better result, which is an awkward thing for a tutoring page to say and true nonetheless.

The other reason is that the Diploma runs three calendars at once. The six subjects have their own internal deadlines. The core has deadlines set by the school rather than by the IB. And in the final year the university application season occupies the same ten weeks as the heaviest coursework. A plan that tracks only the subjects collides with the other two, and that collision is what most Year 13 distress in this belt actually is.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, so the session can start when the student sits down rather than when a car arrives. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to come to an Al Ramth or Al Thamam address. What follows is the calendar, phase by phase, with the dated anchors that are actually verifiable.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma, laid out
paragraphs: The Diploma has a rhythm that varies little between schools. The first term of Year 12 is content at a new pace, with students discovering that Higher Level means a different kind of work rather than more of the same. By the second term internal assessment topics are being discussed and the Extended Essay subject is chosen. The third term of Year 12 usually brings a first set of internal examinations and, in many schools, a draft deadline or two.

Year 13 inverts the balance. The autumn is the heaviest period in the entire course, because coursework deadlines, the core components, the autumn mocks and university applications land in the same ten weeks. Students who arrive at that autumn with the Extended Essay substantially done have a very different term from those who do not, and that is a decision taken a year earlier.

After the autumn comes a quieter stretch where papers are the only real activity, then the session itself. The useful way to think about tutoring across this is as three different products: ceiling work, predicted-grade work, and execution work. A family that buys the same weekly hour across all twenty-four months pays for twenty-four months and gets the benefit of perhaps eight.

The IB's own session and results dates are not restated here. The IB site, through the school's Diploma coordinator, is the only reliable source for them, and any page that publishes them without that check will eventually be wrong. What is safe to plan against is the sequence, and the sequence is stable.

sections.heading: The core, counted backwards
paragraphs: The core causes more distress in this corridor than any single subject, and almost all of it is scheduling rather than difficulty. The Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and CAS all have internal deadlines set by the school, which means they differ between the schools Remraam students attend and cannot be looked up in a general guide.

The Extended Essay is the big one. It runs to 4,000 words with supervised reflection sessions along the way, and the decision that sets its ceiling is the research question, settled before any writing. Most weak essays are not badly written; they are answering a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words with the sources available. One session interrogating the question in the second term of Year 12 is worth more than ten in Year 13.

Theory of Knowledge has two parts. The exhibition asks a student to connect three objects to an internal assessment prompt, and the essay responds to a prescribed title with areas of knowledge structuring the argument. Essays that answer the title in general terms, however fluently, are capped. Choosing a title early and thinking about it over months produces better work than writing it in the term it is due.

CAS is documented rather than graded in the same way, and the documentation is where students lose time in Year 13. Recording activity and reflection as it happens rather than reconstructing it later is the whole trick, and it is the same habit the Extended Essay reflection sessions require.

sections.heading: Predicted grades and why the autumn mock matters most
paragraphs: Predicted grades are produced by the school from the evidence it holds, which in the autumn of Year 13 means mock performance and coursework. A university application in most systems travels on those predictions, which gives an autumn mock a weight far beyond its own marks. Students rarely understand this until afterwards.

The practical consequence is that technique work belongs before the mock rather than after it. A student who sits an autumn mock having never practised under timed conditions produces a score that understates them, and that score then follows them into an application. Four or five timed papers across the preceding weeks is a small intervention with a disproportionate effect, and it is cheap compared with the alternative.

The second consequence is about collision. Applications, coursework deadlines, core components and mocks arrive in the same ten weeks, and students handle each badly because they are handling all four. Mapping the deadlines onto one page at the start of the term, then deciding deliberately what gets less attention, produces a better outcome than attempting everything.

A caution about predictions themselves. They are an estimate from partial evidence, and schools vary in how generously they predict. A prediction below a student's capability can sometimes be revisited with evidence later in the year, and that conversation is worth having politely and early rather than after offers arrive. It is a school conversation, not a tutor's.

One further practical point. Universities in different countries weigh predictions differently, and a student applying to several systems at once may need the same prediction to satisfy more than one threshold. That is a reason to treat the autumn mock as the serious examination it functionally is, rather than as a rehearsal that can be taken lightly and improved on later.

sections.heading: Mock season in a Diploma, read properly
paragraphs: A Diploma mock season produces six subject scripts in a fortnight, and the volume is part of why they get read as grades rather than as evidence. Those scripts are the only specific information anyone has about where marks are going, and they arrive while there is still time to act.

Each script separates four failures that feel identical to the student. Content absence shows as questions untouched. Technique loss shows as right method and lost marks. Timing collapse shows as a strong start and an abandoned final page. Misreading shows as a good answer to the question that was not asked, almost always because a command term was skipped in a long stem.

Reading six scripts together is more useful than reading one, because the same failure usually appears in several. A student who skips command terms does it in chemistry, economics and English alike, and one fortnight of drilling lifts all three. A student whose losses are content-based in a single subject has a narrower problem with a longer timescale. Only the comparison across subjects reveals which case applies.

On the grades themselves, schools set mocks at different severities, and a paper marked harshly to motivate a cohort is not a forecast. Treat the number as a position and the annotations as the information. Where a school publishes its own boundaries, compare them against the most recent published boundaries for the same component rather than assuming they match.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the Dubai academic year
paragraphs: A Diploma plan written in September that assumes uninterrupted weekly sessions for two years is fiction, and finding that out in the spring of Year 13 is expensive. The UAE academic year has long breaks and short dense terms, Ramadan reshapes the day, and families in this corridor travel.

Ramadan is the clearest case. School days shorten, energy patterns change, and many families here prefer sessions after Iftar. Because nothing is being driven anywhere, a change of time costs nothing and can be arranged week by week rather than negotiated once. Fixing those slots at the start of the month is easier than competing for them in the second half of it.

Breaks work the other way and are chronically underused. They are the only stretches with no competing homework, which makes them the natural window for an Extended Essay push, for closing a content gap, or for the first serious run of timed papers. The summer between Year 12 and Year 13 is the single most valuable week-for-week period in the course, and most students spend it recovering from Year 12.

The practical move is to mark the fixed points once at the start of each year: term dates, mock windows, internal and core deadlines, Ramadan, and planned travel. Everything else flexes around them, and the review conversation every few weeks becomes short because the frame already exists.

A short note on travel. Families in this corridor often leave the UAE for several weeks in the summer and for part of a winter break, and a tutoring plan that pretends otherwise produces either wasted fees or an abandoned arrangement. Saying which weeks are gone when the plan is made means the block can be sized to the weeks that actually exist.

sections.heading: Retakes, the November session and what it costs in time
paragraphs: A Diploma result that falls short is not the end of the route, and the options are worth understanding before results day rather than during it. The IB runs two sessions a year and UAE schools sit the May one, so a retake generally means the following session, with the specific dates confirmed through the school's coordinator rather than from any tutoring page.

The cost is mostly in time and sequencing. A retake means preparing one or two subjects while starting something else, often a foundation year or a deferred university place, and it means the new grade arrives well into the following academic year. Any institution holding a place needs to know that timing in advance, and that conversation belongs with them and with the school before an entry is lodged.

There is also an enquiry-upon-results route, which is separate from a retake and has its own deadlines set by the IB and administered through the school. Where a student's performance in a component looks inconsistent with everything else, that route is worth asking the coordinator about promptly, because its windows are short.

The preparation for a retake is narrow rather than general. The content has been taught, the real paper has been sat, and the specific losses are known. Six to eight focused weeks on the failed components plus the technique that lost marks across the paper is almost always a better plan than restarting a subject, and it costs less.

sections.heading: What tuition costs at each phase of the course
paragraphs: Because the three phases are different products, the sensible spend differs across them, and thinking about it that way usually reduces the total. Year 12 wants a modest weekly hour over a long period. The autumn of Year 13 wants a short intense block before mocks. The final stretch wants two sessions a week for eight to twelve weeks. A single weekly hour running for twenty-four months costs more than all three and delivers less.

The bands are published. A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

The cheaper tier exists and has a use. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, which can be reasonable value for routine practice with an organised student. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the price, Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27. All of these are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the questions that save a term
paragraphs: Assessed work must be the student's own, authenticated by the teacher. A tutor teaches the subject, explains what criteria reward, interrogates a research question, critiques a method and marks a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text, or provide data the student did not collect. One provider in this market sells completed internal assessments; refusing that offer is simple, and it is worth explaining to the student why, because the offer reaches them too.

Board material has its own rule. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers, so sessions reference and link to the official pages rather than circulating copies. Nobody holds unreleased material, whatever is implied about examiner connections.

On the legal side, an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. It covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

Three questions save a term. What phase of the course do you think we are in, and why. Which internal and core deadlines fall in the next ten weeks. And what will you refuse to do with a draft. A provider who answers the first two by asking for the school's calendar is doing the right thing.

process.title: Ask the school for its internal calendar
process.description: Coursework draft dates, final submission dates, core deadlines and mock windows are set by the school and differ between the Dubai schools Remraam students attend. Having that calendar in writing is the single most useful thing a Diploma family can hold.

process.title: Say which phase you are in
process.description: First Year 12 report, autumn of Year 13 before mocks, or final stretch. Those three are different products and the message should name which. If you are unsure, say what the last piece of marked work was and when the next deadline falls.

process.title: Attach one marked script or draft
process.description: A marked paper, a returned internal assessment draft or a mock script lets the first session work rather than introduce itself. It also lets a tutor say honestly whether less help is needed than you feared, which happens more often than families expect.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a block with an end date
process.description: A trial over live video at no cost and before payment. What follows should be a block with a defined length and purpose rather than an open weekly commitment, because the right amount of help changes sharply between phases of the course.

process.title: Review at the phase boundaries
process.description: The natural review points are the end of Year 12, the end of the autumn term in Year 13, and six weeks out from the session. At each the plan should change shape, not just continue. Session notes record the named error patterns and which have closed.

whyPoints.title: The phase decides the product
whyPoints.description: Year 12 ceiling work, autumn predicted-grade work and final-stretch execution are three different jobs. Buying the same weekly hour for two years costs more than all three and delivers the benefit of about eight months of it.

whyPoints.title: The core is mapped before it collides
whyPoints.description: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS deadlines are set internally and differ by school, which is why they surprise families. Putting them on one page at the start of Year 12 removes most of the distress the core causes in this corridor.

whyPoints.title: The autumn mock is treated as what it is
whyPoints.description: Predicted grades come from that mock and a university application travels on them. Four or five timed papers beforehand is a small intervention that stops a capable student under-representing themselves at exactly the wrong moment.

whyPoints.title: Blocks have end dates
whyPoints.description: Every arrangement proposed here has a length and a purpose, and we will say when a block should stop. An indefinite weekly hour is easier to sell and worse value, particularly in the quieter stretches of Year 12.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling absorbs a long school run
whyPoints.description: Remraam Diploma students travel further than its IGCSE students. Because nothing is being driven to Al Thamam or Al Ramth, a session starts when the student sits down and can shift within the evening or after Iftar at no cost.

whyPoints.title: IB dates are not invented
whyPoints.description: No IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site through the school's coordinator is the only reliable source. Pages that restate those dates for search traffic are wrong within a year and parents act on them.

faqs.question: Is a tutor near Remraam better than one on a screen for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma the screen usually wins, because the binding constraint is subject and phase expertise rather than presence. Selecting by distance from Al Ramth narrows the field to tutors based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, most of whom work at IGCSE level with Diploma work as an extension. Selecting by subject and level removes that limit. It also removes the arrival window, which matters when a student travels back from Dubai Hills or Al Barsha South each afternoon.

faqs.question: We are in Year 12 and the first report was poor. How urgent is it?
faqs.answer: Less urgent than it feels and more valuable than help bought later. In Year 12 almost every lever is still available: internal assessment topics are being chosen, the Extended Essay question is open, subject levels can sometimes still change, and fluency and notation can be rebuilt without pressure. A weekly hour now buys ceiling. The same money in Year 13 buys execution only, because content genuinely absent will not become secure enough to use. Starting now usually means buying fewer total hours.

faqs.question: What should a Year 13 family expect tutoring to change?
faqs.answer: Technique, timing and marked-script repair, which together still move marks substantially. What it will not change is content that was never learned, because anything acquired in the last weeks is not secure enough to deploy under pressure. An honest plan at this stage names the two or three topics with the heaviest recoverable loss, drills answer construction and command-term discipline, rehearses pacing and question order, and deliberately writes off low-density topics. Anyone promising more than that in eleven weeks is selling.

faqs.question: Why does the autumn mock in Year 13 matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because predicted grades are produced from the evidence the school holds, and in the autumn of the final year that means mock performance and coursework. A university application in most systems travels on those predictions. A student who sits that mock having never worked under timed conditions produces a score that understates them, and the score follows them into the application. Four or five timed papers in the preceding weeks is a small, cheap intervention with a disproportionate effect on the rest of the year.

faqs.question: When should the Extended Essay question be settled?
faqs.answer: In the second term of Year 12, before it is approved. The research question sets the ceiling: most weak Extended Essays are competently written and answer something that cannot be answered in 4,000 words with the sources actually available. One session interrogating the question at that point is worth more than ten spent improving prose in Year 13. It also changes the autumn of the final year completely, because a student arriving at that term with the essay substantially done has room for everything else.

faqs.question: How do we stop the core colliding with everything else?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for its own internal calendar in writing during the first weeks of Year 12. Extended Essay milestones, Theory of Knowledge deadlines, CAS expectations, coursework draft dates and mock windows are set internally and differ between schools, so no general guide can supply them. Put them on one page with the subject deadlines and planned family travel. The distress the core causes in this corridor is almost entirely scheduling rather than difficulty, and scheduling responds to a page of dates.

faqs.question: Is the Theory of Knowledge essay worth paying for help with?
faqs.answer: One or two sessions at the right moment, yes. The common failure is answering a prescribed title in general terms without areas of knowledge structuring the argument, which caps the essay however fluent the writing. Choosing a title early and thinking about it across months produces better work than writing it in the term it falls due. A tutor can explain the assessment expectations, interrogate the chosen title and mark the student's own draft; the essay itself must be entirely their own work.

faqs.question: How should the summer between Year 12 and Year 13 be used?
faqs.answer: It is the most valuable block in the course week for week and is usually spent recovering. The highest-return uses are an Extended Essay push, since the autumn is otherwise impossible, closing one content gap properly, and the first serious run of timed papers so that the autumn mock is not the student's first encounter with a clock. Three or four sessions in a week is realistic when there is no competing homework, and it costs the same per hour as term time.

faqs.question: What happens if a Diploma result falls short?
faqs.answer: There are two separate routes and both have short windows. An enquiry upon results is administered through the school and is appropriate where a component looks inconsistent with everything else; ask the coordinator immediately rather than waiting. A retake means sitting again at a later session, with dates confirmed through the school rather than from any tutoring page. Preparation for a retake is narrow, since the real paper has been sat and the losses are known, so six to eight focused weeks usually beats restarting a subject.

faqs.question: Will sessions continue through Ramadan for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Usually moved rather than paused. School days shorten, energy patterns shift, and many families along this corridor prefer slots after Iftar. Because the lesson arrives over live video and nobody is driving, a change of time costs nothing and can be arranged week by week. Fixing those slots early in the month is easier than competing for them later. Where a family prefers to pause entirely, the slot can be held, and the plan is reviewed against the internal deadlines either way.

faqs.question: Should tutoring run every week for two years?
faqs.answer: No, and we will say so. The sensible shape is a modest weekly hour through Year 12 to build ceiling, a short intense block before the autumn mocks in Year 13, and two sessions a week for eight to twelve weeks in the final stretch. A single hour running for twenty-four months costs more than all three combined and delivers the benefit of about eight months of it. Every block proposed here has a defined length and purpose rather than being open-ended.

faqs.question: How do six mock scripts get used rather than filed?
faqs.answer: By reading them together. Each separates content absence, which shows as untouched questions, from technique loss where the method was right, from timing collapse visible as an abandoned last page, from misreading caused by skipping a command term. Across six subjects the same failure usually appears in several, which makes one fortnight of drilling unusually efficient. A single script hides that pattern and six grades reveal nothing at all. Bring the scripts to a first session rather than a description of the results.

faqs.question: Does the school we moved to change the tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: Considerably, because it sets the scheme of work, the option topics in the sciences, the mock window and every internal deadline. Two Diploma students in Dubai described as taking the same subject can sit different option questions and face coursework deadlines months apart. Naming the school alongside the subject and level in the first message means the tutor works to the right calendar and sets questions from the right option, which is a bigger practical difference than the postcode could ever be.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a university application as well?
faqs.answer: Not as an admissions service, and this page makes no claim to perform or guarantee any admissions outcome. What a subject tutor can usefully do is make the autumn mock go better, since predicted grades flow from it, and help a student articulate why they want a subject, which is useful for interviews and personal statements. Entry requirements should be read from each institution's own published entry profile with the school's careers office, because they differ by country and change between cycles.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-remraam.closingBody: Before choosing a tutor, get the school's internal calendar in writing: coursework drafts, final submissions, core deadlines and mock windows. Then say which phase of the Diploma you are in, attach one marked script or draft, and a free trial lesson over live video is arranged before any payment is taken. What comes back will be a block with a length and a purpose rather than an open weekly commitment. Lessons are delivered online on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only.

intro.heading: There is no such thing as an IB syllabus
paragraphs: Serena sits off Al Qudra Road at the outer edge of the Dubailand belt, among townhouse clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva, with Mudon, Villanova and Remraam close by. Families here searching for an IB tutor nearby are rarely attached to the word 'nearby'. What they want is somebody who genuinely knows what their child is being assessed on, and the local search cannot tell them who that is.

Part of the problem is the phrase itself. The IB is four programmes: the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme, the Diploma Programme and the Career-related Programme. Within the Diploma there are dozens of subjects, each with a Higher and a Standard Level that differ in content, papers and weightings, plus a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS that is assessed on its own terms. 'IB tutor' describes all of it and distinguishes none of it.

The second part is that subject guides change. Several Diploma subjects have been through a revised syllabus in recent years, with different assessment structures from their predecessors. A tutor who taught a subject competently under the old guide and has not read the new one will teach the wrong paper structure confidently. That is not detectable from an advert, and it is not detectable from a conversation about how experienced somebody is.

So this page is a set of questions rather than a sales pitch. What to ask about the programme, the subject and the level. Which components exist and which of them a tutor may legitimately touch. What the core requires and why general subject tutors cannot help with it. Where our own coverage is genuinely thin. And what the Dubai market charges, with sources, so you can judge any quote including ours.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram has no office or centre in the UAE and does not send tutors to UAE addresses, because home visits are a service we run only in India. Serena students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is also why the proximity question is moot for us: the tutor is chosen for the subject and level rather than for being within driving distance of Al Qudra Road.

One standing note. We publish no IB exam or results dates anywhere on this site, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a family plans around has to be checkable. UAE schools sit the May session; ask your child's IB coordinator for the window and for the school's own internal deadlines, which fall earlier and are the ones that bite. For scale, Dubai's private sector runs 227 schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students, with International Baccalaureate programmes at 7 per cent of enrolment, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. A minority programme inside a very large market is exactly the situation in which a local search misleads.
