dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-serena.programmesIntro: Start by naming the programme, because the four are assessed in completely different ways and a tutor strong in one may know nothing about another.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based, with no external examinations and no subject syllabus in the conventional sense. Useful tutoring is about capability rather than coverage: number fluency without a calculator, reading stamina, and writing that holds a reason across several sentences. A tutor who asks which textbook the school uses has misunderstood the programme.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the primary years also carry KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and combined classes prohibited. Families arriving from countries where Arabic was optional often meet this requirement for the first time here, and it is a separate stream rather than something absorbed into general support.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked from 0 to 8, with the criterion names differing by group. There are no past papers. A tutor who cannot name the four criteria in your child's subject is teaching content and hoping it maps onto the marking, which is the single commonest failure in MYP tutoring.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision around the Dubailand belt is thinner than Diploma or British-curriculum provision, so Serena students on this track often travel further to school. That shortens the evening and makes the criterion-focused approach even more important, because there is less time available to waste on content the student already has.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, graded out of 45 with the core alongside. Each subject has its own papers, weightings and Internal Assessment, typically carrying 20 to 25 per cent of the subject grade. This is where level matters most: Higher and Standard Level are different courses with different components, not the same course at different speeds.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and in Dubai schools the internal coursework deadlines generally fall weeks before the IB's own dates. The school's calendar is therefore the planning anchor. Ask the IB coordinator for both sets of dates and treat the earlier one as real.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses combined with a career-related study and a reflective project, plus a personal and professional skills component assessed on written reflection. Tutoring usually concentrates on the DP courses carried into it and on the reflective writing, which is marked against descriptors most students have never been shown.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is limited, so a Serena family weighing it is usually also weighing a change of school and commute. For Ministry of Education equivalency the British-track rules are published in specific terms while no IB points threshold has been read on moe.gov.ae, so verify any equivalency question with the Ministry rather than inferring it from a comparison.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-serena.subjectsIntro: Within the Diploma, these are the subjects Serena households ask about, with the level-specific detail a tutor should be able to state without checking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus. At Higher Level there is a third paper, sixty minutes and 20 per cent of the grade, built on sustained reasoning. A tutor who describes Paper 3 as simply harder questions has not taught it through a cycle.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling, with a graphing calculator permitted throughout. The examinable habit is showing the input and interpreting the output, which is a different teaching job from the hand-fluency work Analysis and Approaches requires.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around structure and reactivity, with a scientific investigation worth 20 per cent marked on four criteria of six marks each. Ask any tutor what Criterion 'research design' requires before they explain any content.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes studied at both levels, with Higher Level extensions concentrated in fields and nuclear physics, and a data-analysis component inside Paper 1 that almost nobody practises deliberately.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense with command terms setting the ceiling on each answer. The marks lost are rarely about knowledge: 'outline', 'explain' and 'discuss' carry different expectations, and answering one as another costs the mark before the biology is read.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest available gain, and the three Internal Assessment commentaries each sit on a different unit with a strict word limit. A tutor should know how many commentaries there are without being told.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based and stimulus-driven, with a pre-released case study for one paper that rewards structured reading months in advance. Marks are lost by applying a tool correctly in the abstract without reference to the case.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two of the three assessed components are oral or non-literary. The Individual Oral needs a global issue narrow enough to sustain ten minutes and two extracts chosen well ahead; a vague global issue is the commonest cause of a low mark.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Distinct from the KHDA-mandated school provision but running alongside it, with text handling, writing and two oral components. Register rather than vocabulary is where non-Arab students lose marks. Availability at Diploma level is the tightest in our whole subject list.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentary plus a prescribed-title essay of 1,600 words. A subject tutor without TOK experience cannot help here: the assessment is about knowledge claims and justification, not about any subject's content.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research with a school supervisor. Legitimate support is process coaching: narrowing an answerable question, building a source base, managing reflection sessions. We do not draft, rewrite or edit an Extended Essay to completion.

subjects.name: CAS
subjects.description: Creativity, activity and service, completed and documented rather than graded, but a Diploma requirement. No tutoring is needed or appropriate; what families occasionally need is help understanding the documentation expectations, which the school sets.

sections.heading: What to ask before you hire anyone
paragraphs: A local search returns businesses by proximity and prominence, which tells you nothing about programme knowledge. The substitute for that signal is a short set of questions, and they work equally well on a neighbour's recommendation, an agency and us.

Start with the programme and the level. Which programme is my child on, and what does that change? For the Diploma: which level, and what components does that level sit that the other does not? A tutor who teaches the subject answers immediately — Higher Level in Mathematics has a third paper; Higher Level sciences have additional content inside the same themes; Higher Level English has a separate essay component. A tutor who has only taught 'the IB' will generalise.

Then ask about the guide. Which subject guide are you working from, and when did it change? Several Diploma subjects have been through revised syllabuses with different assessment structures, and a tutor working from a superseded guide will teach a paper pattern that no longer exists. This question is uncomfortable to ask and it is the single most useful one on the list.

Then ask about the Internal Assessment criteria by name, and what each is worth. Then ask what they will not do with that Internal Assessment. A tutor who hesitates on that last one is a risk to your child's Diploma rather than to your budget. The table below sets out the questions with what a strong answer and a weak answer sound like.

sections.heading: The Diploma's moving parts, and who assesses what
paragraphs: A Diploma student is being assessed by several different mechanisms at once, and families rarely see them laid out. Knowing which is which changes who you should be asking for help and when.

External examinations are marked by the IB and sat in the May session for UAE schools. Internal Assessments are produced by the student, marked by the school and moderated externally, and typically carry 20 to 25 per cent of a subject grade. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are externally assessed and contribute to the award alongside the six subjects. CAS is completed and documented rather than graded, but it is a requirement.

That structure has two practical consequences. The first is that the school holds more of the grade than parents assume: internal deadlines, supervision and moderation all sit with the school, which is why the school's calendar is the real planning anchor and the IB coordinator is the right person to ask about dates. The second is that the ceiling on a large share of each grade is set early, when a research question or topic is chosen, rather than in the revision period.

The column worth reading twice in the table below is the last one. Legitimate help differs by component. On an examined paper, a tutor can teach anything and mark anything. On an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay, a tutor may explain, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and may not produce any part of it. That distinction is the difference between tutoring and misconduct, and it is not a matter of degree.

sections.heading: Why 'twenty years of experience' is the wrong credential
paragraphs: Experience is usually the headline claim in this market, and on its own it is close to uninformative for the IB. The reason is that the thing being examined changes. Subject guides are revised, assessment structures alter, and a long career teaching the previous version of a course can actively mislead a student.

The pattern we see is specific. A tutor teaches a science or a mathematics course for years, the guide is revised with a different paper structure and a different internal assessment, and the tutor continues teaching the shape they know. The content overlaps enough that nobody notices for a term. What surfaces later is a student who has practised the wrong paper format, or who has built an internal assessment against superseded criteria.

The useful credential is therefore current and specific: which guide, which level, which components, and when did you last teach a cohort through to the May session. Those are checkable in a two-minute conversation, and a tutor who teaches the course now will answer them without effort. Nobody should be offended by the question; the ones who are have answered it.

A related caution about a claim that circulates widely in this market: examiner status. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners for anyone whose current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner status in any case gives no access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. If a provider uses it to imply otherwise, that is a reason for scepticism rather than a reason to pay more.

sections.heading: The core: where general subject tutors cannot help
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are the parts of the Diploma most likely to be mishandled by a competent subject tutor, because they are not subject work. A brilliant chemistry teacher has no particular advantage in either.

Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentary and an essay of 1,600 words on a prescribed title. What it rewards is a knowledge claim examined properly: objects that evidence a point about how knowledge is produced or justified, rather than objects that merely illustrate a theme. The commonest low-scoring exhibition is one where the objects are interesting and do not do any work. That is diagnosable in a single session at the choosing stage and almost unfixable afterwards.

The Extended Essay is four thousand words of independent research with a school supervisor, and its outcome is largely determined by the question. A question too broad cannot be answered in the word count; a question with no accessible sources cannot be researched from Dubai; a question that is really a topic produces a descriptive essay that cannot reach the upper bands. Two sessions spent narrowing it are worth more than six spent polishing prose later.

CAS needs no tutoring at all, and anyone offering it is selling something unnecessary. What families sometimes need is help understanding the documentation the school expects, which the school itself is the authority on. The honest summary for the core is that help is cheap, specific and time-sensitive: it belongs at the decision points, not at the deadlines.
bullets: TOK rewards objects that evidence a knowledge claim, not ones that illustrate a theme
The Extended Essay is decided by the question more than by the writing

sections.heading: Academic honesty, stated as a boundary rather than a slogan
paragraphs: This is the point on which a tutoring arrangement is either safe or dangerous, and it deserves plain words because at least one operator ranking for searches like this one sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

What a tutor may do: teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion requires, question a research question until it is answerable, work through a comparable example on a different topic, read a draft the student wrote and say where the reasoning fails, and mark practice work against the published criteria. All of that is teaching, and all of it leaves the assessed work in the student's hands.

What a tutor may not do: choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, produce or process the data, edit prose to a finished state, or supply another student's work as a model. Each of those is the student presenting another person's work as their own, which is academic misconduct under IB rules and a malpractice matter for the school. The supervisor signs declarations about authenticity; the exposure falls on the student, and it falls on the whole Diploma rather than on one grade.

A related rule that is less discussed: IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables should be referenced and linked rather than reproduced or supplied. A provider handing you a bundle of them is redistributing material it does not own, and in the case of unreleased material that is a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. Ask any prospective tutor where their line sits before you book. A vague answer is itself the answer.

sections.heading: Where our coverage is genuinely thin
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is odd, because every tutoring service has one. Stating ours is more useful to a Serena family than a claim to cover everything.

The tightest categories are first-language Arabic at Diploma level, Theory of Knowledge supervision, Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in particular windows, and some of the less commonly taken subjects where UAE demand is low. For those, a request may come back with a wait rather than a slot, and that is true of any provider rather than a peculiarity of ours.

What happens next is the part that matters. The honest options are to offer the windows that genuinely exist even if they are not your preferred ones, to give a realistic estimate of when the preferred window may open, or to say we cannot cover it and that you should look elsewhere. All three get used. What does not happen is a general tutor placed into a specialist request, which would solve our scheduling problem by handing you the real one.

Practical advice independent of who you use: for niche Higher Level subjects, for core components and for coursework supervision, ask three to four weeks before you need to start. The fortnight before an Internal Assessment deadline is when every family in Dubai asks the same question, and good supervision cannot be conjured at that notice by anybody. The corollary is worth saying too: for mainstream subjects at either level, availability is rarely the constraint, and a family asking in term time will usually be matched within a few days.

sections.heading: What the local pool looks like, and what it costs
paragraphs: The geography argument is worth finishing honestly. Serena is among the furthest-out communities in the Dubailand belt, and IB students are a minority of Dubai's private-school population — International Baccalaureate programmes account for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent on UK curricula, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. A small share of a large market, distributed across the city, is not concentrated around Al Qudra Road.

That has a price consequence as well as a quality one. An in-home arrangement here prices a tutor's eighty to a hundred and twenty minute round trip into the hour, which is why market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 including travel — Bestimate's 2026 rate table shows AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500 — against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor online and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors publishing IB from AED 200.

So a family insisting on proximity is paying more to choose from fewer candidates, and the candidates are selected by willingness to drive rather than by programme knowledge. For a mainstream request that may still produce somebody good. For Higher Level Chemistry with an Internal Assessment due, or for TOK exhibition coaching, it frequently will not.

Removing travel reverses both effects: the premium disappears and the pool is selected on programme, subject and level. sections.heading: What the first session should look like
paragraphs: A good first session with an IB student is recognisable, and it looks nothing like a consultation. It starts with the student's own marked work on the screen: two recent papers, an Internal Assessment draft, or the last report with its criterion or component breakdown.

From that, the tutor should be able to say three things by the end of the hour. Which component the marks are leaking from. Whether the losses are content, reasoning or command-term misreading. And roughly how many sessions the job needs, including the possibility that the answer is few. A session that produces none of those has produced nothing except a payment.

What should not happen is a generic diagnostic test, a syllabus walkthrough, or a conversation about which topics the student finds hard. Students are poor witnesses to their own errors, not through carelessness but because the errors are invisible from the inside: a command-term failure looks like a correct answer to the person who wrote it. The marked paper is the only honest witness in the room.

With us, that session is free, there is no card required, and it is taught by the tutor who would continue rather than by a coordinator. If the pace or the style does not suit your child, say so and we match again. That is the whole purpose of making the first lesson real: you are judging teaching rather than a pitch, which is the only test a local search cannot run for you.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor actually based near Serena?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it is a weak thing to optimise for. IB students are around 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, so programme specialists are thinly spread across the city rather than concentrated near Al Qudra Road, and most Serena IB families already travel out of the belt for school. IB Gram teaches online one-to-one, which removes distance from the equation: we have no UAE office or centre, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Independent in-home tutors here charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IB tutor first?
faqs.answer: Which programme and level your child is on and what that changes. A tutor who teaches the course will name the components that exist at Higher Level and not at Standard Level without prompting. Then ask which subject guide they work from and when it last changed, because several Diploma subjects have been revised and a tutor on an old guide will teach a paper structure that no longer exists. Then ask the Internal Assessment criteria by name, and what they will not do with that assessment.

faqs.question: Why is 'twenty years of IB experience' not enough?
faqs.answer: Because what is examined changes. Subject guides are revised, with different assessment structures and internal assessment criteria, and a long career teaching the previous version can mislead a student in a way that is invisible for a term. The content overlaps enough that nobody notices immediately; what surfaces later is practice on the wrong paper format or coursework built against superseded criteria. The better credential is current and specific: which guide, which level, which components, and when they last took a cohort to the May session.

faqs.question: Can a subject tutor help with Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and it is worth being blunt about it. TOK is assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentary and a 1,600-word prescribed-title essay, and what it rewards is a knowledge claim properly examined — objects that evidence how knowledge is produced or justified, rather than objects that illustrate a theme. An excellent chemistry or history teacher has no particular advantage there. The useful help is two sessions at the object-choosing stage, which is diagnosable then and close to unfixable afterwards.

faqs.question: Which IB components carry the most of the grade?
faqs.answer: External examinations carry most of each subject grade and are marked by the IB in the May session for UAE schools. Internal Assessments are produced by the student, marked by the school and externally moderated, and typically carry 20 to 25 per cent per subject. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are externally assessed and contribute to the award alongside the six subjects, while CAS is completed and documented rather than graded. The practical point is that a large share of each grade has its ceiling set when a topic is chosen.

faqs.question: How much can a tutor legitimately help with an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion requires, question a research question until it is answerable, work through a comparable example on a different topic, and give honest feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite text, produce or process the data, edit prose to a finished state, or supply another student's work as a model. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own, which risks the whole Diploma rather than one subject grade.

faqs.question: When is the right moment to get help with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: At the question-narrowing stage, months before the deadline. The outcome is largely determined by the question: too broad and it cannot be answered in four thousand words, too obscure and the sources are not accessible from Dubai, too much like a topic and the essay stays descriptive and cannot reach the upper bands. Two sessions spent there are worth more than six spent polishing prose later. Support is process coaching only — we do not draft, rewrite or edit an Extended Essay to completion, and the school supervisor remains in charge.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find tutors for in Dubai?
faqs.answer: First-language Arabic at Diploma level and Theory of Knowledge supervision are the tightest, followed by Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in particular windows and the less commonly taken subjects where UAE demand is low. That is true across providers rather than peculiar to us. If you need one of them, ask three to four weeks ahead rather than in the fortnight before a deadline, when every family in Dubai is asking the same question and no provider can conjure good supervision at that notice.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost around Serena?
faqs.answer: An IB specialist teaching online is quoted at AED 200 to 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table showing AED 200 to 450+. A qualified subject tutor is AED 150 to 300. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, and Serena sits at the upper end because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. Those are published market figures; our own rate is quoted after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: What should happen in a first session with an IB student?
faqs.answer: The student's own marked work should be on the screen: two recent papers, a draft, or the last report with its component breakdown. By the end of the hour the tutor should be able to name which component the marks are leaking from, whether the losses are content, reasoning or command-term misreading, and roughly how many sessions the job needs. What should not happen is a generic diagnostic test or a conversation about which topics feel hard, because students cannot see their own command-term errors from the inside.

faqs.question: Do I need separate tutors for Higher and Standard Level subjects?
faqs.answer: You need a tutor matched to each level, which sometimes means the same person and often does not. Higher and Standard Level are different courses rather than the same course at different speeds: in Mathematics, Higher Level sits an additional paper worth 20 per cent built on sustained reasoning; in the sciences, Higher Level carries additional content inside the same themes. A tutor comfortable at Standard Level is not automatically comfortable with the Higher Level extensions, and the honest ones say so when asked.

faqs.question: Are tutors teaching Serena students allowed to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring here requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified.

faqs.question: Can you tell me the May exam dates for my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and we would be wary of any page that does. ibo.org blocks automated fetching, which means no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an unverified date is worse than none when a family books travel around it. What we can say is that UAE schools sit the May session and that in Dubai schools the internal coursework deadlines fall weeks earlier than the IB's. Ask your child's IB coordinator for both and plan from the earlier one.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai regulator approve IB tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying it does is making a claim worth challenging. KHDA is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, which is a statement about KHDA rather than an endorsement of any tutoring service. The permit that applies to individual private tutors is issued by MoHRE, not KHDA. A KHDA Educational Services Permit exists for training institutes with premises in Dubai; IB Gram holds none, claims none, and has no UAE office or centre.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-serena.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB tutor near me in Serena, the shortlist matters less than the questions. What will you not do with that assessment. And what does the core require. Send us your child's programme, subject, level and two marked papers, and you will get straight answers plus a free first lesson with the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online.

intro.heading: Proximity is a price. Here is what it costs and what it buys
paragraphs: A near-me search is a filter, and it is worth understanding what you are filtering for. It does not return the tutors who know your child's subject best. It returns the ones who have told Google they operate in your area, and in a city where tuition is overwhelmingly delivered by individuals travelling between villas, that is a filter on willingness to drive. The result is priced accordingly, and the premium is measurable rather than theoretical.

In Dubai, in-home one-to-one tuition runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the figure including travel. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at about AED 150 to 300, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly packages tell the same story: around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits against around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, each attributed in the tables on this page. They are market context rather than IB Gram's price list; our pricing follows a free trial lesson.

Strip the arithmetic down and the proximity premium is somewhere between AED 30 and 150 an hour. Across a weekly session for a Diploma year that is a meaningful sum, and it buys three things: a car journey, a person in the room, and not having to set up a video call. For a seven-year-old the person in the room may matter. For a sixteen-year-old working on Higher Level paper technique it rarely changes anything, and the narrowing of the tutor pool that comes with it frequently does.

The more interesting question for a Sobha Hartland family is not the hourly rate at all. It is the total: what supporting a child through a two-year Diploma actually costs, where in those two years the money does the most work, and which spending patterns produce nothing. Most families never see that figure because they buy a month at a time and discover the total afterwards. This page puts it on the table, with a line-by-line budget, a priority order for a fixed amount, and the six patterns that waste money regardless of the rate paid.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma tuition to Sobha Hartland over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the subject and level rather than to the postcode. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is also why no travel premium appears in what you pay us, and why the pool you choose from is the whole market rather than the drivable part of it. Nothing on this page promises a grade; it gives you the figures and the order to spend them in, which is the part no competitor publishes.

subjects.name: Extended Essay

sections.heading: What proximity costs in this market, priced out
paragraphs: A near-me search deserves a near-me price list, so here it is. The table sets out the Dubai market by how tuition is delivered, with the provider that published each band named and the month we read it. Read the right-hand column rather than the left: the interesting information is not the rate but the size of the pool each rate draws from, because that is what the money is really buying or forfeiting.

Three observations. First, the proximity premium is real but modest in absolute terms, between roughly AED 30 and 150 an hour depending on which bands you compare. Over a weekly session across a Diploma year it adds up to a meaningful figure, but it is not the difference between affordable and unaffordable. Second, the premium is not a quality premium. There is no mechanism by which a drive to Sobha Hartland improves anyone's grasp of Higher Level Physics, and the market does not price for skill in this segment because it cannot observe it.

Third, and most consequentially, the pool column moves in the wrong direction as the price rises. The most expensive delivery model draws on the smallest geographically available group, which means a family paying the in-home premium may be paying more for a tutor whose actual specialism is something adjacent to what their child needs. That is the trade that the near-me filter makes on your behalf without telling you, and it is the whole reason this page exists.

sections.heading: What two Diploma years actually cost to support, line by line
paragraphs: Families buy tutoring a month at a time and discover the total afterwards. Seeing it in advance changes decisions, so the table below sets out a realistic two-year support plan with the market rates from this page applied. It is not a quotation and it is not our price list. It is an arithmetic exercise using published market bands, so you can see which lines are large and which are small.

What the exercise shows is that the lines most parents worry about are small and the lines they do not think about are large. A single internal assessment block is a few sessions. A one-session Extended Essay question review is almost nothing. The large line is open-ended weekly tuition in a subject nobody diagnosed, carried across both years because stopping felt risky. That one line can exceed everything else on the table combined, and it is the line that produces the least.

The second thing it shows is where the leverage sits. Money spent early in DP1 on a foundation gap is cheap and prevents expensive work later. Money spent on an internal assessment question before the work begins is cheap and prevents a term of wasted effort. Money spent in the eight weeks before the session is expensive per month and often necessary, because by then the problem is real and the clock is short. A family that spends in the first two windows generally spends less in the third.

sections.heading: Six ways Diploma tutoring money gets wasted
paragraphs: Having priced the market and the programme, the useful part is naming the failures. These six patterns account for most of the money wasted on IB tutoring in Dubai, and none of them is solved by negotiating a lower rate. They are solved by a diagnosis, an end date and a willingness to have one uncomfortable conversation.

The first and largest is buying duration before diagnosis. A parent reacts to a bad grade by booking weekly sessions indefinitely, and nobody ever establishes what is losing marks. The second is paying a specialist rate for homework supervision, which is a real service worth real money but not specialist money. The third is the reverse: economising in DP2 on the paper technique and internal assessment feedback that actually decide the grade.

The fourth is booking three subjects when one weakness underlies all three, usually algebra under maths and two sciences, or writing structure under two essay subjects. The fifth is the block that renews because stopping feels like a risk, long after its purpose was met. The sixth is paying the proximity premium for a subject where it changes nothing, which at Diploma level is nearly every subject. Each of these is visible in a month if someone is looking, and invisible for two years if nobody is.

What makes them persist is that none of them feels like waste while it is happening. A weekly session that the student attends and the tutor delivers politely looks like progress even when no grade is moving, because attendance is easy to observe and diagnosis is not. The remedy is mechanical rather than clever: write down at the start what the block is for, and check at six weeks whether that specific thing has changed. If it has not, change the plan rather than extending it.

sections.heading: Online against nearby, compared on cost and on consequence
paragraphs: The comparison matters because a near-me search has already made half the decision for you. Set the two models side by side on cost, on who teaches, on how much of the hour is teaching, and on what happens when something changes, and the picture is clearer than either side's marketing suggests.

Cost favours online by the travel premium, which is the easy part. Matching favours online decisively, because the pool is the whole market rather than the drivable subset, and at Diploma level the subject and the level are what determine whether the hour is useful. Paid-hour efficiency favours online, because nothing in the arrangement absorbs a commute and the session can begin as soon as the student is home rather than when the tutor arrives.

Flexibility favours online by a wide margin, and in Dubai that converts into money. Ramadan timings, travel, examination weeks, a school trip: each of these costs a cancelled in-home session and costs nothing online. What in-home genuinely offers is presence, which matters for younger students and for the specific case of a teenager who will not work unless someone is physically there. That is a real category and we will not argue it away. To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the comparison here is between our online delivery and a local arrangement you would make yourself.

One cost that rarely appears in either side's marketing is the cancellation. An in-home session cancelled at short notice usually still costs the family something, because the tutor has committed the slot and often the journey. An online session that has to move costs nobody a journey and is far easier to reschedule inside the same week. Across a Diploma year with mocks, school trips, travel and illness in it, that difference alone can account for several sessions' worth of money.

sections.heading: Six subjects, one budget: how to decide what gets funded
paragraphs: A Diploma student has six subjects and three core components, and almost no family can fund weekly support in more than one or two. So the allocation question is the real question, and it has a defensible answer rather than being a matter of taste. The priority order below is the one we would apply to our own children, and it is driven by what is irreversible rather than by what is worst.

First in the order is anything with a deadline that cannot be revisited. An internal assessment question chosen badly cannot be fixed in March. An Extended Essay built on an unanswerable question wastes a term regardless of how much is spent later. These interventions are small, cheap and time-sensitive, which makes them the clearest value on the whole list.

Second is the subject where a Higher Level choice outruns the student's foundation, because that gap widens every month and is cheapest to close in DP1. Third is the transferable weakness under several subjects, usually algebra or writing structure, because one block serves multiple grades. Fourth is paper technique in DP2, where losses are procedural and fast to correct. Last, and often first in a worried parent's mind, is the subject with the lowest grade, which may well be a symptom of something higher on this list rather than a problem in itself.

There is one thing the order deliberately leaves out, which is the subject the student most dislikes. Dislike is information about motivation rather than about marks, and funding it first tends to produce a student who resents the extra hour in the subject they already resented. The better sequence is to fund something higher on the list, let a grade move there, and use that as the argument for tackling the disliked subject later with a student who now believes the process works.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session: when to spend
paragraphs: Budget forwards from today and a household overspends. Read the two years backwards from the May examination session, which is the session UAE IB schools sit, and the spending plan more or less writes itself. The counterintuitive part, and the part that catches Sobha Hartland families who arrived partway through the programme, is where the binding deadlines actually come from. They are set mostly by the school rather than by the IB. A family assuming the reverse budgets for a distant external examination, then meets an internal assessment deadline months ahead of anything the IB itself publishes, with the money already committed somewhere less urgent.

Two cautions. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, which govern internal assessments, Extended Essay drafts and Theory of Knowledge submissions. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring site, this one included. Treat an internal deadline as firm the moment it is announced, because schools do bring them forward.

Read for cost, the calendar gives a simple rule. Spend small and early on anything irreversible. Spend moderately and steadily on a diagnosed weakness through DP1. Spend heavily and briefly in the final window if the mock says you must, and stop afterwards. The pattern that fails is the inverse: nothing in DP1, panic in DP2, and a large open-ended commitment made in the month when there is least time for it to work.

There is also a collision worth asking about in advance. Internal assessment deadlines in different subjects tend to cluster, and they tend to cluster near the Extended Essay deadline, so the weeks when one subject most needs attention are the weeks the student has least to give. A coordinator can usually say where those collisions fall for a particular cohort. Knowing it in DP1 lets you move a block earlier rather than bidding for evenings that are already committed, and that is a scheduling saving rather than an academic one.

sections.heading: KHDA, the fee freeze, and how to judge whether you are getting value
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school. For a Hartland parent the departmental commentary inside a report is more useful than the headline band, and it is also a free second opinion on whether a weak grade is the student or the provision.

The cost context this year is unusual and worth using. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places. With the fee line flat, discretionary education spending is more visible than usual, which makes this a good year to judge tutoring on what it produces.

How to judge it, concretely. After six weeks, you should be able to see three things: a written statement of what was costing marks, marked practice showing whether that specific thing is improving, and a grade or mark trend in the subject. If all three are absent, the spend is not working regardless of how pleasant the sessions are. That test applies at AED 60 an hour and at AED 450 an hour, and it is the only value measure a parent can apply without understanding the subject.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any service advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something else or saying something untrue, and in a near-me search that phrase appears often enough to be a useful filter.

sections.heading: What is never for sale, at any rate
paragraphs: A cost-led page has to say where the market's cheapest-looking option is actually the most expensive. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For a family under deadline pressure that can look like a solution with a known cost. It is not. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the price is paid by the student, who can lose the Diploma, not by the website that took the payment.

What is legitimately for sale is substantial and worth paying for. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the language the examiner uses, question a research question until it is answerable, warn that a method will produce too little data, teach the underlying content, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. Those are the interventions that appear highest in this page's priority table, and they are cheap relative to their effect.

What is not for sale from us at any rate is choosing the question, supplying the method or the data, writing any part of the text, or editing a draft into its final form. Nor will we hand over a worked example close enough to the student's own task that copying becomes the obvious step. We state this to the student in the first session rather than in small print, and we also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference them and link to the official source, which costs nothing and is both lawful and more useful, because the official version is the current one.

sections.heading: Getting started from Sobha Hartland, with a budget in mind
paragraphs: Begin by naming a figure. Tell us what you are willing to spend a month and for how long, alongside the subject, the level, the latest grade and the teacher's last comment. A tutoring service that does not ask about the budget will recommend more sessions than you need, because recommending more is always the safer answer for them. Knowing the constraint lets us apply the priority order from earlier on this page rather than listing everything that could help.

We then propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Afterwards, ask for a written statement of what is costing marks and which category it falls into. If that statement is general, do not book the block at any rate. Specificity is the thing you are paying the premium for, and it is observable in one conversation.

And the honest part. Availability is finite, and some Diploma areas are thinner than others: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision, Higher Level mathematics Paper 3, and second languages beyond the common ones. When the right tutor is not free at your preferred time, we say so and offer a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus to Gulf Standard Time. We will not substitute a related subject or level and charge the same rate, and if none of the alternatives suits you have lost nothing, because the trial lesson is free and comes first.

process.title: Name the monthly figure first
process.description: Say what you are willing to spend and for how long, alongside the subject and level. The constraint is what lets us apply a priority order instead of listing everything that might help, and a service that does not ask is going to over-recommend by default.

process.title: Fund the irreversible things first
process.description: Internal assessment and Extended Essay question reviews are one or two sessions each and cannot be substituted for later at any price. We will suggest those before suggesting weekly tuition, even though weekly tuition is the larger sale.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then ask for it in writing
process.description: The first session costs nothing. Afterwards ask for a written statement of what is costing marks and which category it falls into. If the answer is general, do not book the block, whatever the hourly rate attached to it.

process.title: Agree sessions, purpose and an end date
process.description: Every block has a number of sessions, a stated purpose and a review date, so the monthly figure stays a decision rather than becoming a subscription nobody revisits. If the work finishes early we say so and the block ends.

process.title: Check the three value signals at six weeks
process.description: A written diagnosis, marked practice showing that specific thing improving, and a mark trend in the subject. If all three are missing after six weeks the spend is not working, and that test applies at every price point in this market.

process.title: Raise intensity late, briefly, then stop
process.description: If the DP2 mock says an intensive block is needed, we run it for an agreed number of weeks and end it after the session rather than carrying it forward. Short and bounded is what makes the highest monthly figure on this page defensible.

whyPoints.title: The proximity premium quantified
whyPoints.description: We price what a near-me search actually costs, roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour over the online equivalent, and say what it buys. No other page in this market tells you that the filter you just used is a price filter rather than a quality filter.

whyPoints.title: A two-year total, not a monthly teaser
whyPoints.description: The budget table sets out what supporting a full Diploma costs line by line at published market rates, so you see the total before you buy the first month rather than afterwards. Most families never see this figure until it has already been spent.

whyPoints.title: A defensible priority order
whyPoints.description: With six subjects and one budget, we fund the irreversible things first, then the widening gap, then the transferable weakness. That order is driven by what cannot be fixed later rather than by which grade looks worst on a report.

whyPoints.title: Six waste patterns named
whyPoints.description: Duration before diagnosis, specialist rates on homework supervision, economising in DP2, three subjects for one weakness, blocks that renew by default, and premiums paid where presence changes nothing. Naming them is what prevents them.

whyPoints.title: A value test you can apply yourself
whyPoints.description: A written diagnosis, marked practice on that specific thing, and a mark trend, all visible at six weeks. It needs no subject knowledge and it works at any price point, including on us.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA does and link to its own material. We do not describe IB Gram or any tutor as KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, because none of that is true and the phrase is common enough in near-me results to be a useful filter.

faqs.question: Does searching for a tutor near me in Sobha Hartland get me a better tutor?
faqs.answer: It gets you a nearer one, which is a different thing. A near-me search filters for providers who have told Google they operate in your area, and in a market delivered mostly by individuals travelling between homes that is a filter on willingness to drive rather than on subject expertise. The premium attached to it runs roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour. For a Diploma student working on paper technique, the wider tutor pool that online delivery opens up usually matters more than the journey being saved.

faqs.question: What is the real cost of supporting a child through the whole IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on one line. Internal assessment and Extended Essay question reviews are one or two sessions each and cost very little. A diagnosed foundation block in DP1 is six to ten sessions. A bounded pre-examination intensive is expensive per month and short. The line that dwarfs everything else is open-ended weekly tuition in a subject nobody diagnosed, carried across both years, which can exceed the rest of the plan combined while producing the least. Seeing the total in advance is what changes the decision.

faqs.question: Where do families in this part of Dubai waste the most on IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Six places, in rough order of cost. Buying duration before anyone has diagnosed the problem. Paying specialist rates for homework supervision. Economising in DP2 on the paper technique and internal assessment feedback that decide the grade. Booking three subjects when one weakness underlies all three. Letting a block renew because stopping feels like a risk. And paying the proximity premium in a subject where presence changes nothing, which at Diploma level is most of them. None of these is solved by a lower hourly rate.

faqs.question: If I can only fund tutoring in one subject, which should it be?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily the one with the lowest grade. Fund the irreversible thing first: an internal assessment or Extended Essay question that cannot be fixed later at any price, which is one or two sessions. Then fund the Higher Level subject chosen above the student's foundation, because that gap widens monthly. Then fund the transferable weakness, usually algebra or writing structure, because one block moves two or three grades. The lowest grade is often a symptom of something higher in that order rather than a problem in itself.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: Check three things at six weeks. A written statement from the tutor of what was costing marks. Marked practice showing whether that specific thing is improving. And a mark or grade trend in the subject. If all three are missing, the spend is not working however pleasant the sessions are, and that test applies equally at AED 60 an hour and AED 450 an hour. It also requires no subject knowledge from you, which is why it is the most useful measure a parent has.

faqs.question: Is a home visit in Sobha Hartland worth the extra money?
faqs.answer: For a younger child, or a teenager who genuinely will not work unless someone is physically present, it can be. For a Diploma student working on paper technique and internal assessment feedback, the premium buys travel and presence rather than teaching, and it narrows the pool to those willing to drive here at four in the afternoon. In-home rates in this market run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against about AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: No. We deliver one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We say so plainly because near me is the phrase parents search and it would be easy to leave the impression open. What we offer instead is a tutor matched to your child's subject and level from the whole available market, on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel premium in the price and no wasted journey when a session has to move.

faqs.question: Is a group class cheaper and is it ever the right answer for IB?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per head, and occasionally right. A group class works when several students share one named topic gap and the pace suits all of them, which happens with a specific piece of content more often than with general Diploma work. It works poorly for internal assessment feedback, for paper technique and for anything personal, because an individual habit will not be noticed in a room of six. The test is whether you can name the gap. If you cannot, a group class is a cheap way of not solving the problem.

faqs.question: Can we start tutoring late in DP2 and still get value?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a changed plan. With eight to twelve weeks of usable time the first session should mark the mock question by question, and the plan that follows should abandon some topics deliberately rather than attempting everything. Expect a high monthly figure for a short, bounded block rather than a modest figure spread thin. What you should not buy at that stage is an open-ended arrangement, because the window closes before an open-ended plan has time to work, and nobody can promise a grade in it.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects carry a scarcity premium in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision are thin everywhere, because almost nobody teaches them as a standalone subject, so they are worth booking earlier than you think necessary. Higher Level mathematics including Paper 3 is thinner than Standard Level. Second languages beyond the commonly taught ones are genuinely scarce. Mathematics at Standard Level, the main sciences, English A and Economics are comparatively well covered. We tell you which category your subject falls into before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's price tell me anything about their quality?
faqs.answer: Less than you would hope. The market does not observe teaching quality directly, so price largely tracks delivery model and claimed credentials rather than outcomes. What does correlate with quality is observable in a single lesson: whether they asked for your child's marked work, whether they can state the paper weightings from memory, whether they talk about method marks, and whether their account of the problem is specific. Run those checks and the price becomes a secondary question rather than the primary one.

faqs.question: Are school fees rising in Dubai this year, and how should that affect our tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest line in the education budget flat, discretionary spending such as tutoring is more visible than usual. Practically, that makes this a good year to judge tutoring on what it produces rather than absorbing it into a general increase, and to check the three value signals at six weeks.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence, and does that affect what they charge?
faqs.answer: They need a permit and it costs them nothing, so it should not appear in a quote. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can we pause or move sessions to save money during holidays and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is what makes pausing cheap rather than disruptive. During Ramadan sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, with no journey to renegotiate at either end, and a holiday pause costs nothing but a held slot. The exception worth noting is the eight weeks before the examination session, where pausing costs more than it saves. Agree any pause in advance so the slot is kept, and if you are leaving the Gulf, agree which time zone the session is pinned to.

faqs.question: Why would a cheaper tutor ever be the right choice?
faqs.answer: Because some problems do not need a specialist. A student who has missed two weeks to illness and needs one topic re-taught is well served by a competent budget tutor, and paying AED 400 an hour for that is a waste. The rungs that justify specialist rates are paper technique, internal assessment feedback and mark-scheme judgement in an examination year. Matching the rung to the problem rather than to the budget, or to anxiety, is the single most effective cost control available to a Diploma family.

faqs.question: What should I send you to get a recommendation that fits our budget?
faqs.answer: Five things. The monthly figure you are comfortable with and for how long. The subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. The latest grade, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than paraphrased. And the time the school day ends, which from Sobha Hartland is often earlier than elsewhere because two schools sit inside the community. A photograph of one marked paper beats all five, and with it we can usually propose a tutor the same day.

We will apply the priority order on this page, propose a tutor, and run the first session at no cost. Then check the three value signals at six weeks, on us as on anyone.

intro.heading: Half past two to half past seven: the only window a TECOM household has
paragraphs: A proximity search assumes the problem is distance. In Barsha Heights it almost never is. The towers sit between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, with Al Barsha 1 on one side and Dubai Internet City on the other, so most of the schools TECOM children attend are a ten-minute drive away in light traffic. The real constraint is the clock. A Dubai school day ends somewhere between 14:00 and 15:15 depending on the year group, the bus takes a loop through Al Barsha and Hessa Street before it reaches the towers, and by the time a child has eaten something it is gone four.

That leaves roughly three usable hours, and they are not interchangeable. The hour straight after the bus is the one a tired fifteen-year-old spends badly. The hour after dinner is the one a working parent can actually be in the flat for. Somewhere between those two sits the slot where a Higher Level Chemistry problem set gets done properly rather than survived. Picking the right one matters more to the outcome than whether the tutor lives two streets away or two time zones away.

The second constraint is housing stock. Barsha Heights is almost entirely apartments. There is no spare study with a door that shuts, so a lesson happens at the dining table with a younger sibling nearby and a lift lobby audible through the wall. That is a practical argument for a headset and a shared screen rather than a visitor in the living room, and it is the argument we make here. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is delivered over live video, one to one.

The third is subject coverage. A TECOM child at Dubai International Academy Al Barsha might be taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics HL and Economics SL. The pool of people within a twenty-minute drive who have taught all three to Diploma standard is small, and the pool who have taught the specific one your child is losing marks in is smaller still. Online delivery replaces that pool with a national one, which is the only honest reason to prefer it.

So this page answers the search literally. It sets out which schools the TECOM towers feed and when each day ends, maps the afternoon hour by hour, costs a month of tutoring at the rates Dubai providers actually publish, and states plainly what happens in the weeks when nobody suitable is free. The aim is that you finish it knowing which evening to book, which exam series your child is actually entered for, and what to ask on the trial lesson.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.programmesIntro: A TECOM household usually meets the IB in one of three forms, depending on which Al Barsha school the bus goes to: a primary programme, the Middle Years Programme in the lower secondary years, or the Diploma in the final two. The tutoring question is different in each, so they are separated here rather than lumped into one offer.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations and no published grades, which is why parents of younger TECOM children often cannot tell whether a wobble is real. Assessment is through the exhibition in the final year and through teacher judgement against transdisciplinary themes. Tutoring at this stage is almost entirely about arithmetic fluency, reading stamina and writing at length, because those are the three things that decide how the Middle Years Programme goes.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai International Academy Al Barsha runs the full IB continuum from PYP upward, so a TECOM child can be in an IB classroom from primary. Note that KHDA mandates Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, so the primary timetable already carries subjects the PYP framework does not describe.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against criteria A to D in each subject on a 1-8 scale, with no papers to practise and no past papers to work through. Reports read as four letters per subject, and a parent cannot easily convert them into a worry. The common pattern is a child who is comfortable in MYP Mathematics and then meets the Diploma and discovers that criterion-based work rewarded different habits from the ones Paper 1 rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Nord Anglia International School Dubai in Al Barsha South and GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh both take TECOM pupils into lower secondary before an IGCSE or MYP split, so neighbours in the same tower can be on different tracks at the same age. That matters for tutoring: a Year 10 criterion C task and a Year 10 IGCSE past paper need different preparation.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, marked by the school against IB criteria and then externally moderated. Dubai students sit the May session. The Diploma is where tutoring demand concentrates, because the two-year calendar stacks coursework deadlines against mock examinations in the same weeks.
programmes.countryNote: For a TECOM family the Diploma complicates the afternoon rather than the week. Internal deadlines are set by the school, not the IB, so two children in the same tower at different Al Barsha schools will have their Chemistry internal assessment due a month apart. Any tutoring plan has to be built from your own school's published deadline sheet, not from a generic calendar.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects TECOM families most often ask about, with what each actually assesses and where the marks go missing. The level matters more than the subject name: an SL request and an HL request in the same subject are different pieces of work and need a different tutor.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. Marks go missing in Paper 1, the no-calculator paper, where a student who can set up a problem on a graphing calculator cannot differentiate by hand under time. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors at a depth SL never reaches.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed throughout, so the failure mode is different: students lose marks on interpretation and on choosing the right statistical test rather than on manipulation. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding modelling. Some engineering courses prefer Analysis and Approaches, which is worth checking before the choice is locked.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mechanics unit decides the grade for most students because everything later borrows from it. HL adds fields, induction and quantum physics. The multiple-choice paper punishes unit slips and the extended-response paper punishes answers that describe when the command term asked the student to explain.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms are where TECOM students most often stall. The course rewards students who can draw a mechanism with curly arrows in the right places and lose nothing on significant figures. HL extends into entropy, equilibrium calculations and more organic synthesis routes.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students who revise by rereading retain little; those who answer past questions against the command terms do better. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments separate the top grades, and they are practisable in a way content revision is not.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation are the two things examiners reward and most students under-practise. The internally assessed commentaries ask for real published articles analysed against syllabus theory, and a weak article choice caps the mark before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Popular in TECOM households where parents work in the free zone and the subject feels familiar. The examination rewards applied answers tied to the case study rather than definitions. HL adds extension topics and a longer research project that needs a real organisation and real constraints.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are the components students handle worst, because both ask for a line of argument rather than coverage. Progress comes from timed writing with feedback, not from reading more secondary criticism.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points to the Diploma total. Students lose marks by writing opinion pieces rather than examining knowledge claims against the prescribed title.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece in a chosen subject, supervised by a school teacher. A tutor may teach research method, discuss structure and give feedback on the student's own draft; a tutor may not write any part of it. The research question, narrow and answerable, decides most of the mark.

sections.heading: A TECOM afternoon, hour by hour, and where the lesson actually goes
paragraphs: Start with the clock rather than the tutor. Dubai private schools finish between 14:00 and 15:15 depending on year group and campus. A bus leaving an Al Barsha campus at 14:40 does not arrive in Barsha Heights at 14:50, because it loops through Al Barsha 1 and Hessa Street first and the junctions around First Al Khail Street are at their worst in exactly that half hour. For most TECOM households the child is through the door between 15:15 and 16:00.

What follows is the part that decides whether tutoring works. Between 16:00 and 17:00 a Diploma student is capable of consolidation work: going over a marked paper, finishing a problem set, being walked through a mechanism they half understand. They are usually not capable of learning a new topic cold. Between 17:00 and 18:30 the household is at its busiest, with activities, siblings and the end of a working day arriving at once, and a booked lesson in that window is the one most often cancelled.

After 19:00 the flat settles. A parent is home, the younger child is occupied, and an hour runs to the end without interruption. This is why the table below exists: it is the schedule we actually plan against for TECOM, and it is worth more to a family than another paragraph about teaching philosophy. If your bus arrives earlier than most, say so on the trial call and the slot moves. The one thing worth checking before you pick a time is how long your own child takes to be genuinely ready to work after walking in, because that number differs by half an hour between siblings in the same flat.

sections.heading: The schools the TECOM towers feed, and what each one ends with
paragraphs: A parent searching for a tutor near TECOM is usually really asking whether anyone understands their child's school. That is a fair question, because the campuses within a short drive of Barsha Heights do not all do the same thing at sixteen. One runs the IB continuum from primary. One is American and ends in Advanced Placement. Several are British and run IGCSE before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. A tutor who knows the IB inside out is the wrong hire for a child sitting Cambridge papers in November.

The practical consequence is that the first question on a trial call should be the campus and the examination, not the year group. Two TECOM thirteen-year-olds can be in MYP criterion-marked lessons and in Key Stage 3 lessons preparing for IGCSE, and both will be described at home as being in Year 9. The work, the marking language and the thing a tutor should be rehearsing are different in each case, and getting that wrong costs a term before anybody notices it has been wasted.

The table below maps the destinations a TECOM bus actually serves to what a child there will be assessed on. Ratings are deliberately absent. KHDA publishes an inspection band for every Dubai private school on a six-point scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the only trustworthy place to read a school's current band is KHDA's own site, not a tutoring page that may be a year out of date.

sections.heading: Six groups, three Higher Levels, and the one the school run breaks
paragraphs: The Diploma asks for six subjects across six groups, three of them at Higher Level, plus the three core elements. On paper that is a workload problem. In a TECOM flat it is a scheduling problem, because the three Higher Levels are not equally damaged by a bad week. A Higher Level language course survives a missed evening; Higher Level Mathematics does not, because each topic stands on the previous one and a fortnight of thin practice shows up two months later in Paper 1.

This is where the afternoon timetable and the subject choice collide. If your child's hardest Higher Level is Mathematics or Physics, the weekly tutoring hour belongs in the 19:00 slot where concentration is available, not in the 16:00 slot where it is cheapest to arrange. Families who get this wrong usually conclude that tutoring does not work for their child, when what failed was the hour.

The second thing worth saying plainly: one tutor for three Higher Levels is a compromise, not a convenience. A person who has taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL to Diploma standard is unlikely to also have examined Chemistry HL mechanisms and marked an Economics commentary. Online delivery is what makes separating them affordable in time, because there is no second journey to pay for. If a provider offers one tutor for everything, ask which of the three they have actually taught at Higher Level in the last two years.
bullets: Higher Level Mathematics and Physics degrade fastest after a missed fortnight

sections.heading: Why the 16:00 lesson and the 19:30 lesson are not the same product
paragraphs: Treat the two slots as two different services, because they achieve different things. The 16:00 hour is best spent on work that already exists: a returned paper with marks lost, a problem set half finished, a mechanism the teacher went through too fast. The student is not being asked to build anything new, so the fatigue that follows a school day and a bus is survivable. Parents like it because the evening stays free.

The 19:30 hour is for the work that needs a clear head. New Higher Level content, a derivation, planning an internal assessment, writing a Theory of Knowledge paragraph against a prescribed title. These are tasks where fifteen minutes of poor attention wastes the whole hour, and they are the tasks that move a grade. A household where both parents commute back from Internet City or Media City can usually guarantee this slot in a way it cannot guarantee a 16:00 one.

There is a cost dimension to this too, and it runs the opposite way to what families expect. Early-evening slots are the ones every family in Dubai wants, so across the market they are the first to go and the last to be discounted. A 19:30 or weekend-morning slot is easier to hold with the same tutor for a whole term, and continuity with one tutor is worth more than the convenience of a slot that keeps moving between three people. If you can hold only one fixed hour a week for the whole year, hold the later one.
bullets: 16:00: consolidation, marked work, short drills
19:30: new teaching, derivations, coursework method
Weekend mornings: the only realistic two-hour block

sections.heading: The Diploma core, and the deadlines your school sets rather than the IB
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the internal assessments are where a TECOM term quietly goes wrong, because none of their deadlines come from the examination board. The school sets them. That means the Chemistry internal assessment at one Al Barsha campus can be due in the same week as the Extended Essay first draft at another, and a family comparing notes in the lift lobby will get contradictory advice about when to worry.

The only reliable planning document is your own school's published deadline sheet for the cohort. Ask the Diploma coordinator for it at the start of Year 12 and work backwards from each date in four stages: topic chosen, data or sources gathered, first full draft written, draft revised after supervisor feedback. Each of those stages is a place a tutor can teach something concrete. None of them is a place a tutor may contribute text.

That boundary is worth stating in full, because two providers in this market cross it. Under IB academic-honesty rules the internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach research method, explain the assessment criteria, discuss whether a research question is answerable and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write a section, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, or supply a dataset. We will not do any of those things, and a provider that offers to is putting your child's Diploma at risk rather than helping.
bullets: Internal deadlines come from the school, not from the IB
Ask the Diploma coordinator for the cohort deadline sheet in Year 12
