sections.heading: Ramadan, exam terms and the weeks the TECOM timetable moves
paragraphs: Three things reliably disturb a tutoring schedule in Dubai, and all three are predictable. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the household rhythm inverts: the usable study window moves to the late morning on non-school days and to after Iftar on school days. A tutoring slot booked for 19:30 in January is the wrong slot in Ramadan, and the sensible move is to agree the alternative in advance rather than cancel four weeks in a row.

The second is the mock season. Most Dubai schools run Diploma mocks in the winter and again before the May session, and in those weeks a student's own school timetable fills with papers. Adding a new topic in that fortnight is counterproductive. The right use of the hour is going through a mock paper that has been marked, which is also the only time a tutor can see, rather than infer, where the marks are going.

The third is travel. TECOM is a professional community and families leave Dubai in the summer and at mid-term. A pattern we see often is a six-week gap followed by a request to catch up in two sessions. That does not work, and it is worth saying so. The better plan is to hold a reduced schedule through the break, one hour a fortnight, which preserves the thread for far less money than the recovery block would cost. Agree that reduced pattern before the holiday starts, because a slot given up in June is rarely the same slot available in September.
bullets: Agree a Ramadan slot before Ramadan, not during it
Mock weeks are for marked papers, not new content
A reduced fortnightly hour through the summer beats a catch-up block
Travel between time zones is survivable online in a way a visit is not

sections.heading: What a month of IB tutoring costs around TECOM, counted monthly
paragraphs: Most providers quote by the hour, which is the least useful unit for a family deciding whether to commit. A household budgets by the month, so this section is organised that way. The figures below are market rates published by other providers in Dubai, each attributed, and reviewed in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's price list; our own model starts with a trial lesson before any payment and a consultation, and we would rather you compare the market honestly than take a number from us on trust.

Read the cheapest band first, because that is where most families start and where most of the disappointment sits. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts budget tutoring at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for one weekly hour, and EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour. At that price the tutor is often a university student. For arithmetic practice in the Middle Years Programme that can be perfectly adequate. For Higher Level Physics in the second Diploma year it usually is not, and the lost term costs more than the saving.

The middle band, AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a weekly hour on Bestimate's figures, is where a qualified subject teacher sits; Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. The specialist exam-year band runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 an hour. A tutor driving into the Barsha Heights towers is quoted across the market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and advertised in-home packages run AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. IB Gram does not sell those visits in the UAE at any price; the comparison is here so you can see what the travel premium buys, which is proximity rather than subject depth.

sections.heading: Starting from a TECOM tower, including the weeks we cannot help
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started is short. You tell us the campus, the year group, the subject and the level, and the window your afternoon actually allows. We propose a tutor who has taught that subject at that level and a slot inside your window. A trial lesson runs before any payment is taken. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial and it costs nothing; if it is right, the slot becomes a weekly booking you hold for the term.

What we will not do is claim permanent availability for everything. Some combinations are thin, particularly a single Higher Level science at short notice in the weeks either side of the mock season, and Theory of Knowledge supervision in the final term. When that happens you will be told the wait rather than handed whoever is free, because a mismatched specialist hour is the one purchase in this market that reliably wastes money. If the wait is unacceptable, we will say what else would help in the meantime.

One last practical note on the delivery question, since the search term that brought you here is a proximity search. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. It is a fair question to ask any tutor, near or far.

process.title: Say which campus and which paper
process.description: Not the year group. A TECOM Year 9 could be marked against MYP criteria or working towards IGCSE, and the two need different preparation. Naming the school and the examination gets you a tutor who has taught that specific thing rather than one who has taught the age.

process.title: Name the window, not the ideal
process.description: Tell us when your bus actually arrives and when a parent is home. If 16:00 is theoretical and 19:30 is real, book 19:30. Most tutoring that fails in Barsha Heights fails because the slot was chosen on a hopeful afternoon rather than a typical one.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as a diagnostic
process.description: Send a marked paper or a returned internal assessment draft beforehand and ask the tutor to work from it. An hour spent on real evidence tells you more about the match than an hour of introductions, and it happens before any payment is taken.

process.title: Fix the slot for a term
process.description: Agree a weekday and a time and keep it, including an agreed alternative for Ramadan and for mock weeks. Continuity with one tutor across a term outperforms a better-qualified stranger every fourth week, which is the pattern a floating slot produces.

process.title: Review against the school's deadline sheet
process.description: Every six weeks, check progress against your own school's internal deadlines rather than a general sense of improvement. If the next thing on the sheet is a Chemistry internal assessment draft, the next few sessions should be about method, and you should be able to see that in the plan.

whyPoints.title: The timetable comes first
whyPoints.description: We plan from the bus arrival and the commute home, not from a generic after-school slot. For a Barsha Heights household that usually means the lesson lands after 19:00, and saying so in advance prevents the three cancelled weeks that end most tutoring arrangements.

whyPoints.title: Subject and level, matched separately
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Mathematics are matched to different tutors, because almost nobody has genuinely taught both to Diploma standard. Online delivery is what makes that affordable: there is no second journey to pay for in time or money.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names who published it and when. Three of the six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. You should be able to verify a number before you act on it.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary, stated
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches method, explains criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft. We will not write, redraft or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. That boundary protects the Diploma your child is working towards.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: When no suitable specialist is free you are told the wait. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying so. A disclosed gap is more useful than a mismatched hour.

whyPoints.title: One claim at a time, no accreditation borrowed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, we are not partnered with any named school, and we have no office in the UAE. We explain what those bodies do and link to them.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in TECOM, or is everything online?
faqs.answer: Everything is online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for TECOM families run live over video, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is subject depth: instead of whoever can reach Barsha Heights by half past four, you get someone who has taught your child's exact subject at your child's exact level. The practical cost is that nobody sits in your living room. For a flat with no spare study and both parents commuting from Internet City, most families find the trade worth making.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson realistically start for a child living in the TECOM towers?
faqs.answer: Plan for 16:00 at the earliest and 19:00 or 19:30 for anything demanding. Dubai schools finish between 14:00 and 15:15, and the bus from the Al Barsha campuses loops through Al Barsha 1 and Hessa Street before it reaches Barsha Heights, so arrival is usually between 15:15 and 16:00. The hour straight after that is fine for reviewing a marked paper and poor for learning a new Higher Level topic. If your particular bus is early, tell us on the trial call and we will move the slot earlier.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in the TECOM towers usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most travel to Al Barsha, Al Barsha South or Al Sufouh. Common destinations include Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, GEMS Dubai American Academy, the American School of Dubai, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha, Dubai Heights Academy, GEMS Wellington International School and Dubai College. Those campuses do not all assess the same way at sixteen: one runs the IB continuum, one ends in Advanced Placement, several run IGCSE before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. That is why we ask for the campus name rather than the year group.

faqs.question: My child is in the MYP at an Al Barsha school. Is that different from IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Quite different. The Middle Years Programme marks against criteria A to D on a 1-8 scale with no papers to practise, so progress is about meeting a criterion descriptor. IGCSE is externally examined with past papers, mark schemes and syllabus codes to work through. A tutor who is strong at one is not automatically useful for the other. Since neighbours in the same TECOM tower can be on either track at the same age, the first thing to establish is which marking language your child's work is actually being judged in.

faqs.question: How much should a TECOM family expect to spend each month on IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Taking Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 bands for one weekly hour: roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for an exam-year specialist. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and TutorChase publishes AED 270. Those are other providers' published figures, reviewed in October 2026, not ours. IB Gram starts with a trial lesson before any payment rather than a published price list.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives near Barsha Heights teach any better than one who does not?
faqs.answer: Proximity tells you about travel time and nothing about teaching. What predicts a useful hour is whether the tutor has taught that subject at that level, can read a mark scheme, and can look at a returned paper and say which command term the student missed. None of those correlate with a postcode. Proximity does buy one real thing, which is a person in the room, and for a very young child that can matter. For a Diploma student working on Paper 1 technique it rarely outweighs having the right specialist.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover three Higher Level subjects for my Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Usually not well. Someone who has genuinely taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is unlikely to have also taught Chemistry HL mechanisms and marked Economics commentaries to the same standard. Online delivery makes splitting them practical, because there is no second journey to fund. If a provider offers one person for everything, ask which of the three they have taught at Higher Level in the past two years, and how recently. The answer is usually one of them.

faqs.question: What happens to our TECOM lesson slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It moves, and it is better to agree the alternative beforehand. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the household rhythm changes, so a 19:30 slot that works in January often does not. The two slots that hold up are late morning on non-school days and after Iftar on school days. Families who plan this in advance keep continuity through the month; families who do not usually cancel three or four weeks and then try to recover the ground afterwards, which costs more and works less well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IB internal assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach research method, explain the assessment criteria, discuss whether a research question is narrow enough to answer, and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor cannot write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, or supply data. Under IB academic-honesty rules that work must be the student's own, and breaching it is a malpractice risk that falls on your child, not on the tutor. One provider in this market sells completed internal assessments. We will not.

faqs.question: Who regulates the schools my child attends, and what does an inspection band mean?
faqs.answer: Dubai private schools come under KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspections place each school in a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. A band describes the school, not your child's teaching group, and it can change year to year, so read the current one on KHDA's own site rather than from a tutoring page. In Abu Dhabi the equivalent body is ADEK and in Sharjah it is the Sharjah Private Education Authority.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and those requirements had to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, because the curriculum expectation and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated in 40-minute lesson units. These subjects sit outside the Diploma points total but inside your child's week.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with caution.

faqs.question: My child has mocks in five weeks. Is it too late to start in the TECOM afternoon slot?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change. Five weeks is not enough to rebuild a Higher Level course and it is enough to fix paper technique, which is where a surprising share of marks sit. The sensible shape is a bounded block of six to eight sessions built from a marked past paper, aimed at one examination component, timed to your school's own mock dates. Avoid starting new content in the final fortnight. After the mock, the marked script is the single most useful document a tutor can work from.

faqs.question: What if nobody is available for the subject and level we need?
faqs.answer: You will be told the wait rather than handed whoever is free. Coverage is thinnest for a single Higher Level science at short notice in the weeks around mock season, and for Theory of Knowledge supervision in the final term. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why we state ours: a mismatched specialist hour is the purchase that most reliably wastes a Dubai family's money. If the wait does not work for you, we will say what would help in the meantime.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office in TECOM or anywhere else in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no premises in the UAE, no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no partnership with any named school or school group. Everything for UAE families is delivered online. We say this plainly because two providers ranking for these searches show a Dubai address on pages for other emirates, and one routes UAE parents to a phone number outside the country. You should know who you are dealing with before a trial lesson.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.closingHeading: Book the hour your week can actually keep
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.closingBody: If you have read this far you probably already know which slot in your week survives contact with a working Tuesday. Tell us the campus, the subject, the level and that slot, and we will propose a tutor who has taught exactly that and can meet you in it, live online and in Gulf Standard Time. The trial lesson happens before any payment, and it is best spent on a marked paper rather than introductions. If we cannot cover your combination this month, you will hear that instead of a substitute, and you can decide what to do with the information.

intro.heading: Why distance is the least useful thing to filter an IB tutor by
paragraphs: The Diploma is six subjects across six groups, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Each of those parts is assessed differently, and several of them have word limits, page limits and criterion letters that a tutor either knows or does not. A search ordered by distance cannot see any of that. It returns the adults nearest to your building, sorted by how near they are, which is a sensible way to find a plumber and a poor way to find somebody who can explain what the three bonus points on the Diploma are for.

The Greens makes the point sharply because of its scale. It is a mid-rise apartment community beside Emirates Golf Club with one school inside it, Regent International School, on the British curriculum. Most local Diploma students are therefore travelling out of the community to study, typically to Al Barsha or across Sheikh Zayed Road to Emirates Living, where the two nearest IB schools sit. The set of people living within fifteen minutes who have taught a specific Higher Level subject is small, and it gets smaller the more specific the subject becomes. For English A or Business Management it may be adequate. For Higher Level Physics, Chemistry, Economics or a Language B, it frequently is not.

IB Gram removes distance from the problem rather than working around it. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That means a Greens family is choosing from tutors matched by subject group, level and the specific internal assessment in front of their child, rather than from whoever is willing to cross Sheikh Zayed Road on a Tuesday evening. For an apartment household there is a secondary gain as well: no visitor parking, no building access, no lift, and a session that begins when a sixteen-year-old sits down rather than when a car finds a space.

The page that follows is built to be checkable. It lists the six subject groups and what each contributes to a score out of 45. It sets out the Higher Level workload in hours, so a family can see what three HL subjects actually costs a week. It publishes the word and page limits for the core components and the main internal assessments in one table, which is information no competitor page in this search carries at all. It explains, with its reasons, why there is no IB examination date anywhere on this page. And it says where IB tutoring money is most often wasted in a community like this one, which is a more useful thing to read than a list of benefits.
Read the limits table and the wasted-money table. Those two together will change how you brief whoever you end up hiring.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes exist and only one of them is what most Greens parents mean by 'IB'. Knowing which one your child is in, and which one they are heading towards, determines what a tutor should be doing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects drawn from six groups, three taken at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours each and three at Standard Level with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three further points from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay for a maximum of 45. Creativity, activity and service runs alongside and is a completion requirement rather than a graded component.
programmes.countryNote: The two nearest Diploma schools to The Greens sit across Sheikh Zayed Road and in Emirates Hills, so local DP students are commuting. That matters for scheduling, because a DP2 student returning at four in the afternoon with three Higher Level subjects has a tighter week than their timetable suggests, and sessions realistically start from six in the evening.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma in a continuum school, assessed against four criteria per subject group rather than by examination. Students arrive in DP1 strong on inquiry and investigation and weaker on timed written answers against command terms, which is a predictable gap rather than a surprise, and the cheapest time to close it is MYP 4 and 5.
programmes.countryNote: Greens families more often arrive at the Diploma from a British-curriculum IGCSE route than from MYP, because the school inside the community runs the British curriculum. That produces the opposite profile: solid examination technique and less experience of extended independent work, which shows up first in the Extended Essay and the internal assessments.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A less common IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Where a school offers it, students take DP subjects alongside the career-related component, so subject tutoring looks much like Diploma tutoring while the project work has its own requirements.
programmes.countryNote: Availability in Dubai is limited compared with the Diploma, so a family considering it should confirm directly with the school rather than assume it runs. For tutoring purposes the DP courses within it are taught identically; the reflective project needs the same process coaching as any independent assessed work.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The primary phase of the IB continuum, inquiry-led and reported against learning outcomes rather than criterion marks or grades. Relevant to a Greens family mainly as a decision point, because choosing a continuum primary school commits a child to criterion assessment from eleven and to the Diploma structure from sixteen unless they switch systems.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum 37%, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7% by enrolment. The IB share is small but growing: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: The Diploma is structured by group rather than by subject, and the group is what a tutor needs to know first because it sets the assessment pattern. The entries below cover the six groups and the two core components that carry word limits.

subjects.name: Studies in language and literature
subjects.description: Usually English A Language and Literature or Literature. Assessment combines written papers with an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied text. The oral is the component students most often under-prepare, because it is the only one where performance under questioning is assessed directly.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.levels: Group 2 · HL, SL and ab initio
subjects.description: A second language at Language B level or, for a beginner, ab initio at Standard Level only. Correct level placement matters more here than in any other group, because a student placed above their level loses marks they cannot recover through effort and one placed below them caps their own score.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Economics, Business Management, History, Geography, Psychology and others. Every subject in this group carries an internal assessment with its own word limit and criteria, and marks in the written papers hinge on command terms: evaluate, discuss and examine each demand a different answer shape.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Design Technology and others. The current courses share an assessment model: a multiple-choice and data-analysis paper, an extended written paper, and a scientific investigation worth twenty per cent with a 3,000-word maximum marked out of 24.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The calculus-heavy route, expected or preferred by many engineering, mathematics and physics degrees. At Higher Level it is among the most demanding subjects in the Diploma, and the mathematical exploration that accompanies it is a 12 to 20 page piece of independent work worth twenty per cent.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics and modelling route, with less calculus and more data handling. Suitable for many social-science and business degrees, and the route to check against the published entry requirements of any specific course your child is targeting rather than against general advice.

subjects.name: The arts, or a second subject from groups 1 to 5
subjects.description: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Film, or a sixth subject taken from an earlier group instead. Arts subjects place heavy weight on documented process and on the exhibition or performance components, which is where students with real ability most often lose marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An externally assessed essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title, plus an internally assessed exhibition with a commentary of up to 950 words. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points to the final score, which is the difference between an offer and a near miss more often than families expect.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a subject of the student's choice, supervised in school. Support is process coaching only: narrowing the research question until it is answerable, reading the criteria properly, and giving feedback on drafts the student has written themselves.

sections.heading: What a 'near me' search returns, and what a Diploma student needs
paragraphs: Be precise about what the search is doing. A local search ranks by proximity and prominence. It returns agencies with a Dubai address, individuals advertising in community groups, and tuition centres with premises, ordered mostly by how close they are to you and how well they have optimised. None of those signals correlates with whether somebody can tell you what the assessment criteria for a Mathematics exploration are, or what happens to a Diploma if a core component is not submitted.

The result is a shortlist that answers a question you did not ask. You wanted someone who knows Higher Level Economics; you got five people who are nearby and available. A proportion of them will be genuinely strong, and there is no way to tell from the listing which ones. In a community like The Greens, where the Diploma is not taught inside the neighbourhood and local students commute to it, the chance that the nearest available person is also a specialist in your child's particular Higher Level subject is simply low.

The table below sets the two things side by side: what the search actually filters for, and what the Diploma actually requires. It is worth reading because it also tells you what to ask. If you can name the subject, the level and the internal assessment, you can replace a proximity filter with a competence filter in a single sentence, and that works whether you are speaking to a neighbour, an agency or a platform.

sections.heading: Six groups, 45 points, and where the three extra points come from
paragraphs: The structure is worth understanding before any tutoring decision, because it tells you where marginal points are cheapest. A Diploma candidate takes six subjects, one from each of groups 1 to 5 plus a sixth from group 6 or a second subject from an earlier group. Three are taken at Higher Level, with 240 recommended teaching hours each, and three at Standard Level, with 150. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, which gives a maximum of 42.

The remaining three points come from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, awarded on a matrix rather than individually. This is the part families most often ignore and it is frequently the cheapest place to find points. A student grinding a Higher Level subject from a 5 to a 6 is buying one point for a great deal of work; a student who writes a careful Extended Essay and a competent TOK essay may collect two or three for considerably less, because both are extended pieces produced over months with feedback available throughout.

That shapes a sensible tutoring plan. Before paying for weekly sessions across several subjects, look at where the realistic gains are: a core component not yet started, an internal assessment with a flawed research question, a subject where a student is one grade boundary away rather than three. The table below lists the groups and what each contributes, so a Greens parent can see the whole score on one screen before deciding where to spend.

sections.heading: Three Higher Level subjects: what that actually costs a week
paragraphs: Parents routinely underestimate the Higher Level load, and the numbers make it concrete. Three Higher Level subjects at 240 recommended teaching hours each and three Standard Level at 150 gives 1,170 hours of taught content across two years, before the Extended Essay, before Theory of Knowledge, and before creativity, activity and service. Spread over the Dubai academic year that is a full working week of school with independent work layered on top.

For a Greens student the commute compounds it. The Diploma is not taught inside the community, so a local DP student is travelling to Al Barsha or across Sheikh Zayed Road, arriving home closer to four than three. By the time they have eaten, the window for anything extra is roughly 6pm to 9pm, and in DP2 part of that window is already committed to internal assessment work with school deadlines attached. Adding three weekly tutoring sessions into that is not ambition, it is arithmetic failure, and it is why some families get worse results after buying more support.

The honest advice is to buy less, more precisely. One Higher Level subject with a standing ninety-minute weekly slot, plus a short core-component block timed to the school's internal deadlines, is a plan that survives a term. Three weekly sessions across three subjects is a plan that collapses in October and leaves a family concluding that tutoring does not work. The table below sets out the load and where support is worth adding.

sections.heading: Word and page limits for every component, in one table
paragraphs: This is the single most useful reference a Diploma parent can have and almost nobody publishes it. Every independently produced component in the Diploma has a stated limit, and students routinely discover a limit after writing well past it. An Extended Essay is 4,000 words. The Theory of Knowledge essay is up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title, with the exhibition commentary up to 950. A sciences scientific investigation runs to a 3,000-word maximum and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each. A mathematical exploration is 12 to 20 pages rather than a word count.

Limits are not merely administrative. They shape what a good piece of work looks like, because a research question that needs 7,000 words to answer is the wrong research question, and most core-component failures trace back to that single decision rather than to weak writing. The most valuable hour of support available on any of these components is the one spent narrowing the question until it fits the limit comfortably, and that hour is best bought months before the deadline.

The honesty boundary is firm and worth stating in the same breath. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each criterion and its marks, ask the questions that expose an unworkable research question, teach referencing and structure, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections or produce any part of an assessed piece. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work must be the candidate's own, and a breach is a malpractice matter for the student. At least one site competing for these searches sells finished internal assessments outright; no IB Gram tutor will produce assessed work for a student. Confirm every limit with your school's IB coordinator, since they are the authority on what applies to your child's session.

sections.heading: Why there is no IB examination date anywhere on this page
paragraphs: You will find pages quoting precise IB examination windows and results dates for upcoming sessions. This page does not, and the reason is worth explaining because it tells you something about how to read the rest of it. The IB's own site returns an error to automated access, so none of the IB session or results dates circulating in secondary sources could be confirmed against the IB itself during the research behind these pages. Publishing an unverified date to a parent planning a revision schedule is a small betrayal with real consequences, so the dates are not here.

What can be said with confidence is the shape of the year. UAE schools sit the May session, there is a November session, and your child's IB coordinator holds the authoritative dates for both along with the school's internal deadlines for every core component and internal assessment. Those internal deadlines are the ones that actually govern a tutoring plan, because they fall months before any examination and they are the points at which work is lost rather than recovered. Ask the coordinator for the full list in writing and build backwards from it.

Where dates are verifiable, this project publishes them. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series with March available for some syllabuses, allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE examinations in May and June and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are from the boards' own pages. The difference between the two halves of this section is the difference between a sourced page and a confident one.

sections.heading: Where IB tutoring money gets wasted in a community like this one
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates give the context. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey giving the same band. Premium named tutors go higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Visiting one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500. All of those are other providers' published figures as of the October 2026 research and not an IB Gram price list.

The waste is rarely in the hourly rate. It is in buying the wrong hours. Three weekly sessions across three subjects in DP2 is the most common expensive mistake, because the student has no capacity to use them and the sessions become supervised homework at a specialist price. The second is hiring a generalist for a Higher Level subject, which costs less per hour and produces nothing, since the gap at Higher Level is almost always command terms and criteria rather than content. The third is starting in February of DP2, when the only available lever is examination technique and the core components are already fixed.

The fourth deserves its own warning. Paying somebody to produce assessed work is not a shortcut, it is a malpractice exposure that sits with your child and not with the seller, and the consequence is borne at the point when it is most costly. The table below lists the five patterns in order of how much money they absorb, with what to do instead in each case. It is written for a Greens household weighing a term's budget rather than a single hour.

sections.heading: Maths AA or AI, and checking it against the course your child wants
paragraphs: One decision in the Diploma causes more retrospective regret than any other, and it is made in the subject-choice weeks of DP1. Analysis and Approaches carries the calculus and algebraic fluency that mathematics, physics and engineering degrees lean on. Applications and Interpretation goes further into statistics, modelling and data handling and lighter into calculus, and suits many social-science, business and design routes. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, which makes four options rather than two.

The reliable method is to work from published entry requirements rather than from reputation. Take the two or three specific degree courses your child is considering, at the specific universities, and read what each one states about Diploma mathematics. Requirements differ between institutions for the same subject, and they differ between courses within one institution. A general belief that Analysis and Approaches is the serious option is not a substitute for reading a course page, and it has pushed plenty of students into a Higher Level course they did not need and could not carry.

Where support genuinely helps is in the diagnosis rather than the opinion. A single session with a mathematics specialist, working through one problem that needs calculus and one that needs statistical reasoning, usually shows which route fits a student's actual strengths. Do it in DP1 while the choice is live. By DP2 the question has become how to survive the course rather than which course to take, and that is a more expensive problem.

sections.heading: Starting from The Greens, and the subjects nobody can cover locally
paragraphs: The enquiry that gets the most useful reply names the subject, the level, the internal assessment and its current state, the last paper or predicted grade, and the two evening windows that are genuinely free. With those five things a specialist can tell you in one message whether the issue is content, technique or a component that has gone wrong, and quote a plan against your week. 'My daughter is struggling with the IB' takes a paid session to decode.

Then a free trial lesson, one per student and bookable without card details, with the tutor who would continue. For a Diploma subject a good trial includes a real question at the real level and a direct reference to the criteria. Expect the tutor to name the component and the command term rather than discuss motivation and confidence. If the match is wrong, say so and ask for another; it costs nothing and it is a better outcome than a term of polite sessions.

The coverage note is where honesty matters most. Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and the less common Language B options are the thinnest specialisms, and the 6pm to 8:30pm weekday band that a commuting Greens student needs is the most contested on the platform. When no suitable tutor is free in that window you will be told, with a date, rather than matched to whoever is available. Where a UAE-based tutor cannot cover a niche subject, the alternative offered is a UAE-timed session with an IB specialist based elsewhere, in the same format at the same Gulf Standard Time hour. No tutor will be sent to a Greens address, because that is not a service offered here.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Send the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, which internal assessment is in progress and what state it is in, plus the last paper or predicted grade. Five specifics let a specialist diagnose the problem in one message instead of spending a paid hour establishing what your child is actually studying.

process.title: Get the internal deadlines in writing
process.description: Ask your school's IB coordinator for the internal deadlines on every core component and internal assessment. Those dates govern a tutoring plan far more than any examination window, because they are the points at which marks are lost permanently rather than recovered with revision.

process.title: A trial that references the criteria
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details needed, with the tutor who would continue. Expect a real question at the real level and an explicit reference to the assessment criteria. A trial spent discussing confidence rather than the subject has told you how specific the teaching is likely to be.

process.title: Buy one subject, not three
process.description: Start with a standing ninety-minute weekly slot in the single subject closest to a grade boundary, plus a short block on whichever core component is furthest behind. Three weekly sessions in DP2 exceed what a student with three Higher Level subjects can absorb, and that is the most common way a budget is wasted.

process.title: Review at each reporting point
process.description: Predicted grades, mocks and internal deadlines are the natural review points. At each one the plan is checked against the mark and the state of the components, and the frequency is adjusted. Stopping a subject that has reached its target is a normal outcome rather than a lost booking.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject group and level
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to Higher Level Economics or Standard Level Chemistry specifically, not to 'the IB'. That is the filter a proximity search cannot apply, and in a community where the Diploma is not taught inside the neighbourhood it is the difference between a useful hour and a supervised one.

whyPoints.title: Component limits published openly
whyPoints.description: Word and page limits for the Extended Essay, both Theory of Knowledge tasks, the sciences investigation and the mathematical exploration are set out in one table on this page. No competitor page examined in the research behind it carries that information at all, and it is the first thing a parent needs.

whyPoints.title: No unverified dates
whyPoints.description: No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because none could be confirmed against the IB's own site during the research. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published where they came from the boards' own pages. Where a figure is unverified, the page says so instead of guessing.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line stated in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, explains criteria and gives feedback on drafts the student has written. No text is supplied and no assessed work is produced. One site competing in this search sells finished internal assessments; that exposure sits with the candidate rather than the seller.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that fit a commuting Diploma student
whyPoints.description: A Greens DP student travels out of the community to school and is home closer to four than three. Slots run from 6pm to 8:30pm in Gulf Standard Time with no parking, building access or lift involved, and a session can shift by half an hour on the day without anybody losing travel time.

whyPoints.title: Rates and coverage both disclosed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it as of October 2026, and the thinnest specialisms are named rather than hidden. IB Gram holds no IB, KHDA or Ministry of Education accreditation and claims none; the facts cited here are cited, not borrowed as credentials.

faqs.question: What does searching for an IB tutor near me in The Greens actually give you?
faqs.answer: A list ordered mostly by proximity and optimisation: agencies with a Dubai address, individuals advertising in community groups, and tuition centres with premises. None of those signals tells you whether somebody knows the criteria for a mathematical exploration or when a school's internal deadlines fall. The Diploma is not taught inside The Greens, so local students commute to it, which makes the chance that the nearest available person is also a specialist in your child's Higher Level subject genuinely low. Replace the distance filter with a subject and level question and the shortlist changes completely.

faqs.question: How many subjects does the IB Diploma require, and at what levels?
faqs.answer: Six, drawn one each from groups 1 to 5 plus a sixth from group 6 or a second subject from an earlier group. Three are taken at Higher Level with 240 recommended teaching hours each and three at Standard Level with 150. Alongside them sit Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. That is 1,170 recommended hours of taught content across two years before any independent work, which is why adding three weekly tutoring sessions in DP2 usually backfires rather than helps.

faqs.question: What is the maximum Diploma score and where do the last three points come from?
faqs.answer: Forty-five. Forty-two of those come from the six subjects, graded 1 to 7 each, and up to three more from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, awarded on a matrix rather than separately. Families routinely overlook the core points, which is a mistake, because they are often the cheapest available. Moving a Higher Level subject up one grade is a great deal of work for one point; writing a careful Extended Essay and a competent TOK essay can produce two or three for less, with months of feedback available along the way.

faqs.question: Which schools near The Greens actually offer the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: None inside the community itself, since the school within The Greens runs the British curriculum. Local Diploma students commute, usually to Emirates International School Meadows or Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills across Sheikh Zayed Road, or to IB provision in the Al Barsha cluster. Schools are named here as context only; programme availability changes year to year, so confirm the current offering with the school and check the published inspection record with KHDA, which is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai.

faqs.question: How long is the Extended Essay, and when should my child start it?
faqs.answer: Four thousand words, on a research question of the student's choosing, supervised by a teacher at school. The useful start point is the summer between DP1 and DP2, and the single highest-value hour of support on it is spent narrowing the research question until it can genuinely be answered in 4,000 words. Most Extended Essay problems trace back to that one decision rather than to weak writing. Support is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts; the essay has to be theirs from first word to last.

faqs.question: What are the word limits on the Theory of Knowledge tasks?
faqs.answer: The externally assessed TOK essay runs to a maximum of 1,600 words on a prescribed title, and the internally assessed exhibition carries a commentary of up to 950 words. Together with the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge contributes up to three points to the final Diploma score. Students usually find the prescribed title harder than the writing, because the title has to be unpacked before anything can be argued. Confirm the limits that apply to your child's session with their IB coordinator, since published requirements are revised periodically.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits, and it is often a good use of a few hours. A tutor can unpack a prescribed title until the student understands what is actually being asked, teach the difference between an example and an argument, explain the assessment criteria, and read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin. A tutor cannot supply text, choose the examples or produce the essay. Theory of Knowledge is also unusually responsive to a small amount of help, because most students lose marks on structure rather than on ideas.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list the IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because none could be confirmed against the IB's own site during the research behind these pages, which returns an error to automated access. Dates circulating in secondary sources may be correct and may not, and publishing an unverified date to a parent planning a revision schedule is not a small error. What can be said is that UAE schools sit the May session, a November session exists, and your child's IB coordinator holds the authoritative dates along with the school's internal deadlines. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear elsewhere on this site because those boards publish them openly.

faqs.question: Three Higher Level subjects sounds heavy. How heavy is it in practice?
faqs.answer: Three Higher Level subjects at 240 recommended teaching hours each plus three Standard Level at 150 gives 1,170 hours across two years, before the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and service commitments. For a Greens student who commutes out of the community and is home closer to four than three, the realistic window for anything additional is roughly 6pm to 9pm, and in DP2 part of that is already committed to internal assessment deadlines. Plan one standing weekly session rather than three, and add a short block on whichever component is furthest behind.

faqs.question: Where do families most often waste money on IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four patterns account for most of it. Buying weekly sessions in three subjects at once in DP2, when the student has no capacity to use them and sessions become supervised homework at a specialist price. Hiring a generalist for a Higher Level subject, where the gap is criteria and command terms rather than content. Starting in February of DP2, when the core components are already fixed and only technique is movable. And paying for assessed work to be produced, which is a malpractice exposure carried by the candidate rather than a shortcut.

faqs.question: How do I decide between the two IB maths routes without guessing?
faqs.answer: Work from published entry requirements rather than reputation. Analysis and Approaches carries the calculus and algebraic fluency that mathematics, physics and engineering degrees lean on; Applications and Interpretation goes further into statistics and modelling and lighter into calculus, which suits many social-science and business routes. Requirements differ between universities for the same subject and between courses at one university, so read the two or three specific course pages your child is targeting. A single diagnostic session in DP1, with one calculus problem and one statistical one, usually settles which route fits.

faqs.question: Can one IB tutor cover subjects from more than one group?
faqs.answer: Some can, and the common pairings are genuine: Mathematics with Physics, Economics with Business Management, two sciences at Standard Level. At Higher Level the useful answer is usually no, because the depth required in each subject plus knowledge of each internal assessment's criteria is a lot to hold for two subjects at once. The arrangement that works for most Greens families is one specialist for the Higher Level subject that is costing points and, where a second subject needs maintenance, a separate tutor in a sequential slot the same evening.

faqs.question: My child needs 38 points for a university offer. Can tutoring deliver that?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise a score, and anybody who does should be treated with real scepticism. What tutoring can do is identify where the points realistically are: a subject sitting one grade boundary below target, a core component not yet started, an internal assessment with a research question that will cap the mark whatever is written. Those are diagnosable and movable. A plan built on them is honest. A plan built on a promised total is not, and the gap between a 36 and a 38 is often two core points rather than two subject grades.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a tutor for from The Greens?
faqs.answer: Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and the less common Language B options are the thinnest specialisms, and demand for them peaks in the same weeks every year. The 6pm to 8:30pm weekday band that a commuting Diploma student needs is also the most contested, which compounds it. When no suitable tutor is free in that window you are told with a date rather than matched to a generalist. The alternatives are usually a Friday morning or weekend slot, or a UAE-timed session with a specialist based elsewhere.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-greens.closingHeading: Replace the distance filter with one sentence
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-greens.closingBody: The most useful change a Greens parent can make costs nothing. Stop asking who is nearby and start asking one sentence: which Higher Level subjects have you taught, and can you name the criteria for this internal assessment? That question is answerable in ten seconds by somebody who knows the course and not at all by somebody improvising, and it works equally well on a neighbour's recommendation, an agency or this page. Send us the subject, the level, the component and the two evenings that are genuinely free, and the trial lesson can be booked with the person who would actually teach it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level into Gulf Standard Time evenings. Before you compare their rates, compare what each one proposes to work on: an hour aimed at a 20 per cent coursework component is not the same purchase as an hour of general revision.

intro.heading: The proximity filter is the most expensive setting in your search
paragraphs: Start at the top of the Dubai market and work down, because that is where the shape becomes visible. One premium provider publishes AED 650 an hour. A 2026 Dubai rate study places examination-year specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and one agency quotes AED 270 for specialist work. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with one agency publishing AED 200 for IB and AED 150 for IGCSE. Platform rates for university-student tutors begin around AED 33 to AED 65. That is a nineteen-fold spread for an hour of somebody's time.

Now add the in-home premium, because the search phrase at the top of this page is a request for one. In-home visits in Dubai are published at AED 180 to AED 350 in that 2026 study and up to AED 500 in independent listings. Against AED 150 to AED 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor working online, roughly AED 60 to AED 150 an hour is the car. For a weekly hour across the two Diploma years that is somewhere between AED 4,000 and AED 11,000 spent on a journey between Al Barsha and Hattan.

What the proximity filter buys is a smaller pool, and a smaller pool costs more for less. Inside a twenty-minute drive of The Lakes there is a finite number of tutors who teach Higher Level Chemistry to DP2 standard, and in any given term some are full. A Diploma student takes three Higher Level subjects, so a geographic search asks you to accept the best available locally in each of them - which in practice is one good match and two compromises, at the higher rate.

So the position, stated plainly because the query invites the opposite. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and nobody arrives at a Lakes address under any arrangement sold here. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with work marked on a shared screen during the lesson. The rate bands above are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and they are printed here so a Lakes family can judge any quote - ours included - against the market.

The rest of this page is about allocation rather than price. Six subjects, three of them Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and a household budget that will not stretch to all of it. Which components carry the most marks for the least money. What the Diploma core is actually worth in points. Which extras sit outside the hourly rate and catch families out. And a practical method for deciding, at six sessions, whether an hour was worth what it cost.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.programmesIntro: The Diploma is the expensive stage and the one this page is costed for, but the two years before it determine how much of it you will need to buy. Here is the sequence a Lakes family is budgeting across.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects - three Higher Level, three Standard Level - plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject's grade is built from externally marked papers and an internally marked assessment, with the coursework component usually carrying around 20 per cent. Higher Level subjects add a third paper in many subjects, which is where the extra teaching hours go.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Diploma tutoring is priced at the top of the market: AED 200 to AED 450 and above for examination-year specialists according to the 2026 rate study, with one agency publishing AED 270. For a Lakes household the practical consequence is that you cannot fund six subjects, so the allocation question matters more than the hourly rate does.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition and the Extended Essay are graded and together contribute up to three bonus points to the Diploma total; CAS is a completion requirement rather than a graded one. None of the three has a daily timetabled lesson, which is why they are underprepared and why they are usually the cheapest available marks in the whole programme.
programmes.countryNote: Three points is the difference between a conditional offer met and missed, and the core is where a small, well-timed coaching spend has the best ratio in the Diploma. Lakes families typically discover this in the DP2 autumn, when the school's internal deadlines for both arrive in the same fortnight as two subject coursework deadlines.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-marked across eight subject groups, each criterion scored 0 to 8 and combined into a grade from 1 to 7, with the Personal Project in MYP 5 and no external examination unless the school enters students for optional eAssessment. The assessment style is quite different from the Diploma's percentage-weighted papers.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest Diploma is one prepared for. MYP work sits at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour while Diploma specialist work starts around AED 200 and runs past AED 450, so a weakness fixed in MYP 5 is bought at roughly half the price of the same weakness fixed in DP1. That is the strongest cost argument available on this page.

programmes.name: IGCSE as the alternative route
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson examinations with syllabus codes and tiers - 0580 Core or Extended, 4MA1 Foundation or Higher - taken by many students at the schools Lakes children attend before they choose between A Level and the Diploma at 16. Tier decisions made in Year 10 determine which Higher Level Diploma subjects are available at 17.
programmes.countryNote: One agency publishes AED 150 an hour for IGCSE against AED 200 for IB, which is the clearest published evidence of the price step between the two. A Lakes family planning ahead should expect roughly a third more per hour once the student enters the Diploma, and budget the two years accordingly rather than reacting in the first DP1 term.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.subjectsIntro: Diploma grades are built from weighted components, so the useful question per subject is not how hard it is but where the marks sit. These are the subjects Lakes families fund most often, with the component that gives the best return named.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level the two papers carry 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20 per cent. At Higher Level three papers carry 30, 30 and 20 with the exploration again at 20. Paper 3 at Higher Level is the component most students never practise under timed conditions, and it is worth a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure as Analysis and Approaches, with a graphical display calculator assumed in every paper. Modelling questions reward method marks that students routinely forfeit by not stating assumptions. The cheapest gain here is calculator fluency, which takes two sessions and is almost never taught.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current guide, Paper 1 carries 36 per cent, Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and the scientific investigation 20 per cent at both levels. Higher Level covers additional content rather than an extra paper. The investigation is a single piece of coursework worth a fifth of the grade and is the highest-return hour in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The same 36, 44 and 20 split applies. Organic mechanisms and energetics carry most of the lost marks at Higher Level, and the data-based section of Paper 1 is recoverable quickly. The investigation has a strict honesty boundary: the tutor questions the design and reads the student's draft, and writes none of it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty, with command terms doing more work than students expect. Paper 2's extended response questions are where the grade is decided, and the fastest recovery is in data interpretation. Short frequent sessions outperform long ones, which also makes them cheaper per useful minute.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Standard Level Paper 1 is 30 per cent, Paper 2 is 40 and the internal assessment 30. At Higher Level there is a third paper and the split moves to roughly 20, 30, 30 and 20. The internal assessment is three commentaries, worth a large share of the Standard Level grade, and it is the component families most often leave unsupported.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Standard Level sits at roughly 35, 35 and 30 across two papers and the internal assessment; Higher Level adds a third paper and the pre-released case study. Because the case study is published in advance, structured preparation across months beats a pre-examination sprint, which makes a steady low-cost weekly hour genuinely efficient here.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Standard Level Paper 1, Paper 2 and the Individual Oral sit near 35, 35 and 30. At Higher Level the HL Essay is added and the weightings redistribute. The Individual Oral is a rehearsed assessment and therefore the most improvable component per hour in the whole Diploma for a student who will practise it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: At Standard Level Paper 1 carries half the grade, Paper 2 a quarter and the internal assessment a quarter; Higher Level adds a third paper. The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experiment with a prescribed format, and the write-up is where the marks are lost. A short coaching block beats a standing weekly hour.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Standard Level runs roughly 30, 45 and 25 across source paper, essay paper and the historical investigation; Higher Level adds a regional-option paper worth around 35 per cent and redistributes the rest. The source paper is a technique component that can be lifted substantially in six sessions, which makes it the efficient place to start.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.regionsTitle: Where the money goes around Emirates Living
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.regionsIntro: Tutor supply and spending patterns differ across the communities that share The Lakes' schools. These notes are about what families in each actually fund, and what the local market can supply.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Villa households, mostly with Diploma or IGCSE-age children at schools outside the community. Demand concentrates on Higher Level sciences and mathematics, which is exactly where the local in-home pool is thinnest and the premium highest.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Emirates International School Meadows sits inside the community and runs the IB continuum, so Meadows households more often fund MYP criterion work - the cheaper band - than Diploma examination support.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: Townhouses with a younger average age, so spending here is on Key Stage 3 and MYP foundations. This is the community where early, low-cost intervention has the longest payback before Diploma rates apply.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Dubai British School Emirates Hills create a split market: IB Diploma families at the specialist band alongside A Level families at a slightly lower one.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Apartment stock with Regent International School inside it. Shorter commutes mean more families attempt an early weekday slot, and more of them pay for a second subject because the evening has room.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Beside Emirates Golf Club and close to the Al Sufouh corridor. Households here report the highest rate of activity-driven cancellations, which makes a package with expiring sessions a poor purchase.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Where most of the schools are, and therefore where most in-home tutors are based. A Lakes family hiring locally is usually hiring from this pool and paying for the return drive in both directions.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: The nearest dense tutor supply outside Emirates Living. The drive in at 16:30 is the reason an in-home visit from here is quoted at the upper end of the published AED 180 to AED 500 band.

sections.heading: What a 'near me' search optimises for, and what that costs
paragraphs: A proximity search sorts tutors by driving distance from The Lakes. That is a sensible way to buy a plumber and a poor way to buy a Higher Level Chemistry teacher, because the thing being optimised - minutes in a car - is not a thing that produces marks. The filter has two costs, and both are measurable. It raises the hourly rate, and it shrinks the pool you are choosing from.

The rate effect first. Dubai in-home visits are published at AED 180 to AED 350 in the 2026 rate study and up to AED 500 in independent listings, while an equivalently qualified tutor teaching online is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300. The difference is the journey, and for a Lakes address that journey happens between 16:00 and 16:30 in the direction everybody else is also driving. Across a weekly hour for the two Diploma years, the premium alone runs into several thousand dirhams.

The pool effect is larger and less visible. A Diploma student takes three Higher Level subjects. Within twenty minutes of Hattan, the set of tutors who can teach Higher Level Chemistry to DP2 standard is small, and in a given term part of it is already committed. The same is true for Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and for whichever third Higher Level the student has chosen. So a geographic search typically yields one good match and two people who are available.

There is a third cost that only appears later. Dubai is a transient market, and an in-home arrangement ends when the tutor's residency does. Families who have rebuilt a Diploma tutoring arrangement in the middle of DP2 will recognise the expense of that, which is not an hourly rate at all but a lost term. A video arrangement survives a relocation on either side, which in a two-year programme is worth more than the hourly difference.

sections.heading: Two years of Diploma support, priced from the top down
paragraphs: Work downward from the most expensive option, because that is how you find out what you are actually buying. At AED 650 an hour - the top published Dubai figure, from one premium provider - a single weekly hour across the two Diploma years is a substantial five-figure commitment in dirhams. At the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 identified in the 2026 rate study, the same weekly hour is roughly a third to two-thirds of that. At the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to AED 300 it is lower again.

The table converts each published band into a two-year figure for one weekly hour, because that is the number a household actually commits to and nobody in this market publishes it. Read the right-hand column before the left one: the question is not which rate is lowest but which band contains a person who can teach the specific component your child is losing marks on. Paying AED 450 for general revision is worse value than paying AED 200 for targeted work on a Paper 3.

Two structural notes about the figures. They assume an hour a week for roughly thirty-six teaching weeks a year, which is what a Dubai school year supports once holidays and examination weeks are removed. And they are single-subject figures: a Diploma student funded in two subjects doubles everything. That doubling is why the allocation question in the next section matters more than the rate negotiation most families spend their energy on.

None of these are IB Gram prices. Our quote is given after the free trial lesson, against the subject, the level and the component involved, and there is no package to buy in order to start. We publish no VAT position, because the UAE treatment of tuition fees is a Federal Tax Authority matter rather than ours to assert - ask any provider directly whether a quoted figure includes it, and get the answer in writing before you transfer anything.

sections.heading: Six subjects, three Higher Levels, and a budget for two
paragraphs: No Lakes household funds six Diploma subjects, so the allocation decision is the real one. It has a method. Start by separating the subjects where a grade is a condition of something from the subjects where it is merely a grade. A Higher Level science required for a medicine or engineering offer is not interchangeable with a Standard Level subject chosen to balance the diploma, and the money follows the condition.

Second, look at the distance from the target rather than the absolute grade. A student sitting at a 4 in Higher Level Chemistry who needs a 6 has a two-grade gap, which is a term's work. A student at a 6 who wants a 7 is chasing the hardest marks in the subject and will often spend more for less movement. The efficient purchase is almost always the two-grade gap in a conditional subject, not the one-grade gap at the top.

Third, look at the component rather than the subject. Around a fifth of most Diploma subject grades sits in an internally assessed piece of coursework, and Higher Level mathematics has a Paper 3 worth another fifth that almost no student practises under timed conditions. An hour aimed at a 20 per cent component that is currently unprepared buys more marks than an hour of general revision across a paper the student already half knows.

Fourth, and least intuitive: fund the core. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together carry up to three bonus points, and neither has a timetabled daily lesson, so they are systematically underprepared. Three or four coaching sessions placed at the right checkpoints is a few thousand dirhams at most, against three points that can decide whether a conditional offer is met. Nothing else in the Diploma has that ratio.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit: component weightings across the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the table nobody in this market publishes, and it is the one a parent allocating a budget actually needs. A Diploma subject grade is built from weighted components, and the weightings differ by subject and by level. Knowing them turns a vague worry about a subject into a specific decision about an hour: if 44 per cent of a science grade sits in Paper 2 and the student's mock showed the losses there, that is where the money goes.

The pattern is worth reading as a whole. Mathematics places 20 per cent in the exploration at both levels and adds a Paper 3 worth another 20 per cent at Higher Level. The sciences under the current guide place 36 per cent in Paper 1, 44 per cent in Paper 2 and 20 per cent in the scientific investigation at both levels, with Higher Level adding content rather than a paper. Economics and Business Management shift substantially between levels, with Higher Level adding a third paper and reducing the coursework share.

Two components are chronically underprepared relative to their weight. The first is Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, a long investigative paper that students meet for the first time in a mock. The second is the internally assessed coursework in every subject, which is worth around a fifth of the grade and is written once, usually late, often without feedback against the published criteria. Both are addressable in small numbers of hours, which is what makes them the efficient purchase.

One caution on the figures. Weightings are taken from the current subject guides and the IB revises them subject by subject on its own cycle, so confirm against your child's own guide or with the school's IB coordinator before planning from them. For the same reason no IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page: ibo.org is the authority and the coordinator is the person who knows your cohort's dates.

sections.heading: Three bonus points: the cheapest marks in the Diploma
paragraphs: The Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay are graded together on a matrix that awards up to three bonus points toward the Diploma total. Three points moves a 35 to a 38. In a market where Dubai specialist tutoring costs AED 270 an hour, those three points are available for a handful of coaching sessions, because the work is underprepared almost universally and because nobody is timetabled to teach it daily.

The Extended Essay goes wrong in predictable places. A research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. A methodology that produces opinion rather than evidence. A first draft submitted without anybody checking it against the assessment criteria. Reflection sessions treated as an administrative formality rather than as assessed evidence of process. Each of those is a single conversation at the right moment, and the right moments are known in advance because the school publishes its internal deadlines.

Theory of Knowledge fails differently. Students write about knowledge in general where the essay asks about a prescribed title and expects real-world examples handled precisely. The exhibition asks for objects connected to a prompt and justified, which rewards specificity over sophistication. Two sessions on structure and example selection move a Theory of Knowledge grade more reliably than a term of discussion about the nature of truth.

The honesty boundary here is absolute and worth restating because the temptation is highest. A tutor questions the research question, reads what the student has written and names the criterion not yet met. A tutor does not write the Extended Essay, does not draft a Theory of Knowledge essay, and does not rewrite paragraphs into their own prose. Line-editing until the words are the tutor's is authorship by instalment. Submissions that are not the student's own work are a malpractice matter for the student.
