sections.heading: Packages, group classes and the extras outside the hourly rate
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the number everybody compares and the smallest part of what is actually being bought. A package of twenty sessions at a discount is only cheaper if all twenty are used before they expire, and in a household in The Views or Zulal where tournaments and travel cancel two or three sessions a term, they frequently are not. Ask for the expiry terms, the cancellation notice period and the refund position before any discount is interesting.

Group classes are the other apparent saving. Six students at a lower per-head rate looks like clear arithmetic until you consider what is being delivered: one explanation at one pace, with no diagnosis of your child's specific component losses. For a cohort revising the same paper to the same deadline that can work. For a student losing marks on command terms in Paper 2 while the person beside them is losing them on calculation, it does not, and the per-mark cost ends up higher than one-to-one.

Then there are the extras that sit outside the rate and are rarely stated up front. Materials, where some providers charge for a workbook that duplicates what the school already issued. Report writing, charged per report by some agencies. Travel, in an in-home arrangement, sometimes billed separately from the hour. Replacement, where the policy if a tutor leaves mid-year ranges from an immediate substitute to nothing. And VAT, which should be stated rather than assumed.

The table compares provider models rather than named companies, on the dimensions that actually produce surprises. Use it as a question list. A provider who answers all eight columns in writing before you pay is a provider whose arrangement will hold; one who answers only the rate column has told you something about how the rest of it will be handled.

sections.heading: Judging whether an hour was worth what it cost
paragraphs: Tutoring is bought on hope and should be judged on evidence, and the evidence has to be agreed before the money starts. The method is short. Before the second lesson, write down which component is being targeted and what the current mark on it is. Set written work to be marked between sessions. At six sessions, compare the mark on that component. That is it, and it is the whole of what distinguishes a measurable arrangement from a subscription.

What counts as evidence is narrower than families expect. A mark on the targeted component in school work or in a marked past paper counts. A tutor's report that the student is more confident does not, because confidence rises in the first three sessions of every arrangement regardless of whether anything is being learned. Nor does the student's own sense that the lessons are useful, which correlates with how pleasant the tutor is rather than with marks.

If the mark has not moved at six sessions there are exactly four possibilities and all four are actionable. The diagnosis was wrong, so change the component. The format is wrong, so change frequency or length - two shorter sessions often beat one long one. The tutor is wrong, so change the tutor. Or tutoring is not the intervention needed, in which case stop and have a conversation with the school about tier, set or subject choice instead.

The reason to agree this at the start is that nobody renegotiates in March. A family six months into a weekly arrangement with no agreed measure will keep paying because stopping feels like giving up, and that inertia is worth more to a provider than any discount. A six-session review with stopping named as one of the options is the single cheapest piece of financial discipline available in this market.

sections.heading: Retakes, remarks and sitting as a private candidate
paragraphs: Three cost questions arrive after results day and almost nobody plans for them. The first is the review of marks, which opens from the student's results release and has a deadline set by the board. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the windows and fees are published by the board and administered through the centre; for the Diploma the process runs through the school. In all cases the decision has to be made quickly, which is why knowing the results date in advance matters.

The second is the retake. The Diploma can be resat in a later session, and the practical questions are how many subjects, whether the coursework carries forward and what the school will support. Each of those has a cost attached and the answers differ by school, so the conversation belongs with the IB coordinator rather than with a tutoring provider. What a tutor can offer is a focused block on the specific papers being resat, which is a shorter and cheaper purchase than a year of weekly support.

The third is sitting as a private candidate, which arises when a student has left a school, is between schools, or wants a subject the school does not offer. Entry is arranged through a school or examination centre willing to accept external candidates, and the fee is set by that centre rather than published centrally. No figure appears on this page because none was verified for it; ask two or three centres directly and compare, because the range is wide.

Across all three, the honest framing is the same. These are administrative processes run by boards, schools and centres, and no tutoring provider performs, accelerates or guarantees any of them. A provider implying that hiring them affects a remark, a retake or an entry is describing something it does not control. What tutoring does is prepare a specific paper for a specific sitting, and that is worth buying on its own terms.

sections.heading: Starting from The Lakes without buying a package
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing and is deliberately small. Tell us the school, the Diploma year, the six subjects with their levels, and the component you believe is weakest - or send a marked mock paper and let us say which it is. We come back with a tutor who teaches that subject at that level, a proposed focus for the first three lessons, and a rate. Then take the free trial lesson in one subject, with no card details collected.

What we will not do is sell you a block to start. Pay-as-you-go is the default here precisely because it is the format with no expiry risk, and because a household that can stop at any point is a household that gets a measurable arrangement rather than an inert one. If a package ever makes sense for you, it will be after six sessions, not before the first.

The limit is availability in narrow combinations. Mainstream Diploma subjects match within a few days. Higher Level Philosophy, a less common Language B, Music, or a request for one tutor across an unusual Higher and Standard pairing can take longer, and the tutor may be based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We state which, and from where, before anything is agreed - a disclosure no competitor page researched in this market makes at all.

Two closing statements of position. IB Gram makes no grade or points promise, publishes no statistic about past students that it cannot evidence, and holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership. And private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit: the private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Asking any provider about it is reasonable.

process.title: Send the subject list and one marked paper
process.description: Six subjects with their levels, plus a photograph of a marked mock. The marked paper is what turns a budget conversation into a specific one, because it shows which component is losing marks and therefore which hour is worth buying first. Without it, any allocation advice is guesswork dressed as a plan.

process.title: We name the component before we name a rate
process.description: The proposal says which component the first three lessons target and why that one rather than another - a 20 per cent coursework piece, a Higher Level third paper, a source-technique paper. The rate follows the proposal. A quote given before a diagnosis is a quote for something unspecified.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one subject, no card
process.description: Sixty minutes on a real question from the student's own paper, on a shared screen. You are checking one thing: whether the tutor's diagnosis matches what the marked paper shows. No card details are collected and nothing is owed afterwards if the answer is no.

process.title: Pay by the session, review at six
process.description: No block, no expiry, no cancellation penalty. Before the second lesson the component and its current mark are written down. At six sessions we compare the mark and name the honest option: continue, change focus, change tutor, or stop. Stopping is a real option and we will say so when it applies.

process.title: Add the core blocks at the school's deadlines
process.description: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay coaching goes in as short blocks placed at the school's own published checkpoints rather than as a standing hour. Up to three bonus points for a handful of sessions is the best ratio in the Diploma, and it does not disturb the weekly subject hour.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider page or rate study that published it, read in October 2026, and converted into the two-year figure a household actually commits to. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars rather than dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Allocation advice, not just a rate
whyPoints.description: The useful question in a six-subject programme is which two components to fund, and this page answers it with a method: conditional subjects first, two-grade gaps before one-grade gaps, unprepared 20 per cent components before general revision, and the core before almost anything else.

whyPoints.title: No package required, ever
whyPoints.description: Sessions are paid as they happen. There are no credits to expire, no cancellation penalty and no block to buy before a first lesson. In a market where package expiry is the most common way families lose money, that is a structural difference rather than a promotion.

whyPoints.title: Online, so the rate buys teaching rather than travel
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. On published figures, roughly AED 60 to AED 150 of an in-home hourly rate is the journey rather than the teaching.

whyPoints.title: A measurable six-session review
whyPoints.description: The component being targeted and its current mark are written down before the second lesson, and compared at six sessions. Four outcomes are named in advance, one of which is stopping. Agreeing the measure at the start is what prevents an arrangement running for a year on inertia.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line and the legal position stated
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work, and produces no coursework, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. IB Gram claims no regulator or board accreditation, no UAE office, and no statistic it cannot evidence. The regulators appear here to explain what each governs.

faqs.question: Does filtering for an IB tutor near me in The Lakes cost us money?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. It raises the price, because Dubai in-home visits are published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor online, and the difference is travel. And it shrinks the pool: within twenty minutes of Hattan the number of tutors who teach Higher Level Chemistry to DP2 standard is small, and some are already committed. A Diploma student needs three Higher Level specialists, and three specialists rarely live in one neighbourhood. Distance is the one search filter that adds cost without adding marks.

faqs.question: What does two years of Diploma tutoring actually add up to?
faqs.answer: For one weekly hour across roughly thirty-six teaching weeks a year: about AED 10,800 at the AED 150 band, about AED 14,400 at AED 200, about AED 19,440 at the AED 270 figure one agency publishes, about AED 32,400 at the AED 450 upper specialist band, and about AED 46,800 at the AED 650 top published rate. Two subjects doubles each of those. Those are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, converted into the figure a household commits to, which nobody in this market publishes.

faqs.question: Three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels. Where should the budget go?
faqs.answer: Four filters, in order. Fund subjects where the grade is a condition of an offer before subjects where it is only a grade. Prefer a two-grade gap in a conditional subject to chasing a 7 from a 6, because the top marks cost the most for the least movement. Target an unprepared component worth around 20 per cent of a grade rather than general revision of a paper already half known. And fund the core, because Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three bonus points for a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for help with a component worth a fifth of the grade?
faqs.answer: It is usually the best purchase available. Most Diploma subjects place around 20 per cent of the grade in internally assessed coursework, and Higher Level mathematics adds a Paper 3 worth a further fifth that most students meet for the first time in a mock. Both are written once, late, and often without feedback against the published criteria. Three or four well-timed sessions on an unprepared fifth of a grade moves more marks per dirham than a term of general revision. Check the weightings in your child's own subject guide, since the IB revises them by cycle.

faqs.question: How many points are Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay worth together?
faqs.answer: Up to three bonus points toward the Diploma total, awarded from the combination of the two grades. Neither has a daily timetabled lesson, which is why both are systematically underprepared and why they are the cheapest marks in the programme. The Extended Essay fails in predictable places - an unanswerable research question, a methodology producing opinion, a draft never checked against the criteria - and each is a single conversation at a known checkpoint. The school publishes those checkpoints, so the coaching can be booked in advance rather than in a panic.

faqs.question: What should I ask about replacement if a tutor leaves Dubai mid-programme?
faqs.answer: Ask it before you start, in writing. Dubai is a transient market and an in-home arrangement generally ends when the tutor's residency does, with no replacement attached. Platform and agency models vary: some rematch within days, some depend entirely on the contract, and some offer nothing. In a two-year programme the cost of rebuilding an arrangement mid-DP2 is a lost term, which is larger than any hourly difference. A video arrangement survives a relocation on either side, which is a practical rather than a marketing advantage.

faqs.question: Six students in a group class at a lower rate. Does that arithmetic work?
faqs.answer: Only when everybody in the room is losing the same marks. A group class delivers one explanation at one pace with no per-student diagnosis, which suits a cohort revising the same paper to the same deadline. It does not suit a student losing marks on command terms while the person beside them is losing them on calculation, and in that case the per-mark cost ends up higher than one-to-one despite the lower per-head rate. Ask what diagnostic the centre runs before placing students, and whether the group is grouped by weakness or by availability.

faqs.question: What are the extras that sit outside the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Five recur. Materials, where some providers charge for a workbook duplicating what the school already issued. Progress reports, billed per report by some agencies. Travel, sometimes charged separately from the hour in an in-home arrangement. Replacement, where the policy if a tutor leaves ranges from an immediate rematch to nothing at all. And VAT, which should be stated rather than assumed - the UAE treatment of tuition fees is a Federal Tax Authority matter, so ask any provider directly whether its quote includes it and keep the answer.

faqs.question: How do I work out whether an hour of tutoring was worth what we paid?
faqs.answer: Agree the measure before the second lesson: which component is targeted and what the current mark on it is. Set written work to be marked between sessions. At six sessions, compare the mark on that component. A mark counts as evidence; a report that the student is more confident does not, because confidence rises in the first three sessions of every arrangement regardless. If the mark has not moved there are four honest options - change the component, change the format, change the tutor, or stop - and all four are better than paying on inertia.

faqs.question: What does it cost to sit IB examinations as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The fee is set by the school or examination centre that accepts external candidates rather than published centrally, so no figure appears here because none was verified for this page. Ask two or three centres directly and compare, because the range is wide. Entry has to be arranged through a centre willing to take private candidates, and availability for Diploma subjects is narrower than for IGCSE. No tutoring provider arranges, accelerates or guarantees an entry; what a tutor can do is prepare the specific papers for that sitting.

faqs.question: If my child resits a subject in a later session, what does that add in cost?
faqs.answer: Less than a year of weekly support, if it is planned properly. A resit is a focused block on specific papers rather than a full re-teach, so it is usually a short run of sessions aimed at the components where marks were lost. The questions that actually determine the cost are administrative: how many subjects, whether coursework carries forward, and what the school will support. Those belong with the IB coordinator rather than with a tutoring provider, because the answers differ by school and each one has a fee attached.

faqs.question: Our tutor is inexpensive but the grades have not moved. What should we change?
faqs.answer: Change the diagnosis before you change the price. Cheap and ineffective is usually a targeting failure rather than a quality one: an hour of general revision at any rate produces little, while an hour aimed at an unprepared 20 per cent component produces marks even at the lower band. Ask the tutor to name the component they are working on and the current mark. If they cannot, the arrangement has no measure and no amount of extra spending will fix that. If they can and it has not moved in six sessions, change the tutor.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level tutoring priced above Standard Level in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Partly content and partly scarcity. Higher Level courses carry additional material and, in several subjects, an extra paper - Higher Level mathematics adds a Paper 3 worth 20 per cent, Economics and Business Management each add a third paper. That requires a teacher who has taught to that level recently, and in Dubai that pool is smaller than the Standard Level pool. The published evidence of the step is visible across boards too: one agency lists AED 150 an hour for IGCSE support against AED 200 for IB.

faqs.question: Can we drop from two subjects to one and still make progress?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is often the better arrangement rather than a compromise. One hour a week with marked work between sessions produces a complete feedback cycle; two hours split across two subjects with nothing in between produces two incomplete ones. If both subjects genuinely need support, alternating them fortnightly with written work set in the off week keeps two cycles running at one subject's monthly cost. What does not work is two subjects, two hours and no marked work, which is the most expensive version of homework supervision available.

faqs.question: Does the price depend on whether the tutor lives in Dubai?

A UAE-based tutor working online is priced within the same AED 150 to AED 300 band as the broader market, while the in-home premium of AED 180 to AED 500 applies only where someone is travelling. Where no UAE-based specialist is free for a narrow Diploma subject, a tutor based elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time may be proposed, and we say so before anything is agreed. intro.heading: Why proximity is the one thing that stopped mattering
paragraphs: The Meadows sits inside Emirates Living, behind gates, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, with The Springs on one side and Emirates Hills on the other. It is a villa community built around school runs. The practical consequence is that most households here already spend forty to seventy minutes a day in a car on school logistics before anyone opens a textbook. Adding a tutor who has to be driven to, or who has to drive, is adding to the wrong column.

A proximity search behaves as though tutoring were a plumbing call-out. It is not. Dubai has 227 private schools running seventeen different curricula, and the IB accounts for roughly 7% of private-school enrolment in the emirate. That is a small slice of a large market, and within it the specialists are thinly spread. A tutor who can teach Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and has sat with the Paper 3 problem-solving format is not a commodity available within every gated community. Searching for an IB tutor near me in The Meadows and accepting whoever appears closest trades the thing that matters for the thing that is easy to measure.

The honest answer to the search is this. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Meadows students happen one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen, a writing surface both people can draw on, and the student's own marked scripts open in front of both of them. The lesson starts at the hour it is booked because nobody is in traffic on Al Khail Road.

That change does something a local tutor cannot. It separates the choice of tutor from the geography of Dubai. A Meadows student taking Chemistry HL, Maths AA SL and History HL can have three different specialists, each matched to that subject, instead of one generalist who happens to live in The Views. It also makes the second weekly session possible. One in-home visit a week is a logistics decision; two online sessions a week is a timetable decision, and timetables are what move grades.

This page is written from the school run outwards. It covers which schools children in The Meadows and the surrounding Emirates Living communities actually attend, what time those days end, when a session can realistically start, what the Dubai market charges for IB support in dirhams, what KHDA requires alongside the Diploma, and where the line sits between legitimate tutoring and work that has to be the student's own. Every regulatory fact is attributed to the authority that published it. The Meadows runs on a school-run rhythm that decides which evening slots are realistically usable, so the timetable here is built from that rather than from an idealised week.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: The IB is four programmes, not one, and a child in The Meadows may move through three of them inside a ten-minute drive. Each has a different assessment logic, so each needs a different kind of help. Below is what each programme asks of a student and what it means for families in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes, and the final year ends in the Exhibition, a student-led inquiry presented to the school community. Assessment is continuous and teacher-led, which means a parent rarely sees a mark they can compare to anything. The useful tutoring here is not exam technique. It is reading fluency, number sense, written structure and the habit of asking a question that can actually be investigated.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates Living has several PYP settings within a short drive, and Emirates International School - Meadows runs the programme inside The Meadows itself. Parents here often arrive at tutoring in Year 5 or Year 6, when the question of secondary entry appears. Online sessions suit this age in 40-minute blocks rather than an hour, scheduled before dinner rather than after it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria, each marked out of 8, which are converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries rather than by percentage. A student can produce confident work and still see a 4, because a criterion was addressed thinly. MYP Year 5 adds the Personal Project, a long independent piece with its own criteria and a process journal. Interdisciplinary units are assessed too, and they are where organised students lose marks for the first time.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where most Meadows families first ask for help, usually in Year 9 or 10 as subject choices for the Diploma come into view. The criterion-based system is the sticking point: parents who grew up with percentages find a 5 out of 8 unreadable. A tutor's first job with a Meadows MYP student is usually to read the school's own criterion descriptors aloud and translate them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1-7, giving 42 points, plus up to 3 more from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, for a maximum of 45. Every subject carries internal assessment worth between 20% and 30% of the grade, marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The Diploma is a two-year machine with deadlines that stack, and most of the damage happens in the first term of Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in The Meadows commonly travel to Emirates Hills, Al Barsha or Al Sufouh for school, so the day is long before any tutoring starts. Dubai schools sit the May examination session. Two 60-minute online sessions a week, placed on different evenings, consistently work better for these households than one 120-minute block at the weekend, because Higher Level content needs sleep between exposures.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development portfolio, service learning and a personal and professional skills course. It is examined in the DP subjects and internally assessed in the rest. Fewer Dubai schools offer it, so a student taking it often finds that general IB tutoring misses the point: the DP courses need DP-standard teaching while the core components need project discipline.
programmes.countryNote: CP students near The Meadows are a minority, and that is exactly why a proximity search fails them. A local tutor is unlikely to have seen a reflective project before. Online matching across a national pool is the only realistic route to someone who has, and the reflective project is the component where that experience shows most quickly.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: A Meadows Diploma student sits six subjects, and the two or three that need outside help are rarely the ones a parent expects. These are the subjects most often requested by families in Emirates Living, described by what the assessment actually asks rather than by what the subject is called.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. At SL, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any gap in manipulation that technology had been hiding. At HL, Paper 3 is a long investigative problem built in stages, and students who have only practised short questions stall at part (c). The Exploration is worth 20% and is marked against five criteria.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed throughout, so marks move to modelling, interpretation and statistical reasoning. The common failure is a correct calculator output with no justification attached, or a regression quoted without comment on its validity. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference, and the step up from SL is larger than the course titles suggest.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current guide the content is organised into themes rather than topics and options have gone. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response and carries the larger weighting. Most lost marks are mathematical rather than conceptual: unit conversion, significant figures and failing to state the assumption a model relies on.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The guide is built around Structure and Reactivity, with HL extending both. Students who learn chemistry as vocabulary do well on recall and badly on Paper 2, where a question asks for an explanation of why a trend exists. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations are the two places a Meadows tutor is most often asked to start.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of content makes Biology look like a memory subject, and that misreading costs the grade. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, evaluate and justify each want a different shape of answer. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments are where strong students are separated from the rest, and they can be practised directly.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed oral and written components plus Paper 1, an unseen guided textual analysis under time pressure. The skill is not interpretation but selection: choosing three features of a text worth 1,200 words. HL adds the essay on works studied. Students in Dubai international schools often read widely and still write essays with no line of argument.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is source-based with a prescribed subject, Paper 2 is comparative essay work across topics, and HL adds Paper 3 on a regional option with far greater depth. The Historical Investigation is internally assessed and has a strict word allowance. Marks are lost on source evaluation that describes provenance instead of using it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry the explanation, and a diagram drawn without axes labelled or equilibria marked scores nothing regardless of the prose around it. HL adds policy calculation and a quantitative paper. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries built on published news articles, and the usual error is an article too broad to support a single syllabus concept.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to a real organisation is the assessed skill. Students who answer with textbook theory and no company context sit in the middle bands. HL adds depth in operations and finance and a longer research project. The tools - Ansoff, force field analysis, break-even - are only worth marks when they produce a judgement.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be used as evidence, not recited, and the examiner wants the limitation of the study as much as the finding. HL extends into additional approaches and research methodology. The internal assessment is an experimental study replication with a formal report structure, and statistical treatment is where most students need an hour of direct teaching.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK produces an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, and together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to 3 points. Students treat it as an opinion piece and lose marks for unsupported assertion. Useful tutoring here is argument structure: claim, counterclaim, example, implication, each tied to a knowledge question.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a subject the student chooses, supervised inside the school. The research question decides the grade before any writing happens: too broad and the essay describes, too narrow and there is no argument. A tutor's legitimate role is question shaping, method discussion and feedback on the student's own drafts.

Emirates Living is a cluster of connected communities that share gates, schools and school buses, and a tutoring timetable that works in The Meadows usually works next door. These are the neighbourhoods whose families sit in the same evening traffic.

regions.note: Nine numbered sub-communities of villas inside Emirates Living, with Emirates International School - Meadows on the doorstep. Most households run on cars; the nearest Red Line stations sit outside the gates. Evening sessions from 16:45 onwards are the realistic window.

regions.note: Townhouses immediately adjacent, sharing the Springs Souk and the same access roads. Dubai British School Emirates Hills sits in Springs 3, so a large share of Springs and Meadows children are on the British track with IGCSE before any IB decision arises.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Lower-density villas on the Emirates Hills side, with a shorter run to Al Sufouh and Al Barsha schools. Families here more often have one child in an IB school and another in a British one, which makes a single generalist tutor an awkward fit.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large plots and the longest internal drives in the cluster. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills anchors the IB offer nearby. Households here are the most likely to have tried an in-home arrangement first and to have found the travel charge difficult to justify.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns when you type it from a Meadows villa
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you get three kinds of result. There are directory listings that rank by paid placement rather than distance. There are agency pages that name Dubai but publish no address and no rate. And there are independent tutors advertising a service area that happens to include Emirates Living. None of these results tells you the thing you want to know, which is whether the person has taught the specific subject at the specific level your child is sitting.

The research behind this page looked at the pages currently ranking for queries like this one across the UAE. Three of six published no price at all. The two that did quoted United States dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. Five of six carried no comparison table of any kind. The best page in the set ran to roughly 2,300 words and named no neighbourhood. A search that looks local is being answered by pages that are not local at all.

The second problem is availability. IB Higher Level specialists are scarce in absolute terms, not just locally. A community of villas, however well served by schools, contains a handful of people qualified to teach Chemistry HL and almost nobody who has supervised a Historical Investigation. Distance is a filter that removes the specialists first, because specialists are rare and rare things are rarely nearby. Drop the distance filter and the pool becomes national instead of residential.

sections.heading: The Meadows school day, counted backwards from the bus
paragraphs: Dubai private schools finish earlier than many parents arriving from Europe expect, and secondary finishes later than primary within the same school. Add the bus route through Emirates Living, add a co-curricular commitment two days a week, and the gap between the last lesson of the school day and the first possible tutoring session narrows to something quite specific. Planning a session at 16:00 for a Year 13 student who is bussed back from Al Barsha is planning a session that will be missed.

Confirm your own school's published timings rather than relying on an average, because they differ by school and by year group, and several Dubai schools run a shorter day on one weekday. The shape, though, is consistent: primary children are home first and have energy until roughly 18:00, secondary students are home later and work better after a break and food than immediately on arrival. A Diploma student asked to think hard at 16:15 after a 06:30 start is being set up to fail.

The practical rule we use with Emirates Living families is that the session slot should be the second thing fixed, after the school day and before anything else. Fixtures, Arabic support classes at school, and the drive to a sibling's activity all compete for the same two hours. A slot that survives for a full term is worth more than a slightly better slot that collapses in week three.

sections.heading: Which schools The Meadows actually feeds, and what that means for tutoring
paragraphs: The cluster around The Meadows carries both of Dubai's dominant tracks at once. The British curriculum is the largest in the emirate by enrolment at around 37%, with Indian at 26% and United States at 14%, and the IB sits at roughly 7%. Inside Emirates Living that national pattern compresses into a few hundred metres: an IB World School inside The Meadows, a large British school in The Springs, and two more within a ten-minute drive. Siblings in one villa are often sitting criterion-marked MYP assessments and Cambridge IGCSE papers in the same fortnight.

This has a direct consequence for anyone hiring one tutor for a household. The MYP wants criteria addressed explicitly in a task designed by the school; IGCSE wants a mark scheme answered in the command words of a specific syllabus code. A tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in the other, and the parent discovers this in week four rather than week one. Matching by programme rather than by postcode avoids an expensive detour.

KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes outcomes on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Those reports are worth reading for the subject-level commentary rather than the headline band: inspectors comment on attainment and progress by subject and phase, which is often the first written confirmation a parent gets that a particular department is struggling. We do not restate any school's rating here, because a rating should be read from KHDA's own publication rather than from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: What IB support costs around Emirates Living, in dirhams
paragraphs: Most pages answering this query refuse the question. Of the UAE competitor pages examined for this project, three published no figure at all and one has a frequently asked question that asks the price and then declines to answer it. The two that did publish quoted dollars. A Dubai parent needs a dirham band, so here is one, drawn from providers' own published rate cards and from a published Dubai tutoring cost table, surveyed in October 2026.

Read the table as the market, not as our price list. These are the figures other providers put in public, and they vary by tier rather than by neighbourhood. Nobody charges a Meadows premium for an online lesson; what varies between communities is the in-home figure, because that number carries travel. A tutor crossing Dubai at 17:30 is charging for the journey whether the invoice itemises it or not, and at Emirates Living distances that is commonly a quarter to a third of the hour's value.

Two further costs are routinely left out of comparisons. The first is the cancellation cost of a plan that depends on a car: a single evening of heavy traffic removes a session that has already been paid for. The second is the cost of the wrong match. Six sessions with a generalist who re-teaches the textbook is not cheaper than four with a specialist who diagnoses a component, even at double the hourly figure. On IB Gram the trial lesson exists for exactly that reason: one lesson in one subject, before any payment, so the match is tested before it is bought.

For context on the household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is one of the few education costs in Dubai that did move this year, which makes it worth costing properly rather than by instinct.

sections.heading: The Diploma core, and where a Meadows family loses time
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service run alongside the six subjects for two years, and together the first two contribute up to 3 points on the 45-point scale. Three points decides university offers. It is also the part of the Diploma that no subject tutor is automatically responsible for, which is why it is the part that drifts. A student can be well supported in Maths and Physics and still arrive at Year 13 with an Extended Essay research question that cannot carry 4,000 words.

The Extended Essay fails or succeeds at the question. A question that is too broad produces description; one that is too narrow produces an essay with nothing to argue. Supervision happens inside the school and belongs there. What a tutor can legitimately contribute is pressure on the question, discussion of method and sources, and written feedback on drafts the student has produced. Authorship stays with the student at every stage, and any provider offering otherwise is offering an IB malpractice investigation.

TOK is the component students most often dismiss and most often lose marks on. The exhibition asks for three objects tied to a prompt, and the essay answers one of six prescribed titles. Both are marked on the quality of the knowledge argument, not on opinion. The useful intervention is structural: a claim, a counterclaim that is actually in tension with it, a real example from a named area of knowledge, and a statement of what follows. That is teachable in four sessions.

CAS is not graded but it is a completion requirement, and an incomplete CAS portfolio blocks the Diploma regardless of points. Meadows students with heavy sports commitments usually have the activity strand covered and the service and reflection strands thin. A reminder in November of Year 12 is worth more than a rescue in March of Year 13.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor must not step over
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries internal assessment, and every piece of it is submitted with an authenticity declaration from both student and supervisor. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice, with consequences that reach as far as the loss of the Diploma. This is not a theoretical risk in this market. Our research found a provider in the UAE search results selling finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is a product no honest tutoring service can sell and no parent should buy.

The permitted territory is wide and useful. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for in plain words, interrogate a research question, discuss whether a method will produce data worth analysing, model a worked analysis on a different data set, read a student's own draft and say where the argument thins, and teach the referencing convention. All of that raises marks and none of it touches authorship.

The forbidden territory is narrow and absolute. The tutor supplies no sentences, no paragraphs, no data, no diagrams and no corrections typed into the student's file. Feedback arrives as comments and questions for the student to act on, in their own words, in their own document. If a tutor has been near the keyboard, the declaration the student signs is no longer true.

There is a related rule parents should know. Abu Dhabi's education authority has set professional-ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the national private tuition permit carries a code of conduct in the same spirit. Treat an offer of private lessons from your child's own classroom teacher as a problem rather than an advantage, and verify the current rule with the relevant authority before acting on it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the part of a Dubai IB education that international tutoring pages ignore completely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA set its current requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with an April 2026 date for schools whose year begins in April. A family can be entirely focused on Higher Level Physics and be caught out by an Arabic report instead.

KHDA's requirements are specific enough to matter. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and the Moral, Social and Cultural strand in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. There is also a hard limit on content: using different or additional material for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Any tutor working on Arabic or Islamic Education must therefore work with the school's own prescribed material rather than a parallel scheme of their own invention.

Practically, Arabic as an additional language is where most non-Arab Meadows families need support, and it is a long game rather than an examination sprint. Twenty minutes of spoken practice three times a week moves a child further than a ninety-minute session once a fortnight, and the school's own reporting cycle is the right place to check whether it is working.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two details are worth knowing before you ask a tutor about it. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who tells you it is expensive or difficult has not applied for it. And the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Holding the permit is a baseline of compliance rather than a mark of subject expertise.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source, so we do not quote one. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is why no honest online platform should describe itself using KHDA permit language.

Ask a prospective tutor three questions. Do you hold the private tuition work permit, and when does it expire? Which syllabus and board have you taught, by code? Can you show a marked piece of student work with your own feedback on it, with identifying details removed? The third question is the most revealing and almost nobody asks it.

sections.heading: Getting started from The Meadows, including what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the school, the programme, the subjects and levels, and what the last report or marked paper actually said. We propose a tutor matched to those components and offer a trial lesson in one subject before any payment is taken. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial and we propose a different person rather than defending the first one. If it is right, we fix a slot that fits your weekday and hold it.

Here is the part other pages leave out. Coverage is not infinite. For a common subject at Standard Level the match is usually quick. For a narrow Higher Level combination, a less commonly taught language, or a niche internal assessment, there may be no suitable tutor free in the window you want. When that happens we say so and give you the honest options: a different slot, a short wait, or a different component to start on while the right person becomes available. What we do not do is place a generalist in a specialist's chair and let you find out in February.

Progress is tracked against the only measures that mean anything in the IB: criterion marks on internal assessment, component-level performance on past papers under timed conditions, and the school's own reporting. We do not promise a grade and no honest provider can, because the grade depends on a student's work in an examination room nobody controls. What can be promised is a diagnosis you can read, a plan with dates on it, and a tutor who knows the component.

A last note on timing. Dubai schools sit the May examination session, so the useful work happens in the fifteen months before it rather than the final six weeks. Confirm the exact session dates with your school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site; we deliberately publish no IB examination date here because we have not been able to verify one from the IB directly.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: A message saying Physics HL is not enough to match well. A message saying Physics HL, Paper 2 extended response, last mock 4, internal assessment due in six weeks is enough to match precisely. The more precisely you describe where the marks are going, the shorter the path to the right tutor.

process.title: We match against the syllabus, not the map
process.description: Matching runs on who has taught that programme, that subject and that level, and who has worked on that assessed component. Location is not a filter because lessons are delivered over live video. That is the single change that makes a specialist available to an Emirates Living household at all.

process.title: Trial lesson in one subject, before payment
process.description: One lesson, one subject, booked before anything is paid. The point is a diagnosis you can read afterwards: what the student can do, where the marks are going, and what the first four sessions would target. A trial that produces only enthusiasm has told you nothing.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school day
process.description: We set the slot after your school's finish time and your fixtures, not before them. For most Meadows secondary students that means 16:45, 17:30 or 19:00 Gulf Standard Time. A slot that survives a whole term beats a theoretically better slot that collapses in week three.

process.title: Review against criteria at week six
process.description: At six weeks we look at criterion marks, timed past-paper components and the school's own feedback, and decide whether to continue, change the target or change the tutor. Reviewing on a fixed date stops a plan drifting for a term because nobody wanted an awkward conversation.

whyPoints.title: The specialist you need is rarely the closest
whyPoints.description: Higher Level specialists are scarce nationally. A twenty-minute radius around Emirates Living removes them first, because rare things are rarely nearby. Online delivery replaces a residential pool with a national one, and the difference shows up in the quality of the diagnosis in the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: No travel charge, no traffic cancellation
whyPoints.description: An in-home arrangement in Dubai prices the journey into the hour, and one heavy evening on Al Khail Road removes a session already paid for. A video lesson starts at the time it was booked. Over a two-year Diploma that difference is measured in whole terms of contact time.

whyPoints.title: Every number on this page has a source
whyPoints.description: The dirham bands come from providers' own published rate cards and a published Dubai cost table surveyed in October 2026. The regulatory facts come from KHDA, MoHRE and u.ae. Where we could not verify something, including IB examination dates, we say so rather than filling the gap.

whyPoints.title: Authorship stays with the student
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment support means teaching content, explaining criteria, interrogating a research question and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. No sentences, data or diagrams come from the tutor. In a market where finished Internal Assessments are sold openly, this is a position worth stating plainly.

whyPoints.title: Honest coverage, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: If no suitable specialist is free for a narrow Higher Level combination, we tell you and offer real options rather than substituting a generalist. A disclosed gap costs one conversation. An undisclosed one costs a term of fees and a student's confidence in the subject.

whyPoints.title: Built for a household, not a single booking
whyPoints.description: Siblings in Emirates Living are often on different programmes at different schools. Separate specialists on one shared calendar keeps the administration to a single timetable, and the per-hour figure does not multiply a travel charge across three bookings.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in The Meadows, or will the lesson be online?
faqs.answer: The lesson is online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Sessions for Meadows students are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and the student's own marked work open in front of both people. The reason is not cost. It is that a Higher Level specialist in a given subject is scarce nationally, so filtering by a twenty-minute radius around Emirates Living removes exactly the people you were searching for. You get the specialist instead of the neighbour.

faqs.question: Which IB and British schools do children in The Meadows and Emirates Living usually attend?
faqs.answer: Emirates International School - Meadows sits inside the community and runs the PYP, MYP and Diploma. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is the other main IB option nearby. On the British side, Dubai British School Emirates Hills is in The Springs and Regent International School is in The Greens, with Dubai College in Al Sufouh and the Al Barsha cluster a little further out. All are regulated by KHDA. Programme offerings change, so confirm with the school directly. We name these as neighbourhood context and claim no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can a Year 13 student in The Meadows realistically start a weekday session?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student bussed back from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, 16:00 is usually too early and the realistic windows are 16:45, 17:30 or 19:00 Gulf Standard Time. Primary children can work earlier and lose focus later, so the 15:30 to 16:15 slot suits them better. Check your own school's published finish time rather than an average, because Dubai schools differ by year group and several run a shorter day once a week. The slot that matters is the one that survives a full term, not the one that looks best on paper in September.

faqs.question: Does driving to a tutor in Dubai Marina really cost us a whole evening?
faqs.answer: Roughly two hours, for one hour of teaching. Dubai Marina, JBR and JLT sit fifteen to twenty-five minutes from Emirates Living off-peak and longer at 18:00, so a round trip plus a 60-minute lesson consumes about an hour and fifty minutes. Al Barsha or Jumeirah pushes that to two hours; Mirdif or Deira past two and a half. The practical effect is that only one subject fits per evening and a second weekly session becomes unrealistic. A video lesson consumes sixty minutes, which is why two subjects can share one evening.

faqs.question: My child is at Emirates International School - Meadows. Will the tutor follow that school's own deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first thing we ask for. The school's internal assessment deadlines, mock windows and reporting dates are what the plan is built backwards from, because those are the dates that actually exist for your child. A tutor working to a generic syllabus timeline will be a month out of step by the second term. Send the assessment calendar, the last report and one marked script at the start. The marked script is the most useful document in the set, because it shows the fault signature rather than the summary.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student in Emirates Living usually need?
faqs.answer: Two 60-minute sessions a week in the weak subject, placed on separate evenings, is the pattern that works most often. Splitting the week matters more than the total: Higher Level content needs sleep between exposures, and a single 120-minute block at the weekend produces less retention than two shorter sittings. Add a defined task of 30 to 40 minutes between sessions, marked against the real criteria. Where two subjects need help, two separate specialists on one shared calendar beats one generalist covering both at a shallower level.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Maths HL and Chemistry HL for the same student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually a compromise. Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Chemistry at Higher Level are both specialist courses with their own assessed components, and the number of people genuinely strong in both is small. Where a single tutor can do it well, we will say so. More often we propose two specialists sharing one calendar, which costs no more per hour online and produces a sharper diagnosis in each subject. The convenience of one person is real but it is bought with depth.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for the Higher Level subject we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Coverage is not infinite, and a narrow Higher Level combination, a less commonly taught language or an unusual internal assessment can mean no suitable specialist is free in the window you want. When that happens the options are an alternative slot, a short wait for the right person, or starting on a different component in the meantime. What we will not do is put a generalist in a specialist's chair and let you discover the mismatch in February, which is the standard failure in this market.

faqs.question: Do we need a dedicated study space in a Meadows villa for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Not a dedicated room, but a fixed place. What matters is a desk at the right height, a door that can be closed, a wired or strong connection, headphones with a microphone, and paper. The student should be able to write and be seen writing, because a tutor who can watch the working can catch the error at the point it happens. Villas in The Meadows usually have the space; apartment households in The Views or The Greens often do better with headphones and a shared family rule about the hour than with a new piece of furniture.

faqs.question: Can Meadows sessions move to post-iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. Dubai school days shorten during Ramadan and the useful hours of the evening move, so a slot that worked in February stops working. Most families shift to a post-Iftar session or move the work to late morning on non-school days. Internal assessment deadlines rarely move to match, which is why Ramadan is the period where plans quietly fall behind. Agreeing the revised slot before the month starts, rather than improvising in week one, is what keeps the sequence of sessions intact.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working in Dubai need a permit, and should I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by MoHRE, which lists Private Tutor Licensing as a service on its own site with a two-working-day completion time. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors around Emirates Living charge per hour in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rate cards surveyed in October 2026 put generalist online tutors at AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and a premium examiner tier above AED 500. In-home visits sit higher, commonly AED 180 to 500, because the travel is inside the hour. Monthly packages seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Those are market figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without breaking IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can press on the research question until it is answerable in 4,000 words, discuss whether a method will generate usable evidence, teach the subject content the essay depends on, explain the assessment criteria in plain words, and give written feedback on drafts the student has produced. The tutor supplies no sentences, no data and no typed corrections, and supervision remains with the school. Any provider offering a finished Extended Essay is offering an IB malpractice case against your child, whatever it is called on the invoice.

faqs.question: Do you cover Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Support has to follow the school's prescribed material, because using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects. For non-Arab families the usual need is Arabic as an additional language, where short frequent spoken practice beats long infrequent sessions.

faqs.question: What does the trial lesson actually involve for a Meadows family?
faqs.answer: One lesson, in one subject, before any payment is taken. The tutor works through a piece of the student's own recent work, usually a marked script or a current assessment task, and uses it to identify where the marks are going rather than covering new content. Afterwards you get a short written diagnosis: what the student can already do, the specific fault pattern, and what the first four sessions would target. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose a different tutor rather than arguing for the first one.

faqs.question: How will we know the tutoring is working, without being in the room?
faqs.answer: Three measures, all of which exist independently of the tutor. First, criterion marks on internal assessment tasks set by the school, which are the IB's own instrument. Second, component-level performance on past papers sat under timed conditions, tracked per paper rather than as a single percentage. Third, the school's own reports and parent meetings. We review all three at week six and decide whether to continue, change the target or change the tutor. No honest provider promises a grade, because the grade is decided in an examination room nobody controls.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper, not the map
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.closingBody: If you have reached this page from a search for an IB tutor near me in The Meadows, the most useful thing you own is not a radius. It is the last marked script your child brought home. Send that, the school, the subjects and the levels, and we will match a specialist to the component where the marks are going and offer a trial lesson in one subject before any payment. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in a slot built around your school day rather than around Al Khail Road. If the right specialist is not free, you will hear that too.

intro.heading: The real question is competence, not proximity
paragraphs: Nobody searching for a tutor near them actually wants a neighbour. They want somebody who will not waste the hour. The phrase near me is shorthand for a reasonable assumption: that a person physically close by can be checked, recommended by another parent, and relied on to turn up. It is a sensible instinct built up over years of finding piano teachers and swimming coaches, and it works badly for the IB Diploma for one reason. The Diploma is a small, specialised qualification, and the number of people who genuinely know a given subject at a given level inside any one Dubai community is very small.

Run the arithmetic. International Baccalaureate programmes account for roughly 7 per cent of private enrolment in Dubai, against 37 per cent on UK curricula. Within that minority, a Diploma student takes six subjects at two different levels, so the specialism you need is not an IB tutor but, say, a Higher Level Economics tutor who has marked internal assessments. Now restrict that to people who can be at a townhouse in Springs 7 by five o'clock on a weekday. The honest description of what remains is a handful of people, and whether any of them teaches your child's subject is largely luck.

That is the uncomfortable answer to the search, and it is better heard now than in week four. What families in The Springs usually discover, if they look locally and insist on proximity, is one of three outcomes: a tutor who knows the subject but not the Diploma, a tutor who knows the Diploma but not the subject at the level required, or a long wait. Each of those costs money and, more importantly, weeks.

The alternative is to drop the geographic constraint and keep every other one. IB Gram matches your child to a tutor chosen for the subject, the level and the assessment component in question, and the lesson happens one-to-one over live video on a Gulf Standard Time slot. IB Gram does not operate a UAE office and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than discovered later, because the comparison only works if it is honest.

The rest of this page is practical. It sets out the eight questions that distinguish somebody who knows the Diploma from somebody who has heard of it, what the Diploma actually contains so that you can judge the answers, which subjects are genuinely thin in this market and what happens when yours is one of them, what The Springs itself does to an evening timetable, what both delivery models cost with the sources named, and where the line sits on Internal Assessment and Extended Essay help.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: The Springs sits between a British-curriculum secondary and several IB continuum schools, so IB requests from these addresses span the whole programme. These are the four stages, with what they need from a tutor.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects drawn from the subject groups, studied at Higher or Standard Level, alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries internal assessment with a fixed weighting, and external examinations at the end of DP2. The load is less about individual difficulty than about simultaneous deadlines, which is what most families actually need help managing.
programmes.countryNote: Several IB World Schools sit within a short drive of The Springs, in Emirates Hills, The Meadows and along Al Sufouh. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new openings, so the local Diploma provision is expanding rather than static.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria in bands rather than by examination, with a Personal Project in MYP 5. For a family in The Springs the commonest MYP request is a bridge: a child moving from the British-curriculum route into an IB continuum school, or vice versa, who needs the assessment language of the new system explained.
programmes.countryNote: Because the British secondary inside Springs 3 and the IB continuum schools in Emirates Hills and The Meadows are minutes apart, switching sector mid-school happens here more often than in most Dubai catchments. That makes assessment translation, rather than content teaching, the first job in a lot of first lessons.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core components that run alongside the six subjects and generate most of the DP1 panic. The Extended Essay is an independent piece of research with a word limit; Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition and an essay; creativity, activity, service is not graded but must be completed. Deadlines for all three collide with subject internal assessments.
programmes.countryNote: Each school sets its own internal deadlines for these components, often months ahead of the IB's own. Those internal dates are the ones that govern your child's year, so ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's published timeline rather than working from anything found online, including this page.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into DP1
programmes.description: The transition request that arrives every July from this cluster. A student from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE brings strong examination technique and little experience of independent research. A student from MYP brings the reverse. A good bridge block teaches whichever of the two is missing, and it is far cheaper in August than in February of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of Dubai private enrolment, so most students entering a Dubai DP1 classroom arrive from IGCSE rather than from MYP. The predictable consequence is a cohort strong on timed papers and underprepared for the Extended Essay, which is exactly where DP1 support concentrates.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects most often requested from The Springs and the surrounding communities, with what each one demands of a tutor beyond knowing the material.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Diploma subject in this catchment. HL is a serious course and the Internal Assessment exploration trips up students who can do the mathematics but cannot frame a question worth exploring. A tutor needs to be fluent in both the content and the exploration criteria.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students heading away from engineering, and frequently misunderstood as the easier option. The modelling and statistical work is genuinely demanding, and the exploration has to use real data convincingly rather than decoratively.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers and a scientific investigation. The specialism a tutor needs is narrow: command of the current theme structure and of the data-analysis questions that come from the practical programme rather than the textbook.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around structure and reactivity, with quantitative work and mechanisms as the two reliable mark-losers. A tutor who cannot discuss command terms and what each one requires is teaching chemistry rather than teaching the assessment.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and marked on precision of expression. Students who revise by reading lose marks that students who write and get marked do not. The investigation requires a measurable variable, which is where many biology investigations fail before they start.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A popular choice in this catchment and one where internal assessment technique dominates the grade conversation. Commentaries have to apply theory to a recent article within a tight word limit, which is a skill entirely separate from understanding economics.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside economics and frequently confused with it. The internal assessment differs substantially between levels, and a tutor who has not read the current guide will prepare a student for the wrong task.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed partly through oral components, which students rarely practise properly. A tutor's most valuable contribution is often rehearsing an individual oral under timing rather than discussing the texts further.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Rewarding and demanding on study recall, where students need named research with enough detail to use as evidence rather than as decoration. The internal assessment is a replication study with its own strict conventions.

subjects.name: Arabic and Language B subjects
subjects.description: Thin specialisms in the private tutoring market, particularly at ab initio level. These are the subjects where a local search most often returns nothing usable, and where honest disclosure about availability matters most.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Students who treat it as an opinion piece score poorly; the marks are in the handling of knowledge claims and counterclaims with real examples.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research piece with a word limit and a supervisor at school. Outside support is legitimate only as process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafting; the research and the writing must be theirs.

sections.heading: Is there anyone near me who actually knows the IB? The honest answer
paragraphs: No, probably not, if near me means inside The Springs and the subject is anything other than mathematics or English. That is the answer and it is worth sitting with for a moment, because every page competing for this search avoids it. The reason is structural rather than a failure of the local market. The Diploma is a minority qualification in Dubai, taken by roughly 7 per cent of private school students against 37 per cent on UK curricula, and each of those students studies six subjects split across two levels.

So the thing being searched for is not an IB tutor. It is a Higher Level Economics tutor who has seen internal assessment commentaries marked, or a Standard Level Biology tutor fluent in the investigation criteria, or somebody who can supervise a History Extended Essay. Each of those is a narrow specialism. Restrict it further to people who can physically reach a townhouse in Springs 9 on a weekday evening and the pool is not small, it is close to empty for most subjects.

What a family actually finds, searching locally and insisting on proximity, falls into three patterns. The first is a subject graduate who has never taught the Diploma and does not know what the internal assessment is marked on; they will teach good economics and will not improve the grade much. The second is somebody familiar with the IB in general terms who is working two levels away from the one required. The third is a genuine specialist who is already fully booked, which leads to a wait the calendar cannot absorb.

The alternative is to keep every requirement except the geographic one. The subject, the level, the component, the hour and the language can all be held constant; only the drive is dropped. That is what online delivery buys, and it is the entire argument. IB Gram matches on subject and level and teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There is no UAE office, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address: home visits are an India-only service, which is also why this page can compare the two models without selling one of them.

sections.heading: Eight questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the Diploma
paragraphs: Since you cannot verify a tutor by meeting them at the school gate, verify them by asking. These eight questions take ten minutes, work equally well on an agency or an individual, and separate genuine Diploma knowledge from general subject competence with unusual reliability. A good answer is specific and offered without hesitation. A bad answer is general, or it changes the subject to experience and enthusiasm.

The questions are deliberately about assessment rather than content, because content knowledge is the easy part. A subject graduate knows the economics. What they may not know is how many commentaries the internal assessment requires, what the word limit is, how the criteria are weighted, what the school's internal deadline looks like, and what a tutor is permitted to do with a draft. Those five facts determine whether an hour of tutoring is useful or merely pleasant.

Two of the questions are about honesty rather than knowledge, and they are the most informative of the eight. Asking what a tutor will not do with an Internal Assessment should produce a clear, confident boundary, not an offer. Asking about the MoHRE private tuition work permit should produce a straightforward answer, because the permit is granted free of charge for two years and a working tutor should know their own position. Hesitation on either is the signal to walk away.

One further note on how to use the list. Ask all eight in a single conversation rather than spreading them across a week, because the value is in the pattern of the answers rather than in any one of them. A tutor who is strong on four and vague on the other four is usually strong on the subject and weak on the Diploma, which is the commonest profile in this market and the hardest for a parent to detect any other way.
