sections.heading: What the Diploma actually contains, so you can judge the answers
paragraphs: To use the questions above you need a working picture of the programme. A Diploma student takes six subjects drawn across the subject groups, studying some at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level. Alongside those sit three core components: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, and creativity, activity, service. Each of the six subjects carries internal assessment, marked at school against published criteria and moderated externally, with external examinations at the end of the second year.

The feature that distinguishes the Diploma from the systems around it is not difficulty in any single subject. It is simultaneity. A DP1 student is carrying six syllabuses, an Extended Essay research question, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition and a service commitment at the same time, with internal deadlines set by the school that cluster in the same few weeks. Families who think their child has a chemistry problem frequently have a scheduling problem, and the two require entirely different help.

That has a direct consequence for tutoring. The first useful act is often not teaching at all; it is laying the school's published internal deadlines on a single sheet and seeing where the collisions are. A tutor who asks for that timeline in the first conversation is thinking about the year. A tutor who starts teaching content in the first thirty minutes may be excellent at the subject and is not yet looking at the problem.

One caution on dates, which matters because this page is read by families planning around them. Dubai IB schools predominantly sit the May session. No specific IB examination or results date is published on this page, because such dates could not be verified from the IB's own site during research. Confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before building a revision plan around it, and treat any tutoring page quoting IB dates with appropriate caution, including the ones that sound confident.

sections.heading: The subjects where a local search genuinely fails, and what happens then
paragraphs: Availability is the thing nobody in this market publishes. Every competitor page implies that any subject can be covered immediately, and none of them discloses a limit. That is a straightforward trust problem, because the limits are real and a parent finds out about them after paying rather than before.

So here is the position stated plainly. Mathematics at both levels and both courses, the three sciences, English A, economics and business management are well covered at evening Gulf Standard Time slots, and a match in those subjects is usually a matter of a few working days. Psychology, geography, history and global politics are covered but thinner, particularly at Higher Level and particularly in the weeks before a session. Language B and ab initio subjects other than the largest are genuinely thin. Arabic at ab initio level, several of the less common language options, music, theatre and film are the subjects where a request may not be fillable at the hour you want.

What happens when yours is one of the thin ones depends on the subject. For a written subject or a language where the work is reading, drafting and discussion, a specialist outside the UAE working on a Gulf Standard Time slot is usually a good solution and is offered as exactly that, with the arrangement described rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number. For a component-heavy subject where timing matters, the fallback is narrower, and sometimes the honest answer is no.

An honest no is worth more than it sounds. If the specialist is not available, the useful alternatives are often adjacent: technique work that transfers across papers, or support in a different subject where a recoverable mark actually exists. A family told in week one that their child's Higher Level theatre request cannot be met, and offered English A support instead, keeps their money and their weeks. A family told in week four has lost both.

sections.heading: What The Springs itself does to an evening timetable
paragraphs: This community has a genuine practical advantage that the villa districts nearby do not, and it is worth naming because it changes what is bookable. The Springs is built tight. Springs 1 to 15 sit close together around the lakes and the souk, with a secondary school inside Springs 3, and a large proportion of children walk or cycle home. A four o'clock session is therefore a real option here, where in Emirates Hills the same booking collapses in the first week because the bus run does not allow it.

That matters more than it appears. The hour between four and five is the most productive tutoring hour available to a teenager, before fatigue and after school. Families who can use it should, and families in The Springs mostly can. The ones who cannot are usually those whose children travel out of community to school, towards Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or across Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road to Arabian Ranches, where thirty-five to forty-five minutes door to door is normal in the evening.

The second local factor is that households here are frequently split between the two routes. A Diploma student and an IGCSE sibling in the same house is a common pattern, because the British secondary is inside the community while the IB continuum schools are minutes away in The Meadows and Emirates Hills. Teaching two children on two systems back-to-back on one evening works well online and is almost impossible to arrange with visiting tutors, since it would require two different specialists to drive to the same address an hour apart.

The third is that this is a community people move within rather than out of. Families trade up from a Springs townhouse to a Meadows or Emirates Hills villa, or down to an apartment in the Marina, and the children stay at the same schools. A tutoring arrangement built on proximity breaks at every one of those moves. One built on a subject specialist and a held time slot does not, which is the most mundane and most frequently decisive argument in this whole comparison.

sections.heading: Online and in-home compared, with the AED attached
paragraphs: A comparison is only useful if both columns are filled in honestly, including the one we do not sell. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear in the market at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Online rates for a qualified subject tutor sit at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour on Bestimate's Dubai tables, with an advertised online package at AED 799 a month for eight sessions, and budget online tutoring advertised from around AED 45 to 150.

What the in-home premium buys is worth separating into parts. Some of it buys a person in the room, which for a younger child or a student whose difficulty is organisational is genuinely valuable and should not be dismissed. Some of it buys travel: a car, a security gate and an hour of evening traffic, which buys nothing academic at all. And some of it buys a smaller pool, because a tutor who can only work a few evenings cannot afford to specialise narrowly, which is the hidden cost that matters most for a minority qualification like the Diploma.

For IB specifically, the balance tilts further than it does for other curricula. An IGCSE maths tutor is a broad specialism and a competent local one is findable. A Higher Level Economics tutor fluent in internal assessment criteria is not, and the difference between the right person and an approximately right person is larger in a subject assessed partly on components a non-specialist has never seen marked. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so this is a description of a market rather than a choice being offered.

Two standing cautions. These are rates published by named providers and read in October 2026, not a price list, so ask for a current quote and establish in writing whether VAT is included and what the replacement terms are. And for context on household costs generally, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion; school fees being held does not mean tutoring rates are.

sections.heading: Internal assessment, the Extended Essay and where help becomes malpractice
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internal assessment, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay sit alongside them. Together those components represent a large share of a student's final result, they are produced over months rather than hours, and they are the point at which the market in this region behaves worst. One site found during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Anybody considering that should understand precisely what is being purchased: a malpractice finding against their own child, with the Diploma itself at risk.

The legitimate boundary is clear and it is not restrictive. A tutor teaches the content. A tutor explains what the assessment criteria reward, in the student's actual subject. A tutor challenges a research question while it can still be narrowed, which is the single most valuable intervention available on any of these components. A tutor reads the student's own draft and gives feedback on it. A tutor rehearses an oral under timing. A tutor never writes, completes or produces the work, and never edits it to the point where the words stop being the student's own.

The practical test a parent can apply is simple: at the end of the process, is there a visible trail of the student's own improvement across their own drafts? If yes, the help was teaching. If the final version appeared from nowhere, it was not. School supervisors are experienced at spotting the second pattern, and the authentication process exists precisely for it.

One further point specific to this market. Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the IB and are not reproduced or distributed by a tutor; they are referenced, and the work is done from what the school provides, which has the advantage of being the correct version for the session being sat. A provider circulating a library of board material is telling you something about how it treats rules in general, and that is information worth having before you hand over a student's coursework.

sections.heading: What a parent in Dubai can actually verify
paragraphs: Since proximity cannot be the check, something else has to be. The useful list is shorter than it looks and every item on it is genuinely verifiable, which is more than can be said for most of what this market advertises.

Start with the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted to you as unverified. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Then the school side. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and its inspection reports are published and free to read, which makes them a far better source on a school than any marketing material. Abu Dhabi is regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator's remit goes well beyond inspection.

Then what nobody can verify, and should therefore be discounted. A satisfaction percentage with no sample size, date or method. A star rating a provider has awarded itself, particularly where the figure in the page markup differs from the one on screen. A claim of examiner status with nothing to evidence it. A claim of KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval: no tutoring platform holds board accreditation, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram does not hold one and does not claim to. And any promise about a grade, which is the clearest signal available that a provider is selling a feeling rather than a service.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB specialist living near The Springs?
faqs.answer: For mathematics or English, possibly. For most other subjects at a specific level, probably not, and it is better to know that now. IB programmes account for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private enrolment, each Diploma student takes six subjects at two levels, and the specialism you need is something like Higher Level Economics with internal assessment experience. Restrict that to people who can reach a Springs townhouse by five on a weekday and the pool is close to empty in most subjects. Dropping the travel requirement, and keeping subject, level and hour, is what makes a genuine match possible.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to find out whether they really know the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Ask about assessment rather than content, because content knowledge is the easy part. Which subject and level have they taught most recently, and when. What exactly is the internal assessment in that subject marked on. What is the word or time limit on it. What will they not do with a draft. How will they show you progress. Do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. What happens if it is not working after a month. A specialist answers all of those without hesitating; a subject graduate with no Diploma experience will redirect to enthusiasm and years of teaching.

faqs.question: Why does my DP1 child seem to be struggling in every subject at once?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma's defining feature is simultaneity rather than difficulty in any one subject. A DP1 student is carrying six syllabuses, an Extended Essay research question, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition and a service commitment, with internal deadlines set by the school that tend to cluster in the same few weeks. Families who believe they have a chemistry problem frequently have a scheduling problem, and the two need completely different help. The first useful step is laying the school's published internal deadlines on one sheet and finding the collisions before buying any teaching.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Language B and ab initio subjects outside the largest languages, and music, theatre, film and visual arts, particularly at Higher Level. Psychology, history, geography and global politics are covered but thinner, especially in the weeks before a session. Mathematics in both courses, the three sciences, English A, economics and business management are well covered at evening Gulf Standard Time slots. Where a subject cannot be filled you should be told before paying, offered a specialist working from outside the UAE on your time slot where that genuinely suits the subject, or given an honest no.

faqs.question: Can a session in The Springs realistically start at four o'clock?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, which makes this community unusual in the area. The Springs is built tightly around the lakes and the souk with a secondary school inside Springs 3, and a large proportion of children walk or cycle home. That makes the four-to-five hour genuinely available, and it is the most productive tutoring hour a teenager has. The exception is students who travel out of community towards Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or across to Arabian Ranches, where thirty-five to forty-five minutes door to door in evening traffic makes half past five the honest booking.

faqs.question: Can one evening cover an IB child and an IGCSE sibling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common request from these addresses, because the British secondary sits inside Springs 3 while the IB continuum schools are minutes away in The Meadows and Emirates Hills. Back-to-back sessions with two different specialists on one evening work straightforwardly online. The same arrangement is close to impossible with visiting tutors, since it would need two people to drive to the same address an hour apart, which is why in-home providers tend to push families towards one tutor covering both children regardless of fit.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to a house in The Springs?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only, and there is no UAE office or centre. The reason is the one this whole page is built on: for a minority qualification assessed partly on components a non-specialist has never seen marked, the gap between the right tutor and an approximately right one is wide, and travel is what forces the compromise.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium actually buy for an IB student?
faqs.answer: Three things, which are worth separating. A person in the room, which genuinely helps a younger child or a student whose difficulty is organisational. Travel, which buys nothing academic: published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor on Bestimate's tables. And a smaller tutor pool, because somebody who can only work a few evenings cannot afford a narrow specialism. For the Diploma that third item matters most, since level and component knowledge is precisely what decides the grade.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match an IB tutor for a Springs student?
faqs.answer: For the well-covered subjects, usually a few working days. Mathematics in both courses, the three sciences, English A, economics and business management are the straightforward ones. The variable is not the subject so much as the hour and the level: Higher Level in a thinner subject in the fortnight before a session can take up to a fortnight to fill or may not be fillable. You are told which situation you are in before booking, with a realistic start date rather than an optimistic one, because an honest wait beats a poor match.

faqs.question: Where is the line between IB tutoring help and malpractice?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward in the actual subject, challenge a research question while it can still be narrowed, read your child's own draft and give feedback, and rehearse an oral under timing. A tutor may never write, complete or produce the work, and may not edit it until the words stop being your child's. The test a parent can apply is whether there is a visible trail of the student's own drafts improving. School supervisors are experienced at spotting work that appeared from nowhere, and the student is the person who carries the finding.

faqs.question: Will a tutor provide IB past papers and subject guides?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to supply a library of them should make you cautious about a provider generally. Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter; for unreleased material it is an assessment-security matter too. A tutor references them and works from what your child's school supplies, which also has the practical advantage of being the correct version for the session being sat. How a provider treats this rule is a reasonable proxy for how it treats others.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and expect a straightforward answer. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service lists a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring platform in Dubai hold a permit from KHDA?
faqs.answer: A training institute with premises in Dubai can hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which requires initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific licence for a specific kind of operation, and it is not something an online matching platform holds. IB Gram does not hold it and does not claim to. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson is making a claim worth asking them to evidence.

faqs.question: Should I believe a provider's published IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Verify them, always, including anything on this page. Dubai IB schools predominantly sit the May session, and that much is safe to plan around. Specific IB examination and results dates could not be confirmed from the IB's own site during research for these pages, so none are published here. Confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before building a plan around it. More practically, the dates that actually govern your child's year are the school's own internal deadlines for internal assessments and the Extended Essay.

faqs.question: What should I do first if my child's results are worse than expected?
faqs.answer: Before buying anything, get the marked components and the school's view of where the marks went. Separate the three causes: content not learned, assessment not understood, or deadlines not managed. Each needs a different response, and only the first is fixed by teaching. Then ask what the school's own plan is, since a Diploma coordinator has information no external provider has. A tutor is worth adding once you know which of the three problems you actually have; adding one before that is how families spend a term on the wrong thing.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Ask the eight questions, then stop worrying about distance
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.closingBody: Take the eight questions on this page to anybody you are considering, including us. A tutor who can name your child's internal assessment criteria, state the word limit without checking, tell you plainly what they will not do with a draft and answer the permit question directly is worth far more than one who happens to live two streets away. Bring the most recent marked work and the school's internal deadline sheet to a free first lesson. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustainabl.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students in The Sustainable City and the surrounding Dubailand communities. Each is listed against the subject and level they teach to examination, because Higher Level depth is the thing a proximity search cannot find locally.

intro.heading: Sorted by syllabus, not by distance
paragraphs: A near me search is a sensible instinct applied to the wrong problem. For a piano teacher, distance is a reasonable first filter. For Chemistry at Higher Level, the first filter should be whether the person has taught the current syllabus through a full examination cycle, knows what the scientific investigation criteria reward, and can tell you why a particular answer scored four out of six. There are perhaps five hundred villas in The Sustainable City. The chance that the right Higher Level Chemistry specialist lives in one of them is small, and distance is the filter that hides that fact.

So this page is organised around content. It sets out what the Diploma assessment actually consists of, where the marks sit, which command terms examiners use and what each one demands, and what a student should do with a past paper beyond reading it. These are the things a parent cannot easily judge from a tutor profile, and they are the things that determine whether an hour a week changes a grade or just occupies a Tuesday.

The Diploma is six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject grade runs from 1 to 7, with up to three further points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. In the sciences, the internal scientific investigation is 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level — a fifth of the grade decided by a piece of work done months before any examination. In mathematics the exploration carries the same 20%. That single fact reorders what tutoring should prioritise in DP1.

Students in this community mostly reach the Diploma through the IB continuum school inside the gates, which has a specific consequence: cohorts are relatively small, so a subject is taught by one teacher and a student who does not click with that teacher's approach has no second option within the school. That is the most common reason a Sustainable City family engages a tutor, and it is a legitimate one. The tutor is not replacing the teacher; they are providing the second explanation.

Delivery is online, and we say so plainly rather than leaving it to the small print. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; household visits are a service we run in India only. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and past-paper questions on screen. The practical effect of that model in a community this size is that the pool of available Higher Level specialists stops being a function of who lives near Al Qudra Road, and starts being a function of who teaches the course your child is sitting. That is the trade this page is arguing for, and the rest of it is the evidence.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustainabl.programmesIntro: Three stages of the IB continuum are tutored here, and the syllabus demands differ sharply between them. What follows is what is actually assessed at each stage rather than a description of the educational philosophy.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every Middle Years subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Criterion A is usually knowing and understanding; the later criteria cover inquiry, communication and reflection depending on the subject group. A student who knows the content and sits on a 4 is almost always losing marks on the criteria that are not about content.
programmes.countryNote: In a continuum school like the one inside The Sustainable City, MYP grades feed directly into Diploma subject-level decisions. A student aiming at Higher Level sciences needs the criterion C and D marks, not just criterion A, because that is where the scientific investigation skills the Diploma examines at 20% are first built.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, external papers plus an internal assessment in nearly every subject. In the sciences the papers are split into a multiple-choice and data-analysis section and a longer written paper, with the internal investigation at 20%. In mathematics there are two or three papers depending on level plus the exploration. Grade bands move year to year, so the useful target is a mark profile rather than a boundary.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and every internal deadline your child faces is set by the school months ahead of it. For a student here, the practical implication is that the internal assessment work has to be timetabled against the school's deadline rather than against the examination, which is a different and much earlier date.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. The Extended Essay is an independent piece of up to 4,000 words with a supervisor and formal reflection sessions. Together they yield up to three points on a published matrix. Neither is taught as content, which is why both are routinely underestimated until the deadline is close.
programmes.countryNote: The single most useful core session is the earliest one, spent narrowing a research question from something unanswerable to something that fits 4,000 words and has accessible sources. IB Gram will give feedback on a student's own draft and question their reasoning; it will not write, rewrite or supply any part of an Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustainabl.subjectsIntro: What follows is the syllabus detail that matters per subject: the components, the weightings where they are published, and the specific place marks are lost. This is the level of specificity a tutoring enquiry should start from.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic structure dominate. Higher Level adds a third paper that is an extended investigative problem, rewarding students who write a structured argument rather than a sequence of results. The exploration carries 20% and is assessed partly on mathematical communication, where notation discipline earns more than ambition.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed throughout, and the recurring failure is presenting a calculator output as an answer rather than as a step requiring interpretation. Statistics, modelling and real-data analysis carry the paper. Higher Level adds substantially more on matrices, graph theory and complex modelling than students expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes run from space, time and motion through the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour and fields to nuclear and quantum physics. Marks go missing on uncertainty propagation and on explanations that describe what happens without naming the mechanism. The scientific investigation is 20% at both levels.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around Structure and Reactivity rather than the older topic list. Energetics sign errors, mechanism arrows drawn from the wrong species and equilibrium questions answered qualitatively when a calculation was demanded are the reliable mark-losers. The internal investigation is 20%.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change. Volume rather than difficulty is the obstacle. Data-based questions reward reading the axes and the units before the stem, and terminology precision separates a 5 from a 7 more than recall does.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided analysis of unseen texts, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, plus an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a written essay. The oral is where strong speakers still lose marks, because the global issue must be demonstrably present in both extracts rather than asserted over them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal assessment, each within a word limit and each requiring a diagram that is actually used in the analysis. Students lose marks summarising the article instead of applying theory. Higher Level extension topics and the quantitative paper need separate drilling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study subject where the command term governs the ceiling. An accurate answer written to the wrong command term sits in the lowest band. The internal assessment requires genuine organisational material, and students who invent figures to make the analysis tidy lose marks for exactly that.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal solution is a working product plus documentation, and the documentation carries more of the marks than the code. Written papers reward precise vocabulary on data structures, abstraction and networking. Fluent coders often produce the weakest design records, which is where tutoring should start.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades sit alongside Diploma subjects on the report and are often the quietest source of lost ground.

sections.heading: What a near me search cannot tell you about an IB tutor
paragraphs: A proximity search ranks by an attribute that has almost no bearing on whether a Diploma grade moves. What matters is whether the tutor has taught this syllabus through examination cycles, can recite what the criteria reward, and knows the difference between an answer that is correct and an answer that scores. None of that correlates with how far their flat is from Al Qudra Road.

In a community of around five hundred villas with one school inside it, the local supply problem is concrete rather than theoretical. Higher Level Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are the three subjects Sustainable City families ask about most, and they are precisely the subjects where a genuinely current specialist is scarce anywhere in Dubai. Filtering that scarce pool further by driving distance is how families end up with a well-meaning generalist and a disappointing second term.

So, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will come to an address in The Sustainable City. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past-paper questions and an optional recording. Home tutoring exists in our India operation only. What that buys a family here is the ability to choose on syllabus rather than on distance, which for Higher Level subjects is the entire difference in outcome. It also removes the two unpaid journeys at either end of a visit, which is why a session can start in the late afternoon rather than at eight in the evening when nobody learns anything useful.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually are in a Diploma subject
paragraphs: Most families discover the internal assessment weighting too late. In the Diploma sciences, the student's own scientific investigation is 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level. In mathematics, the exploration is also 20%. In Economics, three commentaries on published articles form the internal assessment. These are pieces of work completed months before any examination, under a school deadline, and in several subjects they are the single largest discrete chunk of the grade.

The strategic consequence is uncomfortable but clear. A DP1 student who treats the internal assessment as an administrative task and the examination as the real event has already conceded a fifth of several grades. Conversely, a student who gets the investigation right has banked marks that cannot be lost on a bad morning in May. For families deciding when tutoring is worth paying for, that argues strongly for DP1 rather than DP2, which is the opposite of what most families do.

The table below sets out the structure in the subjects most requested in this community. Weightings are published by the IB and are stable across a syllabus cycle, but the IB does revise courses, so a student should confirm the current structure with their subject teacher rather than relying on any website, including this one. What does not change is the principle: find out what each component is worth before deciding where the tutoring hours go. A parent who can name the weighting of every component in their child's six subjects is already making better decisions than one who is reacting to a report card.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides the band
paragraphs: More Diploma marks are lost to command terms than to ignorance. A student who writes an accurate description when the question said explain has answered a different question, and the mark scheme will not reward the overlap. The command terms are published, they are consistent across subjects, and they are learnable in a handful of sessions — which makes this the highest-return work available in the final terms of a Diploma course.

The pattern we see in students from this community is specific. Strong students, particularly those who have come through the Middle Years Programme in the same school, write fluently and at length. Fluency masks the problem: a well-written paragraph that states rather than justifies scores in the lower band while feeling like a good answer. The fix is mechanical. Underline the command term, write the number of marks next to it, and produce exactly the structure that term requires.

The table below gives the terms that cost the most marks in the subjects this community asks about, what the examiner is looking for, and the error that recurs. It is the kind of thing a student should have on the desk while working through past papers, not something to read once. Full published definitions live in the IB's own subject guides, which your child's teacher can provide; we reference them rather than reproducing them, because those guides are the IB's copyright and a tutoring site handing them out as downloads is doing something a parent should question.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and why it is where sciences grades are won
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of a Diploma science grade comes from a piece of work the student designs, carries out and writes themselves. It is marked against published criteria covering the research design, the data analysis, the conclusion and the evaluation. Most of the marks lost in this community are lost in the same two places: a research question too broad to answer with the data collected, and an evaluation that lists limitations without explaining how each one affected the result.

The sequencing problem is the real one. Schools set the investigation deadline well before the examinations, usually with a draft stage before that, so the window in which tutoring can help is in DP1 and the first term of DP2. A family that engages a tutor in the second term of DP2 is too late to influence a fifth of the grade in three subjects. This is the single most expensive piece of timing in the Diploma and almost nobody warns parents about it.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and we state it precisely. They may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a method is reproducible, point out that a conclusion outruns the data, and comment on writing the student has produced. They may not design the investigation, select the data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or supply a model to be adapted. Operations in this market sell completed internal assessments outright; that is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that is really a university decision
paragraphs: This is the most consequential subject decision a Diploma student in this community makes, and it is frequently made for the wrong reason. Applications and Interpretation is not the easy option; it is a different mathematics, weighted towards modelling, statistics and technology use. Analysis and Approaches is weighted towards algebra, calculus and proof. Both exist at Standard and Higher Level, and the Higher Level courses are substantial in different directions.

The decision should be driven by what comes after the Diploma. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and many economics and finance degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Degrees in business, psychology, design, medicine in some systems, and social sciences generally accept either and sometimes prefer Applications. Because requirements differ by university and change, the only reliable method is to check the admissions pages of the specific institutions on the shortlist, early, and work backwards.

Where tutoring genuinely helps is before the choice, not after it. A student whose algebraic fluency is shaky in MYP 5 or early DP1 can be brought to a point where Analysis and Approaches is a real option. Once the choice is locked, tutoring works within it. The table compares the two courses on the dimensions that actually matter for a decision, including how each one feels to a student who prefers process to open-ended problem solving. If a student is putting in effort without marks by the second term, the wrong-fit signal is usually already visible in that row.

sections.heading: How to actually use a past paper
paragraphs: Almost every family says their child is doing past papers. Almost none describe a process that extracts much from them. Reading a paper, then reading the mark scheme, then feeling broadly reassured is not practice; it is recognition, and recognition collapses under timed conditions. The method that works is slower and less comfortable, and it is most of what a technique-focused tutoring session does.

The sequence we run is: attempt the question cold and under timing, with no notes. Mark it against the official scheme without charity, writing the lost marks as a reason rather than as a number. Classify each lost mark — content not known, command term misread, method not shown, arithmetic, or time. Then rework only the questions in the categories that recur. Four questions processed this way are worth more than a full paper read through, and the classification is what turns practice into a plan.

A note on materials, because it matters legally as well as practically. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We reference them and point to the official sources, and your child's school has legitimate access to them. We do not host, reproduce or supply them as downloads, and a tutoring service that offers an unlimited paper bank should prompt a question about where it came from. Working from what the school legitimately holds is both the correct position and, in practice, the papers the school will mark against anyway.

sections.heading: What subject-specialist IB tutoring costs in Dubai, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Take the difference between two numbers rather than the numbers themselves. A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is published at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is published at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500. The gap between those two bands is almost entirely a car journey.

The other gap is the one worth paying for. IB, IGCSE and A Level subject specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and a premium named tutor advertised at AED 650. What separates AED 150 from AED 300 in the online tier is whether the person has taught Higher Level through examination cycles. For a subject where the internal assessment is 20% of the grade, that experience is the thing being bought, and it is not interchangeable with general competence in the subject.

Budget online tutoring sits at AED 33 to AED 65 an hour and has a legitimate use: homework supervision and momentum for a Middle Years student. It is the wrong purchase for a Higher Level paper. All these figures belong to the companies and rate guides that published them and were read in October 2026; they are the market's numbers, not ours. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages, because the right number depends on subject, level and weeks remaining. The next step is a free trial and a quote.

sections.heading: Availability, honesty and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Coverage is not uniform and pretending otherwise wastes a family's time. Across Mathematics in both routes, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, English A, Economics, Business Management and Computer Science, we can usually match a Higher Level specialist quickly. Coverage thins in some Group 2 languages, in several Group 6 arts subjects, and in a handful of smaller Group 3 options. When it does, we say what we can offer and how long a match would take rather than placing an approximate tutor into the slot.

On regulators, the position is narrow and deliberate. Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

On evidence, we publish no star rating, satisfaction percentage or improvement statistic. Competitors in this market publish self-asserted ratings that contradict their own page text, and a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing claim rather than evidence. What a family can check here instead: the AED figures name their publisher, the regulator descriptions are quoted from u.ae, and the academic honesty boundary is stated specifically enough to hold us to it.

process.description: Each session ends with a note recording what was covered and, specifically, which error categories recurred. Over a month that log shows whether the same mistakes are disappearing. If they are not, we change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Chosen by syllabus, not by distance
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means your child is matched to someone who teaches that exact subject at that exact level, rather than to the nearest available generalist. In Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches, that single difference is most of what determines whether the hour is useful.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes worked explicitly
whyPoints.description: Sessions dissect why an answer scored what it scored: which command term applied, which marks were available, which were forfeited for reasons unrelated to understanding. That is where most of the recoverable marks in a Diploma subject sit.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment timing taken seriously
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade in sciences and mathematics is decided before any examination, under a school deadline. We say so early, because families who learn it in the second term of DP2 have already lost the chance to influence it.

whyPoints.title: A clear academic honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and critique the student's own work. They do not design an investigation, write or redraft a report, or supply model answers to adapt, and we do not source completed coursework. Feedback given is recorded in case a school asks.

whyPoints.title: Figures and sources, not adjectives
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names its publisher and the month it was read. Regulator descriptions are quoted from u.ae. We publish no ratings, no satisfaction percentages and no improvement statistics, because a number without a method is not evidence.

whyPoints.title: An honest no when coverage is thin
whyPoints.description: In niche Diploma subjects we will tell you what we can offer and how long a match would take, rather than placing an approximate tutor. For a subject with a coursework component, an out-of-date tutor is worse than none.

faqs.question: Does it matter that an IB tutor is not physically near The Sustainable City?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma subject, distance is close to irrelevant and can be actively harmful as a filter. What determines whether a grade moves is whether the tutor has taught that syllabus at that level through examination cycles and knows what the criteria reward. Filtering a scarce pool of Higher Level specialists by driving distance usually produces a well-meaning generalist. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes at all; lessons are one-to-one over live video, which is what allows the match to be made on syllabus rather than on postcode.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma science grade comes from the internal investigation?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Standard and Higher Level, from a scientific investigation the student designs, carries out and writes. It is marked against published criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because the school sets its deadline months before the examinations, this is the part of the grade most families discover too late to influence. If you are deciding when tutoring is worth paying for in a science subject, that weighting argues for the first Diploma year rather than the second.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost IB students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain, evaluate and discuss, in that order. Explain requires a causal mechanism, and students routinely describe what happens instead of why, which earns the description marks and none of the explanation ones. Evaluate requires a supported judgement, and a list of advantages and disadvantages without a conclusion caps the band. Discuss requires multiple perspectives, so arguing one side thoroughly scores lower than a balanced answer written less fluently. The fix is mechanical: underline the command term and write the mark allocation beside it before answering.

faqs.question: Should my son take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Decide it from what comes after the Diploma rather than from which looks easier, because Applications is not the easy option, only a different mathematics. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and quantitative economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, psychology, design and most social sciences generally accept either. Requirements vary by institution and change, so check the published admissions pages of the specific universities on the shortlist. If fluency is the obstacle rather than preference, that is fixable before the choice is locked, not after.

faqs.question: What is the right way to use past papers for an IB subject?
faqs.answer: Attempt the question cold and under timing with no notes, then mark it against the official scheme without charity, recording each lost mark as a reason rather than as a score. Classify every lost mark as content not known, command term misread, method not shown, arithmetic, or time. Then rework only the categories that recur and retest the same question type. Four questions processed this way beat a whole paper read through alongside the mark scheme, which builds recognition rather than performance.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor's help on the scientific investigation have to stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating explicitly. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a method is reproducible, point out that a conclusion outruns the data, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not design the investigation, choose the data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or supply a model to adapt. Operations in this market sell completed internal assessments; buying one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: Why do students in a small school cohort need an outside tutor more often?
faqs.answer: Because there is usually one teacher per Diploma subject. In a large central Dubai school a student who does not follow one teacher's approach may have a parallel class with a different one. In a smaller community school there is no second option inside the building, so the second explanation has to come from outside. That is the most common and most legitimate reason families in this community engage a tutor, and it is not a criticism of the teaching. The tutor supplements rather than replaces.

faqs.question: How many weekly hours does a Higher Level subject realistically need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per subject is the normal starting point, rising to two in the weeks before a mock block or an internal assessment deadline. The limit is not money but absorption: a Diploma student already carries six subjects, the core, the mandatory UAE subjects and usually a sport. Three tutored hours a week typically produces fatigue and incomplete between-session work. We would rather begin with one subject, establish that the error patterns are moving, and add only when a diagnosis justifies it.

faqs.question: Do you supply IB past papers, mark schemes and subject guides?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be cautious of anyone who offers an unlimited bank of them. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We reference them, cite the official source, and work from material your child's school has legitimate access to. During sessions tutors use questions on screen and the official criteria as published. A service offering wholesale downloads invites a reasonable question about provenance, and in some cases about unreleased material.

faqs.question: My daughter writes well but keeps scoring 5. What is usually going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always command terms and structure rather than knowledge. Fluent writers produce paragraphs that state a position confidently without justifying it, which reads well and scores in the middle band. The diagnosis takes about two sessions: attempt long-answer questions under timing, then compare the answer with the mark scheme line by line to see which specific marks were available and unclaimed. Once a student sees that the lost marks are structural, the correction is fast, and it is the quickest route from a 5 to a 6.

faqs.question: Is the Extended Essay something a subject tutor should be involved in?
faqs.answer: Yes, early and in a narrow role. The highest-value session is the first one, spent narrowing a research question from something unanswerable into something that fits 4,000 words with accessible sources. After that, a tutor can explain what the criteria reward, discuss sources, question whether an argument holds, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite or supply text. Your school's supervisor runs the formal process including the reflection sessions, and nothing a tutor does should bypass it.

faqs.question: What does an IB subject specialist cost online in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200, and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and belong to the companies that published them. IB Gram does not publish an hourly list on these pages; we quote after a free trial, for the actual subject and level.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do you cover less well?
faqs.answer: Coverage is strong in Mathematics in both routes, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, English A, Economics, Business Management and Computer Science at both levels. It thins in several Group 2 languages, some Group 6 arts subjects and a few smaller Group 3 options. In those cases we tell you what is available, how long a match would take and when availability is likely, instead of filling the slot with someone approximate. In a subject with a coursework component, a tutor who is a syllabus revision behind is worse than no tutor.

faqs.question: Do you claim any IB or KHDA accreditation?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is not IB-accredited, not an IB World School, not KHDA-approved, not ADEK-approved and holds no Cambridge or Pearson partnership, nor any UAE office. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and several tutoring sites use wording that implies they hold one when they do not. We describe what each regulator governs because it helps you read your child's school reports, not to borrow authority we have not earned.

faqs.question: How soon can a Higher Level specialist start after we enquire?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Higher Level subjects, usually within a few days: a short diagnostic conversation, a free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan in syllabus terms. Niche subjects take longer and we will tell you how long rather than book a placeholder session. If a school deadline makes the timing urgent, say so in the first message, because it changes which tutors we approach and in what order they are asked.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustainabl.closingHeading: Send the subject, the level and the last marked paper
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustainabl.closingBody: The fastest way to a useful first session is three pieces of information: the subject, whether it is Standard or Higher Level, and a photograph of the most recent marked assessment. That shows where marks are actually being lost, which is rarely where a student thinks they are. We will arrange a free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, on a genuine weakness rather than a demonstration topic, and follow it with a written plan in syllabus terms. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Sustainable City in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. If we cannot match the subject properly, we will say so.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-valley.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students living in The Valley and the communities along the Al Ain road. Each is listed against the subject and level they teach to examination, because in a community whose children attend several different schools the subject is the only reliable basis for a match.

intro.heading: Distance is the one thing that does not help here
paragraphs: A near me search is a reasonable instinct applied to the wrong variable. For a swimming teacher, distance is a sensible first filter. For Chemistry at Higher Level, the first filter should be whether the person has taught the current syllabus through examination cycles, knows what each assessment criterion rewards, and can explain why a particular answer scored four marks out of six. None of that correlates with how far their home is from the Al Ain road.

In The Valley the mismatch is sharper than elsewhere. This is a newer community at the southern edge of Dubai with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing, so students here travel outward in two broad directions and attend several different schools. There is no single local cohort, no shared assessment calendar and no dense local tutor network built around one school gate. A proximity search in this neighbourhood returns a very short list, and shortness is not quality.

So this page is organised around content instead. It sets out what the six Diploma subject groups assess, how the core works and where its three points come from, the published word and page limits for each assessed component, and the places marks reliably disappear. These are the things a parent cannot judge from a tutor profile and the things that determine whether a weekly hour changes a grade or simply fills a Tuesday evening.

Some structure first, because it frames everything else. The Diploma is six subjects, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard, graded 1 to 7, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The core contributes up to three further points through a published matrix. Internal assessment carries substantial weight in most subjects — 20% in the sciences and in mathematics — and is submitted to school deadlines months before any examination.

Delivery is online and we say so plainly rather than leaving it in the small print. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and past-paper questions on screen. Household visits exist in our India operation only. In a community like this one, that model is what makes a genuine Higher Level specialist available at all rather than whoever happens to live nearby. It also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which is what allows a session to run while a student who has already commuted twice can still concentrate on a calculus problem or an organic mechanism. The remainder of this page is the subject detail that should drive the choice instead of the map.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Three stages of the continuum are tutored here, and in a community whose children are spread across several schools the stage matters more than the school name. What follows is what is actually assessed at each.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converting to a 1 to 7 grade through published boundaries. One criterion usually covers knowing and understanding; the others cover inquiry, process, communication or reflection depending on the subject group. A student who knows the content and sits on a 4 is losing marks on the criteria that are not about content.
programmes.countryNote: Valley students reach the Middle Years at several different schools, which means neighbours are often working to different assessment calendars and different task schedules. A family here has to track its own school's summative dates rather than relying on the street, and that is the single most useful administrative habit in this community.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects across the groups, external papers plus an internal assessment in nearly every subject. In the sciences the internal investigation is 20% at both levels; in mathematics the exploration carries the same. Grade boundaries shift between sessions, so the useful target is a mark profile and a component plan rather than a boundary number.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and every internal deadline a student faces is set by their own school months ahead of it. For Valley students, who have a long commute and therefore less incidental contact time with teachers, knowing those deadlines early matters more than it does for a student living beside their school.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is an independent piece of up to 4,000 words with a supervisor and formal reflection sessions. Together they yield up to three points. Neither is taught as content, which is why both are routinely underestimated until a deadline is close.
programmes.countryNote: A long school run reduces the casual corridor contact with a supervisor that students living near their school rely on. For Valley students that makes the earliest core sessions more valuable: narrowing a research question to something answerable in 4,000 words, with sources that are actually accessible, before the drafting starts.

programmes.name: Into the Diploma from IGCSE or MYP
programmes.description: The step into the Diploma is sharpest in independent written work and in the volume of simultaneous deadlines. A student who scored well at IGCSE by producing accurate short answers finds the first Diploma term genuinely hard, because the programme asks for sustained argument and self-managed coursework instead. That is a method problem, not a capability one.
programmes.countryNote: Because families move into The Valley from across Dubai and from abroad, a student may enter the first Diploma year from a different curriculum sequence altogether. A short diagnostic in the first term names the two or three genuinely unmet topics, which is far cheaper than remediation in the second year.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: What follows is the Diploma subject detail that matters: the components, and the specific place marks are lost in each. A tutoring enquiry that names a subject, a level and a component gets a far better first session than one describing a general struggle.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic structure carry the losses. Higher Level adds a third paper that is an extended investigative problem, rewarding a sustained written argument rather than a sequence of results. The exploration carries 20% and is assessed partly on mathematical communication.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed, and the recurring failure is presenting a calculator output as an answer rather than as a step needing interpretation. Statistics and real-data modelling dominate; Higher Level adds substantially more on matrices and graph theory than students expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes from space, time and motion to nuclear and quantum physics, with the scientific investigation at 20%. Marks disappear on uncertainty propagation and on explanations that describe an effect without naming the mechanism behind it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around Structure and Reactivity with the same 20% investigation. Energetics sign errors, curly arrows drawn from the wrong species and equilibrium questions answered qualitatively when a calculation was demanded are the reliable mark-losers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change. Volume rather than difficulty is the obstacle, and terminology precision separates a 5 from a 7 more than recall does.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a written essay. The oral is where confident speakers lose marks, because the global issue must be demonstrably present in both extracts.

subjects.name: Language B and ab initio
subjects.description: Assessed across reading, listening, writing and an individual oral. Students lose marks on register and on the conceptual understandings the course specifies, rather than on vocabulary. Coverage is thinner in some languages, and we say so rather than approximate.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal assessment, each within a word limit and each requiring a diagram used in the analysis. Marks are lost summarising the article instead of applying theory, and Higher Level quantitative work needs separate drilling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study subject where the command term governs the ceiling. An accurate answer written to the wrong command term sits in the lowest band, and the internal assessment requires real organisational material rather than invented figures.

subjects.name: Computer Science and Design Technology
subjects.description: Both carry a substantial project with documentation that outweighs the artefact in marks. Students who build fluently often document weakly, which is a diagnosable distinction and usually the right place for tutoring to start.

sections.heading: What a proximity search cannot tell you in a community like this one
paragraphs: Ranking tutors by distance assumes a dense local supply, and The Valley does not have one. With no school inside the community at the time of writing, there is no school gate around which a tutoring network forms, no single cohort sharing an assessment calendar, and no reliable word of mouth about who teaches Higher Level Chemistry well. The list a proximity search returns here is short, and the shortness is a function of the map rather than of the market.

What matters instead is answerable and specific. Has this person taught this subject at this level through examination cycles? Can they state what each assessment criterion rewards without looking it up? Do they know the published word limit for the component the student is working on? Can they explain why an answer scored four out of six rather than simply marking it wrong? Those questions separate a subject specialist from a capable generalist, and none of them involve a postcode.

So, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will come to an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past-paper questions and an optional recording. Home tutoring exists in our India operation only. What that buys a family at the southern edge of Dubai is the ability to choose on syllabus rather than on distance, which for Higher Level subjects is the whole difference in outcome.

sections.heading: The six groups, and what each one actually assesses
paragraphs: Parents new to the Diploma often find the structure opaque, and the opacity has a cost: it is hard to judge where tutoring would help without knowing what each group assesses. Six subjects are taken across the groups, with three usually at Higher Level. Every group has external papers and nearly every subject has an internal assessment, and the balance between those two differs considerably from group to group, which is where the planning value sits.

The practical point is that two subjects with the same grade can need entirely different interventions. A Group 4 science is 20% a student-designed investigation submitted months before the papers, so late tutoring cannot touch a fifth of it. A Group 1 language is assessed partly through an individual oral, which is a rehearsable performance and improves quickly with practice. A Group 3 subject lives or dies on command terms. Knowing which is which is most of what a parent needs to allocate a budget sensibly.

The table below sets out the groups with the component that most often decides the grade and the trap that recurs. It is deliberately practical rather than descriptive, because what a family needs is a way of deciding where an hour a week should go. Courses are revised periodically, so confirm the current structure of your own child's subjects with their teacher rather than relying on any website, including this one, and ask specifically which components have already been submitted, because anything already banked is outside what tutoring can reach.

sections.heading: The core, and where the three points come from
paragraphs: The Diploma core is where the three additional points live and where most late-stage panic happens. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition of three objects with written commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece of up to 4,000 words with a named supervisor and formal reflection sessions. Together they produce up to three points on a published matrix, and a failing condition in either can affect the award of the Diploma itself.

Neither is content a tutor teaches in the ordinary sense, which is exactly why they are underestimated. A student cannot revise Theory of Knowledge the way they revise a syllabus. What they can do is practise the specific move the course assesses: taking a knowledge question, identifying the assumptions in it, and arguing with real examples rather than abstractions. For the Extended Essay, the equivalent move is narrowing a research question until it can actually be answered in 4,000 words with sources a student in Dubai can reach.

That narrowing session is the highest-value hour in the entire core, and for a Valley student with a long commute and less incidental supervisor contact it matters more than average. What a tutor must not do is write, redraft or supply any part of either piece. We give feedback on the student's own draft, record what feedback was given, and leave the formal process — including the reflection sessions — entirely with the school, where it belongs.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, in one place
paragraphs: This is a table nobody in this market publishes and every Diploma student needs, because the limits are hard constraints rather than guidance and students routinely discover them after writing. Knowing the limit before drafting changes what gets planned: a 4,000-word Extended Essay cannot carry three research questions, and a Theory of Knowledge essay cannot survey an area of knowledge in 1,600 words. The limit is the first piece of information a student should have.

The practical effect of a limit is on scope rather than on style. Students who exceed a limit are usually not over-writing; they chose a topic that cannot be handled in the space available, and the symptoms show up as thin analysis and a conclusion that does not follow. That is why scope-testing is the earliest and most valuable session in any coursework engagement, and why a tutor who starts by asking what the limit is is asking the right question.

Limits and component requirements are set by the IB and are revised from time to time, so treat the figures below as a planning guide and confirm your own child's current requirements with their subject teacher or Diploma coordinator. The principle does not change even when a number does: find the limit, then choose a topic that fits inside it, rather than choosing a topic and discovering the limit during the second draft, when the only options left are deletion and a weaker argument.

sections.heading: Where subject marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Across the subjects Valley families ask about most, the losses are more predictable than students expect, and almost none of them are about not knowing enough. They are about answering a different question from the one asked, stopping an explanation one step short of the mechanism, presenting a result without the interpretation the examiner wanted, or writing accurately in a register that does not suit the audience specified. Each of those is correctable within weeks once named.

The single most common pattern is command-term failure, and it is worth labouring because it is so cheap to fix. A student who writes an accurate description when the question said explain has answered a different question, and the mark scheme will not reward the overlap. Strong writers are the most vulnerable, because fluency disguises the gap: a well-constructed paragraph that states rather than justifies scores in the middle band while feeling like a good answer.

The second pattern is interpretation. In Applications and Interpretation, in the sciences' data-based questions and in Economics, the examiner wants the number explained rather than produced: is the model appropriate, is the prediction inside the range of the data, what does the gradient mean in this context. Students who produce correct results and stop there leave marks on the table in every paper they sit. The table sets the recurring losses out by subject area, with a rough sense of how long each takes to correct, so a family can judge what is realistic in the weeks they actually have.

sections.heading: Points, conditions, and what a target grade really means
paragraphs: Families often fix on a points total without knowing how it is constructed, and that leads to effort in the wrong place. Each of the six subjects is graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42, with up to three further points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix for a maximum of 45. The Diploma requires a minimum points total together with a set of additional conditions covering minimum grades and the core, which your Diploma coordinator can state exactly for your child's combination.

The planning consequence is that not all points are equally expensive. Moving a subject from 5 to 6 is usually a technique problem and often achievable in a term. Moving a subject from 6 to 7 is frequently a different order of work. Securing the core points, by contrast, is mostly about starting early and choosing an answerable research question, which costs very little and is the most neglected point on the whole scorecard.

That argues for a specific sequence. Protect the core points first, because they are cheap and because a failing condition there can jeopardise the award itself. Then address whichever subject is furthest below its realistic ceiling, which is usually a command-term or interpretation problem rather than a content one. Confirm the exact award conditions with your coordinator rather than from a website, including this one, because they are precise and they matter more than any general guidance can.

sections.heading: What subject-specialist and core support cost in Dubai
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and one premium provider advertising AED 650. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. In-home visits are AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included.

For the Diploma the useful distinction is between subject work and core work. Subject work benefits from the specialist tier, because what is being bought is component-level judgement at Higher Level. Core work is usually short: a few sessions scoping an Extended Essay question and a few more reviewing drafts, which at the mid-market rate is a modest total and protects up to three points. Measured per point, the core is the cheapest thing on the list and the most frequently skipped.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, with monthly packages advertised at AED 799 for eight online sessions. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026.
