sections.heading: Honesty, permits and what we will not do
paragraphs: This search result includes operations selling completed internal assessments and Extended Essays at published prices. That is not tutoring, submitting bought work is academic misconduct, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. Because Dubai families are approached by such providers through the same channels as legitimate ones, the boundary belongs on the page before anyone asks.

A tutor may teach the content a piece of coursework rests on, explain what each criterion rewards and what its descriptors mean, test whether a research question can be answered in the words available, read the student's own draft and give feedback, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write any part of the work, supply a question or topic to be adopted wholesale, edit a draft into something the student did not produce, or provide data the student did not collect. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student makes the change.

There is a self-interested version of the same argument, which is more persuasive to a seventeen-year-old. The core components reward the student's own thinking explicitly: the Extended Essay's reflection sessions, the TOK essay's development of a knowledge question, CAS's documented reflection. Work produced by somebody else reads exactly as such, and the criteria that reward engagement collapse first. The students who score well chose a question they could answer, early, and then did the weeks of small steps.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published — Khaleej Times reported the ministry did not specify the amounts — so distrust any page printing a figure, and ask any tutor to show you the permit rather than describe it.

process.title: Ask the school for the deadline calendar
process.description: Not the exam dates but the internal ones: Extended Essay question and draft deadlines, TOK exhibition and essay dates, internal assessment topic approval and submission points, and the mock window. Those are what a tutor plans against, and most families have never asked for them in one list.

process.title: Count the weeks to the nearest one
process.description: That number decides everything else: one session a week or two, and whether the first target is a subject, the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge. A general level of worry produces a general plan, and a general plan in a calendar-driven programme is how families end up working on the smaller half.

process.title: Take the early slot this community allows
process.description: Tilal Al Ghaf pupils are frequently home before four, which makes a four-thirty start realistic rather than optimistic. An earlier session catches a student with attention left, before three hours of homework, and that is worth more than any adjustment to the lesson plan itself.

process.title: A free first lesson with the named tutor
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, with the person who would continue. Ask them what the Extended Essay word maximum is and what the internal assessment in your child's subject is marked out of. A specialist answers immediately. Then watch whether they found the real problem.

process.title: Set work that fits the week you have
process.description: One short timed question set per subject per week, marked at the start of the next session, rather than open revision nobody completes. The written note records what was set and whether it came back, which is the most honest progress signal available between school reports.

process.title: Re-plan at each internal deadline
process.description: Every submission, mock and report is a checkpoint where the plan is tested against evidence rather than renewed by habit. If a component has closed, the hours move to one that is still open. If a subject is secure we say so and stop, rather than rolling a session forward with no target.

whyPoints.title: Planned from dates, not from worry
whyPoints.description: The Diploma banks marks at intervals your child's school sets, so the month you start changes what tutoring can reach. We ask for the internal deadline calendar first and build the plan from it, which frequently moves the first session to a component the family had not thought about.

whyPoints.title: The core components taken seriously
whyPoints.description: A 4,000-word Extended Essay maximum, a 1,600-word TOK essay and an eighteen-month CAS minimum are a calendar, not a specification. No competitor page in this market gives a Dubai parent any of that detail, and it is where the Diploma most often goes wrong.

whyPoints.title: An early slot, because this community allows one
whyPoints.description: Pupils here are home before four more often than anywhere else in this belt, and we use that rather than defaulting to an evening hour. A tired session is a wasted one, and no amount of specialist knowledge compensates for a student who has already worked for three hours.

whyPoints.title: The cost of delay stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Starting in the final two terms costs roughly twice as much per month to reach roughly half as much of the grade. That conversation is harder to sell than the panic one, which is exactly why it belongs on the page rather than waiting to be asked.

whyPoints.title: Availability answered honestly
whyPoints.description: When the subject, level and slot combination does not exist, we say which part is the constraint and where a fallback tutor is based. We also say when we are the wrong provider, including for children who need an adult physically present, which we do not offer in the UAE.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the limits
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE. No part of an Extended Essay, TOK essay or internal assessment written by a tutor. No distribution of IB papers or mark schemes. No guaranteed grades. No approval or accreditation from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, because we hold none.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor based inside Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: Probably not for a Higher Level subject, and in this community it matters less than elsewhere. Tilal Al Ghaf has a school inside its boundary and sits beside DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City, which also have their own provision, so your child is frequently home before four. The hour an in-home tutor would spend travelling is the hour that makes an early session possible. The specialism you need — someone who teaches that exact course — is scarce across the whole emirate rather than only in this postcode.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to Tilal Al Ghaf addresses?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. No tutor is sent to any UAE address. What you gain is a shortlist built from everyone who teaches your child's course at their level, and an earlier start time, because nobody is driving across Dubai to reach you. Where a child genuinely needs an adult in the room, we will say so rather than selling a format that cannot work for them.

faqs.question: Does the short school run in this community buy us an earlier slot?
faqs.answer: Four-thirty is realistic in Tilal Al Ghaf, which is unusual in this part of Dubailand. Because the community has its own school and neighbouring communities do too, the school run is short and pupils are often home before four. That is worth using: a student at four-thirty has attention left, while the same student at seven has done a commute, a full school day and two hours of homework first. An early session is frequently worth more than any change to the lesson plan.

faqs.question: How early should Extended Essay support start?
faqs.answer: In the first Diploma year, because the essay's internal deadlines sit roughly a year before the examinations and the decisions that determine the mark are made at the research-question stage. The 4,000-word maximum is a design constraint rather than a target, and the commonest failure is a question so broad that 4,000 words can only describe it. A narrower question that can actually be answered scores better, and choosing one takes an hour of conversation rather than a term of writing.

faqs.question: Why do students find Theory of Knowledge hard to prepare for?
faqs.answer: Because there is nothing to revise. The prescribed-title essay has a 1,600-word maximum and is assessed on the quality of knowledge-question analysis rather than on content recall, so reading more does not help. What helps is structured argument practice against the actual instrument: one knowledge question developed properly rather than three mentioned shallowly, which is what 1,600 words will actually sustain. Students who try to cover three produce three thin arguments and lose marks on development.

faqs.question: When does CAS need to start?
faqs.answer: At the beginning of the first Diploma year, because CAS runs for a minimum of eighteen months. Confirm the current requirement with your child's coordinator, since the IB revises its guides. The practical failure is not starting late in itself but having no documented reflection, since CAS is evidenced through the student's own record rather than through activity alone. A student with a full calendar of commitments and an empty portfolio is in a worse position than one with fewer activities properly recorded.

faqs.question: How much does starting late actually cost?
faqs.answer: Roughly twice as much per month to reach roughly half as much of the grade. A family starting in the first Diploma year typically runs one weekly session, around AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid market band, and can still reach internal assessment, the Extended Essay and course content. A family starting in the final two terms typically needs two sessions a week, around AED 1,200 to AED 2,400, and can reach only the written papers because everything internal has been submitted. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our prices.

faqs.question: What should we do with the summer between the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the most valuable block in the programme, because it is. Nothing is being banked, no deadlines are running, and four or five sessions a week becomes possible, which is the only realistic way to rebuild fluency rather than patch it. A family that uses it arrives in the second year with first-year content secure, the Extended Essay well advanced and internal assessment topics chosen. A family that does not carries first-year gaps into harder topics while three deadlines converge.

faqs.question: Should we pause sessions through Ramadan or shorten them?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the usable evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot. The adjustment that works is a shorter session at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because in a sequential subject a fortnight's gap costs more than two shortened sessions. Where Ramadan falls close to a mock series or an internal deadline, plan that block before it starts. An online slot is far easier to move than a drive across Dubai, which matters most in exactly those weeks.

faqs.question: Which component should get the first session?
faqs.answer: The one with the nearest deadline that is still open, which is often not the subject the family is most worried about. If an internal assessment worth a fifth of a subject grade has no topic yet, that is where the available marks are. If the Extended Essay question has not been agreed, that is a single hour that changes the whole essay. Paper technique matters, but it is the only thing left once everything internal has been submitted, so it should rarely be first.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week can a Diploma student absorb?
faqs.answer: One subject at two sessions a week, or two subjects at one each, is the sustainable maximum in term time. Beyond that the limiting factor becomes whether the set work gets done, and the set work is where most of the improvement happens rather than in the session. Three tutored subjects produces a student too tired to complete any of it. If three genuinely need attention, sequence them across terms and holiday blocks, and we will say so rather than taking the larger booking.

faqs.question: What if the Higher Level specialist we need has no free slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you which part is the constraint, because the fixes differ. If the specialist exists but not in your slot, another evening usually resolves it, and this community has more usable early evenings than most of Dubailand. If the subject at that level is not covered in UAE hours at all, the fallback is a tutor in another time zone teaching at a Gulf Standard Time-compatible hour, and we tell you where they are based. If we cannot cover it, we say that rather than booking a generalist.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write the Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: No, and that boundary is firm. A tutor can explain what the assessment instrument rewards, discuss whether a knowledge question can be developed in 1,600 words, teach argument structure, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot write any part of it, choose the title approach outright, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. The criteria reward the student's own analysis, so outsourced work loses precisely the marks it was meant to gain, quite apart from being academic misconduct.

faqs.question: Why might my child be the only one in their year taking their HL subject?
faqs.answer: Because the IB is a minority curriculum in a very large market. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment against 37% on the UK curriculum. In a predominantly British-curriculum part of Dubailand, a Diploma cohort can be small and a particular Higher Level option smaller still. The practical consequence is that informal information is scarce, which is a genuine argument for a tutor who has taught the course many times.

faqs.question: Do IB tutors in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so distrust quoted amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingHeading: Ask for the internal dates, not the exam dates
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingBody: The email that changes most is the one asking your child's Diploma coordinator for the internal calendar: Extended Essay question and draft deadlines, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay dates, internal assessment approval and submission points, and the mock window. Put them in one list, count the weeks to the nearest, and you will usually find the first session belongs somewhere other than the subject you were worried about. Then take the early slot this community makes possible, because a student at four-thirty is a different student from the one at seven. Tilal Al Ghaf sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits in the UAE and promise no grades.

intro.heading: How do you tell whether a tutor actually knows the IB?
paragraphs: The honest difficulty with searching for an IB tutor near Town Square is not scarcity of candidates. It is that a parent has no way to distinguish between them. Everybody's profile says experienced IB tutor. Everybody has a degree in something relevant. Everybody is confident on the phone. And the difference between a tutor who has taken a named Diploma course to final grade and a graduate who has read the syllabus is invisible at the point of hiring and expensive to discover in February.

So this page is a verification tool rather than a sales pitch. The questions below are the ones we would want a parent to ask us, and they work on any provider. They are deliberately specific, because specificity is the whole test: somebody who has taught Chemistry Higher Level can tell you what the Internal Assessment criteria are called and roughly what each is worth without pausing. Somebody who has not will reach for general reassurance about experience and passion, and that reach is the answer.

Two structural facts make the questions necessary. First, nobody in the UAE accredits private tutors. Five separate regulators oversee private schools — KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah — and none of them vets tutors. The only requirement on an individual is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which confirms permission to work rather than subject competence.

Second, Town Square's geography removes the usual informal check. In an established community a parent hears about a tutor from three other parents whose children used them. Town Square is a Nshama development off Al Qudra Road, filled relatively recently with young families, and that word-of-mouth network is thin precisely where it would be most useful. Families here are hiring strangers more often than families in Jumeirah or Mirdif are.

IB Gram's position is that the verification problem is better solved by exposure than by assertion. Every match we propose comes with a free trial lesson taught by the specialist who would continue — not a sales call, not a different tutor — and the questions on this page are ones you should put to that person during or after it. If any answer is vague, that is useful information about the match, and we would rather you found out in a free hour than in March.

Lessons for Town Square families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. That is relevant to verification too, because it means the match is made on who has taught the course rather than on who lives within driving distance of Al Qudra Road.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-town-square.programmesIntro: A tutor who knows one IB programme does not automatically know another, and the verification questions differ by programme. These are the stages we cover for Town Square families.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry, continuous teacher assessment against learning outcomes, portfolios, and the Year 6 Exhibition. There are no examinations and no grades in the familiar sense, which means a tutor's job is building reading fluency, number sense and the ability to explain a method rather than preparing for anything.
programmes.countryNote: The verification question at this stage is simple: ask what the PYP Exhibition is and when it happens. A tutor who has worked with PYP children will describe a self-directed inquiry presented to the school community. A Diploma tutor taking on primary work for the fee will not know, which is fine to discover before you hire rather than after.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked 0-8, differing by subject group. Sciences mark knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Year 11 adds the Personal Project, assessed against its own criteria.
programmes.countryNote: Ask an MYP candidate to name the four criteria for the subject group in question. Somebody who has taught it names them; somebody who has not says the MYP is criterion-based and moves on. That single question filters more effectively than any qualification list, and it takes fifteen seconds.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked internally and moderated by the IB. The total runs to 45 points including up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: For the Diploma the useful questions are about the Internal Assessment criteria for the specific subject, what Higher Level adds over Standard, and where students in that subject habitually lose marks. All three have concrete answers, and all three are hard to bluff for more than a sentence.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, service learning, personal and professional skills and language development. The DP courses inside it are marked to exactly the same standard as a full Diploma candidate's.
programmes.countryNote: Rare in Dubai, so Town Square families usually meet the CP as a mid-sixth-form option. If a tutor claims CP experience, ask what the reflective project is and how it differs from the Extended Essay — it is a specific component and the answer is checkable against the school's own documentation.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: The IB subjects Town Square families ask about most, each with the detail a genuine specialist in it will know immediately. Use these as verification prompts as much as a coverage list.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A real specialist will tell you the Exploration is worth a fifth of the grade, that HL adds a third paper, and that most students who name calculus as the problem actually have an algebraic weakness underneath it. Ask what proof by induction is used for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask what AI Higher Level contains that surprises students. The answer is matrices, graph theory and complex numbers, which is not what anyone expects from the modelling route. A tutor who says AI is the easier course has told you they do not teach it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask how uncertainties propagate through a multiplication and what linearising a graph means. Both are routine for a physics specialist and both are examined constantly. Vagueness here is decisive, because these skills carry more marks than any single content topic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask how they teach nucleophilic substitution. A specialist describes electron density and partial charge; a generalist describes reagents and products. The second answer predicts a term of memorisation that collapses on an unfamiliar molecule.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask which command terms students most often misread. The answer should be concrete — outline versus explain, discuss versus evaluate — because in biology that distinction decides more marks than content recall does.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask what the commentaries are assessed on. A specialist will say application to a named real article and will mention that the choice of article sets the ceiling. A generalist will talk about understanding economic concepts.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what the Individual Oral requires. The answer involves a global issue and two works, prepared properly. Anybody describing it as a presentation about a book has not supervised one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask whether a SWOT analysis earns marks on its own. The correct answer is no — marks sit in applying it to the case material and reaching a supported judgement — and it is a question that separates teaching from tutoring quickly.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Ask what has to anchor every argument. The answer is a named study with its method and findings. A tutor who talks about understanding psychological theory in general is describing a different course.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Ask what the two assessed components are. The exhibition of three objects and the prescribed-title essay. TOK is the component most often claimed and least often genuinely covered, so this question matters more here than elsewhere.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Ask how many criteria it is marked against and what usually decides the grade. Five criteria, and the research question. Any answer that starts with writing quality rather than question design suggests the essay has not been supervised before.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Ask what the written papers test beyond programming. Architecture, networks and abstract data structures. Students comfortable at a keyboard lose marks tracing algorithms by hand, which a specialist will raise unprompted.

sections.heading: Ten questions that tell you whether a tutor knows the Diploma
paragraphs: Use these on anybody, including us. They are specific on purpose: specificity is the test. A tutor who has taken a named Diploma course to final grade answers each of them in a sentence or two without hesitation, because these are the things they think about weekly. A tutor who has read the syllabus will produce general reassurance about experience, rapport and passion, and the substitution is audible.

The questions do not require you to know the answers yourself. What you are listening for is whether the reply is concrete and immediate or general and warm. A specialist says the Exploration is twenty per cent of the maths grade and is usually lost on personal engagement rather than mathematics. A generalist says they have helped many students with internal assessments.

Two of the ten are about honesty rather than competence, and they matter at least as much. Asking what a tutor will and will not do with an Internal Assessment should produce an immediate, clear boundary — teaching, explaining criteria, reviewing method, feedback on the student's own draft, and nothing beyond that. Hesitation there, or an offer to help more than that, is the single most useful red flag available in this market.

Ask them in the trial lesson or immediately after it, with the tutor who would actually teach your child, rather than on an initial call with a coordinator. The coordinator's answers tell you about the company. The tutor's answers tell you about the thing you are buying.

sections.heading: Credential claims, and how to check each one
paragraphs: The claims in this market fall into three groups: ones that can be verified, ones that cannot, and ones that describe something which does not exist. Knowing which is which saves a lot of time.

Verifiable: the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It is issued under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services with a stated two-working-day completion time. Ask to see it and check it with MoHRE. Also verifiable: a university degree, a teaching qualification, and whether a named school currently employs somebody, by asking the school.

Not verifiable by a parent: current IB examiner status. We do not describe our own tutors as examiners for this reason, and you should treat any such claim as unevidenced unless the provider can show you something concrete. Examiner status also does not confer access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, and any implication that it does should end the conversation rather than advance it.

Describes nothing that exists: regulator approval for tutors. Five bodies regulate private schools across the emirates — KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education — and none vets private tutors. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a real thing issued to training institutes with premises, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry, and if a provider claims one, ask for the number. IB Gram holds no regulator or awarding-body approval, accreditation, licence or partnership of any kind, has no UAE office or centre, and claims none.

sections.heading: What the Diploma actually requires, so you can judge the answers
paragraphs: The verification questions work better if you know roughly what the course involves, so here is the structure in plain terms. A full Diploma candidate takes six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard. Alongside those sit three core components: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay of 4,000 words, and Creativity, Activity, Service. The total score runs to 45, which is six subjects marked out of seven plus up to three bonus points from the matrix combining the TOK and Extended Essay grades.

Every subject also carries an Internal Assessment, marked by the school teacher and moderated by the IB. That means a full candidate is running six separate coursework projects with six internal deadlines, all set by the school rather than by the IB, and nearly all landing in the same two terms. Understanding this is what tells you whether a tutor's plan is realistic: a tutor who treats a subject in isolation is ignoring the five other deadlines competing for the same evenings.

UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session. We publish no specific IB date, and the reason is worth knowing as a verification point in itself: the IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org. Any provider quoting you a precise IB exam or results date should be asked where they read it. Get dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org.

Cambridge and Pearson dates, by contrast, are published and usable. Cambridge runs International GCSE and O Level in June and November series, with the February/March series offered to India only, so UAE candidates sit June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January, with the November 2025 results landing on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What a first session should look like
paragraphs: Verification continues into the first hour, and what happens in it is informative. A tutor who spends the session establishing rapport and asking how your child feels about the subject has not diagnosed anything, however pleasant the hour was. A tutor who puts real past-paper questions in front of the student within the first ten minutes and watches them work is doing the job.

What a good diagnostic produces is narrower than most families expect. Not a general assessment of ability, but a specific list: method is not being written down, so method marks are being forfeited. Command terms are being misread, so correct knowledge is producing wrong-shaped answers. One topic was missed during a move between schools. The uncertainty work has never been taught properly. Each of those is a plan rather than a diagnosis.

The second thing a good first session produces is a realistic timescale. A technique fault takes a few weeks of marked practice. A missing topic takes a few sessions. A missing year of foundations takes longer than the time available in February of Year 13, and a tutor who says so has told you something valuable about how they will handle the rest of the arrangement.

Our trial lesson is designed to be exactly this: one full session with the specialist who would continue, no card required and no obligation, after which you have a concrete account of what is wrong rather than an impression. If that account is vague, the match is wrong and we would rather you knew in a free hour. The verification questions in the table above are best asked at the end of this session, when you have seen the person work.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: Two of the ten verification questions are about this, and they deserve the detail, because this search result contains operators who sell finished coursework. One advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut with a price; it is an academic-honesty breach, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice.

The permitted ground is wide. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on. They may explain what each criterion asks for and what marks it carries. They may help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. They may review a method and say that it will not generate usable data. They may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. All of that is teaching and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work: not write a section, not supply text to insert, not rewrite the student's prose, not provide a template needing only numbers, not edit a draft to a finish so the submitted text is substantially theirs. The student signs a declaration of authorship and the supervisor signs alongside, so the line is practical rather than ceremonial.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Those are the awarding bodies' copyright, and for unreleased material there is a malpractice exposure as well. We cite them, link the official source and teach from them. If a provider offers you a folder of mark schemes, that is a question worth asking about rather than a benefit.

Ask for the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because the monthly figure is what actually leaves your account, and a tutor who cannot produce it has not thought about the Diploma as a two-year commitment. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240-600 at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages sit inside those brackets at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 a session, and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits, which is closer to AED 400 a visit once the tutor's drive into Town Square is inside the price. sections.heading: When we tell you not to buy sessions
paragraphs: One of the ten questions asks what would make a provider advise against buying, and we should answer our own question. There are four situations in which we say no or not yet.

The first is no specialist available. Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Higher Level Computer Science, smaller Group 2 languages, Music and Film are genuinely scarce, and in some terms we cannot cover them. We decline rather than putting a general tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate, and we have lost enquiries doing it. If the only matching specialist is in a different time zone, we say so and offer the slots that actually exist.

The second is too little time to matter. A student in March of Year 13 missing a year of foundations in a subject cannot have that replaced in eight weeks, and selling the attempt is selling hope. What we will say in that case is which narrower thing can still move — usually technique, command terms and showing method — and that concentrating there is worth more than general coverage.

The third is that nothing is wrong. We have read MYP reports where the criterion profile describes a student doing perfectly well and the parents had been reading an unfamiliar scale as a bad result. The fourth is where the honest answer is a school conversation rather than a tutor: a missed topic that the school should and would reteach, a timetable problem, or a pastoral issue that tutoring would paper over. We say that instead of taking the booking.

We also never offer a UAE home visit as a fallback, because there is no UAE visiting service to fall back on. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch here and nobody on our roster will arrive at a Town Square address.

sections.heading: What we do not claim, and why that is a verification point
paragraphs: Absences are evidence too, and the things missing from this page are things competitors in this search result do publish.

No star rating, no satisfaction percentage, no average points total achieved by students we have supported. Competitors publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, sometimes two conflicting versions in the same document, and one shows a rating from twenty reviews alongside a far larger claimed student count. None states a sample size, a date or a method. A number without those three is decoration, and self-asserted review markup is against Google's structured-data policy as well.

No regulator or awarding-body claim, no UAE address, no non-UAE phone number as the conversion path, and no examiner descriptions we cannot evidence. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers in another country, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. Both are trust failures, and the second is a misrepresentation.

And no guarantee of a grade, a points total or an improvement, because nobody can honestly offer one and the offer itself is diagnostic of the provider. We also will not imply that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression — that is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, and it is worth noticing when anybody makes it to you.

Finally, no school or group is described here as a partner or client. Several competitors list twenty-five or more schools under a trusted-by heading with no relationship behind it, and one lists a school that appears not to exist. We name schools only to describe the landscape around Town Square, and we say so under every list, because a school name used as an implied endorsement is the easiest claim in this market to make and one of the easiest to check.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether an IB tutor near Town Square is genuine?
faqs.answer: Ask specific questions and listen for whether the answer is concrete or warm. Which exact course and level do you teach, in your own words? What is the Internal Assessment worth in that subject and what are its criteria called? What does Higher Level add? Where do students in this subject habitually lose marks? A specialist answers each in a sentence without pausing, because these are weekly concerns for them. A non-specialist substitutes general reassurance about experience and rapport, and that substitution is the answer.

faqs.question: Does any UAE authority approve or vet private tutors?
faqs.answer: No. Five bodies regulate private schools — KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah — and none of them vets tutors. The only requirement on an individual is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which confirms permission to work rather than subject competence. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by an education regulator is describing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: What single question filters out most non-specialists?
faqs.answer: What will you not do with an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay? A genuine specialist gives an immediate, clear boundary: teach the content, explain the criteria and mark allocations, help narrow the research question, review whether a method produces usable data, give feedback on the student's own draft, and nothing beyond that. Hesitation, or an offer to help with the writing, tells you both that they have not supervised the component and that they are relaxed about a rule that can cost your child their Diploma.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a tutor is an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask, and then ask for evidence, because the claim is common and almost never checkable by a parent. We do not describe our own tutors as examiners for exactly that reason. The more important point is what examiner status would mean if true: nothing about access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Any provider implying that an examiner can tell you what is coming or how marking really works has made a claim that should end the conversation rather than advance it.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a new IB tutor look like?
faqs.answer: Real past-paper questions at your child's level within the first ten minutes, with the tutor watching them work rather than discussing how they feel about the subject. What should come out is a specific fault list — method not written down, command terms misread, one topic missed during a school move, uncertainty work never properly taught — plus a realistic timescale for each. A pleasant rapport-building hour that produces no fault list has diagnosed nothing, whatever it felt like.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find a trustworthy tutor in a newer community like Town Square?
faqs.answer: In one specific way, yes. Town Square is a Nshama development off Al Qudra Road filled relatively recently by younger families, so the informal parent network that vets tutors in older districts is still thin. Families here are more often hiring a stranger than hiring their third recommendation. That is why a verification checklist is worth more here than in Jumeirah or Mirdif, and why a free trial lesson with the person who would actually teach is the most useful thing a provider can offer.

faqs.question: Why does nobody publish exact IB exam dates, including you?
faqs.answer: We do not publish them because we cannot verify them. The IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and putting an unverified date in front of a parent who will plan around it is worse than saying nothing. UAE schools sit the May session; get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. Treat any provider quoting you a precise IB date as somebody to ask a source from.

faqs.question: How do I check the MoHRE permit, and what does it prove?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it and verify it through MoHRE's e-services. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time via its smart app, website or e-services. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, lacking one is a choice rather than an obstacle. What it proves is permission to tutor — not subject knowledge, and not that the person has taught your child's course.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own school teacher privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for school staff there. It is the option families most want and the one least available. If a provider markets your child's own teacher privately, that tells you how carefully it reads the rules it operates under, which is worth knowing before anything else about it.

faqs.question: What does the Diploma involve, so I can judge a tutor's answers?
faqs.answer: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The total runs to 45 points, including up to three bonus points from the matrix combining TOK and Extended Essay grades. Every subject also carries an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, so a full candidate runs six coursework projects with school-set deadlines clustered in two terms. A tutor who ignores the other five deadlines is not planning realistically.

faqs.question: Should a provider give me a shortlist of tutors to choose from?
faqs.answer: It sounds generous and it moves the judgement to the person with the least information. A parent comparing five profiles is comparing self-descriptions, which is exactly what this page argues against relying on. We propose one named specialist, say why we think they fit, and let a free trial lesson test it; if the match is wrong we propose somebody else at no cost. The hour of watching somebody teach is worth more than five profiles and a phone call.

faqs.question: What would make you tell a Town Square family not to buy sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things, and we have lost enquiries to each. No specialist free — Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Higher Level Computer Science, smaller languages — in which case we decline rather than substitute a generalist. Too little time to matter, where we name the narrower thing that can still move instead. Nothing actually wrong, which happens with MYP criterion reports read as bad results. And where a school conversation is the right answer: a missed topic the school would reteach, or a pastoral issue tutoring would paper over.

faqs.question: Why should I distrust a star rating on a tutoring site?
faqs.answer: Because almost none of them states a sample size, a date or a method, and without those three a rating is decoration. Competitors in this market publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, occasionally in two conflicting versions on the same page, and one shows five stars from twenty reviews next to a claimed student count orders of magnitude larger. Self-asserted review markup also breaches Google's structured-data policy. We publish no rating at all, which is why this page gives you questions instead.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB tuition to Town Square over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and there is no UAE visiting arrangement at any price. We also hold no UAE office, centre or branch. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel. If you want in-home delivery, the verification questions on this page still apply, and so does asking for the permit.

faqs.answer: Whether the figure is per hour or per lesson and how long a lesson runs, because a fifty-minute session priced as an hour is an increase nobody volunteers. The single-session price with no block. What happens if you stop after one. The cancellation and reschedule terms, which matter with a long school run. Any travel surcharge into Dubailand. Whether diagnostics, reports or materials are charged separately — and if materials are, what is being supplied, since awarding-body papers are copyright.

intro.heading: Judge a tutor on the syllabus, not on the postcode
paragraphs: Umm Al Sheif is a villa district off Al Wasl Road, wedged between Umm Suqeim and Al Safa, a short drive from Jumeirah 3 and the coast. It is a well-served part of Dubai for schools, and the honest consequence is that most families here already have a short list of local tutors. The question is not whether someone is available. It is whether the available person knows the specification well enough to be worth an hour of a Diploma student's remaining time.

There is a quick test and it takes ten minutes on a phone call. Ask what Paper 2 is worth in your child's subject at their level. Ask which criterion letter carries the most marks on the Internal Assessment and how many. Ask what the examiner wants when a question says evaluate, and how that differs from discuss. A specialist answers all three immediately. A general tutor talks about confidence and rapport, which matter but are not what you asked.

That test matters more at Higher Level than anywhere else. The Diploma is examined on components with published weightings, and the weightings differ between Standard and Higher Level in ways that change where revision should go. Paper 3 in Mathematics at Higher Level is a fifth of the grade and does not exist at Standard Level. A student revising evenly across a course where one component carries thirty per cent is wasting effort they do not have.

The second thing this page sets out is the Internal Assessment, which is the most under-taught twenty per cent in the Diploma. Criteria are published, letter by letter, with marks attached. Students routinely lose marks in a criterion they have never read, which is the cheapest loss in the whole qualification to fix. A tutor who makes a student mark their own draft against the descriptors usually finds two or three marks sitting in plain sight.

IB Gram delivers to Umm Al Sheif as one-to-one teaching over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. The reason that works in your favour here is pool size: the people who can teach the data-analysis section of a science paper properly are not distributed by neighbourhood, and removing the drive means you choose from all of them rather than from whoever lives within a twenty-minute radius.

What follows is the detail, in the order a Diploma student needs it: component weightings, command terms, Internal Assessment criteria by letter, how to use past papers so they actually teach something, the local school mix and the hour that works, what each price band in the Dubai market buys, and where a tutor must stop on work that has to be the student's own.

Delivery to Umm Al Sheif is live one-to-one video only

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-umm-al-sheif.programmesIntro: Umm Al Sheif sits inside a school cluster running the full IB continuum as well as British sixth forms, so a single street can contain a Primary Years pupil, a Middle Years student and a Diploma candidate. Each needs a different kind of help.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment, so the PYP is where parents relax and where the gaps start. Inquiry units build research and presentation skills well; arithmetic fluency and sentence construction can drift, and the drift surfaces in Middle Years mathematics two or three years later. The right intervention is short, frequent and skills-based, built around fluency rather than content coverage.
programmes.countryNote: Primary pupils from Umm Al Sheif generally attend schools in Umm Suqeim, Al Safa or Jumeirah, and are often home by 15:00 because the journeys are genuinely short by Dubai standards. That makes a 16:00 start realistic here in a way it is not in the outer communities, and it makes three short weekly sessions more practical than one long one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, each on a one-to-eight scale, converted to a one-to-seven grade. A student can know the material and still score five, because the criterion asked for evaluation and the answer described. Most useful Middle Years tutoring is teaching a child to read the criterion strand before writing, which transfers directly into Diploma Internal Assessments.
programmes.countryNote: The Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim schools include full continuum schools, so many Umm Al Sheif students go from Middle Years straight into the Diploma in the same building. That continuity is an advantage, but it can also hide a gap: a student who scored sixes on criteria-based work may still have never written under timed exam conditions, which the Diploma demands from the first term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. The qualification maxes at 45 points, with up to three from the core. The difficulty is distribution: components carry different weights, internal deadlines cluster, and a student revising evenly across unequal components loses marks to arithmetic rather than to misunderstanding.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Umm Al Sheif attend schools in Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, several with study periods after a 15:30 finish. The usable hours here are wider than in the outer suburbs because the drives are short, so 17:00 and 19:30 both work, and the deciding factor is usually the co-curricular programme rather than the traffic.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with career-related study and a reflective project. Rare in Dubai, but where a school offers it the Diploma courses inside it are examined on exactly the same papers with the same weightings and the same Internal Assessments. A student on this route needs identical subject teaching to a full Diploma candidate in those courses.
programmes.countryNote: Very few schools in the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim cluster run the Career-related Programme, so an Umm Al Sheif family is usually choosing between the Diploma and A Levels rather than considering it. If your child is on it, say so at matching, because the component weightings a tutor plans around are the Diploma ones.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-umm-al-sheif.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the component structure is what a tutor should know cold and the mark loss is what a first session should diagnose. Request by subject and level together; the two are not separable.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level is Paper 1 and Paper 2 at forty per cent each with the exploration at twenty. Higher Level redistributes to thirty, thirty and twenty with Paper 3 at twenty, a long scaffolded investigation. Marks go on unjustified steps and on misreading multi-part stems rather than on arithmetic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure as Analysis and Approaches, different content: statistics, modelling and far heavier calculator dependence. The common loss is graphical display calculator technique, where a student who can do the mathematics cannot produce the required regression or distribution output.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is thirty-six per cent across its multiple-choice and data-based sections, Paper 2 forty-four, the investigation twenty. Uncertainty propagation and gradient interpretation decide a large share of the data marks, and command-term discipline decides most of the rest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same component split as Physics. Organic mechanisms and equilibrium carry the Higher Level difficulty, but the habitual loss is moles arithmetic written without units or significant figures. The investigation rewards a research question narrow enough to measure in the time available.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-volume science, and the one where wording costs most. A mark scheme wanting a named process does not accept fluent paraphrase. Short timed recall on terminology outperforms re-reading notes, and the data-based section rewards the same analysis skills as the other two sciences.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level runs Paper 1 at thirty, Paper 2 at forty and the portfolio at thirty. Higher Level adds Paper 3, the quantitative policy paper, at thirty. Diagram accuracy earns marks before prose is read, and the commentary portfolio is where the easiest marks are most often wasted.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Standard Level is two papers at thirty-five per cent each with the Individual Oral at thirty. Higher Level reduces Paper 2 and adds the HL Essay of twelve hundred to fifteen hundred words. The Individual Oral is prepared worst because it feels informal; it is a ten-minute argument and needs rehearsing like a paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The analytical tools are finite and examinable: Ansoff, SWOT, break-even, cash-flow forecasting, investment appraisal. Marks are lost by describing a tool instead of applying it to the stimulus firm, and by ignoring the quantitative data provided in the case study.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A sixteen-hundred-word essay on a prescribed title, worth roughly two thirds, plus an exhibition of three objects for the remaining third. Abstract writing about knowledge scores badly; the marks are in specific, real examples held against a clear claim. The writing stays entirely the student's own.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research in one subject, supervised by a school teacher, combining with Theory of Knowledge for up to three bonus points. The marks hinge on a question narrow enough to answer and on genuine engagement with sources, both decided in the first fortnight of work.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-umm-al-sheif.regionsIntro: Umm Al Sheif sits in the Jumeirah and coastal belt, where school journeys are short and the limiting factor on a session is the co-curricular programme rather than the road. These are its neighbours and what differs practically between them.

regions.note: Directly west and home to several of the schools Umm Al Sheif children attend, including full IB continuum provision. Journeys of ten to fifteen minutes mean a 16:30 session is genuinely workable here, unlike in the outer communities.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: The coastal strip running towards the city, with primary provision and a well-known Diploma school. Parking and the morning drop at the Jumeirah schools is the usual complaint, not the afternoon return.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Reached in minutes from Umm Al Sheif but with one road on and off. Palm families commonly choose later slots because the single access route makes an afternoon return less predictable than the short distance suggests.

regions.name: Al Manara and Al Wasl
regions.note: Immediately inland, sharing the Al Wasl Road corridor and most of the same schools. The practical difference is proximity to Sheikh Zayed Road, which matters for families whose children attend schools in Al Barsha rather than Umm Suqeim.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: South-west along the coast, containing a selective British senior school that takes students from across Jumeirah. Umm Al Sheif Diploma and A Level students at Al Sufouh schools typically finish later and prefer a 19:30 slot.

regions.name: La Mer and Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: Newer coastal developments with apartment stock and younger families, so primary enquiries dominate. School journeys run inland rather than along the coast, which puts these families on similar timings to Jumeirah 1.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: The immediate cluster, containing full IB continuum schools alongside British provision. The important point for matching is that two children on the same street can be on entirely different assessment systems, so the subject and level matter more than the area ever will.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa, Al Sufouh and the wider Jumeirah belt
schoolClusters.note: A short drive east or west, these schools draw heavily from Umm Al Sheif. Several run extended days with study periods, which is why Diploma families here more often want 19:30 than 17:00.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-umm-al-sheif.modesIntro: Three formats, chosen by component rather than by budget. A Paper 3 problem and an Internal Assessment problem need different engagements, and conflating them is how families end up paying for hours that do not move a grade.

modes.title: Component-targeted weekly one-to-one
modes.description: One subject, one named component, the same tutor weekly. The session starts from the published weighting and works on the technique that component rewards: Paper 3 scaffolding, data-based analysis, diagram accuracy, the Individual Oral. Live video with a shared whiteboard, so worked solutions survive the hour and can be reread before the next paper.

modes.title: Internal Assessment supervision block

The tutor helps narrow a research question, challenges the method, reads a draft and gives feedback against the criterion letters. Every word of the submission is the student's. This is the format most often mis-sold in Dubai, so the boundary is written down rather than assumed.

sections.heading: The ten-minute test for an IB tutor near me in Umm Al Sheif
paragraphs: Three questions separate a subject specialist from a general tutor, and all three can be asked before any money changes hands. What is Paper 2 worth in my child's subject at their level. Which criterion letter carries the most marks on the Internal Assessment, and how many of the total. What does an examiner want when a question says evaluate, as opposed to discuss or describe.

The answers are published, so there is no excuse for vagueness. A Mathematics specialist knows that Standard Level splits forty, forty and twenty across two papers and the exploration, and that Higher Level becomes thirty, thirty, twenty and twenty once Paper 3 arrives. A science specialist knows the current split is thirty-six, forty-four and twenty, and that the investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria. These are not obscure facts; they are the architecture of the grade.

The third question is the one that exposes the most. Command terms are defined by the IB and they are the single largest source of avoidable loss across every subject. A student who writes a competent description in answer to an evaluate question has written something good and scored almost nothing for it. A tutor who cannot explain that distinction crisply will not be able to teach a student out of the habit.

None of this requires proximity to Umm Al Sheif. It requires someone who teaches the specification repeatedly. That is why matching at IB Gram starts with the subject, the level and the component you are worried about, and why the first session is spent on a marked script rather than on a getting-to-know-you conversation.
bullets: Ask for Paper 2's weight at your child's level before anything else
Ask which IA criterion letter carries the most marks
Ask what evaluate requires that describe does not
A vague answer to any of the three is the answer you needed

sections.heading: Higher and Standard Level are different courses, not different difficulties
paragraphs: Parents often describe Higher Level as the harder version of the same thing. It is more accurate to say it is a differently shaped assessment. In Mathematics, Higher Level adds an entire paper, Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade and unlike anything in the Standard Level course: a long, scaffolded investigation that rewards persistence through unfamiliar structure rather than recall.

In English A Language and Literature the redistribution is subtler and more consequential. Standard Level students carry two papers at thirty-five per cent each and the Individual Oral at thirty. Higher Level students keep Paper 1 at thirty-five, drop Paper 2 to twenty-five, and pick up the Higher Level Essay at twenty, with the Individual Oral at twenty. A Higher Level student who revises as though Paper 2 still carried thirty-five per cent is misallocating a term.

Economics does something similar by adding Paper 3, the quantitative policy paper, at thirty per cent, which compresses everything else. A student who found the diagrams manageable at Standard Level can be caught out by the arithmetic demand of Paper 3, and it is a specific, drillable skill rather than a general ability.

The practical instruction is simple: write the weightings for your child's six subjects on one sheet, at their actual level, and put revision time in proportion. Most families have never seen the six numbers together, and seeing them changes the plan more than any amount of general advice about study technique.

sections.heading: Command terms are where the marks actually go
paragraphs: The IB defines its command terms and examiners mark to them. This is the most teachable improvement available in the Diploma and the one schools have least time to drill, because it requires a student to write, be marked, and write again, repeatedly, on the same instruction. Most students lose marks in the same command term across every subject they take, which means one fix pays six times.

The pattern is consistent. Describe asks what, explain asks why, evaluate asks for a judgement supported both ways, and discuss asks for a balanced exploration with a conclusion. Students default to describing because describing is what they can always do. A six-mark evaluate question answered descriptively typically scores two, and the student leaves the exam believing they answered it.

The fix is mechanical rather than inspirational. Underline the command term before reading the rest of the question. Write the structure the term demands before writing any content. In an evaluate answer, that means a claim, evidence for, evidence against, and a judgement with a reason. Taught properly, this takes three or four sessions and then holds for two years across every subject.

A side effect worth knowing: the same discipline improves Internal Assessment marks, because criterion descriptors use the same verbs. A student who has learned to answer evaluate properly writes a better evaluation criterion in a science investigation without being taught anything new. The reverse also holds, which is why a student who treats the investigation as a writing task separate from the examined course tends to underperform in both. One vocabulary, learned once, is doing the work in six subjects and three internal components, and it is the reason command-term drilling returns more per hour than any other single intervention available in the Diploma.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment is typically twenty per cent of a Diploma subject grade and it is marked against published criteria with published mark allocations. Students lose marks here more cheaply than anywhere else in the qualification, because they lose them in criteria they never read. A tutor who does nothing but make a student mark their own draft against the descriptors usually finds two or three marks immediately.

In the current science investigation, the report is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The word maximum is three thousand. Students over-invest in the method and under-invest in evaluation, which is worth exactly as much. A conclusion that compares a result to accepted literature with a cited value scores where a conclusion restating the result does not.

The Mathematics exploration is marked out of twenty: presentation four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. Two of those five criteria reward things students treat as decoration. Personal engagement and reflection together carry six of the twenty marks, and they are won by writing about choices and dead ends rather than by producing more mathematics.

The Economics portfolio works differently again, with three commentaries each marked against diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, a key concept and evaluation. Diagram marks are the most reliably available marks in the entire Diploma and the most routinely dropped, usually for unlabelled axes or an unshifted curve. None of this is secret. All of it is in the subject guide your child's school holds.

sections.heading: Past papers, used so that they teach something
paragraphs: Most families buy past papers and then use them as a confidence thermometer. The student does a paper, gets a mark, feels better or worse, and learns almost nothing. A past paper only teaches when it is marked against the official scheme by someone who can explain why a mark was withheld, and when the resulting errors are written down and revisited.

The method that works is unglamorous. Do one section, timed, not a whole paper. Mark it against the scheme with the student present, aloud. For every lost mark, decide which of four categories it belongs to: content not known, command term misread, working not shown, or time ran out. Keep a running tally across sessions. After five or six sessions the tally tells you what to teach, and it is almost never what the student guessed.

The timing dimension gets neglected and it is often the largest single cause of loss. A student who knows the content but routinely leaves the last question blank is losing a grade boundary to pacing. That is fixed by practising the last question first for a fortnight, which feels strange and works, rather than by learning more content.

One caution on materials. We reference and link official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes rather than supplying them, because reproducing board material is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to the papers, and any provider offering a downloadable archive of mark schemes is offering something it should not.
bullets: Time one section, not a whole paper, then mark it aloud with the student
Sort every lost mark into content, command term, working or time
Practise the final question first if pacing is the problem
Papers and mark schemes come from the school and the board, not from a tutor's archive

sections.heading: Umm Al Sheif, the Jumeirah school mix, and the hour that works
paragraphs: Umm Al Sheif is unusually well placed for schools. Within a short drive sit full IB continuum schools in Umm Suqeim, long-established British schools in Al Safa, a selective senior school in Al Sufouh and a Diploma school in Jumeirah. The consequence for tutoring is that the area's children are spread across several assessment systems, so a neighbour's recommendation is frequently a recommendation for the wrong specification.

The journey times are short by Dubai standards, which widens the usable session window rather than narrowing it. Most Umm Al Sheif children are home between 14:45 and 15:45, and the deciding factor on timing is usually the co-curricular programme rather than the road. A 16:30 start is realistic here for a Middle Years student in a way it is not in the outer communities, and 19:30 remains available for Diploma students with sport or music after school.

Two local wrinkles are worth naming. Palm Jumeirah families, who often share schools with Umm Al Sheif, have one road on and off the Palm, which makes afternoon returns less predictable than the distance suggests. And families whose children attend schools in Al Barsha rather than Umm Suqeim cross Sheikh Zayed Road, which is the slowest part of any Dubai afternoon between 15:30 and 17:00.

Friday is the underused window. Dubai private schools generally finish between 12:00 and 12:30 on a Friday and the weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, so a Saturday morning block catches a student rested. Families who put their heaviest Higher Level subject there report it as the session least likely to be cancelled in a busy fortnight.

sections.heading: What an hour buys at each price point in Dubai
paragraphs: Dubai tutoring prices are public if you look, and the useful question is not what is cheapest but what each band actually buys. The table below runs from the entry level upward with the source of every figure named. None of it is an IB Gram rate card; it is the market, published so you can measure any quote, ours included, against something.

At the lower end, university-student tutors online advertise from around AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya, on their own pages. What that buys is supervision and fluency work, which is genuinely useful in the Middle Years and for keeping a Diploma student on top of problem sets. What it does not buy is somebody who can explain why a Paper 3 answer lost three marks.

The middle band, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online for a qualified subject tutor, is where component-level teaching starts to be available. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Above that sit specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and premium named tutors quoted as high as AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in.

The judgement is about matching the band to the problem. A student who needs two Mathematics topics rebuilt does not need the top band. A student eight weeks from Paper 3 with a specific structural weakness does, and buying four hours at the right band beats twelve at the wrong one. That is also the argument for diagnosing from a marked script before agreeing any number of hours.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops on the IA, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own, and the line is sharper than much of this market pretends. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a research question is answerable, suggest reading, model technique on a different example, and tell a student which paragraph is weak and why. All of that is teaching and all of it raises marks.

No tutor at IB Gram will write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, compose the Theory of Knowledge essay or produce coursework. We do not sell completed assessments at any price, and we will not edit a draft into something a student could not have written. One operation in this market openly offers finished Internal Assessments; the consequence of that falls on the student as a malpractice finding, not on the seller.

Holding the line is easy when the session is structured correctly. The student reads a section aloud. The tutor asks what the criterion actually rewards, where the evidence for the claim sits, and what a reader still would not know. The student writes the fix before the next session. That loop produces a better mark than a rewrite would, and it also improves the next piece of work, which a rewrite does not.

A related point about supervision. The Extended Essay and the Internal Assessment have a school supervisor who signs the work off and who knows the cohort. A tutor works alongside that person rather than instead of them, and a tutor who encourages a student to conceal outside help is creating a risk for the child. We say so at the first session, in those words.
