process.title: Name the component, not just the subject
process.description: Send us Paper 3 in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or the evaluation criterion in a Chemistry investigation, rather than maths or chemistry. The component determines which specialist is the right one, and a component-level request is matched faster because it is a narrower search.

process.title: Send the marked script
process.description: A mock paper, a returned Internal Assessment draft or a graded essay tells us more in two minutes than a conversation does in twenty. We read it for pattern: whether the losses cluster in one command term, one topic, or the last question of every paper. Each pattern has a different fix and a different timescale.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson as a test
process.description: One per family, before any payment and with no card details taken. Ask the tutor the three questions from this page during it. Afterwards the useful check is whether your child can now explain something back, and whether the tutor named a specific thing to change rather than offering encouragement.

process.title: Write the weightings on one sheet
process.description: Before agreeing a plan, list all six subjects at their actual level with their component weightings. Most families have never seen the numbers together. The sheet usually reveals that revision time has been going to a component worth twenty per cent while one worth forty-four is untouched.

process.title: Review against a new marked piece
process.description: At the eight-week mark, look at fresh marked work rather than at how the sessions felt. If the lost marks have moved, continue. If they have not, change the tutor, the component focus or the diagnosis instead of adding hours. Re-matching is free and the diagnosis carries over.

whyPoints.title: Matched from the component backwards
whyPoints.description: A Paper 3 problem and an Internal Assessment problem are different jobs needing different people. We match from the named component, which is why we ask for it first. That is also why a specialist can usually be found quickly even for narrow Higher Level combinations.

whyPoints.title: The weightings are on the page
whyPoints.description: Component percentages, criterion letters and mark totals are published by the IB, and a tutoring provider that will not state them is hoping you do not ask. They are here so you can test us and everybody else on the same facts before you spend anything.

whyPoints.title: Short journeys are not an argument for proximity
whyPoints.description: Umm Al Sheif has short school runs, which widens your session window rather than making a local tutor necessary. The people who teach the data-based section of a science paper well are not distributed by neighbourhood; removing the drive means choosing from all of them.

whyPoints.title: Dirham figures with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate quoted here belongs to a named provider or a published rate table with its date, and none is presented as our price. That is deliberate: three of the six best-ranked pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody here writes an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, and we will not edit a draft to completion. In a market where finished assessments are openly sold, saying so matters.

whyPoints.title: No endorsement we do not have
whyPoints.description: No regulator or examination board endorses IB Gram, and nothing on this page suggests otherwise. KHDA, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE are named to explain what they govern. There is no UAE office, no invented rating and no statistic without its source.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IB tutor near me in Umm Al Sheif on the first call?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. What is Paper 2 worth in my child's subject at their level. Which Internal Assessment criterion carries the most marks and how many out of the total. What does an examiner want from evaluate that they do not want from describe. A subject specialist answers all three without hesitating, because the figures are published in the subject guide. A tutor who moves the conversation to rapport and confidence has told you what you needed to know.

faqs.question: Does proximity to Umm Al Sheif matter when choosing an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Less than almost anything else. Umm Al Sheif has short school runs, so your session window is already wide: most children are home between 14:45 and 15:45 and the limiting factor is sport or music rather than traffic. What proximity cannot do is widen the pool of people who teach a specific Higher Level component repeatedly. Removing the drive means choosing from every specialist free at your hour instead of from whoever lives within a twenty-minute radius.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send someone to our villa in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Umm Al Sheif families are one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own school material on screen. We are direct about this because parts of this market are not, implying a visit and then connecting families to tutors who are not in the country. If you want someone in the room, choose a different provider.

faqs.question: How much of my child's Diploma grade is the Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Typically twenty per cent, and in some subjects more. In the current science courses the investigation is twenty per cent of the grade, marked out of twenty-four across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a three-thousand-word maximum. In Mathematics the exploration is twenty per cent, marked out of twenty. In Economics at Standard Level the portfolio is thirty per cent. It is the most under-taught section of the Diploma relative to its weight, which is why it is often the fastest place to gain marks.

faqs.question: Which Maths IA criterion is worth the most marks?
faqs.answer: Use of mathematics, at six of the twenty available. The other four are presentation at four, mathematical communication at four, personal engagement at three and reflection at three. The pair students neglect is personal engagement and reflection, which together carry six marks and are earned by writing about the choices made, the approaches abandoned and what the result actually means. Students treat that writing as padding around the mathematics, when it is nearly a third of the mark.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter write good answers and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always a command term. The IB defines its command terms and examiners mark to them. Describe asks what, explain asks why, evaluate asks for a judgement with evidence both ways, and discuss asks for balance plus a conclusion. A strong description written in answer to an evaluate question is good writing that scores badly, and the student leaves the exam believing it went well. The fix is mechanical: underline the term, write the structure it demands, then fill it in.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 in Maths HL just a harder version of Paper 2?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way is the common planning error. Paper 3 is a long, scaffolded investigation worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade, where a student is led through an unfamiliar problem in stages. It rewards persistence through structure, careful reading of each part, and justification of every step, and it has no Standard Level equivalent. It needs its own practice on its own past papers. Students who only revise Paper 1 and Paper 2 content arrive at Paper 3 unprepared for the format itself.

faqs.question: How should we actually use past papers rather than just collecting them?
faqs.answer: One timed section at a time, not a whole paper, then marked aloud against the official scheme with your child present. For every lost mark, classify it: content not known, command term misread, working not shown, or ran out of time. Keep the tally across sessions. After five or six sessions the tally tells you what to teach, and it is almost never what the student guessed. The papers and mark schemes come from the school and the board, not from a tutor's download archive.

faqs.question: My son leaves the last question blank every time, so what fixes that?
faqs.answer: Pacing, not content, and it is usually worth a grade boundary. The counter-intuitive remedy is to practise the final question first for a fortnight, so it stops being the question he meets while tired and short of time. Alongside that, time one section rather than a full paper, and have him write a planned time per mark on the top of the page before starting. Students who learn to abandon a stuck question and return to it recover more marks than students who learn more content.

faqs.question: Which Umm Al Sheif schools run the full IB continuum?
faqs.answer: Several schools in the immediate Umm Suqeim and Umm Al Sheif cluster offer the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes in one building, while a short drive east into Al Safa and west into Al Sufouh brings British schools running IGCSE then A Level. The practical consequence for parents is that two children on the same street can be on entirely different assessment systems, so a neighbour's tutor recommendation is often a recommendation for the wrong specification. Check the programme before the person.

faqs.question: What evening hour works best for Diploma students in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: The window here is wider than in the outer communities because the journeys are short. Most children are home between 14:45 and 15:45, so 16:30 is realistic for a Middle Years student. Diploma students with sport, music or study periods after a 15:30 finish usually settle on 19:30. Saturday morning is the most reliable slot of all, since Dubai schools finish around midday on Friday and a Saturday 10:00 block catches a student rested rather than recovering.

faqs.question: Can an Umm Al Sheif student get Extended Essay help without risking malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated at the first session. A tutor can help narrow the research question, challenge the method, suggest sources, explain each criterion and say why a paragraph is weak. No tutor at IB Gram will write the Extended Essay, draft it or edit it to completion. The school supervisor signs the work off and should know outside support exists; a tutor who suggests concealing it is creating a risk that falls on your child, not on them.

faqs.question: Do you provide IB past papers and mark schemes to download?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should anyone else. Reproducing board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is copyright infringement, and for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. We reference the official documents, cite them and link to them, and we work from the papers your child's school legitimately holds. A provider advertising a downloadable archive of mark schemes is offering something it is not entitled to distribute, which is a reason for caution.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying premium rates for a single component review?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is one of the few places the top band makes arithmetic sense. If a student has a specific structural weakness in a named paper eight weeks out, two hours at the specialist band can be worth more than twelve hours at the entry band. Published Dubai rates run from around AED 33 to 65 for student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, and up to AED 650 at the premium end. Diagnose first, then choose the band.

faqs.question: What if the Higher Level combination we need has nobody free?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substitute a generalist. Common Diploma subjects at common hours are usually matched within a few days. A narrow Higher Level combination at one fixed weekday hour, or a less commonly taught language, can take a week or more, and occasionally nobody suitable is available at all. Hearing that honestly is far more useful eight weeks before a paper than finding out in session three that the tutor has never taught the component you were worried about.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "is there anybody near me who knows this syllabus?"
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages respond to a "near me" search by implying abundance: a large local team, immediate availability, somebody just around the corner. That answer is comfortable and it is usually false. The number of people in Dubai who can teach IB Chemistry Higher Level to a student aiming at a 7 - which means knowing the current guide, the Paper 2 mark scheme phrasing and the Internal Assessment criteria - is small. Not secret, not hidden behind the right search query. Small. The honest version of a "near me" page starts there.

Dubai's private-school market had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, and International Baccalaureate schools account for 7% of that enrolment. The UK curriculum accounts for 37% and the Indian curriculum 26%. So the IB cohort in this city is a minority, and the teaching population that serves it is proportionally smaller still. Once you divide that population by subject and by level - HL Chemistry is a different competence from SL Biology - the pool for any specific request is measured in individuals rather than in dozens.

Now add the "near me" filter. Umm Suqeim sits between Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road, and requiring a tutor who can be in your living room by 5pm on a Tuesday means requiring someone who both teaches your subject at your level and lives or works within a short drive. Those two conditions are independent, and multiplying them together is how families end up with a well-meaning general science tutor teaching a subject they last studied a decade ago. The grade does not move, and the family concludes that tutoring does not work.

IB Gram's position is to drop the geographic condition and keep the subject one. Tuition into Umm Suqeim is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we offer in India only - and that is a deliberate trade rather than a limitation we are shy about. It means the answer to "is there anybody who knows this syllabus" can be yes without also requiring them to be eleven minutes away.

The rest of this page is built to be used rather than admired. There is a list of questions that will expose a tutor's actual IB knowledge in a short conversation, a table of component weightings by subject and level so you can check an answer yourself, the Dubai market rates with every figure attributed and dated so you can verify them, the academic-honesty boundary around the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay stated plainly, what KHDA does and what the word approved cannot mean here, and a disclosure of the subjects where we genuinely cannot always help.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-umm-suqeim.programmesIntro: An Umm Suqeim family searching for an IB tutor is usually in one of three places: a child in the Diploma Programme now, a child in MYP 5 choosing routes, or a younger child in an IB continuum school. The programmes work differently enough that the tutoring question differs too.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects from six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Scored out of 45 points, with up to three points available from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination. Assessment is largely external, with an Internal Assessment component in nearly every subject.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost every IB tutoring enquiry from Umm Suqeim originates, and almost always for a Higher Level science or Mathematics. UAE schools sit the May session. Confirm every session and results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, because dates change and no date on a tutoring page should be acted on without that check.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years and eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by school boundaries. There are no past papers in the IGCSE sense, so tutoring works from descriptors and task-specific clarifications rather than from question banks. MYP 5 includes the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within a short drive of Umm Suqeim run the MYP, and the practical issue for families here is that MYP criterion marks do not translate into the percentage language parents expect. A tutor who cannot discuss criteria by name is not equipped for MYP work regardless of how well they know the subject content.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and descriptive rather than numerical reporting. It ends with the Year 6 Exhibition, the first extended independent inquiry most children attempt. Tutoring at this stage is rarely about content and usually about writing volume, number fluency or reading stamina.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Suqeim families in PYP schools tend to approach tutoring later than their British-curriculum neighbours, partly because PYP reporting does not produce an alarming number. The useful early intervention here is writing practice, since the volume demanded in MYP Criterion C surprises children who arrived from a PYP classroom.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Rare in Dubai, and worth checking against the current KHDA school listing rather than an older guide, because availability changes from year to year.
programmes.countryNote: Where the CP is offered near Umm Suqeim, the tutoring need is usually narrower than for the full Diploma: one or two DP courses plus support on the reflective project, which is assessed on process in a similar way to the MYP Personal Project. The same academic-honesty boundary applies to the reflective project as to any assessed work.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-umm-suqeim.subjectsIntro: Below are the DP subjects we are asked for most from this part of Dubai, with the assessment structure in brief. Use these descriptions to test a prospective tutor: a specialist will correct or extend them without hesitating.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At SL the two papers carry 40% each with the Internal Assessment at 20%. At HL there are three papers at 30%, 30% and 20% plus the IA at 20%, and Paper 3 is the extended-response investigation most HL students under-prepare for because it looks unlike anything in the textbook.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-rich and modelling-led, with the same paper weightings pattern as Analysis and Approaches. The route choice between AA and AI matters for university prerequisites, so check the target course rather than the school's default advice, particularly for engineering and economics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 carries 36% and includes a multiple-choice section and a data-based section; Paper 2 carries 44%; the Internal Assessment carries 20%. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations are the predictable HL losses, and the IA is where the most marks are recoverable with coaching that stays on the right side of academic honesty.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same component pattern as Chemistry: Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, Internal Assessment at 20%. Students lose marks less on the physics than on the extended written answers, where a correct chain of reasoning has to be visible rather than implied, and on uncertainties in the practical write-up.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-content DP science, with the same 36/44/20 component split. The failure mode is almost always command words: 'outline', 'explain', 'distinguish' and 'evaluate' demand different structures, and a correct fact in the wrong structure earns nothing on the mark scheme.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: At SL the two papers carry 35% each with the Individual Oral at 30%. At HL Paper 1 is 35%, Paper 2 is 25%, the HL Essay is 20% and the Individual Oral is 20%. The HL Essay is a formal written task on a studied text and is a frequent source of academic-honesty confusion.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At SL Paper 1 is 30%, Paper 2 is 40% and the Internal Assessment portfolio is 30%. At HL a third paper carrying 30% is added alongside Papers 1 and 2 and the IA at 20%. The IA portfolio of commentaries on real news articles is where organised students gain the most ground.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: At SL Paper 1 is 30%, Paper 2 is 45% and the Internal Assessment is 25%. At HL Paper 3 is added and the weightings shift. Paper 1 is a source-based paper with a specific question structure, and it is the component most improved by technique work rather than by additional reading.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through the exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, and contributing to the core points on the 45-point scale alongside the Extended Essay. Tutoring here is argument construction and the discipline of using real-world examples precisely; the essay itself must be entirely the student's own.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a chosen subject, supervised at school. A tutor may teach research method, question formulation, structure and referencing, and may ask the questions a supervisor will ask. A tutor may not research it, draft it, rewrite it or edit it into shape.

sections.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong filter for an IB request
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Umm Suqeim is a search with two conditions buried in it, and they pull against each other. The first condition is competence: someone who teaches your child's subject at your child's level and knows the current assessment structure. The second is proximity: someone who can be here. Each condition reduces the pool, and applying both at once reduces it multiplicatively rather than additively.

Start with the size of the IB population in this city. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with International Baccalaureate schools accounting for 7% of enrolment. Divide the teaching population serving that 7% by subject group, then by Higher and Standard Level, and any one request - HL Chemistry, HL Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, SL History - resolves to a handful of genuinely qualified people spread across the whole emirate.

Now apply the proximity filter. The qualified people are distributed by where they teach, which means Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and the Dubai schools corridor rather than evenly across residential neighbourhoods. The chance that one of them lives near Umm Suqeim, teaches your subject at your level, and is free in your one usable evening slot is low. The chance that someone nearby will cheerfully say yes anyway is high, and that is the failure this page exists to prevent.

So the honest recommendation is to drop proximity as a requirement and hold competence as an absolute. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition into Umm Suqeim over live video in Gulf Standard Time for that reason, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service. What follows is how to check competence yourself, which is more useful than any assurance we could give you.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that separate an IB specialist from a confident generalist
paragraphs: You do not need to know the syllabus to test whether somebody else does. You need questions with checkable answers. The table below gives ten, with what a specialist says and what a generalist says, and you can run it in a trial lesson or a phone call. The component weightings in the next section let you verify several of the answers independently.

The underlying principle is that IB specialists talk in components and criteria, and generalists talk in topics. Ask about a grade and a generalist will describe content coverage; a specialist will ask which paper the marks are being lost on and whether the Internal Assessment is banked. Ask about the Internal Assessment and a generalist will offer to help with it in unspecified terms; a specialist will immediately tell you what they will and will not do, because the boundary is the first thing anyone working legitimately in IB tutoring learns.

Two of the questions in the table are deliberately traps. If a tutor claims to be IB approved, accredited or certified, that claim is not available to private tutors - the IB authorises schools, not tutoring providers - and a tutor making it is either confused or careless about a claim a UAE regulator would take seriously. Similarly, a tutor who says they can get your child a 7, or who promises a fixed uplift in points, has told you something important: that they are comfortable promising an outcome no honest teacher can control.

Run the questions on us as well. The answers we would give are the ones in the specialist column, and if a tutor we match cannot give them, that is a matching failure we want to hear about rather than defend.

sections.heading: Component weightings you can check an answer against
paragraphs: This table exists so that the questions in the previous section are usable. It sets out the component structure for the DP subjects most requested from this area, with Higher and Standard Level shown separately, because the difference between the two is the single quickest way to catch a tutor who has only taught one of them.

Read it with the predicted-grade conversation in mind. If a student is predicted a 5 in HL Chemistry and the Internal Assessment is worth 20%, then an IA sitting at a low band is costing a fifth of the grade regardless of how well the papers go - and the IA, unlike Paper 2, is still in the student's hands. That arithmetic is where tutoring decisions should be made, and it is invisible if you are thinking about the subject as one undifferentiated grade.

The same logic applies to the HL extras. HL Mathematics adds a third paper worth 20%, HL English Language and Literature adds an HL Essay worth 20%, HL Economics and HL History add a third paper carrying a substantial share. Those additions are the components most often neglected, because they are unlike anything in the SL course and arrive late. A student losing ground specifically on an HL extra needs a short component block, not a general subject tutor.

Treat the figures here as a checking tool and confirm the current guide with the school, since the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle and a weighting can change between cohorts. Any tutor who cannot tell you which guide version they teach from is a tutor whose material may be two syllabuses old.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and how to verify it yourself
paragraphs: Everything in this section is checkable, which is the point. Each figure below was read from the provider's own published page during the October 2026 research round, and you can open the same pages and compare. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this search cluster publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars rather than in the currency a UAE family transacts in, so an attributed AED figure is genuinely rare here.

The published bands run as follows. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors: AED 45-150, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutor working online: AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one with travel included: AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200-500. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists: AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutors: AED 500-650 and upwards, BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What a parent can establish independently, without trusting anybody's marketing: ask for the rate per 60 minutes rather than per lesson, since a 45-minute lesson at AED 200 is a different price from an hour at AED 200. Ask whether VAT is included. Ask what happens to a session cancelled at short notice, in writing. Ask whether the tutor teaches your exact subject at your exact level and which guide version. Ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service. Five questions, all verifiable, none of which require you to know anything about the IB.

For context on what these figures represent in a household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Tutoring is the part of the education budget that is not capped, which is a reason to buy it deliberately rather than by volume. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list; our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment and Extended Essay boundary, stated plainly
paragraphs: This is the section that should decide which provider an Umm Suqeim family uses, and it is the section most pages in this market avoid. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the criteria, interrogate a research question, ask why a paragraph is there, and point at where a draft currently fails a criterion. A tutor may not research the work, draft it, rewrite sentences, restructure it for the student, or edit it to a standard the student could not reach alone.

The distinction is practical rather than philosophical. Saying "your methodology section does not explain why you controlled for temperature, and criterion wording asks for justified choices" is teaching. Rewriting the methodology section is malpractice. Asking "what does this graph actually show that your conclusion does not mention?" is teaching. Writing the conclusion is malpractice. A tutor who cannot articulate that line in the first conversation should not be near an IA.

The exposure sits with the student, which is why this matters more than a provider's reputation. An IB academic-honesty investigation can cost a candidate their diploma, and the work is submitted under their name with their supervisor's authentication. A family buying "IA help" without asking what that means is buying a risk on their child's behalf. There are operators in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright at published prices; that is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and no amount of discretion makes it safe.

What a legitimate tutor adds to IA work is substantial and worth paying for. The criteria are specific and most students never read them properly. Research questions that are too broad waste weeks. Data that was collected without a plan cannot be analysed. Reflection that says nothing scores nothing. All of that is teachable, all of it moves marks, and none of it requires anybody else's words on the page.

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulators, and what "approved" cannot mean for a tutor
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map, and ADEK in particular is named by almost nobody in this market.

What KHDA regulates is schools. It inspects them annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, publishes the reports, and operates a permit regime for training institutes with premises - a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which requires initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit is a specific thing issued to specific organisations. It is not something an individual online tutor holds, and "KHDA-approved tutor" is a phrase that should make a parent suspicious rather than reassured.

The permit that does apply to individual tutoring is MoHRE's. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific amount circulating online is unverified.

One further rule is worth knowing because it affects who you should not hire. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify it against current policy, but the direction is clear: your child's own teacher, privately, is not the arrangement to seek. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, including the subjects we cannot always cover
paragraphs: The first step is a short message with four things in it: the subject, the level, the current predicted or recent grade, and where the Internal Assessment stands. If you have a marked paper, send it. That combination tells us whether the request is a subject problem, a component problem or a core problem, and those need different tutors rather than different amounts of the same tutor.

What happens next is deliberately unexciting. We match on subject and level; you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost with your child's own work on screen; you decide. Sessions then sit in a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually from 5pm onwards for a student commuting back from Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. Timings move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan and can pause around internal deadlines. If the match is wrong you say so and it changes.

The disclosure, which this market generally does not make: we cannot always help. Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in the weeks before the May session is the hardest request to fill. Some group-two languages, Theatre, Music, Global Politics and Design Technology are thinly covered. A request in April for a rare HL subject may be answered with a waiting position rather than a tutor. When that is the situation we will say so, because the alternative is placing somebody who is learning the component alongside your child while you pay specialist rates. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, which is informative in itself.

And the fixed limits. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. No claimed approval or partnership from any regulator or examination board. No writing, drafting or editing of Internal Assessments, Extended Essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or any assessed work. No supplied past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents - we reference the official sources and work from your school's own materials. No grade promises, no guaranteed improvements, and no statistics about our own results, because we are not able to publish the sample, date and method that would make such a figure meaningful.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor near Umm Suqeim who knows my child's exact subject and level?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it is the wrong thing to require. International Baccalaureate schools account for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, so the teaching population serving the IB here is a minority of a minority, and once you split it by subject and by Higher or Standard Level any single request resolves to a handful of people spread across the emirate. Adding a requirement that one of them lives near Umm Suqeim and is free in your one usable evening slot usually empties the list. Dropping the proximity condition and holding the subject-and-level condition is what makes a real specialist available.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows the IB or just knows the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask what each component is worth. A specialist names the papers and percentages for the right level without pausing, says whether the weightings differ at Higher and Standard, gives the Internal Assessment percentage and names its criteria, and states exactly what they will and will not do on the IA before you ask. A generalist talks about topics, describes the IA as coursework, and offers unspecified help with it. The ten questions in the table on this page are designed for a ten-minute conversation and the component weightings table lets you check several answers yourself.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be IB approved or IB certified?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor claiming it has told you something useful. The IB authorises schools to deliver its programmes; it does not approve, accredit or certify private tutors or tutoring companies. Nor do KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Education approve individual tutors. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which is a specific licence for a specific kind of organisation. The permit that applies to an individual tutor in the UAE is MoHRE's private tuition work permit. IB Gram claims no approval or partnership from any of these bodies.

faqs.question: My child is predicted a 5 in an HL science. Where do the extra marks realistically come from?
faqs.answer: Start with the Internal Assessment, because it is worth 20% in the DP sciences and is the only component still fully in the student's hands. An IA sitting in a low band caps the grade regardless of paper performance. After that, look at which paper is losing marks: Paper 1 is 36% and Paper 2 is 44% in the current science guides, and the failure in Paper 2 is usually extended-response structure rather than content. A tutor who cannot tell you which of those three blocks is costing you the grade is not in a position to recover it.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do on my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the skills, explain the criteria, stress-test the research question, ask why a section is there, and point at where a draft currently fails a criterion. That is substantial work and it moves marks, because most students never read the criteria properly and most research questions start too broad. What a tutor must not do is research it, draft it, rewrite sentences, restructure it or edit it to a standard the student could not reach alone. The work is submitted under your child's name with their supervisor's authentication, so the malpractice exposure is theirs.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to cover for a family in this area?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in the run-up to the May session is the hardest single request to fill. Group-two languages beyond the common ones, Theatre, Music, Global Politics and Design Technology are thinly covered year-round. A late request in a rare Higher Level subject may be answered with a waiting position rather than a tutor, and we will say so rather than place a generalist at specialist rates. No competitor page in this search cluster discloses a coverage limit, which is worth noticing when every provider you contact says yes immediately.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the tutor has never seen my child's school?
faqs.answer: Much less than families expect. What a tutor needs is the subject guide version, the component structure, the mark schemes and your child's own marked work - none of which depends on the building. School-specific knowledge matters for internal deadlines and for how a particular coordinator runs the Extended Essay process, and that information comes from your child and the school directly. Students we support attend IB schools along the coast and in the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha clusters, but IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them and would be wary of a provider implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Why is the HL extra paper such a common problem?
faqs.answer: Because it is unlike the rest of the course and arrives late. Higher Level Mathematics adds a Paper 3 worth 20% that is an extended investigation rather than a set of textbook questions. Higher Level English Language and Literature adds an HL Essay worth 20%, a formal written task on a studied text. Higher Level Economics and History add third papers carrying substantial weight and a different style of demand. Students who are competent across the shared content often arrive at these components with no practice at all, and a short component-focused block fixes more than a general subject tutor would in a term.

faqs.question: How much should an IB specialist cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published specialist rates sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai guidance putting IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200-450 or more. A qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650. Every one of those is the provider's own published figure, read during the October 2026 research round, so you can open the pages and check. Ask for the rate per 60 minutes and whether VAT is included before comparing anything.

faqs.question: Which exam session do IB students in Dubai sit, and should I trust a date I find online?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. On specific dates, the honest answer is that no date on any tutoring page should be acted upon, including this one. The IB publishes session and results dates on ibo.org and your school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadlines that matter more day to day - draft deadlines for the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay milestones, upload dates. Several pages in this market quote dates confidently from secondary sources. Confirm with the coordinator, diary the internal deadlines rather than the external ones, and treat any site quoting a precise results date as unverified.

faqs.question: Is one subject at a time enough, or should we cover several?
faqs.answer: One, in almost every case, and two at most. A DP student already has six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a service commitment, and the week has no slack in it. Adding three weekly sessions usually means three sessions attended with nothing done between them. There is also a transfer effect worth relying on: command-word discipline and mark-scheme awareness learned properly in one subject improve performance in the others. If several subjects are genuinely weak at once, the conversation that helps is with the school about load, not with us about volume.

faqs.question: What should we do if the predicted grades came back lower than expected?
faqs.answer: Treat the predicted grades as data rather than as a verdict, and find out what they were built on. Ask which components the prediction used, whether the Internal Assessment mark was included or estimated, and which paper the marks are being lost on. A prediction based on a mock sat before half the course was taught says less than it appears to. Then decide by component: an unbanked Internal Assessment worth 20% is the most recoverable thing in the list, and paper technique is next. Buying a general tutor for a general worry is how families spend a term without moving anything.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the same boundary that applies to the Internal Assessment. For Theory of Knowledge a tutor can teach argument construction, show how real-world examples are used precisely, and question whether a claim in a draft is actually supported. For the Extended Essay a tutor can teach research method, test whether a question is answerable in 4,000 words, explain referencing conventions and ask the questions the supervisor will ask. Neither the essay nor the exhibition commentary may be written, rewritten or edited by anyone other than the student. Agree that boundary explicitly in the first session.

faqs.question: What time can an IB session realistically start for a student commuting back to Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Allow 5pm, and later if the gate is in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills. Secondary release across the Dubai schools corridor sits roughly between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and a student travelling back to Umm Suqeim from Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Emirates Hills arrives somewhere between 3:55pm and 4:35pm. Add changing, food and a break and the usable window opens around 5pm. Delivering the lesson over live video keeps that window intact, because there is no second journey and no dependency on how Sheikh Zayed Road is behaving at the time.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us not to book anything?
faqs.answer: Several situations, and we would rather say them than take the booking. If a student understands the content and simply is not doing the work, a tutor becomes an expensive supervisor and the problem survives. If four or five subjects are weak at once, the cause is usually load, sleep or something outside academics, and more sessions make the week worse. If a single mock dipped in a previously strong subject, wait for the next data point. And if a rare Higher Level subject is requested weeks before the session and we have nobody genuinely qualified, the answer is no rather than a generalist at specialist rates.

intro.heading: What 'near me' buys a Villanova family, measured in minutes
paragraphs: A 'near me' search is a request for convenience, and convenience is measurable. For a household in Villanova — the townhouse clusters off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand — the question is how many minutes proximity actually saves on an ordinary weekday afternoon, and what you give up to get them. Both halves of that calculation can be put in numbers, which is what this page does.

Start with the obvious part. If a tutor travels to you, you save no minutes at all; the tutor spends them. What you save is your own driving, which matters if the alternative is a tuition centre in Motor City or Sports City. A round trip to Motor City between 16:00 and 17:00 is twenty-five to forty minutes each way from most of Villanova, plus parking and waiting. For two children on different days that is several hours of a parent's week.

An online session saves the same driving and adds something a nearby option cannot: the tutor pool stops being local. This is where 'near me' quietly costs you. Dubai's strongest Higher Level subject teachers are distributed across the emirate and beyond, and they are not evenly spread around Dubailand. Filter by proximity and you are selecting from whoever happens to be close, then hoping the Chemistry HL specialist is among them.

IB Gram does not operate a centre near Villanova, has no UAE office, and does not send tutors to UAE addresses — home visits are a service we offer only in India. The teaching is live, one-to-one and online, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around your child's actual arrival home. Saying that plainly in the first hundred words is deliberate: a family who specifically wants a venue or a visitor should know immediately and go elsewhere.

For everyone else, the rest of this page covers what the minutes are worth, what the three locally available provider models actually offer, what the Dubai market charges and what the travel premium buys, how KHDA's inspection bands should be read when you look at your child's school report, and which regulator governs what across the emirates. Each figure carries its source.

One note on the IB specifically: Dubai's IB cohort is a minority of the private-school population — International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of students against 37 per cent on UK curricula, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. That minority status is exactly why subject-level IB expertise is thinly spread geographically, and why 'near me' is a weaker filter for an IB family than for a British-curriculum one. A British-curriculum parent in Dubailand has dozens of plausible local options for IGCSE maths. An IB parent looking for Chemistry at Higher Level, with an Internal Assessment due in a month, may find that the nearest genuinely qualified teacher is twenty-five kilometres away and fully booked on the two afternoons that would have worked.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-villanova.programmesIntro: A 'near me' search usually comes from a parent at one of three decision points: a primary child drifting, a MYP student whose criteria marks have dropped, or a Diploma student in trouble in one subject. Each needs a different kind of help.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations, so the measure of progress is capability rather than a score. The work that pays off later is number fluency without a calculator, reading stamina and the ability to write three connected sentences about a reason. Sessions are short — 40 to 45 minutes is the practical ceiling for a primary child after a bus journey — and work best with a parent nearby but not narrating.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the primary years are when Arabic becomes a real timetabled subject under KHDA requirements rather than an enrichment activity, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Villanova families moving from a country where Arabic was optional are often surprised by how much weekly instructional time it carries, which is why Arabic support is usually a separate stream rather than an add-on.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked 0-8, and a descriptor-based system that rewards reading the task sheet. A student whose MYP marks have slipped is usually slipping on one criterion — planning an investigation, or communicating reasoning — rather than across a subject. The diagnostic question is always which criterion, and it is answerable from the last two pieces of marked work.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision around Dubailand is thinner than Diploma or British-curriculum provision, so MYP families in this belt often travel further to school than their neighbours do. That lengthens the afternoon and compresses the evening, which is the practical reason an online slot is easier to sustain for an MYP student here than a venue-based one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, out of 45. Internal Assessments carry 20 to 25 per cent of most subject grades. The Diploma punishes poor sequencing more than weak ability: students who plan backwards from their school's coursework deadlines usually finish calmly, and students who do not spend DP2 recovering.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no IB exam or results dates here, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date. Get the window and the internal upload deadlines from your child's IB coordinator, and note that the school's own deadlines land weeks before the IB's.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study and a reflective project, assessed partly on written reflection against descriptors most students are never shown. It suits a student who wants IB subject depth without six-subject breadth, and tutoring usually concentrates on the DP courses carried into it plus the personal and professional skills component.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is limited, so a Villanova family weighing it is usually also weighing a school change and a longer commute. Because Ministry of Education equivalency rules are published in specific terms for the British track and not for the IB, check any post-16 route against moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority before deciding on that basis.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects most requested from the Dubailand belt, with what each assesses and the specific place marks go missing. Availability is tightest in the Higher Level sciences and in Maths AA HL.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-dependent. Students arrive expecting an easier course and meet chi-squared tests, regression and hypothesis testing. Most lost marks are process marks: an answer with no stated test, or a calculator output transcribed without the method visible. The HL content adds substantial breadth that SL students underestimate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus. HL Paper 3 is a 60-minute extended-response paper worth 20 per cent of the grade and is the single biggest differentiator at HL. Marks leak in binomial proof, sequences and chain-rule differentiation under time pressure rather than in unfamiliar content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense, with command terms deciding the ceiling on each answer. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'discuss' carry different expectations. Genetics and the nerve-and-hormone material produce the widest spread in Dubai cohorts, and HL students routinely under-practise the statistics inside data-analysis questions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the HL grade. Curly-arrow convention is the most diagnosable error in the subject: students who understand the reaction but start the arrow from the wrong electron pair lose the mark every time. Paper 1 timing is where SL students shed recoverable points.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards unit discipline, graph reading and derivation over recall. Fields and circular motion are the reliable weak points once mechanics is secure. The data-based question punishes anyone who has not plotted error bars by hand, and extended response punishes description where derivation was asked for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest available gain: a correctly labelled, correctly shifted diagram earns marks prose cannot recover. The three IA commentaries, each on a different unit and each word-limited, separate organised students from capable ones. HL adds quantitative work students often meet too late.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based and stimulus-driven. Students lose marks by applying Ansoff or break-even correctly in the abstract and never referring to the case. The pre-released Paper 1 case study rewards structured reading months in advance, which almost nobody does without prompting.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two of three assessed components are oral or non-literary, which surprises students expecting novel essays. The Individual Oral requires a global issue narrow enough to sustain ten minutes and two extracts chosen well in advance; a vague global issue is the commonest cause of a low mark.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Distinct from the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision in school but running alongside it. Assessed through text handling, writing and two oral components. Register is where non-Arab students lose marks most often — formal tasks answered in informal grammar — rather than vocabulary range.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentary, plus a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. More coachable than students expect: most low marks come from objects that illustrate a point rather than evidence a knowledge claim. A tutor may challenge the reasoning; the writing must be the student's own work.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research with a school supervisor. Support is process coaching: narrowing the question, building a source base, managing reflection sessions and keeping to the limit. We do not draft, rewrite or edit an Extended Essay to completion, and no legitimate tutor will.

sections.heading: What a 'near me' search actually returns in Dubailand
paragraphs: Type the phrase from a Villanova address and the results are shaped by who has a verified business location, not by who teaches the IB well. You get tuition centres in Motor City and Sports City with map pins, directory listings for agencies based elsewhere in Dubai that have added 'Dubailand' to a service-area list, and freelance adverts whose location field is aspirational. None of those signals subject-level competence at Higher Level.

That is not a criticism of the businesses; it is how local search works. A map pack ranks proximity, prominence and relevance to a business category. 'Teaches Chemistry HL to a standard that fixes a 4 into a 6' is not a business category. So the result set answers a question about geography while the parent was asking a question about teaching, and the gap between the two is invisible until week three.

The practical move is to run two searches rather than one. Use the local search to find out what venues and in-home options genuinely exist near you and what they charge, because that is real information and this page quotes the market rates below. Then run a second, separate search on subject and level — Maths AA HL, Biology HL, Economics IA — and compare the two shortlists. For a mainstream need they may overlap. For a Higher Level science they usually do not.

IB Gram sits firmly on the second list. There is no centre near Villanova, no UAE office, and no tutor who will arrive at a Dubailand address; home visits are an India-only service. What exists is one-to-one live online teaching with a specialist in the specific subject and level, scheduled around the bus. If that trade is not what you want, the local list is genuinely worth working through.

sections.heading: The minutes proximity actually saves, counted honestly
paragraphs: Put numbers on it and the convenience argument changes shape. The table below compares the three realistic options for a Villanova family on an ordinary weekday: drive to a centre in the nearest cluster, host a tutor who drives to you, or run the session online. The columns are the things that actually differ — your driving, the tutor's driving, how much of the household's evening is consumed, and how wide the pool of available teachers is.

The result is not subtle. A centre in Motor City costs a parent fifty to eighty minutes of driving and waiting per session. An in-home visit costs the parent nothing in driving but is paid for in the rate, because the tutor's forty to sixty minutes each way is priced into the hour — market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor online. An online session costs neither side any travel at all.

The column worth staring at is the last one. Proximity-based options are selected from whoever is close; online options are selected from whoever teaches the subject. For Year 7 maths that difference may not matter. For Chemistry HL with an Internal Assessment due, it is the difference between a specialist and a capable generalist, and the generalist will cost the same or more.

Where a venue genuinely wins: a student who cannot concentrate at home, a household with no quiet room, or a parent who wants the child out of the house for an hour. Those are real reasons and the centres in Motor City and Sports City serve them. They are not reasons that apply to most Villanova families most of the time.

sections.heading: The three provider models near you, compared on model not brand
paragraphs: 'Near me' returns at least three different kinds of business, and parents often compare their prices without noticing that they are not the same product. A tuition centre sells scheduled capacity: a room, a timetable and a teacher who may be assigned rather than chosen. A freelance tutor sells their own hours directly, which is why rates vary so widely and why verification falls entirely on the parent. An agency or platform sells matching and replacement.

The table below compares those models on the things that actually differ in practice. It deliberately compares models rather than brands, and quotes rates only where the party named has published them, with the source stated. Comparing yourself against an unnamed 'other platforms' straw man is the standard move in this market and it tells a parent nothing.

Two columns deserve attention. The replacement column matters because tutor turnover is the commonest cause of a failed arrangement: when the tutor leaves, a freelance relationship ends and the family starts again, whereas a matched arrangement should produce a replacement with the notes intact. The permit column matters because private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE permit, and a parent hiring directly is the one who should be checking it.

What none of the models can offer is a guarantee of a grade, and any that does should be read carefully. There is no honest version of that promise in any model, and a refund clause only means something if the exact terms are published on the same page where the promise is made.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Take the proximity question to its logical end: what is a nearby tutor's drive actually worth in money? The answer is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, and for Villanova it sits at the top of that spread because the community is far enough out that few tutors reach it quickly. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, while independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. The same qualified tutor teaching online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300.

That premium does not buy teaching. It buys presence, and presence is worth paying for in specific cases: a young child who needs an adult in the room, a student with a need that makes screen work genuinely harder, a household where the only quiet surface is the dining table and someone has to sit at it. Those are real. Paying the premium because 'in person must be better' is the commonest avoidable cost in this belt.

The table below lays out the full market from the budget end upwards, with every figure attributed to whoever published it. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list; we quote per student after the free trial because an Economics IA block and a Year 5 numeracy slot are not the same product and should not carry the same number. Monthly packages visible in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

For budgeting, Bestimate's monthly estimates for one hour a week are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Diploma family running one specialist subject weekly for a year should plan against the third of those figures, not the first.

sections.heading: Where availability is genuinely tight, and what we do about it
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is a strange silence given that every tutoring service has one. Ours is specific and worth stating: the tightest availability is in Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Maths AA HL, Theory of Knowledge supervision, and Arabic as a first language at Diploma level. Those are the requests most likely to come back with a wait rather than a slot.

What happens when a request lands in one of those gaps matters more than the gap itself. The honest options are to offer the windows that genuinely exist even if they are not your preferred ones, to give a realistic estimate of when the preferred window may open, or to say that we cannot cover it and that you should look elsewhere. All three get used. What does not happen is a general tutor placed into a specialist slot, which solves our scheduling problem by transferring the real one to you.

This is also where the geography argument inverts completely. A near-me search in Dubailand for Chemistry HL has a genuinely small candidate set, and a family that insists on proximity may find nobody at all and settle for a generalist. Removing the travel requirement means the question becomes one of calendar availability rather than catchment, which is a much easier constraint to work around.

Practical advice, independent of who you use: for niche Higher Level subjects and for coursework supervision, ask three to four weeks before you need to start. The week before an Internal Assessment deadline is when every family in Dubai asks the same question, and good supervision cannot be conjured at that notice by anyone.

sections.heading: Reading your school's KHDA inspection report properly
paragraphs: KHDA is 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education' in Dubai, per u.ae, and it inspects private schools on a six-band scale. Those bands appear in school marketing constantly and are understood by parents rarely. They describe a whole school across many measures, which means a school in a strong band can still have a weak department, and a school in a middling band can have an outstanding one.

That is the practical lesson for a tutoring decision. The question is never 'is this a good school' but 'how is this department, for this subject, at this level'. A Diploma cohort's results in Chemistry HL can differ sharply from the school's overall band, and the school's own subject reports or a conversation with the head of department tells you more about whether your child needs support than the inspection headline does.

Context worth having: Dubai's private sector has 227 schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students as of 2024-25, and the sector is still growing — seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

A necessary clarification, because the phrase is abused across this market: naming KHDA and explaining what it does is not a claim of approval. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit of any kind, and the KHDA Educational Services Permit that does exist applies to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any service that describes its tutors as approved by KHDA is making a claim you should ask it to evidence with a permit number.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: This is the part of a Dubai IB timetable that tutoring services almost never mention, and it is mandatory. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific enough to matter. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. For these subjects specifically, the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

What that means for tutoring is narrower than parents assume and should be said plainly. Support in these subjects follows the school's own approved programme rather than any alternative syllabus, and it works best as language and study-skills help alongside the school's material. For a non-Arab Diploma student, these periods are real additional workload in a language not used at home, and they are frequently the only part of the week nobody is helping with.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the seven emirates
paragraphs: A Villanova family only needs KHDA today, but UAE households move, and the regulator changes with the emirate rather than following the school group. The map is complete and published on u.ae, and it is worth knowing before a move to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah turns into a surprise.

Dubai sits with KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate — and which, remarkably, is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this market. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education.

The powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. At the federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations — which is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

One Abu Dhabi rule is worth knowing even from Dubai, because families cross the border for schools. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify it before relying on the exact wording — but never arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately.
