sections.heading: Reading an offer literally
paragraphs: Conditional offers for Diploma candidates are usually compound: a points total plus specific subject grades at a specific level. Taking an illustrative example rather than any real institution's requirement, an offer expressed as a total with three named Higher Level grades requires every element of it. A candidate who exceeds the total while falling a grade short in one named Higher Level subject has not met the offer, and that is the single most common way a place is lost.

This is not a trick and it is not unusual. The named subjects are there because the course needs them, and an admissions office that specified Higher Level Chemistry at a particular grade did so because the first year of the degree assumes it. Substituting a brilliant Standard Level grade or an extra point elsewhere does not supply what the course was asking for.

The practical discipline takes ten minutes and is skipped constantly. Print every offer. Underline each condition separately. Identify which one is furthest from the student's current position, and make that the binding condition. Then weight the final term's funded hours towards it rather than spreading them across six subjects. A student spending equal time on everything when one Higher Level grade is at risk is allocating by anxiety.

The table sets out how different offer shapes should change a plan. It uses generic shapes rather than any institution's actual requirement, because requirements differ by institution, campus, intake and route, and should be read from the published source for the specific intake and kept on file.

sections.heading: The calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: An admissions year is a logistics exercise and the collisions are predictable, which means they can be planned around. The main UCAS deadline falls in January each year, with the current date published on UCAS's own site. United States applications run through the autumn and winter, with early rounds considerably earlier. UAE university applications run on their own institutional timetables. Any Ministry equivalency work runs on the Ministry's.

Those external dates land on top of the school's internal deadlines. Internal Assessment deadlines in six subjects, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay, and the predicted grade finalisation all sit in the same half of the final year as the applications. That overlap, rather than the difficulty of the courses, is what makes the second Diploma year feel unmanageable to families who have not mapped it.

No IB examination or results date appears on this page. The IB publishes its own dates and they could not be verified from the IB's own site for this page, so your Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed dates for your child's session. What can be said is the order, which does not change: internal deadlines, then predictions, then applications, then mocks, then written papers, then results.

The table counts the year backwards from results with what should already be settled at each point. Build your own version with your school's actual dates in the first term; the exercise takes half an hour and is the single most useful piece of admissions preparation available to a Dubai family.

sections.heading: The core points, and why they are the cheapest on the sheet
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points towards the forty-five, and they are the only points in the Diploma that are banked well before the written papers. For a candidate sitting one point below an offer total, that makes them the cheapest points available, and they are also the ones most often left until the deadline week.

The asymmetry is worth stating. A point gained on a written paper in the final term requires moving a subject grade, which means recovering a substantial number of raw marks under examination conditions. A point gained from the core requires a better Extended Essay and a better Theory of Knowledge essay, written over months, with feedback, without a clock. Those are not equally difficult tasks, and yet families consistently fund the first and ignore the second.

The practical work is narrow and well understood. For the Extended Essay, the question has to be narrow enough to research in four thousand words, which is a single session's work and determines the ceiling of everything after it. For the Theory of Knowledge essay, the prescribed title has to be engaged with rather than written around, which is a structural discipline rather than a knowledge one.

The boundary applies here as everywhere. A tutor can test whether a research question is researchable, explain what a criterion descriptor requires, challenge an argument, and comment on a draft by naming the criterion and the band. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. These are assessed components, and submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice with the consequence falling on the student.

sections.heading: Equivalency and attestation, described rather than promised
paragraphs: If a student intends to study at a UAE institution, or to work in the UAE afterwards, recognition of their secondary certificate by the Ministry of Education is likely to come up. It is a process with its own documentation requirements and its own timetable, run by the Ministry, and no tutoring service performs it, secures it or can guarantee its outcome. Describing it accurately is useful; implying any control over it is not.

Two tracks have published requirements that are stable enough to state. On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB Diploma specifically, no points threshold appears anywhere on this page, because none could be verified from an official Ministry source for it. That omission is deliberate and it is the honest position. A figure circulating on tutoring sites is exactly the kind of number a family plans around and then discovers was invented, and the Ministry's own channel is where the current requirement should be read.

The practical advice is short. Start the documentation conversation early rather than in the final term, because certified documents and attestations take time that an examination year does not have spare. Ask the school what it has seen other families need. And treat tutoring as entirely separate from this: it is not a requirement for equivalency, for admission or for progression, and any suggestion otherwise is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: What a tutor can legitimately do, and what we do not do
paragraphs: It is worth being precise, because this is a market with a good deal of blurring. A tutor can raise a subject grade by teaching the subject and by marking work against the published standard. A tutor can coach the process on an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay without producing any of it. A tutor can help a student understand what an offer requires and where their marks currently sit against it. That is a real and useful contribution to an admissions outcome.

What IB Gram does not do is act as an admissions consultancy. We do not write personal statements or application essays, we do not submit applications, we do not advise on which institutions to apply to as a commercial service, and we do not represent students to universities. A student's counsellor at school owns that work, and in Dubai most IB schools have one. Asking the counsellor early and arriving prepared gets more from them than any paid substitute.

Nor can anybody promise a place. No tutor, platform or consultancy can promise admission, a points total or a subject grade, and any claim of that kind should end the conversation. Tutoring is also not a requirement for admission: students are admitted to universities every year without any of it, and suggesting otherwise is a false-urgency claim about somebody else's decision process.

The honest offer is therefore narrower than the category name suggests, and more checkable. Identify the binding condition from the written offer. Measure where the student currently stands in that subject with a marked timed paper. Fund that subject and the core points. Log raw marks so the gap is visible rather than assumed. Everything on this page is designed so a family can judge that work themselves rather than take it on trust.

sections.heading: The evidence record for an admissions year
paragraphs: In a year with this much happening, the record is what prevents drift. Four documents, kept together, do most of the work: the printed offers with their conditions underlined, a single calendar holding internal deadlines and application dates, a log of raw marks by subject with dates and conditions, and the comments on core component drafts.

The raw mark log is the one families never keep and the one that matters most. For each offer-critical subject, record the paper, the level, the date, the conditions and the raw mark, every time one is sat. Over a term that produces a line rather than an impression, and a line can be compared against the grade the offer requires. Without it, the conversation in March is about feelings, and feelings in an admissions year are reliably pessimistic.

The second useful document is a one-page summary of where each offer condition stands: met, likely, at risk, or not reachable. Updating it monthly forces an honest conversation and often reveals that the subject everybody is worried about is comfortable while a quieter one is the actual risk. That reallocation is frequently worth more than additional hours.

The table lists the documents with who holds them and what each one is for. None of them requires expertise to maintain, and all of them can be kept in one folder. In a year where everything happens at once, a folder beats a memory, and it also means that any conversation with a teacher, a counsellor or an admissions office starts from the same set of facts rather than from three different recollections of what was agreed.

sections.heading: Buying this honestly
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates give the arithmetic for the part a tutor can affect. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED's premium named tier at AED 650. A twelve-session offer-critical subject block therefore runs roughly AED 2,400 to 5,400, and a four-session core points block AED 800 to 1,800.

Refuse any admissions service that promises a place, a points total or a subject grade. Nobody can deliver those, the claim is unverifiable, and a provider willing to make it is telling you something useful about the rest of their advice. Refuse equally any suggestion that tutoring is required for admission or for equivalency, which is a false-urgency claim about somebody else's process.

Refuse any offer to write a personal statement, an application essay, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. The first two are the student's own representation of themselves and the last two are assessed components where submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice, with the consequence falling on the student.

Insist instead on three things. The binding condition identified from the written offer, in writing. A marked timed paper in that subject with a raw mark and a date, as a baseline. And a monthly comparison against the grade the offer requires. No university requirement, no Ministry threshold for the IB, no success rate and no admission statistic appears anywhere on this page, because requirements go stale and the rest could not be produced with a sample size, a date and a method.

process.title: Print the offers and underline every condition
process.description: Each condition separately, for every offer including the fallback choices. Then identify which one sits furthest from the student's current position. That is the binding condition, and it should drive the final term rather than the subject that generates the most anxiety at home.

process.title: Ask what feeds the predicted grade, and when it closes
process.description: Put the question to the coordinator in the first Diploma year, not the final term. If mock performance weighs heavily, the weeks before mocks are the ones worth funding. If internal assessment marks weigh heavily, the first Internal Assessment is effectively an admissions document.

process.title: Baseline the offer-critical subject
process.description: One whole timed paper at the real level, marked against the published standard, with losses classified as content, command term, method or time. Record the raw mark, the level, the date and the conditions. That number is what the monthly comparison is measured against.

process.title: Secure the core points early
process.description: Up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, banked long before the written papers and written without a clock. For a candidate a point short of an offer total these are the cheapest points available, and they close in the first half of the final year.

process.title: Model the retake arithmetic before results
process.description: Work out, in advance, which component marks would need to move and by how much if a condition is missed, and ask the institutions in writing what they will accept and by when. A decision made from component marks beats one made in the week after results.

whyPoints.title: We state what a tutor cannot do
whyPoints.description: No tutor, platform or consultancy can promise a place, a points total or a subject grade, and tutoring is not a requirement for admission or for equivalency. Saying that plainly is unusual in this category and it is the precondition for trusting anything else on the page.

whyPoints.title: The binding condition drives the spending
whyPoints.description: Funded hours go to the subject the written offer actually names, identified by printing the offer and underlining each condition. Optimising a points total while missing a named Higher Level grade is the most common way a Dubai family loses a place.

whyPoints.title: The core points are treated as the cheapest
whyPoints.description: Up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, written over months without a clock, against a point on a written paper requiring recovery of many raw marks under examination conditions. Those are not equally difficult tasks.

whyPoints.title: No requirements reproduced, on purpose
whyPoints.description: University requirements differ by institution, campus, intake and route, and no IB points figure for Ministry equivalency could be verified from an official source. Both are read from the source for the specific intake and kept on file rather than published here.

whyPoints.title: A raw mark log instead of reassurance
whyPoints.description: Paper, level, date, conditions and raw mark, every time one is sat, compared monthly against the grade the offer requires. Without it, the conversation in the final term is conducted on feelings, which in an admissions year are reliably pessimistic.

faqs.question: How is a predicted grade actually produced?
faqs.answer: It is a professional judgement by subject teachers, assembled from evidence rather than calculated. The usual inputs are classwork across the first Diploma year and the start of the second, internal assessment marks, and performance in the school's internal or mock examinations, weighted differently by different schools. So the useful question is not what the prediction is but what informs it and when it is finalised. Ask the coordinator in the first Diploma year, because almost all the evidence behind the prediction is generated before it closes.

faqs.question: Can a predicted grade be changed once it has been issued?
faqs.answer: Rarely by request, and sometimes by evidence. Asking for an uplift on the grounds that a student is capable of more does not usually move anything, because a teacher cannot weigh an assertion. What a teacher can weigh is a marked paper at genuine difficulty, sat under timing, in the subject where the prediction looks low relative to recent work. Bring that rather than an argument. And ask early, since the useful window is before the prediction is finalised rather than after.

faqs.question: What does an offer of a points total plus named Higher Level grades mean?
faqs.answer: Both, independently. Taking an illustrative shape rather than any institution's actual requirement, an offer expressed as a total with three named Higher Level grades requires the total and every named grade. Exceeding the total while falling a grade short in one named Higher Level subject does not meet it, and that is the most common way a place is lost. The named subjects are there because the course assumes them. Print the offer, underline each condition separately, and plan the final term around the furthest one.

faqs.question: Does a Standard Level grade ever substitute for a named Higher Level grade?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it should never be assumed. Where a course names a subject at Higher Level, the specification is usually literal, and a Standard Level grade in the same subject is not treated as supplying what the course asked for however high it is. Nor does an extra point elsewhere compensate. The only reliable source is the institution's published requirement for the intake in question, read directly and kept on file, including for the insurance choices where this mistake does the most damage.

faqs.question: What do the three core points actually do for an offer?
faqs.answer: They count towards the total, up to a maximum of three from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combined, and they are the only points banked well before the written papers. For a candidate sitting one point below a required total they are the cheapest points on the sheet, because they come from work written over months with feedback and no clock rather than from recovering raw marks under examination conditions. They are also the points most often left until a deadline week, which is why they are worth funding early.

faqs.question: What is equivalency and will my child need it?
faqs.answer: It is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign secondary certificate, and it typically matters if a student intends to study at a UAE institution or to work here afterwards. It is the Ministry's own process with its own documentation requirements and timetable, and no tutoring service performs it, secures it or can guarantee its outcome. Start the documentation conversation early rather than in the final term, because certified documents take time an examination year does not have spare. Read the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: When do application deadlines fall relative to the IB calendar?
faqs.answer: In the same half of the final year as the internal deadlines, which is the collision that makes the year feel unmanageable. The main UCAS deadline falls in January each year with the current date on UCAS's own site, United States applications run through the autumn and winter with early rounds much earlier, and UAE institutions and the Ministry run their own timetables. Meanwhile internal assessment deadlines in six subjects, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay all close. Build one calendar in the first term.

faqs.question: Do you write personal statements or act as admissions consultants?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, so what we can legitimately affect is the grade in a subject an offer names and the quality of the student's own academic work. We do not write personal statements or application essays, submit applications, or represent students to institutions. Your child's school counsellor owns that work, and most Dubai IB schools have one. Arriving at that meeting with the offers printed and the binding condition identified gets considerably more out of it than any paid substitute would.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses an offer condition by one grade?
faqs.answer: Contact the institution rather than assuming the outcome, because responses vary and some are more flexible than families expect, particularly where the total was met and a single named grade was narrowly missed. Do that quickly and in writing. In parallel, get the component marks behind the subject grade rather than just the grade, because they determine whether a retake could realistically reach the condition and by when. A decision made from component marks beats one made from a disappointing number.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities read the Diploma the same way as institutions abroad?
faqs.answer: They read it, and the specific requirements differ by programme rather than by institution, which is the practical point. A programme at a local institution may name subjects and grades, or a points total, or additional local requirements, and a sister programme at the same institution may differ. Read the published requirement for the exact programme and intake, keep a copy, and check whether equivalency or attestation is expected as part of the process. No institution's requirement is reproduced on this page for that reason.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to our home in Dubai for this work?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. In an admissions year that is a practical benefit. A candidate carrying six subjects, the core and several application deadlines can take a late session without anybody adding a drive to the evening, and the marked work and raw mark log accumulate in one file the student can show a teacher or a counsellor.

faqs.question: Which subject should we fund if an offer looks at risk?
faqs.answer: The one the offer names that sits furthest from the student's current position, measured from a marked timed paper rather than from a report comment. That is frequently not the subject causing the most anxiety at home, and the reallocation is often worth more than extra hours. Where an offer names only a points total, fund the two subjects with the most recoverable marks instead, which means those losing marks to command terms, method and pacing rather than to absent content.

faqs.question: Is a retake worth it to secure a university place?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is answerable with arithmetic rather than hope. Get the component marks, not the subject grade, and establish whether the loss was concentrated in one paper and whether it was habit-shaped or content-shaped. Then ask the institution in writing whether it will accept a result from a later session for the intake in question and by what date. Where the condition is reachable and the institution will wait, a narrow block has a good case. Where either fails, it does not.

faqs.question: What should we keep on file across the admissions year?
faqs.answer: Four things, in one folder. The printed offers with every condition underlined separately, including the fallback choices. One calendar holding the school's internal deadlines, the mock window and every application date. A raw mark log recording paper, level, date, conditions and mark for each timed attempt in the offer-critical subjects. And the comments on core component drafts, naming criterion letters and bands. Add a monthly one-page summary marking each offer condition as met, likely, at risk or unreachable.

faqs.question: Does tutoring improve the chance of an offer?
faqs.answer: It can raise a subject grade, which is the part of an application a tutor is able to affect, and that is all anyone can honestly claim. It is not a requirement for admission: students are admitted every year with no tutoring at all, and any suggestion that it is required is a false-urgency claim about somebody else's decision process. No success rate or admission statistic appears on this page, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method, and nobody can promise a place.

dubai/ib-university-admissions-guidance.closingHeading: Print the offer, then measure the gap
dubai/ib-university-admissions-guidance.closingBody: Admissions work in an IB year is mostly document discipline. Print every offer including the fallbacks and underline each condition separately, so the binding one is obvious rather than assumed. Ask the coordinator what feeds the predicted grade and when it closes, early enough that the answer is still useful. Then take one marked timed paper in the subject the offer actually names and record the raw mark, the level, the date and the conditions. Book the free trial lesson, bring that script, and ask for a monthly comparison against the grade the offer requires. Nobody can promise a place; a measured gap is better than reassurance.

dubai/icse-to-igcse-transition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below name the board and syllabus code they teach alongside the subject. For a student arriving from ICSE the content is rarely the problem, so the match that matters is a tutor who marks the exact specification the new school has entered them for.

intro.heading: A strong starting position, measured properly
paragraphs: ICSE is a broad and demanding programme, and a student arriving from it into an IGCSE course in Dubai brings three specific advantages that are worth naming before anything else. They have studied physics, chemistry and biology as separate subjects rather than as a combined science, which maps directly onto the IGCSE separate-science route. Their English has usually been developed through both language and literature work, which is the closest thing to a clean transfer available in this move. And they have produced internally assessed project work, so the idea that a mark can come from something other than a written paper is familiar.

None of that means the move is frictionless. IGCSE assesses through a published mark scheme that pays for a visible route to the answer, splits several subjects into tiers with different grade ceilings, and in the Cambridge sciences includes a written paper about practical work that no Indian board sets in the same form. Those are real adjustments. They are also short ones, and the reason to start by listing the strengths is that a plan which treats this as a deficit will bill for re-teaching content the student already holds.

This page is organised around evidence, because the only honest way to know whether the adjustment is happening is to look at marked work. A grade in the first term tells you very little: the student is learning the system rather than performing in it. Two comparable papers sat under the same conditions a month apart, with their raw marks written down side by side, tells you a great deal. So does a topic list that shortens and an error log that narrows.

The first administrative step comes before any of that. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and set different papers. The statement of entry carries the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, and reading it takes thirty seconds. Families arriving from a different system have no reason to know the distinction matters, and Dubai households frequently contain children on both boards.

The second is the series. UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June series with November available as a second route, and the Pearson May/June window with a November window. Cambridge offers the February and March sitting to India only, which is relevant here because a family that has just relocated carries the Indian calendar in memory, where it was correct. Entry deadlines belong to the exam centre, usually the school, and fall months before the papers.

Sessions are delivered online, one to one, over live video with the script on a shared screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service. For a family mid-relocation the online format keeps both the tutor and the accumulating record of marked work continuous, which matters more than any single lesson does.

dubai/icse-to-igcse-transition.programmesIntro: Where a student joins decides whether this is a conventions job or a coverage job. These are the three entry points Dubai families encounter, with what each one actually needs.

programmes.name: Joining before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: The cheapest entry. A full year exists before the IGCSE syllabus starts, which is time to meet a published mark scheme, build the habit of writing method out, and choose options on evidence. An ICSE student at this point usually needs only the conventions, because the content pace is comparable.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools confirm IGCSE options during Year 9. An ICSE student used to studying three sciences separately should be asked specifically whether the new school's triple science route is available, because a combined award would narrow what they have already built.

programmes.name: Joining at the start of the IGCSE course
programmes.description: A clean entry point with the syllabus starting from the beginning. The work is paper anatomy rather than catching up: tier, command words, written method, and the Cambridge practical component. Four to six marked tasks usually settle the adjustment, with the raw marks showing it.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions for Core and Extended are confirmed during or at the end of Year 10 in Dubai schools. An ICSE mathematics background typically supports Extended, and a marked Extended paper under timing is the evidence that makes the case to the school.

programmes.name: Joining partway through
programmes.description: Harder, because the series is fixed and part of the syllabus has been taught in the student's absence. Coverage gaps and conventions gaps both exist, and they must be separated in writing, since one is measured in terms and the other in weeks.
programmes.countryNote: For a mid-Year-11 arrival the first question is which board, code and tier the school has entered the student for, and whether the centre's deadline has passed. That decides whether June or the November route is the realistic target, and it is an administrative question rather than an academic one.

dubai/icse-to-igcse-transition.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described in terms of what an ICSE student already holds and what the IGCSE paper will still ask for, which is the comparison that makes a short, evidence-led plan possible.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: ICSE mathematics generally supports the Extended or Higher route comfortably on content. The recoverable marks are method marks: the scheme pays for a visible route, and a student trained to reach answers efficiently loses them until the habit changes. Three marked papers is the usual fix.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Having studied physics as a separate subject is a real advantage, since the IGCSE separate-science route assumes exactly that depth. What is new is units and significant figures treated as marks, and on Cambridge codes a written paper about practical work.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Equation work and mole calculations transfer well from ICSE. The marks sit in conventions: state symbols, named reagents and conditions, and visible working. These are invisible in an ICSE report and visible on a first marked IGCSE script.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: ICSE biology builds strong structured recall. IGCSE rewards precise accepted wording and data interpretation instead, so practice has to be done with the published scheme open rather than from a textbook, which students resist and which works.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: The closest transfer in this move. An ICSE student who has handled both language and literature work arrives with the reading and writing range the paper expects, and usually needs only the task conventions: audience, form and purpose on directed writing.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Where a school offers it, an ICSE background makes this a strong option rather than a risk. The adjustment is to timed comparative and extract-based response structures rather than to the reading itself, which is a matter of two or three marked attempts.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: ICSE covers these within a broader group, so the content emphasis shifts. Source handling structure in history and case study detail with place names and figures in geography are the specific conventions to learn, and both are patterns rather than content.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Often a good fit for an ICSE-trained student heading towards A-Level mathematics or Higher Level IB. Coverage among tutors is thinner than in core mathematics, so it is worth asking about availability early rather than in the examination term.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: ICSE computer applications gives a reasonable foundation, and the IGCSE route is more formal in its treatment of algorithms and data representation. Worth checking which of the two codes the school offers, since they assess quite different things.

dubai/icse-to-igcse-transition.regionsIntro: This move happens across the Dubai communities with established Indian-curriculum provision, and the notes below cover what that means for scheduling and for getting the specification right.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: Indian, British and IB schools within a short radius, so households move between systems without moving home. Where one child is still on ICSE and another has moved to IGCSE, practice folders labelled by board prevent a term of wasted work.

regions.name: Karama, Oud Metha and Bur Dubai
regions.note: Long-established Indian school provision and several British-curriculum options nearby. The statement of entry rather than the school's prospectus is what identifies which specification a transferring student is actually sitting.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Large eastern communities with long commutes, so weekday evening sessions run late and get cancelled. A weekend slot for the timed paper and a short midweek session on practical paper conventions is the pattern that survives a term.

regions.name: International City and Silicon Oasis
regions.note: High turnover with many direct arrivals from India, including mid-year. This is where genuine coverage gaps are most likely, and where separating them from conventions gaps in writing matters most.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Apartment communities with steady new arrivals. Students placed by age may join Year 11 with part of the syllabus already taught, which changes the plan from conventions work to real teaching.

regions.name: Deira and Hor Al Anz
regions.note: Dense school provision and an active tuition-centre market. The useful question for any local provider is price per student per hour, group size, and whether work is marked individually rather than as a class.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Indian-curriculum schools students move from
schoolClusters.note: Students leaving these schools arrive with broad coverage, separate sciences and strong English. The adjustment is paper conventions, which is measurable in weeks when it is named and invisible for a term when it is not.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai British-curriculum schools receiving them
schoolClusters.note: These schools enter candidates with both Cambridge and Pearson and sometimes across different boards within one timetable. Ask specifically whether the separate-science route is available, since an ICSE student has already built that depth.

dubai/icse-to-igcse-transition.modesIntro: Three ways to run this move, all online, each producing a different piece of the record.

modes.title: Baseline and specification check
modes.description: A short first engagement reading board, code, tier and series off the statement of entry, confirming the centre's deadline, then having the student sit one whole paper of that exact specification under timing. The tutor marks it to the published scheme and separates coverage gaps from conventions gaps in writing.
bullets: Board, code, tier and series confirmed in writing
One correct-specification paper sat under real timing
Coverage gaps and conventions gaps listed separately
A raw mark and a date recorded as the baseline

modes.title: Conventions block with bracketed marks
modes.description: Four to six sessions on the mark scheme conventions that are new: written method, command words, accepted biological wording, context application. Bracketed by two comparable marked papers so the result is a pair of raw marks rather than an impression of progress.
bullets: A marked paper before and after, same conditions
Written method drilled on the student's own working
Command words matched before any answer is written
Both raw marks reported side by side at the end

modes.title: Practical paper block
modes.description: Four sessions on the Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper, which needs no laboratory and which no Indian board sets in the same form. Results table conventions, instrument precision, scales, lines of best fit, and specific sources of error. The highest-return block for a transferring science student.
bullets: Fifteen results tables drawn to the scheme's conventions
Instrument precision practised, including the half-division rule
Specific errors and improvements, never human error
A marked practical paper at each end of the block

sections.heading: Three advantages an ICSE student actually arrives with
paragraphs: Transition advice tends to describe every curriculum move as a gap to be closed, and in this case that framing loses real information. The first advantage is the sciences. An ICSE student has studied physics, chemistry and biology as separate subjects, which is the structure the IGCSE separate-science route assumes. A student arriving from a combined-science background into triple science has a genuine depth problem; an ICSE student does not, and should be asked whether the triple route is available at the new school before being placed on a combined award.

The second is English. ICSE develops both language and literature work, and the reading and writing range that produces maps closely onto IGCSE First Language English and, where a school offers it, onto an IGCSE literature specification. This is the nearest thing to a clean transfer available in any of the Indian-board moves, and it means English is usually the wrong place to spend money in the first term.

The third is internal assessment. ICSE subjects carry internally assessed components alongside the written paper, so the notion that a mark can come from work produced over time rather than in an examination hall is already familiar. That matters later, at A-Level coursework or at IB Internal Assessment, more than it does at IGCSE itself, but it is a habit worth recognising rather than rebuilding.

The table sets each advantage against where it lands in an IGCSE programme and what still has to be learned. The third column is the honest part: an advantage reduces the work rather than removing it, and knowing which conventions remain is what keeps a plan short.

sections.heading: What the first marked paper shows
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a transferring family can do is have the student sit one whole paper of their exact specification under proper timing, self-mark it against the published scheme, and then have it marked independently. That hour produces the information that the next three months depend on, and it is the step most often skipped in favour of a conversation about curriculum differences.

For an ICSE student the script typically shows a recognisable distribution. Content is largely present, sometimes conspicuously so in the sciences. Method marks are missing in mathematics and in chemistry calculations, because the working was done mentally. Command words have been answered by instinct, so an accurate account appears where an explanation or a comparison was required. And the practical paper, if attempted at all, is close to blank, because its conventions have never been taught.

That distribution is good news and should be presented as such. Three of those four categories are conventions rather than knowledge, and conventions move in weeks. A student who writes method out, reads the command word before the stem, and has drawn fifteen results tables to the scheme's conventions will see the raw mark move on a comparable paper within a month, and the movement is visible rather than asserted.

The fourth category, genuine coverage gaps, matters only for students arriving mid-course, and it must be separated from the other three in writing. Coverage takes terms and conventions take weeks, and a plan that merges them will either overcharge a Year 10 arrival or under-deliver for a mid-Year-11 one. Ask for the two lists separately after the baseline paper, because that is what makes the rest of the plan honest.
bullets: Sit one paper of the exact specification, under real timing
Self-mark against the published scheme before anyone else sees it
Ask for coverage gaps and conventions gaps as two separate lists
Record the raw mark, the tier and the date as the baseline

sections.heading: ICSE English into First Language English
paragraphs: This is where an ICSE background pays most and where families most often spend money unnecessarily. The reading range, vocabulary and comfort with extended writing that ICSE English develops is largely what the IGCSE paper assumes, and a student with a solid ICSE English record usually needs the task conventions rather than the language itself.

Those conventions are specific and short. Directed writing is assessed on audience, form and purpose as well as on quality of writing, so a well-written piece in the wrong register loses marks that have nothing to do with ability. A letter that reads like an essay, a speech with no sense of an audience, a report with no structure: each is a conventions failure and each is fixable by writing the same task twice a fortnight apart with the published criteria beside both versions.

The reading components reward precise retrieval and concise summary, which is a different discipline from literary appreciation. ICSE students sometimes write beautifully about a passage and fail to answer what was asked, particularly on summary tasks with a word limit. Practising against the limit, with the mark scheme visible, resolves this quickly because the student can see which of their sentences were being counted.

Where a school offers an IGCSE literature specification alongside, an ICSE student is often a strong candidate for it rather than a risk, and it can be a dependable grade on a timetable where the sciences are competing for attention. The adjustment is to timed extract-based and comparative response structures, which is two or three marked attempts, not a term.

sections.heading: Mapping the subjects, with codes
paragraphs: Subject names do not translate directly and the mismatches are where plans go wrong. ICSE Science is already three subjects, which is the cleanest part of the mapping, but a Dubai school may still place a transferring student on a co-ordinated double award or a single combined award for timetable reasons. Those have different paper patterns and a narrower content range, and for an ICSE student that is a step back rather than a simplification. Ask before accepting it.

History and Civics plus Geography at ICSE sits within a broader group than the separate Cambridge or Pearson history and geography subjects, so content emphasis shifts even where the subject name survives. In mathematics the mapping is clean and the code still matters: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers, and Additional Mathematics is worth asking about for a strong candidate.

The second language ICSE requires is the element most often lost in the move. A Dubai school may or may not offer that language as an IGCSE subject, and where it does, an existing strength converts into a graded subject on a crowded timetable. Where it does not, the student has a spare option slot, which is an opportunity rather than a loss, provided somebody notices it in time to choose deliberately.

The table maps the common routes. Treat the middle column as the question to put to the school rather than as the answer, because which award a student is entered for is a school decision recorded on the statement of entry.

sections.heading: The conventions that are still new
paragraphs: Four conventions account for most of the recoverable marks in this move, and all four are shared across subjects, which is why fixing them improves every paper at once. The first is written method. The published mark scheme awards marks for a recognisable route to the answer, so a student who does three steps mentally and writes the fourth is discarding marks already earned. This is the largest single avoidable loss in mathematics and chemistry.

The second is command words. An IGCSE paper uses its instruction vocabulary precisely, and an accurate account offered where an explanation, a judgement or a comparison was wanted earns little. ICSE training produces strong structured recall, which is exactly the material a command word redirects, so this fix is unusually efficient: the knowledge is already there and only its presentation changes.

The third is accepted wording, which bites hardest in biology. The scheme lists the terminology it will credit and that cannot be guessed, so a correct idea in loose language earns nothing. The only remedy is practising with the scheme open, which feels like cheating to students and is in fact the fastest way to learn what is being counted.

The fourth is the Cambridge practical paper, which is new in form even to a student who has done a great deal of laboratory work. It is a written paper about practical work and needs no equipment: results tables with units in the headings, instruments read to the precision they allow, scales that fill the grid, lines of best fit, and specific sources of error rather than human error. Four sessions clears it permanently.

sections.heading: The weekly record, and reading grade movement honestly
paragraphs: A first-term grade is a poor measure of a transition, because the student is learning the assessment system rather than performing in it. A parent who wants to know whether the move is working should look at artefacts instead, and the four that matter are cheap to produce and readable without knowing the subject.

The first is a marked script with a raw mark, the tier and the date. The second is an answer rewritten to a command word, with the original beside it and a note in the student's own words on what changed. The third is a results table or graph marked to the practical paper's conventions. The fourth is a topic list with items crossed off rather than rewritten at the same length.

Movement is then measurable rather than argued about. Two comparable papers, same board, same tier, same conditions, a month apart, with their raw marks written down. If the second is higher, something worked. If it is not, the method changes rather than the hours increasing. That single discipline removes most of the disagreement families have in a transition term, when everybody is anxious and nobody has data.

The table lists the artefact to ask for by session type. Ask for the artefact rather than for a progress update, because progress updates in a transition term are almost always optimistic out of kindness, and marked work is not. Keep the whole set in one folder, in date order, because the folder is what makes the difference between a productive month and a merely busy one visible, and it is also the thing to put in front of the school if a tier or a subject placement needs revisiting later in the year.

sections.heading: Timing, the series and arriving mid-course
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June series with November as the second route, and the Pearson May/June window with a November window. Cambridge offers the February and March sitting to candidates in India only, so a plan carried over from an Indian school needs re-aiming. That is a common and reasonable error, because the calendar a family arrives with was correct where they were.

The deadline that binds is the exam centre's own rather than the board's published date, because the centre collates and submits entries. Ask the school's exams officer for that date in writing in the first week of the move. A missed entry deadline is the only failure in this process that no amount of preparation repairs, and it is most likely to catch a family in the middle of a relocation.

For a student joining partway through Year 11, the series choice is a real decision rather than a formality. Where coverage gaps are substantial, the November route buys several extra months of teaching at the cost of a confirmed grade only in the middle of the following January. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 and its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, which are the published patterns to plan against.

Make that decision with the baseline paper in front of you. A student whose script shows conventions losses and present content can usually target June. A student whose script shows whole questions with nothing usable in them is a coverage case, and entering June regardless frequently produces a grade that needs a resit anyway, which costs an entry fee, a term and the confidence.

sections.heading: Buying this honestly
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates give the arithmetic. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED's premium named tier at AED 650. A four to six session conventions block is therefore roughly AED 600 to 1,800, and a four-session practical paper block around AED 600 to 1,200. Those are market figures; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson with session length and marking inclusion stated.

Refuse a plan that proposes re-teaching the sciences to a student who studied them separately for two years. In this move content is the strongest thing the student holds, and a provider billing for it has not looked at a marked script. Ask instead for the two lists, coverage and conventions, and for the number of sessions aimed at each.

Refuse any offer to supply past papers and mark schemes as downloads. They belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the practical risk is larger than the legal one: private copies are frequently from superseded specifications or retyped with errors, so a student calibrates against the wrong standard. The school is the first source and both boards publish through their own channels.

Insist on the baseline paper before any teaching plan, and on raw marks recorded with dates throughout. No success rate, average grade or satisfaction figure appears on this page, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method, and no tutor can promise a grade on an externally marked paper. What can be promised is a record you can read.

process.title: Read the statement of entry, then ask two questions
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and series for every subject. Then ask whether the separate-science route is available, since an ICSE student has already built that depth, and whether the second language from ICSE is offered as an IGCSE subject. Both answers shape the timetable.

process.title: Sit the baseline paper and record it
process.description: One whole paper of the exact specification, under full timing, self-marked against the published scheme, then marked independently. Record the raw mark, the tier and the date. Everything in the plan afterwards is measured against that one number.

process.title: Ask for two lists, not one
process.description: Coverage gaps and conventions gaps, separately and in writing. Coverage is measured in terms and conventions in weeks, and merging them is how a Year 10 arrival gets overcharged and a mid-Year-11 arrival gets an optimistic plan that quietly fails.

process.title: Clear the conventions first, then the practical paper
process.description: Written method, command words and accepted wording improve every subject at once, so they come first. The Cambridge practical paper block comes next for a science student, because the gap is total and the fix is mechanical and permanent.

process.title: Compare two raw marks each month
process.description: Same board, same tier, same conditions, a month apart, with the two numbers written down. If the second has not moved, change the approach rather than adding hours. That rule is what keeps a transition term honest when everyone is anxious.

whyPoints.title: We name the advantages, because they change the plan
whyPoints.description: Three separate sciences, developed English and real internal-assessment experience are not flattery; they reduce the work. A plan that bills for re-teaching the sciences to an ICSE student has not looked at a marked script and is charging for the strongest thing they hold.

whyPoints.title: Two lists after the baseline, never one
whyPoints.description: Coverage gaps and conventions gaps are separated in writing, because one takes terms and the other weeks. That distinction decides whether June or November is the realistic target and whether a block should be four sessions or a full year.

whyPoints.title: The record is the measure, not the first-term grade
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with raw marks and dates, command-word rewrites with both versions kept, results tables marked to convention, a topic list that shortens. A first-term grade measures system familiarity rather than ability.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper is treated as a new subject
whyPoints.description: The Cambridge alternative-to-practical component needs no laboratory and no Indian board sets it in the same form. Four sessions on tables, precision and specific errors protects a real share of every science grade, permanently.

whyPoints.title: The right series, not the remembered one
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November; Cambridge offers the February and March sitting to India only. Re-aiming a plan carried over from India, and getting the centre's own deadline in writing, is worth more than any single lesson.

faqs.question: What does an ICSE background give my child that other routes do not?
faqs.answer: Three things that genuinely reduce the work. Physics, chemistry and biology studied as separate subjects, which is the structure the IGCSE separate-science route assumes rather than a combined award. English developed through both language and literature work, which is the closest thing to a clean transfer in this move. And internally assessed project components, so the idea that a mark can come from work produced over time is already familiar. Each of those shortens a transition plan rather than removing the need for one.

faqs.question: Does ICSE English map onto IGCSE First Language English?
faqs.answer: Closely, which is why English is usually the wrong place to spend money in the first term. The reading range, vocabulary and comfort with extended writing largely match what the paper assumes. What is new is the task conventions: directed writing is assessed on audience, form and purpose as well as on quality, so a well-written letter that reads like an essay loses marks unrelated to ability. Writing the same task twice a fortnight apart, with the criteria beside both versions, fixes that quickly.

faqs.question: My child studied the three sciences separately. Does that help at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it should influence the placement. The IGCSE separate-science route assumes exactly that depth, so an ICSE student entering 0625, 0620 and 0610 is working at a familiar level. The risk is being placed on a co-ordinated double award or a single combined award for timetable reasons, which narrows the content range and the achievable breadth for a student who has already built it. Ask the school whether the separate-science route is available before accepting a combined placement.

faqs.question: Does ICSE project work prepare a student for IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the benefit arrives later than at IGCSE itself. Most IGCSE subjects are assessed by terminal written papers, with the Cambridge sciences adding a practical component rather than a coursework one, so there is often nothing directly comparable to carry over. Where the habit pays is further on: at A-Level coursework or at IB Internal Assessment, where producing assessed work over time against criteria is the core demand. It is worth recognising rather than rebuilding when that point comes.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE codes should we be looking at?
faqs.answer: Confirm them from the statement of entry rather than from the subject names, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and set different papers. For an ICSE student the likely set is 0580 or 4MA1 in mathematics, 0625, 0620 and 0610 or their Pearson equivalents in the sciences, 0500 or 4EA1 in English, and separate history and geography codes. Additional Mathematics, 0606 or 4PM1, is worth asking about for a strong mathematician.

faqs.question: Will my child find the IGCSE workload lighter than ICSE?
faqs.answer: In subject count, often comparable, since a Dubai Year 11 typically sits eight or nine. In content volume per subject, sometimes lighter. In the way answers must be constructed, heavier, because the published mark scheme pays for a visible route to the answer and for responses pitched to the command word. Students frequently report the content as manageable and the papers as unexpectedly particular, which is the right way round: particular is learnable in weeks whereas content gaps take terms.

faqs.question: What does the first marked IGCSE paper usually reveal?
faqs.answer: A recognisable distribution for this background. Content largely present, often conspicuously so in the sciences. Method marks missing in mathematics and chemistry calculations because the working was mental. Command words answered by instinct, so an accurate account appears where an explanation or comparison was wanted. And the practical paper close to blank, because its conventions have never been taught. Three of those four are conventions rather than knowledge, which is good news and is exactly why the baseline paper comes first.

faqs.question: How do we measure grade movement in a transition term?
faqs.answer: Two comparable papers, same board, same tier, same conditions, a month apart, with their raw marks written down side by side. That is the whole method, and it removes most of the disagreement a family has in a term when everyone is anxious and nobody has data. Support it with a topic list that should be shorter each month and an error log that should be narrowing. A first-term grade measures familiarity with the system rather than ability, so it is a poor instrument here.

faqs.question: Is the ICSE written and internal split similar to how IGCSE works?
faqs.answer: Not really, and the difference is worth knowing. ICSE subjects commonly combine an externally marked written paper with an internally assessed component. Most IGCSE subjects are assessed by terminal written papers alone, with the Cambridge sciences adding a practical or alternative-to-practical component rather than coursework. So a student who relied partly on internal marks to lift a subject total will find the written papers carrying more of the grade, which argues for the conventions work being done early rather than late.

faqs.question: What paper conventions does an ICSE student still need to learn?
faqs.answer: Four, and all four are shared across subjects so fixing them improves every paper at once. Written method, because the scheme pays for the route and not only the destination. Command words, which redirect knowledge the student already has. Accepted wording, especially in biology, where a correct idea in loose language earns nothing. And the Cambridge practical paper conventions, which are entirely new in form: results tables with units in the headings, instrument precision, scales, lines of best fit, and specific sources of error.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Dubai for these sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For a family mid-relocation that is a practical benefit: the tutor and the accumulating record of marked scripts and raw marks stay continuous regardless of which community you settle in, and the tutor is chosen for knowing your child's exact specification rather than for living within driving distance of your building.

faqs.question: Which school year should my child join after ICSE?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools place by age in most cases, which usually puts a Class 8 leaver into Year 9, a Class 9 leaver into Year 10 and a student leaving during Class 10 into Year 11. The first two are clean entries where the IGCSE course has not begun or begins from the start. The third is harder because part of the syllabus has been taught in the student's absence. Ask the school in writing which year the student joins, on what basis, and what has already been covered.

faqs.question: Does ICSE mathematics reach the Extended tier content?
faqs.answer: Generally yes on content, which is why an ICSE student is usually an Extended or Higher tier candidate rather than a Core one. The breadth and algebraic demand of ICSE mathematics supports the longer multi-step questions that the higher tier sets. The gap is written method rather than content: the mark scheme awards marks for the visible route, and a student who computes efficiently loses them until the habit changes. Produce a marked Extended paper under timing to make that case to the school.

faqs.question: What happens to the second language ICSE required?
faqs.answer: Two possibilities, and both are worth checking early. If the Dubai school offers that language as an IGCSE subject, an existing strength converts into a graded subject on a crowded timetable, which is a good use of it. If it does not, the student effectively has a spare option slot, which is an opportunity rather than a loss provided somebody notices in time to choose deliberately rather than by default. Ask at admission, because timetables harden quickly once the year starts.

faqs.question: How long does the adjustment take and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions for the conventions, bracketed by two comparable marked papers so the movement is visible, plus a separate four-session block on the Cambridge practical paper for a science student. At published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online tutor those are roughly AED 600 to 1,800 and AED 600 to 1,200 respectively. Those are market figures from Unitors and Bestimate rather than ours, and any quote should state session length and whether marking is included.

dubai/icse-to-igcse-transition.closingBody: This is one of the better-positioned curriculum moves available, and the plan should reflect that. Read board, code, tier and series off the statement of entry, ask whether the separate-science route and the second language are available, and get the exam centre's own deadline in writing. Then have your child sit one whole paper of that exact specification under timing and self-mark it against the published scheme. Book the free trial lesson, bring the script, and ask for coverage gaps and conventions gaps as two separate lists. For an ICSE student the first list is usually short and the second is usually quick.

intro.heading: Two grading scales, one target, and a tier that decides both
paragraphs: Before any revision plan is worth writing, two documents need checking. The first is the entry, which names the syllabus code and the tier. The second is how the school reports grades, because UAE centres report IGCSE results on both the traditional A* to G scale and the numeric 9 to 1 scale depending on the syllabus and the centre. A family aiming for 'all A stars' may in fact be aiming at grade 9s, and the two are not identical thresholds. Ask the school which scale applies to each of your child's subjects; the answer is often mixed across a single timetable.

The tier is the harder constraint. In tiered subjects a candidate sits either Core or Extended with Cambridge, or Foundation or Higher with Pearson, and the lower tier carries a grade ceiling that the mark cannot exceed. A student entered for Core who answers every question correctly still cannot be awarded a top grade. This is the single most important thing a parent chasing an A* can verify, and it takes one email. We have seen families spend a term on top-band revision for a subject whose entry made a top band unreachable.

Once those two facts are established the work becomes narrow and practical. Students in reach of the top grades do not usually have knowledge gaps. They lose marks in a consistent pattern: the final parts of extended questions, the precision a mark scheme names, command terms answered in the wrong shape, and unwritten method in the quantitative subjects. Each of those is diagnosable from a marked script and each responds to drilling specific question types rather than to re-covering topics.

Dubai context matters for timing and availability. UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai private enrolment, so Year 11 cohorts across the emirate sit mocks in the same November-to-January band and then look for the same specialists in the same fortnight. Top-band work also competes with the KHDA mandatory subjects, which remain timetabled throughout: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Revision hours come from what is left of the week, not from an imaginary clear evening.

There is one more thing worth settling early, which is how many subjects the plan covers. A Dubai Year 11 student sitting nine or ten papers cannot be supported in all of them, and a family that tries ends up with a little help everywhere and no change anywhere. Three or four subjects, chosen because the top band is genuinely within reach and the gap closes quickly, is the plan that holds.

Every UAE session runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For top-band work the format is what makes the match possible: a Dubai family needing someone who knows Pearson 4CH1 at the top band is choosing from everyone who teaches that code rather than from everyone who will drive to their community before dinner.

dubai/igcse-a-star-coaching.subjectsIntro: Top-band marks sit in different places in each subject. The list below pairs the syllabus codes with what the last marks actually require.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The top band is decided in the final questions of the longer paper, where routine method runs out. Candidates at one grade below usually complete everything standard and lose the last three or four marks of each extended question.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mathematics by stronger Dubai cohorts. Calculus applications and trigonometric identities decide it, and the paper is unforgiving of partial method because the questions are long and interdependent.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations at full precision, electrolysis explained by mechanism rather than outcome, and qualitative analysis stated in the exact terms the mark scheme names. Organic chemistry is often taught late, which affects mock evidence.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Top marks require unit and prefix discipline, correct equation selection, and the practical write-up conventions: named control variables, repeatable procedure, specific apparatus. Electricity remains the topic where most candidates leak marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision decides the grade. 'Describe' and 'explain' want different answers, comparisons need comparative language, and the mark scheme frequently names a specific term that a general synonym will not earn.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Top-band reading responses quote precisely and analyse effect rather than content. Directed writing requires a controlled register for a named audience. Fluent writers who do not reference the passage sit a band below their ability.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: The highest band rewards close analysis of language choices supporting a clear argument, not plot coverage. Timed essay practice with marked feedback is the only reliable way to build this, and it is slow work.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: The evaluation question carries the top band. Candidates who present advantages and disadvantages without reaching a supported judgement are capped regardless of knowledge, and diagram accuracy decides the rest.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are where the marks go. Students who program competently in Python often lose marks writing algorithms in the format the mark scheme requires, which is a presentation issue.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: KHDA requires these subjects in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. They occupy timetable space throughout Year 11.

sections.heading: A* or 9: establish the target before the plan
paragraphs: UAE centres report IGCSE results on two scales. Some syllabuses and centres use the traditional A* to G lettering; others use the numeric 9 to 1 scale. Both are in current use in Dubai, sometimes within one student's timetable, and they are not simply translations of each other. The practical effect is that 'aiming for A stars' is an ambiguous instruction, and a family can be working towards a threshold that does not exist in their child's subject.

Ask the school, subject by subject, which scale applies. The answer is usually on the entry statement or in the curriculum handbook, and the examinations officer will confirm it. Then ask the second question, which is the one that matters more: what grade does the intended sixth form require for the courses the student wants. A Dubai school's published A Level entry threshold is a real number, and working towards it is more useful than working towards a letter that the school may not even award.

The tier interacts with both. In tiered subjects the lower tier carries a grade ceiling, so a top grade is only available from Extended with Cambridge or Higher with Pearson. A candidate entered at the lower tier is capped whatever their mark, and the window for changing an entry closes months before the exam because entries are administrative. This is the single most expensive thing to discover late, and it is free to check now.

sections.heading: Where the last marks sit, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: Students in reach of the top band share a profile: they know the content and they lose marks for reasons that have names. That makes top-band work diagnostic rather than remedial, and it is why a marked script is worth more than a term's worth of general revision. The pattern varies by subject group in texture but not in kind.

In the sciences, the losses are about precision and convention. A correct explanation that omits the mechanism, an answer with the right number and the wrong unit, a practical write-up that names no control variable: each costs one or two marks, and across three papers that is a grade. In Mathematics the losses are at the end of long questions and in unwritten method, where correct reasoning earns nothing because it never appeared on the page.

In the humanities and in Business and Economics, the top band is almost always about judgement. A candidate who presents both sides thoroughly and does not reach a defensible conclusion is capped below the top band however much they know. The fix is structural and quick: a closing paragraph that weighs the evidence and commits, supported by the diagram or the source. In English, the equivalent is analysing effect rather than describing content, and quoting precisely rather than referring generally.

The table below pairs the group with what the final marks require, and the right-hand column gives the honest time cost. Not all of these move at the same speed, and a family with a fixed number of hours should spend them where the return is fastest, which is usually the humanities technique and the science precision rather than a Mathematics content gap.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards
paragraphs: Top grades at IGCSE are a function of how many full papers a student has sat under timed conditions before the real one, and that number is decided by when the rotation starts. Counting backwards from the main UAE series is the only way to see whether the plan is feasible. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series, with the February and March series offered to India only, so a Dubai plan uses June as the main sitting and November as the resit route.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Pearson's own record shows how long the tail is: its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official timetable rather than from any restated date, including ours.

One Cambridge administrative point is worth knowing because it has consequences. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your school handles this; the lesson for a family is to read the timetable the school issues rather than one found online.

The order below is what makes a top-band plan either real or decorative. Note that the entry deadline sits long before the exam, which is why tier questions are urgent in the autumn rather than the spring, and that coursework and practical components land in the spring term when revision would otherwise be accelerating.

sections.heading: What top-band coaching costs in Dubai, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: The clearest way to read this market is to ask what the extra money buys at each step. The figures below are other providers' published Dubai rates, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than our price list. Start with in-home, because it is the band most Dubai families consider first and the one where the premium is easiest to explain.

In-home one-to-one is published at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages appearing around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Against that, online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and monthly online packages around AED 799 for eight sessions. The difference between those two columns is largely travel: the hour a tutor spends crossing Dubai at 5pm is inside the rate, and the family pays for it whether or not it teaches anything.

What the premium does buy is a person in the room, which has genuine value for a younger or less self-directed student. What it does not buy is a wider choice of specialists. In fact it narrows the choice sharply, because the pool becomes those willing to drive to your community in the hours a Year 11 student is free. For top-band work on a specific syllabus code, that narrowing is the opposite of what the money should be achieving.

At the specialist end, IB and IGCSE specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and one premium provider at AED 650. For a student already near the top band, that band is usually the correct purchase and the cheaper bands are not, because the work is mark-scheme level. IB Gram publishes no rate card here: the figure depends on code, tier and subject count, and it is confirmed after the free trial lesson.
