sections.heading: Why this is delivered online in the UAE
paragraphs: Top-band IGCSE work depends on one variable above all others: whether the tutor knows the specific syllabus and its mark scheme well enough to say which word was missing from a six-mark answer. That is a narrow expertise. Matching on it, rather than on geography, is the entire argument for online delivery, and it is why IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India; all UAE sessions are one-to-one over live video.

There are two secondary advantages that matter at this level. Marked work is annotated on a shared screen and saved, so a student accumulates a file of their own corrected top-band answers with the specific omission flagged on each. Over a year of Year 11 that archive is a better revision resource than any published guide, because it contains that student's own recurring errors rather than a general list.

The second is scheduling resilience. Dubai families travel, school timetables shift in mock weeks, and Ramadan changes the household rhythm with shortened school days and sessions commonly moving to a post-Iftar slot. A recurring online slot survives all of that. An in-home arrangement pauses whenever the family or the tutor is out of position, and in a year with a fixed June deadline those pauses are expensive.

The fair counterpoint is that some students work better with someone physically present, particularly younger ones and those who struggle to stay on task. For a Year 11 candidate in reach of a top grade, self-direction is usually not the problem; precision is. The right person for that job is defined by what they know about the paper, and online delivery is what makes them reachable from any Dubai community.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the honesty line
paragraphs: IGCSE coursework and controlled assessment must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain the marking criteria, discuss a plan, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, or edit it into shape. That boundary is not a formality: boards investigate malpractice, and a finding can void a grade or a whole entry.

The market reason to state this plainly is that not every provider does. One ranking page in this sector sells completed Internal Assessments for the IB at around AED 3,750, which is the same category of offer in a different qualification. Any provider willing to produce assessed work is a liability to the student who buys it, and the consequence lands on the student rather than the seller.

On past papers and mark schemes, we reference and link rather than redistribute. Cambridge and Pearson own that material, and reproducing syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade boundary tables is a copyright matter. Your child's school holds the official copies and the subject teacher is the correct route to the school's own mock papers. Where a page tells you it will supply a bank of papers as downloads, consider what else it is prepared to do.

A final point specific to top-band ambition. Grade boundaries are set by the boards after each series and move with the difficulty of the paper, so no one can tell you in advance what mark will earn a top grade. Anyone offering a guaranteed grade is making a claim they cannot honour, and we offer none. What is honest is that the predictable losses can be removed, and that is what the work targets.

sections.heading: Starting top-band work, with the entry in hand
paragraphs: Send the subject, the syllabus code, the tier, the most recent marked paper, and the grade the intended sixth form requires. Those five facts make the first conversation useful. If the code and tier are not to hand, a photograph of the mock paper's front page usually supplies both, and the examinations office will confirm the rest in a day.

We will then say which subjects are worth paying for. A student sitting ten subjects cannot be supported in all of them, and spreading hours evenly across them is the pattern that produces no change anywhere. Three or four subjects where the top band is genuinely in reach, prioritised by how fast the gap closes, is the plan that works. Where an entry is capped by tier, we will say that the useful next step is the school rather than us.

The trial lesson is free, with no condition beyond booking a time. It runs on a real question from the student's own marked paper, because that tests the only thing worth testing: whether this tutor can explain precisely where the last marks went and what to do differently. If the fit is wrong we will say so in that hour.

Beyond that, the plan is built against the school's own calendar, including the mock window, coursework and practical dates, and the June series. It is reviewed on marked evidence rather than impressions, and subjects come off the plan as their predictable losses disappear. Knowing when to stop is part of the service, and on a ten-subject Year 11 it is most of the value.

faqs.question: Is a grade 9 the same as an A star at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: They are not interchangeable thresholds, and UAE centres report on both scales depending on the syllabus and the centre. Some of your child's subjects may be graded A* to G and others 9 to 1, within the same timetable. The practical consequence is that 'aiming for A stars' can be an ambiguous instruction. Ask the school which scale applies subject by subject, then ask the more useful question: what grade does the intended sixth form require for the courses your child wants. That published threshold is a real target to work towards.

faqs.question: Can my child get a top IGCSE grade on the Core paper?
faqs.answer: No. In tiered subjects the lower tier, Core with Cambridge or Foundation with Pearson, carries a grade ceiling that the mark cannot exceed. A candidate answering every question correctly still cannot be awarded a top grade from that entry. This is the single most expensive thing a family can discover late, and it is free to check now: the tier is on the entry statement and usually on the mock paper's front page. Entries close months before the exam, so if a change is needed the conversation with the school is urgent.

faqs.question: How early should top-grade coaching start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Year 10, ideally, and almost nobody does. A Year 10 summer mock showing a ceiling against Core content leaves a full year to build towards Extended, while the same information in January of Year 11 usually leaves the entry where it is. Starting early is also cheaper per grade, because the January scramble costs more and achieves less: every Dubai school's mock returns in the same fortnight and specialist availability tightens across the emirate at once. A standing weekly hour from early Year 11 beats three hours a week from February.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects give the fastest gain at the top band?
faqs.answer: Business, Economics and the sciences, in that order. In Business and Economics the top band usually depends on reaching a supported judgement rather than listing both sides, which is a structural fix of two to four weeks. In the sciences it is precision: stating the mechanism, naming the control variable, getting units right, which responds to four to eight weeks of marked practice. English Literature is the slowest, because close language analysis takes a term to build. Mathematics content gaps are slower still, though unwritten method is fast to fix.

faqs.question: What does top-band IGCSE coaching cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and IGCSE and IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and one premium provider at AED 650. Budget online providers publish from AED 33 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. For work at the top band the specialist bands are usually the right purchase, because the feedback has to be mark-scheme level rather than general.

faqs.question: Is a group revision course enough for a top grade?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for this specific goal. Group classes are taught to the middle of the room, and a student near the top band is not there. They are genuinely useful for a student with broad content gaps who needs coverage, and they cost less per hour. But the work that lifts a strong candidate into the top band is individual by definition: it depends on the particular marks that particular student keeps losing, which a class of fifteen cannot address. With a fixed budget, fewer individual hours beat more group hours here.

faqs.question: Do you visit homes in Dubai for IGCSE coaching?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. The reasoning is specific to top-band work: the tutor has to know your child's exact syllabus well enough to name the missing word in a six-mark answer, and that is a narrow expertise. An in-home arrangement restricts the choice to specialists willing to drive to your community in the hours a Year 11 student is free, which is the opposite of what the extra money should achieve.

faqs.question: How many full past papers should a student sit before June?
faqs.answer: As many complete papers under timed conditions as the calendar allows, which is why the start date matters more than the weekly hour count. A student who begins rotation in the spring with a plan can usually complete several full papers per subject with marking in between; a student who begins in May cannot. The marking is the part that counts: an unmarked paper tells a student they finished, while a marked one tells them which two marks they lost and why. Work from the board's own timetable when planning backwards.

faqs.question: My child writes well but keeps missing the top band in English. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer describes content rather than analysing effect, and refers to the passage generally rather than quoting precisely. Fluency reads well and does not score at the top band on its own. The fix is marked timed practice: a short response, marked against the band descriptors, with the specific sentences that would have earned the next mark identified. Six to ten weeks of that changes the habit. It is slower than the fixes available in Business or the sciences, which is worth knowing when prioritising a finite number of hours.

faqs.question: How do practical components affect a top grade in the sciences?
faqs.answer: More than most Dubai families expect, because the write-up is a format rather than a memory. Cambridge offers a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the centre, and Pearson assesses practical skills through its written papers. Marks go on naming independent, dependent and control variables, describing apparatus precisely, and setting out a procedure that could be repeated. Students who have done the experiments in a Dubai school laboratory still lose these marks on the page, and that is correctable in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Should we enter the November series as insurance?
faqs.answer: Not as insurance, no. The November series is a resit route and a decision best made on the actual results statement, narrowed to specific papers rather than taken as a repeat of the year. Pearson's published record shows the timeline involved: its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Entering in advance for a paper that may not be needed costs money and splits revision attention, which is the opposite of what a top-band candidate needs in the spring.

faqs.question: What if my child is sitting ten subjects and wants top grades in all of them?
faqs.answer: Then the plan has to be honest about arithmetic. Ten subjects cannot all be supported, and spreading hours evenly across them reliably produces no visible change anywhere. We prioritise three or four where the top band is genuinely in reach, ordered by how quickly the gap closes, and leave the rest to the school and the student's own rotation. That is a harder conversation than selling ten hours a week, and it is the one that produces results in a Dubai Year 11 with the mandatory UAE subjects still timetabled.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what mark earns a top grade?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who does is guessing. Grade boundaries are set by Cambridge and Pearson after each series and move with the difficulty of that paper, so the mark required changes series to series and is published afterwards rather than in advance. What a specialist can do is read a marked script against the mark scheme and name which marks were available and missed. That is actionable. A predicted boundary is not, and it is also the kind of claim that tells you how carefully the rest of a provider's page was written.

faqs.question: Does Arabic or Islamic Education count towards our equivalency total?
faqs.answer: Not within the five required subjects. As reported in July 2026, the Ministry of Education's British track requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competing provider publishes a six-subject requirement, which is not the rule as reported. Equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring provider performs or influences it.

faqs.question: Will sessions continue during Ramadan and school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing adjusted deliberately rather than by drift. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a changed household rhythm, and recurring slots commonly move to a post-Iftar time, which many students prefer because evening focus is often better than late-afternoon focus. Dubai families also travel over the winter and spring breaks, and because every session runs over live video a student can continue from wherever they are or pause and resume. For a Year 11 working to a fixed June deadline, planned pauses are far better than improvised ones.

dubai/igcse-a-star-coaching.closingHeading: Check the entry, then build the plan
dubai/igcse-a-star-coaching.closingBody: Two documents decide whether a top IGCSE grade is reachable: the entry that names the tier and the syllabus code, and the sixth form's published requirement for the courses your child wants. Send those with the most recent marked paper and we will tell you which subjects are worth paying for, in what order, and whether an entry needs changing before anything else happens. If the tier caps the grade, we will say that the useful conversation is with the school. The trial lesson is free, one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Why this page starts with your child's last Accounting paper
paragraphs: Most Accounting tuition in Dubai is bought on a report card. A C arrives in the January assessment, a parent searches for help, and a tutor begins teaching the syllabus again from Chapter 1. That is expensive and slow, because a C in Accounting is rarely a gap in knowledge across the whole subject. It is usually two or three repeated procedural failures, each worth two to five marks, repeated across eight questions. Find them in the script and the same hour of teaching does four times the work.

So the first thing we ask for is the paper, not the grade. A marked Cambridge 0452 or Pearson 4AC1 script carries more diagnostic information than any school comment. Where did the examiner award a mark for a correct figure and withhold the mark for the label? Which adjustments were attempted and abandoned? Did the candidate lose the final three marks of a question because time ran out, or because the question asked for an evaluation and received a calculation? Those are four different problems with four different fixes, and they are visible on the page.

The second thing we ask for is the school's assessment calendar. A Dubai Year 11 cohort typically sits a full mock in November or January, with teacher-marked unit tests before that, and the real series in May or June. Each of those is a checkpoint where evidence is produced whether anyone reads it or not. A tutoring plan that lines up with those dates can show movement in marks rather than movement in confidence, and movement in marks is the only claim worth making to a parent paying by the hour.

This page is built around that evidence trail. It explains what the two Accounting papers reward, the error patterns that cost the most marks in UAE cohorts, what you should receive after every session, what the Dubai market charges in AED and who publishes those figures, and how entry deadlines for the Cambridge and Pearson series sit months before the paper itself. It also says plainly what we do not sell: nobody drives to a villa in Al Barsha, because tuition for UAE families here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video.

Accounting is also one of the subjects where a tutor can show their working. The subject has right answers. A control account reconciles or it does not. A balance sheet balances or it does not. Ratio commentary either uses the figures it has just calculated or floats free of them. That makes the subject unusually well suited to the week-by-week evidence model described below, and it is why the fortnightly table on this page lists what you will see rather than what you will be told.
bullets: Send the last marked script before the first paid session, not after
Expect a written mark breakdown by question, not a general progress note
Know which board your child sits: 0452 and 4AC1 are not interchangeable
Ask for the fortnightly comparison against the previous timed paper
Lessons run online on Gulf Standard Time, not at a Dubai address

dubai/igcse-accounting-tutor.programmesIntro: Accounting sits in a narrow band of the school timetable in Dubai: a two-year IGCSE course taken at 15 and 16, usually as an option against a second science or a third humanity, and feeding into A Level, BTEC Business or a UAE university foundation year. These are the routes families on this page are usually choosing between.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Accounting (0452)
programmes.description: The course most British-curriculum schools in Dubai run. It moves from double entry and the ledger through control accounts, correction of errors and incomplete records, into partnership and limited company accounts, manufacturing accounts and ratio analysis. Assessment is by written papers only, with no coursework component, so every mark on the certificate comes from timed performance under exam conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's own risk, which matters in Dubai where families often check a timetable found online rather than the one their centre issued. Confirm the current 0452 assessment structure and your centre's zone on cambridgeinternational.org before planning a revision schedule around it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting (4AC1)
programmes.description: The Edexcel route, used by a smaller group of Dubai schools and by private candidates. The content overlaps heavily with Cambridge, but question style and the balance between computation and written evaluation differ, and the specification is assessed in a different paper structure. A student who has practised only Cambridge past papers will meet unfamiliar phrasing on an Edexcel paper.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in a May/June and a November series. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Pre-IGCSE business and accounting foundations
programmes.description: Many Dubai schools give Year 9 a short carousel of business studies, economics and accounting before option choices are made. Students who struggle with the ledger in Year 10 often never secured the idea that every transaction has two sides and that the debit is defined by what the business receives. Fixing that in Year 9 costs a handful of sessions; fixing it in Year 11 costs a term.
programmes.countryNote: Option choices in Dubai are usually locked by February or March of Year 9, and Accounting competes with a second science. Families weighing it should look at how the school staffs the subject, how many candidates it entered in the last series, and whether the teacher also carries the A Level group, because a single-teacher option subject has no second opinion inside the school.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Accounting (9706)
programmes.description: The direct progression from 0452. The step up is in the written analysis rather than the bookkeeping: AS introduces published company accounts and more demanding ratio interpretation, and A2 adds costing, budgeting and investment appraisal. Students who finished IGCSE able to produce statements but unable to comment on them find the first term of AS the hardest part of the course.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school that offers Accounting at 16 offers it at 18, and some route students into BTEC Business or into economics instead. If an A Level in Accounting is the plan, check it is actually timetabled at your child's school before Year 11 ends, because a mid-sixth-form transfer to another Dubai school for one option subject is a harder conversation than it sounds.

dubai/igcse-accounting-tutor.subjectsIntro: Accounting rarely arrives alone. The students we see on this page are usually carrying a maths grade that worries them, a business studies option taught by the same teacher, and an English paper that governs how well the evaluation questions are answered. These are the subjects most often booked alongside IGCSE Accounting by Dubai families.

subjects.name: Accounting
subjects.description: Double entry, ledger and trial balance, correction of errors and the suspense account, control accounts, bank reconciliation, adjustments for accruals, prepayments, depreciation and irrecoverable debts, partnership and limited company accounts, manufacturing accounts, incomplete records and ratio analysis with written commentary.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Often the paired option, and often the subject where students learn to answer evaluation questions properly. Cash flow forecasts, break-even and the basic financial statements appear in both subjects, so a student who understands working capital in Accounting should stop losing marks for it in Business.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Percentages, ratio and simple algebra carry most of the arithmetic load in Accounting. The students who make the most careless errors in a trial balance are usually the ones whose maths is accurate but slow, because slow arithmetic eats the checking time at the end of a paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The third subject in the commerce block in most Dubai schools. Economics rewards diagram work and chains of reasoning rather than format accuracy, so students who do well in Accounting sometimes underperform here until they learn that a correct conclusion with no reasoning scores almost nothing.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: The evaluation marks in Accounting are written marks. A candidate who cannot build a short paragraph that states a position, supports it with a calculated figure and concedes a limitation will leave three to six marks on the table in every paper, regardless of how well the statements were prepared.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Relevant in Dubai because a large share of Accounting candidates work in a second or third language. The subject-specific vocabulary is the obstacle more often than general fluency: provision, accrual, carriage inwards and drawings all carry precise meanings that a general dictionary will not give.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology
subjects.description: Spreadsheet modelling in ICT and ledger work in Accounting reinforce each other. Students who can build a formula-driven spreadsheet understand why a change in the depreciation rate moves the profit figure and the balance sheet together, which is exactly what the harder adjustment questions test.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Dubai cohorts alongside 0580. Useful on this page because students carrying both Additional Maths and Accounting usually have the arithmetic secured and need the written commentary work instead, which changes what a tutoring hour should be spent on.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, so an Accounting option sits inside a timetable that already carries those lessons. Worth knowing when you are deciding which evening is realistically free for tuition.

subjects.name: Commerce and Enterprise
subjects.description: Several Dubai schools run an enterprise or young-entrepreneur strand below Year 10. It builds commercial vocabulary but no bookkeeping discipline, and students arriving from it often assume Accounting will be judged on ideas rather than on format accuracy and arithmetic.

dubai/igcse-accounting-tutor.regionsIntro: Dubai Accounting candidates are clustered where the larger British-curriculum schools sit, and the practical question for a family is never distance to a tutor but which evening is free once the school run, the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons and the commute home have taken their share of the week.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The densest run of large British-curriculum secondary schools in the city. Year 11 cohorts here are big enough that option subjects such as Accounting are properly timetabled, and the common request is marking turnaround rather than teaching from scratch.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle
regions.note: A young community with a high share of families who moved school at least once. The recurring Accounting problem is a student who met double entry under one board in Year 10 and now sits the other board's paper style in Year 11.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Larger villa communities with long school runs towards Al Qusais and Academic City. A 4pm start is rarely realistic here, so Accounting sessions are usually booked at 6.30pm or later, which suits a tutor working to Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown
regions.note: Apartment living, both parents commonly working, and a preference for sessions that run while a parent is still in the office. The written session note matters more here than anywhere else, because it is often the only account of the hour a parent reads.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several of the schools that enter the largest Accounting cohorts, and to the university campuses students progress to. Families here often ask early about the A Level 9706 route and whether their school will actually run it.

regions.name: Deira and Al Nahda
regions.note: Older schools, many with Indian and Pakistani curriculum streams alongside British ones. Students who transfer from a CBSE commerce stream into IGCSE Accounting meet the format and layout rules as the main obstacle, not the content.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Dubai Investment Park
regions.note: The far end of the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor, where an in-home tutor's travel time becomes the dominant cost in the quote. Online delivery removes that line from the bill entirely, which is why most families in this corridor end up there.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Dubai Hills
schoolClusters.note: Large British-curriculum secondaries with established Year 10 and 11 option blocks. Accounting is usually taught here by a specialist who also carries the sixth-form group, which means strong teaching and very little spare marking capacity in the weeks before a mock.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: A mix of British, Indian and American provision, with several schools entering commerce subjects in volume. Students here often share a teacher between Business Studies and Accounting, so a weakness in evaluation writing tends to show up in both subject reports at once.
schools: GEMS Our Own English High School

schoolClusters.city: Academic City, Silicon Oasis and Jebel Ali
schoolClusters.note: The southern and eastern corridor, where several schools run both IGCSE and a sixth form on the same site. Useful for families planning the 9706 progression, because continuity of teacher between IGCSE and A Level is more common in this cluster.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Accounting script: what the annotations actually mean
paragraphs: An examiner's marked Accounting paper is a list of decisions, and each decision is recoverable information. A tick against a figure means the arithmetic and the placement were both accepted. A tick against a figure with no mark for the line beneath it usually means the own-figure rule carried the number forward but the label, the heading or the date was wrong. A long diagonal through a whole section means the candidate answered a different question from the one asked, which is a reading problem rather than an Accounting problem and needs a different fix.

The most useful thing on the page is the pattern of where marks stop. If a candidate scores well on the first half of a question and nothing on the last three marks, that is almost always a command-word failure: the question moved from prepare to comment, or from calculate to advise, and the answer did not. If marks are scattered thinly across every question, the problem is pace, and the fix is timing practice rather than content revision. If one topic is empty across the whole paper, that topic was never secured and needs teaching.

We ask for three things before the first paid hour: the most recent marked script, the mark scheme the school used, and the student's own account of which questions they abandoned. The third is the one families forget. A student who skipped the incomplete-records question because they recognised it and ran out of time has a very different plan from one who skipped it because they did not recognise it at all. The script shows the same blank space in both cases.
bullets: Own-figure marks tell you the method held even where the number was wrong
A blank final part is usually a command word, not missing knowledge
Thin scatter across every question points at pace, not content
Ask which questions were abandoned and why before planning any sessions

sections.heading: The two Accounting papers, and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson assess Accounting at this level by written paper only. There is no coursework, no practical and no oral component, which means the certificate records nothing except performance in a small number of timed hours. That is worth saying to a Dubai family deciding how to spend a tuition budget, because it removes the question that dominates IB conversations, where internal coursework carries a fixed share of the grade.

The structures differ in ways that change how a student should practise. Cambridge 0452 spreads the assessment across written papers that mix short structured tasks with longer preparation questions, so a candidate meets the ledger, the adjustments and the ratio commentary more than once and can recover from a weak start. Edexcel's 4AC1 concentrates the assessment differently, which raises the cost of losing time early. A student who has only ever practised one board's papers will find the other board's phrasing unfamiliar even where the content is identical.

Both boards publish the current assessment structure, the specimen papers and the assessment objective weightings on their own sites, and both revise them between syllabus cycles. Check the version your child's cohort actually sits on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than trusting a restated table anywhere else, including this one. The table below is a map of what each component asks for and where UAE cohorts commonly lose marks on it, not a substitute for the specification. Read it with your child's last script beside it, because the row that matters is the one where their marks stopped, and the specification will tell you how many marks that component carries in the series they are entered for.

sections.heading: Where the marks go: the error patterns worth ranking
paragraphs: Across the marked scripts we see from UAE candidates, a small number of error patterns account for most of the lost marks. They are worth ranking because tuition hours are finite and the patterns are not equally expensive. A labelling habit that costs one mark in eight questions is worth more attention than a misunderstanding of manufacturing accounts that appears once, even though the second feels more serious to the student.

The expensive ones share a structure: an early procedural slip that propagates. A depreciation charge calculated on cost when the question specified reducing balance does not cost one mark, it changes the profit figure, the accumulated depreciation, the carrying amount and the balance sheet total. Examiners award own-figure marks generously on later lines, but the candidate still loses the marks tied to the original calculation and usually loses time rechecking a statement that will not balance.

The cheap ones to fix are the ones that need a rule rather than understanding. Dates on ledger accounts. The narrative on a journal entry. Carriage inwards into cost of sales and carriage outwards into expenses. Drawings never through the income statement. Each is a single sentence a student can rehearse, and together they routinely recover a grade boundary's worth of marks in a candidate whose understanding was already adequate. The ranking below is drawn from the scripts themselves rather than from a textbook's order of chapters, which is why depreciation sits above topics that feel harder: it appears in almost every paper, it propagates into three further figures, and a student can be taught the rule in a single session and then rehearse it against six past questions until the choice between cost and reducing balance is made from the wording of the question rather than from memory.
bullets: Depreciation method applied as remembered rather than as specified in the question

Ledger accounts submitted without dates, narratives or balancing figures

sections.heading: What progress looks like, fortnight by fortnight
paragraphs: A tuition plan that cannot be audited is a plan that depends on trust alone. On an Accounting course that is unnecessary, because the subject produces countable evidence every fortnight: a marked question set, a timed paper, a reconciliation that now clears. The table below sets out what a twelve-week block produces and what a parent should expect to hold at the end of each stage, so that a decision to continue or stop is made on documents rather than on impressions.

The pattern matters more than any single score. A student who scores 58 per cent, then 61, then 57, then 68 on comparable papers is improving, even though one fortnight went backwards. A student whose total stays flat while the distribution of lost marks shifts from the ledger to the evaluation parts is also improving, because the expensive propagating errors have gone and what remains is a writing habit. Reading only the total hides both of those.

We also log what did not happen. If the fortnightly timed paper was not sat because the school ran three assessments that week, the note says so. A progress record that only ever reports good news is not a record. Families who have bought tuition before in Dubai usually recognise this immediately: the thing they could never get from a previous provider was an honest account of a fortnight where nothing moved. A blank fortnight is also information. Three school assessments in one week means the student has produced three marked scripts that nobody has analysed, and the next session is better spent on those than on a fresh past paper.

sections.heading: What IGCSE Accounting tuition costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The bands below are market rates in AED, each attributed to whoever published it, so you can see where a quote sits before you take it. They are not our price list: IB Gram's own figure is given after a trial lesson and a look at the script, because an hour spent recovering labelling marks and an hour spent teaching manufacturing accounts from scratch are not the same product.

Two things move an Accounting quote more than anything else. The first is marking: a tutor who marks a full paper against the mark scheme and writes a breakdown is spending an unpaid hour for every paid one, and either the rate reflects that or the marking does not actually happen. The second is proximity to the series. Demand for Accounting support in Dubai concentrates in the eight weeks before May and the four before November, and availability at those points is narrower than in September.

Monthly packages are common in this market. Figures seen on UAE provider sites include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Read any package against what it includes: marking, written notes and paper supply are the lines that quietly disappear.

paragraphs: A family searching for an Accounting tutor in Dubai is usually picturing someone at the dining table. It is a reasonable thing to want, and the honest answer about what it involves is this: the market charges roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour for a home visit, travel is paid for in money or in a smaller tutor pool, and the pool shrinks further for a minority option subject. Accounting is not Maths. The number of tutors in Dubai who have taught 0452 and 4AC1 to examination and who also live within a twenty-minute drive of Mirdif is small.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India; for Dubai, every lesson is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. That is a constraint, and it is also the reason a family in Jebel Ali can book a specialist who marks Accounting papers weekly rather than the nearest available generalist. For a subject assessed entirely on written papers, the work is screen-shared documents and annotated scripts, which is exactly what a video session handles well.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines sit months before the paper
paragraphs: The most common planning mistake we see in Dubai has nothing to do with teaching. It is a family discovering in February that the entry window for a series closed in November, or a private candidate assuming a centre will accept a late entry because the exam is still months away. Entries, forecast grades and timetable zones are administrative deadlines set by the board, and they do not move for a student who was ill, travelling or undecided.

The two series open to an accounting candidate in the UAE are June and November, and both show the same shape once you read the administrative calendar rather than the exam calendar. Cambridge entries for a June series close in the spring, several months before the first paper, and the exact day is set per series and per timetable zone and reaches you on the school's statement of entry. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 series makes the gap concrete at the other end: the timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the November 2025 results before it reached students on 22 January 2026. The specific series matters less than the gap. Entries close months before the first paper, and the certificate arrives months after it. Plan the tuition block against the entry date, not against the paper date.

Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always open the live PDF on its own site. Cambridge additionally allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone timetable.

sections.heading: KHDA, the permit, and what a Dubai parent can verify before paying
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA regulates schools. It does not certify tutors, and no tutoring business should be described as carrying its approval unless it holds a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises.

Individual private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a different route. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing.

Two checks are worth making before money changes hands, and both are things a parent can do alone. Ask whether the person teaching your child holds the MoHRE private tuition permit, and ask whether they teach at your child's own school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction, so a teacher tutoring their own class privately is a problem wherever in the UAE it happens. Mandatory UAE subjects sit under separate rules again: KHDA requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold its approval to teach those subjects.

process.title: Send the marked script
process.description: Before anything is booked, send the most recent marked Accounting paper, the mark scheme the school used, and your child's own list of questions they abandoned. A photograph of each page is enough. This is what turns the first session into diagnosis rather than a general chat about how the subject is going.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson
process.description: A 30-minute one-to-one lesson over live video, at no cost and with no card details taken. The tutor works two questions from the script with your child and writes up what the errors were. You keep that write-up whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Agree the ranked plan
process.description: You receive the three costliest error patterns in order, with an estimate of the marks tied to each and the number of sessions each is likely to need. Choosing to fix the top two and ignore the third is a reasonable decision, and it is easier to make when the marks at stake are written down.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written notes
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons already in the timetable. Each one ends with a note of what was marked, which marks were gained and lost, and what the student is practising before the next session.

process.title: Fortnightly timed paper
process.description: Every second week the student sits a timed question set or full paper, which is marked against the published mark scheme and returned with per-question timing. The comparison is against their own previous attempt, which is the only comparison that tells you anything useful.

process.title: Review at six weeks, and decide
process.description: At six weeks you get the series of marks, the topic log and an honest view on whether the remaining gap needs more sessions, a different tutor, or nothing at all. If the answer is that the school's teaching is now enough, that is what the review says.

whyPoints.title: The script is read before the first paid hour
whyPoints.description: Most Accounting tuition begins with a syllabus and a start date. Ours begins with the last marked paper, because the paper already contains the diagnosis. It is the difference between paying to be taught the subject again and paying to recover the specific marks that went missing.

whyPoints.title: Marking is included, not an extra
whyPoints.description: A full paper marked against the published mark scheme, with a question-by-question breakdown, is part of the session rather than a separate purchase. On a subject assessed entirely by written paper, marking is where most of the diagnostic value sits, and a rate that excludes it is not cheaper.

whyPoints.title: Both boards, not just the popular one
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0452 and Pearson 4AC1 overlap in content and differ in question style. Tutors on this page have taught to both, which matters for the many Dubai students who changed school mid-course and are now sitting a paper written in a style they have never practised.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and saying so before you enquire is better than discovering it after. It is also what makes a specialist available regardless of which community you live in.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can audit
whyPoints.description: Session notes, a topic log, a fortnightly series of marked papers and per-question timing. The point is that you can tell whether the money is working without taking anyone's word for it, including ours, and can stop at six weeks if it is not.

whyPoints.title: No price invented, no outcome promised
whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page are market bands with the source named. No tutor can promise a grade, and the ones who do are selling something other than teaching. What can be promised is marked work, named error patterns and a record of what moved.

faqs.question: Which Accounting syllabus does my child's Dubai school actually use?
faqs.answer: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai enter candidates for Cambridge IGCSE Accounting, code 0452, and a smaller number use Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting, code 4AC1. The code appears on the school's option booklet, on any past paper sent home, and on the exam entry statement. It matters because the two boards differ in paper structure and question phrasing even where content overlaps, so a student practising the wrong board's papers is rehearsing the wrong format. If you cannot find the code, ask the head of commerce directly rather than guessing from a textbook cover.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell from one marked paper what is going wrong in Accounting?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and more reliably than from a school report. A marked script shows which adjustments were attempted, which were abandoned, where own-figure marks carried a wrong number forward, and whether marks stop at the point a question changes from calculation to comment. One paper is enough to rank the two or three error patterns costing the most marks. What one paper cannot show is pace under full exam conditions if the paper was a short unit test, which is why a timed paper is sat early in any block.

faqs.question: Why does my child balance the trial balance in class but not in the exam?
faqs.answer: Almost always timing rather than understanding. In class the trial balance is the task; in the exam it arrives after a long question that has already eaten the thinking time, and the checking at the end gets cut. The marked script shows this clearly: accurate early work, then arithmetic slips concentrated in the final questions. The fix is practice at speed on the mechanical parts, so that double entry and balancing run without conscious effort and the available time goes to the parts that need judgement.

faqs.question: How many hours of Accounting tuition does a Year 11 student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: If the problem is diagnosable error patterns rather than missing content, a block of eight to twelve one-hour sessions across a term is a common shape, with a timed paper every second week. If a whole topic such as limited company accounts or incomplete records was never secured, add three or four sessions for that topic alone. Starting six weeks before a series changes the arithmetic: the hours go into converting existing knowledge into marks rather than into new teaching, and the gains are narrower but faster.

faqs.question: What does Accounting tuition cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE and A Level specialist. Those bands come from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026. Ask what the rate includes: full-paper marking against the mark scheme is the line most often missing from a cheaper quote.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Accounting tutor to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. For Accounting that works well, because the material is annotated scripts, ledger layouts and screen-shared statements. It also widens the choice of tutor: a family in Jebel Ali or Mirdif gets someone who marks Accounting papers weekly rather than the nearest generalist who is free that evening.

faqs.question: Is Accounting a sensible IGCSE option choice for my child?
faqs.answer: It suits students who are accurate, who tolerate repetitive procedure, and who are willing to write short evaluative paragraphs. It does not reward students who want to discuss ideas without precision, because format and labelling carry real marks. Before choosing it, check two practical things at the school: how many candidates it entered in the last series, and whether the same teacher also carries the A Level group. A single-teacher option subject gives you no second opinion inside the school if something goes wrong.

faqs.question: What is the suspense account and why does it cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: The suspense account holds the difference when a trial balance does not agree, and it is cleared as each one-sided error is corrected. Marks are lost in a predictable way: candidates correct the errors in the ledger accounts, score those marks, then leave the suspense account with a balance or omit it entirely, losing the marks tied to the reconciliation. It is a procedural habit rather than a concept, which is why it is one of the cheapest sets of marks to recover in a short block of sessions.

faqs.question: My child gets the ratios right but still loses marks on the analysis. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the analysis marks are written marks, awarded for using the figures just calculated. A candidate who computes a current ratio of 1.4 and then writes that liquidity looks weak without citing 1.4 has answered a general question rather than this one. Examiners reward a stated position, a figure from the candidate's own working as support, and a limitation or comparison. That is a three-sentence structure a student can rehearse, and it typically recovers three to six marks per paper.

faqs.question: Can we use Cambridge past papers if the school enters us with Edexcel?
faqs.answer: For content practice, yes, with care. The topics overlap heavily, so Cambridge questions on control accounts or depreciation are useful drills. For exam rehearsal, no: paper structure, mark allocation and command-word phrasing differ, and a student who has only sat the other board's papers meets unfamiliar instructions under time pressure. Sit timed papers from the board your child is actually entered with, and use the other board's material for topic practice only. Both boards publish specimen papers on their own sites.

faqs.question: What evidence should I expect after each Accounting session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was marked, which marks were gained and lost, the error pattern behind the losses, and what your child is practising before the next lesson. Every second week, a marked timed paper with per-question timing and a comparison against the previous attempt. At six weeks, the full series plus a topic log showing which syllabus areas are now secure. If a fortnight produced nothing because the school ran three assessments that week, the note should say that too.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a permit to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

faqs.question: Is KHDA involved in approving private Accounting tutors?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai, where u.ae describes it as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Individual tutors fall under the MoHRE permit route instead. KHDA does issue an Educational Services Permit, but that is a licence for a training institute with premises, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Any tutoring service describing itself as carrying KHDA approval should be asked to show that permit number.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start Accounting support before the series?
faqs.answer: Four weeks still changes marks, but it changes a narrower set of them. In that window the work is layout discipline, labelling, showing workings, timing per question and answering the command word that was asked. Those are the cheap, propagating marks and they can move a borderline candidate. What four weeks cannot do is secure a topic never taught properly, such as manufacturing accounts or incomplete records. If a whole topic is missing, be honest about choosing between covering it and protecting the rest of the paper.

faqs.question: Where does IGCSE Accounting lead after Year 11 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The direct route is Cambridge International AS and A Level Accounting, code 9706, where the step up is in written analysis rather than bookkeeping. Other students move into BTEC Business, A Level Economics or Business, or a university foundation year. Check that your child's Dubai school actually timetables 9706 before assuming continuity, because several schools offer Accounting at 16 and not at 18. Note also that UAE Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education.

dubai/igcse-accounting-tutor.closingBody: Send the last marked Accounting script and your child's list of abandoned questions, and book the free 30-minute trial lesson. There is no card required and no commitment attached to it. The tutor will work two questions from that paper with your child over live video, then write up what the errors were and what they cost in marks, and you keep that write-up whichever way you decide. If you would rather read first, the Dubai hub page lists every IB and IGCSE subject covered for families across the emirate, with the same AED market bands and the same online delivery stated on each one.

dubai/igcse-arabic-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below support Arabic for Dubai students on live video. Before quoting anything they establish which of the two needs you have — an examined specification or the school's own mandatory Arabic course — because the second works from the school's materials and the first does not.

intro.heading: Two purchases, two prices, routinely confused
paragraphs: The phrase 'IGCSE Arabic tutor in Dubai' is typed by two different families. The first has a child entered for an Arabic qualification — Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language 0508 or Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544 — and wants examination support for a specification with papers, mark schemes and a grade. The second has a child in a Dubai private school who is struggling with the Arabic lessons every such school teaches regardless of its licensed curriculum, and who may not be entered for any Arabic examination at all.

Those are different products. The first is ordinary subject tutoring: a specification, past papers, a mark scheme, timed practice. The second is support with a course the school designs under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority's mandatory-subject requirements, where a tutor must work from the school's own materials because the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A provider who quotes the same plan for both has not asked the question, and in this subject the question is almost the entire diagnosis.

There is a third thing families often want and rarely name: conversational or community Arabic for a child growing up in the region. That is a legitimate purchase and it is not an examination service, so it should not be priced as one. Paying a specification-matched rate for conversation practice is one of the commonest overspends in this part of the market, and conversation practice is also the one need that is well served at the lower published tiers.

The pricing consequence is substantial. Published rates in this emirate, read in October 2026, run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget end, through AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, to AED 270 at TutorChase for specialist work and AED 200-450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists per the Bestimate survey. Which of those bands is correct for Arabic depends entirely on which of the three needs you actually have.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Arabic is the one subject where the in-home argument is not purely about convenience, because native speakers are locally abundant in this emirate in a way that specialist physics tutors are not. The honest answer is that online widens the pool across the region rather than narrowing it, and that the published premium of AED 180-500 for in-home work against AED 150-300 online still buys a commute rather than a better hour of teaching.

dubai/igcse-arabic-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic appears at several points in a Dubai school career and the reason for studying it changes at each. These are the four that shape what a family should buy.

programmes.name: The mandatory Arabic course, all year groups
programmes.ageRange: Ages 4-18 · throughout a Dubai private school
programmes.description: Arabic is taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language. It is internally assessed, it does not produce an external grade on its own, and it is the course most families are actually asking about when they search.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Teachers of Arabic in Dubai private schools must hold the relevant approval from KHDA for the subject.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language
programmes.description: An examined qualification for students for whom Arabic is a first language, assessing reading comprehension and extended writing in Standard Arabic at a level comparable to a first-language English specification. A genuine subject with its own papers, and a serious piece of work rather than an easy grade for a native speaker.
programmes.countryNote: The common Dubai misunderstanding is that a child who speaks Arabic at home will pass a first-language specification without preparation. Spoken dialect and examined Standard Arabic are not the same register, and the writing requirement in particular catches fluent speakers who have never written at length.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a Foreign Language
programmes.description: An examined qualification for learners of Arabic rather than native speakers, assessing listening, reading and writing at a foreign-language level. A different specification with different expectations, and the right entry for a non-Arab student who has studied Arabic through a Dubai school's mandatory programme.
programmes.countryNote: Placement between the two specifications is the most consequential decision in this subject and it is made by the school. An under-placed native speaker loses access to the top of the range in a harder specification; an over-placed learner is marked against expectations they cannot meet.

programmes.name: Arabic after 16, and the equivalency question
programmes.description: Some students continue Arabic at A Level or as an IB Diploma language, and some stop at 16. The decision interacts with the Ministry of Education equivalency route in a way most families are never told, because Arabic sits outside the subject count that route uses.
programmes.countryNote: The ministry's published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. That does not make Arabic unimportant; it means a family budgeting tutoring hours should know which subjects the count actually uses.

dubai/igcse-arabic-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic support divides into components and needs, and they carry different prices. These are the units a Dubai plan is built from.

subjects.name: Standard Arabic reading comprehension
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0508 and, at a different level, 0544
subjects.description: Extracting information, inferring meaning and responding to a text in Standard Arabic. The component where fluent speakers from a dialect background most often underperform, because reading unvocalised formal prose at speed is a trained skill rather than a consequence of fluency.

subjects.name: Extended writing in Standard Arabic
subjects.description: Composition and directed writing to a specified purpose and audience. The highest-value component to work on for a native speaker, because fluency in speech transfers only partly into structured formal writing and almost not at all into examination structure.

subjects.name: Grammar and morphology
subjects.description: Verb forms, agreement, case endings and sentence structure in Standard Arabic. Drillable, determinate and often the fastest route to visible mark movement, which also makes it the part that can be practised at a lower market tier once the method is taught.

subjects.name: Vocabulary building for the foreign-language route
subjects.description: Topic-based vocabulary tested through listening, reading and writing. A memorisation task that needs scheduling rather than expertise, which means a learner can bank most of it with a well-built list and discipline instead of paid hours.

subjects.name: Listening skills
subjects.description: Comprehension of spoken Standard Arabic at examination pace, which differs from the dialect a student hears around Dubai daily. Practice material matters more than teaching here, and the material has to be in the register the paper uses.

subjects.name: The mandatory Arabic school course
subjects.levels: All Dubai private schools, all year groups
subjects.description: The school's own programme under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements, internally assessed. Support has to work from the school's materials, because the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: Mandatory alongside Arabic in Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Taught with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Arab students in Islamic Education and Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

subjects.name: Conversational and community Arabic
subjects.description: Spoken fluency for a child growing up in the region. A legitimate and valuable purchase that should not be priced as examination tutoring, and the one Arabic need genuinely well served at the lower published market tiers.

subjects.name: Handwriting and script fluency
subjects.levels: Relevant to both specifications and the school course
subjects.description: Writing Arabic script at speed and legibly under examination conditions. An overlooked constraint for students who read comfortably and write slowly, and a mechanical problem with a mechanical fix.

subjects.name: Examination technique in Arabic
subjects.description: Reading the question, allocating time across components, and structuring an extended answer. Identical in kind to the technique work any language specification needs, and frequently absent from Arabic preparation because the subject is treated as a language rather than as an examination.

dubai/igcse-arabic-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the rate does not vary by postcode. What varies is the in-home quote a family is comparing against, and in Arabic that quote behaves differently across the emirate than it does in other subjects.

sections.heading: Which Arabic are you buying, and what each costs
paragraphs: Before any rate is comparable, decide which of three things you need. An examined specification, where a child is entered for Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language 0508 or Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544 and the object is a grade. The school's mandatory Arabic course, which every Dubai private school teaches regardless of its licensed curriculum and which is internally assessed. Or conversational Arabic, for a child growing up in the region whose family wants them to speak it.

Those three need different people and sit at different published bands. Specification support is ordinary subject tutoring at the qualified band of AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and specialist work quoted at AED 270 by TutorChase. School-course support is also qualified-band work but usually fewer hours, because the scope is bounded by what the school is teaching that term. Conversation practice needs a capable speaker and a routine, which is well served at the budget tier where EdFlik publishes from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52.

The most expensive mistake is buying the first when you need the third. A family worried that their child is losing Arabic buys forty hours of specification tutoring at the qualified band, when the actual need was conversation and vocabulary at a fraction of the price and twice the frequency. The reverse mistake also happens: a child entered for 0508 given conversational practice at the budget tier, who arrives at an extended-writing paper having never had a piece of formal Arabic writing marked.

The first question to ask any provider is therefore which of the three they think you need, and whether they asked before quoting. A quote that arrives without that question has been produced from a subject name rather than from a requirement, and in Arabic the subject name tells you almost nothing about the work.

sections.heading: First Language against Foreign Language, and why it changes the price
paragraphs: Cambridge offers Arabic as a First Language, 0508, and Arabic as a Foreign Language, 0544. They are different specifications for different candidates, with different expectations of reading comprehension and writing, and the one a student is entered for is decided by the school. That decision determines which tutor profile is appropriate and therefore what the work costs.

The most common Dubai misconception is that a child who speaks Arabic at home will manage a first-language specification without preparation. Spoken dialect and examined Standard Arabic are different registers. A student can be entirely fluent in conversation and still read unvocalised formal prose slowly, and still have never written eight hundred structured words of Standard Arabic to a specified purpose. The writing component is where that gap appears, and it appears as a mark rather than as a difficulty anybody noticed earlier.

The reverse misplacement is just as costly. A non-Arab student who has studied Arabic through a Dubai school's mandatory programme for several years may be well suited to the foreign-language specification and badly suited to the first-language one. Being marked against first-language expectations produces a low grade that reflects the placement rather than the student, and it is difficult to recover once an entry is made.

The useful intervention is small and specific: two or three sessions producing one marked piece against each specification's expectations, with a written recommendation. That is qualified-band work for a handful of hours rather than a year's commitment, and it is the highest-value Arabic purchase available to a family who is unsure. Ask the school which specification the student is entered for before anything else, because exams officers hold the codes and teachers frequently do not.

sections.heading: The mandatory Arabic course, and the rule that limits what a tutor may do
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority's mandatory-subject requirements, with those requirements due to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a family, the practical point is that their child has Arabic lessons whether or not they are entered for any Arabic examination.

KHDA also sets structure. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

The rule that most directly affects paid support is the content restriction: for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A tutor therefore cannot substitute their own Arabic programme for the school's. Support has to work from the school's materials, its texts and its assessment criteria, which means a family needs to supply those before the first session or the session cannot be properly planned.

That bounds the cost in a useful way. Where the need is the school course, the scope is whatever the school is teaching this term, which is usually far less than a year-long weekly commitment. It also means a provider offering a comprehensive Arabic curriculum for a mandatory-subject problem is offering something that does not fit the requirement. Dubai private schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold the relevant approval from KHDA for those subjects; that applies to school staff, and no tutoring provider should present it as a credential it holds.

sections.heading: Arabic and the five-subject equivalency count
paragraphs: One published fact changes how a family should think about Arabic tutoring hours, and almost no tutoring page in this market states it. The UAE Ministry of Education's equivalency requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That is not an argument for neglecting Arabic. It is information a family is entitled to when allocating a finite tutoring budget across eight or nine subjects. A household choosing between forty hours on Arabic and forty hours on a subject that does count toward the five is making a trade-off, and it should be an informed one rather than one made in the dark. For many families the right answer is still Arabic, for reasons that have nothing to do with equivalency.

Two related points of accuracy. One competing UAE tutoring site states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the ministry's published requirement is five. And the equivalency process is the ministry's own, performed through official channels: no tutoring provider carries it out, guarantees it or can accelerate it, and no page should imply that tutoring is required for it. Verify the current wording on the ministry's own pages before acting, because requirements of this kind are revised.

On the American track the ministry's published figures are different again and worth knowing if a family is comparing routes: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been verified on the ministry's own pages, so none is published here.
