sections.heading: What the travel premium buys in Arabic specifically
paragraphs: In most subjects the argument against the in-home premium is simple: it restricts the tutor pool to driving distance and buys nothing but a commute. Arabic is the one subject in this market where that argument needs qualifying honestly, because Arabic-speaking tutors are locally abundant in Dubai in a way that Higher Level physics specialists are not. A family here can genuinely find a capable Arabic speaker nearby, which is not true of every subject.

The published figures still run one way. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500 and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. Local abundance means a family has more in-home options in Arabic; it does not make the premium cheaper.

What online adds in Arabic is a different kind of range. The pool is not limited to Dubai: it extends across the region, which matters for the specific profiles that are harder to find locally — someone who has taught the 0508 extended-writing component to examination standard, or who marks formal Standard Arabic writing against published requirements rather than correcting it as language. Local abundance of speakers and local scarcity of specification-trained markers are both true at once.

For conversational Arabic the honest position is that either format works and the cheaper one is the budget tier online, because frequency matters more than medium. Three twenty-five-minute conversations a week beat one ninety-minute session, and at published budget rates of AED 33-65 an hour that frequency is affordable in a way it is not at AED 350. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India, and UAE lessons run one-to-one on live video.

sections.heading: Budgeting Arabic across a Dubai household
paragraphs: Arabic creates a budgeting problem specific to this emirate: most families have more than one child in the same school, each with mandatory Arabic, each potentially at a different stage, and the instinct is to buy the same weekly session for all of them. That is usually the wrong shape, because the three needs identified above rarely apply equally across siblings.

The pattern that works is a split. The child with an examination entry gets qualified-band specification support, concentrated on the component the marked evidence names rather than across the whole subject. The child who is struggling with the school course gets a short block of school-material support, bounded by what the school is teaching that term. The younger child who is simply losing spoken Arabic gets frequent short conversation practice at the budget tier, which is both cheaper and more effective than a weekly hour.

The monthly figures in this market support that split arithmetically. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, and advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. A household that places each child at the correct tier spends materially less than one that buys the mid band three times over.

One scheduling note that saves money in practice. Arabic sessions are among the easiest to lose to clashes, because mandatory-subject deadlines, school events and Ramadan timing all move. Short frequent sessions survive disruption better than a single weekly hour, because losing one twenty-five-minute slot out of three is a minor event and losing the weekly hour is the week. Through Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar times and the written task is usually reduced rather than cancelled.

sections.heading: The Dubai context: a growing sector and a regulated subject
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually against six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, and seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake adding 16,846 places, with enrolment up six per cent during 2025-26. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27.

Arabic is the subject where that regulatory structure is most visible to a family, because it is the one mandated across every licensed curriculum. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. Every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement sits on top of that, which is why a British-curriculum school in Dubai teaches Arabic and a British school in Britain does not.

The emirate map is worth knowing if a family moves. Dubai is regulated by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

Three rules of record close this. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service with a stated two-working-day completion time; tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than reproduced. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or Cambridge, operates no UAE office or centre, and makes no claim to the KHDA subject approval that school Arabic teachers are required to hold.

sections.heading: What not to pay for in Arabic support
paragraphs: The first is a comprehensive external Arabic curriculum sold as a solution to a mandatory-subject problem. For the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so a tutor who proposes replacing the school's programme with their own is proposing something that does not fit the requirement. Support for that course works from the school's materials or it is not support for that course.

The second is any suggestion that a provider holds, or can obtain, the KHDA approval that Dubai private schools must ensure their Arabic and Islamic Education teachers hold. That requirement applies to school staff teaching those subjects in a licensed school. A tutoring provider presenting it as its own credential is claiming a regulatory status it does not have, and that is the single most dangerous phrase available in this part of the market.

The third is a promise about a grade. Grade boundaries are determined after a series on the basis of candidate performance, so no provider can commit to an Arabic grade in advance any more than to a maths one. What can be committed to is procedural: a marked piece of formal writing after every session, with the requirement it fell short of named, and a record a parent can read.

The fourth is a specification rate for conversation practice. Spoken fluency needs a capable speaker and frequency, both of which the budget tier supplies at AED 33-65 an hour per published rates. Paying AED 270 for conversational Arabic is the clearest overspend in this subject, and it is common precisely because families searching for an Arabic tutor are rarely asked which of the three needs they have.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge IGCSE Arabic 0508 and 0544?
faqs.answer: They are different specifications for different candidates. Arabic as a First Language 0508 is for students for whom Arabic is a first language and assesses reading comprehension and extended writing in Standard Arabic at a level comparable to a first-language English specification. Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544 is for learners of Arabic and assesses listening, reading and writing at a foreign-language level. The school decides the entry. The decision matters more than almost any other in this subject, because being marked against the wrong set of expectations produces a grade that reflects the placement rather than the student.

faqs.question: My child speaks Arabic at home. Will the first-language IGCSE be easy?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and this is the most common misunderstanding in Dubai. Spoken dialect and examined Standard Arabic are different registers. A student can be entirely fluent in conversation and still read unvocalised formal prose slowly, and still have never written several hundred structured words of Standard Arabic to a specified purpose and audience. The writing component is where that gap shows, and it shows as a mark rather than as a difficulty anyone noticed earlier. One marked extended piece before the entry is made tells a family more than any amount of discussion about fluency.

faqs.question: Why does my child have Arabic lessons in a British-curriculum school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because it is required. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority's mandatory-subject requirements. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for the two groups prohibited.

faqs.question: Can a tutor replace the school's Arabic programme with their own?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering to is offering something that does not fit the requirement. For the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support for a school's Arabic course has to work from the school's own materials, texts and assessment criteria. The practical consequence for a family is that the school's current materials need to be supplied before the first session, and that the scope of the work is bounded by what the school is teaching this term rather than by a year-long curriculum.

faqs.question: Does Arabic count toward the UAE equivalency subject requirement?
faqs.answer: No. The Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That is not an argument for neglecting Arabic; it is information a family allocating a finite tutoring budget across eight or nine subjects is entitled to. The process is the ministry's own, and tutoring is neither required for it nor able to guarantee it.

faqs.question: How much does an Arabic tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends which of three things you are buying, and that is the whole answer. Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online provision at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik, a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and specialist work at AED 270 at TutorChase. Examined specification support sits at the qualified band. School-course support sits there too but for fewer hours. Conversation practice belongs at the budget tier, and paying a specialist rate for it is the commonest overspend in this subject.

faqs.question: Is a home Arabic tutor in Dubai better value than online?
faqs.answer: Arabic is the one subject where the local argument deserves a fair hearing, because Arabic speakers are abundant in this emirate in a way that Higher Level physics specialists are not. A family here genuinely has in-home options. The published numbers still run one way: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 online. What online adds is regional range for the harder-to-find profile, someone who marks formal Standard Arabic writing against published requirements rather than correcting it as language.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to stop a child losing spoken Arabic in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Frequency at the budget tier, not a weekly hour at the qualified one. Three sessions of twenty-five minutes a week with a capable speaker does more for spoken fluency than one ninety-minute session, and at published budget rates of AED 33-65 an hour that frequency is affordable in a way it is not at AED 300. Spoken practice needs a competent speaker and a routine rather than specification expertise. Pair it with a vocabulary list tested in writing and scored, which the family can run themselves at no cost at all.

faqs.question: My child reads Arabic well but writes slowly. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and cheaply, because it is mechanical. Writing Arabic script at speed and legibly under examination conditions is a motor skill, not a language skill, and a student who reads comfortably and writes slowly is losing marks to a constraint that has nothing to do with their Arabic. The fix is one teaching session on technique followed by ten minutes of daily self-run practice, measured by the amount written in a fixed time. It needs no paid hours after the first session, and it is frequently the single quickest improvement available in this subject.

faqs.question: Which Arabic component is worth paying for first?
faqs.answer: On a first-language entry, extended writing in Standard Arabic, because that is where fluent speakers lose most and because it cannot be improved without somebody marking formal writing against the specification's requirements. On a foreign-language entry, listening and vocabulary, both of which respond to material and repetition more than to teaching, and both of which can be substantially self-run once the method is set. On the school's mandatory course, whatever the school is currently assessing, which is why the school's materials come before the plan.

faqs.question: How many Arabic tutoring hours does a Dubai family usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most plans assume, provided each need goes to the right tier. A placement check between the two specifications is two or three qualified-band sessions. A school-course block is usually six weeks and then a review, because the scope is bounded by the term. Extended-writing work on a first-language entry is a weekly session for a term, then fortnightly. Conversation practice and vocabulary testing are frequent, cheap and often self-run. A household that places each child correctly spends materially less than one that buys the mid band repeatedly.

faqs.question: Do Arabic tutors in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the same basis as any other subject. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no provider can justify a charge on licensing grounds, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor claim KHDA approval to teach Arabic?
faqs.answer: A private tutoring provider should not. Dubai private schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the relevant KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and that requirement applies to school staff teaching in a licensed school. A tutoring provider presenting it as its own credential is claiming a regulatory status it does not hold, which is the most dangerous phrasing available in this part of the market. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a separate thing issued to training institutes.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE Arabic exams sat by candidates in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only, so a March date on a tutoring page belongs to another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE qualifications run May/June and November. One administrative point matters as much as the dates: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Can Arabic sessions move during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should, which is one practical argument for short frequent slots over a single weekly hour. Through Ramadan school days shorten and concentration shifts, so sessions move to post-Iftar times and the written task between sessions is usually reduced rather than cancelled. Short slots also survive the ordinary disruption of a Dubai school calendar better: losing one twenty-five-minute session out of three in a week is a minor event, while losing the one weekly hour loses the week. Scheduling is agreed inside school breaks rather than across their start.

dubai/igcse-arabic-tutor.closingHeading: Decide which Arabic you are buying
dubai/igcse-arabic-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest useful step in Arabic is a decision rather than a purchase. Are you buying support for an examined specification with an entry, help with the Arabic course your Dubai school must teach, or spoken fluency for a child growing up in the region? Those three sit at different published price bands and need different people, and most quotes in this market are produced without the question being asked. Establish the need, get the specification code or the school's current materials, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and ask for a plan with a stated hour count.

Each works to one named specification, marks to the published scheme rather than to impression, and tags every lost mark with the command term or the skill it belonged to so the pattern becomes visible after three weeks instead of three terms.

intro.heading: The paper map comes before the biology
paragraphs: Two questions settle most of what an IGCSE biology plan should contain, and neither is about biology. Which board, and which tier. Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is tiered: Core candidates sit one multiple-choice paper and one theory paper, Extended candidates sit the harder versions of both, and all candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1 is untiered and sets two written papers, the longer running two hours and the shorter one hour fifteen, with practical skills assessed inside them rather than separately.

The consequences are immediate. A Cambridge student has a separate twenty per cent of their grade sitting in a paper that tests experimental skills barely present in the content list: describing a method, identifying a control variable, plotting to a sensible scale, reading a result from a table and spotting an anomaly. A Pearson student has no such paper and instead meets those skills embedded in ordinary structured questions. Those two students, nominally doing IGCSE biology in the same Dubai year group, need different revision weeks.

The second thing the paper map tells you is where the weight is. In Cambridge 0610 the theory paper carries fifty per cent on its own. Most revision in Dubai is organised by topic, which is the wrong axis: a student who spends equal effort on every topic while half the grade sits in one paper's question style has allocated against the wrong thing. The honest plan starts from the component weightings and works back to topics. That reordering is free, it takes ten minutes, and it is the single change most likely to make the next three months of revision count for something.

What a session fixes in this subject is unusually predictable. Biology is content-heavy and calculation-light, so lost marks concentrate in three repeatable categories: the command term was misread, the data was understood and not quoted, or a precise term was replaced by a correct paraphrase. All three are visible on a marked script within a fortnight and all three are habits rather than knowledge gaps, which is why a marking-led plan moves biology marks faster than a teaching-led one, and why the first month should look more like an audit than a course.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For IGCSE biology that is a practical advantage: a Dubai family in Mirdif or Al Furjan gets a tutor who has taught their specific specification and component rather than whichever science tutor is within a short drive, and the marked scripts accumulate as files that can be compared across a term rather than disappearing into a folder.

dubai/igcse-biology-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE biology sits in the middle of a longer sequence, and the stage either side of it changes what a session should contain. These are the four points that matter for a Dubai family.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external assessment, which is why biology habits form unchecked. The specific carry-over problems are vocabulary imprecision and answering every question as a description, both of which are tolerated in Key Stage 3 marking and penalised from the first IGCSE paper onward.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai British-curriculum schools begin IGCSE content in Year 9, so a student transferring in from a school that did not can arrive in Year 10 a term behind on content nobody flags. A diagnostic paper on arrival settles it in an hour.

programmes.name: IGCSE Biology, Year 10
programmes.description: Roughly the first sixty per cent of the specification, with the tier decision still open on Cambridge entries. The right year to establish command-term discipline and to begin the practical-skills work, because both are habits and both take weeks rather than days to shift.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's academic year runs late August to late June or early July with a long December break, which gives three uneven teaching blocks. The end-of-Year-10 mock usually falls in the shortest of them, which is worth knowing when reading its result.

programmes.name: IGCSE Biology, Year 11
programmes.description: Remaining content, mocks and the series. Tutoring narrows to the theory paper's question style, the practical component, and the three or four topics still unreliable. A marking-led block here produces more movement than content teaching, because by Year 11 most of the content has been met at least once.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Dubai schools enter overwhelmingly for the summer window with November kept as the resit route.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma biology
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is the entry currency, and Dubai sixth forms typically ask for grade 6 or 7 to continue a science. What transfers best into Diploma or A Level biology is not content but technique: command-term discipline and data handling are the same skills at a higher level.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. The process is the ministry's and tutoring is not required for it.

dubai/igcse-biology-tutor.subjectsIntro: IGCSE biology is taught by topic and examined by paper, and a plan needs both views. These are the topics where Dubai scripts lose most, with what the loss actually is.

subjects.name: Characteristics and classification of living organisms
subjects.description: Early content treated as easy and marked strictly. Marks go to the precise feature named in the specification rather than a reasonable description, which makes it the clearest early illustration of why paraphrase does not score.

subjects.name: Cells, movement in and out of cells
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis and active transport. Osmosis explanations are where most Dubai students first meet a mark scheme that requires direction, gradient and the word used correctly in the same sentence. A partially correct explanation scores nothing here.

subjects.name: Enzymes and biological molecules
subjects.description: Enzyme action, specificity, and the effect of temperature and pH. The topic generates the most common data-based question in the subject, and the loss is reliably the same: the trend described, the figure never quoted.

subjects.name: Plant nutrition and transport
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, extended at Extended tier
subjects.description: Photosynthesis, limiting factors, transpiration and translocation. Limiting-factor graphs are a graph-reading skill before they are a biology skill, and students who cannot say which factor is limiting at a named point on the curve lose marks they understood.

subjects.name: Human nutrition, respiration and gas exchange
subjects.description: A large body of content with precise terminology throughout. Mostly a retrieval problem, and the clearest case where spaced self-testing rather than more explanation is the right intervention.

subjects.name: Transport in humans and coordination
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, substantially extended at Extended tier
subjects.description: Circulation, the heart, homeostasis, nerves and hormones. Explanation questions here want a causal chain in order, and scripts lose marks for giving the right components in the wrong sequence.

subjects.name: Inheritance and variation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, substantially extended at Extended tier
subjects.description: Genetic crosses, variation, selection and at Extended level more demanding inheritance problems. The one biology topic where a student can be defeated by the logic rather than the volume, which makes it worth dedicated session time.

subjects.name: Organisms and their environment
subjects.description: Food chains, nutrient cycles, population growth and human impact. Marks go to answers that name a specific organism or process from the stimulus rather than giving a general ecological statement.

subjects.name: Experimental skills and investigations
subjects.levels: Assessed in Cambridge Paper 5 or 6, embedded in Edexcel papers
subjects.description: Method description, variable control, measurement, recording, plotting and anomaly identification. Twenty per cent of the Cambridge grade sits here and almost none of it appears in the content list, which is why it is the least revised component in the subject.

subjects.name: Command terms and terminology
subjects.levels: Not a topic, and the largest single source of loss
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each buy something different, and biology mark schemes frequently require the exact term rather than a correct paraphrase. One habit, worth marks across every topic simultaneously.

sections.heading: The IGCSE biology paper map, by board and tier
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is tiered and splits across three components. Core candidates sit a multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent and a theory paper worth fifty. Extended candidates sit the harder versions of the same two, at the same weightings. All candidates then sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, worth twenty per cent. The tier caps the grade: Core cannot produce better than a C or 5, Extended runs the full range.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1 removes the tier. One specification, two written papers — the longer running two hours and the shorter one hour fifteen — and the full grade range available to every candidate. Practical skills are assessed inside those written papers rather than in a separate component, which means there is no twenty per cent block to revise as a unit and the same skills appear distributed through ordinary structured questions.

Those differences change the plan rather than decorating it. A Cambridge student should treat the experimental component as a subject in its own right, because its content barely overlaps the biology specification and because twenty per cent of a grade is worth four or five sessions of dedicated work. A Pearson student has nothing to block-book and instead needs practical vocabulary recognised when it surfaces mid-question.

The first action for a Dubai family is therefore administrative rather than academic: ask the school's exams officer for the board, the syllabus code and, for Cambridge, which practical component the school enters. Teachers often do not have the codes to hand; exams officers always do, because entries are made from them. One email removes the largest source of wasted tutoring in this subject.

sections.heading: Half the Cambridge grade sits in one theory paper
paragraphs: The Cambridge 0610 theory paper carries fifty per cent on its own, which makes its question style the most valuable thing a Dubai student can practise. It asks for structured written answers across the specification: short recall items, explanation chains, data interpretation from supplied tables and graphs, and questions built on an unfamiliar organism or context that the student has to reason about rather than recall.

That last category is the one most Dubai students are least ready for. A question presenting an unfamiliar plant and asking the student to suggest why a named adaptation is useful is not testing whether they have met the plant. It is testing whether they can apply a general principle to a new case, and students who revised by memorising examples read it as a question about something they were never taught. Recognising the pattern is a technique lesson, not a content one.

The explanation chain is the second. Marks in biology explanation questions are allocated to steps, in order, and a student who gives the first and third steps of a causal sequence earns less than one who gives the first and second. Scripts routinely contain all the correct biology arranged in the wrong sequence, which reads as understanding and marks as partial. Enforcing the chain structure in marking changes it inside a month.

The third is scale. A fifty per cent paper rewards stamina and pacing, and students who have only ever answered questions in ten-minute homework blocks do not know that they write well for thirty minutes and then compress. A full timed paper under conditions exposes it immediately, which is a strong argument for sitting one early in Year 10 rather than meeting the information in a Year 11 mock.
bullets: Half the Cambridge grade sits in the theory paper's question style
Unfamiliar-context questions test application, not recall of the example
Explanation marks are allocated to steps in order, not to content present

sections.heading: The practical component nobody revises
paragraphs: On a Cambridge entry, twenty per cent of the biology grade sits in a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and almost none of what it tests appears in the content specification. It asks the student to describe a method precisely enough to be repeated, to identify the independent, dependent and control variables, to record measurements in a correctly headed table with units, to plot points to a sensible scale with a suitable line, to identify an anomalous result and to suggest an improvement that addresses an actual limitation.

Because those skills are not content, they do not appear on a revision timetable built from the specification. Students revise topics, sit the alternative-to-practical paper having never practised plotting under time, and lose marks that had nothing to do with biology. Four to six sessions on the component is one of the highest-return purchases available in the subject, and it is almost always overlooked in favour of another pass through human transport.

The specific losses are consistent across Dubai scripts. Axes plotted without units. A scale chosen so the points occupy a quarter of the grid. A line of best fit drawn as a dot-to-dot. An anomaly circled without being excluded from any subsequent calculation. An improvement suggested as 'use more accurate equipment' where the real limitation was the number of repeats. Each of those is a mark, each is mechanical, and each is fixed by doing it wrongly once in front of someone who says so.

On a Pearson 4BI1 entry there is no separate paper, which does not mean the skills are absent. They appear inside ordinary structured questions: a method described in the stem with a flaw to identify, a table to complete, a graph to read. The plan for a Pearson student is therefore recognition rather than block revision, and the practical vocabulary needs to be as automatic as the biological terminology.

sections.heading: The three categories of lost mark in Dubai biology scripts
paragraphs: Mark a Dubai IGCSE biology script against the published scheme and the losses sort into three recurring categories, with very little left over. The first is the command term. State wants a fact with no justification. Describe wants observable detail. Explain wants a causal chain. Suggest wants applied reasoning on unfamiliar material. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence. Calculate wants the working shown. A student who writes a description every time loses marks on every paper simultaneously.

The second is data use. Questions built on a table or a graph require the figure to be quoted, and a biologically correct answer that cites no number scores less than a thinner answer that does. The related trap is answering 'why' where the question asked 'what the data show'. Students lose marks for giving a better answer to a question nobody asked, which is a frustrating way to lose two marks on every data question in a paper.

The third is terminology precision. Biology mark schemes frequently require a specific term rather than a correct paraphrase. A student who writes 'the substance that carries the message' when the scheme wants 'neurotransmitter' has demonstrated understanding and earned nothing. Unlike the first two categories this one is a retrieval problem, which means the fix is spaced self-testing rather than marking, and it can be run by the student alone.

Separating the three matters because they have different costs. Command-term discipline and data-use habits need someone marking against the scheme and tagging the loss, which is paid work for a limited block of six to eight sessions. Terminology precision needs testing, which is free if the student will do it. Families who buy all three as one undifferentiated weekly hour pay for a service where a question bank would have done, and skip the part that needed a specialist.

sections.heading: Core or Extended in biology specifically
paragraphs: On a Cambridge entry the tier caps the grade, so the decision is consequential and it is usually made by the school in the spring of Year 10 or the autumn of Year 11 on the basis of classwork. The decision should be made from marked papers at both tiers instead, and the argument for that is strongest in biology because the content difference between the tiers is unevenly distributed.

Extended biology adds depth rather than breadth in most topics, and the additions concentrate in inheritance, coordination and plant transport. A student who is comfortable across the shared content and specifically weak in genetics logic may be an Extended candidate who needs four sessions on crosses, not a Core candidate. A student whose losses are spread evenly across every topic and every question type is a different case, and for them a secure Core grade is a better outcome than an optimistic Extended entry producing a grade E.

The wrong outcome is not a Core entry. Five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 is what the UAE Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route asks for, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, so a secure grade C counts. The wrong outcome is a tier chosen without marked evidence in either direction, which is what happens when the conversation is held in February with nothing on the table.

Post-16 consequence is the other input. Dubai sixth forms typically ask for grade 6 or 7 to continue a science at A Level or at Diploma Higher Level, which a Core entry cannot produce. A family for whom biology at 18 is the plan should treat the Year 10 tier conversation as a decision about Year 12, and should have marked papers from both tiers before the school's internal deadline rather than after it.

sections.heading: The Dubai timeline, counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai family reading a March date on a tutoring site is reading another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Dubai schools enter overwhelmingly for the summer window and keep November as the resit route for one or two subjects.

Entries are made by the school months before the papers, and on a Cambridge entry they include the tier and the practical component. That is why the tier evidence needs to exist in the spring of Year 10: once the entry is made, a change becomes an administrative negotiation rather than a decision. Ask the exams officer for the school's internal deadline rather than the board's, because the internal one is the date that actually binds a family.

Results timing sets the resit clock. Pearson's published pattern is the clearest illustration available: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. A student improving one subject therefore has a bounded window that opens the week results arrive.

One Cambridge administrative detail catches families who move. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Revising from a timetable downloaded for a different zone is revising to the wrong clock; confirm the zone with the exams officer and work from the live official timetable.

sections.heading: What IGCSE biology support costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Biology is well supplied in this market, which keeps it off the top of the range. Published rates read in October 2026: EdFlik lists online tuition from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

The sensible allocation follows the three loss categories. Terminology precision is retrieval and can be run by the student or at the bottom tier. Command-term and data-use habits need marking against the published scheme, which is the qualified band at AED 150-300 for a block of six to eight sessions with a stated end. The practical-skills block is four to six sessions at the same band. That totals a modest number of paid hours rather than a two-year weekly commitment.

In-home provision is the comparison most Dubai families are weighing. Bestimate puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500 and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. The premium pays for a commute. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

No IB Gram rate card appears here, because an IGCSE biology plan is priced by board, component and hour count. The free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family and with no card details taken, is where the plan and the figure are discussed together. Every AED figure above belongs to the provider or survey that published it, and those are the bands any quote should be held against.

sections.heading: Dubai's regulatory context and the rules a tutor works inside
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually against six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum provision the largest share of enrolment. Seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake, four of them UK curriculum, adding 16,846 places, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27.

The mandatory-subject requirement shapes a Year 10 or Year 11 week more than families expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising no such lesson falls below 25 minutes.

For biology that matters because retrieval practice needs several short slots a week and those slots have to exist. A Year 11 carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus two or three mandatory UAE subjects has a smaller discretionary week than a revision timetable assumes, and twenty-five minutes four times a week is achievable where ninety minutes four times a week is not. For the mandatory subjects specifically, the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, and teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold the relevant approval from KHDA.

Three rules govern how a tutor works. Private tutoring requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's own service with a stated two-working-day completion time; tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and should be referenced and linked rather than reproduced. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre.

process.title: Get the board, the code and the practical component
process.description: Email the school's exams officer for the board, the syllabus code and, on a Cambridge entry, whether the school enters the practical test or the written alternative. Those three facts set the whole plan. Teachers often do not have them to hand; exams officers always do, because entries are made from them.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken, no obligation. It is spent on one structured question marked live against the published scheme with the command term named and the withheld mark explained, because that shows which of the three loss categories you are actually dealing with.

process.title: One timed theory paper, marked and tagged
process.description: A full theory paper for the correct specification and tier, sat under time and marked to the published scheme, with every loss tagged as command term, data use or terminology. The tag distribution decides what gets bought, and it is frequently not what the family expected to buy.

process.title: Marking block with a stated end
process.description: Where command-term and data-use habits are the issue, six to eight sessions with every question marked before the session and the loss tagged. The block has an end date, because a habit either changes within that window or the diagnosis needs revisiting rather than extending.

process.title: Practical-skills block on Cambridge entries
process.description: Four to six sessions on method description, variable control, recording, plotting and anomaly handling, done live rather than discussed. Twenty per cent of the Cambridge grade sits here and almost none of it appears on a revision timetable built from the specification.

process.title: Tier evidence before the school's deadline
process.description: On a Cambridge entry, papers at both tiers marked and a written recommendation with the marks attached, produced before the school's internal entry deadline. Where the evidence points to Core, the recommendation says Core, because a secure grade C beats an optimistic entry and a grade E.

whyPoints.title: The paper map comes first
whyPoints.description: Board, code, tier and practical component are confirmed before any teaching is planned, because Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1 assess practical skills in completely different places. Planning without that is the largest single source of wasted tutoring in this subject.

whyPoints.title: Losses are tagged, not just counted
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is assigned to command term, data use or terminology precision. Those three have different fixes at different prices, and the tag distribution usually tells a family to buy less than they intended rather than more.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is treated as a component
whyPoints.description: On a Cambridge entry twenty per cent of the grade tests skills that barely appear in the content list, so it gets four to six dedicated sessions with plotting and method writing done live. Most revision timetables never touch it because it is not a topic.

whyPoints.title: Half the grade gets most of the hours
whyPoints.description: The Cambridge theory paper carries fifty per cent on its own, so the weekly session is built around its question style rather than around even topic coverage. Allocating effort by topic when the grade is decided by component is the common planning error.

whyPoints.title: Retrieval work is handed back to the student
whyPoints.description: Terminology precision is a testing problem rather than a teaching one, so it is recommended as spaced self-testing the student runs themselves or buys at the bottom tier. That is a smaller sale and the honest answer for the largest part of biology's content load.

whyPoints.title: The tier recommendation can say Core
whyPoints.description: Where two marked papers show losses spread evenly across every topic and question type, the written recommendation is Core, because a secure grade C counts toward the five subjects the Ministry of Education equivalency route requires. A page that only ever recommends Extended is selling optimism.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0610 and Edexcel 4BI1 for IGCSE biology?
faqs.answer: Tiering and practical assessment. Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is tiered: Core candidates sit a multiple-choice paper at thirty per cent and a theory paper at fifty, Extended candidates sit harder versions of both, and all candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper worth twenty per cent. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1 is untiered, sets two written papers of two hours and one hour fifteen, and assesses practical skills inside them rather than separately. A Cambridge student has a twenty per cent block to revise as a unit; a Pearson student does not.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE biology paper carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: On a Cambridge 0610 entry, the theory paper at fifty per cent, Core or Extended. That makes its question style the most valuable thing to practise, and it is why a plan should be organised by component rather than by even topic coverage. On a Pearson 4BI1 entry the longer two-hour paper carries the larger share of the two. Either way the first planning act is to pull the weightings for the specification the school actually entered, because a revision timetable that treats every topic equally has allocated effort against the wrong axis.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how do you revise for it?
faqs.answer: It is the Cambridge written component that replaces the practical test, worth twenty per cent of the biology grade, and it tests experimental skills rather than biology content. It asks for a method described precisely enough to repeat, variables named and the way they were controlled stated, data recorded in a correctly headed table with units, points plotted to a sensible scale, an anomaly identified and an improvement that addresses a real limitation. Because none of it appears in the content specification it never reaches a topic-based revision timetable, which is why four to six dedicated sessions is high-return work.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on IGCSE biology questions they understood?
faqs.answer: Three recurring reasons, and almost nothing else. The command term was misread, so a description was written where an explanation or a deduction was asked for. The data was understood but never quoted, and the mark scheme required the figure. Or a precise term was replaced with a correct paraphrase, which demonstrates understanding and earns nothing. The first two need someone marking against the published scheme and tagging the loss so the pattern becomes visible. The third needs spaced self-testing, which the student can do alone. Separating them is what stops a family overpaying for the cheap part.

faqs.question: How do data questions work in IGCSE biology?
faqs.answer: A table or a graph is supplied and the mark scheme requires the answer to refer to it. A biologically correct response that cites no number scores less than a thinner response that quotes the figure, which feels unjust and is entirely predictable once seen. The second trap is the question wording: asking what the data show is not asking why, and a student who explains the mechanism has given a better answer to a question nobody asked. Both are habits, both show up on a marked script within a fortnight, and both move quickly once tagged.

faqs.question: Should a Dubai student take Core or Extended IGCSE biology?
faqs.answer: Decide it from marked papers at both tiers rather than from a predicted grade. Extended adds depth concentrated in inheritance, coordination and plant transport, so a student who is comfortable across the shared content and specifically weak in genetics logic may be an Extended candidate needing four sessions on crosses. A student whose losses spread evenly across every topic and question type is better served by a secure Core grade. Weigh the post-16 consequence: Dubai sixth forms typically ask for grade 6 or 7 to continue a science, which a Core entry cannot produce.

faqs.question: Is a Core grade in IGCSE biology still useful in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the equivalency route. The UAE Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. A secure grade C from a Core entry counts toward that. What a Core entry generally cannot do is support entry to A Level or Diploma Higher Level biology in a Dubai sixth form. Equivalency is a ministry process; tutoring is not required for it and does not guarantee it.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE biology exams held for Dubai candidates?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only, so March dates on tutoring sites belong to another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. One administrative point matters as much as the dates: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE biology sessions does a Dubai student actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tag distribution from one marked theory paper, and the total is usually modest. A command-term and data-use habit problem is six to eight sessions with a stated end, because the habit either changes inside that window or the diagnosis was wrong. The Cambridge practical component is four to six sessions. Terminology precision is retrieval work the student runs themselves at no cost. A genuine content gap across several topics is a term of weekly sessions. Buying a two-year weekly commitment before the diagnostic is how families spend without seeing marks move.

faqs.question: Can my child catch up on IGCSE biology content volume with more lessons?
faqs.answer: Lessons are the wrong instrument for a volume problem. Diploma and IGCSE biology are both content-heavy and calculation-light, so the characteristic failure is understanding material in October and being unable to retrieve it in May. Retrieval is built by testing rather than by reading or listening: twenty to thirty minutes of scored self-testing against the specification statements, three or four times a week, with the interval increasing as recall becomes reliable. It is tedious, it is the largest single lever in the subject, and it needs administration rather than subject expertise.

faqs.question: Do Dubai schools enter students for the practical test or the written alternative?
faqs.answer: Both happen in this emirate and the choice is the school's, usually driven by laboratory capacity and cohort size. Established schools with well-equipped laboratories are more likely to enter the practical test; newer schools with larger or growing cohorts more often enter the written alternative. It matters because the preparation differs: a practical test needs apparatus handling and timing in a laboratory, while the written alternative needs method writing, plotting and anomaly identification on paper. Ask the exams officer which component the school enters before buying any practical support.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE biology tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online provision at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik, a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, specialist work at AED 270 at TutorChase, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above per the Bestimate survey, and premium named listings at AED 650. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Biology is well supplied in this market, so a family rarely needs the specialist band and should ask what the extra is for if quoted above the qualified one.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE biology tuition effective for a Year 10 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For the work this subject actually needs, yes. Marking against the published scheme, tagging command-term losses, plotting a graph live with the scale chosen first and writing a method to be marked all work at least as well on a shared screen, and the annotated versions are saved rather than carried away in a folder. What online delivery does not provide is a presence stopping a distracted fifteen-year-old opening another tab, which is managed structurally: sessions in a shared room, timed tasks with the camera on, and a written report that makes disengagement visible within a week.

faqs.question: Is a home biology tutor in Dubai better than online for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The published numbers run one way. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500 and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. Most of the gap pays for a drive at the worst traffic hour of the day. Biology is well supplied online in this market, so there is no scarcity argument for restricting the pool to driving distance. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for our specific IGCSE biology specification?
faqs.answer: You should be told, with the options named rather than a general science tutor quietly substituted. Narrow requests do run short — a specific practical component close to the series, or a board combination a school entered unusually — and the honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. All three beat someone planning for the wrong paper map, which in biology means revising for a practical component the student is not entered for. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit.

dubai/igcse-biology-tutor.closingHeading: One email, then one marked paper
dubai/igcse-biology-tutor.closingBody: Two actions settle most of an IGCSE biology plan, and neither costs anything. Email the school's exams officer for the board, the syllabus code and which practical component the school enters. Then have one timed theory paper marked against the published scheme with every loss tagged as command term, data use or terminology. The paper map says what the plan must cover; the tag distribution says what to buy and what to hand back to the student. Send both, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and ask for a plan with a stated hour count and a stated end date.

dubai/igcse-business-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Business to Dubai students on live video. Each works to one named specification, marks against the published assessment requirements, and reports an application tally on every script so a student can see the gap between knowing the theory and earning the mark for it.

intro.heading: Count the context references, then talk about the grade
paragraphs: Business Studies is the IGCSE subject students most often feel they are doing well at while scoring in the middle, and the reason is unusually easy to demonstrate. Take any marked case-study answer, read it with a highlighter, and mark every sentence that refers to something specific about the business in the question: its name, its market, its size, the problem the case described, the figure in the table. In a strong script the highlighter is busy. In a mid-range Dubai script it barely moves.

That tally is the diagnosis. The content is usually there — a student who can define cash flow, list sources of finance and explain motivation theory has learned the specification — and the marks are not, because business mark schemes award application. Credit attaches to theory used on the named business rather than to theory recited correctly. A perfectly accurate paragraph about the advantages of a private limited company earns a fraction of what the same paragraph earns when it is about the private limited company in the case.

So the record this plan builds begins with the tally on every script. Sentences that apply, sentences that do not, and a count. Students argue with it for about two sessions and then it becomes the most useful number in their file, because it is something they can change deliberately. A tally of two moving to a tally of nine across six weeks is attributable, visible progress in a subject where progress otherwise feels like a matter of opinion. It is also the first number in the file that a school engages with, because it is derived from the school's own marked script rather than from a parent's impression of how well their child writes.

The second item on the record is the calculation tally. Business carries quantitative marks — break-even, gross and net profit margins, cash-flow forecasts, return on capital, market share — and a surprising number of Dubai students skip them in a timed paper on the assumption that the written answers matter more. They are the easiest marks on the paper, they are fully determinate, and leaving them is the single most avoidable loss in the subject. Counting attempted calculations against available ones each week fixes it quickly.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For business the shared screen is the right medium: the case-study extract and the student's own answer sit side by side, highlights go on in a second colour, and the marked version is saved so week six can be compared with week one. A Dubai family in Mirdif or Al Furjan also gets a tutor who marks to the specification the school actually entered.

dubai/igcse-business-tutor.programmesIntro: Business is usually a new subject at 14, and the stage either side of Year 11 changes what the work should be. These are the four points that shape a Dubai family's plan.

programmes.name: Starting business studies in Year 10
programmes.description: No prior attainment to read, because most students meet the subject for the first time at IGCSE. The first term should establish three habits: reading the command word, applying every point to the named business, and attempting every calculation. Content accumulates easily once those three exist.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ in whether business studies, economics or both sit in the same option block. Where a student takes both, the overlap in market, cost and external-influence content is substantial and worth planning around rather than revising twice.

programmes.name: IGCSE Business, Year 10
programmes.description: Business activity, ownership, objectives, stakeholders, people in business and the start of marketing in most schemes of work. The application habit is the Year 10 priority because it takes months to build and because every later topic is examined the same way.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's long December break is a useful window for a calculation intensive: four consecutive mornings covering break-even, margins, cash flow and ratios produces more security than the same hours spread weekly across a term.

programmes.name: IGCSE Business, Year 11
programmes.description: Operations, finance, external influences and the case-study technique that carries half the Cambridge grade. The Year 11 priorities are the high-tariff evaluation question and the five-minute approach to an unseen case, both of which are technique rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Dubai schools enter overwhelmingly for the summer window, with November kept as the resit route.

programmes.name: A Level business or IB Diploma business management
programmes.description: The application habit is what transfers. Diploma Business Management requires an internal assessment built on a real organisation, and A Level business raises the evaluation demand sharply. A student who has learned to apply at IGCSE arrives with the only skill that scales.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Tutoring is not required for the process.

dubai/igcse-business-tutor.subjectsIntro: Business is taught by content area and examined by skill, and a plan needs both views. These are the units a Dubai plan is built from, with what the record usually shows about each.

subjects.name: Understanding business activity
subjects.description: Business objectives, classification, ownership types, size measurement and growth. Heavy on terminology, which makes it a bank-and-test topic, and the one where generic answers are most tempting because the theory is tidy.

subjects.name: People in business
subjects.description: Motivation, organisational structure, recruitment, training and communication. Motivation questions are where application collapses most visibly: students name a theory and never connect it to the workers described in the case.

subjects.name: Marketing
subjects.description: Market research, segmentation, the marketing mix and competitiveness. Market share calculations live here and are routinely skipped. Promotion answers lose marks for listing methods rather than choosing one and justifying it for this business.

subjects.name: Operations management
subjects.description: Production methods, productivity, quality, location and scale. Location questions are the clearest application test in the specification: the answer has to be about where this business actually is and what the case said about it.

subjects.name: Financial information and decisions
subjects.description: Sources of finance, cash flow, break-even, income statements and balance sheets, and ratio interpretation. The quantitative heart of the subject and the richest source of determinate marks that students leave on the table.

subjects.name: External influences on business activity
subjects.description: Government policy, international trade, exchange rates, technology, ethics and the environment. A topic where Dubai students have unusually good real material available and almost never use it.

subjects.name: The case-study paper
subjects.description: An unseen case with questions requiring theory used on the business described. The highest-value technique in the subject is the first five minutes: reading the case with a pen and annotating the facts that the questions will need.

subjects.name: Calculations
subjects.levels: Across both papers on both specifications
subjects.description: Break-even, contribution, margins, cash-flow forecasting, market share and ratios. Fully determinate marks with a right answer, and the most avoidable loss in the subject because students skip them under time.

subjects.name: The terminology bank
subjects.levels: Not a content area, and worth banking
subjects.description: Short-answer definitions and two-mark openers accepted in a precise form. Needs testing rather than teaching, which means a student can run it alone and should not be charged a qualified hourly rate to be read a list.

subjects.name: Evaluation and recommendation questions
subjects.levels: The highest-tariff question type on both specifications
subjects.description: A recommendation supported by reasoning and conditioned on something specific to the business. Students answer with balanced lists ending in 'it depends', which is the shape of a judgement without the substance of one.

sections.heading: The application tally, and why it predicts the grade
paragraphs: Business mark schemes separate what a student knows from what they do with it, and the separation is sharp. Knowledge of a concept earns a small amount. The same concept used on the business in the question earns more, and analysis of a consequence for that business earns more again. A student whose answers are accurate and generic has produced the lowest-earning version of a correct answer, repeatedly, across an entire paper.

The tally makes that visible in a way a mark cannot. Read the student's own answer with a highlighter and mark every sentence containing something specific to the case: the business name, its market, its size, the problem described, a figure from the table, a detail about its customers or location. Count the highlighted sentences against the total. A mid-range Dubai script frequently returns a tally of one or two out of twelve, which means the student wrote eleven sentences a textbook could have written.

What changes behaviour is doing the highlighting with the student rather than for them. The first session is usually spent in mild disbelief, because the student recognises the content as correct and cannot initially see what is missing. The second session is spent rewriting three sentences to apply, which is mechanical: name the business, use its actual circumstances, attach the consequence to it. By the fourth week the tally is rising and the student is doing the highlighting themselves.

The tally also fixes a motivational problem specific to this subject. Business feels like a subject of opinions, so a mid-range mark reads as unfair. A tally of two out of twelve reads as a fact, and facts are actionable in a way that a sense of injustice is not. That shift is, in practice, the largest single thing a business tutor does for a Dubai student.
bullets: Mark schemes pay more for theory used on the case than for theory recalled
Highlight sentences containing a case-specific detail and count them

sections.heading: The paper map, and where half the grade sits
paragraphs: On Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 the case-study paper carries fifty per cent of the grade and the short-answer and data-response paper carries the other fifty. Both are an hour and a half. That equal split means neither can be sacrificed, and in practice the case-study paper is the one students prepare least for, because preparing for it requires practising a reading routine rather than revising content.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business 4BS1 also splits across two written papers of ninety minutes at equal weight, with its own distribution of content across them. The practical point for a Dubai family is the same in either case: confirm the specification code with the school's exams officer, then pull the component structure for that code rather than working from a general impression of what business papers look like.

Within each paper there is a question-type ladder, and a student's marked script should be broken down along it rather than by topic. Short definition and identification questions. Explanation questions wanting a developed point. Analysis questions wanting a consequence traced for the business. High-tariff evaluation or recommendation questions wanting a conditional judgement. Calculations with determinate answers. Five different demands, and a middling total can conceal two secure types and three failing ones.

The topic view and the question-type view give different instructions, which is why the distinction matters. A topic breakdown says the student is weak on finance. A question-type breakdown says the student loses every analysis mark on every topic, including finance, and attempts no calculations. Those are different plans with different costs, and only one of them is derived from how the paper is actually marked.

sections.heading: The calculations nobody attempts
paragraphs: Business carries a set of quantitative marks that behave unlike the rest of the subject: they have right answers. Break-even output and contribution per unit. Gross and net profit margins. A completed cash-flow forecast with closing balances. Market share. Return on capital employed. Current ratio. Each is a short determinate calculation, each is worth marks, and a meaningful share of Dubai students leave them blank under time on the assumption that the written answers matter more.

They do not. A skipped calculation is a certain zero on a question where the student could have earned full marks with a formula and thirty seconds of arithmetic. In a paper where every written answer is a judgement against a mark scheme, the determinate marks are the most reliable ones available, and abandoning them is the clearest example in the subject of effort being spent in the wrong place.

The fix is a count rather than a lecture. Each week the marked script records the number of calculations available and the number attempted. A student who sees four available and one attempted three weeks running usually changes behaviour by week four, because the number is embarrassing in a way that advice is not. Four to six sessions of timed calculation practice makes the arithmetic automatic so there is no reason left to skip.

Interpretation is the second half and is frequently missing even when the calculation is done. A margin computed and left as a number earns the calculation mark and not the analysis mark; a margin computed and then compared with last year's or with a competitor's, with a consequence for the business stated, earns both. That is a one-sentence habit and it belongs on the same record as the attempted-against-available count.

sections.heading: Evaluation: a recommendation has to be conditional
paragraphs: The highest-tariff business question asks for a decision: should this business do the thing, and why. Students answer in one of two unsuccessful ways. Either they list advantages and disadvantages and finish with 'it depends on the situation', which is the shape of a judgement with none of its substance. Or they state a recommendation with no counter-consideration at all, which reads as assertion.

The successful shape is explicit. State the case for, applied to this business. State the case against, applied to this business. Make the recommendation. Then state what it depends on, specifically: the firm's current cash position as given in the case, the size of the market it operates in, whether it competes on price or on quality, how long it can wait for a return. The condition has to come from the case rather than from general business theory, which is where the application habit and the evaluation habit meet.

Drilling it means one written evaluation paragraph per session, marked for four things: case applied, counter applied, recommendation made, condition drawn from the case. Six sessions is usually enough. Explained rather than drilled, evaluation stays an instruction to 'develop judgement', which no fifteen-year-old can convert into a sentence.

There is a second-order benefit for Dubai students. A recommendation conditioned on something real is easier to write when a student has seen businesses operate, and this emirate supplies examples a textbook does not: retailers whose trade is seasonal around the summer exodus, businesses whose costs move with rent cycles, firms serving a transient population with high customer turnover, importers exposed to currency and shipping. Those are legitimate anchors for recommendation questions, used to support an argument rather than to replace it.
