sections.heading: The five minutes that decide the case-study paper
paragraphs: The case-study paper is the component students prepare least for and it carries half the Cambridge grade. Preparation is not content revision; it is a reading routine. The highest-value five minutes in the examination are the ones spent before writing anything: reading the case with a pen, annotating the facts, and marking the figures that the questions will almost certainly need.

The routine is specific enough to drill. On the first read, underline what the business does, its ownership type, its size and its market. Circle every number. Mark the problem the case is built around, because the high-tariff question is usually about it. Note anything that looks like a constraint — a cash position, a competitor, a location, a staffing issue — because constraints are what evaluation conditions are made from. Then read the questions and go back.

Students who do not have a routine read the case once, start answering, and return to the text repeatedly under time pressure, which costs minutes and produces answers that cite the case less because the detail was never captured. The annotation is what makes the application tally rise in the examination rather than only in practice, which is the whole point of building the habit.

Timed full papers come after the routine is automatic, not before. A timed paper sat without the routine measures the absence of a routine, which is information the student already had. Six sessions on the routine followed by timed practice produces a different result from six timed papers, and it is a cheaper sequence because the technique sessions do not need to be long.

sections.heading: The terminology bank, handed back to the student
paragraphs: Business carries a large set of short definitions and identifications that mark schemes accept in a precise form: added value, a public limited company, economies of scale, a cash-flow forecast, delayering, a secondary-sector business, a profit margin, market segmentation. Each is worth marks on a short-answer question, and each requires the right words rather than any reasoning.

That makes the terminology bank a discipline task rather than a teaching one. Around fifty terms, written in the form the specification uses, tested in five-minute written sets two or three times a week, scored, with the gap list shortening visibly. A student can run it alone or with a parent, and a family should not be paying a qualified hourly rate for someone to read a list aloud.

Two details make it work. The testing must be written rather than verbal, because a student who recognises a definition will not reliably produce one under time, and only production is examined. And the terms must be in the specification's own phrasing rather than a textbook's paraphrase, which requires someone who has read the specification to build the list in the first place. Building the list is tutoring work; running the tests is not.

The score belongs on the record alongside the application tally and the calculation count. Three countable numbers, dated, is a more honest picture of a business student than any report-card grade: a tally of nine out of twelve, a calculation count of four out of four and a terminology score of 46 out of 50 describes a student who is going to do well, and it says so before the examination rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: Dubai businesses as examination material
paragraphs: Business Studies rewards application, and a student living in Dubai has unusually good material to apply from. Most never use it, partly because nobody suggests it and partly because the textbook examples are about firms in other countries. Observation is a legitimate source of the real-world detail that makes a recommendation convincing.

The useful examples are structural rather than branded. A retail sector whose trade has a visible seasonal pattern around the summer period. Businesses whose cost base moves with commercial rent cycles. Firms serving a population with high turnover, where customer retention behaves differently from a stable market. Importers and distributors exposed to shipping costs and to currency where a peg removes one source of variation. Service businesses in a market with intense competition for a similar customer.

Those observations attach well to specific question types: external influences, location decisions, market research and segmentation, cash-flow pressure, and almost any recommendation question needing a condition. A student who writes about rent as a fixed cost that genuinely moves, or about seasonality they have watched, is giving an examiner a reason to believe the analysis rather than a recited example.

Two cautions. Do not name a company and attribute figures or strategies to it from memory, because an invented number is worse than a general observation. And do not let the local detail replace the theory: the mark scheme still wants the concept, the application and the consequence, in that order, and an answer that is all anecdote scores below one that is all theory. The local material is there to anchor an argument, not to be the argument.

sections.heading: What business support costs in Dubai, and the rules it works inside
paragraphs: Published rates read in October 2026: EdFlik lists online tuition from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate rate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Business allocates across those bands cleanly. The terminology bank belongs with the student or at the bottom tier, because it needs administration. The calculation block can sit at the lower band once the formulae are taught, since the work is timed repetition with determinate answers. Application-tally marking, case-study technique and the evaluation block need someone who knows what the mark scheme pays for, which is the qualified band at AED 150-300. A sequenced plan is therefore a modest number of qualified-band hours.

The in-home comparison is the same as elsewhere in this market: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. The premium pays for a commute. For business the shared screen also keeps every highlighted script in a file, so a tally of two in week one can be set beside a tally of nine in week six. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

Three rules of record. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own service with a stated two-working-day completion time; tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are referenced and linked rather than reproduced. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch.

It is spent highlighting the student's own answer for application and producing the tally in front of them, because that number is the product and seeing it is usually the moment the subject starts to make sense.

process.description: The application tally from one case-study answer, the attempted-against-available calculation count from the same script, and a written terminology test scored out of around fifty. Three numbers, dated. They decide which blocks get bought and which get handed back to the student.

process.title: Hand back the terminology bank
process.description: Around fifty terms in specification phrasing, tested in written five-minute sets two or three times a week and scored by the student or a parent. Building the list is tutoring work; running the tests is not, and charging a qualified rate for the latter would be charging for the wrong thing.

process.title: Weekly marked script with the tally reported
process.description: A case-study question set sat between sessions and marked beforehand, with every sentence highlighted for application and the tally reported alongside the calculation count. Both go to the parent the same evening, and both are compared with the baseline each week.

process.title: Case-study routine before timed papers
process.description: Six sessions drilling the five-minute reading and annotation routine, with timed full papers starting only once it is automatic. A timed paper sat without the routine measures the absence of a routine, which is information the family already had.

whyPoints.description: Every marked script carries a count of applied sentences against total sentences. A mid-range script often returns one or two in twelve, and that number is something a student can change deliberately in a way a mark and a sense of unfairness are not.

whyPoints.title: Skipped calculations are counted
whyPoints.description: Determinate marks are the most reliable on the paper and the most commonly abandoned under time. Recording attempted against available each week changes behaviour faster than any amount of advice, because the number is uncomfortable.

whyPoints.title: The case-study routine comes before timed papers
whyPoints.description: Half the Cambridge grade sits in a paper whose preparation is a reading habit rather than content revision. Six sessions on the five-minute annotation routine, then timed practice, produces a different result from six timed papers.

Used to support the concept and the consequence rather than to replace them, which is where anecdote-heavy answers go wrong.

faqs.question: Why does my child know business theory and still score in the middle?
faqs.answer: Because business mark schemes pay more for theory used on the business in the question than for theory recalled correctly. An accurate paragraph about the advantages of a private limited company earns a fraction of what the same paragraph earns when it is about the private limited company in the case. The test takes two minutes: read a marked answer with a highlighter and mark every sentence containing a case-specific detail — the name, the market, the problem, a figure from the table. A mid-range script frequently returns one or two applied sentences in twelve.

faqs.question: What is an application tally and how is it used?
faqs.answer: It is a count of sentences in the student's own answer that refer to something specific about the business in the question, set against the total number of sentences. It is produced on every marked script and recorded with a date. It works because it is actionable: a tally of two can be improved deliberately by naming the business, using its stated circumstances and attaching the consequence to it, where a middling mark cannot be improved by any specific act. Students argue with it for about two sessions and then start producing it themselves.

faqs.question: Why do students skip the calculations in IGCSE business papers?
faqs.answer: Because they assume the written answers carry the grade and the arithmetic is incidental. It is the reverse of the truth. Break-even, contribution, profit margins, cash-flow closing balances, market share and ratios have determinate right answers, which makes them the most reliable marks on a paper where everything else is judged against a mark scheme. The fix is a count rather than a lecture: recording calculations available against calculations attempted each week usually changes behaviour by the fourth week, because the number is harder to ignore than advice.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE business evaluation answer need?
faqs.answer: Four elements. The case for, applied to this business. The case against, applied to this business. A recommendation stated plainly. And the condition the recommendation depends on, drawn from the case rather than from general theory — the firm's cash position as given, the size of its market, whether it competes on price or quality, how long it can wait for a return. A balanced list ending in 'it depends on the situation' has the shape of a judgement with none of its substance, and it will not reach the top band however accurate the content.

faqs.question: How should a student approach an unseen business case study?
faqs.answer: With a pen, before writing anything. On the first read, underline what the business does, its ownership type, its size and its market. Circle every number. Mark the problem the case is built around, because the high-tariff question is usually about it. Note anything that looks like a constraint, since constraints are what evaluation conditions are made from. Then read the questions and go back to the annotation. Students without a routine read once, start answering, and return to the text repeatedly under time, which costs minutes and produces answers that cite the case less.

faqs.question: How much of the Cambridge 0450 grade is the case study?
faqs.answer: Fifty per cent, with the short-answer and data-response paper carrying the other fifty, and both papers running an hour and a half. The equal split means neither can be sacrificed, and in practice the case-study paper is the one students prepare least for, because preparing properly means drilling a reading routine rather than revising content. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business 4BS1 also splits across two ninety-minute papers at equal weight with its own content distribution, so the first step either way is confirming the code with the exams officer.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai student use local businesses in IGCSE business answers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful examples are structural rather than branded. A retail sector with a visible seasonal pattern around the summer period. Cost bases that move with commercial rent cycles. Firms serving a population with high turnover, where retention behaves differently from a stable market. Importers exposed to shipping costs. Those attach well to external influences, location decisions, cash-flow pressure and recommendation questions. Two cautions: do not name a company and attribute remembered figures to it, and do not let the observation replace the concept, the application and the consequence.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE business studies a good option in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: It suits students who are prepared to be specific. Much of the grade is mechanical — terminology in the right form, determinate calculations, a reading routine, a four-part evaluation shape — which means a disciplined student can score well without unusual aptitude. It suits less well a student who writes fluently in generalities, because fluency is the exact failure mode the mark scheme penalises. Where a school offers both business studies and economics, the overlap in market, cost and external-influence content is substantial and worth planning around rather than revising twice.

faqs.question: How long does it take for an application tally to rise?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks in most cases, because it is a production habit rather than a knowledge gap. The sequence is predictable: the first session is spent in mild disbelief, because the content was correct and the student cannot initially see what is missing; the second is spent rewriting three sentences to apply; by the fourth week the tally is rising and by the sixth the student is doing their own highlighting. The real test is a case-study answer written after Dubai's long December break, because a habit that survives three weeks off is a habit.

faqs.question: Should Year 10 or Year 11 be the focus for business tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 for the application habit, Year 11 for technique. The habit of applying every point to the named business takes months to build and is examined identically in every later topic, so building it early compounds. Year 11 priorities are narrower and more immediate: the five-minute case-reading routine, the four-part evaluation shape, and the calculation count. A Year 11 start is still worthwhile — both of those are six-session blocks with visible results — but a Year 10 start means the Year 11 work begins from a tally that is already moving.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE business tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online provision at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik, a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, specialist work at AED 270 at TutorChase, and premium named listings at AED 650. Business allocates cleanly: terminology testing belongs with the student, timed calculation repetition can sit at the lower band once the formulae are taught, and application-tally marking, case technique and evaluation need the qualified band. A sequenced plan is a modest number of qualified-band hours.

faqs.question: Does online tuition suit a case-study subject like business?
faqs.answer: It suits it well. The case extract and the student's own answer sit side by side on a shared screen, highlights go on in a second colour while the student watches, and every marked version is saved so a tally of two in week one can be set beside a tally of nine in week six. A script highlighted in pen and carried away cannot be compared in March. The published cost difference also runs one way: AED 180-350 for qualified in-home work against AED 150-300 online. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE business exams sat by candidates in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only, so a March date on a tutoring site belongs to another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. One administrative point matters as much as the dates: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with business coursework or a controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that should be agreed in writing before the first session. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, discuss the student's plan, question their choices and comment on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a draft into its final form, or supply text or data for submission. Where a school operates such a component the consequence of crossing that line falls on the student rather than the provider, which is why the boundary belongs in writing rather than in an understanding.

faqs.question: What if no business specialist is free for our specification in Dubai?
faqs.answer: You should be told, with the options named rather than a general humanities tutor quietly substituted. Business requests in this emirate concentrate in the spring term of Year 11, and a tutor who has not taught the specification will not know what the mark scheme pays for in an application or analysis question, which is the whole basis of the tally. The honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit.

dubai/igcse-business-tutor.closingBody: Before buying anything, take your child's most recent marked business answer and highlight every sentence that refers to something specific about the business in the question. Count the highlights against the total. If the count is one or two in twelve, you have found the grade, and the repair is a production habit rather than a content course. Email the school for the specification code, send the script, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and ask for the application tally and the calculation count in writing after every session.

Matching begins with the syllabus code, the tier and which practical paper the school has entered, since those three facts decide what the revision should contain.

intro.heading: Buying IGCSE chemistry help in the right order in Dubai
paragraphs: Chemistry rewards targeted spending more than any other IGCSE science, because the marks are distributed unevenly and some of them are extremely cheap to collect. A student who learns the qualitative analysis observations properly picks up marks on a predictable question type within two sessions. A student who spends the same two sessions discussing bonding theory may gain nothing measurable. Order matters, and almost nobody sells it that way.

The published Dubai bands give the costings their inputs. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the floor. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quoting AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and market home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above.

Ranked against those bands, the picture is clear. Qualitative analysis is the cheapest mark available, because it is recall of a fixed table and two sessions usually settles it. Mole calculations are the most consequential, because the chain from mass to moles to ratio to answer appears across the whole paper and a break anywhere in it loses everything downstream. Organic chemistry is a memory load with a structure, which makes it quicker than students expect. Bonding theory is the most interesting and the least efficient purchase.

Two administrative facts come first. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 are different specifications, and Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences routes cover a reduced subset of the content. The practical element differs too: Cambridge offers a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper, while Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Confirm all of it with the school in writing before buying anything.

Dubai's examination pattern is straightforward once stated. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A student needing more time than the summer allows therefore has a real second route rather than only a compressed one.

Delivery is stated once. Chemistry support for Dubai families runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Equations, calculation chains and observation tables are written on a shared screen and saved, which turns each session into revision material rather than a conversation that evaporates.

dubai/igcse-chemistry-tutor.programmesIntro: Chemistry sits inside a longer route through a Dubai school, and the efficient purchase differs by stage because the arithmetic underneath the subject is built years earlier.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the course
programmes.description: The years in which proportional reasoning is secured or not. Moles, concentration, percentage yield and empirical formula questions are all ratio problems, and a student who is not fluent with ratio and with converting between grams, kilograms and cubic centimetres will lose chemistry marks for two years without the cause ever being named.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families usually first think about chemistry help in Year 10 or later. The cheapest useful intervention is earlier and does not look like chemistry: a short block on ratio, unit conversion and rearrangement in Year 9. It sits comfortably at the lower published rate bands because the job is explanation and repetition rather than criteria-level marking.

programmes.name: Year 10, the content year
programmes.description: Most Dubai schools cover the bulk of the syllabus in Year 10: states of matter, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, acids and bases, the periodic table and an introduction to organic chemistry. Practical work happens here, which is where the skills tested by both practical routes are built whether or not the student notices at the time.
programmes.countryNote: Keep the returned topic tests. Dubai schools assess as they teach, and a sequence of marked topic tests is a precise and free map of which chemistry topics are weak, available months before any mock. Families who bring that sequence to a first session leave it with a ranked plan instead of a diagnosis still in progress.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: Revision, mocks and the series. The content has been taught once, so the work becomes ranking: which of the remaining weaknesses returns the most marks per hour. Organic chemistry and qualitative analysis both move quickly at this stage; conceptual gaps in bonding and energetics move slowly and should be weighed accordingly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock windows run from roughly late November to February depending on the school. A marked chemistry mock is the most useful planning document of the two years because it separates recall losses from calculation losses, and those need different sessions. Acting in January leaves months; waiting until spring converts ranking into triage.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level and IB Diploma chemistry
programmes.description: The IGCSE chemistry grade and tier decide whether A Level Chemistry or IB Chemistry at Higher Level is realistic, and both courses assume the stoichiometry introduced at IGCSE is fluent rather than familiar. Students who passed IGCSE by memorising sequences rather than understanding the mole concept find the first term of either course unexpectedly hard.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families often have A Levels, the IB Diploma and American pathways available within a few kilometres, with different chemistry entry requirements. Deciding the likely post-16 route during Year 10, then working backwards to the tier and grade needed, is better planning than choosing after results when the options have narrowed.

dubai/igcse-chemistry-tutor.subjectsIntro: Chemistry requests from Dubai families usually arrive with maths or another science attached, because the weaknesses are shared. These are the subjects most often bundled with an IGCSE chemistry enquiry.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Multiple choice and theory papers plus a practical route, covering particles, bonding, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, acids and bases, the periodic table, metals and organic chemistry. Marks are lost on the mole chain, on unbalanced equations and on observation recall.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than through a separate practical examination. Content overlaps heavily with Cambridge, but question style and mark allocation differ enough that past papers must match the specification.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The arithmetic underneath chemistry. Ratio, proportion, unit conversion and rearrangement are maths skills assessed in a chemistry paper, and a student losing marks in both subjects usually has one weakness rather than two.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares the calculation discipline and the practical skills. Students who carry units through working in physics tend to do the same in chemistry, and students who do not lose the same marks in both papers for the same reason.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science on a triple-award timetable. Enzyme and respiration content leans on chemistry concepts, and students taking all three sciences need their practical and revision load coordinated rather than left to collide.

subjects.name: Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: The route many Dubai students take instead of three separate sciences, with a reduced chemistry subset. Past-paper practice must come from the combined syllabus, because questions on excluded content waste revision time.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger candidates and genuinely helpful for chemistry, since the algebraic fluency it builds removes most of the difficulty in stoichiometric rearrangement. It is also a real extra load in an examination year.

subjects.name: Environmental Management
subjects.description: Overlaps with the chemistry of the atmosphere, water treatment and resource use. Students taking both can anchor abstract chemistry in applications, which helps with the extended-answer questions that ask for explanation in context.

subjects.name: Food and Nutrition
subjects.description: An unexpected but real overlap in organic chemistry, nutrients and reaction conditions. The habit of recording a method precisely transfers directly to both practical routes in chemistry.

subjects.name: Design and Technology
subjects.description: Shares materials content and the discipline of specifying a process step by step. That discipline is exactly what the alternative-to-practical paper rewards when it asks a candidate to criticise somebody else's method.

modes.description: Two or three sessions on the material that is pure recall and appears predictably: cation and anion tests with their observations, gas tests, flame colours, solubility rules and the reactivity series. modes.description: The mole concept and everything downstream of it: mass to moles, mole ratio from a balanced equation, limiting reagent, concentration, percentage yield, empirical formula. sections.heading: Chemistry interventions ranked by marks per dirham
paragraphs: A family with a limited budget needs a ranking, not a menu. The table below lists the interventions available in IGCSE chemistry, the number of sessions each usually takes, the cost at a mid-market published rate, and an honest note on what it returns. The ranking reflects what we see on marked papers from Dubai schools rather than what is pleasant to teach.

Recall of the qualitative analysis tables comes first because the cost is tiny and the questions are predictable. Tests for cations and anions, gas tests and flame colours appear reliably, the answers are fixed, and the only reason students lose these marks is that nobody made them learn the table properly. Two sessions and a cold test at the start of each session afterwards.

The mole chain comes second, and it is second rather than first only because it takes longer. Its value is that it runs through the entire paper: stoichiometry, concentration, yield, empirical formula and electrolysis calculations all depend on the same links. A student with a broken link loses marks in five separate question types and experiences it as five separate weaknesses.

Bonding and structure comes near the bottom, which surprises people. It is the most interesting part of the subject and the most frequently requested, and improvement in it is slow because it is genuinely conceptual. A family with eight sessions to spend should not spend them here. A family with thirty can afford to, and will enjoy it more.

sections.heading: The mole chain, and why students experience one break as five problems
paragraphs: Stoichiometry is taught as a series of topics and examined as a single chain. A candidate reads a mass, converts it to moles, uses the balanced equation to find a mole ratio, converts back to a mass or a volume or a concentration, and answers. Every quantitative question in the subject is some version of that path, and a weakness at any point produces failure at the end.

What makes this diagnostically awkward is that the student cannot see where the break is. They know they got the answer wrong. They do not know whether the error was the conversion, the balancing, the ratio or the final step, so the experience is of chemistry calculations being generally impossible. A tutor reading a worked attempt can locate the break in thirty seconds, which is why a marked script with working shown is worth more than any amount of discussion.

The commonest break is the balanced equation. If the equation is wrong the ratio is wrong and everything downstream is wrong, however competent the arithmetic. Balancing is cheap to fix and should always be checked first. The second commonest is unit conversion: grams and kilograms, cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, concentration expressed per cubic decimetre while the volume is given in cubic centimetres. Carrying units through every line catches it automatically.

The third is the limiting reagent, where students calculate moles of both reactants and then use the wrong one. That is a reasoning step rather than an arithmetic one and it needs explicit practice rather than more worked examples. Four or five sessions covering the whole chain, with every step written out and units carried, usually converts five apparent problems back into one solved one.
bullets: Check the balanced equation first; a wrong ratio ruins correct arithmetic
Convert units before starting, and carry them through every line
Write every step, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip
Limiting reagent is a reasoning step, not a calculation step
Concentration questions mix cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres constantly
One broken link presents to the student as five separate weaknesses

sections.heading: Qualitative analysis: the fixed tables that pay immediately
paragraphs: Qualitative analysis is the most reliably winnable part of IGCSE chemistry and the part most often left half-learned. The questions ask what is observed when a named reagent is added to a solution containing a particular ion, and the answers are fixed. There is nothing to work out. A student who knows the table scores and a student who half-knows it writes white precipitate and hopes.

The detail is where the marks sit. Adding sodium hydroxide solution to a copper salt gives a light blue precipitate that is insoluble in excess; to iron two it gives a green precipitate; to iron three a red-brown one; to zinc or aluminium a white precipitate that dissolves in excess to give a colourless solution; to calcium a white precipitate that does not dissolve in excess. The distinction between insoluble in excess and soluble in excess is the entire point of several questions, and students who learned only the first colour lose half the available marks.

Anion tests are equally fixed. A carbonate effervesces with dilute acid and the gas turns limewater milky. Acidified silver nitrate gives a white precipitate with chloride, cream with bromide, yellow with iodide. Acidified barium chloride gives a white precipitate with sulfate. Nitrate gives ammonia on warming with sodium hydroxide and aluminium. Gas tests and flame colours are shorter lists still.

The way to learn them is to write them. A student who constructs their own table, in their own layout, and is tested cold at the start of the next three sessions, will hold it. A student handed a printed table files it and never reads it again. This is also why no tutoring service should be distributing awarding-body material: the student building their own reference from the specification learns more than the student given a shortcut, and the material belongs to the awarding body in any case.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: a memory load with a shape
paragraphs: Students describe organic chemistry as the part they cannot remember, which is accurate and fixable. It is a memory load, but it is a structured one, and once the structure is visible the volume shrinks dramatically. Three sessions is the usual cost, and the return is a section of the paper that was previously left blank.

The structure is the homologous series. Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters each have a general formula, a characteristic functional group, a naming pattern and a small set of reactions. Students who learn them as five separate lists of facts have five times the work of students who learn the pattern and then the differences. The naming system in particular is algorithmic rather than arbitrary, and once a student can name a branched chain confidently, half the difficulty disappears.

The reaction set is also short. Combustion, cracking, addition of bromine across a double bond and the test it provides, hydration to an alcohol, fermentation, oxidation of an alcohol to a carboxylic acid, esterification. Each one has conditions that are examinable and routinely forgotten: catalyst, temperature, whether the reaction needs acid. Learning the conditions alongside the reaction, rather than afterwards, is the difference between a mark and most of the marks.

Polymerisation finishes the section and carries predictable questions about repeat units and about the drawing conventions for addition and condensation polymers. The drawing is where marks go missing, usually through bonds left dangling incorrectly or brackets omitted. That is mechanical and worth ten minutes of explicit practice rather than being left to chance on the day.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1 and the practical routes
paragraphs: Two specifications dominate IGCSE chemistry entries in Dubai and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 is widely used across the emirate's Cambridge schools. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 is the main alternative. Content overlap is substantial, which is exactly why families assume the past papers are interchangeable, and the question style and practical treatment differ enough that they are not.

The practical element is the sharpest difference. Cambridge separates it into its own paper: either a practical test in a laboratory or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. A Cambridge student entered for the alternative paper needs to read other people's experiments, identify variables, criticise methods and interpret data on paper, which is a written skill and highly tutorable. A student entered for the practical test needs laboratory technique, which is built at school.

Tiering is the second difference that affects revision directly. Cambridge divides into Core and Extended with supplement content examined only at Extended, and the grade range differs. A Core candidate revising Extended material is spending time on content they will not meet; an Extended candidate revising only Core material is leaving examinable topics untouched. Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences routes reduce the content again.

So the screening questions are specific: which syllabus code, which tier, which practical paper. A tutor who talks about chemistry generally rather than asking those three is working from assumptions, and assumptions are what produce a term of revision aimed at the wrong examination. Confirm with the school and check the awarding body's own syllabus page rather than relying on summaries, which are abundant and frequently out of date.

sections.heading: The UAE exam series, and what a late start can still achieve
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, which means a UAE candidate sits June or November, and any guidance quoting a February entry deadline is written for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

The November series changes what a late diagnosis can achieve. A Dubai student whose January mock is well below target can compress work into the months before the summer, or plan properly for November with several additional months. For chemistry specifically the second option is often materially better, because the mole chain takes time to rebuild and compressing it tends to produce memorised procedures rather than understanding.

Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and that is the administrative fact that catches families. For a sense of the cycle, Pearson's November International GCSE timetable in the current series runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026.

One warning that matters for UAE candidates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Revise from the timetable the school issued and check the awarding body's live timetable page rather than a restated version found elsewhere.

sections.heading: Online chemistry tuition against the in-home market in Dubai
paragraphs: Chemistry involves writing equations and working through calculation chains, which is work that suits a shared screen. Both parties write, the working is saved, and a calculation attempted in October can be reopened in April. The same work in an exercise book is somewhere in the house by revision season, which is a small thing that compounds across two years.

The in-home premium in Dubai is quantifiable. Bestimate puts home visits at AED 180 to 350 and market home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Advertised monthly packages run AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For a ranked plan, eight shorter contacts a month fit better than four long ones, because each ranked item should finish with a timed question and a cold re-test later.

There is a specification argument as well. Two awarding bodies, two tiers and two practical routes produce several combinations, and the right tutor knows your child's. The set of chemistry tutors within a twenty-minute drive of a particular Dubai community who match that exact combination may be small, especially for the alternative-to-practical paper where specific past-paper familiarity does most of the work.

The honest limit should be stated. Laboratory technique is built at school in the laboratory, and no remote session replaces handling apparatus. A tutor in your kitchen does not replace it either. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; that service is part of our India offering only, and chemistry support here runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family should establish before paying
paragraphs: The screening questions are short. Which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for. Which practical paper. What does the marked script show as the top three losses, ranked. What would the first four sessions cover, in order. A tutor who answers all four without hedging is working from evidence; one who discusses chemistry in general is guessing, and guessing at AED 250 an hour is expensive.

The fifth question concerns the permit. Any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and warns that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Be sceptical of outcome claims in this segment particularly, because chemistry is often sold to families planning medical applications and the pressure makes exaggeration profitable. No provider can guarantee a grade. Percentages about how many students improved are meaningless without the number of students, the date and the method, and several ranking pages in this market publish exactly such figures alongside self-asserted star ratings.

Finally, a note on materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies. The correct behaviour from any tutoring service is to reference them and link to the official source, not to distribute copies. A provider handing over material they do not own is telling you something about the rest of their practice.

process.title: Get three facts from the school
process.description: Syllabus code, tier, and which practical paper your child is entered for, all in writing. Revision shape depends on all three, and a tutor who does not ask for them is building a plan on assumptions.

process.title: Send marked work with the working visible
process.description: A mock or a sequence of Year 10 topic tests. For chemistry the working matters more than the mark, because a wrong answer in a calculation only tells you which link in the mole chain broke if the steps are on the page.

process.title: Agree a ranked list, not a syllabus sweep
process.description: Qualitative analysis tables first because they are cheapest, then equation balancing, then the mole chain, then organic chemistry. Bonding theory last. A ranked list spends a limited budget in the right order.

process.title: Run short sessions over live video
process.description: Two shorter slots a week beat one long block, because each ranked item should end with a timed question and be re-tested cold later. Sessions sit around the Dubai school day, mandatory subject lessons, sport and prayer times.

process.title: Re-test cold, then cross items off
process.description: Observation tables tested cold at the start of each session; calculation chains re-tested from the correct past papers every few weeks. Items leave the list or the plan changes. Nothing stays on the list indefinitely by default.

whyPoints.title: Ranked by value, not by interest
whyPoints.description: Qualitative analysis first because two sessions buys predictable marks; bonding theory last because it is slow to move. Most providers sell the opposite order, because conceptual chemistry is more enjoyable to teach and discuss.

whyPoints.title: The observation tables are on the page
whyPoints.description: Precipitate colours, solubility in excess, halide tests, carbonate tests. Published rather than summarised away, because the distinction between insoluble and soluble in excess is the whole point of several questions.

whyPoints.title: The mole chain treated as one thing
whyPoints.description: Students experience one broken link as five separate weaknesses, which is why they buy five topics of tutoring. Teaching the chain as a chain, with working written and units carried, converts five problems back into one.

whyPoints.title: Specification and practical route named
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 differ, Core and Extended differ, and the practical test and alternative paper need different preparation entirely. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole researched competitor cluster.

whyPoints.title: The laboratory limit stated honestly
whyPoints.description: Practical technique is built at school with real apparatus, and no remote session replaces it. A tutor in your kitchen does not replace it either. What is tutorable is everything around it: tables, plotting, gradients, method criticism.

whyPoints.title: No grade guarantees
whyPoints.description: Chemistry is often bought under pressure by families planning medical applications, which makes exaggeration profitable here. No outcome is guaranteed and no percentage about other students appears on this page without a method behind it.

faqs.question: If we can only afford a few chemistry sessions, what should they cover?
faqs.answer: The qualitative analysis tables first. Cation and anion tests, gas tests and flame colours are pure recall with fixed answers, they appear predictably in the papers, and two sessions plus cold re-testing usually settles them. Next, equation balancing, because a wrong equation ruins every calculation downstream. Then the mole chain. Bonding and structure should come last: it is the most interesting part of the subject, the most frequently requested, and the slowest to improve, which makes it a poor use of a small budget.

faqs.question: Why does my child get every mole calculation wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually one broken link in a chain rather than a general inability. Every quantitative chemistry question follows the same path: mass to moles, mole ratio from the balanced equation, back to mass or volume or concentration. The student knows the answer was wrong and cannot see which step failed, so it feels like five separate weaknesses. A tutor reading working that shows each step locates the break in seconds. The commonest break is the balanced equation; the second is unit conversion between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres.

faqs.question: What do the sodium hydroxide precipitate colours actually test?
faqs.answer: The colour identifies the cation and the behaviour in excess discriminates between groups. Copper two gives a light blue precipitate insoluble in excess; iron two green and iron three red-brown, both insoluble in excess; zinc and aluminium give a white precipitate that dissolves in excess to a colourless solution; calcium gives a white precipitate that does not dissolve. Students who memorised only the first colour lose the marks attached to the second half of the observation, which is frequently where the discriminating mark sits.

faqs.question: Which chemistry syllabus does my child's Dubai school use?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because it decides which past papers are useful. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 are both widely used in the emirate, and Co-ordinated or Combined Sciences routes cover a reduced chemistry subset. The content overlap is large enough to make families assume the papers are interchangeable, and the question style, mark allocation and practical treatment differ enough that they are not. Get the code and the tier in writing.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our home in Dubai for chemistry lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Chemistry support for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with equations, calculation chains and observation tables written on a shared screen and saved, so work done in October is still available during revision. The in-home market here is real and quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with the tutor's travel inside the rate.

faqs.question: How long does organic chemistry take to learn properly?
faqs.answer: About three sessions, which is less than students expect, because the volume shrinks once the structure is visible. Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters each have a general formula, a functional group, a naming pattern and a short reaction set. Learned as five separate fact lists it is five times the work. The reaction conditions are the part most often dropped: cracking needs heat and a catalyst, fermentation needs yeast and warmth without air, esterification needs an acid catalyst.

faqs.question: Is there a practical exam for IGCSE chemistry in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the entry. Cambridge offers a practical test sat in a laboratory and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses. Pearson's International GCSE Chemistry assesses practical skills inside the written papers rather than separately. The two Cambridge routes need different preparation: the test needs laboratory technique built at school, while the alternative paper needs the written ability to read someone else's experiment, identify variables and criticise a method. Ask the school which paper appears on the entry.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry practical test?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the limit should be stated plainly. Handling apparatus, measuring carefully and working safely are built at school in the laboratory, and no remote session replaces that. What a tutor can do is drill everything that surrounds it and carries a real share of the marks: designing a results table, significant figures, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient with units, identifying an anomalous result and explaining what to do about it.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended mean for chemistry revision?
faqs.answer: Extended covers the full Cambridge syllabus including supplement content and carries the upper grade range; Core covers reduced content and is capped below the top grades. For revision the consequence is immediate: a Core candidate working through supplement material is spending time on content that will not appear, and an Extended candidate revising only Core material is leaving examinable topics untouched. The tier is set by the school from two years of assessment evidence, and any conversation about it belongs in Year 10.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE chemistry exams held for UAE students?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so advice quoting a February entry deadline is written for another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that candidates must use the correct zone timetable, so always revise from the version the school issued.

faqs.question: Should a weak chemistry mock mean switching to the November series?
faqs.answer: It is worth asking the school rather than assuming. Chemistry is a subject where compressing the mole chain into a few weeks tends to produce memorised procedures rather than understanding, and procedures fail when a question is phrased unfamiliarly. Several extra months before a November sitting often produces a materially better grade. The decision affects entries and post-16 applications so it belongs with the school, but it exists, and a compressed revision programme sold without mentioning it is incomplete advice.

faqs.question: Is my child's chemistry problem really a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth checking before buying chemistry sessions. Moles, concentration, percentage yield and empirical formula questions are proportional reasoning with chemical labels, and unit conversion causes more failures than chemical understanding does. The tell is a marked script where the chemistry reasoning is sound and the arithmetic or the rearrangement breaks down. A short block on ratio, conversion and rearrangement is cheaper than separate tutors for chemistry, physics and maths working around the same gap.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE chemistry tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above on Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quotes AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. At the floor, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Those are the providers' own figures, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Should a tutor give us past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who does is worth questioning. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies, and the correct behaviour from a tutoring service is to reference them and point at the official source rather than distribute copies. There is also a learning argument: a student who builds their own observation tables and reference sheets from the specification retains far more than one handed a finished set, which is why we ask students to write them.

faqs.question: What if no chemistry tutor matches our specification and route?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting quietly. Two awarding bodies, two tiers and two practical routes produce several combinations, and a specific match on the alternative-to-practical paper in the weeks after mock results can be narrower than families expect. The options are a start date in the future, a tutor who covers the content but not that exact route for interim recall and calculation work, or a recommendation to wait until demand eases. Families should be told which applies.

dubai/igcse-chemistry-tutor.closingHeading: Spend the first four sessions in the right order
dubai/igcse-chemistry-tutor.closingBody: Get the syllabus code, the tier and the practical paper from the school, then send marked work with the working visible. The free trial session turns that into a ranked list: the observation tables first because they are the cheapest marks available, equation balancing next, then the mole chain, with bonding theory last. A ranked list spends a limited budget where it returns most, and it can be crossed off as it goes. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are not part of our UAE service.

intro.heading: The price question, answered rather than deflected
paragraphs: A Dubai parent researching IGCSE support meets a strange wall. The pages ranking for this search are detailed about pedagogy and silent about money. One of the best-written competitor pages in the set has a frequently-asked-questions block that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. Another quotes a price in its structured data that contradicts the price in its own body copy. A third prices in US dollars for a market that transacts in dirhams. The effect is that parents end up phoning five providers to assemble a range that could have been published on a page.

So here is the range. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors are advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit broadly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, with travel built in, run from about AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting them at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200-500. Dedicated IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. Premium named tutors go higher again, with BartyED advertising AED 650.

Those are other organisations' published figures, with the source named, and they are the market rather than our price list. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Knowing the range is only half of a buying decision. The other half is knowing what moves a number inside it, because the same subject at the same level can be quoted at AED 150 and AED 450 by two people who both believe they are being reasonable. Tier, specification familiarity, examiner experience, session length, commitment length, travel, format and timing all move it. So does urgency: a family calling six weeks before a June series is negotiating from a weak position and should know that before they call.

IB Gram delivers UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not run group classes at a venue in Dubai and we do not send tutors to UAE addresses - in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. That matters to the cost conversation in a specific way: the travel component that pushes in-home rates to the AED 180-500 band is not in the price, and the tutor is matched to the specification rather than to the half-hour radius around your community.

dubai/igcse-classes.programmesIntro: Cost varies by stage more than parents expect, because the scarcity of tutors who have taught a specific paper changes with the level. These are the four stages Dubai families buy.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before IGCSE begins
programmes.description: The cheapest stage to buy and the one most often skipped. Rates sit at the lower end of every published band because the content is widely taught and the tutor pool is deep. The work here is algebraic fluency, scientific writing and reading stamina, assessed through Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests offered in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is where a relocating student's gap first becomes visible, and where fixing it is least expensive. A Year 9 arriving from another system who is drilled on written-examination convention for one term rarely needs the intensive Year 11 package that the same student would otherwise buy two years later at three times the hourly rate.

programmes.name: Year 10 IGCSE, Core and Extended
programmes.description: Mid-band pricing, and the stage with the best return per dirham because there is time for the work to compound. Buying one session a week through Year 10 generally costs less in total than buying three a week through the spring of Year 11, and it produces the tier evidence that protects sixth-form options.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically fix tier entries during or at the end of Year 10. Families who spend here are buying a decision as much as a grade, since Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available and that ceiling is read by A Level and IB Diploma admissions two years later.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the exam-term intensive
programmes.description: The most expensive stage, for two reasons that have nothing to do with teaching quality. Demand concentrates into January through April, and specialists with a free evening slot in February are scarce. Specialist IGCSE rates in the AED 200-450 band are quoted most often for exactly this window.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock seasons in November and late February drive two demand spikes. Booking a regular slot in September costs less than buying the same slot in February, and any provider telling you otherwise has not looked at their own diary. Rates do tighten closer to exams, which is a supply fact rather than a sales tactic.

programmes.name: Retake and grade-lift blocks
programmes.description: Short, narrow and usually the best-value purchase available, because the problem is normally technique on one paper rather than a missing syllabus. A six-week block on specific question types costs a fraction of a two-year engagement and often does the required job.
programmes.countryNote: The deadlines sit before the information. Pearson's International GCSE November series ran its final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge's own entries for a June series close in the spring, months ahead of the papers, with the exact date set per series and per timetable zone and issued by the school as the centre. Budget for the entry fee at the chosen centre as well as the tuition.

dubai/igcse-classes.subjectsIntro: Subjects do not cost the same, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. Each note says roughly where a subject sits in the market band and how many hours families typically end up buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The deepest tutor pool in Dubai and therefore the most competitive pricing, generally available across the full published range. Families typically buy one weekly hour through Year 10 and two through Year 11. The large recoverable loss is unwritten method, which is cheap to fix and does not need a premium tutor.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mid to upper band. Fewer tutors are genuinely comfortable with the Alternative to Practical paper than claim to be, and that paper is where a meaningful share of marks sits. Ask about it explicitly before agreeing a rate; it is the fastest way to tell a specialist from a generalist.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, with demand concentrated in the spring of Year 11 around moles, electrolysis and organic pathways. Students usually need fewer hours than they fear, because the losses cascade from one or two specific skills rather than spreading across the syllabus.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mid band with good availability. The hours go on command-term discipline rather than content, which means a shorter engagement than parents budget for. A student losing marks by describing where the paper asked them to explain does not need a term of re-teaching.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: The clearest scarcity premium in the IGCSE market. Few tutors in any one part of Dubai have taught these specifications, so rates sit at the specialist end and availability is the binding constraint rather than price. This is also where online matching changes the answer completely.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Wide pool, wide price range, and the greatest variation in actual usefulness. A tutor who teaches writing well is not the same as one who teaches the mark tariffs on the summary and directed-writing tasks, and only the second moves an IGCSE grade. Ask which they do.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Lower to mid band with strong availability in Dubai. The efficient purchase is short and structural: recognising each reading task's fixed shape within the first ten seconds. Students transferred between 0510 and 0500 mid-course need more hours, and should be priced accordingly.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Mid band, and unusually efficient to buy. Application and evaluation habits are teachable in a handful of sessions, and diagram conventions in Economics can be drilled out in two. Families frequently over-buy here because the subjects feel content-heavy.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Upper band because of a supply quirk: tutors who can program are plentiful, tutors who can teach the board's pseudocode convention and trace-table method are not. Verify the second rather than the first before agreeing a rate.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Mid band, with hours concentrated on source interrogation and the extended response rather than case-study recall. A short engagement that installs a fixed reading order for resource questions generally outperforms a long one spent revising content.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Mid to upper band and tight on availability in the evening slots Dubai families want. KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so demand is structural rather than seasonal.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Lower to mid band. The cheapest useful hour in the whole set is often the one spent marking the specification against the student's revision list, because scope confusion here wastes more time than any content gap does.

dubai/igcse-classes.regionsTitle: What families in different parts of Dubai actually ask about price
dubai/igcse-classes.regionsIntro: Price sensitivity and the questions that come with it vary across the city. These notes describe what families ask, not where a tutor sits - delivery is over video throughout.

regions.name: Bur Dubai and Al Mankhool
regions.note: Long-settled districts where households compare hourly rates carefully and ask about session length before credentials. Shorter, more frequent sessions are the usual preference, and they are often the better buy.

regions.name: Karama and Oud Metha
regions.note: Price-led conversations and a strong preference for monthly rather than per-session billing. Families here are most likely to ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT, which is the right question to ask anyone.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: Households frequently supporting two or three children at once, so sibling scheduling and total monthly outlay matter more than the headline hourly rate. The arithmetic that counts is cost per child per month.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Mixed apartment and villa stock with a wide income spread, and the widest range of accepted price points we see in one district. The useful conversation here is about hours needed rather than rate.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Dubai South
regions.note: Outlying communities where an in-home tutor's travel time was historically priced into every quote. Removing the journey takes a real cost out of the number rather than simply relocating it.

regions.name: Jumeirah Golf Estates and Emirates Hills
regions.note: Specialist and examiner-experienced tutors are requested most often from these catchments, which sits at the upper end of every published band. The question worth asking is whether that premium buys something your child's specific losses need.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Heavy co-curricular timetables and late sessions, which pushes families towards shorter blocks. Two 45-minute sessions a week frequently cost the same as one long one and work better.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer communities with young cohorts, so spending starts in Years 8 and 9. That is the cheapest end of the market and the stage with the longest time for the work to compound.

schoolClusters.city: Bur Dubai, Oud Metha and Al Mankhool
schoolClusters.note: An established schooling belt with a broad curriculum mix and the most price-aware conversations in the city. Students we support from these catchments commonly take Cambridge entries with a mixed subject set.

schoolClusters.city: Festival City, Al Jaddaf and Nad Al Hamar
schoolClusters.note: A cluster where British, Swiss and American provision sit close together and families often compare across systems before choosing. Questions here tend to be about hours needed per subject rather than hourly rate.

schoolClusters.note: Villa catchments where specialist and examiner-experienced tutors are requested most, at the upper end of the published rate bands. The honest advice here is often to buy fewer hours of the right specialism rather than more of a premium label.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, by provider model
paragraphs: The useful comparison is not between brands but between business models, because the model explains the price. A marketplace that matches you to a university student has a different cost base from an agency that recruits qualified subject teachers, and both differ from a tuition centre carrying premises, a licence and staff in Dubai. A freelance tutor driving to your community is pricing their car and their evening as well as their teaching.

The table sets these out with the AED bands each model advertises and the source of the figure. Everything in it is another organisation's published rate, named and dated to October 2026. None of it is IB Gram's price list, and a provider that quotes you a number should be able to tell you what it includes, how long the session is, and whether the figure is per hour or per lesson - those are three different questions and they are frequently conflated.

Two patterns are worth noticing. The first is that the in-home band carries a visible travel premium: Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online. The second is that the top of the market is defined by scarcity rather than by format - a specialist in a thinly taught specification commands AED 200-450 or more whether they are on a screen or in a room.

What this means practically is that comparing two quotes requires normalising them first. Per hour or per lesson. Sixty minutes or fifty. Travel included or added. Materials included or billed. One subject or two. Cancellation terms. A quote of AED 200 that is a fifty-minute lesson with a two-session cancellation notice is not cheaper than AED 220 for a full hour with twenty-four hours' notice, and most families never get far enough into the detail to see that.

sections.heading: Group classes against one-to-one: the arithmetic nobody writes down
paragraphs: Group classes look like obvious value and sometimes are. The honest way to compare them is per student per hour of direct attention, not per student per hour of elapsed time, because those two numbers diverge sharply as the group grows. In a class of six, a student receives on average ten minutes of individual attention in an hour. At AED 80 a head that is good value if the content is genuinely new to all six, and poor value if five of them are there for a different reason than your child.

The deciding question is whether the students share the problem. A group works when everyone is meeting a topic for the first time: a new unit, a shared syllabus gap, a timed-paper practice session where the clock does the teaching. A group fails when the members have different error patterns, because the tutor has to choose whose problem to address, and your child's problem may not be chosen.

This is also where diagnosis pays for itself. A parent who knows their child is losing marks to unwritten method and timing does not need a group class on electrolysis, however cheap it is. A parent with no diagnosis buys whatever is on offer and hopes some of it lands. The hour spent getting a marked script read properly changes which product you should buy, and often saves more than it costs.

IB Gram's own arrangement is one-to-one or paired over live video - we do not run group classes at a Dubai venue - so the group rows are included as market context rather than as something we sell. They are genuinely the right answer for some families, and saying so is more useful than pretending otherwise.

sections.heading: What actually moves the number inside the band
paragraphs: Two tutors can quote AED 150 and AED 400 for the same subject and level and both be pricing rationally. The variables are visible once named, and knowing them turns a quote from a mystery into a negotiation you can hold up your end of.

Scarcity dominates. A tutor who has actually taught Cambridge Additional Mathematics or Edexcel Further Pure Maths is rare in any one part of Dubai, and rarity sets the price regardless of format. Tier matters next: Extended and Higher work commands more than Core and Foundation because fewer tutors are secure in the extension content. Timing matters third, and it is the one families control least well - a February slot in a Year 11 exam run costs more than the same slot booked in September, because by February the diaries are full.

Then there are the structural variables. Session length, since a fifty-minute 'hour' is common and should be asked about. Commitment length, since a term booked up front usually prices below a rolling week. Travel, which is the whole difference between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band. Whether materials are included. Whether a second subject with the same tutor attracts a different rate. And urgency, which is a real factor and an uncomfortable one.

sections.heading: The extras that appear after you have committed
paragraphs: The headline rate is rarely the whole invoice, and the gap between them is where most of the dissatisfaction in this market lives. None of the following is dishonest in itself; the problem is that they are usually disclosed at the point of billing rather than the point of decision.

Registration or matching fees, charged once at the start by some agencies. Materials and printing, where a provider supplies workbooks. Assessment or diagnostic fees charged separately from the first lesson. Late-cancellation charges, which vary from twenty-four hours' notice to a full session forfeited, and which matter enormously in a city where a school fixture can move with a day's notice. Rescheduling limits per month. Minimum commitment terms, which can mean a term's notice to stop. Peak-season surcharges in the exam run. Travel surcharges on in-home arrangements for outlying communities. And payment-method differences, where a card payment carries a fee that a bank transfer does not.

The right move is to ask for all of it in writing before the first paid session, in one message with numbered questions. A provider who answers crisply has thought about it. A provider who answers in generalities will be answering in generalities when there is a dispute. This is not a sign of bad faith on their part so much as a sign that the terms do not exist in a form anyone can read, which amounts to the same thing in practice.

On VAT specifically, the only safe position is to ask whether a quoted figure includes it and to get the answer in writing. The tax treatment of education and tuition services in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring provider's summary, and this page does not state it. What a provider can and should tell you is whether the number they just quoted is the number you will pay.
