sections.heading: Tuition in context: fees, the 2026-27 freeze and exam entry costs
paragraphs: Tutoring is a small line next to a Dubai school fee, and placing it next to the other education costs a family carries makes it easier to judge. The emirate's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

That freeze is the right anchor for a tuition budget conversation this year, because it means the rest of the education bill is flat while tutoring is not. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More capacity changes where families can study; it does not change what an hour of specialist teaching costs.

The other cost families forget is exam entry, which is paid through the school in the normal case and directly to a centre for a private candidate. Entry fees are set by the centre rather than the board and vary, so the number has to come from your school's exams officer or from the centre you approach. A retake plan with no entry-fee line in it is an incomplete plan, and the fee is usually payable well before the papers - both Cambridge series close entries months ahead of them, and Pearson's November 2026 window ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with its deadline long past by the time it opened.

The table puts the pieces together. Figures attributed to published sources are marked as such; where a number depends on your own school or centre, the table says so rather than inventing a figure. We publish no fee list for IB Gram here because the right number depends on subject, tier, frequency and availability, and the consultation after the free trial lesson is where it belongs.

sections.heading: How many hours a subject really needs
paragraphs: The hourly rate is only half the cost. The other half is the number of hours, and that is where families both over-buy and under-buy badly. Over-buying looks like three sessions a week in an attempt to feel safe. Under-buying looks like six sessions booked eight weeks before a June series for a syllabus that was never learned.

The honest ranges are narrower than the market implies. A single diagnosed content gap in one topic is commonly three to five sessions with practice between them. A technique habit - method lines, command terms, units - takes two or three weeks of short frequent drilling rather than a term. A full year of maintenance support in one subject through Year 10 is typically thirty to thirty-five hours spread across the year. An exam-term intensive in one subject is typically ten to sixteen hours concentrated into eight to twelve weeks.

What drives the total up is not difficulty but diffusion. A student with no diagnosis consumes hours on whatever they mention each week, and the same topics recur because nothing was fixed. A student with a ranked error log consumes fewer hours to better effect, which is the practical argument for spending one of the first hours on measurement rather than teaching.

There is one case where more hours genuinely is the answer, and it should be named: a student arriving mid-course in the second term of Year 11 from a different system, with real content gaps across a syllabus and no time. That is a triage situation, and the right conversation includes narrowing the subject set with the school or planning for a later series rather than buying into a window that cannot hold the work.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest quote is sometimes the expensive one
paragraphs: A low rate is not a red flag by itself. A capable university student teaching Year 9 algebra at the bottom of the published band is good value and the right purchase for that job. The problem arises when a low rate is bought for a job it cannot do: Extended-tier Chemistry eight weeks from a series, or a specification the tutor has never seen a paper from. That hour is not cheap; it is a term spent and a term lost.

There is also a compliance dimension that Dubai families should understand, because it is almost entirely absent from competitor pages. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, under the service named 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists a two-working-day completion time and no fees.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published - press reporting notes that the ministry did not specify amounts or detail the penalties - so any specific figure circulating online is unverified and we will not repeat one. The permit itself being free of charge is the point worth knowing: a tutor cannot cite permit cost as a reason for a rate.

Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a different thing from an individual's work permit, and it is why 'KHDA approval' is a phrase to treat carefully: it applies to institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and makes no claim of approval or endorsement by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: Judging whether a term was worth the money
paragraphs: At renewal, the question is not whether the sessions happened or whether your child liked them. It is whether the losses that were costing marks in week one are still costing marks in week twelve. That is answerable if the work was documented and unanswerable if it was not, which is the practical reason to insist on written session notes and marked papers from the start rather than at the end.

Three things are worth looking at. The error log, compared with its first version: have the labels changed? Two marked papers from the same specification, placed side by side: has the loss moved from method to something else, which is progress even if the score is similar? And the student's own account of what they do differently in the exam hall, which is often the clearest signal of all.

A flat score with a changed error profile is a term that worked. A flat score with an identical error profile is a term that did not, and the correct response is to change the approach rather than to add hours - adding hours to an activity that is not working simply buys more of the thing that is not working. That sounds obvious written down and it is the most common error in this market.

It is also worth asking what the alternative use of the money was. For some families, one diagnostic session plus a disciplined home routine outperforms a term of weekly tuition, and nobody selling tuition has an incentive to say so. We would rather say it, partly because it is true and partly because the families who come back are the ones who were told the truth the first time.

sections.heading: Getting started without overbuying
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest useful thing, which is a diagnosis. Bring the most recent marked mock script and the exam entry statement listing each subject's board, code and tier. The free trial lesson includes a short timed question so that the first conversation is about evidence rather than impressions, and it costs nothing - no card details are taken to book it.

Then buy the smallest block that could work. One subject, one weekly slot, four weeks, with an explicit review at the end against the error log. That is a modest commitment and it produces enough evidence to decide properly. Families who start by booking three subjects at two sessions a week have bought certainty rather than information, and they generally spend more for less.

Ask us the uncomfortable questions up front. What is the rate, per how many minutes, and does it include VAT. What are the cancellation terms in hours. What happens if the first match is wrong. Which of my child's subjects are you thin on. And: is tuition actually the right purchase here, or is it a mock-reading problem we could hand back to you to act on. All five have answers and you should have them in writing before the first paid session.

Finally, the format, stated plainly. These are live one-to-one video lessons on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram operates no centre or classroom in Dubai and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The cost consequence is straightforward: there is no travel component in the number, and the tutor is chosen for the specification rather than for living within half an hour of your community.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE classes cost per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market rates fall into bands. Budget online tutoring and university students advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit broadly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits run about AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Dedicated IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors higher again. Those are other providers' own published figures as of October 2026, not our price list.

faqs.question: Are small group IGCSE classes better value than one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the students share the problem. Compare per student per hour of direct attention rather than per hour of elapsed time: in a group of six, each student receives roughly ten minutes of individual attention. That is excellent value when all six are meeting a new topic together, and poor value when five of them need something your child does not. A diagnosis changes the answer, which is why a marked script read properly is often the purchase that should come first.

faqs.question: What should a monthly IGCSE tuition package in Dubai actually include?
faqs.answer: Ask for the number of sessions, their length in minutes, the subjects covered, whether unused sessions carry over, the rescheduling allowance per month, and the notice period to stop. Packages circulating in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A package is only good value if the sessions get used, so the rescheduling terms matter more than the headline figure for a family with a fixture-heavy school calendar.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects tend to cost more per hour in Dubai, and why?
faqs.answer: Scarcity rather than difficulty sets the price. Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics carry a clear premium because very few tutors in any one part of the city have taught those specifications. Computer Science sits high for a related reason: tutors who can program are plentiful, tutors who can teach the board's pseudocode convention and trace-table method are not. Extended and Higher tier work costs more than Core and Foundation. Mathematics, Biology and the English specifications have the deepest pools and therefore the most competitive pricing.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai go up closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and it is a supply fact rather than a sales tactic. Demand concentrates between January and April for a June series, the number of evening slots is fixed, and specialists with a free Tuesday at 6pm in February are scarce. Booking a regular slot in September costs less than buying the same slot in February, and it also gives the work time to compound. If you are starting late, expect the upper end of the published band and a shorter list of available tutors, particularly in the thinly taught specifications.

faqs.question: Is an advertised AED rate per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask, because both conventions are in use and a fifty-minute 'hour' is common. The question matters more than it looks: AED 200 for fifty minutes is AED 240 an hour, which moves a quote from one market band into another. Get the session length in minutes, confirm whether the figure is per session or per sixty minutes, and ask whether a 45-minute option exists at the same hourly basis - for drilling work two shorter sessions a week often beat one long one on both effect and cost.

faqs.question: Should I expect VAT to be added to a tutoring invoice in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider whether the figure they quoted includes it, and keep the answer in writing. The VAT treatment of education and tuition services in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority's own published guidance rather than for any tutoring company's summary, and this page deliberately does not state it. What a provider can tell you, and should, is whether the number on the quote is the number you will pay. A provider who cannot answer that about their own invoice has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What extras should I ask about before paying for a term of classes?
faqs.answer: Registration or matching fees, materials and printing, separate diagnostic or assessment charges, the late-cancellation window in hours, the rescheduling allowance per month, minimum commitment and notice to stop, peak-season surcharges during the exam run, travel surcharges where an in-home arrangement applies, and whether a card payment carries a fee a transfer does not. Ask for all of it in one numbered message before the first paid session. A crisp written answer tells you the terms exist; a vague one tells you they will be vague during a dispute too.

faqs.question: How many hours does one IGCSE subject usually need across Year 11?
faqs.answer: Narrower ranges than the market implies. A single diagnosed content gap in one topic is commonly three to five sessions with practice between them. A technique habit such as writing method lines or reading command terms takes two to three weeks of short frequent drilling. Year-long maintenance in one subject runs roughly thirty to thirty-five hours spread across the year, and an exam-term intensive is typically ten to sixteen hours concentrated into eight to twelve weeks. Hours multiply when there is no diagnosis, because the same topics recur without ever being fixed.

faqs.question: Why can the cheapest IGCSE tutor in Dubai turn out to be the most expensive choice?
faqs.answer: Because a rate is only cheap relative to the job. A capable university student teaching Year 9 algebra at the bottom of the published band is good value. The same tutor taking on Extended-tier Chemistry eight weeks before a series has been bought for a job they cannot do, and the cost is a lost term rather than the hourly fee. Ask what specification they have taught, which papers, and at which tier. Also ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge for two years and is required of individuals tutoring in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two or three of my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is specification experience rather than general competence. Physics and Mathematics is a common and credible pairing. Chemistry and Biology is plausible. Mathematics and English is possible but rarer at a specialist standard, and a tutor who claims five subjects across both boards is usually claiming breadth they cannot evidence. Where one tutor genuinely covers two subjects there is often a package rate and always a scheduling advantage. Where they do not, two specialists at fewer hours each is the better purchase.

faqs.question: What happens financially if we decide to stop after one or two lessons?
faqs.answer: That depends on the terms you agreed, which is exactly why they should be in writing first. With us the trial lesson is free and takes no card details, and we would rather you stopped after a short block than committed to a term that was not working. In the wider market, watch for minimum commitment periods, notice requirements measured in sessions rather than days, and prepaid packages with no refund on unused sessions. Ask for the stopping terms before the starting terms; the answer tells you how confident the provider is.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE classes with IB Gram take place at a venue anywhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no centre, classroom, office or branch in the UAE, and does not provide home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the country - in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Classes are delivered as live one-to-one or paired video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. The cost effect is direct: the travel element that lifts in-home rates into the AED 180-500 band is absent from the number, and the tutor is selected for the specification your child sits rather than for proximity to your community.

faqs.question: How do school fees and tutoring costs compare for a Dubai family this year?
faqs.answer: School fees are the far larger line and, unusually, they are flat: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Tutoring is not frozen. Published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Exam entry fees, set by your school or centre, sit alongside both.

faqs.question: How do I judge at renewal whether a term of classes was worth the money?
faqs.answer: Compare the error log with its first version and put two marked papers from the same specification side by side. If the losses have moved - method fixed, timing now the main problem - the term worked even if the score is similar, because a different problem is a nearer problem. If the error profile is identical, the term did not work, and the correct response is to change the approach rather than add hours. Ask your child what they now do differently in the exam hall; that answer is often the clearest signal available.

dubai/igcse-classes.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis, then buy four weeks
dubai/igcse-classes.closingBody: IGCSE classes in Dubai are priced across a wide and public range, from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 for premium named tutors, and the number you should pay depends on a diagnosis nobody has made yet. So start there: bring the most recent marked mock script, take the free trial lesson, and get the rate, session length, VAT position and cancellation terms in writing. Then buy the smallest block that could work and review it against the error log. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

The students who arrive here know their syllabus and still lose eight to fourteen marks a paper to four repeatable causes: unwritten method, command terms read as synonyms, units and significant figures, and time spent in the wrong part of the paper. This page names those causes, puts numbers on them, and sets out the drills that remove them. Sessions run one-to-one over live video.

dubai/igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: These tutors coach exam performance as well as content. Each one marks to the published Cambridge or Pearson scheme, labels losses by cause, and can name the command-term traps on the specific paper your child will sit.

intro.heading: Why a student who knows the work still loses fourteen marks
paragraphs: Open almost any marked IGCSE script from a Dubai Year 11 who is stuck in the middle grades and the pattern is the same. The content is there. The student can tell you about electrolysis or about the quadratic formula or about the causes of a trade deficit. What the script shows is something narrower and more fixable: an answer with no intermediate working, a question that asked for an explanation and received a description, a number without a unit, and three questions at the end of the paper attempted in four minutes.

Add those up and they commonly reach eight to fourteen marks on a single paper. On most IGCSE grade scales that is one or two whole grades. No amount of additional content teaching retrieves them, because they were never content losses. This is the gap coaching is for, and it is the reason this page is organised around causes of lost marks rather than around a syllabus tour.

The distinction matters commercially too. A family who diagnoses a timing problem and buys a term of topic revision has bought the wrong product, usually at AED 150 to 300 an hour based on the market rates providers publish. It is a common and expensive mistake, and it happens because nobody put the script under a lamp first. A mock paper is the cheapest diagnostic instrument available to a Dubai parent and it is almost always sitting in a school bag, unread by anyone except the student who got the score.

Coaching in this sense is unglamorous. It involves reading the mark scheme out loud in the student's own script, which is tedious. It involves doing one calculation forty times until the working writes itself under pressure, which is dull. It involves sitting with a clock. The reason to do it anyway is that it is the highest-yield work available in the final year, and it is the part of preparation that schools, carrying thirty students a class, have the least capacity to deliver individually.

Everything here is delivered as one-to-one live video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Dubai school week. IB Gram does not run a coaching centre in the UAE and does not send tutors to Dubai addresses; in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. For this particular kind of work the online format is not a compromise at all - the script, the mark scheme, the annotation and a visible timer sit in one shared window, and the marked file is still there next week.

One more thing before the detail. Coaching of this kind is not a replacement for the school. The teacher has the syllabus, the internal assessment record and thirty other students, and in most Dubai schools they are doing that job well. What they do not have is the room to sit with one student and read a mark scheme aloud against that student's own script for twenty minutes. That is the gap, it is narrow, and it is where an outside hour is worth paying for.

dubai/igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Coaching looks different at each stage of the IGCSE route, because the thing that limits a grade changes as the exam gets closer. These are the four stages Dubai families ask about.

programmes.name: Year 9: before the options are fixed
programmes.description: The useful work here is habit formation rather than exam technique: writing method lines without being asked, labelling axes, reading a question twice, recording units. None of it is examined yet, which is exactly why it is cheap to install now and expensive to install in Year 11. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint results, offered in March, May and October, are the earliest reliable signal a parent gets.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage is complicated by arrival timing. Students joining a British-curriculum school from a CBSE or American background in Year 9 have usually met the content but not the written-examination conventions, and a Checkpoint result reads lower than their understanding warrants. Coaching that fixes convention at this point prevents a misread tier decision a year later.

programmes.name: Year 10: building the paper habits
programmes.description: The first year of the course, where topics are taught for the first time and the tier decision is approaching. Coaching here means converting new content into examinable form straight away rather than a year later - every new topic practised as a past-paper question within a fortnight of being taught, and the command terms of that subject introduced as vocabulary.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally make tier entries during or at the end of Year 10, and the decision is evidenced by internal assessment. A student whose exam technique is weak looks like a student who should sit the lower tier, and the grade ceiling that follows is permanent. Fixing technique in Year 10 is therefore a decision about Year 12 options.

programmes.name: Year 11: mocks, then the series
programmes.description: The year coaching is most often bought, and the year it has the narrowest window to work in. The sequence that works is: mock papers marked by cause, one error pattern attacked at a time, timed-condition practice from January, and paper-order strategy agreed before the first real paper. Content revision continues but stops being the main event.
programmes.countryNote: Mock windows in Dubai schools commonly fall in November and again in late February, which produces two genuine diagnostics in the right order. Families who treat mocks as a verdict waste them. Families who treat them as data get the single most useful document of the whole two years.

programmes.name: Post-results: the retake or lift
programmes.description: A single grade short of a sixth-form condition is usually a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem, which makes it unusually responsive to coaching. The work is narrow by design: the specific paper, the specific question types that cost the marks, and timed practice. A whole-subject re-teach is rarely the right purchase.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's International GCSE November series and Cambridge's June and November series are the practical windows for a candidate at a school in Dubai, and their entry deadlines fall months before the grades that would justify an entry arrive. Agree the plan in June rather than in August, because by August the decision has usually been made for you by a deadline nobody mentioned at the time.

dubai/igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Each note below names the error pattern that costs the most marks in that subject rather than summarising its content. These are the things coaching actually works on.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Unwritten method is the largest recoverable loss in the whole qualification. Both boards award method marks explicitly, so a wrong final answer with clear working can outscore a wrong answer with none. The drill is mechanical: every question, every time, one line per step, until it survives the clock.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit conversion and formula rearrangement under pressure. Candidates who can quote the equation lose the mark by substituting centimetres into a formula expecting metres, or by rearranging on the fly and dropping a reciprocal. Writing the formula, then the substitution, then the answer with its unit is three marks of insurance.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cascading errors from unbalanced equations. One wrong coefficient in part (a) removes the follow-through marks in later parts unless the working is explicit enough for an examiner to award them. The coaching drill is to balance, check atom counts, then annotate the mole ratio before any calculation begins.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term blindness, more than in any other subject. A question asking the candidate to explain water movement in a root hair cell wants water potential, the partially permeable membrane and the direction named. A description of water moving in scores a fraction of the available marks and feels like a correct answer.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Scope confusion. Students revise content that is not on their route and skip content that is, because the specification subsets are not obvious from a textbook. A single session spent marking the syllabus document against the student's revision list routinely saves a fortnight.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Tariff blindness on the summary and directed-writing tasks. The mark scheme awards content points, and elegant prose that misses them caps the score. Coaching here is largely counting: how many points are available, how many the student found, and how long they spent not finding the rest.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Question-type unfamiliarity rather than language weakness, particularly for students transferred between 0510 and 0500 mid-course. The reading tasks have fixed shapes, and recognising the shape in the first ten seconds is a trainable skill that changes the whole paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Analysis without application. A correct definition about no particular firm earns the knowledge mark and nothing beyond it. The fix is a sentence frame applied to every case study until it is automatic: the concept, then this business, then the consequence, then the judgement with a reason.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Loose diagrams. Axes unlabelled, curves unnamed, the shift drawn but the new equilibrium not marked. Each omission is a mark, they recur on every diagram question in the paper, and the entire problem can be drilled out in two sessions.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Narrative instead of interrogation. The case study is recalled accurately and the source is ignored, which caps the response in the middle band. Coaching teaches a fixed reading order for any resource question: what it shows, what it does not show, and what that means for the question asked.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Provenance left on the table. Source questions award marks for using who wrote it, when and why, and most mid-band answers treat sources as neutral information. The drill is a provenance sentence before any content sentence, every time, until it is habit.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode written as Python. The written paper assesses the board's own pseudocode convention, trace tables and data representation, and fluent programmers lose marks on notation. Trace tables in particular reward a slow, ruled, row-by-row method that nobody adopts voluntarily.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks on any IGCSE paper
paragraphs: Every IGCSE paper is written in a controlled vocabulary. 'State' and 'explain' are not stylistic variants; they instruct the examiner what to accept, and the mark tariff follows from them. A student who treats them as synonyms will write a long answer to a one-mark question and a one-line answer to a four-mark question, and will lose marks at both ends while working harder than the candidate who read the verb.

This is the single most under-taught thing in exam preparation, and it is almost entirely absent from the competitor pages on this search. It is also the fastest intervention available. Most students can be taught the twelve command terms that appear across their subjects in two sessions, and the effect shows up on the next timed paper rather than three months later.

The table below sets out the terms that recur most across Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE papers in the sciences, mathematics and the social subjects, with what the examiner is actually looking for and the error that usually appears instead. Both boards publish their own command-term guidance in the syllabus and specification documents, and those are the authoritative versions - this is a working summary, not a substitute.

The drill is simple and dull. Take ten past-paper questions. Cover the question body. Read only the command term and the mark allocation, and predict the shape of the answer: how many distinct points, whether a reason is required, whether a judgement is needed. Then read the question. Students who do this twenty times stop writing essays in response to 'state' within a fortnight.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT THE EXAMINER IS ACTUALLY LOOKING FOR

sections.heading: The error patterns that cost Dubai candidates the most marks
paragraphs: After enough marked scripts the losses stop looking random. They cluster, they repeat within a student, and they are specific enough to attack one at a time. What follows is the list that recurs most across the Dubai Year 10 and Year 11 scripts that come through these sessions, with the drill that removes each one.

Two things are worth noticing about the list. First, almost none of these are knowledge failures - the student could do the question in conversation. Second, each one has a mechanical fix, which is why coaching works faster than re-teaching. A habit that takes three weeks to install is worth more than a topic that takes three weeks to re-explain, because the habit pays out on every question in the paper rather than on the two questions about that topic.

The order matters. Attack the pattern with the largest mark count first, not the one that is easiest to fix or the one the student finds most annoying. That is the whole purpose of labelling and counting lost marks rather than simply noting them: it produces a ranking, and the ranking is what makes the next four weeks worth paying for.

One caveat about the cost column. The figures are the typical range seen across marked scripts rather than a measured average with a sample size behind it, and they vary by subject and by paper. Treat them as a guide to which pattern deserves attention first, not as a published statistic. The number that matters is the one from your child's current script, counted by a person who marked it strictly to the scheme rather than estimated from memory.

sections.heading: Timing is a budgeting problem, and it is solvable on paper
paragraphs: A candidate who loses six marks in the last section has not run out of ability. They have overspent earlier, usually on a question they could already do, because writing more felt like working harder. The exam is a budget: a fixed number of minutes to collect a fixed number of marks, and every paper has an implied spending rate that can be calculated before the student ever sits it.

The arithmetic is worth doing explicitly with a Year 11 because it is persuasive in a way that advice is not. Take the paper's total marks and its duration, subtract five minutes for reading and checking, and divide. That is the marks-per-minute rate the paper requires. Then take the student's last mock and work out where they actually spent the time. The mismatch is usually concentrated in two or three questions.

From there the rules are simple and the discipline is hard. A hard move-on rule: if a question has consumed its budget and has not yielded, leave it and return. An order strategy: some candidates do better collecting the back-end marks first, which is permitted and rarely considered. And a checking allocation that is genuinely protected rather than theoretically reserved, because unchecked unit and transcription errors are among the cheapest marks on the paper.

Practising this requires real exam conditions, which almost no student imposes on themselves. A visible clock, no phone, no pausing to look something up, and a strict stop. Over video that is easier to enforce than it sounds: the timer is on the shared screen, the tutor is watching, and the script is photographed and marked immediately afterwards while the decisions are still fresh enough to discuss.

sections.heading: The Alternative to Practical paper, and why it rewards vocabulary
paragraphs: Most Dubai science candidates on the Cambridge tiered specifications sit an Alternative to Practical paper rather than a live practical examination. It assesses experimental method in writing, and it is one of the highest-yield papers to coach because the skill it tests is narrow, explicit and almost never taught as a skill in its own right.

What it rewards is naming. The independent variable, the dependent variable, the variables held constant and how. The instrument and its precision. A repeat and a mean. An anomalous result identified and what to do about it. An improvement that is actually an improvement rather than 'be more careful'. A student who writes 'measure the temperature and record the results' has described something true and collected very little, because the mark scheme is looking for specific nouns.

The graph questions carry their own set of marks and their own set of avoidable losses: axes the wrong way round, a scale chosen so the points occupy a quarter of the grid, points plotted without a sharp pencil, a line of best fit drawn through the first and last points rather than through the distribution. Each is a mark, and all of them are mechanical.

This is also the clearest answer to parents who worry that online coaching cannot cover practical work. The paper is a writing paper. Method rehearsal, variable identification, instrument precision and graph technique transfer perfectly over a shared screen. Where a school enters a component requiring laboratory work, that work happens at school under the school's supervision, and coaching prepares the method and the write-up conventions beforehand.
bullets: Name the independent, dependent and controlled variables explicitly, every time
State the instrument and its precision rather than the action
Identify anomalies and say what you would do about them
'Be more careful' is never an improvement; a named change is

sections.heading: What a mark converts to, and why boundaries move
paragraphs: Parents often ask what score equals a grade 7, and the honest answer is that it depends on the series. Grade boundaries are set after each examination to account for the difficulty of that particular paper, which means a raw mark that earned one grade last June may sit a boundary either side of it this June. Boards publish boundaries after each series, and those published tables are the only reliable reference.

The practical consequence for coaching is that planning to a target raw mark is reasonable and planning to a historical boundary is not. The sensible approach is to look at the spread of recent boundaries for the specification, plan for the upper end of that spread, and treat anything closer than three or four marks to a boundary as a coin toss rather than a result. Students sitting three marks under a boundary are the population for whom technique work pays the most, because three marks is one unwritten method line and one unit.

A second point about boundaries belongs here because it affects tier decisions. On tiered specifications the lower tier caps the grade available regardless of raw mark, so a student scoring near the top of the Core or Foundation paper cannot reach the top grades at all. That is a structural ceiling rather than a boundary effect, and it is the reason a tier conversation has to happen before entries close rather than after a strong mock.

We do not reproduce or distribute boundary tables, syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. They are published by Cambridge Assessment International Education and by Pearson and should be read on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. A provider offering to supply you with a library of those files is telling you how it treats rules generally.

sections.heading: The diagnostic session, in detail
paragraphs: The first session is not a lesson, and a family should be suspicious of a coaching service that starts by teaching. It is a measurement exercise, and it has a shape. Thirty minutes of timed work from a real past paper on the correct specification, done with a visible clock while the tutor says nothing. Then the marking, strictly to the published scheme, with the student watching rather than being handed a score afterwards.

The marking happens in four passes. The raw mark, done without generosity. Then every lost mark labelled by cause: recall, method, arithmetic, command term, units, or time. Then the labels grouped and counted, which converts a score into a ranked diagnosis. Then one cause selected and three further questions found that attack it. That output - a ranked list and a first target - is the deliverable of the session.

What this produces for a parent is unusually concrete. Not 'your child needs to work on algebra', but 'eleven marks lost: five to unwritten method, three to command terms, two to units, one to recall, and the recall gap is in one named topic'. That is actionable by the family even without further sessions, which is why we are content for some people to buy only the diagnostic and leave.

Doing this over video has a practical advantage worth naming. The script is photographed or shared on screen, the mark scheme sits beside it, and the annotation is saved as a file with a date on it. Six weeks later, the second diagnostic can be placed next to the first and compared directly. A paper sheet handed over in a living room does not survive to be compared with anything.
bullets: Thirty minutes of timed work before any teaching happens
Four marking passes: mark, label, group, target
Output is a ranked diagnosis and one first target, in writing
Files are dated so the next diagnostic can be compared with this one

sections.heading: Coaching through the Dubai mock season
paragraphs: Dubai's British-curriculum schools typically run mock examinations in November and again in late February, and those two windows are the most valuable and most wasted resource in the IGCSE year. They are valuable because they produce a full marked script under something close to real conditions, which is the only instrument that reveals timing behaviour. They are wasted because the script is usually read once, for the score, and then filed.

The right sequence is to coach lightly before a mock and heavily after it. Before: confirm the timing plan, rehearse the question-order strategy, and resist the urge to cram new content, which displaces sleep and rarely appears on the paper. After: the full post-mortem, with every lost mark labelled, and a revised ranking for the next eight weeks.

The February mock has a particular function in Dubai, because it falls close enough to a June series to be predictive but far enough away to be fixable. A student whose February script shows the same error ranking as their November script has not been doing the work between them, and that is a conversation about practice rather than about hours. A student whose ranking has changed - method fixed, timing now the main loss - is on track, even if the score has barely moved.

Ramadan is the other calendar feature that reshapes this. The school day shortens, routines move, and a 5pm session that worked in January becomes the worst slot available. Sessions shift to a post-Iftar window, lengths shorten slightly, and the fortnight either side of Eid is treated as consolidation rather than new work. Because lessons are delivered over video, moving a slot costs nothing beyond a message.

sections.heading: What coaching never includes
paragraphs: A coaching relationship that touches assessed work has a boundary, and it is not a soft one. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has produced and point at where a criterion is not met, and set more practice. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final state, or develop an investigation on the student's behalf.

The Gulf market makes this worth stating plainly. One site in this search landscape sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is malpractice, it is detectable, and the penalty falls on the student rather than the seller. A coaching service worth its fee will refuse that request and explain why, and will be more useful than the one that does not, because the skills it builds transfer to the examination where no help is available.

There are three other things we do not do. We do not promise grades or grade improvements, because no honest tutor can - a coach can remove avoidable losses and cannot control a boundary. We do not publish satisfaction statistics or star ratings we cannot evidence with real, countable, attributable data. And we do not claim approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because IB Gram holds none of those and operates no premises in the UAE.

What we will do is tell you when coaching is the wrong purchase. If a diagnostic shows genuine content gaps across half a syllabus eight weeks before a series, more technique sessions will not fix it and someone should say so. Sometimes the right advice is to narrow the subject set with the school, plan for a later series, or spend the money on nothing at all.
bullets: Criteria explained, method rehearsed, feedback given on the student's own work
No text supplied for submission and no investigation developed on their behalf

sections.heading: Starting: bring a marked paper
paragraphs: The most useful thing a Dubai parent can bring to a first conversation is the most recent marked mock script, with the mark scheme if the school released it. Second best is the exam entry statement with each subject's board, code and tier. With either of those, a coaching plan can be built in one session. With neither, the first two sessions go on discovery.

The free trial lesson is the right place to test whether a coach is specification-literate. Ask them what the papers are worth on that code, which command terms carry the most marks in that subject, and where candidates typically lose time on the particular paper your child sits. Specifics come back from someone who has coached that paper. Generalities come back from someone who knows the subject, and generalities are what the mark scheme declines to reward.

Expect a direct answer about availability. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English, Business Studies, Economics and Geography are well covered at both tiers and on both boards. Additional Mathematics, Further Pure Mathematics and the less commonly entered languages are thin, and in those cases the honest options are a wait, a different pattern, or a recommendation to look elsewhere.

On format, to leave no room for doubt: sessions are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no coaching centre in Dubai and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE - in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For error-pattern work the screen is genuinely the better room: the script, the scheme, the timer and the annotation sit in one frame, and the whole record is saved with the date on it.

process.title: Send the script
process.description: The most recent marked mock paper, with the mark scheme if the school released it, plus the subject's board, code and tier. One marked script tells a coach more than an hour of conversation, because it contains the behaviour rather than a description of it.

process.title: Timed diagnostic
process.description: Thirty minutes of real past-paper work under a visible clock during the free trial lesson, with no teaching and no prompting. This establishes the baseline and, more importantly, shows how the student behaves when the clock is running rather than how they behave when helped.

process.title: Four-pass marking and ranking
process.description: The raw mark taken strictly to the scheme, every lost mark labelled by cause, the causes grouped and counted, and one target selected. The output is a ranked written diagnosis, which is the document the whole plan is built from.

process.title: Drill the biggest-loss cause
process.description: Short, frequent sessions on one labelled cause at a time, with three same-type questions set between sessions. A pattern is declared fixed only when it survives a timed question, not when the student can do it slowly with help.

process.title: Re-diagnose at six weeks
process.description: A second timed paper, marked the same way, placed beside the first. If the ranking has changed the plan is working even when the score has barely moved; if the ranking is identical, the conversation is about practice between sessions rather than about buying more hours.

process.title: Mock post-mortem and final-run plan
process.description: After each school mock, a full post-mortem produces a revised ranking and a timing plan for the series. From January the emphasis moves almost entirely to timed-condition work and question-order strategy.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session measures rather than teaches. A score is converted into a ranked list of causes, so the money goes to the largest loss instead of the most obvious topic.

whyPoints.title: Drills, not explanations
whyPoints.description: A habit that survives exam pressure needs repetition, not insight. Sessions are short and frequent by design, with practice set between them and a rule that nothing counts as fixed until it holds under a clock.

whyPoints.title: The boards' own vocabulary
whyPoints.description: Command terms, mark tariffs and practical-method language are taught in the wording Cambridge and Pearson publish, and those documents are linked rather than redistributed.

whyPoints.title: Mocks used as data
whyPoints.description: Dubai schools produce two full marked scripts a year in November and February. Both get a proper post-mortem, which is where most of the diagnostic value in the whole course sits.

whyPoints.title: An error log a parent can read
whyPoints.description: What was lost, to what cause, how many marks, and whether it recurred. Two minutes of reading tells you what an hour bought, which is more than any progress report will.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the ceiling
whyPoints.description: Coaching removes avoidable losses. It cannot move a grade boundary, change an entry tier or replace a missing half-syllabus, and we will say so rather than sell sessions into a problem they cannot solve.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE coaching and ordinary subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: Tutoring generally teaches content the student has not mastered. Coaching works on how the student converts what they know into marks: method lines written down, command terms read correctly, units recorded, time budgeted across the paper. The two are different purchases and they suit different problems. A student who cannot do the topic needs teaching. A student who can do the topic in conversation and still drops twelve marks a paper needs coaching, and buying the wrong one of these is the most common and most expensive mistake families make.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Dubai IGCSE candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: 'Explain' and 'describe' confused with each other, which costs two to four marks on most science papers. 'Suggest', which asks for principle applied to an unfamiliar context and usually receives a recalled textbook fact. 'Compare', which requires explicitly linked statements and usually receives two separate descriptions. And 'evaluate' or 'discuss', which carry the biggest tariffs and are regularly answered with one side argued well and no judgement at the end. Both Cambridge and Pearson publish their own command-term guidance in the syllabus documents, and those are the versions to work from.

faqs.question: My child understands the topic but still drops marks - what is actually going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of four things, and a marked script will tell you which. Method not written down, which discards marks the scheme awarded explicitly for working. Command terms read as synonyms, so the answer addresses a question that was not asked. Units and significant figures. Or time, with marks left uncollected in the final section because earlier questions were over-answered. Add them up on a real script and they commonly total eight to fourteen marks, which is one or two grades on most scales. None of them responds to more content revision.

faqs.question: How do I read a mock paper myself to work out what to fix first?
faqs.answer: Go through it four times. First, confirm the raw mark against the scheme without being generous. Second, write a label next to every lost mark: recall, method, arithmetic, command term, units or time. Third, count the labels and rank them. Fourth, pick the one at the top of that list and find three more questions of the same type. That converts a score into a plan, and it is the single most useful hour a Dubai parent can spend on an IGCSE year. If the top cause is recall in one named topic, that is a teaching problem; otherwise it is technique.

faqs.question: Why does my child run out of time on papers they can otherwise do?
faqs.answer: Because they are overspending early on questions they already know, which feels like working hard. Every paper has an implied rate: total marks divided by minutes available, less five for reading and checking. That is usually somewhere around 0.7 to 1 mark per minute depending on the paper. Compare it with where the time actually went in the last mock and the overspend is usually concentrated in two or three questions. The fixes are a hard move-on rule, a considered question order, and a checking allocation that is genuinely protected rather than theoretically reserved.

faqs.question: What does the Alternative to Practical paper actually test?
faqs.answer: Experimental method in writing. Naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables and how each is controlled. Stating the instrument and its precision rather than the action. Including a repeat and a mean. Identifying an anomalous result and saying what you would do about it. Proposing an improvement that is a named change rather than 'be more careful'. The graph questions carry separate marks for scale, axes, plotting accuracy and the line of best fit. All of this is a writing skill, which is why it coaches well over video and why it is rarely taught explicitly in class.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grade boundaries move between series, and should we plan around them?
faqs.answer: They move, because boundaries are set after each examination to account for that paper's difficulty. Boards publish the tables after each series and those published versions are the only reliable reference. The practical implication is to plan to a raw mark with margin rather than to a historical boundary, and to treat anything within three or four marks of a boundary as genuinely uncertain. That margin is exactly where technique work pays most: three marks is one unwritten method line plus one missing unit, which is a fortnight of drilling rather than a term of revision.

faqs.question: How many sessions does one weak IGCSE topic usually take to fix?
faqs.answer: A genuine content gap in a single topic is commonly three to five sessions, with practice between them, assuming the underlying skills are in place. A technique habit takes longer in weeks but less time in hours: two or three weeks of short, frequent drilling, because the point is repetition rather than explanation. The slow case is a topic that depends on a missing earlier skill - mole calculations resting on weak ratio work, for instance - where the fix has to go back a level first. A diagnostic distinguishes these in one session.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start coaching eight weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: For technique work, no - eight weeks is enough to remove most avoidable losses, and that is often worth a grade. For a half-learned syllabus, it is too late and an honest coach should say so rather than sell into it. The practical plan at eight weeks is narrow: diagnose from the most recent mock, pick the two largest error causes, drill those, and run weekly timed papers with a strict post-mortem. New content is added only where a diagnostic shows a specific named gap that appears reliably on the paper.

faqs.question: Should my child practise past papers untimed or under exam conditions?
faqs.answer: Both, in the right order. Untimed practice is for learning a method and should be used while a habit is still being installed - there is no point rushing something that is not yet automatic. Timed practice is for proving the habit survives pressure, and it is the only way to see timing behaviour at all. Most students do neither properly: they do papers at a vague pace with the answers nearby. A visible clock, no phone, no lookups and a hard stop is the condition that makes the result mean anything.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is the subject or the exam technique?
faqs.answer: Ask your child to explain a question they got wrong, verbally, without writing. If they can explain it correctly, the knowledge is there and the loss was technique - method, command term, units or time. If they cannot, it is content. Do this across six or eight wrong answers on a mock and the split becomes obvious, usually within fifteen minutes. The reason it matters is cost: a term of topic revision bought for a timing problem is wasted money at the AED 150 to 300 an hour that providers in this market publish for qualified online tutors.

faqs.question: Can coaching compensate for an IGCSE subject my child's school is teaching weakly?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is worth being realistic about the limits. Coaching can cover syllabus content, teach the paper and build technique, and that handles most of what a weak teaching year costs. What it cannot replace is laboratory time, coursework supervision where a component requires it, or the internal assessment decisions the school makes. If a department has changed hands mid-course - which happens, including in schools with strong overall inspection outcomes - read the subject-level judgements in the school's inspection report rather than the headline band before deciding how much outside support to buy.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram run IGCSE coaching classes at a centre in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no centre, office or branch in the UAE, and does not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Coaching is delivered as live one-to-one video sessions on Gulf Standard Time. For this kind of work the screen is arguably the better room: the script, the mark scheme, a visible timer and the annotation all sit in one frame, the whole thing is saved with a date, and a second diagnostic six weeks later can be compared directly with the first.

faqs.question: How should coaching change during the Dubai mock season?
faqs.answer: Light before, heavy after. Before a mock, confirm the timing plan and the question-order strategy and resist cramming new content, which displaces sleep and rarely appears on the paper. After it, run the full post-mortem: every lost mark labelled, the causes counted and ranked, and the next eight weeks rewritten from that ranking. Dubai schools commonly mock in November and again in late February, which gives two genuine diagnostics in a useful order. A February script showing the same ranking as November means practice between sessions is not happening.

faqs.question: What will a coach refuse to do with my child's assessed IGCSE work?
faqs.answer: Supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final form, or develop an investigation on the student's behalf. What a coach may do is explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, rehearse method, read what the student has already produced, point at where a criterion is not yet met and set further practice. One site in this search landscape sells completed assessed work outright; that is malpractice and the penalty falls on the student. A coach who cannot say which side of that line a request falls on has answered the question.

dubai/igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the script, not the syllabus
dubai/igcse-coaching.closingBody: IGCSE coaching in Dubai earns its fee when it finds the marks a student is already entitled to and is losing to habit. That begins with one marked paper, four passes of honest marking and a ranked list of causes - not with a tour of the syllabus. Send the most recent mock script and the subject's board, code and tier, take the free trial lesson, and ask the coach to name where candidates lose time on that specific paper. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in short frequent blocks built around your child's school week.

intro.heading: Reading code and writing code are different abilities
paragraphs: The most common pattern in a Dubai IGCSE computer science enquiry is a student who is comfortable in lessons, follows worked examples easily, and then produces almost nothing on the programming section of a timed paper. Parents interpret that as nerves or carelessness. It is neither. Reading code and writing code from a written specification are different abilities, and a course that teaches mostly by demonstration builds the first one and leaves the second largely untested until an examination exposes it.

The diagnostic for this takes ten minutes and needs no equipment beyond paper. Give the student a short algorithm written out and ask them to produce a trace table: the value of each variable after each iteration, in columns. A student who can trace reliably understands control flow. A student who cannot trace a nested loop, or who loses track once a counter and an accumulator are both changing, has the gap that explains their programming marks, and it is a gap in a specific, teachable skill rather than a general aptitude.

The second diagnostic is production. Hand over a written specification — three or four sentences describing what a program must do, with no code visible — and twenty minutes. The output is either working code or a precise record of where the student stopped: at declaring variables, at the loop structure, at the validation condition, at the output formatting. That record is worth more than a mark, because each of those stopping points has a different fix and a different number of sessions attached.

So this plan keeps two records rather than one. The theory record tracks the specification's written content — data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, networks, emerging technologies — as a dated topic list with scores from timed question sets. The programming record tracks trace accuracy, production from specification, pseudocode convention compliance and the structures the student can deploy without prompting. Merging the two is how a student ends up with a middling overall mark and no idea which half is failing.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For this subject the online format is the natural one: the student types in a shared editor while the tutor watches and comments, the code is saved with its date, and the next session can open last week's attempt rather than a memory of it. A Dubai family in Mirdif or Al Furjan also gets a tutor matched to the specification rather than to a driving radius, which matters because this subject has fewer specialist tutors than any other option subject in the emirate.

dubai/igcse-computer-science-tutor.programmesIntro: Computer science is a new subject at 14 for most students and a continuation for a few, and what sits either side of Year 11 changes the plan. These are the four points a Dubai family needs to place.

The specific carry-over problem is that block environments remove syntax and variable declaration, so a student can have three years of successful programming experience and no experience of writing a declaration or debugging a syntax error.

programmes.countryNote: Dubai's long December break is a strong window for a production intensive: four consecutive mornings each producing a small program from a written specification builds more than four weekly sessions, because the habit needs repetition close together.

programmes.name: IGCSE Computer Science, Year 11
programmes.description: Remaining theory, databases, Boolean logic and examination technique on both papers. The Year 11 priorities are pseudocode convention compliance, data representation arithmetic under time, and the longer programming question that students abandon partway.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and on Pearson the on-screen practical paper has its own logistical requirements at the centre.

programmes.name: A Level computer science or IB Diploma computer science
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is the entry currency and the production habit is what transfers. A Level computer science and Diploma computer science both require substantial independent programming, and a student who reached 16 able to read code but not write it struggles immediately rather than gradually.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Tutoring is not required for the process.

dubai/igcse-computer-science-tutor.subjectsIntro: Computer science splits into a theory half and a programming half with almost nothing in common, and a plan needs separate work on each. These are the units it is built from.

subjects.name: Data representation
subjects.description: Binary, denary and hexadecimal conversion, binary addition, overflow, logical shifts, character sets, images and sound. Arithmetic under time, which makes it a drilling task. Marks are lost to conversion errors rather than to misunderstanding the concept.

subjects.name: Data transmission and networks
subjects.description: Packet structure, transmission methods, error detection including parity and checksums, and network hardware. Error-detection questions want a worked demonstration rather than a description of the method, which is where scripts fall short.

subjects.name: Hardware and logic gates
subjects.description: Processor architecture, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, memory and storage, and logic circuits with truth tables. Truth tables are mechanical marks: a student who builds them column by column rather than guessing rarely loses any.

subjects.name: Software and system software
subjects.description: Operating systems, utilities, compilers and interpreters, and types of programming language. A recall topic, which means it belongs on a tested list rather than in taught sessions, and it is where a terminology bank pays for itself.

subjects.name: The internet, security and emerging technologies
subjects.description: Web technologies, cyber-security threats and countermeasures, encryption, and automated or emerging technologies. Answers lose marks for naming a threat without describing the mechanism or without matching a countermeasure to it.

subjects.name: Algorithm design and problem solving
subjects.description: Decomposition, flowcharts, pseudocode, trace tables, validation and test data, and standard methods such as searching and sorting. Trace tables are both an examined skill and the best available diagnostic for control-flow understanding.

subjects.name: Programming: sequence, selection and iteration
subjects.description: The fundamentals, and the point where reading and writing diverge most sharply. A student who cannot construct a nested loop from a written description has the gap that most programming marks depend on, regardless of how well they follow a demonstration.

subjects.name: Arrays, procedures and file handling
subjects.description: Indexing, iteration over arrays, parameter passing and, where the specification includes it, reading and writing files. Off-by-one errors and parameter confusion are the two recurring losses and both are visible in a trace table.

subjects.name: Databases and SQL
subjects.description: Single-table database structure, field types, primary keys and querying. A small topic with determinate marks, which makes it high value per hour of revision and the sort of thing that gets skipped because it feels peripheral.

subjects.name: Pseudocode conventions
subjects.levels: Across both papers, and a source of avoidable loss
subjects.description: Mark schemes accept pseudocode written to published conventions, and a logically correct answer in a student's own invented notation can lose marks. Learning the conventions is a short, mechanical task that almost nobody does deliberately.

dubai/igcse-computer-science-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, which matters more in this subject than in most, because specialist supply is thin across the emirate. What the postcode changes is when a student can sit a long programming task uninterrupted.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Short commutes and apartment study space. Programming work needs a machine and headphones rather than silence, so an after-school slot works here even where a three-hour practical simulation does not.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Several large British-curriculum schools, but computer science option cohorts are usually small even in big schools. That means fewer parallel sets to benchmark against, so an external production diagnostic is more informative here than a class position.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Damac Hills
regions.note: Long bus routes and evening commitments. The production task is set for a weekend morning so the student has an uninterrupted stretch at a machine, and the session reviews the saved attempt rather than starting one.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Established schools with longer-running computer science provision and specialist teachers. The gap a tutor fills in this cluster is individual production practice, which a class of fifteen cannot provide per student every week.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: A wide curricular mix and frequent transfer. Students arriving mid-course may have learned a different programming language, so the first task is establishing which language the school's examination work uses and whether the student can produce in it.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to the universities and the technology sector, so budget-tier undergraduate tutors are easy to find. For language practice and debugging that is a reasonable tier; for pseudocode convention marking and theory question sets it is not the same purchase.

regions.name: Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and Dubai South
regions.note: Newer schools where computer science may be taught by a teacher covering ICT and other subjects. This is the cluster where an external specification-matched tutor adds most, because subject-specific internal moderation is thinnest.

schoolClusters.city: Established Dubai British-curriculum schools
schoolClusters.note: Longer-running computer science provision with specialist teachers and laboratory access. Even here option cohorts are small, so families usually buy individual production practice and pseudocode marking rather than content teaching.

schoolClusters.city: Newer British-curriculum provision
schoolClusters.note: Growing option blocks where computer science may share a teacher with ICT or design technology. Smaller cohorts and less subject-specific moderation make an independent diagnostic more useful, particularly on the programming half.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with strong technology uptake
schoolClusters.note: Where computer science and ICT both run with substantial numbers. The two subjects are frequently confused by families at option time, and they assess very different things, which is worth settling before Year 10 begins.

dubai/igcse-computer-science-tutor.modesIntro: This subject needs three distinct kinds of session, and the most common failure of a tutoring plan here is running all three as a single weekly conversation about code.

modes.title: Production session: the student types
modes.description: Sixty minutes in a shared editor with the student at the keyboard throughout. A written specification is given, the student writes, the tutor comments on what appears and does not type. Where the student stops, that point is recorded. The code is saved with its date and the next session can open it rather than describe it.
bullets: 60 minutes, live video, student at the keyboard for the whole session
Specification given in writing; no model code visible
The stopping point recorded, because each one has a different fix
Code saved and dated, so last week's attempt is openable

modes.title: Trace and pseudocode block
modes.description: Four to six sessions on trace tables and pseudocode conventions. Trace accuracy is measured: a nested loop traced correctly, a counter and accumulator tracked together, an off-by-one error located rather than guessed at. Pseudocode is then marked against the published conventions rather than only for logic.
bullets: Four to six sessions with a stated end rather than open-ended
Trace accuracy scored on progressively harder algorithms
Pseudocode marked for convention compliance as well as logic
Test data chosen deliberately: normal, boundary and erroneous

modes.title: Theory question sets with a tested list
modes.description: The written half handled as a dated topic list with scored timed question sets rather than as explanation. Data representation arithmetic is drilled separately because it is pure practice. The terminology for software, networks and security is tested in writing, which the student can run alone.
bullets: Dated topic list with a score from a timed set, not a feeling
Binary and hexadecimal arithmetic drilled in short frequent bursts
Terminology tested in writing, runnable by the student at no cost
Mechanism required in security answers, not just a threat named

sections.heading: The trace table as a diagnostic, not just a question type
paragraphs: Trace tables appear on the examination in their own right, and they are also the fastest way to find out whether a student understands control flow. The method is to hand over a short algorithm and ask for a table: one column per variable, one row per iteration, every value written down. No code is run and no machine is needed. The accuracy of the result is informative in a way that almost nothing else in this subject is.

The levels of failure are distinct and each points somewhere. A student who cannot trace a single loop does not yet hold the idea that a variable persists between iterations. A student who traces a single loop and loses a nested one has not internalised that the inner loop completes for each outer iteration. A student who traces correctly until a counter and an accumulator change in the same iteration is making a sequencing error rather than a conceptual one. Those three need different sessions and different numbers of them.

The reason this matters so much is that trace ability predicts production ability closely. A student who cannot trace cannot debug, because debugging is tracing applied to code that is already wrong. They also cannot plan, because planning a loop requires imagining its state over time. Most of the programming marks on an IGCSE paper depend on that one capacity, and most revision addresses it by demonstrating more code, which does not build it.

The record tracks trace accuracy on progressively harder algorithms with a date against each. It is a small number of entries and it is the single most predictive page in a computer science file. When trace accuracy is secure, production improves without anything else changing, which is the clearest sign that the diagnosis was right.

sections.heading: The production gap, and the point where students stop
paragraphs: The second diagnostic is production from a written specification. Three or four sentences describing what a program must do, twenty minutes, no model code visible, and the student at the keyboard. What matters is not whether it works but where they stopped, because the stopping points are few and each one has a short, specific repair.

Some students stop before anything is typed, because they do not have a routine for turning a description into a structure. The repair is a decomposition habit: write the inputs, the outputs and the processing steps as three short lists before coding. Some stop at variable declaration, which is usually the residue of a block-based background where declaration never existed. Some write a correct structure and stall at validation, because validating input requires a loop that most demonstrations skip.

Some produce code that runs and does the wrong thing, which is the best failure of the five, because it means production is intact and the problem is interpretation of the specification. And some write code that is correct and in a notation the mark scheme will not credit, which is a convention problem rather than a programming one and takes about two sessions.

Recording the stopping point each week turns this into a visible sequence. A student who stopped before typing in week one, at validation in week four and nowhere in week eight has made measurable progress through a known ladder. A student stuck at the same point for six weeks tells you the method needs changing rather than repeating, which is a conversation worth having on evidence.
bullets: Written specification, twenty minutes, student at the keyboard
What is recorded is the stopping point, not the mark
