dubai/igcse-february-march-exam-preparat.programmesIntro: Where a student is in the sequence changes what a preparation plan can achieve, and families arriving from an Indian school are frequently placed by age rather than by syllabus coverage. These are the three stages that matter.

programmes.name: The year before IGCSE
programmes.description: The cheapest year to fix anything. Algebra fluency, scientific vocabulary and the habit of writing method out in full are built here, and all three are assumed rather than taught by the IGCSE papers. A student arriving from an Indian school mid-Year 9 usually has strong computation and no experience of a published mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools confirm IGCSE option choices during Year 9, so a term of support here informs a decision as well as a grade. Triple science without the algebra to carry physics is the predictable version of this going wrong, eighteen months later and much more expensively.

programmes.name: IGCSE first year
programmes.description: Half the syllabus is untaught, so topic questions marked to the published scheme are the right work and whole papers are not. This is where the evidence habit should start: a marked question set every week, with the raw mark recorded, so that by the examination year the student already knows what the scheme pays for.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions for Cambridge Core and Extended, or Pearson Foundation and Higher, are usually confirmed in or at the end of Year 10. A marked paper of the correct tier is better evidence for that conversation than a class test, and it is the kind of thing a school will genuinely look at.

programmes.name: IGCSE examination year
programmes.description: Whole papers under timing, marked and reworked, with the practical or alternative-to-practical component drilled separately. The constraint is eight or nine subjects in one week, so the paper cycle has to be allocated to the two subjects where marks are most recoverable rather than spread across everything.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE candidate in this year enters the June series, with November as the resit route. Mock examinations in Dubai schools usually fall in the second term, and Ramadan currently sits across the February-and-March part of the academic year, shortening school hours for several weeks.

dubai/igcse-february-march-exam-preparat.subjectsIntro: The grid below names, for each subject, the piece of evidence that shows whether preparation is working. That is a more useful thing to know than a content summary a student already has from school.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The evidence is a marked paper with the method visible. A student who begins writing the route to the answer usually gains across every paper, and the same question re-marked a fortnight later with the method written shows the movement directly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The evidence is a results table and a graph marked against the scheme's conventions, plus a question on sources of error. On Cambridge codes the alternative-to-practical component needs no laboratory and produces the clearest week-by-week improvement of anything in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The evidence is a marked calculation with the steps shown and an equation with state symbols included. Students arriving from an Indian school often have excellent computation and have never been asked to annotate conditions and reagents for marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The evidence is a data-based question marked against the accepted wording. This is the subject where a student can self-mark honestly once shown how, which makes a monthly audit the sensible purchase rather than a weekly block.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: The evidence is two versions of the same directed writing task a fortnight apart, with the scheme beside both. Structural improvement in audience, form and purpose is visible between drafts in a way that reading model answers never shows.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with comprehension and functional writing. Confirm which one is on the entry form first, because this is one of the commonest mismatches in Dubai households and it costs a grade.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Frequently taken by students heading for mathematics-heavy A-Levels or Higher Level IB. Tutor coverage is thinner here than in core mathematics, so the evidence to ask for early is a marked paper rather than a reassuring conversation.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: The evidence is an extended answer that names the firm or economy in the stem and ends with a judgement. Both are patterns, and four marked questions a fortnight apart make the change visible on the page.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: The evidence is a source question marked on structure and a case study answer containing place names and figures. Structure improves quickly with marking; content is a memory task the student can carry alone.

dubai/igcse-february-march-exam-preparat.regionsIntro: This search comes disproportionately from the parts of Dubai with the largest Indian-curriculum communities and the most movement between schools. These notes cover what that means for scheduling and for getting the entry details right.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense, established Indian and British school provision, with households that frequently contain children on different boards. Labelling practice material by syllabus code from the start saves a surprising amount of wasted work here.

regions.name: Karama, Oud Metha and Bur Dubai
regions.note: Older central communities near several long-established schools. Many families here have moved between Indian and British curricula within the same household, which makes the entry-form check the first task rather than a formality.

regions.name: International City and Silicon Oasis
regions.note: High turnover and many mid-year arrivals, which is precisely the group most likely to be working from the wrong country's examination calendar. One session confirming board, code, tier and series pays for itself immediately.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long eastern commutes and large year groups. Weekday sessions finish tired, so the weekly marked artefact is better produced from a weekend block than from a 20:00 weekday hour.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Apartment communities with a steady flow of new arrivals from India and elsewhere. Students here are often placed by age on arrival, which can leave a genuine syllabus gap that no amount of technique work addresses.

regions.name: Deira and Hor Al Anz
regions.note: Several long-standing schools within a short radius and a strong tuition-centre presence. The useful question to ask any local provider is the same one as anywhere: price per student per hour, and whether work is marked individually.

sections.heading: The series question, settled
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The additional sitting that generates this search is offered by Cambridge to candidates in India only, so it is not a route available to a candidate entered through a centre in the UAE. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in a May/June window and a November window.

The practical consequence is a planning one. A family building a revision calendar around dates that belong to India will aim at a sitting their child cannot enter, and will discover the mismatch at the point when the correct entry deadline has already closed. Entry deadlines are administered by the exam centre, usually the school, and fall months before the papers, so the cost of this particular error is a full series rather than a few weeks.

Cambridge adds a second detail that no competitor in this market mentions. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and the board states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. For a family already working from the wrong country's calendar, checking the live official timetable for the centre's own zone is the obvious next step.

sections.heading: Why this search happens in Dubai, and why it is nobody's mistake
paragraphs: Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with Indian programmes accounting for 26 per cent of students and UK programmes 37 per cent. Those two figures explain most of this search. A very large Indian-curriculum community sits alongside a very large British-curriculum one, families move between the two, and a household can easily contain a student on CBSE and a sibling on Cambridge IGCSE.

Search results compound it. Indian tutoring and revision sites produce a great deal of content about the additional sitting that Cambridge offers in India, that content ranks in UAE results, and nothing on the page says which country it is written for. A parent reading it has no way to know, and the sites themselves have no incentive to clarify. This page is the correction, written where the search actually happens.

Movement between the two countries is the third factor. A family that relocated from India in the last year or two carries that examination calendar in memory, and the memory is correct for where they were. Teachers who moved with them sometimes carry it too. None of this is carelessness; it is a reasonable assumption that happens to be wrong on one specific and consequential point.

The useful response is a short checklist rather than an explanation. Find the entry form. Read the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series from it. Ask the school's exams officer for the centre's zone and its own entry deadline. Then plan. Those four facts take ten minutes to gather and they settle every scheduling question that follows.

sections.heading: The calendar that does apply, counted backwards
paragraphs: With the series settled, the plan becomes straightforward and can be counted backwards in blocks rather than dates, so it stays true from year to year. The entry closes months before the papers at the centre's own deadline. Mock examinations in most Dubai schools fall in the second term. The practical or alternative-to-practical component should be drilled six to eight weeks out, because it is narrow and fast. Whole-paper rehearsal belongs in the final four to six weeks.

Results are the fixed point at the other end, and here real dates can be given with a source. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those published dates are the honest basis for planning a resit route, because they show the lag.

One Dubai-specific collision belongs in the plan. Ramadan currently falls across the February-and-March part of the UAE academic year and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, shortening school hours and changing household routines for several weeks. That period overlaps the mock window in many schools. The practical adjustments are to place timed papers on weekend mornings, hold the weekly slot after Iftar for families who are fasting, and front-load content-heavy work.

sections.heading: The evidence method, week by week
paragraphs: A parent who does not teach the subject can still audit preparation, provided the right things are produced. The test is whether something exists at the end of each week that did not exist at the start, and whether you can look at it without an explanation. A marked script with the scheme beside it. A raw mark with the paper reference, the tier and the date. A topic list with two items crossed off. An error log with a category cleared.

The error log is the part most families have never been shown, and it is the cheapest tool in the whole plan. Four columns: paper reference, question number, category of loss, and the fix. The four categories are content not known, command term misread, method not shown, and time ran out. After three marked papers the log shows a pattern, and the pattern is almost always narrower than the student feared.

Grade movement is then measurable rather than asserted. Two comparable papers, same tier, same conditions, a month apart, with their raw marks written down. If the second is higher, something worked. If it is not, the method changes rather than the hours increasing. That single discipline removes almost every argument a family has about whether tutoring is helping, because the question stops being a matter of opinion.

sections.heading: Where marks go for students who arrived from an Indian curriculum
paragraphs: This group has a characteristic profile on a marked script, and recognising it saves weeks. Computation is usually strong, often stronger than the local average, and content knowledge is broad. What is missing is the mark scheme. A student taught to arrive at correct answers efficiently has frequently never been shown that the scheme pays for a visible route, which means a page of correct answers can score well below its apparent quality.

The second characteristic loss is command terms. Indian board papers and Cambridge or Pearson papers use different question registers, and a student answering by instinct produces competent prose at the wrong depth: a full explanation where one exact point was wanted, or a description where a judgement was required. The published command term list fixes this quickly, and it transfers across every subject at once.

The third is the practical component, which is often entirely new. On Cambridge science codes the alternative-to-practical paper asks for results tables with units in the headings, instruments read to the correct precision, scales that fill the grid, lines of best fit, and specific sources of error. None of that is science knowledge and none of it appears in most students' prior experience, which makes it the single highest-return component for this group.

The fourth is genuine syllabus coverage, and it has to be separated from the three above. A student placed by age on arrival may be sitting a paper covering topics their previous school taught in a different year or not at all. That is a teaching problem rather than a technique problem, it takes longer, and it should be stated plainly in the first written note rather than discovered in April.

sections.heading: What a mid-year arrival needs to settle before buying any hours
paragraphs: Families arriving in Dubai partway through a course spend money in the wrong order more often than anyone else, and the fix costs nothing. Settle five things first. Which board and syllabus code the new school has entered or will enter the student for. Which tier. Which series, which for a UAE candidate means June or November. The centre's own entry deadline. And whether the specification has a coursework or practical component that requires anything beyond written preparation.

The fifth of those is the one that catches people. A science specification assessed by a practical test needs laboratory access that the centre must provide, while one assessed by a written alternative can be prepared for entirely at a desk. A student who transferred late may also have missed a coursework window that their previous school had not reached, which is a question for the new school rather than for a tutor.

Only then does the academic diagnosis make sense, and it should be a single marked paper of the correct specification rather than a conversation. That paper tells you, in one sitting, which of the four loss types is dominant: mark scheme technique, command terms, the practical component, or genuine coverage gaps. The first three are weeks of work. The fourth is terms, and it needs to be known early enough to consider the November route rather than entering June regardless.

Consider that option seriously rather than dismissing it. For a student who arrived with half a syllabus untaught, a November entry buys several extra months of teaching and produces a confirmed grade in the middle of January. For some progression routes that is unacceptable and the question is closed; for others it is simply a later date. It deserves arithmetic rather than reflex.

sections.heading: Honest limits, and what to refuse
paragraphs: Refuse any calendar that cannot name the series your child is entered for. That is the error this page exists to correct, and it is produced by copying content written for another country. A provider who cannot tell you, in writing, which series and which zone timetable applies has not looked at your child's entry form and is planning from a template.

Refuse any offer to supply past papers and mark schemes as downloads. Those documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson. The risk to your child is practical rather than legal: privately circulated copies are frequently from superseded specifications or retyped with errors, so a student learns the wrong accepted wording and calibrates against the wrong standard.

Refuse any offer to write, complete or finish coursework in subjects that carry it. A tutor may explain a criterion, question a method, narrow a question and comment on a draft by naming the criterion and the band. A tutor may not produce the work. The consequence of breaching that falls on the student, not on whoever was paid, and in this market there are sites selling exactly that service.

Finally, treat any outcome statistic with suspicion, including on this page, where there are none. No success rate, average grade or satisfaction figure appears here because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method. No tutor can promise a grade on an externally marked paper. What can be produced is a record: marked scripts with raw marks and dates, a topic list that shortens, an error log that narrows, and two comparable papers showing movement or not showing it.

process.title: Find the entry form and read four facts off it
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and series, for every subject. Then ask the exams officer for the centre's administrative zone and its own entry deadline. For a family who arrived at this page from Indian-curriculum content, these ten minutes are the most valuable part of the whole process.

process.title: Sit one paper of the exact specification
process.description: Correct board, code, tier and where possible variant, sat under full timing in one go with no notes, then self-marked against the published scheme before anyone else sees it. That self-marking is where a student first meets what the scheme actually pays for, which is usually the central discovery.

process.title: A free trial lesson on that script
process.description: A real session with the tutor who would continue, no card details taken beforehand, spent on the student's own marked paper. It ends with the losses classified into the four categories and a written note naming which are weeks of work and which are terms.

process.title: Start the weekly record
process.description: Each week produces a marked artefact with a raw mark and a date, plus an updated topic list and error log. Keep them in one folder. The folder is the product: it is what makes the difference between a productive month and a busy one visible rather than contested.

process.title: Compare monthly, change the method if nothing moved
process.description: Once a month, two comparable papers sat under the same conditions have their raw marks put side by side and the topic list is counted. If neither has moved, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing. That rule is what keeps a plan honest over a whole year.

whyPoints.title: We tell you the series is wrong before selling you anything
whyPoints.description: Cambridge offers the February and March sitting to India only, and saying so costs us the easy version of this sale. A plan aimed at a series your child cannot enter is worse than no plan, because it consumes the window that was available.

whyPoints.title: The record is the product
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with raw marks, tiers and dates, a topic list that shortens, an error log that narrows, and bracketed before-and-after attempts on component blocks. All readable by a parent who does not teach the subject, which is the point of keeping it.

whyPoints.title: Built for the profile this search actually comes from
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from an Indian curriculum typically have strong computation, broad content and no exposure to a published mark scheme or a practical component. Naming that profile honestly in the first session is faster than discovering it over a term.

whyPoints.title: Coverage gaps separated from technique gaps
whyPoints.description: Three of the four common loss types are weeks of work; genuine syllabus coverage is terms. Stating which you are dealing with in writing allows a family to consider the November route rather than entering June and resitting anyway.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure elsewhere on this site is attributed to the provider that published it, no entry fee is quoted because none could be sourced, and no success rate or average grade appears here because neither could be produced with a sample size and a method.

faqs.question: Is there a February or March IGCSE series available in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and offers the additional February and March sitting to candidates in India only. A candidate entered through a centre in the UAE therefore sits June, with November available as a second route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs a May/June window and a November window. Cambridge also runs Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which are a different thing from an IGCSE series and are entered by the school rather than by a family.

faqs.question: Why do my search results show a series that does not apply to us?
faqs.answer: Because a great deal of IGCSE revision content is written for Indian parents and ranks in UAE search results without saying which country it was written for. Dubai has a large Indian-curriculum community, with Indian programmes accounting for 26 per cent of private school students against 37 per cent on UK programmes, so both examination calendars circulate locally. Families who relocated recently also carry the Indian calendar in memory, where it was correct. The fix is to read the series from your child's own entry form rather than from any website.

faqs.question: Which series should a Dubai candidate actually be entered for?
faqs.answer: The June series for Cambridge, or the May/June window for Pearson, with November as the second route in both cases. The entry is submitted by the exam centre, usually the school, at the centre's own deadline, which falls months before the papers and earlier than the board's published date. Cambridge candidates should also establish which of the six administrative zones the centre sits in, because each zone has its own timetable version and the board states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who uses the wrong one.

faqs.question: My child sat Cambridge exams in India. Can they continue the same pattern here?
faqs.answer: The qualification continues, but the series pattern changes with the centre. A candidate now entered through a UAE centre sits the June series, with November available, and cannot be entered for the sitting Cambridge offers in India only. Carried-forward results, cashing in and subject combinations are administered by the centre, so the new school's exams officer is the right person to confirm what transfers. Do that before planning anything, because the answer determines which deadline you are working to.

faqs.question: We are moving to India mid-course. Does the series change for us?
faqs.answer: Potentially, and it is a question for the receiving school rather than for a tutoring page, because the entry is made by whichever centre the candidate is registered at. What is worth knowing in advance is that the sitting pattern available to a candidate depends on the centre's country, so a relocation can change the dates your plan is aimed at. Ask the new school's exams officer which series it will enter the candidate for and what its internal deadline is, in writing, before the move if possible.

faqs.question: What evidence should I see after only two weeks of preparation?
faqs.answer: Two marked artefacts with dates. In practice that usually means one whole paper or component sat under timing with a raw mark, a tier and a paper reference recorded, plus one marked question set. You should also have a written note classifying the lost marks into content not known, command term misread, method not shown and time ran out, and a topic list in priority order. Two weeks is too early for movement and not too early for a diagnosis, and the diagnosis is what the first fortnight is for.

faqs.question: How do we measure grade movement rather than guess at it?
faqs.answer: Two comparable papers, same board, same tier, same conditions, a month apart, with their raw marks written down beside each other. That is the whole method and it removes almost every argument a family has about whether tutoring is working. Supplement it with a topic list that should be shorter each month and an error log that should be narrowing rather than growing. If the second raw mark has not moved, the response is to change the method rather than to add hours at the same rate.

faqs.question: Is it worth marking papers when the examination is still months away?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one adjustment: early in the course, mark topic questions rather than whole papers. Half the syllabus is untaught in the first IGCSE year, so a whole paper mostly measures the gap, whereas a marked question set on taught content teaches the student what the scheme pays for. That habit is what makes the examination year cheaper, because a student who already writes method and reads command terms arrives needing pacing practice rather than a rebuild.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Dubai for this preparation?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For this audience there is a particular benefit beyond cost: families who move between India and the UAE, in either direction, keep the same tutor through the move. Marked scripts, raw marks and the error log stay in one place rather than being abandoned with a local arrangement, which matters more than any single session does.

faqs.question: What does a preparation block cost in Dubai, and what should it include?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist per Bestimate's 2026 rate table. Those are the providers' figures rather than ours. Whatever the rate, insist on three things in writing: whether setting and marking work between sessions is included, the number of sessions, and the end date.

faqs.question: My child's subject has a coursework component. Can a tutor help with the draft?
faqs.answer: Within a stated limit. A tutor can explain what an assessment criterion is asking for, question a method, narrow a research question and comment on a draft by naming the criterion, the band it currently sits in and what the band above requires. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The work has to be the student's own, the consequence of breaching that falls on the student rather than on whoever was paid, and written comments left in the student's own file are the honest record of what help was given.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss the entry deadline for the next series?
faqs.answer: The next opportunity is the following series, which for a Cambridge candidate means waiting from June to November or from November to June. The deadline that binds is the centre's own, not the board's published date, because the centre has to collate and submit entries. That is why the first task on this page is to ask the exams officer for the centre's internal deadline in writing. A missed deadline is the one failure in this process that no amount of preparation can repair.

faqs.question: Could we enter as a private candidate in India instead?
faqs.answer: A candidate's available sittings follow the centre they are registered at, so entering through a centre in another country is an administrative question for that centre rather than a tutoring one. Before considering it, weigh the practical costs: travel for each paper, a practical component that may need laboratory access at that centre, results released through a route you are not in daily contact with, and deadlines set by a centre you cannot visit. For most Dubai families the June series locally is the simpler and cheaper plan.

faqs.question: How long does it take to see movement on marked papers?
faqs.answer: Habit losses move fastest. Writing method, matching command terms, including units and significant figures, and putting a judgement at the end of an extended answer typically show up on a second or third marked paper, so roughly three to six weeks with weekly marked work. Pacing takes three full timed papers, because the student has to learn what six minutes of writing feels like. Genuine content gaps take terms, not weeks, and a plan that conflates the two will disappoint on a schedule nobody stated.

faqs.question: Which three things should a Dubai family turn down flat when buying IGCSE help?
faqs.answer: Three things. A calendar that cannot name the series and zone timetable your child is entered for, since that is the error this page exists to correct. An offer to supply past papers and mark schemes as downloads, because they belong to the boards and private copies are often from superseded specifications or retyped with errors. And any offer to write or finish coursework, which transfers the risk entirely to your child. Insist instead on session length, marking inclusion, session count, end date, and what the block will not reach.

dubai/igcse-february-march-exam-preparat.closingHeading: Read four facts off the entry form, then start the record
dubai/igcse-february-march-exam-preparat.closingBody: The series question is the one that brought you here and it has a short answer: Cambridge offers that additional sitting to India only, and a candidate entered through a UAE centre sits June or November. So find the entry form, read the board, code, tier and series from it, and ask the exams officer for the centre's zone and its own deadline. Then have your child sit one paper of exactly that specification under timing and self-mark it. Book the free trial lesson and spend it on that script. From there, every week should leave a marked artefact with a raw mark and a date, and the folder you build is the only honest measure of whether this is working.

Each works to one named specification and reports a score against one named skill after every session, so a parent can see whether the listening track, the writing track or the speaking track is the one that needs the next month.

intro.heading: One grade, four unrelated problems
paragraphs: A French report card gives a Dubai parent one letter, and that letter is an average across four separately assessed skills that have almost nothing to do with one another. A student can read French comfortably and understand almost nothing spoken at examination pace. A student can speak fluently and write with two tenses and no accents. A student can have excellent vocabulary recall and lose marks across the writing paper for register. One grade conceals all of that, and so does one weekly conversation about French.

So this plan keeps four records. The listening track, scored on timed audio sets at examination pace. The reading track, scored on timed comprehension sets. The speaking track, scored on rehearsed and unrehearsed tasks against the published requirements. The writing track, scored and additionally annotated for tense range, register and accent accuracy. Each entry is dated. Four short lists are more informative than any amount of general discussion, and they take the same time to produce as the discussion would.

What the four tracks almost always reveal in Dubai students is an imbalance rather than a general weakness. The most common shape is strong reading, adequate writing, weak listening and an unrehearsed speaking component. That shape is unsurprising: reading and writing get homework, listening gets occasional classroom practice at a gentler pace than the examination uses, and speaking gets talked about rather than timed. The remedy follows directly from the shape, and it is usually cheaper than the family expected, because two of the four tracks improve on habits a student runs themselves rather than on hours anybody bills for. Diagnosing the shape is therefore worth more than any single session that follows it.

The second thing the tracks reveal is that vocabulary is a separate problem again and a cheap one. Topic-based vocabulary is a memorisation task with a determinate answer, which means it needs testing rather than teaching and can be run by the student with a good list. Paying a qualified hourly rate for someone to read vocabulary aloud is among the most common overspends in language tutoring, and it sits alongside the far more useful work that genuinely does need a tutor.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For French the format is an advantage: audio can be played and replayed with the transcript revealed afterwards, the speaking task can be recorded and played back so the student hears themselves, and every written piece is saved and dated. A Dubai family in Mirdif or Al Furjan also gets a tutor matched to the specification rather than to a driving radius.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 French, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Topic-based vocabulary, present tense and some past-tense work, usually assessed through short written tasks. programmes.description: Topic coverage, tense range and the beginning of examination-format work across all four skills. The right year to build listening at examination pace and to start the speaking component, because both improve slowly and both are the ones left latest.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's long December break is a useful listening window, because listening improves with daily short exposure rather than weekly sessions. Fifteen minutes a day of examination-pace audio across three weeks moves the listening track more than a term of fortnightly practice.

programmes.name: IGCSE French, Year 11
programmes.description: Remaining topics, the speaking examination, and technique across the written papers. The Year 11 priorities are speaking rehearsal under timed conditions and the writing checklist, because both are mechanical gains available late in the course.

dubai/igcse-french-tutor.subjectsIntro: French divides into four assessed skills plus a vocabulary load, and each needs different work at a different price. These are the units a Dubai plan is built from.

subjects.name: Listening
subjects.levels: A separately assessed component on both specifications
subjects.description: Comprehension of recorded French at examination pace, which is faster and less clearly enunciated than most classroom audio. The track that is weakest in most Dubai students and the one that responds to daily short exposure rather than to weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Reading
subjects.levels: A separately assessed component on both specifications
subjects.description: Comprehension of written texts across the specification's topics, with questions in French or English depending on the component. Usually the strongest track, because it is what homework has always practised, and therefore rarely where hours should go.

subjects.name: Speaking
subjects.levels: A separately assessed component on both specifications
subjects.description: Role play, a presentation or picture-based task, and conversation, conducted at the centre. The component most often discussed and least often rehearsed under timed conditions, which makes it the largest easy gain in the subject.

subjects.name: Writing
subjects.levels: A separately assessed component on both specifications
subjects.description: Short and extended writing to a specified purpose. Marks go to tense range, register and accuracy of accents and agreement as well as to content, which means a well-expressed piece in one tense scores below a plainer piece in three.

subjects.name: Tense range and verb accuracy
subjects.description: Present, perfect, imperfect, future and conditional, with the correct auxiliary and agreement. The single most reliable way to lift a writing or speaking mark, because the credit is explicitly for range and most students default to one tense under pressure.

subjects.name: Register and opinion language
subjects.description: Formal against informal address, and the ability to give and justify an opinion rather than state a fact. Students lose marks writing a correct informal message where a formal one was required, which is a checklist item rather than a language problem.

subjects.name: Topic vocabulary
subjects.description: The specification's topic areas, each with its own lexical set. A memorisation task with determinate answers, which means it needs written testing rather than teaching and can be handed to the student at no cost once the list is built.

subjects.name: Accents and written accuracy
subjects.description: Accents, agreement and spelling, which carry accuracy marks and are routinely lost by students who speak well. A mechanical problem with a mechanical fix: a proofreading routine applied to the student's own marked work.

subjects.name: Dictionary and inference strategy
subjects.description: Working out an unfamiliar word from context rather than stopping at it, and recognising cognates and word families. A technique that converts partial comprehension into marks and is almost never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Examination technique per component
subjects.description: Timing, question-reading and answer-format discipline, which differ by component. The speaking component in particular has a structure students can rehearse, and a student who has rehearsed it behaves differently in the room.

sections.heading: Four records, and what the usual shape tells you
paragraphs: The first week of a French plan produces four numbers rather than an impression. A timed listening set, scored. A timed reading set, scored. A speaking task performed under time against the published requirements, scored. A written piece marked for content and annotated separately for tense range, register and accuracy. Four numbers and a date. That page is more useful than any report card, because a report card averages the four and the average is what hides the problem.

The shape that recurs in Dubai students is strong reading, adequate writing, weak listening and an entirely unrehearsed speaking component. Each part of that has a cause. Reading is what homework has practised for five years. Writing is marked often enough to be moderately developed. Listening is practised in class at a pace gentler than the examination uses, because a teacher speaking to a class naturally enunciates. Speaking is discussed rather than timed, because timing it requires one-to-one attention a class cannot supply.

That shape has a specific and relatively cheap remedy, which is why diagnosing it matters more than it sounds. Reading needs almost no hours. Listening needs daily short exposure the student runs themselves. Speaking needs four to six rehearsal sessions with playback. Writing needs a checklist and marked pieces. The total paid hours are modest and they go to speaking and writing, which are the two tracks where a tutor is genuinely necessary.

The alternative shape appears less often and matters when it does: a student who speaks fluently, often from a French-speaking family background, and whose writing is limited to one tense with missing accents. That student needs the opposite plan, with almost all the hours on written accuracy and tense range and none on speaking. Buying the standard French package would have given them the hours they least needed.

sections.heading: The component map, and why the code matters
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE French as a Foreign Language 0520 assesses the four skills as four separate components, and that separation is the reason a four-track record works so cleanly for this specification. A student knows which paper each number refers to, and a weak component can be attacked directly without touching the other three.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE French 4FR1 distributes the skills differently across its components, and schools vary in how they handle the speaking element. The practical instruction is the same as in every other subject on this site and is skipped as often: email the school's exams officer for the specification code and the component structure for that code, then build the plan from the actual weightings rather than from an assumption about how language papers are arranged.

There is one logistical item specific to languages. The speaking component is conducted at the centre on a schedule the school sets rather than on a date the board publishes for the written papers, and it frequently falls weeks before the written examinations. A family planning speaking rehearsal backwards from the written series will plan it too late. Ask the exams officer for the speaking window as a separate question, because it is the one date in this subject most commonly missed.

The second logistical item is the vocabulary list the specification defines. Where a specification publishes topic areas and an associated lexical scope, the testing list should be built from that rather than from a textbook's selection, which will include material the paper will not use and omit material it will. Building the list from the specification is expert work done once; running the tests afterwards is not, and should not be billed as though it were.

sections.heading: Speaking: the component nobody rehearses
paragraphs: The speaking component is the largest easy gain in IGCSE French and it is the one most Dubai students arrive at having never performed under timed conditions. Classes prepare it collectively: topics are discussed, useful phrases are distributed, and students are reassured. Almost nobody sits in front of one other person with a clock running and performs the whole thing from start to finish before the day it counts.

Rehearsal changes the result for reasons that have little to do with language. A student who has performed a role play six times knows how long ninety seconds feels, knows not to stop when they cannot retrieve a word, and has a repertoire of recovery phrases that buy thinking time without silence. A student who has only discussed it freezes at the first gap, and the silence costs more than the missing word would have.

The playback is the part that produces the most change per session. Students do not know what they sound like: they do not hear their own hesitation, their own flat intonation on questions, or the moment they switched to English. Recording a task and playing it back is uncomfortable and effective, and it is far easier on a video platform than at a kitchen table, because the recording is already in the right place.

Three elements are worth drilling specifically. Opinion language with justification, because stating a fact where an opinion was wanted loses credit that was freely available. Recovery phrases for the moment of retrieval failure, so a gap becomes a pause rather than a stop. And tense range inside speech, because the credit for range applies here as it does in writing and most students speak entirely in the present under pressure.

sections.heading: Listening: the gap between classroom French and examination audio
paragraphs: Listening is the weakest track for most Dubai students and the reason is structural rather than personal. A teacher addressing a class speaks clearly, at a measured pace, with repetition and visual support. Examination audio is recorded at natural pace, often with more than one speaker, without visual context and with limited repetition. A student can follow every lesson and still score poorly, and when they do they conclude they are bad at French.

Listening improves with frequency and almost not at all with session length. Fifteen minutes a day for three weeks produces more movement than a ninety-minute weekly session for a term, because the skill is pattern recognition at speed and pattern recognition needs repeated short exposure. That makes listening the cheapest of the four tracks to fix properly, because the work is self-run once the method and the material are set.

The method matters. Listen first without the transcript and answer the questions. Then listen again. Only then read the transcript and identify which words were missed and why — unfamiliar vocabulary, a liaison that obscured a word boundary, or a known word spoken faster than it was ever heard in class. Checking the transcript during the first listen converts the exercise into a reading task and teaches nothing about listening.

Dubai supplies one practical advantage worth naming: long commutes. A student in Arabian Ranches or Dubai South spends a meaningful amount of time on a bus each day, and fifteen minutes of examination-pace audio each way costs no study time at all. The habit survives Ramadan, school events and examination weeks better than any scheduled session, which is precisely why it is the recommendation rather than a paid listening block.

sections.heading: Writing: the checklist that lifts the mark
paragraphs: Writing marks in IGCSE French are allocated to more than correctness. Content has to address the task, and language credit attaches to the range of structures used, the appropriateness of the register and the accuracy of accents, agreement and spelling. A fluent, error-free paragraph written entirely in the present tense scores below a plainer paragraph that uses three tenses correctly, which is counter-intuitive to students and entirely consistent once the criteria are read.

That makes the writing fix a checklist rather than a course. Before submitting a piece: have I used at least three tenses, is the register right for the audience the task named, have I given and justified an opinion, have I checked every accent, and have I checked agreement on adjectives and past participles. Five items, two minutes, and reliably worth marks. Students resist checklists and then adopt them once a marked piece shows two marks recovered by the accent check alone.

The marking has to support the checklist for it to stick. A piece returned with corrections shows the student what was wrong; a piece returned with a tense count, a register judgement and an accent error count shows them what to do differently next time. Those three numbers go in the writing record alongside the content mark, which is what makes the writing track a track rather than a sequence of corrected essays.

One further point specific to Dubai's multilingual classrooms. Students who speak French at home frequently write with excellent idiom and poor accuracy, because spoken French does not expose accents or written agreement. Their writing track needs accuracy work and no fluency work at all, and the standard French plan would give them the reverse. That is the clearest argument for diagnosing four tracks separately before buying anything.

sections.heading: Vocabulary: the half that should cost nothing
paragraphs: Topic vocabulary is a large part of the French load and it is a memorisation task with determinate answers. That puts it in the same category as data representation arithmetic in computer science or definitions in economics: it needs scheduling and testing rather than teaching, and it is the part of the subject a family should not be paying a qualified hourly rate for.

The work is built once and run many times. The list comes from the specification's topic areas rather than from a textbook's selection, because a textbook will include material the paper will not use and omit material it will, and building the list from the specification requires someone who has read it. After that the routine is written testing: twenty items in five minutes, scored, three times a week, with the gap list shortening visibly.

Written testing rather than verbal is the detail that makes it work. A student who recognises a French word when they hear it will not necessarily produce it in a writing task or recognise it at speed in audio, and production is what the paper examines. Scoring written tests also makes the vocabulary track countable, which is what lets it sit in the record beside the other four numbers.

The budget consequence is direct. A French plan that bills every vocabulary topic as taught time is charging the qualified band for administration. The honest version hands the list and the routine to the student, keeps the paid hours for speaking rehearsal and marked writing, and arrives at a smaller total. Published budget rates in this market start at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik if a family wants someone to administer the testing, which is the right tier for that task.

sections.heading: The six-week four-track cycle
paragraphs: Language skills move at different speeds, which argues for a measurement cycle short enough to catch the fast ones and long enough to show the slow ones. Six weeks works. Week one scores all four tracks plus vocabulary. Weeks two to five run the weighted weekly rotation with the daily listening habit and the vocabulary testing continuing underneath. Week six re-scores all four and places the pairs side by side.

What a six-week cycle typically shows is uneven movement, and that is useful rather than disappointing. Speaking usually moves fastest, because rehearsal addresses behaviour rather than knowledge. Listening moves steadily if the daily habit was actually done, and not at all if it was not, which makes it the honest measure of whether the self-run work happened. Writing moves in steps as checklist items become automatic. Reading barely moves, because it was already the strongest.

The cycle also decides what the next six weeks contain. A listening score that did not move means the habit was not run, which is a conversation about fifteen minutes a day rather than a reason to buy listening sessions. A speaking score that moved sharply means the rehearsal block can end. A writing score where the tense count rose and the accent errors did not fall means half the checklist landed and the other half needs enforcing.

Placement in the Dubai calendar is worth one note. Re-scoring in the second week of January rather than the week before the December break measures retention of a habit across three weeks away from school, which is the number that predicts examination performance. A listening score that holds in January is a skill; one that falls was recent practice, and the spring plan should be written accordingly.

sections.heading: What IGCSE French costs in Dubai, and the rules around it
paragraphs: Published rates read in October 2026: EdFlik lists online tuition from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate rate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

French allocates cleanly across those bands once the four tracks are diagnosed. Speaking rehearsal with playback and marked writing with tense, register and accent counts need someone who knows the published requirements, which is the qualified band at AED 150-300 for a bounded number of sessions. Vocabulary testing and the daily listening habit are administration and discipline, which belong with the student or at the budget tier. Reading usually needs nothing. A sequenced plan therefore has a modest qualified-band hour count.

The in-home comparison runs as it does across this market: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. For French the online format also does something a home visit cannot easily do: it records the speaking task and plays it back, which is the single most effective part of speaking preparation. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

Three things stated for the record, because language tuition attracts more unverifiable claims than most subjects. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, holds no such status and claims none, and runs no UAE office or centre; nobody here is presented as an authorised speaking examiner. The tutor teaching your child does need a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own service with a stated two-working-day completion time, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. And the French specifications, past papers and mark schemes referred to throughout are the property of Cambridge and Pearson; this page links them at source instead of reproducing them.

sections.heading: Dubai's school context and the French week
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually against six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, and seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake adding 16,846 places. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27.

For a language plan the most relevant feature of this landscape is how full the week already is. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising no such lesson falls below 25 minutes.

A Year 11 therefore carries eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus two or three mandatory UAE subjects, at least two of which are languages. Any French plan that assumes an hour of daily study has not looked at the timetable. The fifteen-minute daily listening habit is designed around that reality: it fits a bus journey, it survives a busy week, and it does not compete with written homework for a desk.

Two closing points of record. For the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, and teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai private schools must hold the relevant approval from KHDA for those subjects; neither point applies to French, and neither is a credential any tutoring provider holds. And a modern language does count toward the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route requires at no less than grade E or grade 3, unlike Arabic and Islamic education, which the ministry excludes from that count.

faqs.question: Why does my child get a middling IGCSE French grade with no clear reason?
faqs.answer: Because the grade averages four separately assessed skills that fail for unrelated reasons, and the average hides which one is responsible. A student can read French comfortably and understand almost nothing spoken at examination pace. Another can speak fluently and write with one tense and missing accents. The diagnostic is four scores in one week: a timed listening set, a timed reading set, a speaking task performed under time, and a written piece marked with separate counts for tense range, register and accuracy. Four numbers and a date say more than a term of reports.

faqs.question: Why is listening the weakest skill for most Dubai French students?
faqs.answer: Because classroom French and examination audio are different things. A teacher addressing a class speaks clearly at a measured pace with repetition and visual support; examination recordings run at natural pace, often with more than one speaker, without visual context and with limited repetition. A student can follow every lesson and still score poorly, then conclude they are bad at French. The gap is pattern recognition at speed, which is built by frequency rather than session length: fifteen minutes daily for three weeks beats a ninety-minute weekly session for a term.

faqs.question: How should a student practise IGCSE French listening?
faqs.answer: Fifteen minutes a day, with the transcript checked only afterwards. Listen first without it and answer the questions. Listen again. Then read the transcript and identify exactly which words were missed and why — unfamiliar vocabulary, a liaison that hid a word boundary, or a known word spoken faster than it was ever heard in class. Reading the transcript during the first listen turns the exercise into reading practice and teaches nothing about listening. Long Dubai bus commutes are the best available slot, because the habit then costs no study time at all.

faqs.question: Why does speaking rehearsal matter so much in IGCSE French?
faqs.answer: Because most students arrive having discussed the component and never performed it under time. Rehearsal changes the result for reasons that are only partly about language: a student who has performed a role play six times knows how long ninety seconds feels, knows not to stop when a word will not come, and has recovery phrases that buy thinking time without silence. A student who has only discussed it freezes at the first gap, and the silence costs more than the missing word would have. Four to six rehearsal sessions is usually the whole fix.

faqs.question: What does recording a French speaking task actually achieve?
faqs.answer: It shows the student what they sound like, which they do not know. Students cannot hear their own hesitation, their flat intonation on questions, the moment they switched into English, or how much of the task they delivered entirely in the present tense. Playback is uncomfortable and it is the single most effective element of speaking preparation, because it converts habits the student cannot perceive into things they can change. It is also considerably easier on a video platform than at a kitchen table, since the recording is already where it needs to be.

faqs.question: Why does a well-written French paragraph still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because language credit attaches to range and register as well as to correctness. A fluent, error-free paragraph written entirely in the present tense scores below a plainer paragraph that uses three tenses correctly and addresses the right audience. The fix is a five-item checklist applied before submitting: at least three tenses, register matched to the named audience, an opinion given and justified, every accent checked, and agreement checked on adjectives and past participles. Two minutes, reliably worth marks, and students adopt it once a marked piece shows marks recovered by the accent check alone.

faqs.question: My child speaks French at home but writes badly. What is the plan?
faqs.answer: The reverse of the standard one. Students from a French-speaking background usually have excellent idiom and spoken fluency and poor written accuracy, because speech does not expose accents or written agreement. Their writing track needs accuracy work and tense range, their speaking track needs almost nothing, and buying a standard French package would give them the hours they least need. This is the clearest single argument for scoring four tracks separately before any purchase, because the average grade conceals exactly this shape.

faqs.question: When is the IGCSE French speaking examination held in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is scheduled by the school rather than published with the written timetable, and it commonly falls weeks before the written papers. That makes it the one date in this subject most often missed by a family planning backwards from the written series. Ask the exams officer for the speaking window as a separate question at the start of Year 11. For the written components, Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates — the February/March series is offered to India only — and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: Should we pay a tutor to test French vocabulary?
faqs.answer: Only if nobody at home will do it. Topic vocabulary is a memorisation task with determinate answers, which means it needs scheduling and written testing rather than teaching. Building the list from the specification's topic areas is expert work done once, because a textbook selection will include material the paper will not use and omit material it will. Running twenty written items three times a week and scoring them is administration. Published budget rates in this market start at AED 33-65 an hour if someone is needed to administer it, which is the right tier for that task.

faqs.question: How many tenses does an IGCSE French student need to use?
faqs.answer: More than one, and that is the practical point rather than a precise number. Credit for language range means a student who writes and speaks only in the present tense caps their own mark regardless of accuracy. The useful working set is present, perfect, imperfect, future and conditional, with correct auxiliary choice and agreement on past participles. Under pressure almost all students default to the present, which is why the tense count belongs on the writing record as a number: a student who can see their count rise from one to three has something concrete to aim at.

faqs.question: Can a student start IGCSE French in Year 10 from nothing?
faqs.answer: It happens in Dubai because of mid-course transfers and language switching, and it is possible with a different plan rather than a compressed version of the normal one. A two-year course from a standing start means vocabulary acquisition becomes the dominant activity for the first year, speaking rehearsal starts later, and listening needs the daily habit from week one rather than from Year 11. Saying this plainly at the outset is more useful than optimism, because a student doing a five-year course in two years needs realistic targets and will otherwise conclude they are failing.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE French tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online provision at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik, a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, specialist work at AED 270 at TutorChase, and premium named listings at AED 650. For French the allocation is clean: speaking rehearsal and marked writing need the qualified band for a bounded number of sessions, while vocabulary testing and daily listening belong with the student or at the budget tier. Reading usually needs nothing at all.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for a speaking-based subject?
faqs.answer: For French it has a specific advantage. The speaking task can be recorded and played back inside the session, which is the most effective element of speaking preparation and awkward to arrange any other way. Audio for listening practice can be played, paused and replayed with the transcript revealed only afterwards, and every written piece is saved with its date so a term's tense counts are comparable. The published cost difference also runs one way: AED 180-350 for qualified in-home work against AED 150-300 online. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: Does French count toward UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: A modern language counts toward the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the ministry's published British-track route requires at no less than grade E or grade 3, unlike Arabic and Islamic education, which the ministry explicitly excludes from that count. The route also requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The process is the ministry's own, performed through official channels: no tutoring provider carries it out or guarantees it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Verify the current wording on the ministry's own pages.

faqs.question: What if no French specialist is available for our specification in Dubai?
faqs.answer: You should be told, with the options named. Language requests in this emirate concentrate in the weeks before the speaking component, which falls earlier than most families expect, and a tutor who has not taught the specification will not know its speaking structure or its vocabulary scope. The honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. All three beat conversation practice sold as examination preparation. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/igcse-french-tutor.closingHeading: Get four numbers before buying any hours
dubai/igcse-french-tutor.closingBody: One French grade cannot tell you what to buy. Four can. A timed listening set, a timed reading set, a speaking task performed under time, and a written piece marked with separate counts for tense range, register and accents will show you the shape of the problem in a single week. In most Dubai students that shape points to speaking rehearsal and marked writing as paid work, with listening and vocabulary handed back as daily habits. Email the school for the code and the speaking window, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and ask for all four scores in writing.

intro.heading: What families in Dubai are really asking for when they search for home tuition
paragraphs: The phrase "IGCSE home tuition in Dubai" gets typed into Google by a parent holding a school report. Something in it is wrong. Either a predicted grade slipped, or a mock paper came back with a mark that does not match the effort going in at the kitchen table. Home tuition is the word parents reach for because it means the opposite of a crowded classroom: one adult, one child, undivided attention. That instinct is correct. The delivery assumption behind it is the only part worth revisiting.

Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school pupils as of the 2024-25 year, with 37% of that enrolment following a UK curriculum. That makes IGCSE the single largest qualification cohort in the emirate at age 16. It also means the tutoring market here is deep but uneven. There are plenty of people who will teach maths. There are far fewer who can tell you that your child is losing four marks a paper on 0580 Paper 4 because they are rounding mid-calculation rather than at the end, and then show you the three questions where it happened.

That is the difference this page is built around. IGCSE is not a general knowledge test. It is a tightly specified syllabus with numbered papers, published assessment objectives, and command words that mean exact things. "State" wants one line. "Explain" wants a mechanism. "Suggest" wants a plausible answer the examiner has never seen before, marked on reasoning rather than recall. A tutor who does not teach that distinction explicitly is leaving marks on the table every single paper, no matter how well they know the content.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition as one-to-one live video lessons. We do not send a tutor to a Dubai address, and home visits in Dubai are not a service we sell anywhere in the UAE. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation. A family in Mirdif searching for a Cambridge Chemistry 0620 specialist is choosing from everyone we work with, not from whoever happens to be a 25-minute drive away at 5pm on a Tuesday. In a city where the school run and the evening traffic between Al Barsha and Dubai Silicon Oasis can eat 40 minutes each way, that pool difference is the whole decision.

What follows is the detail a parent actually needs before spending money: how the grading scales work and why your child's report may carry two of them, how the Core and Extended decision caps the grade before a single paper is sat, where marks go subject by subject, what the Dubai market charges in dirhams, how the exam calendar runs backwards from the paper to the entry deadline, and what the mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside IGCSE require. Every figure is attributed. Nothing here is a promise about a grade.
