faqs.question: How do I know whether an IGCSE tutor is actually working?
faqs.answer: Compare a measurement with an earlier measurement of the same thing. Before any teaching, record a timed past-paper component marked question by question, how much of the paper was left unfinished, and how many questions were answered at the wrong command word. At six weeks, repeat the same component and mark it identically. The difference is a fact. Without that baseline the question cannot be answered at all, which is why so many Dubai families reach half term having spent real money and learned nothing about whether it helped.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's Dubai school for before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: The marked scripts, not the grades, and a written list of subject, awarding organisation, syllabus code and tier. Schools here generally release marked papers on request and most families never ask, which means the richest evidence available sits in a cupboard. Put the scripts in front of anyone you are considering hiring and watch what they do with them. A specialist reads them for pattern and names two or three components within ten minutes. Somebody who talks about attitude instead has told you something useful about themselves.

faqs.question: How much can an IGCSE grade realistically move in one term?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on how far below a boundary the student currently sits, which is why marks are the honest unit and grades are not. A student a handful of marks short, losing those marks to pace or command-word errors, can move within a few weeks because those are training problems. A student fifteen or twenty marks short with losses spread across topics is looking at content work over a longer period. Nobody can promise a grade, because boundaries are set by the awarding organisation after each series and move between series.

faqs.question: What does my child's mock grade actually predict?
faqs.answer: Less than it appears to. Schools must mark mocks against some boundary, usually a previous year's, and boundaries move between live series, so the grade is a function of that choice as much as of the script. Read the marks instead. Also read across the whole mock set, because nine papers produced in one fortnight is the only chance in the year to see whether a problem is global or subject-specific. And remember a mock usually falls before any real revision period, so it is a diagnostic snapshot rather than a forecast.

faqs.question: My child says the sessions are going well but the marks have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat that as information rather than as a contradiction. It usually means the sessions are addressing something other than what the marks are losing, which is a targeting problem rather than a teaching one. Go back to the baseline, check which items were ranked top, and ask the tutor which item the last four sessions were on and how many marks it was worth. If the answer is general revision, the plan was never targeted. Changing the target component is cheaper and faster than changing the tutor, and should be tried first.

faqs.question: Is unmarked practice worth anything at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Very little, and sometimes less than nothing. A student who completes a past paper without marking it against the published scheme has rehearsed whatever they already do, including the errors, and has reinforced them. Worse, they have used up a paper that could have produced a measurement. Marking is the part that converts practice into information: it identifies which components lost marks and which error types produced the loss. If a budget is tight, fewer papers properly marked beats more papers done and filed.

faqs.question: Which single fix usually recovers the most IGCSE marks?
faqs.answer: Command-word reading, in most cases, because it costs marks in every subject at once. A student who answers describe when the question says explain, or explain when it says evaluate, loses a few marks per paper across eight or nine papers, and the fix is three to five sessions bought once and used everywhere. Pace is the other strong candidate where a paper is unfinished, since the marks left blank at the end are often the largest single block available. Both are training rather than teaching, which is why they are fast.

faqs.question: Should we fix the subject my child is most worried about?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and usually not first. Rank the repairs by marks available divided by time needed, and weight technique items because they transfer across the whole timetable. On that ordering the subject producing the most distress at home frequently comes fourth, and the top item is often something nobody had noticed, like an unfinished paper or a pattern of poor question selection. Fix the distress eventually, because it matters, but fix the cheap marks first. That is also the fastest way to change how a student feels about the subject.

faqs.question: How often should a tutor send a written update?
faqs.answer: Every session, and one line is enough: the component worked on, what the student produced, and what to attempt before next time, with the marked work attached. A monthly report written in general language is worse than nothing, because it looks like evidence and contains none. The test to apply is whether a stranger could read the sequence of notes and say what changed. If the notes describe effort and attitude rather than components and marks, they are not an audit trail and the plan cannot be judged from them.

faqs.question: Does a strong KHDA inspection rating mean my child is doing well?
faqs.answer: No. Dubai private schools are inspected on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the report describes the school's provision, leadership and cohort outcomes. It says nothing about one student's marks in one subject. Families conflate the two constantly, and a strong band is genuinely reassuring about something it does not measure. The documents that describe your child are the report, which summarises, and the marked scripts, which diagnose. Only the second one will tell you where the marks went.

faqs.question: What evidence should exist by the time we reach the mock series?
faqs.answer: A dated baseline from before the first session, a sequence of weekly marked pieces, and one repeat of the baseline component at around six weeks marked identically to the first. If all three exist you can read the mock as the fourth data point in a series rather than as a verdict out of nowhere. If none exists, the mock becomes the baseline by default, which works but costs you a term of information you could have had for the price of one hour in September.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a non-examined component without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be visible in the record. A tutor can teach the skills the component assesses, discuss the requirements, question the student's choices and give feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor must not supply content that ends up in the submission. The work has to be the student's own, and a provider offering otherwise is offering the student a malpractice finding rather than a grade. Our session records keep the student's words and the tutor's feedback separate so the boundary can be checked rather than taken on trust.

faqs.question: What should make me suspicious of a Dubai tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Three things. A promised grade or money back tied to a result, which cannot be delivered because boundaries are set after each series. A statistic without its sample size, period and method on the same page, which several providers in this market publish and none can substantiate. And any implication of KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, which no tutoring provider acquires by operating. What can be evidenced is a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, valid for two years, and therefore reasonable to ask to see.

faqs.question: Can a parent in the next room tell whether teaching is any good?
faqs.answer: They can tell whether it is pleasant, which is a weak predictor of marks moving. What is actually checkable is the artefact: a timed question marked against the published scheme, dated, with the marks visible. That can be audited by anyone at any time, and it does not depend on where the tutor was sitting. The in-home format does have one real advantage here, which is that an adult in the room can notice a phone or close a door, and an online session cannot. The study space has to be set up once instead.

faqs.question: Why is the lesson online when I searched for a home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because that is the phrase parents use, and we would rather answer it plainly than let you find out after an enquiry. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we provide only in India, and we run no in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE. Every session is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The published in-home market rate in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside it; the online qualified-teacher band runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300. intro.heading: One number, six things inside it
paragraphs: A tuition quote in Dubai arrives as a single hourly figure, which is why comparing two of them is so unreliable. AED 200 from one provider and AED 320 from another may be the same teaching with different marking attached, or entirely different teaching with the same marking, or one with a cancellation policy that costs you a session a month and one without. The hourly rate is a summary of at least six decisions, and the only way to compare quotes is to ask what each decision was.

The six are teaching time, travel, marking between sessions, reporting to parents, materials, and the terms around cancellation and commitment. For a visiting tutor, travel is often the largest hidden share: a journey across Dubai in the afternoon peak can be most of an hour each way, and somebody pays for it. For an online tutor the travel line disappears, which is a large part of why the published online bands sit below the published in-home ones in this market.

The published figures are worth setting out plainly, because three of the six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all and two of the ones that do quote US dollars. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors ranging to AED 500, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tier. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market rates, attributed to whoever published them. They are not IB Gram's price list, and this page does not publish one, because an hourly figure that ignores the subject, the tier and the series is the kind of number that has to be revised in a phone call anyway. What IB Gram does publish is the delivery model: tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India.

That is stated at the top rather than buried, because this page is about fees and the honest version of the comparison is part of the fee discussion. The in-home market in Dubai is real, it charges what it charges for good reasons, and a family that wants a person in the room has a legitimate preference. What this page does is show you exactly which lines of the bill exist because of that preference, so the choice is made on arithmetic rather than on a provider's sales pitch.

programmes.description: Mid-band rates, and the stage where weekly work costs least per grade moved, because the tutor is fixing this week's lesson rather than rebuilding a year. The tier decision also sits here, and an evidenced opinion on Core versus Extended is worth several sessions on its own if it changes the entry.
programmes.countryNote: Because Dubai entries are submitted months ahead of the papers, Year 10 is when a fee spent on diagnosis changes the outcome rather than merely improving it. A family that establishes in October that Extended is reachable has a different two years ahead of them than one that discovers it in March, and the hours required are substantially fewer.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: The most expensive hours, for two reasons that have nothing to do with teaching quality. Demand peaks from January into the summer series, and the tutors who know a specific paper's mark distribution are scarce at exactly that moment. Specialist and exam-year rates in this market run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres enter candidates across Cambridge's March, June and November series and Pearson's May/June and November series, so the demand peak is not one season but two or three overlapping ones. Booking a named specialist in September for a May series costs less and gets a better match than booking the same person in March, which is the single largest saving available in the exam year.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: Priced at the scarce end, because the work includes sequencing that a school would normally do and because few tutors handle private-candidate logistics. Entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the examination centre rather than to a tutor, and that amount is set by the centre, so it must be confirmed with the centre directly.
programmes.countryNote: A resit decision in Dubai is partly a calendar decision. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series here, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a student who misses a grade in the summer can often sit again in the autumn rather than waiting a full year. Entry deadlines sit months ahead: Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry for it had to be in long before that, which is why the resit conversation belongs in August.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Subject is the biggest single driver of an IGCSE tuition quote in Dubai, and it is driven by scarcity rather than difficulty. These are the subjects families ask about, with what moves the fee in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The deepest tutor pool in Dubai and therefore the most competitive rates. Expect the middle of the qualified band for Extended and the lower end for Core. The fee rises in the exam term because demand does, not because the teaching changes.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Scarce, and priced accordingly near the top of the specialist band. Few tutors who teach 0580 also teach 0606 properly, and the honest question is not what it costs but whether anyone available teaches it at a workable hour.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Upper-middle of the qualified band. A tutor who has marked the practical paper's answers charges more than one who has taught only theory, and for a Year 11 candidate that difference is usually worth paying because the practical losses are patterned and fixable.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Similar to Physics, with the mole work driving the value. A tutor who can diagnose mole weakness in one session saves hours of general revision, which is the clearest case in the sciences for paying mid-band rather than budget rates.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Mid-band and a deeper pool than the other sciences. Much of the work is command-term discipline rather than content, which is highly teachable, so a shorter block often produces more movement per dirham than a full year of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0510)
subjects.description: Mid-band, with a deep pool in Dubai. Before paying for anything, confirm which route your child is entered for: a child on the wrong one of the two is capped or stretched administratively, and that is a free conversation with the school.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, with a thinner pool than the sciences. The value sits in long-question technique, so sessions built around marked written work are worth more than sessions built around content recap, and should be priced as such.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Scarce in the form that matters. Programmers are plentiful; tutors who teach to the published pseudocode conventions are not, and that is the distinction the fee should reflect. Ask directly whether they have taught Paper 2 answers to those conventions.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Scarce, and complicated by the fact that the two routes are different courses. Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and schools are required to ensure teachers of Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach it.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Priced as one subject but containing three, which makes a diagnostic that separates performance by discipline unusually good value. Families often pay for general science tuition when the actual deficit is in one of the three.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: For a visiting tutor, the community a family lives in is a cost input: the journey is inside the fee and the dead time is paid for. These notes price that reality by area, and explain what disappears from the bill when delivery moves online.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Bluewaters
regions.note: Central and well connected, so travel is not the constraint; parking and tower access is. Visiting tutors commonly add time for building entry, and sessions start late because school buses arrive late. Online removes both the access delay and the surcharge.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Journeys crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road double in the afternoon peak, so a visiting tutor's round trip can exceed the teaching hour. This is where the travel share of an in-home fee is largest and where it buys a parent nothing.

regions.name: Mudon, Town Square, Dubailand and Dubai South
regions.note: Outlying communities where the pool of tutors willing to drive is thinnest and the surcharge highest. Requests for scarce specifications from these areas are the ones most likely to go unmatched locally, whatever fee is offered.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Villa communities with schools close by, so children are home early and a 16:00 start is realistic. Travel from the city centre is moderate, which keeps in-home quotes nearer the bottom of the published band than JVC quotes are.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Long internal distances inside the communities themselves, so a visiting tutor's journey does not end at the gate. Families here often want two subjects in one evening, which multiplies the travel cost in-home and costs nothing extra online.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Short school runs and the earliest feasible session starts in the city. Travel is cheap for a visiting tutor here, which is why in-home quotes for these addresses sit closest to online rates and the comparison is tightest.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown and DIFC
regions.note: Easy to reach, hard to work in: the binding constraint is a room with a door that shuts rather than a journey. Any quote should be tested against where the session will actually happen, because a session in a shared living room is not the product.

regions.name: Deira, Bur Dubai and Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense older districts with strong IGCSE Maths and science demand and a reasonable local tutor supply, so in-home rates here are more competitive than in the outlying communities. Session timing is built around Maghrib and family dinner.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Marina, Al Barsha and Tecom
schoolClusters.note: Large IGCSE cohorts with post-16 routes splitting towards A Level or the Diploma. Each school's published fee sits on its KHDA profile, which is the figure to use when putting tuition costs in proportion. Students we support attend schools in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: British and Indian-curriculum provision side by side, with early home times and heavy demand for Maths and the sciences. Fee sensitivity is higher here and the local tutor supply is better, which keeps in-home quotes closer to the published floor.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Dubai Hills, the Ranches and Al Qudra
schoolClusters.note: Wide catchments and long internal journeys, several campuses running both post-16 routes. Families here most often book two subjects together, which is the scenario where the in-home travel multiple is most visible on an invoice.

sections.heading: What IGCSE home tutor fees in Dubai actually cover
paragraphs: An hourly tuition rate in Dubai is paying for six things, and providers bundle them differently. Teaching time is the obvious one. Travel is the one that only exists if someone drives. Marking of written work between sessions is the line most often absent from cheap quotes and most responsible for whether the hours achieve anything. Reporting to parents, materials, and the terms governing cancellation and commitment make up the rest. Two quotes that differ by AED 100 usually differ on marking and cancellation rather than on teaching.

The published market figures give the shape of each band. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors reaching AED 500, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 online. TutorChase quotes AED 270. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, and at that level the hour is supervision rather than marked teaching. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tier.

When you take a quote, ask for it line by line. Not what is your rate, but: is marking of written work included between sessions, how long is the session, what notice do you need for a cancellation, what happens if we stop after three sessions, and does the figure include VAT. A provider who answers all five in one message is quoting a product. A provider who answers only the first is quoting a number, and numbers in this market have a habit of acquiring extras later.

sections.heading: The travel line, priced by Dubai community
paragraphs: Travel is the part of an in-home fee that parents accept without pricing, and it is often the largest avoidable share. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to Jumeirah Village Circle at 16:30 is not making a twenty-minute journey; in the afternoon peak that round trip can approach the length of the teaching session. Nobody absorbs that for free. It appears either as a higher hourly rate, as a minimum session length that makes the trip worthwhile, or as a tutor who takes only clients within a narrow radius.

The minimum-session effect is the one families notice last. A visiting tutor who will not travel for less than ninety minutes has, in practice, raised your weekly bill by fifty per cent regardless of whether your child needs ninety minutes. For a Year 9 student, sixty minutes of focused work is often more productive than ninety, and paying for the extra half hour because of a journey is paying for the journey. Online, session length is set by the student's attention rather than by a drive.

The second effect is on the pool. A tutor pool defined by a twenty-minute radius around Mudon is a very different pool from one defined by who teaches Cambridge 0606 at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time. For common subjects the local pool is deep enough that this hardly matters. For Additional Mathematics, Computer Science pseudocode work, Arabic as a first language, or a private candidate who needs sequencing as well as teaching, the radius is the binding constraint and no fee overcomes it.

sections.heading: Monthly packages and what a lock-in actually costs
paragraphs: Packages look like a discount and sometimes are. Monthly arrangements seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. The arithmetic is worth doing before you agree, because the effective hourly rate inside a package is sometimes higher than the provider's own advertised hourly figure.

The real cost of a package is rarely the rate. It is what happens to unused sessions. Dubai school calendars contain half terms, long weekends, school trips, study leave and examination periods, and a package month with four scheduled sessions and two usable weeks hands the provider the difference. Ask three questions before signing: do unused sessions roll over, is there an expiry, and what notice cancels the arrangement. A package with rollover and a month's notice is a convenience; one with expiry and a term's notice is a commitment with a discount attached.

There is also a quieter effect on behaviour. A family inside a twelve-month package stops asking whether the tuition is working, because the decision feels already made. The arrangements that produce results are the ones with a review point: a date at which comparable marked work either moved or did not, and at which continuing is an active choice. If a package removes that date, the discount is being paid for with the thing that made the spending accountable.

sections.heading: The extras that appear on the second invoice
paragraphs: Most unexpected tuition costs in Dubai are not dishonest; they are simply not mentioned in the first conversation because nobody asked. A short list covers almost all of them. Late-cancellation charges, where a session cancelled inside the notice period is billed in full. Minimum session lengths that raise the weekly cost. Separate charges for mock marking or for reading a piece of written work outside session time. Rate increases at the start of the exam term. Charges for a second child in the same household. Materials billed separately.

Two of these deserve particular attention. The first is exam-term pricing. Several providers in this market charge more from January onwards, which is defensible given demand, but a family that budgeted in September on an autumn rate finds the number rising at exactly the point they are least able to change tutor. Ask in September what the rate will be in February and get the answer in writing. The second is the second-child question: families with two children at IGCSE often assume a household discount exists, and where the sessions are separate one-to-one hours, usually it does not.

The VAT question needs care rather than confidence. Whether and how tuition is treated for UAE VAT is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and depends on the provider's circumstances, so this page does not state a treatment. What a parent can reasonably do is ask whether a quoted price includes VAT, ask for an invoice that shows the amount charged, and ask for the provider's tax registration number where VAT is being charged. A provider unable to answer those three questions is worth a second look for reasons beyond tax.

sections.heading: What a fee cannot buy, and what it should
paragraphs: No fee in this market buys a grade. No provider controls the paper, the marking or the boundaries, and a promised grade is only honest where refund terms are published and honoured. Any Dubai provider offering a guaranteed band should be asked, politely and immediately, where those terms are published. The same applies to a self-published star rating: one provider in this market shows its own aggregate rating of 4.9, and two show different review counts on the same page.

What a fee should buy is specific and checkable. A diagnosis in the first session, from marked timed written work rather than a conversation. An estimated hour count, given in writing, by someone prepared to be shown wrong. Written work marked against the published criteria between sessions, with annotations at the point of loss. A short note after each session. And a review date at which comparable marked work either moved or did not, with a stated consequence either way. That list is worth more than any discount.

It is also worth knowing what a fee must not buy. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, and gives feedback on work the student produced; no part of an assessed submission is supplied or edited to completion for a student. One operation researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student at risk rather than the provider. A quote that includes anything of that kind is not cheap at any price.

sections.heading: Tuition fees against the rest of a Dubai education budget
paragraphs: Tuition is easier to judge next to the numbers around it. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second of the emirate's economic incentives packages, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Each school's own fee is published on its KHDA profile, so any parent can check the figure without asking the school. Against a frozen school fee, tuition becomes the education line that is actually moving, which is a good reason to examine it carefully once a year.

Exam entry is the number families overlook. School candidates have entry costs folded into the school's charges. Private candidates pay the examination centre directly, and the amount is set by the centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so it must be confirmed with the centre you intend to use. The deadlines matter more than the amounts: a Cambridge June entry has to be lodged in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and the November series closes in the summer, with the exact day published per series and zone. Missing an entry deadline costs a whole series.

The table below is a planning frame rather than a price list. Put your own school's published fee and your own centre's entry charge into it, then add the tuition rows. The exercise takes ten minutes and tends to produce better decisions than either guilt or panic, because it shows tuition in proportion and makes the review conversation a budgeting one rather than an emotional one.

sections.heading: What moving the session online removes from the bill
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Because this is a page about fees, the right thing to do is show which lines of a bill that decision removes and which it does not, rather than describe the choice as an advantage and move on.

Three lines disappear. Travel, which in the outer communities can approach the cost of the teaching hour. The minimum session length that exists to justify a journey, which means a sixty-minute session is available where sixty minutes is what the child needs. And the second-subject travel multiple, so a family wanting Maths and Chemistry in one evening pays for two hours of teaching rather than two journeys. Two lines are unchanged: marking between sessions and reporting are properties of the provider's model, not of the format.

One thing is genuinely lost, and it is worth naming. A tutor physically present can hold the attention of a younger or very distractible child in a way a screen has to work harder at, and for some families that is decisive. Against it sits the pool question: the difference between a Physics graduate who can teach 0625 and a teacher who has marked Paper 6 answers across several series is large, and it is not a difference you can find twice inside a twenty-minute drive of Town Square. Online, the constraint becomes the clock instead of the map.

sections.heading: Five questions that produce a real quote
paragraphs: Most tuition conversations in Dubai begin with what is your hourly rate, which is the least informative question available. Five others produce a quote you can actually compare. What is the session length, and is a shorter one available. Is written work marked against the published criteria between sessions, and by the tutor who teaches them. What notice cancels a session and what is charged inside that notice. What will this rate be in February. And what happens if we stop after three sessions.

Add two that are specific to IGCSE. Which specification code and tier has this tutor taught, and how many cohorts. And what will I receive in writing after each session. The first establishes whether you are buying specification experience or general teaching, which is the largest determinant of value in Year 11. The second establishes whether there will be a record, which is what makes a review conversation possible later.

A provider who answers all seven in one message is quoting a product, and the number they give you means something. A provider who answers only the rate has given you a figure that will be revised on contact with reality. The whole purpose of taking a fee apart is that the parts are comparable where the total is not, and ten minutes of asking at the start saves the conversation that otherwise happens in February, when nobody involved has any room left to move. Send the questions by message rather than asking them on a call, so the answers are written down and can be read again in six months.

faqs.question: What are IGCSE home tutor fees in Dubai made up of?
faqs.answer: Six things, bundled into one hourly figure: teaching time, travel, marking of written work between sessions, written reporting to parents, materials, and the terms around cancellation and commitment. Travel only exists where someone drives, and it is often the second largest share. Marking is the line most often absent from cheap quotes and the one most responsible for whether the hours achieve anything. Two quotes differing by AED 100 usually differ on marking and cancellation rather than on teaching quality, which is why comparing headline rates across Dubai providers tells you very little.

faqs.question: What hourly fee does the Dubai in-home IGCSE market actually publish?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors ranging up to AED 500, according to Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tier. Those are market rates attributed to whoever published them, not IB Gram's prices. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; tuition here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video.

faqs.question: Why does the same tutor cost more for our villa in Mudon than for a family in Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Because travel is inside the fee and the journeys are not comparable. A round trip to Jumeirah 2 in the afternoon is short and predictable; a round trip to Mudon or Town Square can approach the length of the teaching session, and in the outer communities the pool of tutors willing to make it is thin enough that scarcity adds to the rate. It also shows up as a minimum session length, since a tutor who will not drive for less than ninety minutes has raised your weekly bill by half. Online delivery removes both effects.

faqs.question: Is an AED 799 monthly tuition package good value in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Do the division before deciding. AED 799 for eight sessions is roughly AED 100 per teaching hour, which is competitive if those sessions are the length advertised and if written work is marked between them. The cost that catches families is unused sessions: Dubai school calendars contain half terms, trips, study leave and exam periods, and a package month with four scheduled sessions and two usable weeks hands the provider the difference. Ask whether unused sessions roll over, whether there is an expiry, and what notice ends the arrangement before you sign anything.

faqs.question: What unexpected charges do Dubai tuition providers add later?
faqs.answer: Six recur. Late-cancellation fees charged inside a notice period. Minimum session lengths that raise a weekly bill. Separate charges for marking mocks or written work outside session time. Rate increases from January, when demand peaks and you are least able to change tutor. A second full rate for a sibling where parents assumed a household arrangement. And materials billed separately. None of these is dishonest; they simply go unmentioned because nobody asks. Each has a question that surfaces it in advance, and asking all six takes one message.

faqs.question: Should an IGCSE tuition quote in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask rather than assume. How tuition is treated for UAE VAT depends on the provider's own circumstances and is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, so no honest page should state a treatment as fact. What you can do is ask three things: does the quoted figure include VAT, will the invoice show the amount charged, and what is the provider's tax registration number where VAT is being added. A provider who cannot answer those three is worth a second look for reasons that go beyond tax, because they indicate how the rest of the billing is run.

faqs.question: Do tuition rates in Dubai rise before the IGCSE exam series?
faqs.answer: Commonly, yes, and the increase lands at the worst moment for a family. Demand for specification specialists peaks from January into the May and June series, when every Year 11 cohort in Dubai is chasing the same small pool of subject specialists at once. Several providers price accordingly. The protection is simple and nobody uses it: in September, ask what the rate will be in February, and ask for the answer in writing. Booking a named specialist months ahead both costs less and produces a better match than trying to find one in April, three weeks before the first paper.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tuition cheaper than a home tutor in Dubai, or just different?
faqs.answer: Both. Three lines leave the bill: travel, the minimum session length that exists to justify a journey, and the second journey when a family wants two subjects in one evening. Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 against an in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500. Two lines do not change, because marking and reporting are properties of the provider's model rather than the format. What is genuinely lost is a person in the room, which matters most for younger or very distractible children.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we pay for before deciding whether tuition is working?
faqs.answer: Buy a bounded block rather than an open arrangement. Four to six sessions is enough to produce a diagnosis from marked timed work, an estimated hour count and a written plan, including the recommendation not to continue where that is honest. Then set a review point at roughly session six of any ongoing arrangement, where comparable marked work either moved or did not. The expensive failure in this market is not a bad tutor; it is a standing monthly payment with no date at which anybody asks the question.

faqs.question: Do siblings studying IGCSE together get a lower rate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually not, where the sessions are separate one-to-one hours, because the tutor is teaching twice. Where providers do discount a household, it is normally because the children are taught together, and that is a different product: two students sharing one hour means roughly half the individual feedback each. For siblings in the same year sitting the same specification, shared sessions can work well. For siblings two years apart, or on different tiers, the saving is paid for in attention. Ask which arrangement is being offered before comparing it to a single rate.

faqs.question: What should I receive in writing for the fee I am paying?
faqs.answer: Four things. A diagnosis from the first session based on marked timed written work rather than a conversation. An estimated hour count, given by someone willing to be shown wrong. Written work marked against the published criteria between sessions, with annotations at the point of loss rather than a grade and a comment. And a short note after each session saying what changed and what is set for the week. If none of that arrives, you are buying lesson time only, and that should be reflected in what you pay for it.

faqs.question: How do IGCSE tuition fees compare with Dubai school fees?
faqs.answer: Put them side by side, because the comparison is informative. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, and each school's fee is published on its own KHDA profile. Against a frozen school fee, a weekly online one-to-one subject at AED 180 to AED 360 per hour across thirty teaching weeks is a meaningful but not enormous addition, and it is the only education line in the household you can change mid-year. That is the reason to review it deliberately once a year rather than by instinct.

faqs.question: What does a private candidate pay to enter IGCSE exams in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The amount is set by the examination centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so it has to be confirmed with the centre you intend to use; no honest page can quote you a figure that applies everywhere. The deadlines matter more than the amount. A Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, months ahead of the paper, and the November series closes over the summer, with the exact day printed on the statement of entry. On the Pearson side, the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Can a tuition fee in Dubai come with a promised grade improvement?
faqs.answer: Not honestly. No provider controls the paper, the marking or the grade boundaries, and the only way to offer such a promise properly is to publish refund terms and honour them, which almost nobody in this market does. Where you see a guaranteed band, ask where the terms are published and read them. Treat a self-published star rating the same way: one provider here shows its own aggregate rating of 4.9, and two show conflicting review counts on a single page. What a fee can buy is diagnosis, marking, reporting and a review date.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to start IGCSE tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A free trial lesson, then a bounded diagnostic block of four to six sessions at an agreed total. The trial costs nothing and requires no card details, and it is where you test whether the tutor can read one of your child's returned scripts and name where the marks went. The block then produces a plan and an hour estimate, so any larger commitment is made with a number in front of you. Starting with a twelve-month package is the most expensive way to find out whether tuition was the right intervention.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.closingHeading: Take the number apart before you agree to it
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-fees.closingBody: Ask for session length, marking between sessions, written reporting, cancellation notice, the February rate and what happens if you stop after three sessions. Then ask which specification code and tier the tutor has actually taught. Seven questions, one message, and the quote you get back is comparable with the next one, which the headline rate never is. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card details and no commitment, and the diagnostic that follows should hand you an hour estimate you can budget against rather than an open monthly payment.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barari.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects for families in Al Barari and the Dubailand communities around it. Each teaches named syllabuses rather than a general subject, and you meet the person who will take every session before you commit.

intro.heading: Two years, two decision points, one calendar
paragraphs: The IGCSE is a two-year qualification that most Dubai families treat as a single event at the end. That is where the trouble starts. By the time a Year 11 mock result lands in the first term, the grade trajectory has already been set by eighteen months of accumulated understanding, and the remaining months are spent either consolidating it or trying to reverse it. An IGCSE home tutor in Al Barari is therefore doing a completely different job in September of Year 10 than in January of Year 11, and the honest version of this page tells you which job you are buying.

Al Barari has no school inside the community. It is a low-density villa district off Al Ain Road, and every pupil commutes out to the Dubailand and Nad Al Sheba school belt or west to Motor City, Arabian Ranches and Al Barsha South. That geography has one practical effect on IGCSE tutoring: the school day finishes, then a drive happens, and a weekday session realistically starts at five rather than four. It has a second effect that matters more. Children from the same street attend schools using different exam boards, so two neighbours sitting 'IGCSE Physics' may be sitting different papers with different codes and different tiering rules.

That is why the first question we ask is which board and which syllabus code, not which subject. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is 0625. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is 4PH1. They cover similar science and assess it differently, and a tutor working from the wrong specification will teach content that is not examined and skip content that is. Asking a parent for a syllabus code sounds pedantic until you have watched a term wasted on the wrong paper structure.

The second question is the tier. Cambridge Core and Extended are not the same course with different difficulty settings; they cap at different grades and set different papers, and a child entered for Core cannot be awarded above the Core ceiling no matter how well the paper goes. Families regularly discover this in Year 11. If your child is on Core in a subject they need for an A Level or a Diploma route, the conversation to have is with the school, this term, about whether the entry can still change.

Finally, one thing stated plainly. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one online lessons. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. The phrase 'home tutor' is the one parents type, so this page uses it and answers the home-tutoring question properly below, with the market rates and the travel arithmetic. But nothing here promises a tutor at an Al Barari gate, because that is not a service we run.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barari.programmesIntro: Al Barari pupils reach IGCSE from several directions, and the entry route changes what a Year 10 tutor has to do first. These are the three paths we see most, with what each one leaves unprepared.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 into IGCSE
programmes.description: The standard British-curriculum route. Year 9 ends with subject choices and the IGCSE specification begins in Year 10. The gap that causes trouble is written fluency in the sciences and algebraic manipulation in maths: Key Stage 3 rewards getting the answer, while IGCSE marks method, units and the command term. Pupils who have always been told they are good at maths frequently lose their first Year 10 marks to presentation rather than understanding.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this route dominates by enrolment, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37% of private pupils in the 2024-25 KHDA figures. For Al Barari families the practical consequence is choice of board: the schools in the Dubailand belt do not all use the same one, so a tutor hired on a neighbour's recommendation may be teaching a different specification from the one your child sits.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme into IGCSE
programmes.description: Some pupils move from an IB continuum school into a British-curriculum school at Year 10, or sit IGCSE subjects alongside MYP. The transition is harder than it looks. MYP assessment is criterion-based and spread across the year; IGCSE is a terminal written paper with a mark scheme. A student used to being marked on investigation and reflection has to learn to answer a four-mark question in four marks' worth of words.
programmes.countryNote: This route is common in the Dubailand belt precisely because the area mixes IB continuum schools with British-curriculum schools within a short drive. The first job for a tutor is usually not content at all but exam format: past-paper exposure under timing, so that the student finds out in September what the paper actually asks rather than in a Year 11 mock.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum into IGCSE
programmes.description: Pupils arriving from CBSE or ICSE are typically ahead on mathematical content and behind on extended written response and practical-skills questions. In the sciences the gap is in experimental design and data evaluation; in English it is in the reading-response and directed-writing formats. The content catch-up is small and the format catch-up is substantial, which is the reverse of what most families expect.
programmes.countryNote: Indian-curriculum schools accounted for 26% of Dubai private enrolment in the 2024-25 figures, so this transition is routine in the emirate and the Dubailand belt sees plenty of it. A Year 10 block of weekly sessions aimed squarely at paper format usually does more for the eventual grade than another term of content teaching.

programmes.name: IGCSE into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The destination that should shape Year 10 decisions and usually does not. A Level and IB Diploma courses assume specific IGCSE content, and the Extended tier in maths and the sciences is effectively a prerequisite for the Higher Level and A Level versions. A child entered for Core in a subject they intend to continue arrives in Year 12 with a genuine content hole rather than a confidence problem.
programmes.countryNote: Schools near Al Barari split both ways at 16: some into A Levels, some into the IB Diploma, a few offering both. Ask the school which route it expects and what IGCSE tier and grade each sixth-form course requires, then work backwards. That is a Year 10 conversation, not a Year 11 one.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Barari families ask about most, with the syllabus codes and the places marks actually go. A tutor who cannot name the papers for your board is not teaching your child's course.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers on both boards, with Extended and Higher tiers reaching into functions, calculus-adjacent gradient work and more demanding algebra. Marks disappear in method: an unshown step forfeits the method mark even where the answer is right. Rounding and units cost more marks across a paper than any single topic.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Sat by pupils heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Maths AA. It introduces calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities ahead of time. It is where students who coasted through 0580 discover that fluency and understanding are different things, usually in the differentiation topic.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves, thermal physics and magnetism. Electricity is the reliable weak point: circuit reasoning requires holding current, potential difference and resistance relationships together rather than recalling one formula. Practical-skills questions reward naming the variable being controlled, which is a teachable habit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bonding, moles, rates, organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. Mole calculations are where the grade is decided, because they recur across the paper and compound: a unit error at the first step survives to the final answer. Qualitative-analysis recall is pure learned content and the cheapest marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content load with precise terminology. Students lose marks writing everything they know instead of answering the command term, and on diagrams where labelling must be exact. Transport, respiration and inheritance are the usual trouble spots; inheritance in particular rewards drawing the cross rather than reasoning in prose.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, assessed on comprehension, summary skill and control of register. The summary question is the most coachable on the paper: it rewards selection and compression, not style. Students who write beautifully and select badly score below students who do the reverse.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, where entered, speaking. Text-type accuracy is assessed: an email, a report and an article are marked partly on format and register. Candidates with confident spoken English frequently underperform here because the marks are in conventions they have never been taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Market mechanisms, the macro economy and international trade. Diagram accuracy decides the longer questions: a mislabelled axis undermines every sentence built on it. Evaluation marks on the extended questions require a stated judgement, which students routinely omit after writing a strong explanation.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Applied case-study assessment where context carries the marks. The commonest failure is answering with textbook theory and never referring to the business in the stimulus. Calculation questions on costs, revenue and ratios are straightforward marks that get skipped under time pressure.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, data representation, algorithms and programming. Binary, hexadecimal and logic gates are learnable in a small number of sessions and recur every series. Pseudocode tracing by hand is the skill most students lack, because they have learned to run code rather than to predict what it does.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with a skills component on maps, graphs and data. Case-study specificity carries the top marks: a named place with named figures beats a general description every time. The skills questions are reliable marks that reward practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language, plus MoE-mandated strands
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring splits on the same line: literary and grammatical work for first-language pupils, script fluency and spoken confidence for additional-language pupils.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: find out before you hire anyone
paragraphs: Two children on the same Al Barari street can both be sitting IGCSE Physics and be sitting different qualifications. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is syllabus 0625. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is 4PH1. The science overlaps heavily; the paper structure, the tiering and the practical-skills treatment do not. A tutor teaching from the wrong specification spends the term covering material that will not be examined while leaving out material that will.

So the first thing to establish is which board, which syllabus code and which tier, and the school's exams officer can tell you all three in one email. It is worth getting this in writing rather than relying on what your child believes, because pupils routinely do not know, and a Year 10 who says 'Cambridge' because the textbook cover looked familiar has cost you nothing until you hire a tutor on that basis.

The tier question is the one with consequences. On Cambridge, Core and Extended are different courses: different papers, different content, and different grade ceilings, so a Core entry caps the achievable grade regardless of performance. Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics tiers as Foundation and Higher with the same logic. If your child is on the lower tier in a subject they need for an A Level or Higher Level course, that is a conversation with the school this term, while the entry can still move.

sections.heading: The two IGCSE years counted backwards
paragraphs: This is the planning frame nobody in this search result publishes. Entry deadlines sit months before papers are sat, tier decisions close before that, and a resit after results has to be entered for the next series rather than taken at a convenient moment. A family who understands the sequence makes decisions when they are available; a family who does not finds out that a door closed in November.

Work from the end. The June series is the one most Dubai schools enter for, with November available as a resit route. Before the series there is an entry deadline set through the centre, and before that a tier decision that effectively caps the grade. Before that sit the Year 11 mocks, which are your best available evidence and usually the trigger for hiring anyone. Before that is the whole of Year 10, which is where the grade is actually made and where tutoring is cheapest in effort per mark.

The verifiable dates in this picture come from Pearson, and they are worth quoting precisely because they show the scale of the lag. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking, which is why they carry dates; for any session still ahead, use the month and check the live official timetable, since Pearson publishes provisional versions that can be revised.

One Cambridge-specific trap belongs here. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone your child's centre is in before you plan study leave around a timetable you downloaded yourself.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor costs in Dubai, read monthly
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages quote an hourly rate because it sounds smaller. The number that lands in a household budget is monthly, so start there. Market monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session in Dubai, read in October 2026, run around AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the mid tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package pricing shows around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Put that next to the school bill and the decision looks different. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. So the fee line is flat, and a tutoring line at one session a week is a modest addition to it. Two subjects at two sessions a week through a Year 11 spring term is not modest, and a family should decide that deliberately rather than by drift.

What separates the tiers is specification knowledge. A capable university student in the AED 45 to AED 150 band can help a Year 8 with simultaneous equations. They cannot tell a Year 11 where the Edexcel mark scheme awards method credit on a multi-step mole calculation, because that comes from teaching and marking the paper. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; TutorChase publishes AED 270; the premium band reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Those are their figures, published by them, read in October 2026.

IB Gram does not print an hourly rate here. The honest reason is that the right figure depends on the subject, the tier and how many weeks remain, and one number covering every IGCSE subject would mislead. What we publish instead is the market band above, so any quote you receive from anyone can be checked, plus a free trial lesson so the first hour costs nothing and you judge the tutor rather than the brochure.

sections.heading: Online against a tutor driving to Al Barari
paragraphs: The home-tutoring question deserves a straight answer rather than a deflection. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is widely available and market rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. It works, and for some children it is the right format. IB Gram does not offer it in the UAE, and this page is not going to pretend the option does not exist.

What it costs you beyond the rate is selection. An in-home tutor for Al Barari is drawn from the people willing to drive to a villa community off Al Ain Road at five on a weekday and hold that slot every week for a term. For general Year 9 maths that pool is fine. For Extended-tier Chemistry 0620, or Additional Mathematics 0606, or Edexcel Further Pure 4PM1, it is thin, and families end up with a competent generalist instead of someone who knows the paper. Online removes geography from the shortlist and leaves only the question of whether the tutor teaches that specification.

The second cost is reliability, and it is specific to this part of Dubai. A tutor crossing the city in the afternoon peak to reach Al Barari is exposed to Al Ain Road traffic twice. Two cancellations in a Year 11 spring term is two weeks removed from a fixed countdown to the series, and in April that is not recoverable. An online slot fails only if the tutor is ill.

Where in-home genuinely wins is the youngest and the most distractible pupils, where an adult physically present is the intervention. We say that rather than arguing against it, because a family who books the wrong format wastes a term. For Year 10 and Year 11 work, where a session means worked problems and a marked past paper, the screen is not the limitation.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Ask a Year 11 what they are weak at and you will get a topic. Mark a paper and you will usually get something else. Across the subjects we cover, a large share of lost marks across the whole paper comes from four habits rather than from missing content, and all four are fixable in a handful of sessions.

The first is method. IGCSE mark schemes award credit for steps, so a correct answer with no working scores below a wrong answer with sound method. Students who do mental arithmetic well are the worst affected, because they have been rewarded for speed for years. The second is units and significant figures, which bleed one mark at a time across every calculation question and add up to a grade boundary. The third is the command term: 'describe', 'explain', 'compare' and 'evaluate' ask for different structures, and writing everything you know satisfies none of them.

The fourth is timing, and it is the most common. A student who knows the material but spends fourteen minutes on a six-mark question will not finish the paper, and unanswered questions score nothing regardless of understanding. This only shows up under real timing, which is why the first session of a Year 11 block is a timed paper rather than teaching. Marking it against the published scheme almost always relocates the problem away from where the family thought it was.

Content gaps are real too, and when they exist they are usually narrow and identifiable: electricity in Physics 0625, moles in Chemistry 0620, inheritance in Biology 0610, algebraic fractions in Mathematics 0580. Those are weeks of work, not months. What takes months is teaching a specification that was never learned, which is why Year 10 tutoring is worth so much more per hour than Year 11 tutoring.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what five IGCSE subjects have to show
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules matter more than any league table, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions them. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. So a child with five passes of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not have five for this purpose. At least one competitor page ranking for UAE tutoring searches states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Count the five, exclude those two, and check the current requirement on the authority's own channel before relying on it.

There is a second trap worth naming. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. That is a different track from the British one, and families with children in American-curriculum schools near Al Barari sometimes read British-track numbers and plan against the wrong rule.

For the IB track, this page publishes no points threshold. The source that verifies the British and American requirements does not state one, and no IB figure should be put in front of a parent without being read on the Ministry's own pages or confirmed with the emirate's attestation channel. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and does not guarantee any outcome in that process; we describe it and point you to the official route.

sections.heading: Regulation: your child's school, and your child's tutor
paragraphs: Two separate regimes apply, and parents routinely conflate them. The school is regulated by the emirate. In Dubai that is KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspecting annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The useful part of an inspection report is not the headline band but the subject-level commentary, which frequently names the exact weakness a parent has been sensing without evidence.

The tutor is regulated federally. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services.

No fine figure appears on this page, and you should treat any page that prints one with suspicion. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the amount circulating online could not be verified. Equally, IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, or licensed or accredited by the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and nobody should claim otherwise without showing a permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes operating premises in Dubai.

The practical use of all this is leverage. Ask any tutor three questions before booking: do you hold a MoHRE private tuition permit, which board and syllabus code do you teach, and do you work at a school my child attends. The last one matters because ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled pupils, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar.
