sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and what we will not do
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the Diploma, but the honesty questions still arise, particularly around practical work, controlled assessment where it applies, and the growing market in supplied answers. The position is the same across every subject we teach: a tutor explains, demonstrates, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not produce work that will be submitted as the student's.

The same boundary applies to materials. We do not publish, reproduce or supply awarding-body syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to Cambridge and Pearson and reproducing them is copyright infringement. What a tutor does is work through questions with the student from legitimately obtained material and teach them to read the mark scheme themselves, which is a more durable skill than being handed answers.

There is a related claim worth being sceptical about across this market. Several providers describe their tutors as examiners. We do not use examiner status as a selling point for any individual whose current status we cannot evidence, and no tutor should imply that examiner experience gives access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content, because it does not. If a provider leans on that claim, ask what specifically it gives your child that a subject specialist does not.

Finally, no grade promises. We will not tell you that a block of sessions produces a grade 7, a 9, or any specific improvement, and any provider that does is either guessing or guaranteeing something they cannot control. What we will do is tell you after the first diagnostic session what the evidence suggests is reachable in the weeks available, and revise that honestly as mock results come in.

process.title: Send us the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Before anything else we need which awarding body, which syllabus code and which tier your child is entered for in each subject. The school's exams officer can confirm all three. This single email prevents the most expensive mistake in IGCSE tutoring, which is a term spent teaching the wrong specification well.

process.title: One timed paper, marked properly
process.description: The diagnostic is a past paper or a recent school assessment worked under timing and marked against the published scheme. The output is a list of lost marks by question type: content, method, units, command term or timing. This frequently disagrees with both your theory and your child's, and that disagreement is the useful part.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the named tutor
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, taught by the person who would take every session afterwards. Judge whether they know the paper structure for that code, whether they found the real gap, and whether the work they set was clear enough to attempt alone. If any answer is no, tell us and we match again.

process.title: A fixed slot planned to the series
process.description: The weekly slot is yours for the term, and the plan runs from your child's school calendar and the series they are entered for. Al Barari commutes mean a five o'clock or later weekday start is usual. Holiday weeks become intensive blocks; Ramadan weeks move to earlier afternoon or post-Iftar and shorten rather than stop.

process.title: A written note after each session
process.description: What was covered, what was got wrong, what is set, what comes next, sent the same evening. This is how you see progress between reports rather than waiting for the school's next one, and it is also the record that shows the work in any assessed task is your child's own.

process.title: Re-plan at each piece of evidence
process.description: Every mock, report and marked past paper is a checkpoint where the plan is tested against results rather than continued by habit. Sometimes the right answer is to stop in one subject and move the hour to another, and we will say so. A weekly session with no current target is a routine, not a plan.

whyPoints.title: We teach the specification your child actually sits
whyPoints.description: Board, syllabus code and tier are established before the first lesson, and the tutor works from that specification. Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 are not interchangeable, and a tutor who treats them as the same subject will cover content that is not examined while missing content that is.

whyPoints.title: Year 10 is treated as the cheap year
whyPoints.description: Most of this page argues for starting earlier, because the effort required per mark rises steeply after a Year 11 mock. We will say that to you even when a later, larger booking would suit us better, because a family who starts in Year 10 and succeeds is a family who comes back for the sixth form.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen by syllabus, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: Because the lessons are online, the shortlist is everyone who teaches that code at that tier rather than everyone who will reach Al Barari at five on a Tuesday. For Extended-tier sciences and Additional Mathematics that difference decides whether you get a specialist or a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are competitors' own published figures with the date they were read, so any quote you receive, including ours, can be judged against something real. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all and one declines to answer its own pricing question.

whyPoints.title: No supplied answers, no reproduced papers
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on your child's own work, and we do not host or hand over awarding-body papers, mark schemes or boundary tables. Teaching a student to read a mark scheme is worth more than giving them its contents, and it is the only version that is lawful.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE. No special-educational-needs assessment. No guaranteed grades or score promises. No claim of approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, because we hold none of them.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a house in Al Barari?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. The page uses the phrase 'home tutor' because that is what parents search for, and the question deserves a direct answer. The practical trade is in your favour for most IGCSE work: the shortlist becomes every tutor who teaches your child's syllabus code rather than every tutor who will drive to a villa community at five on a weekday.

faqs.question: Which awarding body does an Al Barari pupil's school usually use?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject. Do not rely on what your child says, because pupils often do not know and a textbook cover is not evidence. The codes matter: Cambridge Physics is 0625, Edexcel is 4PH1, and the papers are structured differently. Get it in writing before hiring anyone. A tutor working from the wrong specification can teach very well for a whole term and still leave your child unprepared for the paper they actually sit.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended, and can we still change?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge, Core and Extended are different courses with different papers and different grade ceilings, so a Core entry caps the achievable grade however well the paper goes. Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher tiers with the same logic. Whether the entry can change depends on the school and how close the entry deadline is, so ask now rather than after the mock. If your child needs the subject for an A Level or a Higher Level Diploma course, the higher tier is usually a prerequisite rather than an ambition.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. UAE candidates use those. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a March exam window is wrong about your country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: My child's Year 11 mock came back badly. How many weeks do we need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the losses were content or technique, and the only way to know is to read the paper question by question. If marks went to method, units, command terms and timing, a block of eight to ten weeks at two sessions a week moves a great deal, because those are habits. If half a specification was never understood, the honest answer is that the remaining weeks will lift the grade without reaching the one you hoped for. We will tell you which case you are in after the first session rather than after a term of invoices.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost per month in the Dubailand area?
faqs.answer: Market monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session in Dubai, read in October 2026, run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package pricing shows around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are the market's figures with their sources, not IB Gram prices. Our first lesson is free, so you can judge the tutor before discussing any number.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 rather than waiting?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the argument is arithmetic rather than sales. In Year 10 a tutor consolidates content as the school teaches it, builds method and units discipline before the questions get harder, and can flag a wrong tier entry while it can still change. In Year 11 the same tutor is undoing eighteen months of habit against a fixed deadline. The hourly rate is identical; the marks per hour are not. A family that starts in Year 10 usually needs fewer total sessions to reach the same grade.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking competitor states six subjects are needed, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency or attestation.

faqs.question: Do you cover Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are both taught, and they are genuinely different work from the main maths course. They introduce calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities ahead of A Level or Higher Level Maths AA, and they are where pupils who found 0580 or 4MA1 easy discover the difference between fluency and understanding. Differentiation is usually the point at which a weekly session becomes necessary. Tell us which qualification your child is entered for, because the two specifications are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supply past papers and mark schemes for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. What a tutor does instead is work through questions with your child from legitimately obtained material, and teach them to read a mark scheme themselves so they can see where credit is awarded. That skill outlasts any set of answers, and it is the thing that changes how a student approaches the next paper.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect a Year 11 revision schedule in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the usable part of the evening moves, so sessions shift to the earlier afternoon or to a post-Iftar slot. The adjustment we recommend is shorter sessions at the same frequency rather than skipped weeks, because continuity is what holds a revision sequence together. Where Ramadan falls close to the series or a mock window, plan the block before it begins rather than improvising week by week. An online slot is far easier to move than a tutor's drive across Dubai, which is one of the quieter practical advantages of the format.

faqs.question: Are tutors in Dubai required to hold a permit, and should I ask?
faqs.answer: Yes, and yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with suspicion. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask the same of any agency.

faqs.question: Why is Arabic compulsory at a British-curriculum school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the emirate requires it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Two things follow: the timetable carries subjects beyond the IGCSE list, and Arabic is one of the most requested tutoring streams in Dubai, split along the same first-language and additional-language line.

faqs.question: What should I actually judge a trial lesson on?
faqs.answer: Not whether your child enjoyed it. Three things. Did the tutor demonstrate knowledge of the specific syllabus code and paper structure, rather than the subject in general? Did they locate the real gap, or accept your child's account of it? Was the work set afterwards clear enough to attempt without help at home? If any answer is no, say so and we will match again. One free hour settles the most important variable in tutoring before any money moves, which no published hourly rate can do.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both maths and a science for the same child?
faqs.answer: Often, and in Year 11 it is frequently the better arrangement. Where the same tutor covers Mathematics 0580 and Physics 0625, they can see that a physics problem is really a rearranging-equations problem, which a second tutor would diagnose as a physics weakness. The sessions remain separate one-to-one lessons in consecutive slots, not a combined lesson. The limit is specialism: at Extended tier in two sciences the right answer is usually two specialists rather than one generalist covering both.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free in our weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you which part is the constraint, because the fixes differ. If a specialist for that code and tier exists but not in your slot, a different evening or a weekend morning usually resolves it, and in a community with long commutes that is often easier than it sounds. If the subject is not covered in UAE hours at all, the fallback is a tutor in another time zone teaching at a Gulf Standard Time-compatible hour, and we say where they are based. If we cannot cover it, we tell you that rather than booking you in anyway.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barari.closingHeading: Get the code, then get the calendar
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barari.closingBody: Two emails decide most of this. The first goes to your child's exams officer asking for the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier in each subject. The second asks for the mock window, the entry deadline and the series the school is entering. With those in hand you know what you are buying and when it has to work by, and you can judge any tutor, including ours, against something concrete. Then book a free trial lesson with the named specialist who would teach every session and see whether they know the paper. Tuition for Al Barari families runs live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. We do not make home visits in the UAE and we do not promise grades.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barsha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses to students at Al Barsha and Al Barsha South schools. Matching starts from the syllabus code on your child's entry form, because 0580 and 4MA1 are different examinations with different papers and a tutor who knows one is not automatically useful on the other.

intro.heading: Two neighbourhoods, one answer: why the comparison settles faster than parents expect
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Barsha is a tutor who drives to a villa or apartment in Al Barsha 1, 2 or 3 and teaches one student there. That market is active and priced: independent tutors and agencies in Dubai quote roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for an in-home one-to-one visit, with travel inside the figure. IB Gram does not sell it. We arrange home visits only in India, and nothing on this page should be read as a promise that anybody will arrive at a Dubai address. What we deliver across Al Barsha and its neighbours is one-to-one tuition over live video, one tutor to one student, at a time agreed with the family.

The comparison most Al Barsha families are actually running is geographic. Households move between Al Barsha 1 and Al Barsha South, or between Al Barsha and Barsha Heights, far more readily than they change school, because a lease ends and a school place does not. The natural question is whether tutoring gets easier or harder on the other side of the move. For in-home tutoring the answer genuinely changes: Al Barsha 1 sits on the Red Line at Mall of the Emirates with a dense cluster of schools inside walking distance, while Al Barsha South has no Metro station and everything is car-dependent, which adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes to an arriving tutor's journey at exactly the hour a school run ends.

For online tutoring the answer does not change at all, and that is the point of this page. A Year 10 student sitting Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 in Al Barsha 3 and one sitting the same paper in Al Barsha South 4 are matched against the same bench of specialists at the same hour. The variable that decides quality in IGCSE tuition is not distance. It is whether the tutor teaches the exact syllabus the school entered the student for, knows which paper the practical skills are assessed on, and can read a mark scheme out loud.

That matters because the Al Barsha school cluster is unusually mixed on boards. Within a few kilometres you have British-curriculum schools entering Cambridge, British-curriculum schools entering Pearson Edexcel, American schools running no IGCSE at all, and schools on Ministry of Education and Indian tracks. Two children in the same compound can sit mathematics examinations with different paper structures, different tiering rules and different formula provision. A parent comparing districts is usually comparing the wrong variable: the thing to compare is the syllabus code, not the postcode.

The rest of this page does both comparisons properly. It sets Al Barsha against the districts either side of it on the things that genuinely differ. It then sets Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel code by code, explains the Core and Extended tier decision and what each implies for a grade ceiling, prices the market cheapest option first, and covers the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether an IGCSE set converts into a UAE university application at all. The permit position and the availability limits are at the end, because they are the two things providers tend to leave out.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barsha.programmesIntro: An Al Barsha family on the British track usually touches three stages, and the tutoring question changes at each handover. The notes below are specific to this cluster, where a move between districts is common and a move between boards is more common than parents expect.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: Years 7 to 9 are the only stage with no external examination attached, which makes them the cheapest place to fix a problem and the easiest place to ignore one. The content that matters later is narrow and identifiable: algebraic fluency, fraction and index work, scientific notation, and the ability to write a paragraph that answers the question asked. A student who leaves Year 9 shaky on those four arrives in IGCSE already behind.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha schools set IGCSE option choices in Year 9, and the choice is partly made for the student by set placement in mathematics and science. A student placed in a lower set in Year 9 may be steered towards Core rather than Extended two years later. That is the decision worth a term of tutoring, and almost nobody treats it as one.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally at the end. Cambridge grades on a nine-point scale from A* to G with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and is structured differently. Papers are the whole grade in most subjects, so technique and timing carry weight that coursework cannot offset. The highest-return tutoring work is past-paper practice marked against the published mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage at which Dubai families collide with Ministry of Education equivalency for the first time. Five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not among the five. Families regularly discover this in Year 11 rather than Year 9, by which point the subject set is fixed.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma or BTEC
programmes.description: The post-16 split is where IGCSE grades stop being a report card and start being a gatekeeper. A Level subject entry typically requires a grade 6 or B at IGCSE in that subject or in mathematics; IB Diploma Higher Level choices carry similar informal thresholds. The IGCSE grade therefore determines which of two very different two-year programmes is available, which is why Year 11 tutoring is a decision investment and not just exam preparation.
programmes.countryNote: In the Al Barsha cluster both routes are available within a short drive, which makes the IGCSE grade unusually consequential: a student with the grades can switch from a British school to an IB Diploma at a neighbouring school without moving home. MoE equivalency on the British track also requires one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade on top of the five IGCSE subjects.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Barsha and Al Barsha South families ask about most, with the syllabus codes that decide what is actually being taught. Each note names the component where marks go missing rather than restating the syllabus, because the syllabus is on the board's own website and this is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended sets two papers, one calculator-free in most series and one with; Edexcel 4MA1 Higher sets two calculator papers of equal weight. Marks are lost in the same places on both: algebraic manipulation, compound interest and growth, and the trigonometry of non-right-angled triangles. Method marks are available on almost every multi-step question and students throw them away by not writing the working.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Electricity is the reliable problem, and the cause is almost always the same: students can recite the formulae and cannot read a circuit diagram to decide whether components are in series or parallel. The practical paper, or the alternative-to-practical paper where the school enters it, rewards a very specific style of answer about variables, repeats and sources of error that is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and reacting-mass calculations account for a large share of lost marks at Extended, and the failure is usually arithmetic discipline rather than chemistry: units dropped, significant figures abandoned, a mass used where moles were required. Qualitative analysis and ionic equations are the other two reliable gaps, and both respond quickly to drilling against mark schemes.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Biology looks like a memory subject and is actually a command-term subject. Describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different answer shape, and students who write everything they know on a four-mark question score two. Genetics, osmosis and enzyme graphs are the content areas where Extended candidates lose most, usually because the biology is known and the data interpretation is not.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Coordinated Science 0654 is a double award covering all three sciences in two grades; Combined Science 0653 is a single award. The risk in both is coverage: the content is reduced per science but the papers still sample across all three, so a student strong in biology and weak in physics cannot hide. Tutoring works best when it is pointed at the weakest of the three sciences specifically.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500, 0990, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the grade, and the marks sit in audience, form and structure rather than in vocabulary. Students over-prepare content and under-prepare the shape of the answer. Reading questions on 0500 reward quotation selection and brevity; long paraphrase answers routinely score below short precise ones.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Both subjects reward application to the case material in front of the student, and both punish generic answers. Economics marks are won on diagrams drawn early, labelled fully and referred to in the prose; Business Studies marks on evaluation that comes to a conclusion rather than listing advantages and disadvantages. These are the two subjects where technique teaching moves a grade fastest.

subjects.name: ICT and Computer Science (0417, 0478)
subjects.description: ICT 0417 carries practical components that are assessed on skill with specific software operations, which is where students who use the tools casually lose marks. Computer Science 0478 fails students on pseudocode and trace tables rather than on programming, because both are practised less than coding and are tested more directly.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Al Barsha schools serve a large Arabic-speaking population alongside families with no Arabic at home, and KHDA requires the two groups to be taught separately. Placement in the wrong stream is a two-year problem. The IGCSE Arabic examinations are separate from the KHDA mandatory Arabic requirement, and families frequently conflate them.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure (0606, 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB Higher Level maths route, and the single best preparation for either. The content reaches into calculus and advanced trigonometry, so it exposes any weakness in core algebra immediately. Students who take it and struggle are usually struggling with Year 9 algebra rather than with the new material.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barsha.regionsIntro: The districts below are the ones an Al Barsha family actually compares when a lease ends. The notes are operational: what each one does to a school run, which schools it feeds, and what it means for the first workable evening session.

regions.name: Al Barsha 1
regions.note: Red Line Metro at Mall of the Emirates and the densest school cluster in the district. Short pickups, so the earliest realistic weekday session start here is around 16:15, the best in the comparison set.

regions.name: Al Barsha 2
regions.note: Villa compounds behind Umm Suqeim Road with American School of Dubai and Kings' School Al Barsha close by. A 16:30 start works; earlier collides with pickup on the Al Barsha 2 side.

regions.name: Al Barsha 3
regions.note: Further from the Metro and more residential. Families here often run two pickups in opposite directions, which pushes the first workable slot past 17:00 regardless of how tuition is delivered.

regions.name: Al Barsha South
regions.note: No Metro station, car-dependent, and stretching towards Dubai Science Park and Jumeirah Village. Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Safa Community School sit inside it. Adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes to any arriving tutor's journey.

regions.name: Barsha Heights
regions.note: Towers rather than villas, formerly Tecom, on the Red Line. Smaller households, more single-child families, and a clear preference for sessions after a parent commute rather than straight after school.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Immediately east across Sheikh Zayed Road, mixed industrial and residential, with several schools drawing Al Barsha families. The eastbound evening crossing is the slow direction.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: North towards the coast along the Umm Suqeim Road corridor. Students here commonly attend Al Barsha schools, and the northbound run home after pickup is slower than the reverse.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle
regions.note: South-west of Al Barsha South and growing fast, feeding the same southern school cluster. Journey times into Al Barsha at 15:30 are the binding constraint on any in-person arrangement.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha 1, 2 and 3
schoolClusters.note: The core cluster, and genuinely mixed on exam boards: British-curriculum schools entering Cambridge sit alongside schools entering Pearson Edexcel and schools running American or Ministry of Education programmes with no IGCSE at all. The practical effect is that two neighbours' children can sit different mathematics papers.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South, Dubai Science Park and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: The southern cluster leans British and therefore IGCSE-heavy, which is why Al Barsha South generates a disproportionate share of IGCSE enquiries relative to its size. Cohorts in individual subjects can be small, so a student needing a specific option may be one of a handful.

sections.heading: Al Barsha against the districts either side of it
paragraphs: Start with the comparison, because it is what brought most readers here. On everything that touches an arriving tutor, the four districts differ substantially. Al Barsha 1 has a Metro station and a dense school cluster, so pickups are short and a tutor can plausibly be in the room by 16:15. Al Barsha 2 is a villa district behind Umm Suqeim Road with two large schools adjacent, and 16:30 is realistic. Al Barsha 3 is further out and more residential, and families there routinely run two school runs in opposite directions, which pushes everything past 17:00. Al Barsha South has no Metro at all and sprawls towards Dubai Science Park, adding fifteen to twenty-five minutes at the worst hour of the day.

On exam boards the districts differ too, but not in the direction parents expect. The southern cluster around Al Barsha South, Jumeirah Village and Dubai Science Park leans British, so it produces proportionally more IGCSE candidates than its population suggests. The core Al Barsha cluster is more mixed, with American and Ministry of Education programmes sitting alongside British ones. This means a family moving from Al Barsha 1 to Al Barsha South is statistically more likely to end up in an IGCSE cohort, and a family moving the other way may find their child's board changes if they change school.

On tutor pool, which is the variable that actually decides teaching quality, the districts do not differ at all once delivery is online. This is the part that settles the comparison. An in-home tutor's catchment is a drive radius, so moving three kilometres south genuinely shrinks the pool of adults who can reach you at 16:45. A specialist teaching Cambridge 0620 over live video is equally available to Al Barsha 1, Al Barsha South, Barsha Heights and Al Quoz. The geography stops mattering the moment the car stops mattering.

The practical reading of that is straightforward. If you are weighing a move and worrying about tutoring continuity, the worry is misplaced for online delivery and justified for in-home. And if you are already in Al Barsha South and have been told the tutor pool is thinner there, that is true of the in-home market and false of the online one.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, code by code
paragraphs: The comparison that matters more than any geography is the one between boards, and it is the one Al Barsha parents are least often shown. Both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel are examined in the UAE, both are accepted for Ministry of Education equivalency as accredited qualifications, and both are recognised by universities. They are not the same examination. The syllabus codes differ, the paper structures differ, the tiering rules differ, and the practical science assessment differs in a way that affects how a student should be taught.

In mathematics, Cambridge 0580 splits candidates into Core and Extended with different papers and a different grade ceiling, and sets one paper without a calculator in most series. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher and sets two calculator papers of equal weight. A student who has spent two years on 4MA1 and then sits a 0580 past paper will be caught out by the non-calculator work, and a student the other way round will be caught out by the pace of two full calculator papers. Tutoring that ignores which code the school entered is teaching the wrong examination.

In the sciences, Cambridge offers separate Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 alongside Coordinated Science 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single award, each with Core and Extended tiers in most cases. Pearson Edexcel runs single-tier International GCSEs including 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Cambridge schools choose between a practical examination and an alternative-to-practical paper, and which one the school enters changes what a student needs to be able to write about variables and error. Pearson's structure also permits modular entry in some qualifications, meaning a student can sit components in different series rather than all at the end.

What a parent should do with this is short. Find the syllabus code on the entry confirmation or ask the examinations officer. Give it to the tutor before the first lesson. A tutor who asks for it unprompted is a good sign; one who says the content is broadly the same is describing the content and ignoring the papers, which is where the grade is decided.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision and the grade ceiling
paragraphs: The tier decision is the most consequential thing that happens to an IGCSE student in Al Barsha and it is usually made quietly, by set placement, in Year 9. On Cambridge syllabuses with tiers, Core and Extended are different papers with different content and different grade ranges available. A Core entry caps the grade a student can achieve; an Extended entry opens the full range but sets harder papers, and a student entered for Extended who is not ready can come out below what Core would have given them. Pearson Edexcel's Foundation and Higher split works on the same logic with different labels.

The decision is made on evidence or on habit, and in a lot of cases it is habit. A student placed in set three in Year 9 mathematics is frequently steered towards Core by default, and the placement itself may have rested on a single assessment sat shortly after moving schools. In a district like Al Barsha, where families arrive mid-year from other systems with some regularity, that happens more than it should. A student who moved from an Indian or American system in Year 9 may test low in the first fortnight purely because the topic order is different, and then carry that placement into an entry decision two years later.

What a tutor can usefully do here is narrow and valuable. Two or three sessions on the actual Extended content a student would face, followed by a timed Extended paper marked properly, produces real evidence about whether the tier is right. That is a far better basis than a set placement, and it is a conversation the school will engage with if a parent brings a marked script to it. The window for it is the end of Year 10 and the first term of Year 11, before entries are finalised.

The reverse case matters too, and nobody says it. Some students are entered for Extended and should not be. If a student is consistently scoring in the bottom band on Extended papers with eight months to go, a Core entry that produces a secure grade C may serve them better than an Extended entry that produces a D, particularly where the Ministry of Education equivalency threshold is grade E or 3 and the objective is a secure pass in five subjects rather than a top grade in one.

sections.heading: What the market charges, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Price comparisons in this market usually start at the premium end, which flatters the seller. Start at the other end instead. The cheapest real option in Dubai is a budget online tutor, frequently a university student, advertised from AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Scaled to a single weekly hour, Bestimate's Dubai estimates put that at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month. For a Year 10 student who needs homework supervision and someone to keep them at a desk, that is a defensible purchase and there is no reason to spend more.

The next step up is a qualified subject tutor online, at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. On a weekly hour that is around AED 600 to 1,200 a month. This is the band where the tutor can be expected to know the syllabus code, read a mark scheme accurately and diagnose a paper. For most IGCSE work it is the right band, and the jump in usefulness from the budget tier is larger than the jump in price.

Above that, IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, reaching AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more a month in an examination year. The premium tier, named or examiner-led tutors, runs AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED publishing AED 650. And in-home one-to-one visits sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour across tiers, because travel is inside the rate rather than on top of it; monthly in-home packages advertised in this market include AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Two cautions. These are rates published by other providers, read in October 2026, and any of them can change without notice; they are not IB Gram's price list. And the travel premium deserves scrutiny, because it is the one part of a rate that buys no teaching at all. A family paying AED 350 an hour in-home against AED 250 online is paying roughly AED 100 for a car journey, which over a year of weekly sessions is about AED 4,000 for transport. That is a legitimate thing to buy if a physical presence is what the child needs. It is worth knowing that it is what you are buying.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same from either side of Umm Suqeim Road
paragraphs: Pull the two comparisons together and the conclusion is narrower than it looks. The geographic comparison produces real differences, and every one of them is a difference in logistics: Metro access, drive time, pickup overlap, how late a session has to start. The board comparison produces real differences too, and every one of them is a difference in teaching: which paper, which tier, which practical route, which calculator policy. Those are two different kinds of variable, and only the second one changes a grade.

This is why a family in Al Barsha South and a family in Al Barsha 1 end up with the same recommendation. The logistics problem is solved by removing the car from the arrangement, which online delivery does identically in both districts. The teaching problem is solved by matching to the syllabus code, which is also identical in both districts. The thing that differs between them has been taken out of the equation, and the thing that matters was never geographic to begin with.

There is one honest exception, and it is worth naming rather than glossing. A young child, or a student with an attention or organisational difficulty that makes an unsupervised screen genuinely unworkable, benefits from an adult in the room in a way that no amount of specialist matching replaces. For that student the in-home market is the right market and the AED 180 to 500 band is the budget. For an IGCSE candidate in Year 10 or 11 working towards a June or November series, the specialist usually matters more than the proximity, and the money spent on the drive buys nothing.

The second thing worth taking from the comparison is about moving house. Families in this cluster move between these districts frequently, and an in-home tutoring arrangement often does not survive the move, because the tutor's catchment changes even when the family's school does not. An online arrangement does survive it, along with the schedule, the tutor and the written record of what has been covered. That is a small practical point and it decides more cases than it should.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency and the five-subject rule
paragraphs: The single most consequential fact on the British track in the UAE has nothing to do with tutoring and everything to do with what an IGCSE set is for. For Ministry of Education equivalency, students on the British curriculum must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must additionally submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is the one families get wrong, and so does at least one competitor page ranking for these searches, which tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The correct rule is five accredited subjects at no less than E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count. A student taking exactly five subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, has three towards the requirement and a problem that only becomes visible when an application is assembled.

For comparison, because Al Barsha households frequently contain children on different tracks, the American route works differently. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no figure we will publish, because none has been read on an official Ministry of Education source; any points threshold circulating on a tutoring page should be checked against moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly.

Two things follow. Equivalency is a regulatory process carried out by the Ministry and the attestation authority, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not required for it. And the time to check the subject count is Year 9, when options are chosen, not Year 11, when they are fixed. A single conversation with the school's university counsellor at the right moment is worth more than a year of tuition at the wrong one.

sections.heading: Who may tutor your child in Dubai, and what a permit does not tell you
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, and both halves of that sentence matter. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Eligibility is deliberately broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools may hold the permit, as may employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. That breadth is the point to take away: the permit establishes that somebody may lawfully charge for lessons. It establishes nothing whatever about whether they can teach Cambridge 0620 Extended. A provider that leads with permit status as a quality signal is answering a question you did not ask.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, which means any specific amount quoted on a tutoring page is not sourced; the ministry did not specify fine amounts or detail the penalties. Separately, Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct similarly bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than taken from the current ADEK document, so verify it there before relying on the exact wording, but the principle is clear enough that no family should be paying their child's own classroom teacher for private lessons.

On our own status, plainly: IB Gram holds no KHDA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and does not describe its tutors as approved by any of them. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument for training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Any page claiming its tutors are approved by KHDA either holds that permit and can show the number, or is saying something that is not true.

sections.heading: Getting started in this cluster, and where availability runs out
paragraphs: The sequence is short and it starts with a document rather than a conversation. Send the syllabus code from the entry confirmation, the school, the year group, and either a recent marked paper or the mock result breakdown. That is enough for a specialist in the right code to be identified. A trial lesson at no cost follows, at a time that works around the school run in your district, and after it you get a written view of what the work should cover before the next series. Nothing is paid before the trial and nothing is committed after it.

The subjects where availability is tightest in this cluster are predictable: Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure 4PM1, the separate sciences at Extended in the weeks immediately before a series, and Arabic as a first language, where the stream requirement narrows the field. Where no specialist in the exact code is free at the hour an Al Barsha family needs, we will tell you which of three things applies: another slot with the right person, a date when they free up, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same code over the same live video at the same Gulf Standard Time hour. We will not substitute a generalist and describe it as a match.

Timing through the Dubai year has its own shape. The first workable weekday slot runs from about 16:15 in Al Barsha 1 to around 17:00 in Al Barsha 3 and Al Barsha South. Ramadan moves families to post-Iftar sessions and the shortened school day opens a late-morning window. The July and August break is the most underused window in the IGCSE calendar: a Year 10 student going into Year 11 can close an algebra gap in six weeks of quiet work that will otherwise be fought over in February alongside nine other subjects.

On the enquiry form, since it collects information about a minor: we ask for year group, subject, syllabus code, school and a parent contact. We do not need a photograph, a full report card or identity documents to arrange a trial. Anything sent for diagnosis, such as a marked script, is used for that alone, and you can ask for it to be deleted at any point. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the framework, and the privacy link on this page sets out retention and the deletion route.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not just the subject
process.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are different examinations with different papers and tiering. The code is on the entry confirmation or available from the school's examinations officer, and handing it over before the first lesson is the single most useful thing a parent can do.

process.title: Send something marked
process.description: A mock script with the marks on it, or a recent assessment breakdown, tells a specialist in five minutes what a half-hour call cannot. Where nothing marked exists, the tutor sets a short diagnostic inside the trial lesson and works from that instead.

process.title: Trial with the specialist who would teach it
process.description: A no-cost lesson with the tutor who would actually take the course, at a time that fits the school run in your district. The question to ask yourself afterwards is whether they identified the paper and the topic where marks are going before you told them.

process.title: Settle the tier question early
process.description: Where Core or Extended is still open, two or three sessions plus one timed Extended paper marked to the scheme produces real evidence. Bring the marked script to the school. Entries close months before the series, and after that the decision is made.

process.title: Review at the halfway mark
process.description: Four weeks in, timed work either shows movement against the error log or it does not. If it does not, the right response is to change the diagnosis or the tutor rather than add hours, and we would rather say that at week four than at week ten.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A tutor is assigned against 0580 or 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1, and against the tier the school entered. Past papers from the wrong board are not interchangeable practice, and a tutor who treats them as such is teaching a different examination from the one the student will sit.

whyPoints.title: The same bench from every district
whyPoints.description: A student in Al Barsha South reaches exactly the same specialists as one in Al Barsha 1, because the catchment is not a drive radius. This is the whole practical argument for online delivery in a cluster where families move between districts regularly.

whyPoints.title: The tier decision treated as a decision
whyPoints.description: Core against Extended is a grade-ceiling choice usually made by Year 9 set placement and rarely revisited. We will produce the evidence to revisit it, with a marked timed paper the school can look at, in the window before entries close.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown with their sources and their date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it and dated to October 2026. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not what a Dubai family pays in.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A ranking competitor publishes six subjects. Getting this wrong costs a family an application, not a grade.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in the exact code is free when you need one, you get the real position and the real alternatives, including a tutor outside the UAE delivering over the same live video. The option we do not offer is a generalist presented as a specialist.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor in Al Barsha cost?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and monthly in-home packages advertised in this market run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with AED 799 a month for eight sessions advertised at the lower end. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's rates. The gap between the in-home and online bands is essentially the cost of the drive, which over a year of weekly sessions is a meaningful amount of money for no additional teaching.

faqs.question: Is the tutor pool genuinely better in Al Barsha 1 than in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: For in-home tutoring, yes. Al Barsha 1 sits on the Red Line with a dense school cluster, so more tutors can reach it quickly; Al Barsha South has no Metro station and adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes of driving at the worst hour of the day, which shrinks the catchment. For online tutoring the difference disappears completely, because the catchment is not a drive radius. A student in Al Barsha South 4 is matched against the same specialists as one beside Mall of the Emirates, at the same hour, with no travel in the price.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's Al Barsha school use, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: It varies within the district, which is exactly why it has to be checked rather than assumed. British-curriculum schools in this cluster enter both, and some schools split by subject, entering Cambridge for sciences and Pearson Edexcel for mathematics or the reverse. The reliable source is the entry confirmation or the school's examinations officer, who will give you the syllabus code. That code is what a tutor needs: 0580 and 4MA1 have different paper structures, different tier labels and a different calculator policy, so past papers from one are not practice for the other.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: On evidence rather than on set placement. Core caps the available grade but sets accessible papers; Extended opens the full range and sets a steep final third. The useful test is a full Extended past paper, timed and marked against the published mark scheme, with the result looked at alongside two more. Consistency matters more than one good score. If the post-16 plan needs A Level or IB Higher Level in that subject, Extended is usually necessary; if the objective is a secure pass across five subjects for equivalency, a safe Core grade can be the better buy.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry of Education actually count?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one competitor page ranking for these searches states six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted in the five equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The Ministry of Education's clarification is explicit that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. This catches families who take exactly five subjects including those two and discover in Year 12 that they have three. The separate point is that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, so a student is taking them anyway; they simply do not count towards the equivalency total and have to be planned around when options are chosen in Year 9.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE examinations actually sat in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Always check the live official timetable rather than a date restated elsewhere.

faqs.question: If lessons happen over video, who assesses the science practical work?
faqs.answer: Practical skills are assessed by the school and the board, not by a tutor, and the route depends on the entry. Cambridge schools choose between a practical examination and an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson Edexcel assesses practical skills within the written papers. In every case the marks come from writing about method: independent and dependent variables, controls, repeats, sources of error and how to reduce them. That is a written skill with a recognisable mark-scheme vocabulary, and it is taught perfectly well over video. The hands-on laboratory work itself happens at school.

faqs.question: What does modular entry mean with Pearson Edexcel, and does it help?
faqs.answer: In some Pearson Edexcel qualifications a student can sit components in different series rather than all at the end of Year 11, banking a result and carrying it forward. Where a school offers it, the benefit is load-spreading: a student sits fewer papers in one sitting and can resit a single weak component rather than a whole subject. The cost is that early entries are sat on less teaching. Cambridge entries are generally taken as a complete set at the end. Whether the option exists at all is a school decision, so ask the examinations officer before planning around it.

faqs.question: My child is already in Year 11. Is it too late to start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, but what tutoring can achieve narrows as the series approaches. With two terms left, past-paper technique, command-term handling and the recurring errors a mock exposes are all still very much in play, and those are often worth a grade on their own. With six weeks left, it is paper practice and error correction only; learning a topic from nothing is no longer realistic. The honest first step either way is a marked mock script read question by question. If the losses cluster, the job is tractable. If they are even across everything, the conversation is about expectations rather than hours.

faqs.question: Can one child be entered with Cambridge for science and Edexcel for maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this cluster it happens more often than parents realise, because schools sometimes enter Cambridge for one department and Pearson Edexcel for another. It has no effect on university recognition or on Ministry of Education equivalency, which counts accredited subjects regardless of board. It does affect tutoring, because it means a single student may need past papers from two boards with different paper structures and different question styles. Collect every syllabus code at the start of Year 10 and keep them in one place; it saves a conversation every term.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students in this part of Dubai struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Extended mathematics and the separate sciences, consistently. Within those, four specific areas account for most of the lost marks: algebraic manipulation without a calculator, moles and reacting-mass calculations in Chemistry, series and parallel circuit reasoning in Physics, and data interpretation in Biology where the content is known but the graph is not. English Language is the quiet fifth, because students prepare content and not answer structure. All five are narrow enough to be targeted in four to six sessions once a marked script identifies which one applies.

faqs.question: Are group classes a reasonable cheaper option for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For some purposes. A small group works where the need is pace and content coverage, and where every student in it is on the same syllabus code and the same tier. It stops working the moment the requirement is diagnostic, because a group cannot be pointed at one student's specific recurring error. We deliver one-to-one only, so the honest answer is that a tuition centre group class in Dubai is cheaper per hour and is the right purchase for a student who needs structure rather than diagnosis. For a tier decision or a single weak paper, it is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: We are moving from Al Barsha to Al Barsha South mid-year. Does tutoring have to change?
faqs.answer: Not if it is online. The tutor, the schedule and the record of what has been covered all move with you, because nothing about the arrangement depends on the address. This is a practical reason families in this cluster end up with online delivery even when they started out looking for a home tutor: moves within New Dubai are common, leases end on their own timetable, and an in-home arrangement frequently does not survive one because the tutor's catchment changes. If your child is also changing school, send the new syllabus codes, since they may not match the old ones.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE tutor be matched for a family in this district?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects at the common codes, usually within a few days, because the constraint is the hour rather than the specialist. Tight cases are Additional Mathematics, Further Pure, Arabic as a first language and the separate sciences in the fortnight before a series, when demand concentrates. If no specialist in the exact code is free at the time you need, you will be told which of three things applies: a different slot with the right tutor, a named date when they free up, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching the same code over the same video at the same hour.

intro.heading: Two questions in one search, and the second one is urgent
paragraphs: A parent typing IGCSE home tutor in Al Barsha South is usually asking two things. The first is logistical: can somebody come to the house, and what does that cost. The second is the one that actually decides a grade: is there still enough time before the series, and if so what should the next two months contain. This page answers the first honestly and then spends most of its length on the second, because the calendar is where the money either works or does not.

So, the home-tutoring question, answered without evasion. There is a real market for it in Dubai and its published rates are known. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one visits including travel at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and independently advertised home tutors run from AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly packages circulate at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions in the home. By comparison, qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150 for IGCSE by Unitors, specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and the budget end of the online market advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Those are the providers' own figures, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

IB Gram's own position is fixed and stated the same way on every UAE page. Tuition for families here is one-to-one online tuition delivered over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; tutors are not sent to UAE addresses, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. If what your household needs is a person physically present, that is a legitimate requirement and this is not the right provider for it. If the requirement is really somebody who can teach the exact paper your child sits at a time that works after the Al Barsha South school run, read on, because that is what the rest of this page is about.

Now the urgent question. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, which matters because general advice circulating online quotes its dates to Gulf parents. The datable anchors that do apply are Pearson's: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs June and November and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, with an explicit warning that the correct zone timetable must be used.

Those dates are the frame for everything that follows. The point of a calendar page is that the same money buys very different amounts depending on when it is spent, and that an honest provider will tell a family in March what cannot be achieved by May rather than selling them a plan that assumes it can.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barsha-sout.programmesIntro: Support in the IGCSE years is bought at four distinct points in a calendar, and what each point can deliver differs sharply. The notes below describe them by remaining time rather than by difficulty.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10, the coverage year
programmes.description: The year in which a syllabus can be covered rather than selected from. Cambridge and Pearson both run two-year courses, and the content met in Year 10 is the content Year 11 assumes. A weekly session here, aligned to the school's scheme of work, is the lowest cost per mark available in the whole sequence, because nothing is being repaired against a deadline and tier readiness can still be assessed before the centre's entry decision.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha South families rarely buy here, and the reason is understandable: nothing has gone wrong yet. The arithmetic is still against waiting. A weekly session across Year 10 at the mid-market band costs less in total than a three-session-a-week programme in the spring of Year 11, and it produces coverage rather than triage.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11, the technique year
programmes.description: Coverage finishes, mocks happen, final entries are confirmed and the papers arrive. The useful work shifts from teaching content to teaching how marks are awarded: method shown, accuracy held, answers in the form the question demanded, questions not abandoned after an early error. This is the year families buy in, usually after a mock, and the window that follows a mock is genuinely productive.
programmes.countryNote: The one Year 11 date worth chasing early in this catchment is the centre's final entry confirmation, because it fixes the tier. Once Extended or Higher is confirmed, the past-paper diet is settled; once Core or Foundation is confirmed, a grade ceiling applies and no amount of teaching exceeds it.

programmes.name: The November series as a resit route
programmes.description: A grade that falls short in June can be retaken in November. Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the preparation window after August results is roughly eight to ten weeks and the new grade arrives in January. Cambridge also runs a November series; confirm entry arrangements with the centre.
programmes.countryNote: Whether a resit is worth buying in Al Barsha South depends on what the January grade is for. If the sixth-form or university application it was meant to support closes before January, the money buys a corrected transcript rather than an opened door. That may still be worth it, and it should be a decision rather than a reflex.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the clock starts
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention point and the only one with no deadline attached. The work is algebraic fluency, proportional reasoning and scientific vocabulary: the things Extended and Higher tier papers assume without teaching. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October and provide a school with a benchmark rather than a certificate.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Barsha South, where many families have arrived recently from other systems, this band is also where a curriculum gap is most cheaply closed. A student who joined a British-curriculum school in Year 8 from an American or Indian system has a specific and identifiable gap, and closing it before Year 10 costs a fraction of closing it in Year 11.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-barsha-sout.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Barsha South families most often ask about, with the syllabus codes and a note on how much calendar each one needs, since time rather than difficulty is the constraint this page is about.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject and the one most sensitive to tier. Extended and Higher carry algebraic fractions, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and vectors. Needs the longest calendar of any subject because the topics build on each other, so a late start here achieves less than a late start in a content-heavy subject.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Electricity and circuit reasoning take the most time to repair, and graph work where a gradient becomes a physical quantity with units recurs across the paper. The alternative-to-practical paper is the fastest win available in this subject and can be taught in three or four sessions at any point in the year.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles and concentration calculations need consecutive weeks because they rest on proportional reasoning. Organic chemistry reorganised by reaction type rather than by name list is a two or three session job with a large return. Qualitative analysis recall is efficiently learned late in the calendar.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The most forgiving subject for a late start, because the losses are linguistic rather than cumulative. Command-term precision, describing against explaining, and naming a structure with its function are teachable in two or three sessions and then self-sustaining, which makes biology a sensible first purchase when time is short.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 · 0653)
subjects.description: Needs a scope-setting session before anything else, because freely available revision material is written for separate sciences and covers topics these routes exclude. Two sessions establishing what is out of scope saves more time than any amount of teaching, and the saving is largest when the calendar is tight.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 · 0990 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Marked against band descriptors rather than a scheme of facts, so improvement comes from structure and timing rather than content coverage. That makes it unusually responsive to a short calendar: a student who writes well and ignores the question's command verb can move bands within a few weeks of focused work.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0993)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different descriptors. The listening paper is where marks leak, usually from writing a full phrase where a single word was wanted. Exam technique here is worth more than vocabulary work and responds quickly, which again suits a short window.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 · 0450)
subjects.description: Both marked against levels rather than points, so evaluation outranks recall. Students who list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement cap below the top band regardless of knowledge. Teaching judgement structure is short work and is often the single highest-return intervention in these subjects.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 · 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode convention and trace-table discipline are the recurring losses, and both are trainable. Students describe what a program does instead of tracing what it outputs. Requires less calendar than mathematics and more than biology, because the technique has to be practised rather than understood.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in every Dubai private school. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups prohibited.

sections.heading: The home-tutoring question, answered properly
paragraphs: Families in Al Barsha South ask about home tutoring for sensible reasons. The district is spread out, the evenings are busy, and having somebody arrive removes the organising burden from a parent who is already running a household. It is a real service with a real market here and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection.

What it costs is published. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one visits including travel at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, independently advertised home tutors run from AED 200 to AED 500, and monthly packages circulate at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions in the home. What it costs in time is less often discussed and matters more in this district than in most. A tutor travelling between two addresses within Al Barsha South loses meaningful time; a tutor arriving from the Al Barsha cluster or from further east at the evening peak loses twenty to forty minutes each way. That time is recovered inside the rate, and it caps a visiting tutor's day at two students in this district where it might be three in a denser one.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards
paragraphs: This is the part of the search that decides the outcome. The same money spent in September and in March buys very different things, and a family can see which by counting backwards from the series their child is entered for. UAE candidates sit the June series or the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so dates quoted for it do not apply to a child in Dubai, however often they appear in general advice.

The table below is a counted-back plan rather than a list of dates, because the dates that matter most are the centre's. It assigns realistic session counts and costs at the mid-market online band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, which are market figures and not IB Gram prices. The pattern it shows is consistent across subjects: the earlier phases buy coverage, which cannot be compressed, and the later phases buy technique, which can.

Two rows deserve emphasis. The twenty-four to twenty-week row is the cheapest and most skipped: confirming board, code and tier from the statement of entry, and listing the syllabus gaps. One or two sessions, AED 150 to AED 600, against a decision that governs the whole year. And the twelve-to-eight-week row, where whole timed papers start being marked against the published scheme by somebody other than the student, which is the point at which a tutoring arrangement acquires a diagnosis rather than a feeling.

The row families most often arrive at is four to eight weeks out, and the honest answer there is that technique moves and content does not. At that point a plan should include a written list of topics being deliberately abandoned with the reason. Families find that list uncomfortable and it is the most valuable document in the arrangement, because the alternative is covering everything thinly and securing nothing.
