sections.heading: Why the entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: The single most useful calendar fact for an Al Barsha South parent is that the decisions which bind a candidate are taken long before the papers are sat. Entries are confirmed by the centre. Tier is fixed at that point. Timetables are issued per series and, for Cambridge, per zone. By the time a family is worried enough to search for a tutor, several of the choices that shape the outcome have already been made by somebody else.

Cambridge's arrangement is worth understanding precisely. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge's exams officers' guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the exams officer for the zone and the dated timetable in the same email as the entry confirmation.

Pearson's is datable and worth writing down. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The useful habit is to collect the three school-held items early: the statement of entry, the zone and dated timetable, and the mock window. All three are free and all three change what a sensible tutoring plan looks like.

sections.heading: Al Barsha South geography and what a visit costs in minutes
paragraphs: This district is the reason the home-tutoring question gets asked here more than in denser parts of Dubai, so it is worth being concrete about the distances rather than gesturing at traffic.

Al Barsha South 1, 2 and 3 are spread out, with villa and townhouse streets and schools distributed across them rather than clustered. Jumeirah Village Circle and Jumeirah Village Triangle sit immediately south, dense internally and slow to leave at the peak. Dubai Science Park and Arjan sit north-east with a largely working population. Motor City and Dubai Sports City sit further inland again, and the crossings into the Al Barsha cluster go over Umm Suqeim Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, both slow between five and seven.

The practical consequence is a working-day ceiling. A visiting tutor in a dense district can fit three students into an afternoon and evening. In Al Barsha South, with twenty to forty minute journeys at the peak, two is realistic. That lost hour has to be recovered inside the rate, which is why the published in-home band reaches AED 500 at its top end, and it is also why the latest slot a visiting tutor can offer is set by whoever they saw before you.

The mirror-image fact is where the calendar comes back in. A pre-series block needs frequency to rise from one session a week to two or three for eight to twelve weeks, and then fall again. For a visiting arrangement that means rebuilding a route twice in a term, which is why in-home providers in districts like this one prefer selling fixed monthly packages of longer sessions. For an online arrangement it is a scheduling change. The flexibility the calendar demands is the thing the geography makes expensive.

sections.heading: November as the resit route, and the January consequence
paragraphs: Some of the most expensive IGCSE tutoring in Dubai is bought in the last week of August, and a lot of it is bought without a clear view of what the November grade will be used for. The arithmetic takes twenty minutes and is worth doing before any money changes hands.

The datable sequence is Pearson's. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a family deciding in the third week of August has roughly eight to ten weeks of preparation, and the new grade arrives in January. Cambridge also runs a November series; entry arrangements and the zone-correct timetable come from the centre.

The question that should precede the purchase is what the January grade is for. If it supports a sixth-form place, an apprenticeship or a university application that closes before January, the money buys a corrected transcript rather than an opened door. That can still be the right purchase, particularly where a subject is a prerequisite for a chosen A Level, and it should be a decision taken with the facts rather than a reflex taken in the week results arrive.

At two sessions a week on the mid band, an eight to ten week resit block is roughly AED 2,400 to AED 6,000, with specialist rates higher. What that block can realistically do is the same as any late-phase block: technique, timing, answer forms, units and the two or three recurring errors an error log exposes. It cannot teach a syllabus from a standing start, and nobody should promise a specific grade from it in any window.

sections.heading: Mock weeks, Ramadan and the weeks not to buy
paragraphs: A calendar-led plan should also name the weeks where paying the usual fee buys nothing. There are three in a UAE academic year and all three are visible in September.

Mock weeks are the first. A school running mocks across two weeks takes the student's evenings for revision across every subject at once, and a normal content session dropped into that period is one nobody can prepare for. Front-load in the fortnight before, then switch to short technique work or pause. The mock's value is the script rather than the grade: a marked paper showing whether losses were method, accuracy, answer form, units or abandoned questions is the diagnosis the whole technique phase works against.

Ramadan is the second and it falls within the academic year. School hours shorten and evening study moves to after Iftar. Sessions can shift to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards. The thing that damages plans is improvising that in the second week rather than agreeing it in advance, because a month of half-attended sessions lands wherever the heaviest work happens to sit. If a school's mock window falls near Ramadan, that collision is worth seeing early.

End-of-term breaks are the third, and the useful move is counter-intuitive. Two or three sessions in the final week of a break, previewing what the term opens with, are worth more than the same sessions in the first week. For Year 11 students specifically, the break before the final term is the last stretch of uninterrupted time available, and it is the cheapest place to put a whole-paper run. Frequency changes of that kind are straightforward when no route has to be rebuilt around them.

sections.heading: How families in this district actually choose
paragraphs: Having set out both the home-tutoring market and the calendar, it is worth describing honestly how the decision tends to get made here, because the pattern is consistent and recognising it is useful.

Most families start with proximity because a search box offers proximity. They then discover one of two things. Either the available local tutor does not teach the right syllabus code, which emerges in the first month when the past papers look unfamiliar; or the available local tutor is excellent and can only offer five o'clock, which works until the term's third fixture clash. Both discoveries happen around week six, which in a Year 11 autumn is expensive timing.

The families who do best tend to work in the other order. They obtain the statement of entry first, so the syllabus code and tier are known. They decide the hour the household can genuinely protect, which in Al Barsha South is usually later than they first assume. Then they look for somebody who teaches that code and is free at that hour. Doing it that way removes both week-six discoveries before they happen.

On the home-visiting question specifically, the honest framing is this. Presence is worth paying for where the student will not engage with a screen, or where supervision rather than teaching is the real need, and a household in that position should buy it locally and read the calendar sections of this page anyway. Where the need is really a competent teacher of a specific paper at an hour that survives a busy week, the travel component of the published AED 180 to AED 500 band is buying a journey. IB Gram sells only the online version in the UAE and says so rather than leaving a parent to find out.

sections.heading: Permit, claims and what a parent can verify for nothing
paragraphs: Whichever format a family chooses, four checks cost nothing and matter more than any marketing claim. They apply equally to a visiting tutor and an online one.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you; a figure circulating as a fixed sum could not be verified.

The teacher question, which arises constantly in a district where everybody knows which teacher is strong. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against current policy, but the direction is unambiguous: arranging for your child's own subject teacher to tutor them for money is arranging something the teacher may not be permitted to do.

The accreditation and premises question. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it regulates schools rather than tutoring platforms. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. Any provider describing itself as approved should produce the permit or centre number. And nobody should be selling you past papers or mark schemes as a download bundle: those belong to the awarding bodies and should be referenced and linked at source.

faqs.question: Can we get a tutor to come to our house in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for UAE families here is one-to-one online tuition over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service offered only in India, so tutors are not sent to UAE addresses. There is a local market for home visits and its published rates are AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel at Bestimate, with independently advertised home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. A household that genuinely needs a person present should hire locally and still read the calendar sections of this page.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor in this part of Dubai charge per month?
faqs.answer: Published monthly packages in this market run AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions in the home, against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who publish them, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: How much time does a visiting tutor lose travelling in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Twenty to forty minutes each way at the evening peak, depending on whether the journey is internal to Al Barsha South or crossing from the Al Barsha cluster, Motor City or Al Quoz. The district is spread out and the crossings use Umm Suqeim Road and Sheikh Zayed Road. The practical consequence is that a visiting tutor fits two students into an evening here where a denser district might allow three, and that lost hour is recovered inside the published rate.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Al Barsha South sit?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with an explicit warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March series is offered to India only.

faqs.question: Is there still time if the papers are eight weeks away?
faqs.answer: Enough for technique and not enough for a syllabus. Eight weeks moves timing, answer forms, units, method presentation and the two or three recurring errors a marked script exposes, and at two sessions a week on the mid band of AED 150 to AED 300 that is roughly AED 2,400 to AED 4,800. What it cannot do is teach a topic nobody covered. An honest plan at that point names in writing which topics are being abandoned and why, which is uncomfortable and better than the alternative.

faqs.question: When does the centre fix my child's tier, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: At final entry confirmation, which the centre controls and which usually happens in the first half of Year 11. It matters because tier sets a ceiling: Cambridge 0580 Core caps at grade C, or 5 on the numeric variant, and Pearson 4MA1 Foundation caps at grade 5. A student entered at the lower tier who is capable of the higher one is paying for teaching against a ceiling. One timed paper at each tier, marked to the published scheme, settles the question with evidence before the deadline.

faqs.question: What should we ask the exams officer for?
faqs.answer: Four things in one email. The statement of entry, which names board, syllabus code and tier for every subject. The centre's Cambridge administrative zone, since Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. The dated timetable for the series. And the school's mock examination window. All four are free, all four change what a sensible tutoring plan looks like, and most families never ask for any of them.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth paying for after August results?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the January grade is for, and that question should precede the purchase. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, its November 2026 papers run from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So the preparation window is roughly eight to ten weeks and the grade arrives in January. If the application it was meant to support closes before January, the money buys a corrected transcript rather than an opened door.

faqs.question: How should we handle mock weeks in the tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: Front-load before and lighten during. A school running mocks over two weeks takes the student's evenings for revision across every subject simultaneously, and a normal content session dropped into that is one nobody can prepare for. The mock's real value is the script rather than the grade: a marked paper showing whether losses were method, accuracy, answer form, units or abandoned questions gives the technique phase something concrete to work against for the following two months.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and evening study moves to after Iftar, so sessions shift to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards. The thing that damages plans is improvising that in the second week rather than agreeing it in advance, because a month of half-attended sessions lands wherever the heaviest work happens to sit. If the school's mock window falls near Ramadan, that collision is worth identifying in September rather than discovering in February.

faqs.question: Which subject should we support first if the calendar is short?
faqs.answer: Usually the one where the losses are linguistic or technical rather than cumulative, because those move fastest. Biology responds in two or three sessions to command-term precision work. English Language is marked against band descriptors, so structure and timing work can move a band quickly. Mathematics needs the longest calendar because its topics build on each other, so a late start there achieves less per session. A diagnostic hour on a marked script will say which applies to your child.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IGCSE subjects to save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether the underlying problem is shared. A student losing marks in physics and chemistry to algebra rather than to science has one problem presenting as two, and one tutor can close it once. Where the two subjects need different specialist knowledge, two tutors usually beat one generalist. On cost: two subjects at one weekly session each on the mid band is roughly AED 1,200 to AED 2,400 a month, and the student's available evenings are a real limit too.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it raise the price?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it adds nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Why is self-marking past papers not enough in the final weeks?
faqs.answer: Because a candidate cannot see a mistake they do not know is a mistake. Self-marked scores drift upward while the same method errors repeat, which is why a student can complete eight papers and report improvement with no change in outcome. Marking against the published scheme shows whether a lost mark was method, accuracy, answer form, units or timing, and those five need different fixes. In the last eight weeks that distinction is the whole of the diagnosis.

faqs.question: My child joined a school in Al Barsha South mid-course. What first?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic hour that maps what the previous school actually taught against the new school's scheme of work, because schools sequence topics differently and the previous grades describe a different subset of the course. Mid-course arrivals are frequent in Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills. The same session should confirm the board, code and tier at the new centre, since all three can change with a move, and produce a written gap list with a week count attached.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai tutoring provider claim accreditation from KHDA?
faqs.answer: Not legitimately, unless it holds the relevant permit and can show the number. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and regulates schools rather than tutoring platforms. An operation with premises and staff here needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and claims no board or regulator accreditation of any kind.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.tutorsIntro: These are the tutor profiles Al Furjan families are matched with for Year 10 and Year 11: teachers who work to one board's syllabus codes and mark schemes rather than a general subject outline, and who can name the paper your child is losing marks on.

intro.heading: The board question comes before the tutor question
paragraphs: Al Furjan sends children to British-curriculum schools in four directions, and those schools do not all enter the same board. Some run Cambridge International, some Pearson Edexcel, and a few split by department so a student sits Cambridge Mathematics and Edexcel Physics in the same year. The syllabus codes differ, the paper structure differs, the tiering differs, and the grade boundaries are published separately. A tutor who knows IGCSE Maths in general and 0580 in particular are not the same person.

This is the most common and most avoidable failure in the Dubai home-tutoring market. A parent in the Masakin or Quortaj districts hires a tutor who can reach Al Furjan by 17:00, the tutor is competent, and six weeks later the student is still underperforming because the practice papers are from the wrong board. Nothing about the lesson looks wrong. The command terms, the formula sheet and the number of papers are simply not the ones the student will sit.

The second constraint in this community is the clock. Al Furjan is a villa and townhouse community between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, and the school buses run long loops across its districts. Arrival times spread from 15:20 to 16:10, and Year 11 students with after-school revision sessions are later still. Any tutoring arrangement that ignores this loses two sessions a month to traffic and fixtures.

IB Gram answers both constraints the same way. We match on the board and syllabus code your child is entered for, and we deliver every lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Saying that plainly costs us some enquiries from families who want someone at the door, and saves everyone else a wasted phone call.

One more thing is worth saying before the detail. The useful tutoring year for an IGCSE student begins in Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11. A tutor who sees marked class work every week through Year 10 finds the tiering problem or the algebra fluency gap while there is still a year to fix it, and the total cost over two years comes out lower than a single intensive term in the spring. The families in this community who get the strongest results are almost always the ones who started before anything looked urgent.

What follows is written for a Year 10 or Year 11 family in this corridor. It sets out how to find out which board your child is entered for, what Core and Extended tiering does to the grade ceiling, the June and November series counted backwards from results day, what the Dubai market charges per month rather than per hour, and where the line sits on coursework. Every AED figure is attributed to the provider who published it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Al Furjan students arrive at IGCSE from several directions, and what they need from a tutor depends on which route they took. These are the three stages that matter either side of the Year 11 exams.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE begins, where the gaps that later cap a grade are formed. Algebraic fluency, the ability to rearrange a formula without guessing, and writing a paragraph that answers the question asked are the three skills that decide whether Extended tier is viable. Assessment is school-set, so there is no external signal and a student can look fine on a report while carrying a gap that becomes visible in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Furjan this is the stage where tutoring is cheapest and most effective, and the stage families most often skip. Year 8 and Year 9 students are home earlier than Year 11 students, so a 16:30 slot works, and one session a week for two terms in Year 9 is a smaller investment than a Year 11 rescue block. It is also the moment to confirm which board the school enters, because the Year 9 choices decide the tier.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, and a final grade set almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge grades 9 to 1 alongside A* to G in some subjects; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Tiering in mathematics and the sciences caps the grade available, and the decision is made at entry rather than at the exam. Most marks are lost to command-term errors and to method marks not shown, not to missing content.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Al Furjan enquiries sit. Year 11 students in this corridor are home between 15:40 and 16:30 depending on the school and the route, with later arrivals on days with school revision clinics. A 17:00 or 17:30 slot is the realistic pattern, moving to two shorter sessions a week through the mock window. Students entered for the November series run on a different rhythm and need support through the UAE summer.

programmes.name: What follows IGCSE: Advanced Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: The Year 11 grade profile determines which post-16 route is open. Most British-curriculum schools require grade 6 or 7 in a subject before accepting it at Advanced Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asks for the same. Students who sat Core tier mathematics frequently find both routes closed in that subject, which is why the tiering decision deserves a conversation in Year 10 rather than a shrug.
programmes.countryNote: Al Furjan families moving from IGCSE into the IB Diploma usually change schools to do it, because the full Diploma is thinner on the ground in the Jebel Ali corridor than further north. The gap between Extended IGCSE mathematics and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is the widest single transition in this set, and it is worth four to six weeks of bridging work over the summer rather than a scramble in the first term.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency track
programmes.ageRange: Applies at the end of school
programmes.description: Not a programme but a requirement that shapes subject choice. The published British-track rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Students who learn this in Year 13 have no room to act on it.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Al Furjan planning on a UAE university place should read the rule in Year 9. The exclusion of Arabic and Islamic Education from the five-subject count catches people out, because those are subjects every Dubai private school teaches by KHDA requirement. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency; it is a Ministry process and the Ministry's own channel is where current requirements should be checked.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Requests from Al Furjan concentrate on the subjects where board differences bite hardest: mathematics, the sciences and English. Each note names the syllabus code families should check on their child's entry form.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers in each tier, one with a calculator and one without in some entries. Extended tier reaches grade 9; Core is capped. Marks are lost in method rather than answer, especially in multi-step algebra and in bearings and transformations questions where working is not shown.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Sat alongside the main mathematics entry by students heading for Advanced Level maths or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities arrive a year early. It is the best available bridge into Diploma mathematics and the most under-taught subject in this corridor.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, forces and motion, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. The Cambridge entry includes a practical component with an alternative-to-practical option; the Edexcel route differs. Students lose marks on graph gradients, on unit conversion, and on describing an experiment without naming the control variables.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, moles and stoichiometry, organic chemistry and chemical tests. Mole calculations and the chemical tests table account for a large share of lost marks. Students who learn the tests as a list rather than as observations and conclusions lose them in the exam even when they know the chemistry.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, genetics, ecology and human physiology. The subject rewards precise language and punishes vague cause-and-effect answers. Genetic crosses and the required practical techniques are the two places where a few sessions change the grade substantially.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award science taken instead of three separate subjects. The content is reduced but the paper structure still covers all three disciplines, so a student weak in one area carries it into every paper. Al Furjan families should check which award the school has entered, since it affects Advanced Level eligibility.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. The reading questions reward selective quotation and precise explanation of effect, not summary. Most lost marks come from students writing everything they noticed rather than answering the specific question in the paper.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts, unseen poetry and extract-based essay questions. The grade depends on argument structure and embedded quotation rather than quantity of plot recall. Timed essay practice with marked feedback is the intervention that moves this subject, and it needs to start before the mock window.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram-led analysis in economics and case-study application in business. Both are command-term subjects: explain, analyse and evaluate each require a different answer shape, and students who write the same paragraph for all three cap out around grade 6.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Computational thinking, algorithms, pseudocode and data representation, with a practical element in ICT. Students who code confidently often lose marks writing pseudocode to the board's conventions, which is a teachable and narrow gap rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to all pupils under KHDA rules, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. For IGCSE entries the assessed skills are reading, writing and, in some entries, listening and speaking. Support works from the school's own prescribed material.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source analysis, case-study recall and extended writing under timing. The common failure is learning content without learning the mark scheme's expectations for a source question. Both subjects respond quickly to structured essay drilling with marked feedback.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.regionsTitle: Al Furjan and the IGCSE corridor around it
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.regionsIntro: These are the communities sharing Al Furjan's school routes. Families in them book the same slots, sit the same board entries, and queue at the same gates at pickup.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Four districts of villas and townhouses with two Route 2020 metro stations. Bus loops across the districts spread arrival times by up to fifty minutes, which is why neighbours on the same school run report different workable session times.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Apartment blocks immediately north, feeding many of the same British-curriculum schools. The constraint here is a quiet corner rather than travel, and headphones plus a shared desk is the normal setup for a Year 11 student.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: Established schools and long-settled families south of Al Furjan. Parents working in the free zone often finish later, so Year 10 and 11 sessions here commonly run at 19:00 with a parent present at the end.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Several of the schools Al Furjan children attend sit here, which makes the morning run short and the afternoon one slow when the gates queue. The earliest workable session starts in this cluster.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: Low-rise villas and apartments inside Dubai Investments Park, close enough to school for a ten-minute run. Families here can start a session at 15:50 and finish homework before dinner.

regions.name: Dubai South and Emaar South
regions.note: Newer villa districts near the Expo site, with thin local school provision and the longest bus runs in the corridor. Year 11 students here are frequently the last home and book the 18:30 and 19:00 slots.

regions.name: Dubai Production City
regions.note: Townhouses and apartments north-east along Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, sharing the Al Barsha school corridor. Board entries here are mixed, with several schools running Pearson Edexcel across the sciences.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools nearest Al Furjan
schoolClusters.note: The short run, mostly Cambridge and Edexcel entries at 16 with Advanced Level or Diploma afterwards. These are the schools whose Year 11 timetables shape the afternoon in the Masakin and Quortaj districts.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park schools
schoolClusters.note: The southern cluster, carrying large British and Indian-curriculum schools alongside IB continuum provision. Many Al Furjan IGCSE students sit their entries here, and the board varies by department in more than one of them.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-furjan.modesIntro: Three patterns cover Year 10 and Year 11 in this community, and the right one depends on how far the exam series is away rather than on budget.

modes.title: Weekly subject session through Year 10
modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week in a fixed slot, running alongside the school's teaching rather than ahead of it. The value is early diagnosis: a tutor who sees marked class work every week finds the tiering problem or the algebra gap in Year 10, when it can still be fixed cheaply. Al Furjan families who do this rarely need a Year 11 crisis block.

modes.title: Twice weekly through mocks and the final run-in
modes.description: Two forty-five to sixty minute sessions a week, used from the mock window onward. The structure is simple: a paper set on the first session and marked against the board's own mark scheme on the second, with the errors grouped by type rather than by question. This is the pattern that moves a grade 5 to a grade 7 in the final term when the content is already known.
bullets: Past paper by component, timed, then marked feedback
Errors grouped by command term and by topic
Short gap between sessions so set work actually gets done
Runs as a defined block of weeks, not an open commitment

modes.title: November series and resit support
modes.description: A separate rhythm for students entered for the November series, whether as a first entry or a resit after June. Work runs through the UAE summer and into the autumn, which is when most tutoring demand falls away and specialist availability is best. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and Cambridge runs June and November, so the resit route exists in both boards.
bullets: Planning from the published official timetable, not from memory
Summer sessions while availability is at its widest
Focus on the specific papers that pulled the grade down
Entry deadlines confirmed with the school's exams officer

modes.title: Bridging block into Advanced Level or the Diploma
modes.description: Four to six sessions after the June results, closing the gap between Extended IGCSE and the first term of Advanced Level or IB Diploma Higher Level. In mathematics that means calculus notation and algebraic fluency; in the sciences it means quantitative treatment of data and uncertainty. It is the cheapest intervention in this whole set and the one families most often skip.

sections.heading: Find out which board your child is entered for before you hire anyone
paragraphs: Two boards dominate British-curriculum schools in Dubai: Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel. They are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580; the Pearson International GCSE equivalent is 4MA1. Cambridge Physics is 0625; Pearson is 4PH1. The number of papers, the tier names, the formula provision and the mark-scheme conventions differ in each pairing, and the published grade boundaries are separate documents.

The way to find out is to ask the school's exams officer for the entry list, which carries the board and the syllabus code for every subject. Do not rely on the subject name on the report card, and do not assume consistency across departments. Several schools in the Jebel Ali corridor enter Cambridge for mathematics and Pearson for one or more sciences, which means one student can need two different sets of past papers in the same term.

This is where in-home hiring in Al Furjan tends to fail. The pool of tutors willing to drive into the villa districts for a 17:00 start is small, and a parent choosing from a small pool takes the available tutor rather than the right one. The tutor then works from whichever board's material they know. Six weeks of competent teaching on the wrong papers looks identical to six weeks of good teaching until the mock result arrives.

Online matching removes that compromise, because the constraint becomes a calendar rather than a map. IB Gram matches on the board and code you give us, confirms it before the trial lesson, and works from the papers the school has issued. We cite and link official syllabus and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, since reproducing board material is a copyright matter.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the entry decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: In Cambridge mathematics and the sciences, a student is entered for either Core or Extended tier, and the tier caps the grade available. Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher to the same effect. This is an entry decision made months before the exam, usually by the school on the evidence of Year 10 performance, and it is reversible only inside the entry window. Many Al Furjan parents meet it as a notification rather than a conversation.

The consequences run past Year 11. Most British-curriculum schools want grade 6 or 7 in a subject before accepting it at Advanced Level, and IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asks for the same. A capped tier can therefore close a post-16 route in a subject the student is otherwise capable of. That is the real cost of a tier decision, and it is why the useful tutoring window is Year 10, not the spring of Year 11.

The honest counterweight is that Extended tier is not right for everyone. A student placed in Extended on ambition rather than evidence can score below what they would have achieved at Core, because the paper assumes fluency they do not yet have. The decision should rest on marked work across a full year, not on one strong assessment or on what the neighbours' children are doing.

What a tutor contributes here is diagnostic rather than motivational. Reading three marked Year 10 papers tells you whether the gap is content, method or timing. A content gap is closable in a term. A timing problem is closable in weeks. A fluency gap in algebra is the one that genuinely argues for the lower tier, and saying so early is more useful than saying it in March.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit two series, and knowing which one matters more than any revision technique. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and must not be used to plan a UAE entry; a page that quotes a February exam window to a Dubai parent is quoting a date for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Cambridge adds a detail that costs candidates every year. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. So the right document is not the generic timetable but your school's zone timetable, which the exams officer holds.

Published Pearson dates give a usable picture of how far ahead the calendar runs. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and keep their dates; forward planning should use the live official timetable, because provisional timetables are revised.

Counted backwards, the working year looks like this. Entries close months before the papers. Mocks sit in the winter. Coursework or practical components are completed before the written papers. Then the series itself, then results, then the narrow window for an enquiry about results or a November resit entry. A family that maps this in September spends less in total than a family that discovers it in April.

sections.heading: Fitting a Year 11 session into the Al Furjan afternoon
paragraphs: The practical question in this community is not whether tutoring helps but when it can happen. Buses serving Al Furjan run loops across the Quortaj, Masakin, Dar and Murooj districts, so arrival spreads from 15:20 to 16:10 for the same school. Year 11 students frequently stay for subject revision clinics, which adds forty minutes. The first genuinely usable minute for most is 17:00, and for students travelling the Al Barsha corridor it is closer to 17:45.

That makes some arrangements impossible rather than inconvenient. A visiting tutor crossing Dubai for a 19:00 start in evening traffic is either expensive or unavailable, usually both. An online session at 19:00 is ordinary. It also means a session missed because of a late bus moves to the following evening rather than the following week, which over a term is the difference between thirty-two sessions and twenty-four.

The scheduling advice that actually works is to book the slot that survives a bad day. Pick the time your child can make after a fixture, a clinic and a traffic delay, not the time that works on a good Tuesday. Families who book optimistically renegotiate weekly, and renegotiated slots are the ones that quietly disappear in the term where they matter most.

One more detail specific to Year 11 in this corridor. In the four weeks before the June series, schools run study leave, which frees the afternoon entirely. That is the window for two or three sessions a week on papers, and it is worth planning for in advance because every Year 11 family in Dubai wants the same tutors in the same fortnight.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in Dubai per month, not per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tutoring look cheap and monthly totals make it real, so start with the month. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Working back to the hour, published Dubai rates run from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik for budget online provision with university-student tutors. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors online. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the examiner end.

Set against that, Dubai school fees themselves are a fixed quantity this year: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. A family budgeting for IGCSE support is therefore working against a stable fee base, which makes a planned weekly session easier to commit to than an emergency block.

These are market figures from the providers who published them, read in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list, and we do not publish one on these pages. Our own numbers get discussed after the free trial lesson, when there is something concrete to price: a subject, a level, a slot and a number of weeks.

sections.heading: Practical science, the alternative to practical, and why it is worth marks
paragraphs: Science IGCSEs carry a practical component, and it is the part of the grade that students most often leave to chance. Depending on the entry, a candidate sits either a laboratory examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper that tests the same skills on paper: reading instruments, tabulating results, plotting, identifying anomalies, and describing a method with controlled variables named. Which route applies depends on the board and the school's entry.

The skills examined are narrow and highly trainable, which makes this the best value-per-session work in the whole IGCSE science syllabus. A student who can read a measuring cylinder to the correct precision, write a table with units in the headings, plot a line of best fit rather than a dot-to-dot, and state one control variable with a reason will collect most of the available marks. None of that requires a laboratory to practise.

The errors are predictable across every cohort. Units written in the body of the table instead of the heading. A graph scaled to make the data occupy a quarter of the grid. A method that says the temperature was kept the same without saying how. An anomalous result circled but not explained. A conclusion that restates the data rather than answering the hypothesis. Each of those is a mark, and together they are often a grade.

For Al Furjan families with a child taking Coordinated or Combined Science rather than three separate sciences, the practical skills carry across all three disciplines in the same paper. That means practical technique work benefits every science mark the student scores, which is a better return than a term spent on a single weak topic.
bullets: Units belong in the table heading, not in the cells
Scale a graph so the plotted data fills most of the grid
Name the control variable and say how it was controlled
Explain an anomaly rather than only identifying it

sections.heading: Coursework, controlled assessment and what a tutor may legitimately touch
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects still carry assessed work produced in school, and a few UAE providers treat that as a commercial opportunity. One business in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments for the IB. The same logic gets applied to IGCSE coursework, and the consequence falls on the student: submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the grade or the entry is what is at risk.

A tutor's legitimate contribution is larger than parents usually assume. A tutor can teach the technique the task requires, explain what each assessment strand rewards, question a weak plan until it becomes answerable, model how a published piece of writing is structured, and give written feedback on the student's own draft against the published criteria. All of that is teaching, and it is where most of the recoverable marks sit.

What a tutor must not do is write, rewrite, dictate, outline for the student to fill in, or supply content that then appears in the submission. IB Gram tutors state this at the first session of any coursework block and give feedback in writing, so that if the school asks what support was received there is a clear and defensible answer. A parent should expect that boundary from any tutor and be wary of one who does not mention it.

The same principle governs materials. We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We cite the official sources, link them, and work from whatever the school has issued to the student. That protects the student and keeps the support auditable.
bullets: A tutor teaches technique, questions a plan and gives written feedback
A tutor never drafts, rewrites or supplies submitted content
Feedback is written down so the school can see the support given
Official board material is cited and linked, never reproduced

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade 3 or above: planning equivalency from Year 9
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education equivalency rule should be read in Year 9, when subject choices are still open. The published British-track requirement is that students pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submit proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches Dubai families is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, and both are taught in every Dubai private school because KHDA requires them regardless of the licensed curriculum. A student counting them towards the five arrives at the application with four qualifying subjects. One ranking competitor page in this market tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced rule is five, excluding those two.

For families on the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency through a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. For the IB there is no points figure published here, because none has been read on a Ministry source, and we will not print an unsourced threshold.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a Ministry process, and the Ministry's own channel is where a parent should confirm current requirements before acting on them. Tutoring is not required for equivalency; it affects the grades, not the process.

sections.heading: When the timetable leaves no slot, and what we say instead of yes
paragraphs: Availability is where tutoring pages stop being honest, so here is the real position. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English at IGCSE level are usually matched within a few days for an Al Furjan family. Additional Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science and the smaller humanities entries take longer. In the four weeks of study leave before the June series, everything takes longer, because every Year 11 family in Dubai is looking at once.

When the right tutor is not free for your slot, you get one of three answers: a different time with the correct specialist, a short wait with a date on it, or a straight no and a suggestion to look elsewhere. What you will not get is a tutor who teaches the other board, or a generalist presented as a subject specialist. In a two-year course with terminal papers, that substitution costs a term before anyone notices.

The free trial lesson is the check on all of this. Bring a marked paper, name the paper number, and see whether the tutor can tell you where the marks went. If the answer is vague, the match is wrong and you should say so; nothing has been paid and there is no obligation. Families who treat the trial as an interview get better outcomes than families who treat it as a formality.

The structural fix is timing. Booking in September for a June series costs less and gets better tutors than booking in April. Booking in the summer for a November entry is the easiest match in the whole year, because demand collapses and specialists have space.
bullets: Core IGCSE subjects usually matched within a few days
Additional Mathematics and Arabic first language take longer
Study leave before the June series is the tightest fortnight of the year
November entries are the easiest to staff, because summer demand is low

process.description: Choose the time that works after a fixture, a revision clinic and a traffic delay, then keep it for the term. In Al Furjan this is usually 17:00 or later, and sometimes 18:30 for students on the Al Barsha run. Fixed slots are the difference between four sessions a month and two.

process.description: From the winter mocks, the structure changes: one timed paper set, then marked feedback grouped by error type rather than by question. Through study leave this usually becomes two or three sessions a week. The plan is built from the published zone timetable your school holds.

process.description: After the June series there is a narrow window to act on results: an enquiry about results, or an entry for the November series. We review the paper-level outcome with you and say honestly whether a resit is likely to move the grade, rather than selling another block by default.

whyPoints.title: Board and code matched, every time
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different exams. We match on the code your child is entered for and confirm it before the trial, because the most common waste in this market is competent teaching aimed at the wrong papers.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool larger than the Al Furjan map
whyPoints.description: In-home hiring here draws from whoever will drive into the villa districts for a 17:00 start. Online draws from everyone available in UAE evening hours, which is how a family in Masakin gets a Chemistry specialist rather than the nearest generalist.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the official timetable
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and warns that the wrong zone timetable can cost a candidate an exam, so we plan from the school's own zone document.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it, with October 2026 as the reading date. We do not present market rates as our own prices and we do not publish a rate card on a landing page.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach technique and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write or rewrite submitted work. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, having that in writing protects the student's entry.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE home tutor come to our villa in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video; visiting homes is a service we run only in India. Dubai does have visiting tutors, generally at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, so the option exists. For Year 10 and Year 11 work from Al Furjan the online route usually produces a better match, because the tutor is selected from everyone free in UAE evening hours rather than from the small group willing to drive into the villa districts at 17:00.

faqs.question: Al Furjan schools use different boards. Where is the entry list that proves which one?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the entry list. It shows the board and the syllabus code for every subject, which is what a tutor needs. Do not rely on the subject name on a report, and do not assume the whole school uses one board: several schools in the Jebel Ali corridor enter Cambridge for mathematics and Pearson for one or more sciences. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Pearson is 4MA1; Cambridge Physics is 0625, Pearson is 4PH1. The papers, tiers and mark schemes differ in each pairing.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE exams in February or March in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. If a tutoring page quotes you a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline for a UAE entry, it is using dates from another country's calendar. Your school's exams officer holds the correct timetable, and for Cambridge it is the version for your centre's administrative zone rather than the generic one.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter for a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong timetable was used. For a family in Al Furjan the practical step is to get the zone timetable from the school rather than downloading a generic one, then build revision and tutoring around those paper dates specifically.

faqs.question: Does Core tier limit what my child can study after Year 11?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Core and Foundation tier entries cap the grade available, and most British-curriculum schools want grade 6 or 7 in a subject before accepting it at Advanced Level. IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asks for the same. So a tier decision taken in Year 10 can quietly close a post-16 route in a subject your child is capable of. That is why the useful time to review the tier with marked evidence is through Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11 when the entry window has closed.

faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly tutoring budget for a Year 11 student in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts monthly cost for one weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures from the providers that published them, read in October 2026, and not an IB Gram price list. Our own pricing is discussed after the free trial.

faqs.question: My child's school is in Dubai Investments Park. When can a session start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than for most of the corridor. Children on Dubai Investments Park and Green Community routes are often home between 15:20 and 15:40, which makes a 15:50 start workable and leaves the evening clear. The variable is pickup: those school gates queue, so arrival drifts later on fixture and club days. Book the slot that holds on a slow afternoon rather than a quick one. Year 11 students staying for subject revision clinics should assume 17:00 as the first realistic start instead.

faqs.question: Is the alternative-to-practical paper worth tutoring for?
faqs.answer: It is among the best value work in the science syllabus, because the skills are narrow and trainable. The paper tests reading instruments to the right precision, tabulating with units in the headings, plotting a sensible scale and a line of best fit, naming a control variable and saying how it was controlled, and explaining an anomaly rather than circling it. None of that needs a laboratory to practise. For a student taking Coordinated or Combined Science the same skills earn marks across all three disciplines in one paper.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate help on assessed IGCSE work stop being legitimate?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the technique the task needs, explain what each assessment strand rewards, question a weak plan until it works, and give written feedback on your child's own draft against the published criteria. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, dictate or supply content that appears in the submission. IB Gram tutors state this at the first session of a coursework block and give feedback in writing, so that if the school asks what help was received there is a straight answer on record.

faqs.question: Al Furjan families applying to UAE universities: is it five IGCSE subjects or six?
faqs.answer: Five, not six. The published British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which matters in Dubai because KHDA requires every private school to teach them. One competitor page in this market states six subjects; the sourced requirement is five. Confirm current rules through the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Should my child resit in the November series after June results?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision should come from the paper-level breakdown rather than the overall grade. A student who missed a boundary by a few marks on one paper, in a subject they need for a post-16 offer, is a good candidate. A student whose marks were spread evenly below the target across every component usually needs a different plan, not another sitting. The window to enter is short after August results, so review the breakdown in the first week rather than the third, with the school's exams officer involved.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to match a tutor for in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science and the smaller humanities entries. Mathematics, the three sciences and English are usually covered within a few days. Availability also tightens sharply during the four weeks of study leave before the June series, when every Year 11 family in Dubai is looking at the same time. If we cannot cover your subject and slot we will say so rather than offering a tutor who teaches the other board.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic alongside IGCSE in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, since the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Support for these subjects works from the school's own prescribed material, because using different or additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the study leave weeks before the June series?
faqs.answer: Timed papers by component, marked, with the errors grouped by type. In practice that means two or three sessions a week: a paper set in one session and the marking discussed in the next, with topics revisited only where the marking shows a pattern. What does not work in study leave is fresh content teaching across a whole syllabus, because there is not enough time to consolidate it. Book this block in advance; it is the most contested fortnight in the Dubai tutoring year.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE to the IB Diploma. How big is the gap?
faqs.answer: In mathematics it is the widest transition in this set. Extended IGCSE builds procedural fluency; Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level expects calculus notation, proof structure and sustained multi-step reasoning from the first term. In the sciences the gap is quantitative: uncertainty treatment, graph interpretation and extended response. Four to six bridging sessions over the summer after Year 11 close most of it, and they cost a fraction of catching up during the first Diploma term. Al Furjan families usually change schools for the Diploma, which adds a settling period too.

faqs.question: Can we start in Year 10 rather than waiting for Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is the cheaper and better option. A weekly session in Year 10 lets a tutor see marked class work as it happens, which is how a tiering problem or an algebra fluency gap gets found while there is still time to fix it. Families who start in Year 10 rarely need an intensive Year 11 block, and the total cost over two years is usually lower than a single crisis term. It also means the tutor is already matched and available when study leave arrives and everyone else is looking.

intro.heading: The school run decides whether tutoring survives the term
paragraphs: Al Garhoud is a compact neighbourhood between Dubai International Airport, the Creek and the bridge that carries its name. Almost nobody who lives here goes to school here. Children leave early and come back across water or across the airport road, and the arrival time varies by twenty to forty minutes depending on which school and which route. That single fact decides more about whether tutoring works than the choice of tutor does, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions it.

The pattern we see repeatedly runs like this. A family books a weekly in-home session for 4pm because that is when the tutor can come. Week one works. Week two the Year 11 student has an after-school revision clinic and arrives at 4:35pm, so forty minutes of a paid hour are spent settling. Week three there is traffic. Week four the session is cancelled. The teaching was never the problem; the slot was set to the tutor's availability rather than to the household's actual rhythm.

Then there is the week itself. An IGCSE student in a Dubai school is typically entered for eight to ten subjects and also timetabled for Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies, which are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of curriculum. Add after-school activities, Friday and Saturday being the weekend, and the fact that most IGCSE homework arrives in clusters around assessment weeks, and the number of genuinely free evening hours is smaller than a parent assumes. A sensible tutoring plan claims one or two of them and protects those, rather than claiming four and losing three.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We say that plainly because the search phrase for this kind of help is a home-tutor phrase, and because the online format is what makes the scheduling problem solvable. A slot can be set to 5:20pm if that is when your child walks in. It can move by a day when there is a mock. It does not depend on anybody's car.

What follows is organised around time rather than around marketing. There is a table of typical finish times for the schools Garhoud families use and the first workable session slot for each. There is a Core and Extended comparison, because parents often do not know which tier their child is entered for. There is a Cambridge and Pearson code table, because the board changes the papers. There are the Dubai market rates in dirhams with sources. And there is the examination calendar counted backwards, including why entries close months before the papers are sat.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, with Core and Extended tiers in several of them. Cambridge runs examinations in a June series and a November series, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A Dubai parent should therefore take dates from their own school's zone timetable, not from a general listing.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run in the 4-series, such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology. Examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Several Pearson subjects are assessed through fewer, longer papers than their Cambridge equivalents, which changes revision strategy.

June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, before IGCSE
programmes.description: The three years that decide whether a student starts Year 10 ready. Checkpoint tests give a benchmark, and the gap that matters most is algebraic fluency in Mathematics and written explanation in the sciences. Both are cheaper to fix in Year 9 than in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Garhoud families often start tutoring in Year 9 specifically to protect the Extended tier option in Mathematics and the sciences, since a school may place a student on Core if Year 9 attainment is weak. That placement decision is worth asking about before it is made rather than after.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: Dubai students leaving IGCSE split between A Levels and the IB Diploma, and a handful move to other post-16 routes. Subject choices at 16 are constrained by IGCSE tier and grade, so a Core entry in Mathematics closes doors that an Extended entry leaves open.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Garhoud families ask about most. The syllabus code matters: two students in the same year group at two different schools can sit entirely different papers in a subject with the same name.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision is the whole subject. Extended and Higher reach into algebraic manipulation, functions and trigonometry that Core and Foundation do not, and the grade ceiling differs. Most lost marks sit in multi-step problems where a correct method is abandoned early, so method marks are the first thing a tutor should be chasing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and forces dominate the marks and the confusion. Students who can recite a definition often cannot explain a cause and effect in the order the mark scheme wants. Calculation layout is worth real marks: formula, substitution, answer with unit, every time.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. The practical paper or alternative-to-practical component rewards precise language about apparatus and error, which is learnable quickly because the question types repeat across series.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the challenge rather than difficulty. Students lose marks by writing fluent paragraphs that never use the specific term the mark scheme requires. Command-term drilling and a condensed definition list do more here than reading the textbook again.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Two or one award covering all three sciences, common where a student takes nine or ten subjects. The syllabus is narrower than the separate sciences but the papers still demand full explanation quality, and students coached on separate-science material waste time on content they will not be asked.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Reading and writing assessed through directed response, comparison and composition. Marks concentrate in the reading paper's analysis questions, where students summarise instead of analysing effect. A fixed quotation-plus-technique-plus-effect structure lifts scores inside a few weeks.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language with its own mark scheme and a speaking component in some variants. Students are sometimes entered here when First Language would have been achievable, and that entry decision is worth discussing with school before Year 11.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study application and diagram accuracy. In Economics, badly labelled diagrams cost marks that content knowledge cannot recover. In Business, the highest marks go to answers that reach a justified judgement rather than listing advantages and disadvantages.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two very different subjects routinely confused by parents. Computer Science is algorithmic and theoretical with pseudocode; ICT is practical and application-based with a substantial coursework element. Check which one is on the timetable before booking a tutor.

subjects.name: Arabic and modern languages
subjects.description: Arabic as a first language is both an IGCSE option and part of the mandatory provision Dubai schools must deliver, so a student may encounter it twice in a week in different forms. Support here stays inside the school's prescribed curriculum for the mandatory element.

sections.heading: What time can a session actually start?
paragraphs: Dismissal time is not arrival time, and in this part of Dubai the gap between them is the whole problem. A student finishing at 2:50pm in Al Qusais may be home later than a student finishing at 3:15pm inside Garhoud, because the first one crosses the airport road at the hour it is worst. Booking a session from a school's published finish time is therefore a mistake families make once and then stop making.

The second variable is what happens between the gate and the front door. Year 10 and Year 11 students in Dubai schools frequently have after-school revision clinics, sport fixtures or music commitments two or three afternoons a week, often ending at 4:15pm or 4:30pm. A tutoring slot set at 4pm on one of those days will simply never happen. Before booking anything, write out the week and find the two afternoons with nothing after school; those are the slots that will hold.

The third is food and decompression. A student who walks in at 4:15pm and sits down at 4:20pm produces about twenty usable minutes. The same student starting at 5pm, having eaten, produces fifty. Families routinely pay for the first arrangement and wonder why progress is slow. The table below pairs the commonest Garhoud school destinations with a realistic arrival window and the first slot that genuinely works.

Because lessons are online, these slots can be set precisely and changed permanently without renegotiating with a tutor's driving schedule. That is the practical argument for the format in this neighbourhood, and it is a bigger one than cost.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: find out which one your child is entered for
paragraphs: A surprising number of parents discover in Year 11 that their child is entered for the Core or Foundation tier in Mathematics or a science, and that the highest grade available is therefore capped. Schools make that decision on Year 9 and Year 10 attainment, often without a conversation that makes the consequence clear. It is the single most important thing to check before paying for tutoring, because the tier determines both the content to teach and whether tutoring can change the outcome at all.

The two tiers are not the same paper at two difficulties. Extended and Higher papers cover additional content and ask for sustained multi-step reasoning; Core and Foundation papers cover less and cap the available grade. A student sitting Core who is tutored on Extended material wastes hours on topics they will never be asked about. A student capable of Extended who has been placed on Core may be able to move, but usually only if the request is made early in Year 10, not in the term before the examinations.

The practical sequence is: ask the school in writing which tier or paper your child is entered for in each subject, ask what the deadline is for changing it, and only then book a tutor. If a change is possible and worth pursuing, the tutoring brief becomes specific — close the gap on the Extended-only topics by the school's decision deadline — which is a far better brief than general improvement.
