sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson? The board changes the papers
paragraphs: Two boards dominate Dubai IGCSE provision and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language — while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses the 4-series, such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The content overlaps substantially. The paper structure, the number of papers, and the way practical skills are assessed do not.

This matters when buying tutoring because past-paper practice is most of the value, and the wrong board's papers teach the wrong habits. A student sitting a Pearson paper who has drilled Cambridge multiple-choice papers has practised a question type they will not meet. A student sitting Cambridge who has only seen Pearson's longer papers has not practised pacing across the correct number of components. Ask the school for the exact syllabus code of every subject, write them on one sheet, and give that sheet to any tutor before the first session.

The dates differ as well and both boards publish them officially. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson runs May/June and November; its November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

One warning that matters specifically for UAE families: Cambridge's February and March examination series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. Any revision plan built around a February sitting is built on the wrong country's calendar.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in this part of Dubai, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market because that is where most families start. Online generalist tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. At that price the tutor is typically a university student or a generalist rather than somebody who has taught a named syllabus, and for supervised homework in Year 9 that can be perfectly adequate. For Year 11 paper technique on 0580 Extended it generally is not, because the skill being bought is mark-scheme literacy and that takes training.

One step up, qualified subject tutors online sit around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialists are quoted higher: TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. At the top of the market BartyED publishes AED 650 for named or examiner-level tutors. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget session, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

In-home visiting rates sit awkwardly across those bands because they include travel: Bestimate quotes AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors up to AED 500, with monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against online packages near AED 799 for eight sessions. For a Garhoud household, the premium is paying for a car crossing a bridge at the busiest hour of the day.

All of those are market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to whoever published them. They are not IB Gram's price list. Our model is one free trial lesson per subject before any payment, then a written quote against a plan, because eight weeks of Year 10 Mathematics and a Year 11 triple-science rescue are not the same job.

sections.heading: Why entries close months before the papers are sat
paragraphs: Parents are regularly surprised that an examination in one half of the year was entered for in the other. Entries are an administrative process run by the school as a registration centre, and the board needs the candidate list and the paper allocation long before the series. The consequence for a family is that decisions about tier, subject and whether to resit are made much earlier than the examination date suggests, and a decision missed cannot usually be recovered.

For Pearson, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a date copied from a website.

For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June series with November available as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in and get the zone timetable rather than a generic one.

The practical use of all this is backwards planning. If the June series is the target, mock results in the preceding months are the real diagnostic, the resit decision for November follows the August results date, and tutoring bought after the entry deadline cannot change the tier a student sits. That ordering is the single most useful thing on this page for a Year 11 family, and no competitor page in this market publishes it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the shortened school day
paragraphs: Dubai schools shorten the day during Ramadan and reduce after-school activities, and the family evening reorganises around Iftar. For a Year 11 student this falls in the half of the year where revision should be building, so it needs planning rather than improvising. The good news is that a shortened school day frees the early afternoon, which is the only time in a normal Dubai term when a student is both awake and unburdened.

Two patterns work. The first is an early-afternoon session, taken shortly after a shortened day ends, while concentration is still available and before the long wait to Iftar. The second is a post-Iftar slot, later than a family would normally accept, which suits older students who have adjusted their sleep. Both are straightforward online and both are difficult with a visiting tutor, whose own schedule and travel are also compressed.

Prayer times matter year-round and not only in Ramadan. Families frequently ask for slots that do not collide with Maghrib, which moves through the year, and the sensible approach is to fix the session relative to prayer rather than to the clock and adjust it every few weeks. A tutor who treats that as an inconvenience is the wrong tutor for a UAE family.

Plan the change before the period starts. The failure mode we see is a session that quietly stops for a month and is never rebuilt, so a student loses six weeks of momentum in the term that mattered most. Agreeing a reduced but real pattern — one session a week instead of two, at a different hour — keeps the thread intact.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies inside an IGCSE week
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies whatever international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance states that its requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For an IGCSE family this is timetable arithmetic: those lessons occupy periods that might otherwise hold a tenth subject or a study period, and they appear on reports alongside IGCSE grades.

The organisational rules are worth knowing because they explain what your child's week looks like. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught primarily in Arabic for Arab students; non-Arab students take Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so any tutoring in them stays inside the prescribed curriculum.

Two things follow for tutoring. These subjects are not optional and should be in the weekly plan rather than treated as spare capacity. And for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required IGCSE subjects, which matters when a family is choosing which five results to rely on.

sections.heading: Why no tutor will arrive at your door, and what you get instead
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation we are embarrassed about, and the reasons are the ones this whole page has been describing.

A visiting tutor's slot is set by their route. Yours is set by your child's. In a neighbourhood where arrival home varies by forty minutes depending on which Creek crossing is moving, those two schedules cannot be reconciled reliably across a thirty-week term, and the session that gets dropped is always the paid one. An online slot can be 5:20pm, can shift to Wednesday during mock week, can become early afternoon through Ramadan, and can carry on while a family is away for a long weekend.

There is also the matter of who is available. Matching on syllabus code rather than on postcode means a student sitting 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences gets somebody who has taught 0654, not somebody who has taught separate sciences and will cover material that is not on the paper. Across eight to ten IGCSE subjects and two boards, the chance that the right specialist for each one lives within a short drive of Al Garhoud is small.

Where in-home tutoring is genuinely better — a young child who will not settle on screen, a household with no quiet corner — the Dubai market provides it at the rates published above, and a family should use it. We are simply clear about not being that provider, and we say so in the first paragraph rather than the footer.

process.description: Ask the school in writing which tier or paper your child is entered for in each subject, and what the deadline is for changing it. If a change is possible, the tutoring brief becomes specific and measurable. If it is not, we teach the tier your child is actually sitting.

process.description: One free trial lesson per subject before any payment, taken at the proposed slot time so you can see whether that hour genuinely works for your child. Bring the most recent marked paper and the syllabus code.

process.description: After the trial you get a short written plan: the topics, the paper technique, which school assessment or mock it is aimed at, and what evidence will show it worked. The plan names the weeks it will not run, including breaks and Ramadan, so nothing disappears by accident.

process.title: Reviewed at the next mock
process.description: Mocks are the real diagnostic in an IGCSE year, so that is the review point. If the paper score moved, we pick the next target. If it did not, we change the tutor or the method and say which we think it was.

whyPoints.title: Slots built from arrival time
whyPoints.description: We set the session from when your child actually walks through the door, not from when school finishes. In a neighbourhood split by Creek crossings and the airport road, that difference is the reason most tutoring arrangements quietly fail by the fourth week.

whyPoints.title: Matched on syllabus code
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers, and 0654 is not the separate sciences. We ask for the code before matching, because past-paper practice is most of the value of a session and the wrong board's papers teach habits your child will not be able to use.

whyPoints.description: Entries close months before the papers. This page sets out the order — tier decision, entry deadline, mocks, zone timetable, examination window, results — so a Year 11 family can see which decisions are still open and which have already closed.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names who published it and is dated October 2026. Several pages ranking for Dubai tutoring publish no price at all, and the ones that do often quote dollars, which is not the currency a Garhoud household pays in.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan planned, not improvised
whyPoints.description: The plan says in advance what happens during shortened school days and prayer times, including early-afternoon and post-Iftar options. The usual failure is a session that stops for a month and is never rebuilt, in the term when momentum mattered most.

whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; that is part of our India service. It is in the first paragraph of this page because a parent searching a home-tutor phrase should not learn it after paying.

faqs.question: What time should an IGCSE session start if my child schools in Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Assume arrival home between 3:45pm and 4:15pm, and book 5pm. The dismissal time is misleading because the Creek crossing adds a variable twenty minutes and a student needs food and a few minutes of decompression before anything useful happens. A 4pm booking in that situation routinely produces twenty usable minutes out of sixty. If there is an after-school clinic that day, move the session to a different evening entirely rather than pushing it later, because a 6:30pm start after a long day rarely works for a Year 11 student.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: Ask the school in writing, subject by subject, and ask for the deadline to change it. Schools decide tier on Year 9 and Year 10 attainment and often do not spell out the consequence, which is that Core and Foundation papers cap the grade available and can close post-16 science and mathematics routes. If a change is still possible it is normally early in Year 10 rather than in the term before the examinations. Until you know the tier, a tutor may be teaching content your child will never be asked about.

faqs.question: Does the exam board my child's school uses change what a tutor should do?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. Cambridge codes such as 0580, 0625, 0620 and 0610 differ from Pearson's 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 in paper structure, paper count and how practical skills are assessed, even where content overlaps. Past-paper work is most of the value of a session, and the wrong board's papers train the wrong pacing and the wrong question types. Get the exact syllabus code for every subject from school, put them on one sheet, and hand that sheet to any tutor before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my child in Al Garhoud be entered for?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs both, with November functioning as the resit route, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that using the correct zone timetable is essential because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss a paper after using the wrong version. Pearson offers May/June and November. One important warning: Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February sitting is using the wrong country's calendar.

faqs.question: How many free evenings does an IGCSE student in Dubai really have?
faqs.answer: Fewer than parents expect. A typical Dubai IGCSE student is entered for eight to ten subjects and also timetabled for Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies, which are mandatory in all Dubai private schools. Two or three afternoons usually carry revision clinics, sport or music. With Friday and Saturday as the weekend, that often leaves two genuinely free weekday evenings. The practical conclusion is to claim one or two slots and protect them absolutely, rather than booking four and losing three by the fourth week.

faqs.question: Can we get a tutor to come to the house in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are part of our India service. Every UAE lesson is online, one-to-one, over live video. The Dubai market does provide in-home tutoring at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, so a family who genuinely needs a tutor in the room can find one. We are open about not being that provider because the phrase most parents search is a home-tutor phrase, and the format should not be a surprise.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost per hour in old Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026: online generalists from roughly AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 plus for examination-year specialists.

faqs.question: Is one long weekly session better than two shorter ones?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE, two shorter sessions on separate evenings usually wins. The subject rewards repeated retrieval and spaced practice rather than long single sittings, and a ninety-minute weekday session normally collides with homework and ends with a tired student. The exception is timed paper practice, which cannot be done properly in fifty minutes; that belongs on a Friday or Saturday morning or in a holiday block, when a full paper can be sat to time and then marked together.

faqs.question: How should tutoring change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Plan it before the period starts. Schools shorten the day and reduce activities, which frees the early afternoon, so a session shortly after a shortened day ends often works better than any slot available in a normal term. The alternative is a post-Iftar slot, which suits older students who have adjusted their sleep. Either is straightforward online. The failure to avoid is a session that simply stops for a month and is never rebuilt, costing six weeks of momentum in the half of the year when revision should be building.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE results should a Garhoud family rely on for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student also needs either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One currently ranking competitor page states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule, so check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority rather than a tutoring website.

faqs.question: My child has nine subjects and is drowning. Which do we tutor?
faqs.answer: The one where a small intervention changes the most. Usually that is Mathematics, because its grade gates post-16 options and because method-mark discipline transfers to the sciences. Second choice is whichever science is both weakest and entered at Extended, since Extended is where multi-step reasoning is examined. Avoid starting three subjects at once; a Dubai IGCSE week does not have room for it, and three half-attended sessions produce less than one protected one. Review at the next mock and move the target then.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Garhoud IGCSE students attend?
faqs.answer: Al Mawakeb School Al Garhoud is inside the neighbourhood. Many families cross the Creek to Dubai Festival City for Deira International School or Universal American School, or travel to Oud Metha for The Indian High School Dubai, St Mary's Catholic High School or Dubai Gem Private School. Others go east to Al Qusais for The Millennium School Dubai, Westminster School Dubai or Dubai Scholars Private School. These names are context only; we have no affiliation with any of them and claim no endorsement.

faqs.question: What happens to the session during mock exam weeks?
faqs.answer: It moves rather than stops, and ideally it moves to the day before the paper that matters most. Mock weeks are the highest-value tutoring window in an IGCSE year because the marked papers that come out of them are the only honest diagnostic a family gets before the real series. A good plan sets aside a session after the mocks specifically to go through the scripts question by question, working out whether marks were lost on content, on method or on reading the question.

faqs.question: Is a university student at AED 50 an hour good enough for Year 11?
faqs.answer: For supervised homework, often yes. For Year 11 paper technique, usually not, because the skill being bought is mark-scheme literacy — knowing what the examiner awards and in what order — and that comes from having marked work against a scheme. The published budget band is roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for specialists, and the honest way to judge is to ask any candidate to mark one page of your child's work aloud, saying what each annotation is worth.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both Mathematics and a science?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but check rather than assume. A tutor with a physics or engineering background often handles Mathematics and Physics credibly at IGCSE; Chemistry and Biology are usually a different person. The real risk is a generalist taking both and being thin in each. Two separate specialists on two evenings costs the same per hour and produces better paper technique, and because lessons are online you are not restricted to whoever can cover two subjects within one drive of Al Garhoud.

faqs.question: How long before the June series should we start?
faqs.answer: If the aim is a grade change rather than damage limitation, start in the autumn term of Year 11 or earlier, because tier and entry decisions close months before the papers and because paper technique takes repeated practice across a term to become automatic. Starting six weeks out is still worth doing — targeted work on two topics and on timing can move a boundary — but it cannot change the tier your child is entered for, and it cannot build the retrieval practice that a full term allows.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingHeading: Send us the week and the syllabus codes
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingBody: Two things make a Garhoud tutoring plan work: a slot set from when your child genuinely gets home, and a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code on the entry form. Send the school, the subjects, the codes if you have them, and the two afternoons with nothing after school, and we will propose a slot and a plan built around them. The first lesson is free, one per subject, taken before any payment, and it is worth taking at the proposed time so you can see whether that hour actually works. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Comparing three addresses, and finding one real difference
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City sits on Sheikh Zayed Road at the point where Business Bay ends and the Al Safa and Jumeirah side begins, with the Dubai Water Canal running past it. That position is why families here reflexively compare themselves with the neighbourhoods either side when they start looking for tutoring: Business Bay towers to the east, the Al Safa and Al Wasl villa streets to the west. The comparison gets made on the assumption that one of those addresses must be better served than the others. It is worth doing the comparison properly, because the finding is more useful than the assumption.

Start with what is genuinely shared. All three addresses draw on the same school map. The British-curriculum schools in Al Safa, Jumeirah and Al Barsha serve children from Al Habtoor City towers, Business Bay apartments and Al Wasl villas without distinction, and the Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf schools are a similar drive from each. That means the specifications are shared too: the same split between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, the same tier decisions, the same practical paper arrangements. A tutor who understands one family's requirement understands the next street's.

The tutor pool is also shared, and this is where the assumption breaks down. Tutors working these central districts do not specialise by tower. A person who teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended and can reach Sheikh Zayed Road in the late afternoon is available to all three addresses, and the same person will be unavailable to all three on the evenings they are already teaching. Nobody in Business Bay has access to a specialist that an Al Habtoor City family does not.

The one real difference is access time, and it favours neither the towers nor the villas as a class. It favours whoever is easier to reach. A visiting tutor serving an Al Habtoor City apartment leaves Sheikh Zayed Road, parks in a basement, registers at a desk, waits for a lift and arrives at a floor. In Al Safa they park on a street and walk to a door. Neither is dramatic in isolation, and across two IGCSE years of weekly visits it is a measurable quantity of paid time that is not teaching. The towers also carry an access process that varies by building, which is the kind of friction that gradually pushes a 5pm booking later.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Habtoor City families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason that follows from the comparison rather than contradicting it: if the school map, the specifications and the tutor pool are identical across three adjacent addresses, then the only thing a visiting arrangement can differentiate is access time, and online delivery removes it entirely for all three.

sections.heading: Three addresses compared, line by line
paragraphs: The table below compares Al Habtoor City with the two districts families here most often weigh themselves against. It is deliberately specific about what differs and what does not, because the pattern is the useful part.

Read down the right-hand column. The rows that say the same are the ones that matter academically: the school map, the awarding bodies in use, the tier decisions, the practical paper arrangements, the depth of the available tutor pool. Those are city-level and school-level facts rather than neighbourhood facts, and no amount of moving between these three addresses changes any of them.

The rows that differ are logistical. A high-rise address adds basement parking, a visitor registration process and a lift wait at each end of a visit, and the process varies by tower. A villa address adds a street park and a short walk. The canal and Sheikh Zayed Road position adds a particular kind of approach problem in the late afternoon, which is shared with Business Bay and Downtown and is slightly worse than the Al Safa side.

None of those logistical differences affects what a tutor teaches. They affect how much of a paid hour is teaching, and how reliably a 5pm booking stays at 5pm across a two-year course. That is a real cost, it is worth seeing, and it is the only thing a neighbourhood comparison in this part of Dubai actually produces. The conclusion most families draw from it is that the choice they should be making is about format rather than about postcode.

sections.heading: What high-rise access actually costs across two years
paragraphs: Access time sounds like a quibble until it is multiplied. A visiting tutor at an Al Habtoor City tower exits Sheikh Zayed Road, enters a basement, finds a visitor bay, takes a lift to a lobby, registers at a desk, and takes a second lift to a residential floor. On departure the sequence reverses. Each stage is short. The total is not, and it recurs weekly across an IGCSE course.

There are three ways that cost gets absorbed and none of them is good for the family. It is absorbed into the hourly rate, which is why in-home tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. It is absorbed into the lesson, so a sixty-minute booking becomes fifty minutes of teaching. Or it is absorbed into the schedule, so the 5pm slot drifts to 5:20pm and then to 5:30pm and the student's evening compresses around it.

Tower access also introduces a failure mode villa addresses do not have, which is procedural variation. Different buildings have different visitor policies, some requiring pre-registration, some requiring a resident to authorise entry, some limiting visitor parking at particular hours. A tutor who has not visited before will be slower, and a replacement tutor covering a session will be slower again. Across two years that produces a handful of sessions that start fifteen minutes late for reasons nobody can prevent.

The reason this matters more in exam year than in Year 10 is sequencing. A session that loses ten minutes in October is a small loss. A session that loses ten minutes in the week after the mocks, when the plan is to work through a marked script and build a topic list, is a session that does not finish the job. The cost lands precisely where the value was highest.

sections.heading: The answer that does not change with the address
paragraphs: Having established what the comparison actually reveals, the useful move is to say what a family should do instead of comparing neighbourhoods. The answer is the same for Al Habtoor City, Business Bay and Al Safa, and it has nothing to do with geography.

Find the awarding body and tier on the exam entry statement. This is the one fact that changes what a session should contain, and it varies school by school within a few kilometres. Cambridge 0580 Extended candidates sit a two-hour paper with no calculator and a two-hour calculator paper, each 100 marks. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 candidates sit two two-hour papers with a calculator permitted in both. In the sciences, Cambridge separate sciences carry a practical component worth 20 per cent entered as Paper 5 or Paper 6, while Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 assess those skills inside the written papers. A tutor prepared for the wrong structure wastes months regardless of how close they live.

Then test for specification knowledge rather than for proximity. Ask which code the school enters for and why it matters. Ask the calculator policy on each maths paper. Ask how practical work is assessed in the relevant science. Ask where students lost marks on the last paper the tutor marked, and listen for a topic, an error and a mark value rather than a general observation about practice. Ask how they would decide between Core and Extended, and expect an answer involving a marked timed past paper rather than an argument about ceilings.

Finally, make the tier decision with evidence. Cambridge Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so the choice sets a ceiling before teaching begins. Classroom impressions flatter the confident and undersell the quiet. A marked Extended past paper under timed conditions, read for whether the losses are technique or content, is the only reliable instrument, and it costs one session to obtain. None of those four steps is affected by which side of Sheikh Zayed Road a family lives on.

sections.heading: The school map from Sheikh Zayed Road
paragraphs: Because the school map is the thing all three compared addresses share, it is worth setting out with the practical detail a family actually needs: roughly how the commute behaves and what that does to the available tutoring slot.

The Al Safa, Jumeirah and Al Wasl cluster is the closest, and the one most students from these towers attend. Senior school days there end between about 2:45pm and 3:20pm. The return journey crosses Al Wasl Road and rejoins Sheikh Zayed Road, which in the late afternoon takes thirty to forty-five minutes, so a student is home around 3:30pm to 4:15pm. Add tower access and the realistic start for a session is 4:45pm at the earliest.

The Al Jaddaf and Sobha Hartland cluster is a different direction and a comparable duration, serving several newer schools. The Al Barsha cluster is further west and generally later, with senior days running to about 3:30pm and activity programmes to 5pm, which for a family in these districts pushes any session into the evening window from 6:45pm.

One further variable belongs in the same calculation, which is the school bus. A student on a late route may be dropped at 4pm whatever time the bell rang, and that moves the usable window as decisively as any activity programme does. Families who drive instead often gain the earlier slot and lose it again to the Al Wasl Road crossing. The table maps it. The point of including it is that the commute, not the address, is what determines the usable slot, and the commute is a function of which school a family chose rather than which tower they live in. Two neighbours in the same building can have quite different workable session times, which is the opposite of what a neighbourhood comparison would predict.

sections.heading: Rates across the three districts, and what varies
paragraphs: A neighbourhood comparison usually ends in a question about price, so it is worth being explicit about which figures move with an address and which do not.

The published market rates, read in October 2026 and belonging to the providers named: in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Budget online options from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Premium examiner-branded providers at AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. None of these is an IB Gram price list.

Of those figures, only the in-home band moves with an address, and it moves with access difficulty rather than with prestige. A tower with a slow visitor process and restricted basement parking produces quotations at the upper end of the band; a villa street with a front door produces quotations lower in it. That is a travel and friction premium, and it is identical in character to the one families in Business Bay and Downtown pay. Online rates do not move at all across any of these districts, which is the clearest single demonstration that the comparison this page started with is a logistics comparison rather than an academic one.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Al Habtoor City families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so there is no access time inside the rate, no registration desk between the booking and the lesson, and no reason for a 4:45pm slot to drift. For a tower address that is the single most relevant feature of the delivery model, which is why it appears in a section about price rather than at the end of a sales conversation.

sections.heading: The examination calendar, which is also the same everywhere
paragraphs: One more thing a neighbourhood comparison cannot change is the calendar, and it is worth setting out because no competitor page in this search does it. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any February or March dates quoted to a Dubai family should be disregarded entirely. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Checkable reference points, stated with their provenance. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and that is what makes them verifiable. The live official timetable is what should be checked before acting, because provisional timetables are revised before each series.

There is one Cambridge administrative point with a real consequence. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the exam timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. This is a school-level fact rather than a district-level one, so ask the school which zone it sits in and make sure any revision plan is built against that version.

Counting backwards gives the shape of the year. Entries and the tier decision are settled in the autumn term. The winter mock window is the only honest diagnostic a family gets, and the weeks immediately afterwards are the highest-value tutoring hours of the entire course, spent on a diagnosed list rather than on revision in general. In the final four weeks the paid hours should reduce rather than increase, because accuracy and pace set through the student's own timed practice. And a small reserve is sensible, because a November resit decided in August needs funding in September and produces a grade the following January.

sections.heading: Checking the permit, wherever the tutor is coming from
paragraphs: The regulatory position applies equally across all three compared districts, and the checks are short and free. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

Because there is no fee, lacking one is a choice rather than an obstacle. Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, a specific amount quoted at you cannot be substantiated.

Two further points are worth knowing in these districts specifically. There are tuition centres along this corridor, and a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And on who may teach whom, in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a restriction echoed by the MoHRE permit's code of conduct.

Two further things should affect how any offer is read. Nobody should be described as approved or accredited by a regulator or an examination board, because no private tutor or platform holds that status in the sense the phrase implies. And no grade, improvement or outcome can honestly be guaranteed, which means a promise of one tells you something about the rest of the claims surrounding it. Both checks are free and neither depends on which side of Sheikh Zayed Road anybody lives on.

intro.heading: Take the invoice apart before you sign it
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Jaddaf is a product with two components, and almost nobody separates them. One component is teaching: a person who knows Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher and can mark against the published scheme. The other is logistics: that person physically arriving at your building, which means time in a car on the roads around Dubai Healthcare City and the Creek crossings at exactly the hour they are busiest. You are charged for both in one number, and the second part is invisible.

The published figures make the split visible. Bestimate's rate table for Dubai puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350; home-tutor providers quote AED 200 to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Those are different providers rather than a controlled comparison, but the direction is consistent across every source we could read, and the logistical component is the obvious explanation. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions sit in the same market alongside AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Jaddaf or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Saying so early matters on a page like this, because the rest of it is a cost argument and you should know who is making it. The argument is not simply that online is cheaper. It is that the premium buys presence in the room while costing you the size of the pool you can choose a specialist from, and for IGCSE the specification matters more than the room.

Then there are the costs that are not the hourly rate at all, and these catch Al Jaddaf families more often than the rate does. Whether a quote is per hour or per lesson. Whether a sixty-minute session is actually fifty. Whether VAT is included in the figure you were given. What happens to a paid-for session cancelled at short notice. Whether a monthly package expires. Whether the tutor charges travel separately in addition to the hourly figure, and whether a second child in the same session costs more. None of these appear in a headline rate and all of them change the annual total.

A second category of cost sits outside tuition entirely and belongs in the same budget. Examination entry fees, if a student is entered as a private candidate rather than through a school. Replacement textbooks for a changed specification. The cost of a November resit if a June grade is not what was needed. Families plan for the tutor and are surprised by the rest, and the resit is the expensive one because it arrives unbudgeted at the end of an already expensive year.

What follows itemises all of it: the premium taken apart, what each AED tier actually buys, a monthly budget across Year 10 and Year 11, the extras in a table, the equivalency rule that determines how many subjects you are paying for in the first place, and how Al Jaddaf's short commute makes each hour cheaper in real terms than it is for neighbouring districts.

Deciding in advance what June result would trigger a resit turns a surprise into a plan.

programmes.name: What the grades are being bought for
programmes.description: IGCSE grades feed into A Level, IB Diploma or other post-16 routes, and tier ceilings matter here. A Level Mathematics, Physics and Economics and IB Higher Level sciences assume the Extended or Higher tier content, so a lower-tier entry taken for safety can close a route.

Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which does not match the sourced rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: Where Al Jaddaf families actually spend their IGCSE tutoring budget, and what the money is buying in each subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most commonly bought subject and the one where the cheapest tier is least adequate at the top. Extended and Higher work is algebraic fractions, formula rearrangement and multi-step probability, where a method written in full earns marks a correct answer alone would forfeit.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and atomic physics. Pearson candidates need apparatus and variable-control questions drilled on paper because practical skills are assessed in the written papers. Unit conversion inside multi-stage calculations is the reliable loss.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, electrochemistry, organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. Moles arithmetic decides the grade, and a student who can construct a half-equation rather than recall one scores consistently higher on the longer paper.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Wide content and precise marking. Marks go to named structures, named processes and correctly directed diagram arrows. It is the subject where cheap support is most often adequate, because the work is recall discipline rather than technique.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Two or three sciences in a smaller award, broad per paper and shallower per topic. Revision needs to rotate rather than block. Students moving into a post-16 single science from this route usually carry a real gap in quantitative chemistry.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing and composition. Marks move when a student selects evidence for an argument rather than summarising a passage. Register errors in directed writing cost more than grammar errors do.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0993)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an optional speaking endorsement. Vocabulary range is scored, so a student recycling one connective across four paragraphs caps their own band regardless of accuracy.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Data response and case-study application decide the marks. A generic answer earns knowledge credit and stops; the same answer anchored to the named firm or dataset in the stem earns application and analysis credit too.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, binomial expansion, advanced trigonometry and vectors taken alongside 0580. The most expensive subject to support because specialist availability is thin, and the one with the clearest post-16 payoff.

sections.heading: The in-home premium, itemised
paragraphs: Here is the premium taken apart. A visiting tutor in Dubai is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour across the sources we could read, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online. The difference is not a quality difference, because it is frequently the same calibre of teacher. It is a bundle of costs that exist only because somebody travels, and once they are listed separately the decision becomes straightforward rather than emotional.

The first item is the tutor's unpaid travel time, which has to be recovered inside the billed hour. For Al Jaddaf that means getting onto and off a road network shared with Dubai Healthcare City, the Creek crossings and Business Bay traffic in the late afternoon. The second is route density: a visiting tutor can only serve families whose homes cluster, so their diary is built around geography rather than subject, and your match is constrained by their route before it is constrained by your child's specification.

The third is schedule rigidity. A visiting tutor cannot absorb a late finish, so a session delayed by twenty minutes is a session shortened by twenty minutes, and a cancellation inside the travel window is usually charged in full because the time cannot be resold. The fourth is replacement cost. If the arrangement ends mid-term, a local replacement takes weeks because the pool is bounded by the same geography, and in the final term before a series that delay is the expensive part rather than the rate.

What the premium genuinely buys is also worth stating, because there are cases where it is the right purchase. A younger or easily distracted student benefits from an adult physically present. Primary work with manipulatives and physical materials works better in a room. A household with unreliable connectivity has a practical reason. For a Year 10 or Year 11 IGCSE candidate working on past papers, none of those apply, and the premium is buying logistics rather than learning.

sections.heading: What AED 50, AED 150 and AED 300 an hour actually buy
paragraphs: Price tiers in this market correspond to real differences, and the useful question is not which tier is best but which tier matches the job. Buying above the job is waste and buying below it is a term spent not solving the problem. For a lot of IGCSE work, the cheap tier is genuinely sufficient, which is not something a tutoring provider normally says out loud.

At the bottom, budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik. That typically means somebody who sat the subject recently rather than taught it to a series. For unblocking a Core or Foundation homework problem, for Biology recall discipline, or for a Year 10 who needs company while working rather than instruction, it can be entirely adequate and buying more would be money spent on reassurance.

The middle tier, AED 150 to AED 300 online with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, buys someone who has taught the specification and can mark against the published scheme. That is the capability that matters for Extended and Higher tier work, because the gap at those tiers is usually technique rather than knowledge, and identifying an unclaimed method mark requires somebody who has read the scheme. This is where most IGCSE spending belongs.

Above it, specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the top. For IGCSE those rates are justified in narrow cases: Additional Mathematics 0606, a scarce subject combination, or a compressed pre-series rescue where experience of what moves marks quickly has real value. Outside those, the middle tier does the same job. Every figure here belongs to the named provider and was read in October 2026.

sections.heading: A two-year IGCSE budget, written out
paragraphs: Families plan a month and get surprised by a year, so here is the arithmetic across Year 10 and Year 11. Bestimate's published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are per subject. A family supporting three subjects at the middle band is looking at a materially different number from one supporting one.

The shape of a sensible two-year spend is uneven rather than flat. Year 10 is where a short diagnostic block costs little and prevents a lot, because a technique problem identified at fifteen is cheap to fix and the same problem at sixteen is not. The first half of Year 11 is where weekly support earns its place if a genuine gap exists. The eight to twelve weeks before the series is the expensive window, and it is expensive precisely because everyone buys at the same time, so booking the slot earlier costs the same and secures a better match.

Two line items sit outside tuition and belong in the same budget. If a student is entered as a private candidate rather than through their school, examination entry fees apply and the school or centre will quote them; this matters for a resit or for a subject the school does not offer. And the November resit itself is the commonly unbudgeted one: an entry, a compressed autumn of intensive work at peak demand, and results arriving in the new year. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The cost in context is worth anchoring. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against a school fee that is not increasing, a tutoring budget that doubles year on year deserves a question. The honest test is whether the last block of hours moved a measurable mark, and if nobody can say, that is the answer.

sections.heading: The extras that catch Al Jaddaf parents off guard
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the number everyone compares and it is not where the surprises live. Ask whether the quote is per hour or per lesson, because a fifty-minute lesson billed as an hour is a twenty per cent price increase hidden in a definition. Ask whether VAT is included in the figure you were given; we limit ourselves to stating whether our own quoted prices include it rather than making claims about the UAE tax treatment of tuition, which would need a Federal Tax Authority citation to assert.

Ask about cancellation. A visiting tutor who has already travelled cannot resell the slot, so late cancellation is normally charged in full, and over a term with illness and school trips that adds up to real money. Ask whether a monthly package expires, and whether unused sessions roll over, because an eight-session package bought in a month containing a school holiday can quietly become a six-session package. Ask whether a second child in the same household and the same session is charged separately.

Ask about materials. We do not supply past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads, because Cambridge and Pearson documents are copyright works that should be referenced and linked rather than redistributed. A provider offering a library of papers is offering something a legitimate operation would not, and it is worth noticing what else they might be relaxed about. We work from the official source in the session and show the student how to find it themselves.

Finally, ask what happens if the match is wrong. The useful answer is a replacement inside the same week, which is only possible when the pool is not bounded by driving distance. The unhelpful answer is a credit note. For an Al Jaddaf family in the final term before a series, the speed of replacement is worth more than a small difference in the hourly rate.

sections.heading: How many subjects are you actually paying for?
paragraphs: This question decides the budget before any hourly rate does, and it is where a widely circulated error costs money. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must submit proof of five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

One competitor page ranking for Gulf parents states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. That does not match the sourced rule. A family that believed it and bought support for a sixth subject purely to satisfy equivalency has spent money on a requirement that does not exist. We publish the five-subject figure with its source because being right about it is worth more than any marketing line, and because it is a decision a parent makes with real money attached.

Two things that follow. First, equivalency and school requirements are different things: a school may require more subjects than equivalency does, for its own curricular reasons, and that is the school's decision to explain. Second, nothing about equivalency implies tutoring is needed for it. It is a regulatory process with published requirements, performed by the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority, and IB Gram neither performs it nor guarantees it. Verify your own case with the authority rather than with any tutoring provider, including this one.

The American-track figures are sourced too and worth knowing if a household has children on both. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section; mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math. No IB points threshold appears in the source we read, so no IB equivalency figure is published on this page.
bullets: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education
Plus one Advanced Level at E, or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels at E

sections.heading: Why an Al Jaddaf hour costs less in real terms
paragraphs: If the rate is fixed, the real unit price is the rate divided by the usable fraction of the hour, and that fraction depends on when the session starts. Al Jaddaf is unusually well placed on this measure. The district is compact, sits beside Dubai Healthcare City Phase 2, and is minutes from the Creek crossings, so a student at a school inside the district or across in Dubai Festival City is frequently home in time for a 16:30 start. That is earlier than most Dubai neighbourhoods manage.

The arithmetic matters most for mathematics and the sciences, which degrade faster with fatigue than reading subjects do. Holding four steps of an algebraic rearrangement in working memory at 18:30, after a commute and a meal, is measurably harder than at 17:00. If you are paying the same rate either way, the later session is the more expensive one. We will recommend a shorter earlier session over a longer later one, which is less revenue and better value.

The counterpoint is for Al Jaddaf families whose children attend schools further out, in Nad Al Sheba or on the far side of Al Khail Road. Those students arrive home at the time their Al Jaddaf-schooled neighbours are starting, which converts a geographic advantage into a scheduling constraint. For them a weekend morning is the cheapest hour available, and it also widens the choice of tutor, because the weekday window from 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest in the UAE tutoring day.

A small operational point that saves money in households with two IGCSE candidates: schedule both sessions back to back on one evening. It keeps the rest of the week clear, keeps a parent supervising once rather than four times, and makes the arrangement survivable across a whole term, which is the thing most families underestimate when they buy.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the claims to price in
paragraphs: Some of what you are quoted is a claim rather than a service, and the claims are checkable. Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. A KHDA inspection rating judges a school. It does not transfer to a tutor, and no tutoring provider inherits it. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff that we do not hold.

Tutoring itself is regulated by permit, and this one you can ask about directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time. Because it is free, a provider citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is citing a cost that does not exist.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, which is why no amount appears here and why any specific figure quoted to you should be treated as unverified. A figure circulating in this market could not be confirmed against any official source, and the ministry was reported as not having specified amounts.

One more boundary. An Al Jaddaf parent may be offered their child's own subject teacher privately. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The person who sets and marks the school's assessments should not be separately paid by one family in the class, whatever the rate.

The MoHRE private tuition permit is free for two years, so permit cost cannot justify a rate

sections.heading: Getting started, and the cheapest first step
paragraphs: The cheapest first step is a diagnostic rather than a purchase. Send the board, the specification code, the tier and the series the entry is for, plus two evening windows that genuinely work from Al Jaddaf after the school run. We match a specification specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details required to book it, and the tutor writes a short note on what they found.

Judge the arrangement on that note. If it names a specific weakness and the evidence that would show it has moved, the match is sound and a short block with a stated endpoint is usually the right purchase. If the note is general, no amount of hours will fix the problem, because nobody has identified it. That is the test, and it costs you one free hour to run.

If no specialist is free in your window we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Scarcity concentrates in Additional Mathematics 0606, in Pearson Specification B, and in the weeks immediately before a series when demand peaks across the whole market. Booking the pre-series window early costs the same and gets a better match, which is the only free improvement available in this process.

Two limits stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; those are regulatory and institutional processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than a tutoring provider is where to verify them.

One free trial lesson per student, with no payment or card details beforehand

process.title: Price the job, not the tier
process.description: Decide what the problem actually is before choosing a price band. Recall discipline and Core homework sit at the budget tier honestly. Extended technique and scheme-level marking need the middle tier. Only scarce subjects and compressed pre-series work justify specialist rates, and buying above the job is waste.

process.title: Confirm the specification in writing
process.description: Board, code and tier: Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended, 0606, Pearson 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher, or 4MB1. A photograph of the statement of entry settles it, and it prevents a term of competent teaching aimed at an adjacent paper.

process.title: Run one diagnostic paper first
process.description: A timed past paper on the exact code and tier, marked against the published scheme question by question. The marking writes the topic list, and it frequently shows the problem is unclaimed method or reverse percentages rather than a content gap, which is cheaper to fix.

process.title: Ask the invoice questions before the first session
process.description: Per hour or per lesson. VAT included or not. The cancellation window. Package expiry and rollover. Second-child pricing. None of these appear in a headline rate and all of them change the annual total, and all are easier to ask before money has moved.

process.title: Fix the earliest slot the commute allows
process.description: Al Jaddaf's short journeys often make 16:30 workable, which makes each paid hour more productive. If the school is further out, take a weekend morning instead: it is the cheapest hour in real terms and it widens the choice of specialist.

process.title: Review against a measurable mark
process.description: At the school's next assessment, ask whether the targeted weakness moved. If nobody can point to a specific mark, the block ends rather than renewing. That single discipline prevents most of the money wasted in this market.

whyPoints.title: Every figure sourced, dated and attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED number on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the strongest pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency Dubai families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: No travel line, because no travel happens
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not visit UAE addresses. The in-home premium of AED 180 to AED 500 per hour exists partly to recover a tutor's time on the Creek-side roads at five o'clock, and removing it also removes the constraint that your match must live near you.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to buy a cheaper tier
whyPoints.description: For Core homework and recall discipline, budget online tutoring at AED 33 to AED 65 is genuinely adequate and buying a specialist would be reassurance rather than teaching. Recommending the cheaper option where it fits is the only way the expensive recommendation means anything.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with a stated endpoint
whyPoints.description: Six to eight sessions aimed at a named weakness, ending when the next school assessment shows movement. It is less revenue than an open weekly arrangement and better value, and it is what we recommend whenever the diagnostic points at technique.

whyPoints.title: Right about the equivalency rule
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. A ranking competitor says six, and a family acting on that pays for a subject the rule does not require.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims to pad the price
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit is free. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval. Any provider implying regulator endorsement or citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is charging you for something that is not there.

faqs.answer: On published figures, roughly a third to double. None of those four appears as a line on the invoice.

For Extended technique or scheme-level marking it is not, and the limit is specificity rather than ability.

faqs.question: What should a two-year IGCSE tutoring budget look like?
faqs.answer: Uneven rather than flat, and counted per subject. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A short diagnostic block in Year 10 costs little and prevents a lot. Weekly support belongs in the first half of Year 11 only where a genuine gap exists. The eight to twelve weeks before the series is the expensive window, so book it early.

faqs.question: What is the cost that catches families out after the June results?
faqs.answer: The November resit. It arrives unbudgeted at the end of an already expensive year and carries three costs: an entry made through the school's exam office, a compressed autumn of intensive tuition at the point when demand across the market is highest, and a results date in the new year rather than in August. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Deciding in advance what June result would trigger a resit converts the surprise into a plan you have already priced.

faqs.question: Does the UAE private tutoring permit cost anything that would push rates up?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. A provider citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is citing a cost that does not exist, which is worth noticing.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects do we actually need to pay for?
faqs.answer: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the sourced rule is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor publishes six, and a family acting on that pays for a subject the rule does not require. Your school may require more for its own reasons; that is separate.

faqs.question: Will you supply past papers and mark schemes as part of the fee?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who does is offering something a legitimate operation would not. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works, to be referenced and linked rather than redistributed. We work from the official source inside the session and show the student how to find the current document on the board's own site, which is a more durable skill: a student who can locate a syllabus can also check a claim a tutor has made.

faqs.question: Does an earlier session really get better value for the same money?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is measurable in usable minutes. The real unit price is the rate divided by the fraction of the hour that works, and that fraction falls as the evening goes on. Al Jaddaf is well placed here: short journeys mean a student at a school inside the district or across the Creek is often home for a 16:30 start. Mathematics and the sciences degrade faster with fatigue than reading subjects do, so we will recommend a shorter earlier session over a longer later one.

faqs.question: What if we cancel a session at short notice?
faqs.answer: Ask for the policy in writing before the first lesson, because this is where a term's budget quietly inflates. A visiting tutor who has already travelled cannot resell the slot, so late cancellation is normally charged in full, and across a term with illness and school trips that becomes real money. An online session is easier to move, but a clear notice window should still be stated either way. A provider who will not put the cancellation terms in writing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two of my children in the same session to save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on how close the two are in specification and tier rather than in age. Two students on the same code and tier working on the same paper can share an hour productively. Two on different boards, or one on Core and one on Extended, cannot, and a shared session becomes two half sessions at full price. Ask how a second child is charged before assuming a saving. Scheduling two separate sessions back to back on one evening is usually the better arrangement.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any KHDA authorisation, and would that justify a higher rate?
faqs.answer: No to both. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority and is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools, and an inspection rating judges a school rather than a tutor. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff. A provider implying regulator endorsement to justify a rate is selling a claim, not a service.

faqs.question: Should we be planning for a February or March IGCSE series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and acting on that would waste a term. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only; UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Several pages aimed at Gulf parents quote a February or March window with an Indian entry deadline, and a family budgeting intensive tuition towards it would be paying for revision before an exam their school cannot enter them for. Treat that quote as a reason to check everything else the provider has said.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the last block of tutoring was worth the money?
faqs.answer: Ask whether a specific mark moved, and insist on an answer at the school's next assessment. If the tutor can point to the weakness that was targeted and the evidence that it shifted, the block worked. If the answer is general improvement in confidence, the block did not, and renewing it will not change that. One timed paper marked to the published scheme before and after is the cheapest evaluation available, and it is the discipline that prevents most of the money wasted in this market.

intro.heading: Two years, four fixed points, and one deadline nobody mentions
paragraphs: IGCSE looks like a two-year teaching course with examinations at the end. Operationally it is a sequence of four fixed points, and every useful decision a family makes is positioned relative to one of them. The first is the tier entry, settled in Year 10 or early Year 11 and the only one that changes the grade ceiling. The second is the board's final entry date, which closes months before the papers. The third is the mock series in the winter of Year 11. The fourth is the exam window itself.

The tier entry is the one almost nobody discusses with parents. In Cambridge mathematics and the sciences a Core entry caps the achievable grade at C; in Pearson mathematics a Foundation entry caps it below what most A Level mathematics courses require. The decision is generally made by the school on Year 10 performance, and a family that wants it reconsidered needs timed-paper evidence and needs to produce it before entries are submitted, not after.

The second fixed point catches families because the gap is counter-intuitive. Entries close long before the examinations, and the school's own internal deadline sits earlier still because the exams officer has to collate a whole cohort. By the time a Year 11 student starts to worry in the spring, the entry, the tier and the subject list are settled. Checking the statement of entry when it arrives is a ten-minute job that occasionally catches an error worth a whole grade.

The third point, the winter mock series, is the most valuable piece of data a family ever receives and the most frequently wasted. A mock is only diagnostic if it is marked against the published scheme and the losses are categorised, and most students receive a total and a comment. Sorting twelve lost marks into content, method, misreading and clock tells a tutor what to do; a total of sixty-three per cent tells nobody anything.

The fourth is the window, and the thing to know about it in the UAE is specific. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those two. The February/March series exists but Cambridge offers it to India only, so a revision plan built around a spring sitting belongs to a different country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

This page also answers the home-tutoring question directly rather than dodging it, because the search phrase is honest and deserves an honest reply. In-home tutoring in Dubai is a real market with published rates and real advantages for some students. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and the comparison below exists so the decision is made with numbers rather than by default.

sections.heading: Year 10: the tier decision and the deadline attached to it
paragraphs: The single most consequential thing that happens in IGCSE happens in Year 10 and is rarely framed as a decision at all. Schools place students on Core or Extended in Cambridge mathematics and the sciences, and on Foundation or Higher in Pearson mathematics, largely on the strength of Year 10 performance. The placement sets a grade ceiling: Core caps at C, and a Foundation mathematics entry sits below what most A Level mathematics courses ask for.

There is a genuine case for the lower tier. A student who would score across the bottom of an Extended paper can come out with a secure C rather than an insecure E, and where science or mathematics is not a prerequisite for the next step that is the better outcome. The case against is that the ceiling closes IB Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and most A Level science and mathematics routes, and sixteen-year-olds rarely understand the consequence when the placement happens.

What converts this from a complaint into a plan is evidence and timing. Schools move students between tiers on timed-paper performance, not on parental preference, so six weeks of honestly marked higher-tier papers gives a head of department something to act on. And it has to happen before entries are submitted: board entry dates close months before the papers and the school's internal collation deadline sits earlier still.

Practically that means a Year 10 family in Al Khail Gate who suspects the tier is wrong should start gathering papers in the spring of Year 10 or the first weeks of Year 11, not in the spring of Year 11. By then the entry is made, the statement of entry has been issued, and the only remaining question is how high within the capped range the student can reach.
