sections.heading: The June series counted backwards
paragraphs: Counting backwards from the June series is how a final-year plan gets built, and the first milestone is administrative rather than academic. The school's internal entry deadline comes first, set weeks ahead of the board's own final entry date because a whole cohort has to be collated. Then the board's final entry date. Then the statement of entry, which should be checked line by line against what the student is actually studying.

Then mocks, usually in the winter term, which produce the only genuinely diagnostic data of the two years. Then a specification coverage check about twelve weeks out, where every topic not yet taught becomes a named risk rather than a surprise in May. Then the timed-paper phase in the final eight weeks, which is where measurable grade movement happens. Then the window, then results, then the resit decision.

Pearson's published dates illustrate how long the tail runs after the papers. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Its November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official timetable is the only one to plan against.

Cambridge adds a complication worth knowing about. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, and Cambridge states that using the correct version for your zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Dubai family that means one rule: use the timetable the school's exams officer issues, not one found through a search.

sections.heading: The November series: resit route, and sometimes the better first sitting
paragraphs: The November series is the UAE's resit route for both boards, and it is also an option some families never consider as a first sitting. A student who is clearly not ready in June, perhaps after a mid-course school change or a long absence, can sometimes be better served by sitting a subject in November with an extra term of teaching behind them, provided the school is willing to enter them.

As a resit route the thing to understand is how early the entry closes. Results arrive in August for the June series, and the November entry has to be made while a family is still digesting them. A student who misses a target grade on results day and spends three weeks deciding what to do has often lost the window. Having a provisional answer before results arrive, so the decision takes a day rather than a month, is the practical response.

Pearson's published pattern shows how long the November tail runs: its November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That is a long gap between papers and results, and it matters if a sixth-form or university offer depends on the grade. A family in that position should check with the receiving institution what date it needs the result by before assuming a November resit solves the problem.

One correction worth making explicitly, because a previous generation of advice circulating for UAE families got it wrong. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. A Dubai student cannot use it as an earlier resit route, and any schedule showing a spring sitting for a UAE candidate is a schedule for a different country.

sections.heading: What to do with mock results, which is more than read them
paragraphs: The winter mock series produces the most useful data a family receives across the two years, and most of its value is thrown away within a week. A student is given a total, perhaps a grade, and a comment. The script goes into a bag. Nobody categorises the losses, so nobody knows whether the problem is content, method presentation, misreading or running out of time, and the revision that follows is therefore guesswork dressed as diligence.

The alternative takes an afternoon. Get the script back, mark it against the published scheme question by question, and label every lost mark with one of four causes. Content means the student did not know it. Method means they knew it and did not write the working that earns the credit. Misread means they answered a different question from the one asked, including answering at the wrong command term. Clock means the marks were lost at the end because time ran out.

The four causes need entirely different responses. Content means teaching. Method means a mechanical habit, write the relationship, substitute, state the answer with units. Misread means command-term drills and slower reading of the stem. Clock means budgeting minutes against marks before writing anything. A student with twelve lost marks that are nine method and three clock does not need more revision at all, and more revision is exactly what they will be told to do.

This is also the moment a tier conversation either happens or is lost. A mock sat on a higher-tier paper with a respectable raw mark is the evidence a head of department needs, if entries have not yet closed. A mock sat on a lower-tier paper tells you only how high within a capped range the student sits, which is worth knowing but is not a decision.

sections.heading: Entry admin that goes wrong, and the ten-minute check that catches it
paragraphs: Examination administration is not glamorous and it occasionally costs a grade. The statement of entry a school issues lists every subject, every syllabus code, every tier and every component the student has been entered for. Errors do occur: a subject entered at the wrong tier, a component missing, a student entered for Core after a tier change was agreed verbally but not processed, or a syllabus code that does not match the textbook the class has been using all year.

Checking it takes ten minutes and the window to correct an error is narrow, because entries close months before the papers and late amendments may not be possible at all. The check is mechanical: read each line, confirm the subject, confirm the tier, confirm the code matches what the student is being taught, and query anything that does not match in writing rather than in a corridor conversation.

The zone question is the second administrative item. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, warning that the correct version must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong timetable. A family that downloads a timetable from a search result rather than taking the school's is taking an avoidable risk for no benefit.

The third is the private candidate route, which some families in this belt use for an extra subject the school does not offer or for a resit after leaving a school. Private entry is made through an approved centre rather than directly with the board, carries its own fees and deadlines, and for subjects with practical or coursework components may not be available at all. Anyone considering it should establish those three things before planning any teaching around it.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Al Khail Gate, priced against the calendar
paragraphs: In-home tutoring in Dubai has published rates and they are higher than online for comparable qualifications. Bestimate's rate work puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, travel included. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly packages in the market run roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Read against the calendar, the travel cost shows up in a second way that money alone does not capture. The exam term needs flexibility: a session moved to the day before a mock, an extra hour in the week three papers land, a long weekend block for a full timed paper. A tutor crossing the city can offer one window per evening and loses a session rather than moving it when the school bus is late. Across a twelve-week exam term that is several hours paid for and not delivered.

What the in-home premium genuinely buys is presence, and for some students that is the whole difference. A student who will not work unsupervised, or a younger Year 10 student who drifts at a screen, benefits from a person at the table in a way no format argument overrides. A family in that position should buy in-home from somebody who sells it, using the published bands above as the benchmark for what is reasonable.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and the published mark scheme shared on screen.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE subjects and the summer between Year 10 and Year 11
paragraphs: Three features of the UAE calendar are missing from any revision schedule imported from the UK. The first is that KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with its requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those are real timetable hours and real homework on top of eight or nine IGCSE subjects.

KHDA also sets the organisation: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for the two groups strictly prohibited, Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit with a recommendation that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. A Dubai Year 11 week is fuller than a UK one, so three fixed tutoring sessions a week look decisive and collapse by week four.

The second is Ramadan, which compresses the school day and moves the household evening, and which falls inside the stretch where the timed-paper phase should be doing its work for a June series. In this community sessions commonly move to after Iftar or to weekend mornings for the month. Online delivery makes that a calendar change rather than a renegotiation, but the weeks still need planning rather than absorbing.

The third is the summer between Year 10 and Year 11, which is the best-value stretch in the whole qualification and is almost always wasted. It is the only period with free time and no deadlines, and it is the natural moment for a tier-evidence block or for teaching the content a student missed during a school transfer. Two or three sessions a week for the final weeks of summer, aimed at specific named gaps, changes the starting position of the final year.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, board materials and what we will not do
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, and the honesty boundary still matters, particularly as a student moves towards A Level or Diploma investigations where most of the assessed writing happens at home. The working rule is that the student produces the work and the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on it. A tutor who returns a rewritten version has substituted their own judgement and created a problem the student carries.

What a tutor can legitimately do is wide: explain why a method is uncontrolled, ask what the student thinks the next step is, mark a practice answer against the published scheme, show a worked example of a comparable question, and say plainly where credit stopped. What a tutor must not do is write an answer for submission, edit assessed work to completion, or supply a model response to be handed in. Families should ask any provider where that line sits and treat a vague reply as the answer.

There is a second boundary on materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. A tutor should reference and link them at their official source rather than distributing copies. A provider advertising a downloadable library of board material is describing its standards more accurately than its marketing copy does.

Stated plainly for completeness: IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Individual private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, and a parent is entitled to ask any individual tutor whether they hold it.

process.title: Establish where in the cycle you are
process.description: Year 10 with the tier open, Year 11 with entries closed, or post-mock with eight weeks left. Those three positions call for completely different plans, and naming which one applies takes a minute and prevents buying the wrong intervention.

process.title: Send the statement of entry and a marked paper
process.description: The statement of entry gives the syllabus codes, the tiers and the components. A recent marked paper gives the pattern of loss. Those two documents are enough to build a dated plan rather than a general arrangement.

process.title: Free trial on a real past-paper question
process.description: The trial marks the student's own answer live against the published scheme and names the dominant cause of lost marks. No payment is taken before it, and if the honest conclusion is that the tier rather than the teaching is the problem, that is what gets said.

process.title: Put the hours where the calendar puts the pressure
process.description: A tier-evidence block in Year 10, a diagnostic block immediately after mocks, and a weekly paper routine in the final term. Hours spread evenly across two years cost more and achieve less than the same hours placed at those three points.

process.title: Decide the November question before August
process.description: If a resit is plausible, have the answer provisionally ready before results arrive, because the November entry closes while families are still digesting August results. A decision that takes a day rather than a month keeps the option open.

whyPoints.title: The tier treated as the decision it is
whyPoints.description: A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade and closes post-16 science and mathematics routes. We say so early and gather timed higher-tier papers as evidence while the entry is still open, because afterwards no amount of teaching lifts a ceiling.

whyPoints.title: Mocks turned into data
whyPoints.description: A mock total tells nobody anything. Re-marking the script to the scheme and labelling every lost mark as content, method, misread or clock tells a tutor exactly what to do with the remaining weeks.

whyPoints.title: Series dates taken from the boards
whyPoints.description: UAE centres sit Cambridge June and November; the February/March series is offered to India only. Cambridge's six administrative zones each have their own timetable, so we point families to the exams officer rather than restating dates.

whyPoints.title: The in-home premium shown honestly
whyPoints.description: Published figures put in-home at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 online, and monthly packages at roughly double for the same eight contact hours. Families should see that before choosing a format.

whyPoints.title: Plans that survive a Dubai term
whyPoints.description: KHDA's mandatory subjects, Ramadan inside the June run-up and a heavy school commute mean three fixed sessions a week collapse. One well-used weekly session plus a paper routine lasts the term, which is what actually moves marks.

whyPoints.title: Online only in the UAE, said up front
whyPoints.description: All UAE lessons run live over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we hold no regulator accreditation of any kind.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 10 in the Dubailand belt. Is it too early for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the best time, and almost nobody uses it. Year 10 is when the tier placement is decided in Cambridge mathematics and the sciences, and in Pearson mathematics, and that placement sets the grade ceiling for everything afterwards. A block of honestly marked higher-tier past papers in Year 10 gives a head of department evidence to act on while entries are still open. The same money spent in the spring of Year 11, after entries close, can only work on how high within a capped range he reaches.

faqs.question: How far before the exams do IGCSE entries actually close?
faqs.answer: Months, and the school's internal deadline sits earlier still because the exams officer has to collate a whole cohort. That is why a tier conversation opened in the spring term of Year 11 has usually missed the window for the next series. Once entries are submitted, the statement of entry is issued and the subjects, codes and tiers are fixed. Checking that document line by line when it arrives is a ten-minute job that occasionally catches an error worth a whole grade.

faqs.question: Can a Dubai student use the Cambridge February or March series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. This matters because advice circulating for UAE families has previously shown a spring sitting with an autumn entry deadline, which is a plan for a different country and a date a parent might act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Confirm your own dates with the school's exams officer, who issues the correct timetable for your centre.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish six different timetables?
faqs.answer: Because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and each zone has its own timetable. Cambridge states in its guidance to exams officers that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Dubai family the practical rule is simple: use the timetable your school issues, not one found through a search engine, however official the page looks.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with my daughter's mock results?
faqs.answer: Get the script back and re-mark it against the published scheme question by question, then label every lost mark as content, method, misread or clock. Those four causes need completely different responses: teaching, a working-out habit, command-term drills, or budgeting minutes against marks. A student whose twelve lost marks are nine method and three clock does not need more revision, which is precisely what they will otherwise be told to do. The afternoon this takes is the best-value afternoon of the year.

faqs.question: When does a November resit entry have to be made?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, often while August results are still being absorbed. Pearson's pattern shows the shape: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while its November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. The practical response is to have a provisional answer ready before results arrive so the decision takes a day, and to confirm the deadline with the exams officer.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to our apartment in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and published mark scheme shared on screen. If in-home delivery is what your household needs, the published Dubai band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium buy better teaching or just a journey?
faqs.answer: Mostly a journey, with one genuine exception. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online. Monthly packages run roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for eight in-home contact hours against about AED 799 for eight online. The exception is presence: a student who will not work unsupervised, or a Year 10 student who drifts at a screen, genuinely benefits from a person at the table.

faqs.question: How many timed papers a week should a Year 11 student sit?
faqs.answer: One per subject, properly. Sat under a clock with no notes and the phone elsewhere, marked against the published scheme the same day, with every lost mark categorised. Four papers a week produces fatigue and sloppy marking, and the marks stop responding. One paper per subject per week plus a short midweek task on a named weakness is sustainable through a whole exam term, and sustainability matters more than intensity in the final eight weeks before a series.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an extra IGCSE subject as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and three things need checking first. Private entry is made through an approved centre rather than directly with the board, it carries its own fees and deadlines, and for subjects with practical or coursework components it may not be available at all. Establish all three before planning any teaching, because a student taught for a year and then unable to enter has lost the year. Approved centres in Dubai will state what they accept and by when.

faqs.question: Does the summer between Year 10 and Year 11 matter?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value stretch in the qualification and the most commonly wasted. It is the only period with free time and no deadlines, which makes it the natural slot for a tier-evidence block or for teaching content missed during a school transfer. Two or three sessions a week in the final weeks of summer, aimed at named gaps rather than general revision, changes the starting position of the final year. Using the whole summer is counterproductive; students come back tired to a harder year.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan fit into preparing for a June series?
faqs.answer: It falls inside the stretch where the timed-paper phase should be doing its work, so it needs planning rather than absorbing. The school day compresses and the household evening moves, and in this community sessions commonly shift to after Iftar or to weekend mornings for the month. Because delivery is online, that is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation with a driver. The practical approach is to front-load full papers before the month and keep shorter targeted sessions running through it.

faqs.question: Do Dubai's mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons reduce revision time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and UK revision schedules ignore it entirely. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools must also run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of those subjects. A Dubai Year 11 week therefore has fewer free evenings, which is why three fixed sessions a week tend to collapse by week four.

faqs.question: What if the statement of entry shows the wrong tier?
faqs.answer: Raise it in writing with the exams officer immediately, because the window to amend is narrow and late changes may not be possible at all. Errors do happen: a tier change agreed verbally but never processed, a component missing, or a syllabus code that does not match the textbook the class has used all year. Reading each line and confirming subject, tier, code and components takes ten minutes. A corridor conversation is not a record; an email is.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting eight weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right problem. Eight weeks is enough to fix technique, because nothing new is being learned: method marks written down, command terms read properly, Paper 6 practical questions drilled, minutes budgeted against marks. It is not enough to reteach two years of content across several subjects, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling. The honest plan at that distance is triage: pick the one or two subjects closest to a grade boundary and spend the hours there rather than spreading them.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.closingHeading: Find out which of the four fixed points you are between
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Khail Gate, the plan depends entirely on where in the two-year cycle your child sits. Year 10 with the tier still open is the cheapest and most valuable place to act. Post-mock in Year 11 is the point where the best data of the two years has just arrived and is usually thrown away. Send the statement of entry and a recent marked paper, and a specialist can tell you which position you are in and what the next eight weeks should do. The trial lesson marks a real answer live against the published scheme, and no payment is taken before it. All UAE lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE.

intro.heading: Eight subjects, ninety minutes, and a decision nobody wants to make
paragraphs: An IGCSE candidate in Al Khawaneej is in a genuinely difficult position, and the difficulty is arithmetic rather than academic. They carry eight or nine examined subjects. They travel out of the community to a school in Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais or further, because the community itself holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus rather than a large secondary cohort. They arrive home late. And after a break and a meal there are perhaps ninety minutes in which real work can happen on a school night.

Ninety minutes across nine subjects is ten minutes each, which is obviously useless, so what happens instead is triage by panic: whichever subject has homework due tomorrow gets the evening. That is a survivable strategy in Year 9 and a damaging one in Year 11, because the subjects that quietly decay are the ones without weekly homework, and they reappear in the mocks as a surprise. Any tutoring decision taken in this situation has to start by accepting that the hours are finite and choosing what they are for.

That is where the home-tutor search usually begins, and it deserves an honest answer in three parts. What the in-home market charges around here, which is published and higher than most families expect because the figure contains a drive out to the eastern edge of Dubai. What the drive does to the start time, which is worse than the price. And what IB Gram actually does, which is to teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India.

There is a factor specific to Dubai that most tutoring pages ignore entirely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those subjects occupy real timetable hours and real homework time, and they do not count towards the five-subject total the Ministry of Education uses for British-track equivalency. A family planning an IGCSE revision programme without them in the calculation is planning with the wrong number of hours.

The rest of this page is the working. How many subjects can honestly be tutored, and what each one costs. Which subject earns the hour when only one can have it. What the mock cycle is actually for and how to use it. Where the usable time in an Al Khawaneej week really sits. And why checking the exam board and syllabus code matters more than checking the tutor's postcode. Read it with a pen and your child's own timetable next to you rather than as general advice.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.subjectsIntro: The subjects an Al Khawaneej IGCSE candidate is usually carrying, with a note on how much weekly attention each genuinely needs. The point is to show which can be left to look after itself and which cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject with the highest leverage, because its skills appear inside every science paper. Needs regular short practice rather than occasional long sessions, and decays faster than any other subject if left alone for a fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High recall volume and strict command-term discipline. Suits frequent twenty-minute retrieval blocks on tired evenings, which makes it one of the few subjects that genuinely works in a short weekday window.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic first, then everything else. The calculation work tolerates a tired slot; ionic equations and organic pathways need a clearer head. Easy definitional marks are routinely given away and are cheap to secure.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Loses more marks to missing units and failed rearrangement than to physics. Twenty minutes a week of pure algebra practice with no physics context fixes more physics marks than an equivalent amount of topic revision.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Rewards practice at writing under time pressure more than it rewards content. One timed piece a week, marked against the criteria, moves this subject faster than any amount of reading about technique.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Depends on knowing a small number of texts extremely well rather than broadly. Quotation security is the limiting factor for most students, and it responds to short daily work far better than to weekend sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and excluded from the five-subject count for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency. It still occupies real timetable and homework hours, which must appear in any honest revision plan.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools, taught in separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA requires teachers of this subject to hold its approval to teach it.

subjects.name: Business Studies or Economics
subjects.description: Definition-dependent and heavily rewarded for precise terminology. A student who can define terms exactly scores well; one who paraphrases loses marks on questions they understood, which makes it a high-return subject for short focused work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logical decomposition plus a practical component that rewards documenting what was actually done. Shares problem-solving habits with mathematics and physics, so progress in one tends to show up in the others.

sections.heading: The arithmetic: nine subjects against the hours that actually exist
paragraphs: Write the numbers down and the decision makes itself. A Year 11 candidate in Al Khawaneej has five school evenings, of which one or two are usually taken by co-curricular commitments or a late arrival, leaving three or four with a usable window of roughly ninety minutes. Add a weekend and the honest weekly total for independent academic work is somewhere between six and nine hours, including homework that must be submitted.

Nine subjects do not fit into that, and pretending otherwise is how a revision plan becomes decoration. What fits is homework, plus genuine work on two subjects, plus light maintenance on the rest. Any plan that allocates real time to five subjects is allocating imaginary time, and the first week it meets a late bus and a chemistry deadline it collapses, taking the student's confidence in planning with it.

The table below is the exercise worth doing on paper with your child. It is deliberately unflattering, because the useful version of this calculation is the one that produces a decision rather than a feeling. Most families who do it arrive at the same conclusion: tutor one subject well, maintain the rest, and revisit the choice after the mocks when there is real evidence about where the marks are being lost. One more reason to do it on paper: a student who has seen the numbers stops believing that the problem is their own laziness, which is the belief that makes the whole situation worse. The hours genuinely are not there, and naming that out loud changes the conversation from blame to planning.

sections.heading: What a visiting tutor costs per subject, and why families over-commit
paragraphs: Consider the money from the subject-count end rather than the hourly end, because that is where the mistake happens. Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's rate table, with independent home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500 an hour. Monthly in-home packages circulate at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Qualified tutors teaching online are published lower: Unitors from AED 150 an hour for IGCSE, TutorChase around AED 270, and the budget online band from around AED 33 to 65 at Tutopiya and EdFlik.

Now multiply. A family that decides three subjects need in-home help is looking at three times a single-subject monthly figure, which at the published package rates runs into several thousand dirhams a month before anybody has asked whether three subjects can even be worked on in the available hours. They cannot. The commonest expensive mistake in this market is not paying too much per hour; it is buying more hours than the week can absorb, and then watching attendance decay.

The useful move is to spend the single-subject budget on the best available teaching for the subject that matters most, and to accept maintenance on the others. The in-home premium is, by the market's own pricing, roughly the cost of the drive: eight hours delivered in-home is priced at about double eight hours delivered online. Redirect that difference into subject expertise rather than travel and the same money buys a specialist in the right board and syllabus. All of the figures above are provider-published and were read in October 2026; they are market information, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Which subject earns the hour
paragraphs: If one subject gets real attention, the choice should be made on evidence rather than on which subject produces the most complaining. Three tests, applied in order, settle it in most households. The first is leverage: does this subject's weakness show up inside other subjects? Mathematics does. A student whose algebra is insecure is losing marks in physics and chemistry as well, so an hour spent there buys marks in three places.

The second test is distance from the boundary. A subject sitting two marks below a grade boundary is a far better investment than one sitting fifteen marks below, because the work required is proportionate and the result is visible quickly, which sustains a student's willingness to keep going. Marked papers tell you this; feelings do not. If the school has not given a grade estimate with a mark, ask for the raw mark rather than the grade.

The third test is whether the subject matters for the next step. A student heading for science A Levels or Diploma sciences needs Extended-tier science grades, and a subject that will be abandoned at sixteen can be allowed to land where it lands. Families frequently invest in the subject that is most distressing rather than the one that is most consequential, which is understandable and expensive. Make the choice explicitly, write it down, and revisit it with the mock results rather than every fortnight. A written choice also survives a bad fortnight, where a choice held only in somebody's head quietly becomes whichever subject shouted loudest that week.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the hours nobody counts
paragraphs: Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with an April 2026 date for schools whose year begins in April. These are not optional add-ons. They are timetabled subjects with homework, and any revision plan written as though an IGCSE candidate has only their examined international subjects to manage is working from the wrong total.

KHDA's own guidance carries detail worth knowing. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two practical notes follow. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allowing schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which means tutoring support here has to work from the school's own material rather than from anything imported. It also matters for equivalency: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five subjects required for the Ministry's British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: The mock cycle, and the most valuable fortnight of the two years
paragraphs: Mock examinations are treated by most families as a prediction and by most students as a disaster or a relief. They are neither. A mock is a diagnostic that has already been paid for, and the fortnight after the marked scripts come back is the highest-value tutoring period in the whole IGCSE course, because the evidence is fresh, specific and nobody has to generate it.

Using it properly takes a procedure. Collect the marked scripts rather than just the grades. For each one, log the losses by cause rather than by topic: marks lost to missing units, to command terms answered descriptively, to mole conversions, to rearrangement, to running out of time. Count them. Three causes will dominate, and those three are what the block between mocks and the series should attack. Everything else is a distraction, however uncomfortable it feels to leave it.

The reason this works is that causes transfer across topics and topics do not. A student who stops losing marks to missing units gains them in every question in every paper. A student who revises one more topic gains marks only if that topic appears. With limited hours, which is the defining condition of an Al Khawaneej week, the cause-based approach is simply more efficient. It also has the advantage of being finite: a student can see three items on a list and believe in finishing them. There is a secondary benefit worth naming. A student who has watched three causes shrink across six papers has evidence that effort changes outcomes, which is a different thing from being told that it does.

sections.heading: Where the evening actually is, and how to protect it
paragraphs: Everything above depends on knowing when your child can work, which is not when the school day ends. The sequence is the bell, then the bus departure, then the arrival in Al Khawaneej, then a break and a meal, then the first page open. For a short run to Mirdif that chain is manageable. For a long run to Al Qusais or deep into Al Warqa it can consume an hour and a half, and on a day with an after-school commitment it consumes the evening entirely.

Measure it for one week, writing down only the final number: the time the first page was genuinely open. Then protect what is left. The two rules that hold up are not to book anything immediately after arrival, because the hour is wasted and the student learns to resent the arrangement, and to put a session early in the school week so there are days left to act on it. A session on the final school evening of the week lands its feedback into a weekend and loses most of it.

The weekend morning is the resource nobody uses. One hour on a Saturday morning, with a rested student, will carry the hardest subject better than two tired weekday hours. The trade that persuades most students is explicit: one weekend morning hour in exchange for one weekday evening entirely free of academic work. During Ramadan the whole structure moves after Iftar rather than pausing, which keeps the two years continuous instead of leaving a hole in the middle of Year 11.

sections.heading: Check the board and the code before you check the tutor
paragraphs: Two Al Khawaneej neighbours in the same year group can be sitting different syllabuses in the same subject, because the schools this community feeds use different boards. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both run international GCSE qualifications, their question styles differ, their practical assessment arrangements differ, and in mathematics the tiering language differs. A tutor fluent in one board prepares a student competently for the content and imperfectly for the paper.

Finding out takes five minutes. The statement of entry names the board and the syllabus code. So does the front page of any past paper the school has issued. Where a subject is tiered, ask the school directly which tier your child is entered for and what the highest available grade is at that tier, because that answer is not reversible once the series has been sat and it is the single most consequential administrative fact of the two years.

Then ask any prospective tutor which board and which code they teach, and treat a vague answer as the answer. This matters more than proximity by a wide margin: a tutor three streets away who teaches the other board is worse for your child than a specialist in the right syllabus teaching over video from anywhere. It is also the reason the postcode question, which is where most families start, turns out to be the least important question on the list. The postcode question is where almost every family starts, and it is comfortably the least useful question on the list.

sections.heading: Starting, and what the first month should produce
paragraphs: Send three things and the first session does real work. The statement of entry, showing board, code and tier for the subject in question. The most recent marked paper with the teacher's comments intact. And the measured time your child is genuinely able to work on a weekday, from the week-long exercise above. Those three facts turn a trial lesson from an introduction into a diagnosis.

The free trial runs one-to-one over live video. Ask the tutor to work through the marked paper and name the causes of the lost marks, then say what the first block will target. If the answer is specific enough that you could repeat it to your child in two sentences, book it. If the hour was spent on the tutor's experience, it has not answered the question you asked. Changing tutor in week one is normal and costs nothing; changing in week nine costs a term.

What the first month should produce is a shorter loss log, not a happier feeling. By the fourth session there should be a marked piece of work showing fewer marks lost to the specific causes you targeted. If there is not, the method changes or the tutor does, rather than more hours being added to a plan that has already been shown not to work. On availability: coverage is by board and syllabus, and where no UAE-based specialist for your child's code has a slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable, you will be told and offered a specialist elsewhere teaching over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Do the arithmetic first
process.description: Count the usable evenings, subtract homework, and see how many subjects the week can actually hold. Most Al Khawaneej families arrive at one subject tutored properly plus maintenance on the rest, and arriving there deliberately is much cheaper than arriving there after three months.

process.title: Send the board, the code and a marked paper
process.description: Statement of entry for board, syllabus code and tier, plus the most recent marked script with comments intact. A tutor fluent in the wrong board teaches the content competently and prepares the student imperfectly for the paper they will sit.

process.title: Free trial used as a diagnostic
process.description: One hour over live video with the script read in advance. Ask for the causes of the lost marks and the target of the first block. You should be able to repeat the answer to your child in two sentences, which is the test of whether it was specific.

process.title: Place the slot and protect it
process.description: Nothing straight off the bus, a short session early in the school week, and a weekend morning for the hardest work. Co-curricular days are no-tutoring days. Ramadan sessions move after Iftar rather than pausing for the month.

process.title: Judge the first month on the loss log
process.description: At four sessions, look for a marked paper with fewer marks lost to the causes you targeted. If the log has not shortened, change the method or the tutor. Adding hours to a plan that is not working is the most expensive available response.

whyPoints.title: The hours are counted honestly
whyPoints.description: Nine subjects against six to nine real weekly hours is the actual problem, and this page does that arithmetic before recommending anything. Plans that allocate real time to five subjects collapse in their first bad week and take the student's confidence in planning with them.

whyPoints.title: Cost framed by subject count
whyPoints.description: The expensive mistake in this market is buying more hours than the week can absorb, not paying too much per hour. Published in-home package rates multiplied by three subjects runs into thousands a month for sessions nobody can attend.

whyPoints.title: Mandatory UAE subjects in the calculation
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are timetabled in every Dubai private school and are excluded from the Ministry's five-subject equivalency count. No competitor page reviewed for this project has a section on them.

whyPoints.title: Board and code before postcode
whyPoints.description: A specialist in the right syllabus teaching over video beats a tutor three streets away who teaches the other board. Competitor pages reviewed mention almost no syllabus codes at all, which is how a plan ends up approximate.

whyPoints.title: Mock evidence used properly
whyPoints.description: The fortnight after marked mock scripts return is the highest-value period of the two years. Losses are logged by cause rather than by topic, because causes transfer across every paper and topics only pay if they appear.

whyPoints.title: No drive on either side
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the session starts when the student is ready. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is offered only in India.

faqs.question: How many subjects can an Al Khawaneej IGCSE week realistically absorb?
faqs.answer: One, in most Al Khawaneej households, with two as a stretch if they are alternated rather than run weekly. The constraint is not money, it is hours: a Year 11 candidate here has three or four usable weekday evenings of about ninety minutes, plus a weekend, and homework takes a large share of that. A plan allocating real time to three or more subjects is allocating time that does not exist, and it fails the first week a late bus meets a deadline.

faqs.question: Do you provide an IGCSE tutor who comes to the house in Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. UAE teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is deliberate. It removes the drive from both sides, so the session starts when your child is fed and ready rather than when a car reaches the eastern edge of the city, and it widens the choice of tutor from whoever will travel out here to whoever teaches your child's exact syllabus.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject is the best use of one tutored hour a week?
faqs.answer: Apply three tests in order. Leverage: mathematics weakness shows up inside physics and chemistry marks, so an hour there often buys marks in three subjects. Distance from the boundary: a subject two marks below a grade boundary is a far better investment than one fifteen below, and raw marks rather than grades tell you which. And consequence: a subject needed for science A Levels or Diploma sciences matters more than one being abandoned at sixteen. Decide once, write it down, revisit with mock results.

faqs.question: Why do Arabic and Islamic Education matter to an IGCSE revision plan?
faqs.answer: Because they are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and they occupy real timetable and homework hours that a plan counting only examined international subjects ignores. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects, calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, and requires teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education to hold its approval. They are also excluded from the five-subject count used for the Ministry's British-track equivalency.

faqs.question: What should we do with my child's marked mock scripts?
faqs.answer: Treat them as a diagnostic you have already paid for, and do not settle for the grades. Collect the scripts, and for each one log the losses by cause rather than by topic: missing units, command terms answered descriptively, mole conversions, rearrangement, running out of time. Count them. Three causes will dominate and those three are what the block before the series should attack. Causes transfer across every paper; a topic only pays if it appears.

faqs.question: Is an in-home IGCSE tutor worth the extra cost in the eastern suburbs?
faqs.answer: The market has largely answered this. Published Dubai in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 from independent tutors, with monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, against around AED 799 for eight online sessions. The same quantity of teaching is priced at roughly double when somebody drives. The premium buys presence and an hour in the car, not a better teacher or a wider choice, and it pushes the session start later.

faqs.question: My child does all the homework and still gets mediocre IGCSE grades. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because homework is being done rather than used. Submitted work keeps a student out of trouble; it does not reveal why marks are being lost, and the subjects without weekly homework decay unnoticed until the mocks expose them. The change that helps is small: after any marked piece of work, spend ten minutes identifying the cause of each lost mark and writing it in a running log. Three causes will recur, and fixing those three is worth more than another term of diligent submission.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's school use?
faqs.answer: Check the statement of entry or the front page of any past paper the school has issued. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both run international GCSE qualifications and their papers differ in style, structure and practical assessment arrangements. Two Al Khawaneej neighbours in the same year group can be sitting different syllabuses in the same subject. Ask any prospective tutor which board and which code they teach, and treat a vague answer as the answer; the right syllabus matters more than a short distance.

faqs.question: How short is a realistic weekday session for a Year 11 student here?
faqs.answer: Forty-five to sixty minutes, placed after arrival, a break and food rather than straight off the bus. Short and frequent beats long and tired for recall work, command-term practice and timed questions. Ninety-minute weekday blocks look efficient on a calendar and produce a student transcribing worked solutions in the final half hour. Save sustained work for a weekend morning, where a rested student can genuinely hold a difficult problem for an hour or more.

faqs.question: Can we tutor two subjects without doubling the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, by alternating weeks rather than halving sessions. A full-length session each week, switching subject fortnightly, keeps momentum in both; thirty minutes each produces two conversations and no practice. It works best when the two subjects share an underlying weakness, such as mathematics and physics both resting on rearrangement, because work in one week pays into the other. If neither subject moves after a month, drop to one and do it properly.

faqs.question: Does a Core tier entry affect what my child can do after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It can, and this is the administrative fact most worth checking early. Where a syllabus is tiered, Core entry caps the highest grade available, and science and mathematics A Levels and Diploma sciences commonly require Extended-tier grades. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is entered for in each subject and what the ceiling is under the grading scale in use. The entry is not reversible once the series has been sat, so the conversation belongs in the term before entries close.

faqs.question: When is it too late to start IGCSE tutoring in Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is rarely too late, but the plan has to change shape as the runway shortens. Early in Year 11 there is time to repair a foundation. In the final term there is not, and the work becomes triage: the three dominant loss causes from marked papers, the highest-frequency question types, and the easy definitional marks that are routinely given away. A content sweep in that window produces anxiety and very little movement. A diagnostic on a recent marked script in the first session is what makes triage accurate.

faqs.question: How do we keep a tutoring arrangement alive past week six?
faqs.answer: Place it where it can survive. Arrangements in this catchment fail for scheduling reasons rather than academic ones: a slot booked straight off a long bus route, or on a day with a co-curricular commitment, is attended badly twice and then cancelled. Measure the real window first, book inside it, treat activity days as no-tutoring days, and review at four sessions against a marked paper rather than against a feeling. A plan with one stated aim survives; a plan with five does not.

faqs.question: What does an Al Khawaneej family need to send before an IGCSE trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Three items. The statement of entry showing board, syllabus code and tier for the subject in question. The most recent marked paper with the teacher's annotations left on, because that is where the diagnosis comes from. And the measured time your child is genuinely able to work on a weekday, taken from a week of writing down when the first page was actually open. Those three facts turn the trial hour from an introduction into a piece of work.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.closingHeading: Fewer subjects, better placed, honestly costed
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.closingBody: The IGCSE problem in Al Khawaneej is arithmetic before it is academic: nine subjects, three or four usable evenings, and homework taking most of them. Count the hours, pick the one subject that earns them, and protect a weekend morning for the hardest work. Check the board and the syllabus code before you check anybody's postcode, because the right syllabus matters and the distance does not. Send a marked paper, take the free trial as a diagnostic, and judge the first month on whether the loss log got shorter. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
